The Menai Strait lies between Anglesey and the northwestern coast of mainland Wales.
a1-geography-0121: Which color usually represents water on maps?
Many maps use blue to represent seas, rivers and lakes.
a1-geography-0122: Which combination of conditions favors a braided river channel?
No sediment and closed underground flow
A deep tidal estuary with no bars within the channel
A large bed load, easily eroded banks and variable discharge
A small sediment load, stable rocky banks and regular discharge
Abundant bed load, easily eroded banks and fluctuating discharge help build mid-channel bars and divert flow among multiple channels.
a1-geography-0123: Which two countries are separated by the river whose mouth is at Saint-Louis?
The Senegal River forms much of the border between Senegal and Mauritania.
a1-geography-0124: What distinguished Ptolemy's Geographia in the history of mapmaking?
It recorded ocean depths using sound waves
It was limited to daily weather maps
It combined place names with their coordinates
The work included an extensive directory of places with latitudes and longitudes and guidance for constructing maps of the known world.
a1-geography-0125: Which resource triggered Johannesburg's rapid growth after its discovery nearby in 1886?
Johannesburg emerged and grew rapidly as a mining center after the discovery of Witwatersrand gold.
a1-geography-0126: What border characteristic defines Europe Square between Gorizia and Nova Gorica?
An international harbor shared by two countries
A sovereign enclave within one city
A shared urban space on the border line
The square lies between the Italian and Slovenian cities and was redeveloped as a cross-border public space linking the two urban areas.
a1-geography-0127: What falls as hard balls of ice during some storms?
Hailstones may fall from powerful storm clouds.
a1-geography-0128: An increase in the proportion of a country's population living in cities represents which process?
Urbanization is an increase in the share of people residing in areas classified as urban.
a1-geography-0129: Which hill has a castle overlooking Barcelona's port?
Montjuic Castle stands on a hill overlooking Barcelona's port.
a1-geography-0130: What historical function is represented by the wooden Bryggen complex on Bergen's waterfront?
Bryggen was a Hanseatic League trading quarter, and its wooden buildings reveal how merchants' activities at the port were organized.
a1-geography-0131: Following the Russian-Chinese border eastward leads to a major watercourse. What is its name?
The Amur flows east along long stretches of the Russian-Chinese border before reaching the Pacific Ocean.
a1-geography-0133: Which river flows out of Ethiopia's Lake Tana?
The Blue Nile flows out of Lake Tana in Ethiopia.
a1-geography-0134: What is the main task of autonomous floats in the global Argo program?
Measuring ocean temperature and salinity down to about two thousand meters
Imaging national borders from a fixed orbit above the equator
Drilling rock samples from the deep ocean floor
Guiding commercial ships using coastal light signals
Argo floats descend through the water column and rise periodically, recording temperature, salinity and pressure down to about two thousand meters and transmitting measurements via satellites.
a1-geography-0135: Which stage of the demographic transition model has low birth and death rates, with growth stabilizing at a low level?
Stage four is characterized by low birth and death rates and slow or stable population growth.
a1-geography-0137: What caused the Sunda Strait tsunami in December 2018?
The collapse of a river dam on Java
A deep earthquake off Japan's coast
A tropical cyclone over the Java Sea
An eruption of Anak Krakatau and the collapse of part of its flank
The tsunami followed an eruption of Anak Krakatau and a partial collapse of the volcano's flank, an unconventional volcanic source of a tsunami.
a1-geography-0138: Which sea lies between Papua New Guinea and the archipelago whose capital is Honiara?
The Solomon Sea lies between Papua New Guinea and the Solomon Islands archipelago.
a1-geography-0139: What is the largest lake lying entirely within Switzerland?
Lake Neuchatel is the largest lake whose entire area lies within Switzerland.
a1-geography-0140: On which American mountain were the faces of four presidents carved?
The faces of four American presidents are carved into the rock of Mount Rushmore.
a1-geography-0141: Which mountain holds the statue of Christ overlooking Rio?
The Christ the Redeemer statue stands on the summit of Corcovado above Rio de Janeiro.
a1-geography-0143: Which island is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei?
Borneo is divided between Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei.
a1-geography-0145: What do we call the water droplets that wet grass leaves in the morning?
Dew consists of water droplets that appear on grass and cold surfaces in the morning.
a1-geography-0146: What made the Challenger expedition a turning point in mapping the ocean floor?
Taking systematic depth measurements along a global route
Using satellites to measure the sea surface
Publishing current maps based on port records
Relying on aerial photographs covering coasts
Challenger repeatedly sounded depths on a worldwide voyage, and many of its measurements still contribute to the foundations of seafloor maps.
a1-geography-0147: Which turquoise river flows near the Slovenian town of Bovec?
The Soca flows near Bovec and is famous for its vivid turquoise color.
a1-geography-0148: How is a tornado's intensity estimated when its wind speed cannot be measured directly?
From the pattern of damage it leaves in trees and buildings
Only from the cloud's color before touching the ground
From seawater salinity outside the storm's path
From sunshine hours in the previous month
Tornado winds are difficult to measure directly, so intensity is usually estimated from the damage pattern in buildings and trees.
a1-geography-0149: Why does rising air cool even without losing heat to its surroundings?
Because sunlight does not reach rising air
Because gravity turns it into ice
Because it expands as pressure decreases, using internal energy
In adiabatic cooling, air does work as it expands at lower pressure, causing its temperature to fall.
a1-geography-0152: The Namib Desert lies beside an ocean. Which marine factor supports its coastal aridity?
The Benguela Current cools low-level air and limits convection, making clouds and fog more common than rain.
a1-geography-0153: In inverse distance weighting interpolation, which points usually receive greater weight?
Only the earliest points in time
Points farther from the estimation location
Points always lying to the north
Points closest to the estimation location
Weight decreases as distance increases, so nearby observations have more influence than distant ones.
a1-geography-0154: What ongoing geomorphological role does the Colorado River play within the Grand Canyon?
Eroding the bed and exposing deeper rock layers
Covering the walls with new lava
Raising the mountain by folding the crust
Building a coral reef above the bed
The Colorado continues to erode the canyon bed and transport sediment, exposing deeper rock layers in the walls.
a1-geography-0156: Which Kenyan mountain is Africa's second highest?
Mount Kenya is Africa's second-highest mountain after Kilimanjaro.
a1-geography-0157: Which Australian desert is famous for long parallel red dunes?
The Simpson Desert is famous for long rows of red sand dunes.
a1-geography-0158: Which sea separates Australia from New Zealand?
The Tasman Sea lies between Australia's eastern coast and New Zealand.
a1-geography-0161: What meaning is conveyed by the Maori name Tamaki Makaurau, associated with Auckland?
Auckland Council presents Tamaki Makaurau as a traditional name meaning Tamaki desired by many, referring to the area's resources and location.
a1-geography-0164: Stone Town is the old town on Zanzibar Island.
a1-geography-0165: What three conditions are needed for a periodic hot-water fountain such as a geyser?
Living coral, a wave and a coast
Heat, water and a network of narrow channels
Water heats in a confined system, allowing pressure to build until water and steam erupt periodically.
a1-geography-0166: What is New Zealand's highest mountain?
Aoraki, also known as Mount Cook, is New Zealand's highest peak.
a1-geography-0169: What are England's White Cliffs of Dover made of?
The White Cliffs of Dover consist mainly of chalk.
a1-geography-0170: Who founded Alexandria on the Mediterranean coast in 331 BC?
Alexander the Great founded the city bearing his name in 331 BC, west of the Nile Delta.
a1-geography-0172: Which lake formed behind the Aswan High Dam?
Lake Nasser formed behind the High Dam on the Nile.
a1-geography-0173: Air is heated without adding water vapor. How does its relative humidity usually change?
It stays unchanged regardless of temperature changes
Saturation vapor pressure increases with temperature. With water vapor held constant, relative humidity falls.
a1-geography-0174: Which volcano rises above the French island of Martinique?
The volcanic Mount Pelee rises in northern Martinique.
a1-geography-0175: Which island country east of Madagascar has Port Louis as its capital?
Mauritius is an island country east of Madagascar, with Port Louis as its capital.
a1-geography-0176: What internal component distinguishes a pingo from an ordinary earthen hill?
An ice core that raises the soil cover
A marine cavity filled by tidal water
A petrified tree trunk supporting the hilltop
A lava channel continuously melting the soil
A pingo is an ice-cored hill. It grows when freezing water under pressure pushes the ground cover upward.
a1-geography-0177: Which two bodies of water are connected by the Bosphorus Strait?
The Black Sea and the Sea of Marmara
The Caspian Sea and the Black Sea
The Arabian Sea and the Arabian Gulf
The Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden
The Bosphorus forms the passage through Istanbul between the Black Sea to the north and the Sea of Marmara to the south.
a1-geography-0178: What best describes a seiche in a lake or partly enclosed body of water?
A permanent bottom current circulating around the basin's center
A surface wave moving continuously in one direction
A standing water oscillation rocking between the basin's sides
A regular astronomical tide raising the entire basin equally
Wind or pressure differences may push water to one side of the basin. After the force stops, the water continues to oscillate back and forth as a standing wave.
a1-geography-0179: Which famous river feature lies on the Zambezi at the Zambia-Zimbabwe border?
The Zambezi plunges at Victoria Falls into a gorge on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
a1-geography-0180: Which large bay lies west of France and north of Spain?
The Bay of Biscay extends along western France and northern Spain.
a1-geography-0181: Which Greek island is famous for rocky Navagio Beach?
Navagio Beach, surrounded by cliffs, is on Zakynthos.
a1-geography-0182: If a cell value in a digital terrain model is modified, which property has changed at that location?
The time the satellite passes over the site
The name of the road closest to the cell
The ground surface elevation represented in the cell
A digital elevation model represents terrain with an elevation value in each cell, so modifying that value changes the elevation represented there.
a1-geography-0184: What is Nakhchivan's constitutional status within Azerbaijan?
An independent state with full sovereignty
An administrative area managed by the United Nations
An autonomous republic and an integral part of the state
Azerbaijan's constitution states that Nakhchivan is an autonomous republic and an integral part of the Republic of Azerbaijan.
a1-geography-0185: What is a long steep slope separating two surfaces at different elevations called?
An escarpment separates two terrain levels and may be associated with a fault or differential erosion.
a1-geography-0186: The sequence of ages of the Hawaiian Islands away from the active island indicates which mechanism?
Plate movement over a stationary hotspot
The retreat of an ancient inland lake
The plate moves over a nearly stationary magma source, forming a chain of volcanoes that become older farther from the active site.
a1-geography-0188: Why are successive aerial photographs taken with substantial overlap?
To enable stereoscopic viewing and derive surface form from two perspectives
To prevent any feature from being recorded twice
To eliminate the need for camera calibration
To turn each photograph into a political map
Overlap shows the same area from two different perspectives, creating a stereoscopic view that can be used for measurement and terrain mapping.
a1-geography-0189: What is converting a postal address into coordinates on a map called?
Geocoding finds the spatial location corresponding to a description such as a street address or place name.
a1-geography-0191: Which pair of countries shares an 8,891-kilometer border described by the International Boundary Commission as the longest between two neighboring countries?
The Canadian-American border stretches from the Atlantic to the Pacific, then between Alaska and Canada to the Arctic Ocean, totaling 8,891 kilometers.
a1-geography-0192: Which concept identifies the age below which half the population falls and above which the other half falls?
Median age divides the age distribution into two numerically equal halves.
a1-geography-0193: Which ancient Jordanian city has facades carved into rock?
Petra is famous for its facades and temples carved into rose-colored rock.
a1-geography-0194: Which urban feature forms the open cultural heart of Marrakesh's old city?
Marrakesh's old city centers on Jemaa el-Fna Square, a public space for markets, performances and oral traditions.
a1-geography-0195: How are yardangs usually aligned relative to the winds that carved them?
They always point north regardless of wind changes
They form closed circles around a water source
They are perpendicular to prevailing winds
They extend parallel to prevailing winds
Sand-laden winds carve grooves and ridges in their direction of movement, making yardang axes parallel to prevailing winds.
a1-geography-0196: Which structure divides the Ethiopian Highlands into northwestern and southeastern blocks?
The Main Ethiopian Rift runs diagonally across the country, separating the northwestern and southeastern highlands.
a1-geography-0198: What hydrological exception does South America's Casiquiare River represent?
It seasonally becomes a glacier tongue with no flowing water
It rises from the Amazon and flows into the Pacific Ocean
It ends in a high closed basin within the Andes
It branches from the Orinoco and carries its water to the Rio Negro in the Amazon Basin
The Casiquiare is a natural distributary that takes some Orinoco water to the Rio Negro, thus connecting the Orinoco and Amazon basins.
a1-geography-0199: Which Canadian island is reached by the long Confederation Bridge over the sea?
The Confederation Bridge connects Prince Edward Island with New Brunswick.
a1-geography-0200: Where should the reader look for explanations of map colors and symbols?
The legend links each symbol or color to the meaning intended by the mapmaker.
a1-geography-0201: What is the longest river lying entirely within Italy?
The Po is the longest river flowing entirely within Italian territory.
a1-geography-0202: Which flightless bird symbolizes New Zealand?
The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird that has become a famous national symbol.
a1-geography-0203: Which wide ocean bay lies directly east of India?
The Bay of Bengal lies east of India and is a broad part of the Indian Ocean.
a1-geography-0204: Which tree is tallest in California's coastal forests?
The coast redwood is the tallest tree species and grows near California's coast.
a1-geography-0206: Why can kriging attach statistical uncertainty to an estimated value?
Because it sorts values alphabetically before estimating them
Because it ignores distances between measurements
Because it always copies the most distant point's value
Because it builds a model of spatial variance and correlation
Kriging estimates the structure of spatial variation, then uses it to calculate weights and the uncertainty accompanying the estimate.
a1-geography-0207: In which Australian state is Perth?
Perth is the capital of Western Australia and lies on the Swan River near the Indian Ocean.
a1-geography-0209: What happened to Endurance after it was compressed by Weddell Sea ice?
It became a permanent scientific station on the ice
It was crushed and sank after becoming trapped
It continued sailing to the South Pole
Sea ice trapped the ship for months and then crushed its hull. The expedition abandoned it before it sank in the Weddell Sea.
a1-geography-0213: Which bridge crosses the entrance to San Francisco Bay?
The Golden Gate Bridge crosses the entrance between San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean.
a1-geography-0214: What atmospheric process makes the edges of Kelvin-Helmholtz clouds look like breaking waves?
Freezing rain falling from a stationary cloud
Vertical shear between two layers moving at different speeds
Equal air speed at all elevations
The speed difference creates shear and instability at the boundary between the layers, curling the edge into ripples resembling sea waves.
a1-geography-0215: What is the elevated plain between Andean ranges in Bolivia and Peru that contains Lake Titicaca called?
The Altiplano is a high interior plateau of the central Andes between mountain ranges.
a1-geography-0216: Which Icelandic waterfall's name means golden waterfall?
Gullfoss means golden waterfall in Icelandic.
a1-geography-0217: A road network reveals line endpoints that do not connect at intersections. What do topology rules test here?
The number of spectral bands in the image
The integrity of connections between line features
Topology describes relationships such as line connectivity and polygon adjacency, so a disconnected endpoint appears as a potential connectivity error.
a1-geography-0218: Lake Garda is Italy's largest lake by area.
a1-geography-0219: Which ancient Roman wall stretches across northern England?
Ancient Hadrian's Wall stretches a long distance across northern England.
a1-geography-0220: Circles in Tissot's indicatrix become elongated ellipses in part of a map. What can be inferred?
The complete absence of distortion in that area
Local distortion of shapes or angles
Equal distances from the map's center
The transformation of meridians into contour lines
Changes in the shape of Tissot's indicatrices show the extent of local distortion. Elongation reveals changes in shapes or angles from their original form.
a1-geography-0221: Which polar animal's Baffin Bay population winters in the pack ice of Davis Strait?
The Baffin Bay narwhal population winters in the pack ice of Baffin Bay and Davis Strait, after dispersing in summer through the Canadian Arctic and western Greenland waters.
a1-geography-0222: What drainage type does the Jordan River represent when it ends in the Dead Sea?
Internal drainage that does not reach the ocean
Polar drainage reaching an icy sea
Oceanic drainage ending in the Atlantic
Distributary drainage building a coral island
The Dead Sea is a closed terminal basin. Jordan River water reaches it, but no watercourse flows from it to any ocean.
a1-geography-0223: Which islands between Iceland and Scotland belong to the Kingdom of Denmark?
The Faroe Islands lie in the North Atlantic between Iceland and Scotland and belong to the Kingdom of Denmark.
a1-geography-0224: If rifting in East Africa continues for millions of years, what movement is driving its widening now?
Parts of the continental lithosphere moving apart
River sediment accumulating in a depression
The East African Rift is a zone of continental extension in which blocks of the lithosphere move apart.
a1-geography-0226: Which Moroccan city is famous for its blue alleyways?
Chefchaouen is famous for its alleyways and buildings painted in shades of blue.
a1-geography-0227: Which extensive grassland plain covers central Argentina?
The fertile grassy Pampas extend across a large part of central Argentina.
a1-geography-0228: Which major naval battle took place in the Korea Strait in 1905 between the Japanese and Russian fleets?
The Battle of Tsushima took place on May twenty-seventh and twenty-eighth, 1905, between the Japanese and Russian navies in the Korea Strait.
a1-geography-0230: A coastal city and an inland city lie at the same latitude. Why is the annual temperature range often smaller in the coastal city?
Because gravity is weaker at the shore
Because the sea heats and cools more slowly than land
Because clouds prevent night in coastal cities
Because latitude changes daily near the sea
Water's high heat capacity delays temperature changes, moderating summer heat and winter cold near coasts.
a1-geography-0231: Which elevated plateau covers most of central Spain?
The Meseta Plateau covers a large area of central Spain.
a1-geography-0232: Which Spanish island contains Mount Teide?
Mount Teide rises on Tenerife in the Canary Islands.
a1-geography-0233: How does a satellite navigation receiver determine its position from signals from several satellites?
By calculating distances from signal arrival times
Signal arrival time differences lead to distance estimates, after which the receiver solves for its position and clock.
a1-geography-0234: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, while the Dominican Republic occupies the larger eastern portion.
a1-geography-0237: What economic opportunity may arise when the share of working-age people increases relative to dependents?
A demographic dividend is a potential growth benefit associated with an age structure dominated by working-age people, together with appropriate policies.
a1-geography-0239: Which massive rock in Yosemite has a Spanish name meaning the captain?
El Capitan is a massive rock cliff in Yosemite Valley, and its name means the captain.
a1-geography-0240: Near tall buildings, why might a satellite navigation device's position drift even when the satellites are functioning correctly?
Because reflected signals arrive along longer paths and distort distance estimates
Because all satellites transmit the same signal at the same instant
Because buildings temporarily stop the Earth's rotation
Because the receiver converts elevation into color
Multipath occurs when a signal reflects off walls before reaching the receiver, corrupting travel time and the inferred distance.
a1-geography-0242: Which river forms much of Mexico's border with Texas?
The Rio Grande, known in Mexico as the Rio Bravo, follows a long stretch of the Texas-Mexico border.
a1-geography-0245: Streaks of precipitation extend from a cloud, then disappear in dry air before reaching the ground. What is this phenomenon?
Virga is precipitation falling from a cloud base that evaporates in a dry air layer before reaching the Earth's surface.
a1-geography-0246: Which country contains Pamukkale's white terraces filled with warm water?
Pamukkale's white water-filled terraces are in western Turkey.
a1-geography-0247: By which climatic criterion is Antarctica classified as a desert even though ice covers most of it?
Antarctic snowfall corresponds to a very small annual rainfall amount, so the precipitation criterion places the continent among deserts.
a1-geography-0248: What idea did Humboldt's diagram of plants on Mount Chimborazo highlight?
Mountain plants are confined to the northern slope alone
Forest boundaries always coincide with meridians
Vegetation zones change with elevation and climate
Vegetation remains constant from base to summit
The diagram combined plant locations, temperature and elevation on one cross-section, revealing successive vegetation belts as conditions change with increasing height.
a1-geography-0249: Which Egyptian desert is famous for unusually shaped chalk rocks?
Egypt's White Desert is famous for its bright white chalk rocks in unusual shapes.
a1-geography-0250: Where does the Danube rank in length among Europe's rivers?
The International Commission for the Protection of the Danube describes it as Europe's second-longest river, after the Volga.
a1-geography-0251: Which country has a green cedar in the middle of its flag?
A green cedar appears in the middle of Lebanon's flag.
a1-geography-0252: Which polar sea receives the Lena River after its journey across eastern Siberia?
The Lena builds a vast delta on the coast of the Laptev Sea, one of the Arctic Ocean's seas.
a1-geography-0254: Which flat-topped mountain overlooks Cape Town?
Flat-topped Table Mountain rises above Cape Town.
a1-geography-0255: In which year did the Channel Tunnel between Britain and France open?
The Channel Tunnel officially opened on 6 May 1994, providing a fixed link between Britain and continental Europe.
a1-geography-0257: Which desert covers much of Botswana?
The Kalahari Desert extends across a large area of Botswana.
a1-geography-0259: What is the main function of a world file accompanying a raster map image?
Compressing image colors to reduce its size
Storing feature names in an attribute table
Ordering map layers by creation time
Linking image rows and columns to map coordinates
A world file stores transformation parameters for cell size, rotation and offset, converting row and column positions to map coordinates.
a1-geography-0260: Why are lower-resolution pyramid levels built for a large raster file?
To speed up display when zoomed out
To convert its cells into boundary polygons
To raise its original resolution beyond the source resolution
To remove the image's spatial reference
Pyramids hold progressively lower-resolution copies. When zooming out, the appropriate level is read instead of reading and resampling the entire original file.
a1-geography-0261: Why is a river's name often placed along the curve of its course rather than horizontally far away?
To eliminate the need for a map legend
To indicate that river depth is constant
To connect the label to the line feature it follows
To turn the river into an administrative boundary
Orienting the name parallel to a line feature or along its curve helps the reader associate the label with the correct river.
a1-geography-0262: Which term describes a solitary rocky mountain rising abruptly above a broad erosion plain?
An inselberg is an isolated elevation remaining after the weaker surrounding rocks have eroded.
a1-geography-0263: What is the world's deepest lake, located in Siberia?
Lake Baikal in Siberia is the world's deepest lake.
a1-geography-0264: What is the highest mountain in the Sultanate of Oman?
Jabal Shams is the highest mountain in the Sultanate of Oman.
a1-geography-0267: In urban geography, what is an interconnected chain of neighboring major urban areas called?
A megalopolis is an extensive region where several major urban areas are connected functionally and spatially.
a1-geography-0269: What wetland vegetation dominates the Mahakam Delta by the Makassar Strait?
Extensive wetlands dominated by mangrove ecosystems spread through the Mahakam Delta, alongside farming and aquaculture.
a1-geography-0271: Which French overseas territory has land borders with Brazil and Suriname?
French Guiana lies in South America, bordering Brazil to the east and south and Suriname to the west.
a1-geography-0272: When more people leave a country than enter during a period, what is net migration?
Net migration is arrivals minus departures. If departures are greater, the result is negative.
a1-geography-0273: Which broad waterfall lies near the Swiss town of Schaffhausen?
The Rhine Falls lie near Schaffhausen, where Rhine water plunges over rocks.
a1-geography-0274: How does a census classify student accommodation designed to house large groups?
Collective living quarters are buildings equipped to house large groups or several households. They include student residences when used as usual accommodation.
a1-geography-0276: Why does the Moon appear copper-colored during a total lunar eclipse instead of disappearing entirely?
Because the Moon's surface emits red light from its interior
Because the atmosphere scatters blue light and transmits red light toward Earth's shadow
Because Mars lies between Earth and the Moon during the eclipse
Because the Sun temporarily turns into a cooler star
Some sunlight passes through the edge of the atmosphere. Shorter wavelengths scatter more, while red and orange light reach the Moon inside the shadow.
a1-geography-0278: Which scientific method distinguished Pytheas's description of northern Europe?
Using aerial photography to map coasts
Applying analytical chemistry to mineral samples
Applying mathematical astronomy to latitudes and tides
The surviving fragments about Pytheas reveal that he used mathematical astronomy to investigate latitudes and tides, combining travel with quantitative observation.
a1-geography-0279: Which extensive rainforest mass covers central Africa?
The Congo rainforests cover an extensive area around the Congo River and its tributaries.
a1-geography-0280: What is the angular spacing between cells of the GEBCO global terrain grid in its 2024 release?
The current GEBCO grid provides land elevations and sea depths on a global grid at fifteen-arc-second spacing.
a1-geography-0281: Which set of elements forms the vector data model?
The vector model represents individual locations as points, routes as lines and areas as polygons.
a1-geography-0282: On a warning map, why should red and green alone not be used to distinguish two categories?
Because all maps must be monochrome
Because some readers cannot distinguish the two colors and need an additional symbol or pattern
Because the two colors prevent any text from being printed
Because red and green change the map scale
Accessibility requires that color not be the only means of conveying meaning. It can be supported by a distinguishable shape, pattern or text.
a1-geography-0283: How do the Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Current influence western Europe's climate?
They transport ocean heat toward high latitudes, moderating winter
They prevent every low-pressure system from crossing the Atlantic
They stop ocean evaporation near Europe
They transport polar ice to the Mediterranean in summer
Warm currents transport energy from tropical regions, after which the ocean exchanges some of it with the atmosphere.
a1-geography-0285: A sensor records more numerous and narrower bands than another sensor. What advantage does it gain?
A better ability to distinguish similar spectral characteristics
Increasing the number of bands and narrowing them raises spectral resolution, helping distinguish finer spectral differences between materials.
a1-geography-0286: What geographical idea led Columbus to propose sailing west from Europe?
His belief that the North Pole was near India
His belief that Asia could be reached westward across the Atlantic Ocean
His belief that Africa was an island within the Mediterranean
His belief that the Atlantic Ocean was enclosed by land
Columbus based his plan on reaching Asia by sailing west and estimated a distance shorter than the actual one.
a1-geography-0287: Who led the first expedition confirmed to have reached the South Pole?
Amundsen's team reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911, before Scott's team.
a1-geography-0288: What is the seasonal effect of the Tonle Sap River reversing its flow during the Mekong flood?
The lake level falls to its annual minimum
The lake expands and stores a large share of floodwater
All the water becomes permanent groundwater flow
The lake separates from the river and immediately dries up
The rising Mekong pushes water backward along the Tonle Sap toward the lake, greatly increasing its area and volume before water returns to the river in the dry season.
a1-geography-0289: Which Malabar Coast port did Vasco da Gama reach on his first voyage to India?
Da Gama's fleet reached Calicut on the Malabar Coast in fourteen ninety-eight after crossing the Indian Ocean.
a1-geography-0290: Which mountains separate France from Spain?
The Pyrenees extend along most of the border between France and Spain.
a1-geography-0292: Why are major deserts concentrated near thirty degrees north and south latitude?
Because atmospheric circulation is absent there
Because those latitudes are near the poles
Because dry air descends in the descending branches of Hadley cells
Because saturated air rises in every season
Air that has lost much of its moisture descends in subtropical latitudes, suppressing clouds and precipitation.
a1-geography-0293: On which New Zealand island is Auckland?
Auckland lies in the northern part of New Zealand's North Island.
a1-geography-0294: Which bodies of water does the Qiongzhou Strait connect south of the Leizhou Peninsula?
The Andaman Sea and the Bay of Bengal
The Sulu Sea and the Celebes Sea
The Gulf of Tonkin and the South China Sea
The Yellow Sea and the Sea of Japan
The Qiongzhou Strait lies between Leizhou and Hainan, connecting the Gulf of Tonkin to the South China Sea.
a1-geography-0295: Why might congestion return after widening an urban road temporarily reduced it?
Because every widening eliminates the road network
Because new capacity may attract additional car trips
A shorter travel time may make driving more attractive, generating additional trips that fill the new capacity and restore congestion. This mechanism is known as induced demand.
a1-geography-0297: Which Madagascan animal has a long tail striped in black and white?
The ring-tailed lemur lives naturally in Madagascar and is distinguished by its striped tail.
a1-geography-0298: What does a researcher infer from the orientation of the long axes of a drumlin field?
The depth of the ancient sea at the site
The equator's location at the time of formation
The direction of past ice movement
Ice movement shapes drumlin hills into elongated forms, so their orientation is used to reconstruct former ice flow.
a1-geography-0299: What type of observation distinguishes the Sentinel-2 mission?
Sentinel-2 was designed to image land and vegetation in multiple visible and infrared bands.
a1-geography-0301: Why are coordinate calculations performed on a reference ellipsoid rather than the irregular geoid?
Because the ellipsoid matches Earth's terrain without approximation
Because the geoid is unrelated to mean sea level
Because the ellipsoid follows every local variation in gravity
Because the ellipsoid is a smooth mathematical surface that can be described and calculated
The ellipsoid is a regular shape approximating Earth whose equations allow coordinate calculations, unlike the geoid's irregularities.
a1-geography-0303: Which Jordanian city is the country's only one on the Red Sea?
Aqaba is Jordan's coastal city overlooking the Red Sea.
a1-geography-0304: What is the origin of the name of the cross-border SaarLorLux region?
The names of three mountain ranges
The names Saarland, Lorraine and Luxembourg
The names of three federal capitals
The names of three European rivers
The name combines parts of Saarland, Lorraine and Luxembourg, the historical core of cross-border regional cooperation.
a1-geography-0305: A smooth cloud shaped like stacked discs appears behind a mountain range and remains in place. What type is it?
A lenticular cloud condenses at the crests of standing air waves formed when wind crosses a mountain barrier.
a1-geography-0306: Which two countries have part of their border along the Orange River?
The Orange River forms a section of the international border between Namibia to the north and South Africa to the south before reaching the Atlantic.
a1-geography-0307: Mount Fuji is Japan's highest mountain.
a1-geography-0309: Which American city faces Mexico's Tijuana across the border?
San Diego lies directly north of Tijuana on the American side of the border.
a1-geography-0310: Which combination of characteristics makes navigation through the Istanbul Strait among the world's most difficult?
Permanent freezing and a complete absence of cities and ships
Strong currents, sharp bends and variable weather
A wide straight passage with almost no currents
A dry desert bed unreached by seawater
The Istanbul Strait combines a narrow channel, strong currents, sharp bends and variable weather, passing through a busy city.
a1-geography-0311: What watercourse is traditionally formed by the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates near al-Qurnah?
The Tigris and Euphrates meet in southern Iraq to form the Shatt al-Arab, which flows toward the Gulf.
a1-geography-0312: What is Gagauzia's legal status within Moldova?
An autonomous territorial unit with special status
A territory administered by the United Nations
Moldova's constitution and a 1994 law grant Gagauzia the status of an autonomous territorial unit while it remains an integral part of the state.
a1-geography-0314: What color are the waters of Australia's Lake Hillier famous for?
Australia's Lake Hillier is famous for its pink water.
a1-geography-0316: Which country shares Niagara Falls with the United States?
Niagara Falls lie on the border between Canada and the United States.
a1-geography-0317: What is Scotland's largest lake by area?
Loch Lomond is Scotland's largest lake by surface area.
a1-geography-0318: In Barcelona's planning, what is a grouping of several residential blocks with through traffic kept on the perimeter and traffic calmed on internal streets called?
A superblock reorganizes several neighboring blocks so that through vehicles travel around the perimeter and internal streets are devoted to pedestrians and local use.
a1-geography-0319: Why is a worker's daily journey to another city not considered population migration?
Because it severs ties with the place of residence
Because the person's usual residence does not change
Migration involves changing one's usual residence, whereas a daily commuter returns home after work or study.
a1-geography-0320: Which maritime company did Abel Tasman work for when he led the voyage of sixteen forty-two?
Tasman served the Dutch East India Company and was chosen to lead its expedition to unexplored southern and eastern lands.
a1-geography-0321: What pattern of protection exists on the two sides of the Strait of Bonifacio?
A continental agricultural field far from any islands
A nature reserve in Corsica and a national park in the La Maddalena Archipelago
A shared mining area without coastal protection
A permanent ice reserve around the North Pole
France's Bouches de Bonifacio reserve adjoins Italy's La Maddalena Archipelago National Park across the maritime boundary in the strait.
a1-geography-0322: What does it mean for a satellite image to have a spatial resolution of 10 m?
Each ground cell represents an area of approximately ten meters by ten meters
The location is revisited every ten minutes
Spatial resolution describes the dimensions of the ground patch represented by an image pixel.
a1-geography-0325: What does the intersection of a known latitude and longitude identify on the geographical grid?
A specific location on Earth's surface
A time difference unrelated to place
The area of the continent surrounding the intersection
A constant height above sea level
Geographical coordinates identify a location using a latitude-longitude pair, with its position at their intersection.
a1-geography-0326: Which description defines how an active sensor works?
It emits energy toward the target and measures the returned signal
It calculates population only from a census
An active sensor supplies its own illumination or pulse, then analyzes the return time or intensity.
a1-geography-0329: What is the collective geographical name for Puget Sound, the Strait of Georgia and the Strait of Juan de Fuca?
The official name Salish Sea was adopted as an umbrella term for these three inland waters and their connecting channels between Canada and the United States.
a1-geography-0330: Which measure divides the population by the area of the region where it lives?
Population density expresses the number of people per unit area, often in persons per square kilometer.
a1-geography-0332: What is the most prominent defensive feature defining the appearance of Dubrovnik's old city?
A continuous ring of stone walls
A continuous system of stone walls and towers surrounds Dubrovnik's old city overlooking the Adriatic.
a1-geography-0333: What effect do more roads and impervious surfaces in a neighborhood have on stormwater?
Roads and hard surfaces prevent some water from infiltrating the soil, increasing the volume of surface runoff and the speed at which it reaches channels.
a1-geography-0334: Which African country is known as the Land of a Thousand Hills?
Rwanda is famous for its numerous hills and is therefore known as the Land of a Thousand Hills.
a1-geography-0338: Which change after heavy rain may destabilize an earthen slope?
Immediate evaporation of water from depth
Increased cohesion of all grains without exception
Greater mass weight, higher water pressure and reduced friction
The entire slope turning into igneous rock
Water saturates pores, adds weight to the mass and may reduce shear resistance, increasing susceptibility to sliding.
a1-geography-0339: Why did early explorers call the Ross Ice Shelf the Great Barrier?
Because coastal mountains blocked the view of the pole
Because its high ice wall prevented ships from proceeding south
Because warm currents pushed ships north
Because volcanic rocks closed the sea entrance
Ships encountered an ice shelf wall about thirty meters high and could not continue south, so it was called the Barrier.
a1-geography-0341: What is the most prominent spatial consequence of the Aral Sea's retreat?
Its fragmentation into separate water basins
Its transformation into an open gulf
Its expansion as far as the Black Sea
Its connection with the Caspian Sea
Severe retreat divided the former water body into smaller, separate basins in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
a1-geography-0342: What color is the sand on Iceland's Reynisfjara Beach?
Reynisfjara's sand looks black because it consists of dark volcanic rocks.
a1-geography-0343: What is the main sensor type on Sentinel-1?
The Sentinel-1 mission carries active radar that enables imaging under different lighting and weather conditions.
a1-geography-0345: Which ancient Peruvian city was the capital of the Inca Empire?
Cusco was the heart and capital of the Inca Empire.
a1-geography-0346: What explains time zone boundaries deviating from regular longitudinal divisions?
Making all time zones equal in area
The source states that time zone boundaries are adjusted in practice to accommodate countries' political boundaries, rather than adhering to the theoretical divisions every fifteen degrees.
a1-geography-0347: What is the usual seasonal destination of beluga whales that summer in Nunavik?
They migrate in winter to Hudson Strait, Ungava Bay and the Labrador Sea
They remain in Nunavik's rivers all year
They move upstream to inland lakes to reproduce
They cross into the Pacific Ocean through the Bering Strait
Beluga populations summer in western and eastern Hudson Bay and Ungava Bay, then occur in winter in Hudson Strait, Ungava Bay and the Labrador Sea.
a1-geography-0349: Which pink animal swims in the waters of South America's largest river?
The Amazon river dolphin lives in fresh water and may appear pink.
a1-geography-0350: Which event at the end of the Ice Age turned the plain between Tasmania and mainland Australia into Bass Strait?
Falling sea levels and expansion of the land bridge
A glacier turning into a belt of dunes
Rising sea levels and flooding of the land bridge
A single eruption building a chain of volcanic islands
Global ice melt raised sea levels, flooding the land plain that had connected Tasmania with mainland Australia and forming Bass Strait.
a1-geography-0351: What makes a hot pyroclastic flow more dangerous than an ordinary distant ash cloud?
Cold vapor rising slowly into space
A dense, extremely hot mixture rushing close to the ground
Pure water seeping beneath the soil
Pyroclastic density currents carry hot gas, ash and rocks and descend slopes at great speed.
a1-geography-0353: How can a dust devil usually be distinguished from a tornado?
It starts only from a volcanic crater
It never rotates around an axis
It is a thermal vortex in clear weather, unconnected to a storm
It always forms over a cold ocean
A very hot surface generates a small convective column that may start rotating and lift dust without a storm cloud.
a1-geography-0354: Why does a geostationary satellite appear to remain above approximately the same location?
Because it orbits a pole every hour
Because it descends into the atmosphere during the day
Because its orbital period matches Earth's rotation and it is above the equator
Because it never moves at all
The satellite travels in a circular equatorial orbit with a period matching Earth's rotation, appearing stationary relative to the surface.
a1-geography-0355: Why might a distant desert road look as though it is covered with water?
The Moon reflects daylight off the asphalt
Light bends through air layers with different temperatures and densities
Groundwater seeps onto its surface every noon
The temperature gradient changes the air's refractive index, bending rays so that a displaced image resembling a reflection reaches the eye.
a1-geography-0359: Why was a marine chronometer keeping a known reference time essential for determining a ship's east-west position?
To determine wind speed from wave direction
To convert the time difference from local noon into a longitude difference
To count stars visible from the deck
To convert water temperature into sea depth
Comparing reference time with local solar time reveals a difference in hours that can be converted into an angular difference in longitude.
a1-geography-0360: Which mountains rise south of Marrakesh?
The High Atlas rises south of Marrakesh.
a1-geography-0361: What idea underlay Nansen's polar voyage aboard Fram?
Crossing the desert in steam-powered vehicles
Letting the ship drift with Arctic Ocean ice
Fram was designed to withstand ice pressure and drift with the ice across the polar basin rather than resist it directly.
a1-geography-0363: What is the distinguishing feature of a passive sensor?
It records naturally reflected or emitted energy
It operates without any electromagnetic energy
It sends a pulse and then measures its echo
It measures distance with a ground tape
A passive sensor relies on radiation from the Sun or the observed object rather than illuminating the target itself.
a1-geography-0364: Why does ground over ice-rich permafrost subside when it thaws?
Because frozen water expands and always raises the surface
Because melting ice removes volume and support from within the soil
Because winds press the soil downward from above
Because waves carry sand from the coast to the mountains
When excess ground ice melts, the soil loses some of its volume and strength, causing surface subsidence and thermokarst landforms.
a1-geography-0365: When a thick basalt flow cools, why may it fracture into polygonal columns?
Because sea tides push the lava upward
Because cooling causes lava to contract and fracture
Because winds carve each column from a separate rock
Because ice melts basalt into channels
Lava contracts as it cools, generating cracks perpendicular to the cooling surface and producing columns often hexagonal in cross-section.
a1-geography-0367: Which historic transport system connects Valparaiso's port to its neighborhoods on steep hills?
Funiculars serve Valparaiso's steep slopes, connecting the coastal area with higher neighborhoods.
a1-geography-0368: Which river system builds the vast delta shared by Bangladesh and India?
The Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna converge to build a huge Bengal delta that includes the Sundarbans.
a1-geography-0369: What did the floor of the Taiwan Strait look like when exposed during the ice ages?
Vast grasslands and wetlands crossed by land animals
A recent lava field surrounded by craters
Ice ages lowered sea levels by more than a hundred meters, exposing the floor and turning it into grasslands and marshes crossed by animals from mainland Asia.
a1-geography-0370: Which lake in Djibouti is surrounded by white salt flats?
White salt flats surround the waters of Lake Assal in Djibouti.
a1-geography-0371: What is the huge red rock in central Australia called?
Uluru is a huge red rock mass rising in central Australia.
a1-geography-0373: One satellite images a location every 48 hours and another every sixteen days. Which is better for monitoring a rapidly changing flood?
The satellite that images every sixteen days
Both are equal regardless of revisit time
Temporal frequency cannot be used to monitor floods
The satellite that images every two days
A shorter revisit time improves the temporal ability to observe rapid changes, so two days provides more observations during a flood.
a1-geography-0374: What is the geomorphological relationship between a bajada and alluvial fans?
A bajada forms from adjoining alluvial fans merging
A bajada is a sea trench unrelated to sediment
Fans form from the breakup of a floating glacial bajada
Both are volcanic ridges in the middle of the ocean
Alluvial fans spread at the foot of mountains. When neighboring fans overlap, they form a continuous sediment cover called a bajada.
a1-geography-0376: What coastal feature does the Ob River's mouth form before connecting to the Kara Sea?
A ring delta surrounding a coral island
A long gulf known as the Gulf of Ob
A high waterfall at a continental margin
A closed lake without an outlet
The lower Ob widens into the long Gulf of Ob, which opens northward onto the Kara Sea.
a1-geography-0378: Why are cumulus clouds and rain frequent near the Intertropical Convergence Zone?
Because solar radiation is absent at noon
Because the ocean freezes at the equator
Because dry polar air continually descends
Because winds converge and warm moist air rises
Trade winds converge near the equator, causing moist air to rise, cool and condense.
a1-geography-0379: Who renamed the Cape of Storms the Cape of Good Hope after Bartolomeu Dias's voyage?
Dias named it the Cape of Storms. King Joao II then ordered that maps show the name Cape of Good Hope, expressing hope of reaching India by sea.
a1-geography-0380: Why do volcanic arcs align behind many ocean trenches?
Because plate subduction adds fluids that help melt the mantle
Because ice compresses the ocean until it boils
Because tidal waves build mountains from sand
Because trade winds pierce the crust
The descending plate releases water and volatile substances that lower the melting temperature of mantle rocks, allowing magma to rise.
a1-geography-0381: In which city do the White Nile and Blue Nile meet?
The White Nile meets the Blue Nile in Khartoum.
a1-geography-0383: Moist winds blow toward a mountain. Where does orographic rainfall usually begin?
On the leeward side before the air reaches the summit
Above the shaded slope after descending air warms
On the ocean floor because salinity increases
On the windward slope after rising air cools
The barrier forces air to rise, expand and cool until it reaches saturation and its water vapor condenses.
a1-geography-0385: Why does a tributary glacial valley remain above the floor of the main valley?
The main glacier carved a deeper floor
Wind filled the tributary valley floor
Sediments raised the tributary valley floor
Tides lowered the main valley floor

The larger glacier in the main valley could erode more effectively than the tributary glacier, deepening its floor further. After the glaciers retreated, the tributary valley remained hanging above it.
a1-geography-0387: When classifying values on a choropleth map, what distinguishes the quantile method?
Each class contains approximately the same number of features
Class boundaries fall at the largest natural gaps
Classes are built around the mean and standard deviation
Each class covers a numerical interval of equal width
The method sorts values and distributes features among classes so that each class contains a similar number of features, rather than making the numerical intervals equally wide.
a1-geography-0389: If water flows from central Siberia along the Yenisei, in which general direction does it travel toward its mouth?
The Yenisei runs north from the Asian interior and empties into the Kara Sea through a broad estuary.
a1-geography-0391: Where is information such as a road's name and type usually stored alongside its spatial shape?
Each feature is linked to a record in an attribute table containing its non-geometric descriptions.
a1-geography-0392: What gives a shield volcano gently sloping sides over a broad area?
Low-viscosity basaltic lava that spreads far
Ice masses accumulating beneath the cone
Rivers carving its sides into vertical channels
Highly viscous lava confined near the vent
Low-viscosity basaltic lava spreads great distances before solidifying, building broad, gently sloping layers.
a1-geography-0393: Why is a belt near the equator known as the doldrums?
Water vapor is absent all year
Horizontal winds are weak and variable near the convergence zone
It has the world's highest pressure
Air rises strongly in the equatorial convergence zone, while its horizontal movement may be weak and variable.
a1-geography-0394: In which general direction do polar easterlies blow at Earth's surface?
From east to west and from the pole toward lower latitudes
From west to east and from the equator toward the pole
Vertically from sea level into space
From south to north in both hemispheres
Air flows outward from polar high-pressure areas and is deflected by Earth's rotation, acquiring an easterly component.
a1-geography-0395: What electrical separation precedes a flash of lightning within a storm?
All water vapor turns into salt
Charge becomes equal everywhere with no electric field
Opposite charges accumulate in different parts of a cloud or between the cloud and the ground
Collisions between ice particles separate charges. When the electric field becomes strong enough, an electrical discharge occurs.
a1-geography-0396: What is the traditional small sailing boat on the Nile called?
A felucca is a traditional small sailing boat used on the Nile.
a1-geography-0397: Why must a reference epoch accompany high-precision geodetic coordinates?
The epoch converts lines of longitude into contours
Crustal movement changes point coordinates over time
It determines the color of the point symbol on a map
Reference-frame stations move with tectonic plates and crustal deformation, so the time of the coordinates must be specified or the coordinates transformed to another epoch.
a1-geography-0398: Which regional authority coordinates planning for the larger region surrounding the capital of Maharashtra?
The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority prepares regional plans and coordinates infrastructure projects across the metropolitan region.
a1-geography-0009: Which small landlocked republic lies within Italy on Mount Titano?
San Marino is a landlocked state surrounded by Italian regions, with its historic center on Mount Titano.
a1-geography-0210: Which small country lies between France and Spain?
Andorra is a small independent country with land borders with France and Spain.
a1-geography-0010: Which cold landmass is surrounded by the Southern Ocean?
The waters of the Southern Ocean surround Antarctica.
a1-geography-0016: On which continent is Singapore, a city and a country?
a1-geography-0044: On which continent are the Atlas Mountains?
The Atlas Mountains extend across northwestern Africa.
a1-geography-0357: On which continent are the Rocky Mountains?
The Rocky Mountains extend through western North America.
geo-0023: On which continent is the South Pole?
The geographic South Pole lies within Antarctica.
a1-geography-0011: On the shores of which Great Lake does Chicago stand?
Chicago lies on the southwestern shore of Lake Michigan.
a1-geography-0171: In which Canadian lake is Manitoulin Island?
Manitoulin Island lies in the Canadian part of Lake Huron.
a1-geography-0017: Which part of the United Kingdom faces France across the Strait of Dover?
The Strait of Dover separates the French coast from the English coast.
a1-geography-0081: Which part of the island west of Great Britain belongs to the United Kingdom today?
Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom.
a1-geography-0366: Which part of Britain has a red dragon on its flag?
A large red dragon appears on the flag of Wales.
a1-geography-0024: In which Asian country is Kyoto, a city with ancient temples?
Kyoto is an ancient Japanese city that was the country's capital for a long period.
a1-geography-0089: Which country does the Wakhan Corridor touch at its eastern end?
The narrow eastern end of the Wakhan Corridor reaches the Chinese border.
flag-0001: Which country's official flag is neither rectangular nor square?
Nepal's flag consists of two joined triangular shapes and is the only national flag that is not quadrilateral.
a1-geography-0028: Which Danish city faces Malmo across the strait?
Copenhagen faces the Swedish city of Malmo across the Oresund Strait.
cap-0017: What is the capital of Norway?
Oslo is Norway's capital, while Stockholm, Copenhagen and Helsinki are the capitals of Sweden, Denmark and Finland respectively.
a1-geography-0032: Which desert extends across India and Pakistan?
The Thar Desert extends across northwestern India and eastern Pakistan.
a1-geography-0323: What is the name of the vast desert between China and Mongolia?
The Gobi Desert extends across parts of northern China and southern Mongolia.

gemini-hadith-003: Complete the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, warning against bad friends: «الرَّجُلُ عَلَى دِينِ ...، فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَحَدُكُمْ مَنْ يُخَالِلُ» [A man follows the religion (i.e. ways and manners) of ... . gemini-hadith-b2-001: What is a hadith (Prophetic report) narrated by a weak narrator in contradiction to trustworthy narrators called?

gemini-hadith-b2-002: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «لا ضَرَرَ ولا ...» [There should be no harm or ...]

gemini-hadith-b2-011: How many hadith (Prophetic reports) does Al-Arba'in an-Nawawiyyah actually contain?

gemini-hadith-b2-012: What is a hadith (Prophetic report) with one or more narrators omitted from the beginning of its chain called?

gemini-hadith-b2-014: Complete the Prophet's guidance to avoid doubtful matters: (دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا ...) [Leave what you doubt for what you do not ...]

gemini-hadith-b2-017: Which Companion served the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) for 10 years and narrated much about his life?

gemini-hadith-b2-019: Many confuse takhrij (source tracing), sharh (commentary), and tahqiq (critical editing). How do hadith scholars define takhrij?
Identifying a report's sources and stating its grading

Takhrij (source tracing) attributes a hadith (Prophetic report) to the original sources that transmitted it with their chains, stating its grading as authentic or weak. Explaining meanings is sharh (commentary); establishing the text and preparing it for publication is tahqiq (critical editing).
gemini-hadith-b2-020: Sunan Abi Dawud primarily collected hadith (Prophetic reports) concerning:
In his Sunan, he restricted himself to, or focused on, reports of legal rulings from which jurists derive rulings.
gemini-hadith-b3-003: When a hadith (Prophetic report) is described as 'narrated by the two shaykhs' or muttafaq alayh (agreed upon), who are the two shaykhs?
Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrating a report gives it the highest degree of authenticity.
gemini-hadith-b3-007: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: (لا يدخل الجنة من كان في قلبه مثقال ذرة من...) [Anyone has an atom's weight of ... in his heart will not enter Paradise.]
Majesty belongs to Allah. Arrogance, meaning rejecting the truth and looking down on people, prevents initial entry into Paradise.
gemini-hadith-b3-008: Complete the hadith (Prophetic report): (المؤمن القوي خير وأحب إلى الله من المؤمن الـ...) [The strong believer is better and dearer to Allah than the ... believer.]
Weak, and there is good in both
Strength here includes strength of faith, body, and resolve, while affirming the basic goodness of the weak believer because of his faith.
gemini-hadith-b3-010: What is a mursal hadith (a Successor-attributed Prophetic report)?
One narrated by only one Companion
One the Prophet sent in a letter to kings
One a Successor attributes directly to the Prophet, omitting the intermediary Companion
One narrated through more than one chain
A mursal report is a type of weak hadith (Prophetic report) because the omitted intermediary between the Successor and the Prophet is unknown.
gemini-hadith-b3-011: In which book did Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj collect the hadith (Prophetic reports) he judged authentic?
Sahih Muslim is the second of the two Sahih collections. It is distinguished by gathering the transmission routes of a single report in one place.
gemini-hadith-b3-013: He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: (البر حسن الخلق، والإثم ما حاك في صدرك و...) [Righteousness is good morals, and sinfulness is what your heart is not at ease with, and ...]
You hate that people know about it
You hide it from your family
You learn it from someone else
This is a precise Prophetic criterion for recognizing sin through sound natural disposition and a Muslim's shame at its exposure.
gemini-hadith-b3-017: He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: (البخيل من ذُكرت عنده فلم...) [The miser is the one in whose presence I am mentioned, but he does not ...]
Invoking blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) when he is mentioned is a sign of love and spiritual generosity. Neglecting it is miserliness.
gemini-hadith-b3-018: Complete the hadith (Prophetic report): (كل أمتي معافى إلا...) [All of my Ummah may be forgiven except ...]
A person who publicizes sin disobeys Allah at night and Allah conceals it, then exposes himself in the morning and boasts of his sin.
gemini-hadith-b3-020: A shadh hadith (an anomalous Prophetic report) is:
A report narrated by someone with very poor memory
What a trustworthy narrator transmits in contradiction to someone more trustworthy
A report with two consecutive narrators omitted
A report with no chain at all
A shadh report is rejected because it contradicts firmly reliable expert narrators. Its narrator's unique transmission contradicting them is not accepted.
gemini2-hadith-002: Complete the Prophet's hadith (Prophetic report): (إنما الأعمال بـ...) [Verily, the reward of deeds depends on ...]

إنما الأعمال بالنيات، وإنما لكل امرئ ما نوى. [Verily, the reward of deeds depends on intentions, and each person will be rewarded according to what he intended.] This is the basis for the acceptance of deeds.
gemini2-hadith-004: A famous hadith (Prophetic report) in which Jibril questioned the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to teach the Companions their religion is called:
He asked him about the pillars of Islam, iman (faith), and ihsan (excellence in worship). It is known as Hadith Jibril.
gemini2-hadith-005: What is the precise definition of a mutawatir hadith (a mass-transmitted Prophetic report) in hadith terminology?
What one person narrated directly from the Prophet
What a large group narrated whose agreement on a lie is impossible
Only what Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated
What has a connected chain and trustworthy narrators
A mutawatir report yields certain knowledge because its narrators are so numerous at every generation that their agreement on a lie is impossible.
gemini2-hadith-006: Which discipline distinguishes accepted hadith (Prophetic reports) from rejected ones?
Mustalah al-hadith (hadith terminology) is the discipline of rules for assessing chains and texts as regards acceptance or rejection.
gemini2-hadith-007: A man asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) for advice. He repeatedly said: (لا...) [Do not ...]
لا تغضب [Do not get angry.] He repeated it several times because anger brings together all evil.
gemini2-hadith-008: What does matn (text) mean in the terminology of hadith scholars?
The chain of narrators conveying the report
The wording of the report at which the chain ends
The name of the book that traced the report's sources
The grading of a report as authentic or weak
Sanad (chain) is the sequence of narrators; matn (text) is the wording of the report at which that sequence ends.
gemini2-hadith-009: What is a hadith qudsi (a sacred report)?
What the Companions said long ago
What the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) narrates from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic
What appears only in the Qur'an

A hadith qudsi (sacred report) is what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) narrates from his Lord. According to the well-known view, its meaning is from Allah and its wording from the Prophet. Its recitation is not an act of worship as the Qur'an's is.
gemini2-hadith-010: In hadith studies, the sequence of narrators who transmitted a report from one another is called:
Jarh wa ta'dil (narrator criticism and accreditation)
Sanad (chain) is the route or sequence of men leading to the matn (text).
gemini2-hadith-016: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) listed five rights a Muslim owes another Muslim. The first concerns meeting someone. What is it?

He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «حقُّ المسلمِ على المسلمِ خمسٌ: ردُّ السلام، وعيادةُ المريض، واتّباعُ الجنائز، وإجابةُ الدعوة، وتشميتُ العاطس» [A Muslim owes another Muslim five rights: returning the greeting of peace, visiting the sick, following the funeral processions, accepting invitations, and saying tashmīt (yarhamuk Allah) (may Allah show mercy to you) to the person who sneezes.]
gemini2-hadith-017: Complete the hadith (Prophetic report): (تبسمك في وجه أخيك لك...) [Your smiling at your brother's face is ... for you.]
This report shows the merit of cheerfulness and good character.
gemini2-hadith-018: من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا... [Part of a person's excellence in Islam is his leaving what does not ...]
It means leaving unnecessary matters and interference in other people's affairs that do not concern one.
gemini2-hadith-020: A hadith (Prophetic report) meeting the conditions of authenticity, except that one narrator's precision of memory is slightly lower, is called:
A hasan (good) report meets the conditions of a sahih (authentic) report, except that its narrator's precision is lower.
hadith-0002: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): المسلم من سلم المسلمون من... [A Muslim is the one from whose ... Muslims are safe.]
Part of a person's complete Islam is refraining from harming others through words and actions.
hadith-0003: Which noble Companion narrated the most hadith (Prophetic reports)?
Abdullah ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both)
Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both)
Abu Hurayrah stayed close to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), memorizing many reports.
hadith-0005: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «الدِّينُ ...» [Religion is ...], قيل: لمن؟ قال: لله ولكتابه ولرسوله ولأئمة المسلمين وعامتهم. [We said: 'To whom?' He said: 'To Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the Muslim leaders and their common folk.']
The hadith (Prophetic report) summarizes that the foundation and support of religion rest on sincerity, truthfulness, and faithfulness.
hadith-0006: Which famous hadith (Prophetic report) did Imam al-Bukhari place at the beginning of his Sahih?
بني الإسلام على خمس [Islam is built on five]
من حسن إسلام المرء تركه ما لا يعنيه [Part of a person's excellence in Islam is his leaving what does not concern him.]
إنما الأعمال بالنيات [Verily, the reward of deeds depends on intentions]
لا يؤمن أحدكم حتى يحب لأخيه ما يحب لنفسه [None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.]
Al-Bukhari made it the first report in his Sahih as a constant reminder of the importance of ikhlas (sincerity) in every deed.
hadith-0007: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «مَنْ غَشَّنَا فَلَيْسَ...» [Whoever cheats us is not ...]?
Cheating conflicts with Muslim character, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) disavowed its perpetrator.
hadith-0008: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) described three signs of a hypocrite, saying: «إِذَا حَدَّثَ كَذَبَ، وَإِذَا وَعَدَ ...، وَإِذَا اؤْتُمِنَ خَانَ» [When he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he ...; and when entrusted, he betrays the trust.]
Breaking promises is a trait of hypocrisy in conduct against which Islam warned.
hadith-0009: Complete the hadith (Prophetic report) that is a major foundation for rejecting bid'ah (religious innovation): «مَنْ أَحْدَثَ فِي أَمْرِنَا هَذَا مَا لَيْسَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ...» [Whoever introduces something into this matter of ours that is not part of it will have it ...]?
This report is a criterion for accepting deeds: every act of worship that does not accord with the Shariah (Islamic law) is rejected.
hadith-0010: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «لَا يَدْخُلُ الجَنَّةَ قَاطِعُ...» [The one who severs the ties of ... will not enter Paradise.]
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) warned against severing ties with relatives and kin, making it one of the grave sins that prevent entry into Paradise.
hadith-0011: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «مَنْ سَلَكَ طَرِيقًا يَلْتَمِسُ فِيهِ عِلْمًا، سَهَّلَ اللَّهُ لَهُ بِهِ طَرِيقًا إِلَى...» [Whoever treads a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to ...]
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) explained that seeking beneficial religious knowledge is among the greatest means of attaining Allah's pleasure and entering Paradise.
hadith-0012: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) held up his index and middle fingers, leaving a small gap, and said: «أَنَا وَكَافِلُ ... فِي الْجَنَّةِ هَكَذَا» [I and the one who cares for ... will be like this in Paradise.] Who is meant?
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) explained the great status of an orphan's guardian and his very close proximity to him in Paradise.
hadith-0013: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «لَيْسَ مِنَّا مَنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْ صَغِيرَنَا، وَيَعْرِفْ شَرَفَ...» [He does not belong to us who does not show mercy to our young and honor our ...]
Islam taught us to respect and honor the elderly and show mercy to the young.
hadith-0014: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «لَا تَحَاسَدُوا، وَلَا تَنَاجَشُوا، وَلَا تَبَاغَضُوا، وَلَا تَدَابَرُوا... وَكُونُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ...» [Do not envy one another, do not raise prices by overbidding against one another, do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another ... and be, O slaves of Allah, our ...]
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) prohibited diseases of the heart and actions that divide society, and commanded Islamic brotherhood.
hadith-0015: What great reward did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) announce for someone who invokes blessings upon him once?
Allah builds him a house in Paradise
Allah bestows blessings upon him ten times
He is freed from the Fire

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ وَاحِدَةً، صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَشْرًا» [Whoever invokes blessings upon me once, Allah will bestow blessings upon him ten times.]
hadith-0016: Complete the Prophet's hadith (Prophetic report) encouraging work and refraining from begging: «الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ...» [The upper hand is better than the ... hand.]
The upper hand spends, gives, and offers charity; the lower hand begs and receives.
hadith-0017: To what did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) liken believers' solidarity and cooperation when he said: «الْمُؤْمِنُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِ كَالْـ... يَشُدُّ بَعْضُهُ بَعْضًا» [A believer to another believer is like a ... whose parts support one another.]?
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) interlaced his fingers to show how a believer supports his brother like a strong, firmly joined building.
hadith-0018: In the hadith (Prophetic report) about «سبعة يظلهم الله في ظله» [There are seven whom Allah Almighty will shade in His Shade], which young man did the Prophet mention?
A young man who sought knowledge early
A young man who grew up in the worship of his Lord
A young man who fought in Allah's cause
A young man who memorized the Qur'an

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) singled out the young man who devoted the energy and vigor of his youth to obeying Allah for shelter under the shade of the Throne of Ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) on the Day of Resurrection.
hadith-0019: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «الْمُسْلِمُ أَخُو الْمُسْلِمِ لَا يَظْلِمُهُ وَلَا...» [A Muslim is a Muslim's brother: he does not wrong him or ...]
His saying ولا يسلمه [or abandon him] means not deserting him or leaving him in the hands of someone who harms or oppresses him.
hadith-0020: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «لَا يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لِأَخِيهِ...» [None of you believes until he loves for his brother ...]
What he loves for his friend
What he gives him in charity
This report is a major foundation for encouraging selflessness and loving good for others as one loves it for oneself.
hadith-0021: Complete the Prophet's saying (peace and blessings be upon him): «مَنْ سَنَّ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ سُنَّةً حَسَنَةً، فَلَهُ...» [Whosoever introduces a good practice in Islam, there is for him ...]
The pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic
Its reward and the reward of those who act upon it
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) explained that whoever initiates a good deed and is followed by others receives rewards like theirs without their rewards being diminished at all.
a5-hadith-0311: When Urwah's mursal (Successor-attributed) route, which omits the Companion, conflicts with the route connected through Aishah, what is the sound critical basis for preferring one narration?
The order of the book's chapters
Narrated by Muslim (205) and at-Tirmidhi (2310). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0320: What do hadith critics call a hidden, damaging defect that affects authenticity and appears only after collecting and comparing transmission routes?
Narrated by Muslim (274) and at-Tirmidhi (100). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0328: If a gharib (single-route) report has an authentic chain but its narrators do not reach the number required for tawatur (mass transmission), to which basic numerical class does it belong?
Narrated by Muslim (770) and at-Tirmidhi (3420). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0329: When distinguishing mashhur (well-known) in hadith scholars' technical usage from general popularity, what is the main factor in a scholar's final description of a report?
The number of its transmission routes
Narrated by Muslim (405) and at-Tirmidhi (3220). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0334: If every narrator demonstrably heard from the narrator above him in a report ending with Anas without attribution to the Prophet, what precisely describes its chain?
a5-hadith-0336: When a chain has several equally strong forms that cannot be reconciled or ranked, what do hadith critics call it?
Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (142) and Muslim (375); also by at-Tirmidhi (5). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0305: When a Companion explicitly reports a saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), which form of marfu' (Prophet-attributed) report is it?
Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (4860) and Muslim (1647); also by at-Tirmidhi (1545). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0306: Aishah's report describing an action she witnessed in the Prophet's prayer belongs to which technical form of marfu' (Prophet-attributed) report?
Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (6310) and Muslim (736); also by Abu Dawud (1335). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0307: A Companion reports an act done during the Prophet's lifetime that came to his knowledge and he did not disapprove of. Which form of marfu' (Prophet-attributed) report is this?
a5-hadith-0308: If an isnad (chain of narrators) ends with Ibn Umar's words without attributing them to the Prophet, how do hadith scholars describe the report?
Narrated by Abu Dawud (2230). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0310: Ibn Abbas narrating a Prophetic event from before his age of discernment, without naming the intermediary, represents which form of irsal (omitting a narrator)?
a5-hadith-0312: Abu Qilabah lived at the same time as Abu Tha'labah, but at-Tirmidhi states he did not hear from him. Which hidden type of interruption does this reveal?
a5-hadith-0314: A connected chain, upright and precise narrators, and freedom from shudhudh (contradicting a more reliable narrator) and hidden defects give a report which accepted grade through its own strength?
a5-hadith-0316: A hasan li-dhatihi report (good in itself, with slightly lower narrator precision) gains multiple comparable transmission routes. To which higher grade does it rise?
Narrated by Muslim (728) and at-Tirmidhi (415). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0317: Slight weakness not arising from lying is strengthened by several independent supporting reports. What accepted grade results?
a5-hadith-0318: When two trustworthy narrators differ over one chain, what do early critics call the narration agreeing with the more accurate narrator, as opposed to the shadh (anomalous) narration?
Narrated by al-Bukhari (6052) and at-Tirmidhi (70). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0319: When a munkar route (a weak narrator's contradictory transmission) differs from trustworthy narrators' reports, what is their opposing narration called?
a5-hadith-0321: Multiple transmission routes for Abu Musa's report, with the Companion at the origin remaining the same, are generally called what in i'tibar (corroborative examination)?
Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (3674) and Muslim (2403); also by at-Tirmidhi (3710). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0324: A report conveying the meaning of wiping over khuffs (leather socks), narrated from Ali rather than Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, is called what in relation to Khuzaymah's chain?
a5-hadith-0333: What is the technical term for collecting routes of one text through different narrators and Companions to find corroborations and supporting reports?
a5-hadith-0322: Ibn Abi Adi agreeing with Mu'adh in narrating a supplication report from their shared teacher Hisham is which precise type of mutaba'ah (corroboration)?
Shahid lafzi (supporting report with matching wording)
Agreed upon: narrated by al-Bukhari (6346) and Muslim (2730); also by at-Tirmidhi (3435). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0323: Sufyan's route joins Muhammad ibn Ja'far's route above the latter's teacher Shu'bah in the chain. Which specific type of mutaba'ah (corroboration) is this?
Shahid ma'nawi (supporting report with matching meaning)
Narrated by Muslim (2726) and at-Tirmidhi (3555). Grade: sahih (authentic).
a5-hadith-0326: A large group transmitting the Prophet's warning against lying in identical words represents which form of tawatur (mass transmission precluding collusion)?
Narrated by Ibn Majah (30). Grade: sahih (authentic).
