a5-hadith-0327: Many incidents of raising the hands in du'a (supplication), narrated with different wording but sharing one meaning, establish which technical type of tawatur (mass transmission precluding collusion)?
gemini-rashidun-002: Which wronged Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph was martyred while reading the Qur'an in his home, patiently seeking Allah's reward?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Rebels besieged Uthman's home and killed him while he recited verses of Allah's Book. To avoid strife, he did not order his guards to fight them.
rashid-0001: Who was the first Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph to assume the caliphate after the Prophet's death?
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
The Muslim community agreed to pledge allegiance first to as-Siddiq because of his merit and companionship.
rashid-0002: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph was called Dhu an-Nurayn because he married two daughters of the Prophet in succession?
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman married Ruqayyah. After her death, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) married Umm Kulthum to him.
rashid-0003: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph was called Al-Faruq because Allah distinguished truth from falsehood through him?
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar was called Al-Faruq for his firmness in upholding truth and his strict justice.
rashid-0004: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph ordered the first collection of the Noble Qur'an into one mushaf (written volume) after the Battle of al-Yamamah?
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr ordered the Qur'an collected on sheets out of concern for its preservation after many reciters were killed in the Wars of Apostasy.
rashid-0005: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph ordered uniform copies of the Qur'an made and sent to the provinces to prevent disagreement?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
The Qur'an was first collected under Abu Bakr, but Uthman copied it to unify readings after the conquests expanded.
rashid-0006: Which Companion became the fourth Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Imam Ali assumed the caliphate after Uthman ibn Affan's martyrdom and is the fourth Rashidun caliph.
rashid-0007: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph personally traveled to Bayt al-Maqdis to receive its keys and granted its people a document of safe conduct?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab peacefully received Jerusalem's keys and wrote Al-Uhdah al-Umariyyah, which guaranteed its people's freedom.
rashid-0010: Which caliph bought the well of Rumah in Madinah and made it a waqf (endowment) so Muslims could drink from it free of charge?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) encouraged purchasing the well. Uthman ibn Affan bought it with his own money and made his bucket equal to other Muslims' buckets in access to it.
rashid-0012: Who was the second caliph, assuming leadership of the Muslims after Abu Bakr as-Siddiq's death?
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq designated Umar ibn al-Khattab to succeed him, making him the second Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph.
rashid-0013: Which caliph firmly confronted those withholding zakah (obligatory alms) and apostates after the Prophet's death, preserving Islam's unity?
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Bakr insisted on fighting apostates and those withholding zakah (obligatory alms), saying: 'By Allah, I will fight anyone who separates prayer from zakah.'
rashid-0014: During which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph's reign was the first Islamic naval fleet established?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Mu'awiyah established the fleet with Uthman's permission, so it was founded during Caliph Uthman ibn Affan's reign.
rashid-0018: Who was the third Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph, succeeding Umar ibn al-Khattab?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan is the third Rashidun caliph and assumed the caliphate after Al-Faruq's martyrdom.
rashid-0019: Which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph consulted the Companions and adopted the Prophet's Hijrah (migration) as the starting point of the Islamic calendar?
Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
Uthman ibn Affan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him)
Umar gathered the Companions, and they decided to begin dating from the Hijrah (migration), because it distinguished truth from falsehood.
gemini2-rashidun-003: Which decisive battle opened Iraq to the Muslims during Umar's reign?
The Muslims, led by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, defeated Rustam's army. The conquest of Al-Mada'in, the Persian capital, followed.
gemini-rashidun-005: Which member of the Khawarij assassinated Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib as he went out for Fajr (dawn prayer) in Kufah?
Ibn Muljam treacherously stabbed Imam Ali in Kufah under an agreement with the renegade Khawarij.
rashid-0011: Which Zoroastrian slave assassinated Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab while he led the Muslims in Fajr (dawn prayer)?
Abu Lu'lu'ah al-Majusi treacherously stabbed Al-Faruq Umar with a poisoned dagger during Fajr (dawn prayer).
gemini-rashidun-b2-014: During which Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph's reign were Egypt conquered and the Fortress of Babylon captured?
Umar ibn al-Khattab sent reinforcements to Amr ibn al-As to complete Egypt's conquest.
gemini2-rashidun-007: About which caliph did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say that the devil flees, taking a different path from his?
As stated in the hadith (Prophetic report): ما لقيك الشيطان سالكا فجا إلا سلك فجا غير فجك. [whenever the devil sees you walking on a path, he follows a path other than yours.]
gemini-rashidun-b2-016: Which of the four Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliphs ruled the longest?
Uthman ibn Affan ruled for nearly 12 years.
gemini-rashidun-b3-004: Who relinquished the caliphate to spare Muslim lives, leading that year to be called Am al-Jama'ah?

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said of him: «إنّ ابني هذا سيّد، ولعلّ اللهَ أن يُصلحَ به بين فئتينِ عظيمتينِ من المسلمين» [This son of mine is a leader, and perhaps Allah will reconcile through him two great groups of Muslims.] That was in 41 AH.
gemini-rashidun-b3-008: Which commander was martyred while leading the Muslims at the Battle of Nahavand?
Nahavand took place in 21 AH and was called Fath al-Futuh. An-Nu'man was martyred; Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman took the banner, and victory was achieved.
gemini2-rashidun-009: Who led the great Battle of al-Qadisiyyah, in which the Muslims defeated the Persians?
Umar ibn al-Khattab sent him to lead the army at Al-Qadisiyyah, where he achieved victory.
gemini-rashidun-b3-013: Which Companion did Abu Bakr send to collect and trace the Qur'an from written fragments and people's memories into a single mushaf (written volume)?
Zayd ibn Thabit was a scribe of revelation: young, meticulous, and a memorizer of the Qur'an. He accomplished the task excellently.
gemini-rashidun-b4-003: Which Companion did Umar ibn al-Khattab send to Kufah to teach its people fiqh (religious understanding) and the Qur'an?
Umar wrote to the people of Kufah: 'I have sent you Ammar as governor and Ibn Mas'ud as teacher and adviser. I have preferred you over myself by sending him.'
gemini-rashidun-001: Where were Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliphs Abu Bakr as-Siddiq and Umar ibn al-Khattab buried after their deaths?
Beside the Prophet in his chamber in Madinah
Before their deaths, they sought Lady Aishah's permission to be buried beside their companion, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and it was granted.
gemini-rashidun-b2-001: How long was Abu Bakr as-Siddiq's caliphate?
About two years and three months
His caliphate was brief, but during it he consolidated the Islamic state's foundations and defeated the apostates.
gemini-rashidun-b2-004: What nickname did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) use for Ali ibn Abi Talib when he found him asleep in the mosque with dust on him?
He gently said to him: قم أبا تراب [Get up, Abu Turab.] It was Ali's favorite nickname.
gemini-rashidun-b2-018: Which daughter of the Prophet married Imam Ali and bore him Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn?
She bore him Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them all.
gemini-rashidun-b3-005: How was the temporary dispute between the Ansar (Helpers) and Muhajirun (Emigrants) resolved at Saqifat Bani Sa'idah after the Prophet's death?
By direct election by all Madinah's people
Through speeches by Abu Bakr and Umar, followed by the Ansar's pledge
By dividing the state in two
Consultation and frank discussion at the Saqifah settled the matter. The Ansar (Helpers) yielded out of concern for Muslim unity.
gemini-rashidun-b3-007: Which diwan (bureau) did Umar ibn al-Khattab establish to register soldiers' names and stipends?
Umar established the registers in 20 AH and arranged stipends according to early acceptance of Islam and kinship with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).
gemini-rashidun-b3-010: The six-member shura (consultative council) Umar ibn al-Khattab appointed before his death to select the caliph consisted of:
Six senior Companions with whom the Prophet was pleased when he died
Only six commanders of conquering armies
They were Uthman, Ali, Talhah, Az-Zubayr, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, to choose a caliph from among themselves.
gemini-rashidun-b3-011: What was the year of severe drought and famine during Umar ibn al-Khattab's reign called?
It was so called because the ground darkened from lack of rain until it resembled ash. Umar abstained from ghee and meat until people had abundance again.
gemini-rashidun-b3-017: Which false claimant to prophethood was killed at the Battle of al-Yamamah during Abu Bakr as-Siddiq's reign?
He claimed prophethood among Banu Hanifah and caused one of the fiercest battles of the Wars of Apostasy before he was killed.
gemini2-rashidun-001: In which major battle of the Wars of Apostasy was Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab killed?
It took place at Al-Yamamah in 12 AH under Khalid ibn al-Walid. Many Qur'an memorizers were martyred there, prompting its compilation into a mushaf (written volume).
gemini2-rashidun-002: How many years did Umar ibn al-Khattab's caliphate last?
He assumed the caliphate in 13 AH and was martyred in 23 AH, so it lasted about ten and a half years.
gemini2-rashidun-004: Which son of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq brought him and the Prophet news of Quraysh while they were in the cave?
Abdullah spent the night with them, then left before dawn to be among Quraysh in the morning as if he had slept there. He remembered any plot he heard against them and brought them the news.
gemini2-rashidun-006: What title was given to Abu Bakr for affirming the Prophet's account of Al-Isra' wa al-Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension)?
He immediately believed the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) without hesitation.
gemini2-rashidun-010: How was Uthman ibn Affan chosen to assume the caliphate?
Through an explicit statement by the Prophet
Through Abu Bakr directly appointing him as successor
Through the six-member shura (consultative council) appointed by Umar
Through general elections in all the state's provinces
Umar entrusted the matter to consultation among six Companions, who chose Uthman after deliberation.
gemini2-rashidun-016: How many years did Uthman ibn Affan's caliphate last?
He became caliph in 23 AH and was martyred in 35 AH. His was the longest Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliphate.
gemini2-rashidun-017: What are the wars Abu Bakr as-Siddiq led against tribes refusing to pay zakah (obligatory alms) called?
He fought apostates and those withholding zakah (obligatory alms) until stability returned to Islam in Arabia.
gemini2-rashidun-020: Which extremist sect rebelled against Ali ibn Abi Talib and declared Muslims disbelievers for major sins?
They rebelled after the arbitration at the Battle of Siffin and declared Ali and Mu'awiyah disbelievers.
rashid-0008: To which city did Caliph Ali ibn Abi Talib move the caliphate's capital from Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah?
Imam Ali moved the capital to Kufah in Iraq because its central position facilitated managing the dispersed armies.
rashid-0009: Why was the first caliph, Abu Bakr, given the title As-Siddiq?
Because he never lied in the pre-Islamic era
Because he kept his promises to Quraysh
Because he immediately believed the Prophet's account of Al-Isra' wa al-Mi'raj (the Night Journey and Ascension)
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave him this title for his constant readiness to affirm and believe news from heaven.
rashid-0015: How was the fourth Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph, Ali ibn Abi Talib, related to the Prophet Muhammad?
He was the Prophet's maternal uncle
He was the Prophet's paternal uncle
He was the Prophet's paternal cousin
He was the Prophet's foster brother through nursing
Ali was the son of Abu Talib, the Prophet's uncle. He grew up in the Prophet's household and married his daughter Fatimah.
rashid-0016: How many years did the Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliphate last before becoming kingship, as the Prophet stated in the hadith (Prophetic report)?

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «الخلافة في أمتي ثلاثون سنة، ثم مُلك بعد ذلك» [The caliphate in my community will last thirty years, then kingship will follow.] It ended with Al-Hasan relinquishing power to Mu'awiyah, may Allah be pleased with them.
rashid-0017: Which young Companion's army did Abu Bakr as-Siddiq insist on dispatching to ash-Sham, carrying out the Prophet's final orders before his death?
Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah (may Allah be pleased with him)
Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him)
Usamah ibn Zayd (may Allah be pleased with them both)
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) appointed Usamah to command the army. Abu Bakr dispatched his expedition immediately upon becoming caliph despite some Arabs' apostasy.
gemini-umayyad-003: Which Umayyad caliph greatly expanded the Prophet's Mosque and Al-Masjid al-Haram and attended to preparing roads for pilgrims?
Al-Walid was known for his enthusiasm for construction. He ordered the Prophet's Mosque expanded and adorned Al-Masjid al-Haram.
gemini-umayyad-005: Which Umayyad caliph made the major sovereign decision to Arabize the administrative bureaus so their records would be in Arabic?
Abd al-Malik ordered the bureaus Arabized and Arabic coins minted, strengthening the state's administrative and economic independence.
gemini2-umayyad-009: Which Umayyad caliph made Ar-Rusafah in ash-Sham his residence and was known for firmness and accumulating wealth?
Hisham ruled for about twenty years, the longest Umayyad reign after Mu'awiyah. The state's financial organization reached its peak under him.
gemini2-umayyad-018: Who was the last Umayyad caliph in Damascus, killed after fleeing to Egypt?
He was killed after his crushing defeat by the Abbasids at the Battle of the Zab.
umaw-0001: Which Companion founded the Umayyad state after Al-Hasan ibn Ali relinquished power?
Amr ibn al-As (may Allah be pleased with him)
Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (may Allah be pleased with him)
Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both)
The Umayyad era began when Mu'awiyah assumed power in 41 AH, Am al-Jama'ah.
umaw-0003: Which Umayyad caliph completed the construction of the Dome of the Rock in Al-Masjid al-Aqsa?
Abd al-Malik completed the architectural masterpiece of the Dome of the Rock.
umaw-0005: Which Umayyad caliph was so renowned for justice and asceticism that historians called him the fifth Rashidun (Rightly Guided) caliph?
His reign was distinguished by redressing injustices and spreading justice and prosperity throughout the state, earning him that title.
umaw-0008: Which Umayyad caliph ordered the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus built and took exceptional care over its construction?
Al-Walid was interested in construction and built the Umayyad Mosque, considered a masterpiece of Islamic architecture.
umaw-0010: Which Umayyad prince escaped the Abbasids, fled to Al-Andalus, and founded a powerful Umayyad emirate there?
He was called Ad-Dakhil because he entered Al-Andalus after an arduous escape. Abu Ja'far al-Mansur called him Saqr Quraysh.
umaw-0015: Which Umayyad caliph established Diwan al-Khatam to stamp and seal letters with wax to prevent forgery of state orders?
Mu'awiyah established this bureau as a strict security measure to protect official correspondence from tampering and forgery.
umaw-0018: Which Umayyad ruler in Al-Andalus reunified the country, proclaimed himself caliph, and bore the title An-Nasir li-Din Allah?
Abd ar-Rahman III came to power when Al-Andalus was fragmented, unified it, and proclaimed the Umayyad caliphate in Al-Andalus in 316 AH.
umaw-0002: Which city did the Umayyads make their state's capital?
Mu'awiyah moved the capital to Damascus, his supporters' stronghold.
gemini-umayyad-b3-010: The Battle of Balat ash-Shuhada', or Poitiers, took place in France. Which Muslim army commander was martyred there?
Al-Ghafiqi advanced deep into France and nearly conquered it, but he was martyred and the army later withdrew in 114 AH.
gemini2-umayyad-004: Which Umayyad commander besieged Constantinople during Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik's reign?
Maslamah ibn Abd al-Malik besieged Constantinople by land and sea for about two years (98-99 AH), then the siege was lifted.
umaw-0007: Which Umayyad commander built Al-Qayrawan in Tunisia as an advanced Muslim base?
Uqbah ibn Nafi' founded Al-Qayrawan in 50 AH as a starting point for conquests in North Africa.
umaw-0017: Which brave Umayyad commander conquered vast areas of Central Asia known as Ma Wara' an-Nahr?
Qutaybah led armies in the east during Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik's reign and achieved extensive conquests in Central Asia.
gemini2-umayyad-019: Which decisive battle saw the Muslims defeat the Goths and fully open the way into Al-Andalus?
It took place in 92 AH under Tariq ibn Ziyad, and King Ludhriq's army was destroyed.
umaw-0016: Which major battle in France halted the Umayyad advance in Western Europe and saw commander Abd ar-Rahman al-Ghafiqi martyred?
Historically known as Balat ash-Shuhada', or Poitiers, the battle took place in 114 AH and halted the Islamic advance in France.
gemini-umayyad-002: Which beautiful Andalusian city became the Umayyad state's capital in Al-Andalus, present-day Spain?
Abd ar-Rahman ad-Dakhil made Qurtubah his capital. It later became one of Europe's greatest centers of learning.
gemini-umayyad-b2-001: Which grandson of the Prophet relinquished his claim to the caliphate to Mu'awiyah to reunite the Muslims after division?
Al-Hasan relinquished power to spare the community's lives, fulfilling the Prophet's prediction.
gemini-umayyad-b2-005: Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr refused to pledge allegiance to Yazid. What did he do?
Declared an independent caliphate in Makkah and held out for years
Immediately surrendered and pledged allegiance to Yazid
Joined the Byzantine army as a combatant
He remained caliph in the Hijaz for several years until Al-Hajjaj besieged and killed him.
gemini-umayyad-b2-008: What congregational mosque did the Umayyads build in Qurtubah that became one of their greatest monuments in Al-Andalus?
Abd ar-Rahman ad-Dakhil began it in 170 AH, and his successors expanded it. Its many columns led to its description as a forest of columns.
gemini-umayyad-b2-010: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ath-Thaqafi was the young commander who conquered which vast region and spread Islam there?
He conquered Sindh at age 17 on Al-Hajjaj's orders.
gemini-umayyad-b2-013: Which famous Umayyad desert palace in Jordan is among the most prominent surviving Umayyad monuments?
Qusayr Amrah is distinguished by its murals and unique baths.
gemini-umayyad-b2-016: Which sect rebelled against the Umayyads under the slogan 'Judgment belongs only to Allah'?

The Khawarij first rebelled against Ali, then continued rebelling against the Umayyads. Their slogan takes Allah's words ﴿إِنِ الْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ﴾ [Legislation is not but for Allāh.] with a corrupt interpretation.
gemini-umayyad-b3-004: Which magnificent Islamic building did Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik complete in Damascus, decorating it with mosaics to rival Byzantine churches?
The Dome of the Rock Mosque
The Umayyad Mosque in Damascus remains among the greatest testimonies to the splendor of Umayyad architecture.
gemini-umayyad-b3-007: Which kingdom did the Muslims overthrow when they conquered Al-Andalus?
Al-Andalus was held by the Visigoths and their king Ludhriq, who was defeated at Wadi Lakkah in 92 AH.
gemini-umayyad-b3-014: The Battle of the Zab was the decisive battle that:
Defeated the last Umayyad caliph and established the Abbasid state
The Battle of the Great Zab in 132 AH ended the Umayyad caliphate in the east.
gemini-umayyad-b3-018: Which Christian poet praised the Umayyads and was one of the three poets of naqa'id (poetic invective exchanges)?
The naqa'id (poetic invective exchange) poets were Jarir, Al-Farazdaq, and Al-Akhtal. Al-Akhtal was a Christian from Taghlib who joined the Umayyad court and praised Abd al-Malik.
gemini2-umayyad-003: To which Quraysh clan do the Umayyads belong?
Umayyah was the son of Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf, so Banu Umayyah and Banu Hashim share descent from Abd Manaf.
gemini2-umayyad-008: Who introduced grammatical vowel dots into the mushaf (written Qur'an)?
Grammatical vowel dots are attributed to Abu al-Aswad ad-Du'ali. Dots distinguishing similarly shaped letters are attributed to Nasr ibn Asim and Yahya ibn Ya'mar.
gemini2-umayyad-010: Which Umayyad governor built Wasit in Iraq as a base for his troops?
Al-Hajjaj built it in 83 AH between Kufah and Basrah. Its name reflects its location midway between them.
gemini2-umayyad-016: Which state immediately succeeded the Umayyad state in the east?
The Abbasid state was established in 132 AH after the Umayyads fell at the Battle of the Zab.
gemini2-umayyad-017: Which Byzantine capital did Umayyad armies subject to a long, harsh siege during Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik's reign?
This was the second siege of Constantinople, led by Maslamah ibn Abd al-Malik. The city was not conquered then.
umaw-0004: What is the large historic mosque the Umayyads built in their capital, Damascus, called?
The Umayyad Mosque in Damascus is among the most prominent masterpieces of Islamic architecture built by the Umayyads.
umaw-0009: What was the principal gold currency Muslims used that the Umayyads fully Arabized?
The gold dinar was the principal currency. Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan Arabized it and minted it entirely in Arabic.
umaw-0011: Which administrative system did Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan develop to carry letters and news quickly across the state using horses?
Mu'awiyah organized the post using relay horses at distributed stations to accelerate the transmission of orders and news.
umaw-0012: Al-Andalus was the great region the Umayyads conquered and ruled for centuries. On which continent is it?
Al-Andalus, present-day Spain and Portugal, is in southwestern Europe.
umaw-0013: Which famous strait did the Muslim commander Tariq ibn Ziyad cross to conquer Al-Andalus, and which still bears his name?
The strait separating Morocco and Spain became known as the Strait of Jabal Tariq, or Gibraltar, to commemorate his crossing.
umaw-0014: In which present-day Arab country is Damascus, formerly a powerful Umayyad capital?
Damascus is Syria's present-day capital. It was the Umayyad state's political and cultural center for nearly a century.
abbas-0003: Which Abbasid caliph demanded jizyah (tribute) from Nikephoros, the Byzantine ruler, in a letter beginning 'From the Commander of the Believers to Nikephoros, dog of the Byzantines'?
Ar-Rashid sent this stern letter in response to the Byzantines' violation of the treaty.
abbas-0005: Which Abbasid caliph ordered Samarra built as the military capital for his army?
Al-Mu'tasim built Samarra to move his large army away from crowded Baghdad.
abbas-0006: Who was the original founder and first caliph of the Abbasid state?
Abu al-Abbas as-Saffah was proclaimed caliph in Kufah after Umayyad rule fell, formally establishing the Abbasid state.
abbas-0008: Which Abbasid caliph strongly encouraged translation and expanded the role of Bayt al-Hikmah during his reign?
Al-Ma'mun encouraged scholars and translators to study and translate Greek and other sciences into Arabic.
abbas-0013: Which best-known Abbasid caliph was renowned for frequent Hajj (pilgrimage) and military campaigns and associated with many historical stories?
Harun ar-Rashid is among the most famous Abbasid caliphs. The state reached the height of its cultural glory under him.
gemini-abbasid-b4-001: Which Abbasid caliph fought a war against his brother Al-Ma'mun that ended with his own death?
Al-Amin ibn Harun ar-Rashid was deposed and killed in 198 AH after Baghdad's siege, leaving power firmly with Al-Ma'mun.
gemini2-abbasid-001: Which Abbasid caliph ended the ordeal over the doctrine of the Qur'an's createdness and supported Ahl as-Sunnah (the Sunni community)?
Al-Mutawakkil ended the ordeal in 234 AH, upheld the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition), and honored Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal after what he had endured under previous rulers.
gemini2-abbasid-004: Which Abbasid caliph exchanged gifts and embassies with Charlemagne, king of the Franks?
Harun ar-Rashid sent Charlemagne gifts, including a remarkable water clock. They exchanged embassies in the late second century AH.
abbas-0012: Which powerful Persian family held the vizierate under Harun ar-Rashid before he dismissed them and destroyed their influence?
Ar-Rashid relied on the Barmakids to administer the state for years, then brought them down when their influence exceeded acceptable limits.
abbas-0015: Which Sunni Turkish dynasty took control of Baghdad and rescued the Abbasid caliphate from Shiite Buyid influence?
Tughril Beg the Seljuk entered Baghdad in 447 AH, ended Buyid control, and restored the Abbasid caliphate's prestige.
abbas-0017: Which outstanding Muslim scholar of the Abbasid era is considered the founder of modern optics and wrote Kitab al-Manazir?
Ibn al-Haytham corrected misconceptions about vision and scientifically established that light reflects from objects into the eye.
gemini-abbasid-b2-018: Which physician wrote Al-Hawi fi at-Tibb and first distinguished smallpox from measles?
Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ar-Razi wrote the famous treatise Al-Judari wa al-Hasbah, the first precise clinical description distinguishing them.
gemini2-abbasid-008: Which famous Abbasid-era physician and scholar wrote Al-Qanun fi at-Tibb, studied in Europe for centuries?
Ibn Sina was a great physician and philosopher who lived and flourished intellectually in the Abbasid era.
gemini-abbasid-b2-004: What severe intellectual ordeal led to Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal being imprisoned and tortured in the Abbasid era?
The doctrine of the Qur'an's createdness
Scholars were forced to adopt the Mu'tazilah's view that the Qur'an was created. Imam Ahmad refused and stood firm.
abbas-0001: Which famous city did the Abbasids build as their state's capital?
Abu Ja'far al-Mansur built it as the metropolis of the Abbasid caliphate.
abbas-0002: In which Hijri year did Baghdad, the Abbasid caliphate's capital, fall to the Mongols?
Hulagu stormed Baghdad and overthrew the caliphate in 656 AH.
abbas-0007: On the banks of which river did the Abbasids build Baghdad as their capital?
Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur chose Baghdad's site on the Tigris for its defensibility and available water.
abbas-0009: Which Mongol commander led his armies to invade and destroy Baghdad and overthrow the Abbasid caliphate in 656 AH?
Hulagu led the Mongol army in besieging and destroying Baghdad and killing its last Abbasid caliph.
abbas-0010: From which uncle of the Prophet are the Abbasid caliphs descended?
Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him)
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him)
The Abbasid state traces its lineage to Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, from whose descendants its caliphs came.
abbas-0011: What geometric shape was Baghdad originally designed in when Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur built it?
Al-Mansur designed Baghdad as a complete circle surrounded by a moat and two walls, hence its name Al-Madinah al-Mudawwarah.
abbas-0020: Who was Baghdad's last Abbasid caliph, killed by the Mongols when they invaded and the capital fell?
Al-Musta'sim Billah was Baghdad's last Abbasid caliph. His death ended the eastern Abbasid caliphate in 656 AH.
abbas-0021: Which Persian Shiite dynasty controlled Baghdad and stripped the Abbasid caliphs of effective power for over a century before the Seljuks arrived?
The Buyids entered Baghdad in 334 AH and took control of government, leaving the Abbasid caliph merely a religious symbol without effective authority.
gemini-abbasid-005: Which famous Seljuk vizier established a network of major schools in the Abbasid era to support Sunni education?
Nizam al-Mulk founded the Nizamiyyah schools in Baghdad and elsewhere to teach the Sunni school and counter other intellectual currents.
gemini-abbasid-b2-005: Which outstanding Abbasid scholar was called the Second Teacher after Aristotle?
Abu Nasr al-Farabi was known for his precise commentaries on Greek philosophy.
gemini-abbasid-b2-008: Which great Abbasid poet wrote the poem Al-Khayl wa al-Layl wa al-Bayda' Ta'rifuni and was killed because of his poetry?
Al-Mutanabbi is among the Arabs' finest poets and was known for pride and chivalry.
gemini-abbasid-b2-015: In which field did Abbasid physicist Al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham bring about a major revolution and correct misconceptions?
Optics and the theory of vision
His book Al-Manazir established that light reflects from objects into the eye, not the reverse.
gemini-abbasid-b2-017: Which great congregational mosque was built in the Abbasid era and is famous for its spiral Al-Malwiyyah minaret?
The Al-Malwiyyah minaret in Samarra is one of history's unique architectural masterpieces.
gemini-abbasid-b3-004: Who were the Barmakids in the early Abbasid era?
An Arab tribe rebelling against the caliphate
A Persian family Harun ar-Rashid appointed as viziers and later brought down
Byzantine army commanders who embraced Islam
The Barmakids had immense influence in the state until Ar-Rashid brought them down for monopolizing power.
gemini-abbasid-b3-006: Which devastating event caused the fall of the Abbasid capital, Baghdad, in 656 AH and the death of its caliph Al-Musta'sim?
The Mongol (Tatar) invasion led by Hulagu
Hulagu destroyed Baghdad, burned its libraries, killed hundreds of thousands, and overthrew the eastern caliphate.
gemini-abbasid-b3-008: Which city did Al-Mu'tasim build as a military capital for his Turkish troops?
He built it in 221 AH after Baghdad's people became exasperated with his troops. It remained the capital for about fifty-six years.
gemini-abbasid-b3-018: Which historian wrote Tarikh ar-Rusul wa al-Muluk and the Qur'an commentary Jami' al-Bayan?
Muhammad ibn Jarir at-Tabari was an authority in tafsir (Qur'an commentary) and history. His historical work is among the most extensive compiled in the third century AH.
gemini2-abbasid-002: Approximately how many centuries did the Abbasid state in Baghdad last?
From its founding in 132 AH to Baghdad's fall to the Mongols in 656 AH: approximately five centuries.
gemini2-abbasid-003: Which scholar established Arabic prosody and compiled the first Arabic dictionary, Al-Ayn?
Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi, Sibawayh's teacher, identified poetic meters and arranged Al-Ayn by letters' articulation points.
gemini2-abbasid-005: Who overthrew the Abbasid caliphate in 656 AH after destroying Baghdad?
Hulagu invaded Baghdad with his Mongol army, destroyed its civilization, and overthrew the caliphate.
gemini2-abbasid-006: What was the major scholarly movement that flourished in the Abbasid era, transferring Greek, Persian, and Indian sciences into Arabic?
They translated books of medicine, philosophy, and mathematics to preserve and develop them.
gemini2-abbasid-019: Which Sunni Turkish dynasty controlled Baghdad in the later Abbasid era and revived jihad (armed struggle) against the Byzantines?
The Seljuks entered Baghdad, eliminated Buyid influence, and protected the caliphate.
ayyub-0001: Which heroic commander liberated Jerusalem from the Crusaders and founded the Ayyubid state?
Salah ad-Din was the liberator of Al-Aqsa and the hero of the Battle of Hattin.
ayyub-0005: Which famous English king led the Third Crusade and fought fierce battles against Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi?
England's King Richard the Lionheart was a leading Crusader commander who confronted Salah ad-Din. Their conflict ended with the Treaty of Ramla.
ayyub-0012: What was the name of Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi's full brother, who aided him in war, later ruled the Ayyubid state, and preserved its strength?
Al-Malik al-Adil, Sayf ad-Din Abu Bakr, was Salah ad-Din's right-hand man and reunified the Ayyubid state after his death.
ayyub-0015: By which royal title was Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi known when he became independent ruler of Egypt and ash-Sham?
His full title was Sultan Al-Malik an-Nasir Abu al-Muzaffar Salah ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub.
ayyub-0016: Which vizier and eloquent writer did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi rely on, saying of him, 'Do not think I gained the lands through your swords, but through his pen'?
Al-Qadi al-Fadil, Abd ar-Rahim al-Baysani, was Salah ad-Din's strategist and vizier, famed for his exceptional eloquence.
ayyub-0019: Which Ayyubid sultan signed the Treaty of Jaffa, peacefully handing Jerusalem to the Crusader emperor Frederick II?
In 626 AH, Al-Malik al-Kamil made a treaty surrendering Jerusalem to the Crusaders without fighting, provoking widespread Muslim anger.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-002: Who supervised the construction of Qal'at al-Jabal and Cairo's wall for Salah ad-Din?
Qaraqush al-Asadi had been Asad ad-Din's mamluk (military slave). Salah ad-Din put him in charge of Cairo's construction projects, and he built the citadel, wall, and bridges.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-013: Which Ayyubid sultan relied heavily on purchasing Bahri Mamluks (military slaves) and entrusting the army to them?
He formed them into a powerful army and settled them on Ar-Rawdah Island. They later founded the Mamluk state.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-018: Which preacher delivered the first Friday khutbah (sermon) in Al-Masjid al-Aqsa after its liberation, at Salah ad-Din's request?
He delivered an eloquent sermon that moved those present to tears and reminded them of the greatness of the conquest and blessing.
gemini2-ayyubid-003: Which ruler sent Salah ad-Din and his uncle Shirkuh to Egypt?
Nur ad-Din Mahmud Zangi, ruler of ash-Sham, sent three campaigns to Egypt led by Asad ad-Din Shirkuh, accompanied by his nephew Salah ad-Din.
gemini2-ayyubid-016: Which uncle of Salah ad-Din led the armies of ash-Sham into Egypt and paved the way for Salah ad-Din to become vizier there?
Shirkuh led Nur ad-Din's army into Egypt, and Salah ad-Din was among his young commanders.
gemini2-ayyubid-019: Who was the last effective Ayyubid sultan in Egypt, killed by the Mamluk emirs?
Turan Shah's death effectively ended Ayyubid authority in Egypt, transferring it to the Mamluks.
ayyub-0002: Which decisive battle saw Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi defeat the Crusaders and pave the way for Jerusalem's conquest?
The Battle of Hattin broke Crusader power in ash-Sham.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-010: From which first political capital did Salah ad-Din govern his state and abolish the Fatimid caliphate?
He became vizier in Egypt and administered it from Cairo before setting out to unify ash-Sham.
gemini2-ayyubid-002: Which holy city did Salah ad-Din recover from the Crusaders, bringing joy to the Muslims?
He restored Al-Masjid al-Aqsa to the Muslims after a long occupation.
ayyub-0009: Which state's rule did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi end in Egypt to return it to the Sunni Abbasid caliphate?
Salah ad-Din ended the Fatimid (Ubaydi) caliphate in Egypt in 567 AH and unified the Islamic front.
gemini2-ayyubid-006: Which state arose in Egypt after the Ayyubid state?
The Mamluk state arose in 648 AH after Ayyubid rule in Egypt ended.
gemini-ayyubid-b3-002: Approximately how many years did the Ayyubid state rule Egypt?
From 567 AH until the Mamluk state's rise in 648 AH: about eighty years.
gemini2-ayyubid-001: Approximately how many years did Jerusalem remain under Crusader control before Salah ad-Din liberated it?
The Crusaders entered it in 1099 CE. Salah ad-Din liberated it in 1187 CE after Hattin, about eighty-eight years later.
gemini-ayyubid-b3-003: Who wrote Ar-Rawdatayn fi Akhbar ad-Dawlatayn, chronicling Nur ad-Din and Salah ad-Din?
Abu Shamah al-Maqdisi (d. 665 AH). The two states were Nur ad-Din's and Salah ad-Din's.
gemini2-ayyubid-005: Who wrote Wafayat al-A'yan wa Anba' Abna' az-Zaman?
Ibn Khallikan (d. 681 AH) wrote the most famous biographical dictionary in Islamic history.
ayyub-0007: Which blessed mosque did commander Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi liberate from the Crusaders and restore to the Muslims?
Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi crowned his victories by entering Jerusalem and cleansing the blessed Al-Masjid al-Aqsa.
ayyub-0008: Which formidable fortress did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi order built on Al-Muqattam Hill in Cairo?
Salah ad-Din built it on Al-Muqattam Hill. Also known as Salah ad-Din's Citadel, it remained Egypt's seat of government for centuries.
ayyub-0010: How did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi treat Jerusalem's Crusader inhabitants after defeating them and conquering the city?
Killed them all in revenge for their actions
Demolished their homes and expelled them with nothing
Captured them and sold them in slave markets
Guaranteed departure for those who paid ransom, pardoned many, and enslaved others
Departure required ransom. Salah ad-Din freed many without it, while others were enslaved. One fate cannot correctly be generalized to everyone.
ayyub-0014: Which famous treaty did Salah ad-Din sign with Richard the Lionheart, leaving Jerusalem with the Muslims while allowing pilgrims to visit?
The Treaty of Ramla was concluded in 588 AH after long battles and affirmed Muslim sovereignty over Jerusalem.
ayyub-0017: Which Arab country did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi first rule and establish his state in before unifying ash-Sham?
Salah ad-Din became vizier in Egypt, then ended the Fatimid caliphate and founded the Ayyubid state from Cairo.
gemini-ayyubid-004: What happened to the large state Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi had unified after his death?
The Abbasids immediately took it over
It collapsed and was wholly occupied by Crusaders
It was divided among his sons and brothers, weakening it
The empire was divided among his sons and relatives in Damascus, Aleppo, and Egypt, leading to internal conflicts that weakened the state.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-003: Which coastal city did the Crusaders subject to a long, bitter siege until it fell after the Battle of Hattin?
The siege of Acre lasted nearly two years. It fell despite Salah ad-Din's efforts to lift the siege.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-007: After the Ayyubid state split following Salah ad-Din's death, who eventually secured effective leadership and reunified it?
Al-Malik al-Adil Sayf ad-Din Abu Bakr, Salah ad-Din's brother, reunified the Ayyubid state after the sons' disputes.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-016: What was the heavy weapon Muslims used to hurl large stones and demolish fortress walls called?
The mangonel was an effective, destructive siege weapon against fortress walls before cannons were invented.
gemini2-ayyubid-004: Who was the last Fatimid caliph, whose death marked the end of their state in Egypt?
Salah ad-Din stopped the khutbah (sermon) in Al-Adid's name in 567 AH and had it delivered in the Abbasid caliph's name. Al-Adid died days later.
gemini2-ayyubid-007: In which Hijri year did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi die?
He died, may Allah have mercy on him, in 589 AH/1193 CE, six years after Jerusalem's conquest.
gemini2-ayyubid-009: Which madhhab (school of Islamic law) did Salah ad-Din al-Ayyubi follow and spread in Egypt?
Salah ad-Din followed the Shafi'i school and built schools to spread Sunni fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) after two centuries of Fatimid rule in Egypt.
gemini2-ayyubid-010: Which school did Salah ad-Din establish beside Imam ash-Shafi'i's tomb in Cairo?
It was among his earliest schools for teaching Shafi'i fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) and a pillar of the revival of the Sunni school in Egypt.
gemini2-ayyubid-017: What did Salah ad-Din order built to enclose Cairo, Al-Fustat, and the citadel within one wall?
Baha' ad-Din Qaraqush supervised it. The aim was to join the two cities and the citadel within one stronghold that would be difficult to storm.
gemini2-ayyubid-020: Which book did Al-Imad al-Isfahani write about Salah ad-Din's conquest of Jerusalem?
Mufarrij al-Kurub fi Akhbar Bani Ayyub
Al-Imad al-Isfahani was a writer in Salah ad-Din's chancery and recorded Jerusalem's conquest in Al-Fath al-Qussi fi al-Fath al-Qudsi.
gemini-mamluk-b2-003: Who became the Mamluk state's first sultan after Shajar ad-Durr relinquished power to him?
She married him to give the rule legitimacy after the Abbasid caliph objected to a woman ruling.
gemini-mamluk-b2-013: Which sultan ordered the citadel in Alexandria built to protect the coast from pirates and Crusader threats?
Qaytbay Citadel is among the most important Mamluk maritime fortresses.
gemini-mamluk-b4-003: Which Mamluk sultan ruled three times and saw the state's greatest building boom during his reign?
An-Nasir Muhammad ruled in three separate periods spanning about forty-two years. Buildings, canals, and mosques multiplied under him.
gemini2-mamluk-009: Which Mamluk sultan built a large medical complex and magnificent mosque in Cairo that still bear his name?
Qalawun's bimaristan (hospital) and complex are among the greatest monuments of Mamluk architecture.
gemini2-mamluk-010: Which Mamluk sultan was defeated and killed fighting the Ottomans at Marj Dabiq in 1516 CE?
With Al-Ghawri's death, ash-Sham fell to the Ottomans and the way into Egypt opened.
mamluk-0002: Which Mamluk sultan led the Muslim army to victory at the Battle of Ayn Jalut?
The victorious commander Qutuz united the Muslims to confront the Mongols.
mamluk-0003: Which Mamluk sultan shared command with Qutuz at Ayn Jalut and then succeeded him?
Az-Zahir Baybars rose to prominence in the battle and later became the strongest Mamluk sultan.
mamluk-0007: Which Mamluk sultan finally expelled the Crusaders from ash-Sham by conquering Acre in 1291 CE?
Al-Ashraf Khalil led a huge army and conquered Acre, ending the Crusader presence on the coast of ash-Sham.
mamluk-0010: After the Mongols destroyed Baghdad, which Mamluk sultan revived the Abbasid caliphate in Cairo to unite the Muslims?
Baybars brought an Abbasid prince to Cairo and pledged allegiance to him as caliph to legitimize Mamluk rule and unite the Muslims.
mamluk-0011: Which Mamluk sultan built Cairo's huge medical complex, Al-Bimaristan al-Mansuri, to treat people free of charge?
Sultan al-Mansur Qalawun founded this great hospital as a charitable waqf (endowment) to treat poor and rich alike.
mamluk-0013: Which Mamluk sultan built an enormous school and mosque in Cairo with four huge iwans (vaulted halls), regarded as a jewel of Islamic architecture?
Sultan Hasan's school and mosque is among the greatest Mamluk monuments, with an open courtyard surrounded by 4 iwans (vaulted halls).
mamluk-0014: Who was Egypt's last Mamluk sultan, who bravely resisted the Ottomans at Ar-Raydaniyyah before being hanged at Bab Zuwaylah?
After Al-Ghawri was killed at Marj Dabiq, Tuman Bay took command and resisted Selim I's entry into Egypt to the end.
mamluk-0020: Which sultan is considered the effective founder of the Burji (Circassian) Mamluk state after Bahri Mamluk rule ended?
Az-Zahir Barquq took power in 784 AH, ending the rule of Qalawun's descendants and founding the Burji Mamluk dynasty.
gemini-mamluk-b2-014: Which military office corresponded to commander-in-chief in the Mamluk hierarchy?
The atabak controlled the army, and the office usually qualified its holder for the sultanate.
gemini2-mamluk-002: In which famous battle did the Mamluks first defeat the Mongol (Tatar) army?
Ayn Jalut in Palestine halted the Mongol advance and saved the Islamic world.
gemini2-mamluk-019: In which battle did the Ottomans defeat the Mamluks in northern ash-Sham in 922 AH?
Marj Dabiq is near Aleppo. Sultan al-Ghawri was killed there, and the matter was settled at Ar-Raydaniyyah in Egypt in 923 AH.
gemini-mamluk-003: Why were the Bahri Mamluks given this name in Islamic history?
Because they came from across the Mediterranean
Because their barracks were on Ar-Rawdah Island in the Nile, called al-bahr
Sultan as-Salih Ayyub settled them in barracks on Ar-Rawdah Island in the Nile, which Egyptians call al-bahr (the sea).
gemini-mamluk-b2-007: In which city are most mosques and public drinking fountains built by the Mamluk sultans concentrated?
Mamluk monuments are concentrated in Historic Cairo, especially Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah Street and its surroundings.
gemini-mamluk-b2-011: What was the predominant ethnic origin of the Burji Mamluks who ruled late in the state's history?
The Circassians prevailed over the Turkish Mamluks and established their Burji state.
gemini-mamluk-b2-017: In which city is Qaytbay Citadel, built on the site of its ancient lighthouse?
Sultan al-Ashraf Qaytbay built it in 882 AH on the site of Alexandria's lighthouse, destroyed by earthquakes, to protect the port from the Ottomans and Franks.
gemini-mamluk-b2-019: Which large commercial building in Mamluk cities contained an inn and merchants' storerooms to stimulate economic activity?
Wikalahs, such as Al-Ghawri's, served as international commercial centers at that time.
gemini2-mamluk-001: In which country did the Mamluk state arise and establish its capital?
It arose in Egypt in 648 AH with Cairo as its capital, and its authority extended to ash-Sham and the Hijaz.
gemini2-mamluk-003: In which Hijri year did the Battle of Ayn Jalut take place?
It took place in Palestine in 658 AH/1260 CE and halted the Mongol advance toward Egypt and ash-Sham.
gemini2-mamluk-006: In which Hijri century did the Mamluk state arise in Egypt?
It arose in 648 AH after Ayyubid rule in Egypt ended, in the middle of the seventh Hijri century.
gemini2-mamluk-016: On which river is Cairo, the Mamluk state's capital?
Cairo arose on the Nile's eastern bank. Its flood was the basis of the state's agriculture and kharaj (land tax).
gemini2-mamluk-020: In which book did Ibn Iyas chronicle the Mamluk state's end and the Ottomans' entry into Egypt?
Ibn Iyas witnessed the state's fall in 923 AH and recorded its events with the rare detail of an eyewitness.
mamluk-0001: Which invaders' destructive advance did the Mamluks halt at the Battle of Ayn Jalut?
The victory at Ayn Jalut protected the Islamic world from Tatar destruction.
mamluk-0004: Which Arab city did the Mamluks make their capital and seat of government?
Cairo in Egypt was the Mamluk state's political and military capital.
mamluk-0005: Which woman ruled Egypt briefly, paving the way for power to pass to the Mamluks?
Shajar ad-Durr was As-Salih Ayyub's wife and played a decisive role in the transfer of power and beginning of the Mamluk era.
mamluk-0009: Which fast birds did the Mamluks train to carry important messages quickly between Egypt and ash-Sham?
The Mamluks relied on homing pigeons as a rapid communication network for military news and correspondence.
mamluk-0015: Which famous historic market was built in the Mamluk era and remains one of Cairo's major tourist landmarks?
Jaharkas al-Khalili founded it during Sultan Barquq's reign. It is among the Islamic world's oldest traditional markets.
mamluk-0016: The Mamluk era is historically divided into which two main states that ruled Egypt and ash-Sham successively?
Historians divide their state into the Bahri Mamluks, who lived on Ar-Rawdah, and the Burji Mamluks, who lived in the citadel's towers.
mamluk-0019: What official title did the Mamluk state's ruler use instead of caliph?
Mamluk rulers called themselves sultan to express their military and political supremacy, such as Sultan Qutuz.
gemini2-ottoman-009: In which battle did Sultan Selim I defeat the Shiite Safavid state in 1514 CE?
The Battle of Chaldiran halted Safavid expansion and secured the Ottoman state's eastern borders.
gemini2-ottoman-018: In which famous naval battle was the Ottoman fleet defeated, marking the beginning of the loss of its naval prestige?
At Lepanto in 1571 CE, the European allied fleet destroyed most of the Ottoman fleet.
othman-0004: In which decisive battle did Sultan Selim I defeat the Mamluks north of Aleppo in 1516 CE?
Marj Dabiq was the decisive battle that ended Mamluk rule in ash-Sham in favor of Ottoman sultan Selim I.
othman-0016: In which famous naval battle of 1571 CE was the Ottoman fleet first defeated by the European Holy League?
Lepanto was the Ottomans' first major naval defeat. Nevertheless, they rebuilt their fleet in record time.
gemini-ottoman-b2-018: The Committee of Union and Progress was a political and military movement that led the coup deposing which sultan?
They led a constitutional coup that stripped Sultan Abdulhamid II of his powers, then deposed him.
gemini-ottoman-b4-005: Which powerful Ottoman sultan shifted conquests eastward, defeated the Mamluks in ash-Sham and Egypt, and annexed them to the empire?
He won at Marj Dabiq and Ar-Raydaniyyah, paving the way for the caliphate's transfer to the Ottomans.
gemini2-ottoman-004: Which Ottoman sultan, called Yildirim, the Thunderbolt, for his speed, was defeated and captured at Ankara?
The Mongol commander Tamerlane captured him at Ankara. He died of illness in captivity.
othman-0002: Which Ottoman sultan was called Al-Qanuni and was known in Europe as Suleiman the Magnificent?
He was known as Suleiman al-Qanuni for establishing laws that organized Ottoman state affairs.
othman-0003: Which emir was the Ottoman state's original founder and gave it his name?
Emir Osman made his principality independent and expanded it. The dynasty and state were known as Ottoman after him.
othman-0010: Which Ottoman sultan annexed Egypt and ash-Sham in 1517 CE and ended the Mamluk state?
After his victory over the Mamluks in 1517 CE, the symbolism of the caliphate passed to the House of Osman, although a formal transfer is disputed among historians.
othman-0013: Which Ottoman sultan rejected Theodor Herzl's financial offers in exchange for allowing Jewish settlement in Palestine?
Sultan Abdulhamid II rejected Theodor Herzl's enormous financial offers and issued decrees prohibiting Zionist immigration to Palestine.
othman-0001: Which great city did Ottoman sultan Muhammad al-Fatih conquer in 1453 CE?
He was called Al-Fatih because he conquered Constantinople, the Byzantine capital.
othman-0019: Which historic European capital did the Ottomans besiege twice, in 1529 CE and 1683 CE, without conquering it, marking their furthest reach in Europe?
Vienna, Austria's capital, was besieged twice: first under Sultan Suleiman al-Qanuni and then under Mehmed IV. It did not fall.
gemini-ottoman-002: What official religion did the Ottoman state defend and govern its conquered lands by?
The Ottoman state was a Sunni Islamic state that made protecting Islam a central mission in its conquests and administration.
gemini-ottoman-005: Which major legal code compiled rulings on transactions in fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) late in the Ottoman era?
The Constitution of the Tanzimat Reforms
The Majallah was the first official codification of Hanafi fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence) as modern legal articles applied by courts.
gemini-ottoman-b2-004: What was the millet system adopted by the Ottoman sultans?
An economic system for collecting taxes
A military system for training cavalry
A system allowing non-Muslim communities to administer their religious affairs
This system guaranteed Christians and Jews freedom of belief and adjudication within the empire.
gemini-ottoman-b2-007: Which sultana was famous for her strong influence in the Ottoman palace during Suleiman al-Qanuni's reign?
Hurrem, also known as Khurrem or Roxelana, was Suleiman al-Qanuni's wife and was renowned for her extensive palace influence.
gemini-ottoman-b2-010: What was the main purpose of the Ottoman devshirme system?
Collecting children from Christian families and raising them for state service
Devshirme collected children from Christian families in the Balkans and raised them as Muslims to become Janissaries or administrators wholly loyal to the state.
gemini-ottoman-b2-015: After World War I, which harsh treaty was imposed to partition and tear apart the Ottoman state, then rejected and annulled by the Turks?
The Turkish national movement under Ataturk rejected the Treaty of Sevres of 1920 CE and fought to revise it at Lausanne.
gemini-ottoman-b4-003: What was the movement of administrative and legal reforms that began in the Ottoman state in 1839 CE called?
It began with the Gulhane Imperial Edict under Sultan Abdulmejid I and reorganized the army, judiciary, and finances along modern lines.
gemini2-ottoman-002: In which battle did the Ottomans lose to Tamerlane and Sultan Bayezid I fall captive?
It took place in 1402 CE and was followed by an interregnum during which Bayezid's sons fought for about eleven years.
gemini2-ottoman-003: Which island did Suleiman al-Qanuni conquer in 1522 CE, expelling the Knights of Saint John?
Rhodes was a base from which the Knights of Saint John attacked Muslim ships. Suleiman conquered it and allowed the knights to leave. They later moved to Malta.
gemini2-ottoman-006: Approximately how many centuries did the Ottoman state last?
From 1299 CE to the abolition of the caliphate in 1924 CE: about six and a quarter centuries.
gemini2-ottoman-007: What was the Ottoman state's prime minister called?
The Grand Vizier headed the executive administration and deputized for the sultan, carried his seal, and presided over the Imperial Council.
gemini2-ottoman-016: Which famous Istanbul mosque has six minarets and is sometimes called the Blue Mosque?
Sultan Ahmed I built it, and it became famous for its stunning blue Iznik tile decoration.
gemini2-ottoman-019: What railway did Sultan Abdulhamid II build to connect Damascus to Al-Madinah al-Munawwarah?
It was built with Muslim funding to serve pilgrims, connect parts of the empire, and facilitate troop transport.
othman-0005: What official title was given to the Ottoman state's supreme ruler?
The House of Osman's rulers were titled sultans, such as Sultan Muhammad al-Fatih and Sultan Selim.
othman-0009: What were the elite infantry units and the sultan's regular army in the Ottoman state called?
Janissary means 'new army.' They were the elite force and backbone of Ottoman conquests.
othman-0011: Istanbul, the great city conquered by the Ottomans, occupies a unique site linking which two continents?
The Bosporus divides Istanbul, formerly Constantinople, and its neighborhoods extend across both Asia and Europe.
othman-0014: Which modern country occupies the region that was the Ottoman state's heartland and capital?
The Ottoman state arose in Anatolia. The modern Turkish Republic is the geographical and political center of its heartland.
othman-0015: What red head covering with a black tassel became official men's dress late in the Ottoman era?
Sultan Mahmud II imposed it as part of official modernization, and it became a symbol of Ottoman state employees.
a1-arab-0002: Which small, shimmering bird did Palestine adopt as a national symbol?
Palestine adopted the Palestine sunbird as its national bird.
a1-arab-0003: What is the historic reservoir system south of Bethlehem called?
Solomon's Pools comprise stepped stone reservoirs that collected water and conveyed it through channels.
a1-arab-0004: In which town is the Palestinian Museum?
The Palestinian Museum is in Birzeit near Ramallah.
a1-arab-0006: Which monastery rises above the rocks of Wadi al-Qelt?
Saint George's Monastery was built on a rocky side of the valley.
a1-arab-0009: What archaeological monastic site is also known as Tell Umm Amer?
UNESCO identifies the site as Saint Hilarion Monastery or Tell Umm Amer.
a1-arab-0010: In which coastal region is the monastic site of Tell Umm Amer?
The site is near Dayr al-Balah on Gaza's coast.
a1-arab-0011: What is the famous tower in central Jaffa called?
Jaffa's tower has a visible clock on its facades.
a1-arab-0014: From which grains are Palestinian maftoul granules traditionally made?
Maftoul granules are hand-rolled from wheat flour and bulgur with water.
a1-arab-0016: The Palestinian Basic Law stipulates that Arabic is the official language.
a1-arab-0018: Which marine material was Bethlehem's decorative craft famous for?
Bethlehem's craftspeople used mother-of-pearl in boxes and decorative objects.
a1-arab-0019: On which bread is musakhan traditionally served?
Musakhan combines tabun bread, olive oil, onions, sumac, and chicken.
a1-arab-0021: Who wrote the poetry collection Awraq az-Zaytun?
a1-arab-0023: Which tree is central to Battir's historic agricultural landscape?
Olive trees cover large parts of the agricultural terraces in Battir's landscape.
a1-arab-0025: What is the narrow rocky passage leading into the heart of Petra called?
The Siq runs between rock walls to the facade of Al-Khaznah.
a1-arab-0026: What does a visitor see after Petra's narrow passage?
Al-Khaznah's carved facade appears on emerging from the passage.
a1-arab-0027: What color is Petra's rock famous for?
Petra's rocks appear in shades of pink and red.
a1-arab-0028: What decoration covers Qasr Amrah's walls and dome?
Paintings from the Umayyad era cover Qasr Amrah's walls.
a1-arab-0029: What art decorates the floors of Umm ar-Rasas's churches?
Umm ar-Rasas contains mosaic floors depicting cities and landmarks.
a1-arab-0032: Al-Maghtas is on the Jordan River's eastern bank.
a1-arab-0037: Which valley gives its name to a Jordanian reserve near the Dead Sea?
Al-Mujib Reserve takes its name from the valley extending toward the Dead Sea.
a1-arab-0038: Which Jordanian reserve extends between the Ash-Sharah Highlands and Wadi Arabah?
Dana spans a wide range of elevations and ecosystems.
a1-arab-0039: By what other name is historic Ajloun Castle known?
Historic Ajloun Castle is also known as Qal'at ar-Rabad.
a1-arab-0041: On which tool are Jordanian rugs woven?
Weaving threads are stretched on the loom to form the rug.
a1-arab-0042: What is Jordan's well-known national flower?
The black iris is considered Jordan's national flower.
a1-arab-0043: What is the modern name of the Jordanian archaeological site known in classical sources as Pella?
Tabaqat Fahl lies in the northern Jordan Valley and is the site of ancient Pella.
a1-arab-0049: Which archaeological site in Tyre contains a triumphal arch, a colonnaded road and tombs?

Nuh (peace and blessings be upon him) built it at Allah's command.
prophets-0002: Who is called the father of the prophets?
Adam (peace and blessings be upon him)
Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him)
Idris (peace and blessings be upon him)
Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him) is Allah's close friend and the father of the prophets.
prophets-0003: Which prophet was swallowed by the great fish?
Yunus (peace and blessings be upon him)
Yaqub (peace and blessings be upon him)
Zakariyya (peace and blessings be upon him)
Yunus (peace and blessings be upon him), in the story of the great fish.
prophets-0004: Which prophet was sent to the people of Ad?
Hud (peace and blessings be upon him)
Salih (peace and blessings be upon him)
Shuayb (peace and blessings be upon him)
Hud (peace and blessings be upon him) was sent to Ad.
ihist-0001: With which event does the Hijri calendar begin?
It begins with the Prophet's Hijrah (migration).
phys-0002: What is the fastest thing in the universe?
Light is the fastest thing known.
quran-0011: What does al-falaq mean in Surat al-Falaq?
Al-falaq means daybreak: the splitting of darkness to reveal daylight.
prophets-0008: Which prophet was known for patience in adversity?
Ayyub (peace and blessings be upon him)
Sulayman (peace and blessings be upon him)
Idris (peace and blessings be upon him)
Ayyub (peace and blessings be upon him) is an example of patience.
seerah-0010: Which Companion was called the trustworthy one of this ummah (Muslim community)?
Abu Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him.
anim-0008: How many eyes does a bee have?
phys-0004: What do we see in the sky after rain when the sun appears?
bio-0004: Which gas do we breathe to stay alive?
chem-0004: Which gas does fire need to burn?
prophets-0009: Who was the first prophet and the father of humankind?
Adam (peace and blessings be upon him)
Nuh (peace and blessings be upon him)
Shith (peace and blessings be upon him)
Adam (peace and blessings be upon him) was the first human and prophet.
prophets-0011: Which prophet did Allah raise up to Himself?
Isa (peace and blessings be upon him)
Yahya (peace and blessings be upon him)
Zakariyya (peace and blessings be upon him)
Allah raised Isa (peace and blessings be upon him) up to Himself.
cap-0014: What is the capital of Switzerland?
anim-0010: Which animal is called the ship of the desert?
bio-0007: How many teeth are in a complete set for an adult human?
whist-0005: Who is credited with inventing the practical electric light bulb?
prophets-0022: Which prophet spoke as a baby in the cradle?
Isa (peace and blessings be upon him)
Yahya (peace and blessings be upon him)
Ismail (peace and blessings be upon him)
Isa (peace and blessings be upon him): «قال إنّي عبدُ الله» [Indeed, I am the servant of Allāh.].
prophets-0025: Which prophet supplicated: «أنّي مسّني الضرُّ وأنتَ أرحمُ الراحمين» [Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the most merciful of the merciful.]?
Ayyub (peace and blessings be upon him)
Zakariyya (peace and blessings be upon him)
Yaqub (peace and blessings be upon him)
Ayyub (peace and blessings be upon him), during his affliction.
prophets-0028: How many messengers are known as Ulu al-Azm (those of firm resolve), according to the commonly cited view?
Five: Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Isa and Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon them).
seerah-0019: How many years did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) live, according to the commonly cited view?
He (peace and blessings be upon him) lived sixty-three years, according to the commonly cited view.
seerah-0023: How old was the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) when he was commissioned as a prophet?
He (peace and blessings be upon him) was commissioned at forty.
adab-0004: What should you do before entering other people's rooms or homes?
Ask permission and offer the greeting of peace
Seeking permission three times is part of Islamic etiquette that protects people's privacy.
cap-0015: What is the capital of the State of Palestine?
Al-Quds al-Sharif (Jerusalem) is the capital of Palestine.
geo-0014: What is the world's smallest independent state by area and population?
Vatican City lies within Rome, Italy.
chem-0009: Which metal is the only one that is liquid at room temperature?
Mercury is a liquid metal used in thermometers.
amma-0010: Which surah mentions the story of the birds in flocks that destroyed Abrahah's army?
Surat al-Fil tells the story of the protection of the Kabah from Abrahah al-Ashram.
adab-0015: How many times should a Muslim ask permission to enter someone's home before leaving if permission is not granted?
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught us to ask permission three times, emphasizing respect for the privacy of homes.
pal-0001: Which archaeological site represents the oldest known settlement in the Nablus area?
Tell Balata lies east of Nablus and is considered the site of the oldest known settlement in the area. It is also associated with the ancient city of Shechem.
deen-0015: What great sin does Allah never forgive for someone who dies committing it without repentance?
Allah Most High explained that shirk (associating partners with Allah) is the only sin not forgiven if a person does not repent of it before death.
hadith-0004: Complete the Prophet's hadith (peace and blessings be upon him), which shows the importance of cleanliness: «الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ...» [Purity is half of ...]?
Purification means cleanliness and wudu (ablution). It is half of faith because of its great importance in Islam.
prophets-0042: Which prophet did Allah speak to directly, earning him the title Kalim Allah (the one to whom Allah spoke)?
Allah Most High singled out Musa, peace be upon him, by speaking to him without an intermediary. He is therefore called Kalim Allah (the one to whom Allah spoke).
abbas-0004: What great library and translation center was founded in Baghdad and flourished in the Abbasid era?
Bayt al-Hikmah was a beacon of learning and a destination for scholars translating books from other civilizations into Arabic.
ayyub-0004: Which major geographic region did Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi unite with Egypt to form a strong front?
Salah al-Din united Egypt and the Levant under one banner so he could encircle the Crusaders.
amma-0017: Which surah warned against being preoccupied with amassing wealth and boasting about it until death overtakes a person?
The surah explains that competing for and boasting about possessions distracts people until they enter their graves.
umaw-0006: What historical name did Muslims give Spain and Portugal after conquering them in the Umayyad era?
The Iberian Peninsula was known in Islamic history as al-Andalus.
mamluk-0008: In which decisive battle did the Ottomans defeat the Mamluks in Egypt, bringing about the complete fall of their state?
The Battle of al-Raydaniyyah took place near Cairo in 1517 CE and ended the Mamluk era.
othman-0007: Which brilliant architect designed hundreds of great buildings in the Ottoman era, including the Suleymaniye Mosque?
Mimar Sinan is considered the greatest architect in Ottoman history and lived through the reigns of several sultans.
salah-0023: According to most jurists, when may a traveler begin shortening four-rakah prayers?
After leaving the built-up area of their town
Upon deciding to travel while still at home
After a full day of travel

According to the majority, a traveler does not shorten prayer until leaving the inhabited area of their town, because they are legally considered a resident until then. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) shortened prayers when he left Madinah.
ihist-0014: Which blessed city was the Muslims' first qiblah (direction of prayer), before the Kabah?
Muslims prayed toward Al-Aqsa Mosque in al-Quds for several months before Allah commanded them to face the Kabah.
ihist-0016: Which young Umayyad commander conquered Sindh, now Pakistan, and spread Islam there before the age of twenty?
Al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf tasked him with conquering Sindh. He successfully led his army and achieved great victories in the east.
ayyub-0011: Which just ruler united the Levant, commanded Salah al-Din and paved the way for him to liberate Al-Aqsa?
Nur al-Din was a great, ascetic and just leader who laid the foundations of the strength with which Salah al-Din continued his work.
othman-0008: Which emblem appeared on the Ottoman banner and is still used on the flags of Turkey and several Islamic countries?
The crescent and star became the best-known symbol of the Ottoman state and many Islamic countries after it.
quran-0032: According to most jurists, which surah contains two prostrations of recitation?
The Shafiis and Hanbalis count two prostrations in Surat al-Hajj: at verse 18 and verse 77. The Hanafis and Malikis hold that it contains only one, the first.
salah-0027: Which is the only obligatory four-rakah prayer performed at night after the red twilight disappears?
Isha is the only four-rakah prayer whose call is made after darkness begins.
abbas-0014: Which prominent Muslim scholar in the Abbasid era founded algebra and laid the foundations of algorithms?
Al-Khwarizmi founded algebra and worked at Bayt al-Hikmah in Baghdad. Algorithms are named after him.
ayyub-0013: What do we call the invading European armies that occupied Jerusalem and were fought by Salah al-Din al-Ayyubi?
These campaigns were called Crusades because their soldiers adopted the cross as an emblem on their chests and shields.
mamluk-0012: In Mamluk architecture, what is a small building providing free drinking water to passersby called?
The Mamluks took care to build asbilah, the plural of sabil, as charitable works to give people water in the streets of Cairo and elsewhere.
othman-0012: Which sea did Ottoman fleets strongly control to protect the Islamic coasts of North Africa from European attacks?
Thanks to great commanders such as Khayr al-Din Barbarossa, the Ottoman navy gained supremacy in the Mediterranean.
cuis-0011: What cooking method removes air from an impermeable bag containing food, then cooks the food inside the bag?
Sous vide involves vacuum-sealing food in an impermeable bag, then cooking it inside that bag.
salah-0029: What special prayer do we perform on the nights of blessed Ramadan after Isha prayer?
Tarawih (Ramadan night prayer) is an emphasized sunnah (recommended practice), performed in congregation on Ramadan nights to draw closer to Allah and seek its special reward.
salah-0030: How many rakahs are in the emphasized regular sunnah prayers each day and night, for which a house in Paradise is built for whoever maintains them?
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) specified: 4 before Zuhr and 2 after it, 2 after Maghrib, 2 after Isha and 2 before Fajr.
ihist-0021: Which ancient mosque and university was built in Cairo over a thousand years ago and remains a beacon of learning in the Islamic world?
Al-Azhar Mosque was built in 361 AH in the Fatimid era and developed into one of the most important Islamic universities.
abbas-0016: Which official color did the Abbasids adopt for their banners and state clothing?
The Abbasids adopted black as their symbol from the beginning of their revolution and were historically known as al-Musawwidah (those who wear black).
mamluk-0017: In which battle did Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun lead his army to decisively defeat the Tatars in the Levant in 702 AH, with Imam Ibn Taymiyyah participating?
The Battle of Shaqhab completely ended the Mongol threat to the Levant. Ibn Taymiyyah played a prominent role in encouraging the troops and participating.
adab-0030: According to Islamic etiquette, what should you do when someone else speaks to you?
Listening well without interrupting is among the most important Islamic manners of conversation and company, out of respect for the speaker.
ihist-0025: Which decisive battle did Tariq ibn Ziyad lead in 92 AH, bringing down the Visigothic kingdom and beginning the conquest of al-Andalus?
The Battle of Wadi Lakkah, or Shadhunah, was the major confrontation in which Muslims defeated King Roderic, after which al-Andalus was conquered.
ayyub-0018: Which treacherous Crusader prince of Karak did Salah al-Din swear to kill personally because he attacked caravans of unarmed Muslim pilgrims?
Arnat broke agreements and attacked Muslim trading caravans and pilgrims. Salah al-Din fulfilled his oath and killed him after his capture at Hattin.
mamluk-0018: Which animals did the Mamluks train to ride skillfully for fighting in battle?
The Mamluks were cavalrymen rigorously trained in horsemanship, riding and using weapons.
othman-0017: Which massive Byzantine landmark in Istanbul did Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror turn into a great mosque upon entering the city?
Hagia Sophia was the greatest Byzantine church. Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror prayed there and made it a congregational mosque for Muslims.
othman-0018: Which high Ottoman administrative title was granted to senior military commanders, ministers and provincial governors?
Pasha was one of the highest honorary ranks in the Ottoman state, applied to senior officials and commanders to distinguish them.
chatgpt-geography-005: Which warm ocean current carries water from the Gulf of Mexico region across the North Atlantic?
The Gulf Stream is a strong warm current originating in the Gulf of Mexico region and flowing across the North Atlantic.
chatgpt3-world-history-002: Which two brothers achieved the first successful controlled flight of a powered aircraft in 1903?
Wilbur and Orville Wright achieved a successful controlled flight at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, in 1903.
gemini-quran-001: In which blessed Hijri month did the Quran begin to be revealed to the heart of Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him)?
Allah Most High says: ﴿شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ﴾ [The month of Ramaḍān [is that] in which was revealed the Qur’ān].
gemini-juz-tabarak-005: In Surat al-Qiyamah, Allah swears by the Day of Resurrection and a soul that continually blames its owner for shortcomings. Which soul is it?

Allah Most High says: ﴿وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ﴾ [And I swear by the reproaching soul[1800] [to the certainty of resurrection].]. It is the believer's soul that blames them for committing sins and neglecting obedience.
gemini-adhkar-005: Which transmitted supplication is said when entering graveyards to visit the dead and remember the Hereafter?
Allahumma ajirni fi musibati wa-khluf li khayran minha (O Allah, reward me in my affliction and replace it with something better)
Inna lillahi wa-inna ilayhi rajiun, Allahumma ajirni (We belong to Allah and to Him we return; O Allah, reward me)
As-salamu alaykum dara qawmin muminin, wa-inna in sha Allahu bikum lahiqun (Peace be upon you, abode of believing people. Allah willing, we will join you)
Subhana alladhi amata wa-ahya wa-huwa ala kulli shayin qadir (Glory be to Him who causes death and gives life, and who has power over all things)
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) taught his Companions this supplication to greet the dead, pray for their forgiveness and remember their own eventual fate.
gemini-prophets-003: Where did Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, flee from Pharaoh's oppression and work as a shepherd for several years before being entrusted with his mission?
Musa headed to Madyan after leaving Egypt in fear. He married the righteous man's daughter and worked for him as a shepherd.
gemini-islamic-history-002: Which famous Muslim traveler journeyed across the Islamic world for nearly thirty years and documented his travels in a book?
Ibn Battutah is the most famous Arab and Muslim traveler. His book Tuhfat al-Nuzzar is a major historical and geographical document.
gemini-islamic-history-003: Which ancient Islamic university was founded by Fatimah al-Fihriyyah in Fez, Morocco?
Fatimah al-Fihriyyah founded Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque in 245 AH. It developed into one of the world's oldest continuously operating universities.
gemini-islamic-history-004: What do historians call the great scholarly movement that transferred Greek and Persian learning into Arabic?
The translation movement peaked in the Abbasid era, when major scientific works were translated into Arabic, initiating a scientific renaissance.
gemini-rashidun-003: Who was the first caliph in Islamic history to be addressed as Amir al-Muminin (Commander of the Faithful)?
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him
Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him
Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him
Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him

Abu Bakr was called the successor of Allah's Messenger. When Umar took office, people said the successor of the successor of Allah's Messenger, then agreed to call him Amir al-Muminin (Commander of the Faithful).
gemini-umayyad-001: Which color distinguished the Umayyad state's banners and served as its official symbol on ceremonial occasions?
The Umayyads adopted white for their banners and clothing at official state occasions.
gemini-abbasid-001: Which profession flourished in Baghdad because of the abundance of books and libraries in the Abbasid era?
Wiraqah means copying and selling books. It flourished in Baghdad because of its many libraries and the translation and authorship movement.
gemini-abbasid-002: Which wife of Caliph Harun al-Rashid became renowned for building a pilgrimage route with wells and rest stops?
Zubaydah spent great sums preparing the pilgrimage route from Iraq to Makkah, which became known as Darb Zubaydah.
gemini-abbasid-003: Which main language was used for the most important scientific and medical books in the Abbasid era and became the language of science?
Thanks to the flourishing translation and research movement in Baghdad, Arabic became the language of science and philosophy in the advanced world of that time.
gemini-abbasid-004: Which high political office did the Abbasids introduce, making its holder the second-ranking figure in the state and an assistant to the caliph?
The Abbasids introduced the vizierate so the vizier could assist the caliph in governing and administering the state bureaus.
gemini-mamluk-004: Which devastating worldwide epidemic swept through the Mamluk state in 1347 CE, killing vast numbers of residents and soldiers?
