Known as the Black Death, it swept through Egypt and the Levant in 1347 CE, killing vast numbers of residents and soldiers.
gemini-mamluk-005: Which global economic event in 1498 CE dealt a crushing blow to the Mamluk state's economy?
The Nile drying up for years
The Portuguese discovery of the Cape of Good Hope route
The burning of Fustat's great markets
The discovery of this sea route around Africa diverted world trade away from Egypt, depriving the Mamluks of customs revenue.
gemini-ottoman-001: Which enormous destructive weapon did Sultan Mehmed the Conqueror use to break down Constantinople's fortified walls?
The Conqueror enlisted engineers to make unprecedentedly large cannons to batter the strong Byzantine walls.
gemini-ottoman-003: Which large region of Eastern Europe did the Ottomans rule for centuries and spread Islam in?
The Ottomans controlled the Balkans, including Bosnia and Albania, establishing Islamic administration and civilization there for centuries.
gemini-ottoman-004: In which beautiful Islamic art did the Ottomans excel, using it extensively to copy Qurans and decorate their mosques?
The Ottomans excelled in developing Arabic scripts, such as Thuluth and Diwani, and used them to decorate mosques and manuscripts beautifully.
chatgpt4-world-history-003: In which city did Bayt al-Hikmah flourish as a center of translation and learning in the Abbasid era?
Bayt al-Hikmah was associated with Baghdad and a broad movement to translate knowledge into Arabic in the Abbasid era.
chatgpt4-cuisine-009: Food continuing to rise in temperature and cook slightly after removal from the heat
Heat stored in the outer portions continues moving inward after cooking stops.
chatgpt4-cuisine-010: Why is the surface of a bread loaf slashed before putting it in the oven?
To stop the yeast from working completely
To guide dough expansion and steam release at specific points
To cool the center of the loaf immediately
Slashes allow bread to expand in an orderly way and reduce random tearing of the crust.
gemini2-deen-003: What is the tree cursed in the Quran that is food for the people of Hell?
Allah Most High says: ﴿إِنَّ شَجَرَتَ الزَّقُّومِ * طَعَامُ الْأَثِيمِ﴾ [Indeed, the tree of zaqqūm / Is food for the sinful.]. In Surat al-Isra, He calls it the tree cursed in the Quran.
gemini2-prayer-001: A traveler prays behind a resident imam performing four rakahs. According to most jurists, what must the traveler do?
Shorten it to two and end before the imam
Pray alone rather than join him
Join, then intend to separate after two rakahs

According to the majority, a traveler must complete the prayer when following a resident, as Ibn Abbas said when asked: «تلك السُّنّة» [That is the sunnah (Prophetic practice)]. Following the imam takes precedence over the concession to shorten prayer.
gemini2-prayer-006: According to most jurists, what travel distance permits shortening prayers?
Any departure from home, however short
Prayers may be shortened only during Hajj

The majority, the Malikis, Shafiis and Hanbalis, set the distance at four burud, roughly eighty kilometers. The Hanafis hold that it is three days' travel at a camel's pace. The matter is disputed, with no consensus.
gemini2-prayer-009: A latecomer joins the imam in the final tashahhud. According to most jurists, has he caught Jumuah, or must he perform Zuhr?
He has not caught Jumuah and completes four rakahs as Zuhr
He has caught Jumuah and completes two rakahs
He starts Jumuah again with others

According to the majority, whoever catches one rakah of Jumuah (Friday prayer) completes it as Jumuah; whoever catches less completes four as Zuhr. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «من أدركَ ركعةً من الصلاةِ فقد أدركَ الصلاة» [Whoever catches one rakah of the prayer has caught the prayer].
gemini2-prayer-010: According to the Hanbalis and Hanafis, what is the ruling on the first tashahhud in three- and four-rakah prayers?
Obligatory, with prostrations of forgetfulness compensating for accidental omission
A pillar whose omission always invalidates prayer
Recommended, with no prostrations of forgetfulness prescribed
Permissible, with no reward for performing it

The Hanbalis and Hanafis hold that the first tashahhud (testimony recitation) is obligatory and compensated for by prostrations of forgetfulness. The Malikis and Shafiis hold that it is recommended. When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) stood up without the first tashahhud, he made two prostrations and did not repeat the prayer.
gemini2-prayer-012: According to most jurists, how does deliberately eating during prayer differ from eating forgetfully?
Deliberate eating invalidates prayer; a small amount eaten forgetfully does not
Both prayers are valid and nothing is required
The deliberate eater prostrates for forgetfulness; the forgetful eater repeats the prayer
Deliberate eating and drinking contradict the form of prayer and invalidate it. A small amount eaten forgetfully does not invalidate it according to most jurists, since forgetfulness is excused.
gemini2-prayer-015: A man is certain he performed wudu, then doubts whether it was invalidated. According to most jurists, what should he rely on?
Rely on his certainty of purity and pray in that state
He must repeat wudu as a precaution
Repeat the prayer after performing wudu

The majority's principle is that certainty is not removed by doubt. Whoever is certain of purity but doubts an invalidating occurrence remains pure. Regarding someone who feels something during prayer, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «لا ينصرفْ حتّى يسمعَ صوتًا أو يجدَ ريحًا» [He should not leave (his prayer) unless he hears a sound or perceives a smell.].
gemini2-prayer-017: How many rakahs are in Asr prayer?
Asr consists of four obligatory rakahs (prayer units).
gemini2-quran-003: In Quranic studies, what are Makkan surahs?
The correct criterion for Makkan revelation is that it preceded the Prophet's Hijrah (migration), even if revealed outside Makkah.
gemini2-juz-amma-004: What is the difficult pass mentioned in Surat al-Balad that Allah urges people to cross?
Freeing a slave or feeding people on a day of severe hunger

Allah Most High says: فما اقتحم العقبة * وما أدراك ما العقبة * فك رقبة أو إطعام... [But he has not broken through the difficult pass.[1926] / And what can make you know what is [breaking through] the difficult pass? / It is the freeing of a slave / Or feeding...].
gemini2-juz-tabarak-015: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah heard the Quran and admired it, then told his people: «إنْ هذا إلّا سِحرٌ يُؤثَر» [This is not but magic imitated [from others].]. Verses threatening him with Saqar were then revealed. In which surah?

These words of Allah Most High were revealed about him in Surat al-Muddaththir: ﴿فَقَالَ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾ [And said, "This is not but magic imitated [from others].] ﴿إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلَّا قَوْلُ ٱلْبَشَرِ﴾ [This is not but the word of a human being."] ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾ [I will drive him into Saqar.[1793]].
gemini2-adhkar-008: When does the time for reciting morning adhkar (remembrances) begin?
The preferred morning time for reciting adhkar (remembrances) begins at dawn.
gemini2-seerah-003: What was the first major battle in which Muslims defeated Quraysh despite being outnumbered?
It occurred in the second year after the Hijrah (migration) and distinguished truth from falsehood.
gemini2-seerah-010: Which battle took place immediately after the conquest of Makkah, when Muslims were initially impressed by their numbers but later won?
Allah Most High says: ويوم حنين إذ أعجبتكم كثرتكم [and [even] on the day of Ḥunayn, when your great number pleased you].
gemini2-manners-020: Riya is dangerous and nullifies deeds. What does it mean?
Performing worship so people see and praise it
Doing worldly work well, sincerely for Allah
Abandoning good deeds for fear of people's comments
Riya (showing off in worship) is minor shirk (associating partners with Allah), because it combines the intention of pleasing people with worship of Allah.
gemini2-islamic-history-010: Which great commander led the conquests in Transoxiana, now Uzbekistan and surrounding areas?
Qutaybah was one of the greatest commanders of the conquests in the Islamic east.
gemini2-islamic-history-016: How many years did the Rashidun Caliphate last, as stated in the hadith?

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «الخلافةُ في أمّتي ثلاثونَ سنة، ثمّ مُلكٌ بعدَ ذلك» [The caliphate in my ummah (community) will last thirty years, followed by kingship]. It was completed by the caliphate of al-Hasan ibn Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both.
gemini2-islamic-history-017: Which large Arab tribe controlled Makkah before Islam?
Quraysh was the Prophet's tribe (peace and blessings be upon him), dominant in Makkah and among the Arab tribes.
gemini2-hadith-003: Who first compiled the Prophetic sunnah under an official order from Caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz?

Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz wrote to the provinces ordering the collection of the Prophet's hadiths (peace and blessings be upon him), fearing their loss. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri was the first to compile them in response.
gemini2-hadith-019: What does muttafaq alayh (agreed upon) mean at the end of a hadith citation?
Reported by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi
Agreed upon by all the Companions
Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim from the same Companion
Reported by Malik and Ahmad in their books
This term is shorthand for reported by the two shaykhs, al-Bukhari and Muslim.
gemini2-rashidun-008: What document did Umar ibn al-Khattab give the people of Jerusalem upon its conquest?

In it he guaranteed the people of Aelia safety for themselves, their churches and their crosses, pledging that the churches would neither be occupied nor demolished. It is one of the best-known documents of tolerance.
gemini2-umayyad-006: Which Muslim commander crossed the sea to conquer al-Andalus in the Umayyad era?
He crossed the strait in 92 AH to conquer al-Andalus, and the strait was named after him.
gemini2-umayyad-007: Under which Umayyad caliph did the state reach its greatest extent, from the borders of China to al-Andalus?
His reign was the golden age of the great Umayyad conquests in the east and west.
gemini2-umayyad-020: What was the military system Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan adopted for regular raids and campaigns against the Byzantines to protect the borders throughout the year?
He organized continuous summer and winter campaigns to wear down the Byzantines and secure the frontier.
gemini2-abbasid-009: Which physician and translator headed the translation movement and translated Greek medical books into Arabic?
Hunayn ibn Ishaq al-Ibadi mastered Greek, Syriac and Arabic, translated Galen and Hippocrates, and oversaw translation at Bayt al-Hikmah.
gemini2-abbasid-010: After Baghdad fell, which Mamluk sultan nominally revived the Abbasid Caliphate in Cairo?
Al-Zahir Baybars summoned a surviving Abbasid prince and pledged allegiance to him as caliph to legitimize Mamluk rule.
gemini2-abbasid-016: Which blind poet of the Abbasid era wrote Risalat al-Ghufran and Luzum Ma La Yalzam?
Abu al-Ala Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Maarri called himself the prisoner of two confinements: blindness and his home.
gemini2-abbasid-017: What was the devastating revolt led by enslaved people in southern Iraq that lasted a long time and exhausted the Abbasid state called?
It was led by someone who claimed descent from the Prophet's family, and its participants wreaked havoc for years.
gemini2-abbasid-018: The famous Battle of Dandanqan led to the rise of which powerful state, nominally subject to the Abbasid Caliphate?
The Seljuks won under Tughril Beg and established their great empire.
gemini2-abbasid-020: What prepared road linked Baghdad to Makkah to serve pilgrims and was named after Harun al-Rashid's wife?
Zubaydah, al-Rashid's wife, took care to pave the route and dig wells for pilgrims.
gemini2-ayyubid-008: What hospital did Salah al-Din establish in Cairo to treat patients free of charge?
Salah al-Din established it in the former Fatimid caliphal residence and endowed it so the poor could be treated free of charge.
gemini2-ayyubid-018: Which scholar and judge accompanied Salah al-Din for years and wrote his detailed biography in Al-Nawadir al-Sultaniyyah?
He was the army's judge and a constant companion of Salah al-Din, recording the events of his life and death accurately.
gemini2-mamluk-005: Which scholar issued a ruling to fight the Mongols, encouraged the army and attended the Battle of Shaqhab?
Ibn Taymiyyah went to urge the sultan into action, ruled that fighting the Tatars was obligatory even if they professed Islam, and attended the battle in 702 AH.
gemini2-mamluk-007: What famous cry did Sultan Qutuz utter at Ayn Jalut to encourage his retreating soldiers?
Ya khayla Allahi irkabi (O cavalry of Allah, ride forth)
Labbayka Allahumma labbayk (Here I am, O Allah, here I am)
He threw down his helmet and shouted Wa Islamah (O Islam!), inspiring his army to return to the attack.
gemini2-mamluk-008: Historically, the long Mamluk era is divided into which two states or periods?
The Bahri Mamluk state and the Burji Mamluk state
They were named for the locations of their military barracks, on the Nile and in the towers, and for their ethnic origins.
gemini2-mamluk-017: Which office was responsible for writing the sultan's letters and the Mamluk state's records?
The Katib al-Sirr headed the chancery, read incoming correspondence to the sultan and wrote his replies. Al-Qalqashandi was one of its scribes.
gemini2-mamluk-018: How did power and rule usually pass among the Mamluks?
By strict inheritance to the eldest son
To the militarily strongest emir: rule belonged to the victor
By direct appointment from the Abbasid caliph
Their political principle was that power was seized by force and control of the army.
gemini2-ottoman-005: Which sultan was famous for categorically refusing to sell Palestinian land to the Zionist movement despite offers to pay the state's debts?
His famous historical position was to refuse to cede any part of Palestine because it belonged to the Islamic ummah (community).
gemini2-ottoman-010: How were the Janissaries finally eliminated after becoming a source of continual revolt?
Through a long civil war lasting years
In the Auspicious Incident, when their barracks were bombarded and they were wiped out
Through a popular referendum and trials of their commanders
Sultan Mahmud II ordered artillery to destroy their barracks in 1826 CE, in what was called the Auspicious Incident.
gemini-deen-b2-016: Zakah is giving a portion of one's wealth to the (___) and the needy.
Zakah (obligatory almsgiving) is a financial right Allah assigned to the poor.
gemini-prayer-b2-005: According to most jurists, what is the ruling on prostrating when reciting a verse of prostration outside prayer?
Obligatory, with sin for omitting it

According to the majority, the Malikis, Shafiis and Hanbalis, prostration of recitation is a sunnah (recommended practice). Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said on the pulpit: «إنّ اللهَ لم يفرِضِ السجودَ إلّا أن نشاء» [Indeed, Allah did not make such prostration (of recitation) obligatory; we can do it if we wish to do so.]. The Hanafis hold it obligatory, so the matter is disputed.
gemini-prayer-b2-015: A latecomer finds the imam bowing, says the takbir and bows with him before the imam raises his head. According to most jurists, does that rakah count?
No, he must make it up
It counts if he recited all of Al-Fatihah before bowing
It counts in voluntary but not obligatory prayers

Most jurists hold that catching the bowing with the imam means catching the rakah (prayer unit), and reciting Al-Fatihah in that rakah is waived. They cite Abu Bakrah's hadith: he bowed before reaching the row, and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «زادكَ اللهُ حِرصًا ولا تَعُدْ» [May Allah increase your keenness, but do not do that again.], without ordering him to make it up. Some scholars disagreed and required that rakah to be made up.
gemini-prayer-b2-017: In which two prayers is recitation quiet?
Quranic verses are recited quietly in the daytime prayers, Zuhr and Asr.
gemini-prayer-b2-019: According to most jurists, how long may a resident wipe over khuffs (leather footwear)?
Without limit as long as they are worn

Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) allowed three days and nights for a traveler and one day and night for a resident. This is the majority view. The Malikis hold that wiping has no time limit, so the matter is disputed.
gemini-quran-b2-003: What do tartil and tajwid of the Quran mean?
Giving letters their proper articulation and qualities, and beautifying the voice
Tartil (measured recitation) means reading slowly, articulating letters clearly and reflecting on meanings.
gemini-quran-b2-017: Which surah is called Surat al-Nisa al-Sughra?
Surat at-Talaq contains detailed rulings concerning women, such as iddah (the waiting period).
gemini-quran-b2-019: إِنَّ بَطْشَ رَبِّكَ لَشَدِيدٌ [Indeed, the assault [i.e., vengeance] of your Lord is severe.]
إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُّبِينًا [Indeed, We have given you, [O Muḥammad], a clear conquest[1507]]
لَيْسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ [Of it, [from those] besides Allāh, there is no remover.]
أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ [Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?]
The first verse of Surat al-Fath is ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُّبِينًا﴾ [Indeed, We have given you, [O Muḥammad], a clear conquest[1507]].
gemini-juz-tabarak-b2-001: Early in Islam, Allah revealed to His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) the command to stand in prayer all night except a little. The obligation was eased at the end of the same surah. Which surah is it?

The beginning of Surat al-Muzzammil states ﴿قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا﴾ [Arise [to pray] the night, except for a little -]. The easing comes at its end: ﴿۞ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَعْلَمُ أَنَّكَ تَقُومُ أَدْنَىٰ مِن ثُلُثَىِ ٱلَّيْلِ وَنِصْفَهُۥ وَثُلُثَهُۥ وَطَآئِفَةٌ مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَعَكَ ۚ وَٱللَّهُ يُقَدِّرُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ ۚ عَلِمَ أَن لَّن تُحْصُوهُ فَتَابَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنَ ٱلْقُرْءَانِ ۚ عَلِمَ أَن سَيَكُونُ مِنكُم مَّرْضَىٰ ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يَضْرِبُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ يَبْتَغُونَ مِن فَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ ۙ وَءَاخَرُونَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ فَٱقْرَءُوا۟ مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ ۚ وَأَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتُوا۟ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَقْرِضُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا ۚ وَمَا تُقَدِّمُوا۟ لِأَنفُسِكُم مِّنْ خَيْرٍ تَجِدُوهُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرًا وَأَعْظَمَ أَجْرًا ۚ وَٱسْتَغْفِرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌۢ﴾ [Indeed, your Lord knows, [O Muḥammad], that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allāh determines [the extent of] the night and the day. He has known that you [Muslims] will not be able to do it[1785] and has turned to you in forgiveness, so recite what is easy [for you] of the Qur’ān. He has known that there will be among you those who are ill and others traveling throughout the land seeking [something] of the bounty of Allāh and others fighting for the cause of Allāh. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakāh and loan Allāh a goodly loan.[1786] And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allāh. It is better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Merciful.], at the words فاقرءوا ما تيسّرَ منه [So recite what is easy from it].
gemini-juz-tabarak-b2-008: In Surat al-Qalam, Allah forbids His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to obey a man described by nine vile traits, including habitual worthless swearing, slander and spreading gossip. Who is meant, according to most commentators?

Allah Most High says ﴿وَلَا تُطِعْ كُلَّ حَلَّافٍ مَّهِينٍ﴾ [And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer] ﴿هَمَّازٍ مَّشَّآءٍۭ بِنَمِيمٍ﴾ [[And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -]. Most commentators favor al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, while another view identifies al-Akhnas ibn Shariq.
gemini-juz-tabarak-b2-014: In Surat al-Muddaththir, how many angels are assigned to guard Hell, Saqar?
Allah Most High says: عليها تسعة عشر [Over it are nineteen [angels].].
gemini-juz-tabarak-b2-019: According to the best-known interpretation, what does (الْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا) [By those [winds] sent forth in gusts] at the beginning of Surat al-Mursalat mean?
Most commentators interpret it as winds following one another like the hairs of a horse's mane.
gemini-adhkar-b2-009: On hearing thunder, the Companions would say: Subhana alladhi yusabbihu ar-radu bihamdihi wa... (Glory be to Him whom thunder glorifies with His praise, and ...)
The mountains in awe of Him
The angels in fear of Him
The earth in dread of Him
This dhikr (remembrance) is drawn from the Quranic verse and is the transmitted remembrance for thunder.
gemini-adhkar-b2-019: What is the best phrase to say to someone who has done you a service or helped you, to repay them?
Yatik al-afiyah (May you be granted well-being)
Jazaka Allahu khayran (May Allah reward you with good)
Tislam yadak (May your hands be safe)

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: من صُنع إليه معروف فقال: جزاك الله خيراً فقد أبلغ في الثناء [Whoever has a favor done for him and says, Jazaka Allahu khayran (May Allah reward you with good), has offered the fullest praise].
gemini-prophets-b2-009: How many actions did Musa, peace be upon him, object to during his journey with his companion, as related in Surat al-Kahf?
He objected to damaging the ship, then killing the boy, then rebuilding the wall without payment. The third led to their separation.
gemini-manners-b2-005: What virtue means being fully content with the sustenance and life Allah has allotted, without coveting what others possess?
Contentment is richness of the soul and brings lasting happiness and satisfaction.
gemini-islamic-history-b2-005: Which Muslim thinker and scholar is considered the first founder of human sociology and wrote Al-Muqaddimah?
Abd al-Rahman ibn Khaldun laid the foundations and principles of the science of human civilization.
gemini-islamic-history-b2-010: Which European island did Muslims rule and build a great civilization on before the Normans arrived?
The Islamic Emirate of Sicily contributed greatly to transmitting civilization to Europe.
gemini-islamic-history-b2-014: Which scholar founded algebra in mathematics and had his works transmitted to Europe?
Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi wrote Al-Jabr wa al-Muqabalah.
gemini-islamic-history-b2-016: Which animal was widely used to carry goods and messages in the desert and called the ship of the desert?
Camels were very important in the Muslim economy and conquests.
gemini-islamic-history-b2-020: Which scholar and musician moved to al-Andalus, added a fifth string to the oud and influenced clothing and table etiquette?
Ziryab brought eastern refinement to Cordoba and established a school of art and ways of life there.
gemini-hadith-b2-005: An invented lie falsely attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)
A report agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim
A mawdu (fabricated) hadith is the worst type of rejected report. It may not be mentioned except to warn against it.
gemini-rashidun-b2-008: Which woman claimed prophethood during the Ridda wars and married Musaylimah the Liar?
Sajah bint al-Harith, of Banu Tamim, claimed prophethood and then allied with Musaylimah. She returned to Islam after his death.
gemini-rashidun-b2-011: Which caliph patrolled at night to inspect his subjects' conditions and personally feed their poor?
Umar was known for justice and a strong sense of responsibility toward his subjects.
gemini-umayyad-b2-002: Which governor established the first Islamic naval fleet under Uthman and later became the first Umayyad caliph?
Uthman allowed Muawiyah to establish the fleet during his reign. Muawiyah later became the first Umayyad caliph.
gemini-umayyad-b2-015: Marwan ibn al-Hakam is considered the second founder of the Umayyad state after Yazid's death. He united the Umayyad house following a conference in which place?
At al-Jabiyah, the Umayyads pledged allegiance to Marwan ibn al-Hakam and united to save the collapsing state.
gemini-umayyad-b2-018: Al-Farazdaq, Jarir and al-Akhtal were among the most famous:
Poets of invective exchanges in the Umayyad era
Invective exchanges in poetry flourished in the Umayyad era, and these three became famous for them.
gemini-abbasid-b2-007: What was the official color of the Abbasid Caliphate's banners and clothing?
They adopted black as their emblem and became known as al-Musawwidah (those who wear black).
gemini-abbasid-b2-010: Why was the Abbasid Muslim scholar Jabir ibn Hayyan called the father of chemistry?
He established a precise experimental method in the laboratory
He developed experimental chemistry in place of ancient mythical alchemy.
gemini-abbasid-b2-013: Which Islamic group in the Abbasid era gave reason and logic precedence over transmitted texts in interpreting beliefs and was influenced by philosophy?
The Mutazilah applied reason to beliefs and adopted the view that the Quran was created.
gemini-ayyubid-b2-005: Which major historian wrote the encyclopedia Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh and lived through and documented the Crusades?
Izz al-Din ibn al-Athir al-Jazari is considered the primary reference for that important period.
gemini-mamluk-b2-005: Who was the historian of Egypt and its capital Cairo in the Mamluk era who wrote the great Al-Khitat al-Maqriziyyah?
Al-Maqrizi left the greatest topographical and historical description of Cairo and its institutions.
gemini-mamluk-b2-008: Which global trade did the Mamluks monopolize as a major source of wealth before the Cape of Good Hope route was discovered?
They imposed high customs duties on spices passing through Egypt and the Levant to Europe.
gemini-mamluk-b2-009: Which mosque and school, a vast architectural masterpiece, was built by a young sultan in Cairo to accommodate the four schools of law?
Sultan Hasan Mosque is one of the greatest and largest Islamic buildings.
gemini-mamluk-b2-020: A two-story Mamluk charitable building provided drinking water below and a kuttab above. What was the kuttab for?
Teaching orphaned children the Quran and calligraphy
The two were built together as an integrated charitable endowment, serving the body with water and the spirit with learning.
gemini-ottoman-b2-002: Which was the first major city the Ottomans under Orhan ibn Osman conquered and made their capital in Anatolia?
Bursa marked the true emergence of the state as a political and commercial entity.
gemini-ottoman-b2-008: In which decisive battle in 1526 CE did Suleiman the Magnificent crush the Hungarian army in just two hours?
The Battle of Mohacs led to the collapse of the Kingdom of Hungary and Ottoman control over Central Europe.
gemini-ottoman-b2-013: Which fortified island did the Ottomans try to conquer in its Great Siege of 1565 CE, withdrawing after the Knights of St John defended it desperately?
The Siege of Malta was a turning point that halted Ottoman naval expansion toward the western Mediterranean.
gemini-ottoman-b2-017: Which luxurious modern palace was built on the Bosporus in a European-influenced style and became the residence of later sultans?
Dolmabahce Palace, on the Bosporus, was built in the European style, and later sultans moved there.
gemini-prayer-b3-014: According to most jurists, what is the ruling on combining two prayers while traveling?
Permissible as a concession, at the earlier or later prayer time
Permissible only at Arafah and Muzdalifah

According to the majority, a traveler may combine prayers at the earlier or later time as a concession, not an obligation. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) combined prayers while traveling. The Hanafis disallow combining except at Arafah and Muzdalifah, so it is incorrect to claim consensus.
gemini-prayer-b3-017: Which phrase is added to the Fajr adhan and not said in other calls to prayer?
As-salatu khayrun min an-nawm (Prayer is better than sleep)
Qad qamati as-salah (The prayer has begun)
Allahu akbaru kabira (Allah is supremely great)
It is called tathwib (the added call) and is said twice to wake sleepers for prayer.
gemini-prayer-b3-020: According to most jurists, what does the hadith «وبيوتُهنَّ خيرٌ لهنَّ» [and their homes are better for them] show concerning women's prayer?
Praying at home is better for her, but she must not be barred from the mosque if she seeks permission
Entering the mosque is always forbidden for her
Her prayer at the mosque is invalid
Congregational prayer is obligatory for her as for a man

The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «لا تمنعوا نساءَكم المساجدَ، وبيوتُهنَّ خيرٌ لهنَّ» [Do not prevent your women from the mosques, and their homes are better for them]. This both states what is better for her and forbids barring her. The hadith establishes preference, not prohibition.
gemini-quran-b3-014: Aws ibn al-Samit declared zihar against his wife. She came to complain to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and plead with him. Allah then revealed the opening of which surah, mentioning that He heard her complaint?

The opening of Surat al-Mujadilah, ﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوْلَ ٱلَّتِى تُجَـٰدِلُكَ فِى زَوْجِهَا وَتَشْتَكِىٓ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱللَّهُ يَسْمَعُ تَحَاوُرَكُمَآ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌۢ بَصِيرٌ﴾ [Certainly has Allāh heard the speech of the one who argues [i.e., pleads] with you, [O Muḥammad], concerning her husband and directs her complaint to Allāh. And Allāh hears your dialogue; indeed, Allāh is Hearing and Seeing.], was revealed concerning Khawlah bint Thalabah, may Allah be pleased with her. Zihar is a declaration likening one's wife to a permanently forbidden female relative.
gemini-quran-b3-020: The portion of the Quran from Surat Yunus through Surat an-Nahl consists mainly of surahs known as:
Al-Miun are surahs of around one hundred verses, coming after al-Tiwal.
gemini-juz-amma-b3-008: In Surat az-Zalzalah, what does the earth do on the Day of Resurrection?
Speak, bringing forth its burdens and reports
Allah Most High says: يومئذ تحدث أخبارها [That Day, it will report its news].
gemini-juz-amma-b3-009: What does sijjil mean in Surat al-Fil?
ترميهم بحجارة من سجيل [Striking them with stones of hard clay,] means baked clay like stone.
gemini-juz-amma-b3-019: Which short surah is called the foundation of religion and one-third of the Quran because it is devoted to explaining the attributes of Allah, the One?
It is called Al-Ikhlas because it is devoted to describing ar-Rahman (the Most Merciful) and frees its reciter from shirk (associating partners with Allah).
gemini-juz-tabarak-b3-017: In Surat Nuh, what did Nuh promise his people if they sought their Lord's forgiveness?
He would send abundant rain and increase their wealth and children
He would make them kings of the earth
He would remove the duty of prayer
He would give them rivers of honey
He said: يرسل السماء عليكم مدراراً * ويمددكم بأموال وبنين... [He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers / And give you increase in wealth and children...].
gemini-seerah-b3-008: In which battle were many polytheists captured, some ransoming themselves by teaching Muslim boys to read and write?
This great incident at Badr shows Islam's high regard for learning and literacy.
gemini-seerah-b3-018: In which battle did the Jews of Banu Qurayzah break their treaty and ally with the confederates to betray the Muslims from within?
Their betrayal came at the most difficult point of the siege, so they were punished severely after the battle.
gemini-manners-b3-018: In Islam, what is the best response when someone privately advises you about a mistake you made?
Publicize their advice and complain about them
Accept their advice, thank them and reflect quietly
Quarrel with them and accuse them of jealousy
Private advice expresses love and protects one's dignity. A believer is their fellow believer's mirror and accepts the truth.
gemini-islamic-history-b3-004: In which Islamic period did the idea of an Islamic naval fleet seriously take shape to fight the Byzantines?
Uthman ibn Affan's reign, through Muawiyah's efforts
Muawiyah urged Umar, who refused because of the sea's dangers. Uthman later agreed, and the fleet was built.
gemini-islamic-history-b3-005: Who were the mawali in early Islamic history, in the Umayyad and Abbasid eras?
Only enslaved people sold in markets
Non-Arab Muslims affiliated with Arab tribes
They played a tremendous civilizational, scholarly and administrative role in the Umayyad and Abbasid eras.
gemini-islamic-history-b3-012: What great palace did Muslims build in Granada in al-Andalus that is considered an enduring masterpiece of Islamic architecture?
The Nasrid dynasty built the Alhambra in Granada. It remains a historical and tourist jewel today.
gemini-islamic-history-b3-020: What is the waqf system that Islamic civilization used to fund schools, hospitals and mosques for centuries?
Preserving an asset and permanently directing its income to charity
Collecting daily donations in the streets
Waqf (charitable endowment), an institutional form of ongoing charity, is the secret behind the independence and continuity of scholarly and medical institutions.
gemini-hadith-b3-005: What does ilm al-rijal, or al-jarh wa al-tadil, in hadith studies examine?
The number of words in a hadith
Narrators' lives, memory and honesty to assess whether their hadiths are accepted
Without this science of narrator criticism and accreditation, narrators' lies or errors would have entered religion as if they were part of it.
gemini-hadith-b3-015: The Six Books considered the principal collections of the Prophetic sunnah are the two Sahihs and ...
Sunan Abi Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasai and Ibn Majah
Muwatta Malik, Musnad Ahmad, Sunan al-Darimi and Al-Sunan al-Kubra
Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah, Sahih Ibn Hibban, Al-Mustadrak and Al-Mujam
Musannaf Abd al-Razzaq, Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah, Al-Sunan al-Sughra and Al-Mujam al-Kabir
These six books are the most important and most relied upon collections for deriving rulings and transmitting the sunnah (Prophetic practice).
gemini-umayyad-b3-002: What tax was collected from protected non-Muslim subjects in return for protection and exemption from military service?
Jizyah (poll tax) is levied on eligible protected non-Muslim individuals; kharaj (land tax) on agricultural land; and ushr (tithe) on Muslim land.
gemini-umayyad-b3-005: Tariq ibn Ziyad conquered al-Andalus and crossed the strait named after him. Who was his superior and the governor of Ifriqiyah who planned the conquest?
Musa ibn Nusayr planned the conquest of the far Maghreb and al-Andalus and sent Tariq as the vanguard.
gemini-abbasid-b3-010: Which dangerous, devastating revolt lasted 14 years in southern Iraq around Basra, exhausted the Abbasid economy and was led by someone claiming descent from the Prophet's family?
The Zanj leader gathered enslaved people and agricultural workers, who caused tremendous destruction before al-Muwaffaq al-Abbasi defeated them.
gemini-abbasid-b3-014: Which dangerous secretive sect stole the Black Stone from Makkah, took it to Bahrain for several years and killed pilgrims in the Abbasid era?
The Qarmatians were an extremist esoteric movement that committed horrific massacres in Makkah and violated the Sacred Sanctuary.
gemini-abbasid-b3-020: The crisis over the creation of the Quran, when scholars were tested and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal stood firm, followed al-Mamun, al-Mutasim and al-Wathiq adopting which group's beliefs?
The Mutazilah intellectually dominated the caliphs and imposed their opinion through state power until al-Mutawakkil ended the ordeal.
gemini-ayyubid-b3-008: Which fortress did Arnat use as a base for raids on Muslim pilgrim caravans?
Karak lies east of the Dead Sea and overlooked the pilgrimage and trade route between Egypt and the Levant.
gemini-ayyubid-b3-010: The Ayyubid sultan al-Malik al-Kamil entered a disastrous agreement called the Treaty of Jaffa. What did he concede?
He handed Cairo to the Crusaders
He handed Jerusalem to Frederick II without fighting
He paid half of Egypt's land-tax revenue to the Mongols
He gave his fleet to France
This treaty aroused widespread anger in the Islamic world because it squandered Salah al-Din's achievement.
gemini-ayyubid-b3-014: What was the main aim of the Salahiyyah schools that spread in Egypt and the Levant in the Ayyubid era?
Spreading Sunni doctrine and combating esoteric thought
The Sunni schools were an intellectual weapon for correcting beliefs and building a strong generation to confront the Crusaders.
gemini-prayer-b4-004: A worshipper forgets the first tashahhud and stands fully upright. According to most jurists, what must he do?
Continue praying without returning, and prostrate for forgetfulness
Return to the tashahhud even after standing fully upright
Restart the prayer from the beginning

According to the majority, once fully upright he should not return, but continue and compensate with prostrations of forgetfulness, as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) did in Ibn Buhaynah's hadith. Many hold that deliberately returning after standing fully upright invalidates the prayer. Tashahhud is the seated testimony recitation.
gemini-prophets-b4-005: For which great quality did Ayyub, peace be upon him, become proverbial after Allah tested him for years?
He lost his wealth, children and health, but remained patient, seeking Allah's reward, until Allah removed his affliction.
gemini-islamic-history-b4-003: In which Hijri year did the conquest of al-Andalus begin?
Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed the strait in 92 AH (711 CE) and defeated the Visigoths at Wadi Lakkah.
gemini-hadith-b4-005: What is a hadith narrated by no fewer than two people at every level of its chain called?
Aziz (a report with at least two narrators at each level) is named for its rarity or the strength gained from another route. It ranks above gharib and below mashhur.
gemini-umayyad-b4-005: What great sovereign and economic decision did Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan take to end Muslim dependence on the Byzantines and Persians?
Arabizing government bureaus and minting the Islamic dinar
This decision achieved the Islamic state's complete economic and administrative independence.
gemini-mamluk-b4-005: What global economic development weakened the late Mamluks and deprived them of their main source of customs wealth?
The Nile drying up and agriculture declining
The discovery of the Cape of Good Hope route and diversion of trade
Their long wars with the Abbasids
Their abandonment of agriculture and industry
Losing the spice route deprived Egypt of huge revenues, eventually weakening the Mamluk army.
poetry-fusha-0001: In Imru al-Qays's line, 'A night like sea waves let down its sudul upon me, with every kind of grief to test me,' what does sudul mean?
Sudul means curtains, singular sadl. He likens night's darkness to curtains lowered over him.
poetry-fusha-0002: In Imru al-Qays's line, 'I said to it as it stretched out its spine, followed with its hindquarters and weighed down with its kalkal,' what is kalkal?
Kalkal means chest, plural kalakil, as explained by al-Zawzani.
poetry-fusha-0003: Imru al-Qays says: 'O long night, clear away with morning, though morning is no amthal than you.' What does amthal mean here?
Amthal means better. Morning is no better than night to him because his worries never leave him.
poetry-fusha-0004: Imru al-Qays describes the night: 'What a night, as though its stars were bound by flax amras to solid rocks.' What are amras?
Amras is the plural of maras, meaning rope. It is as though the stars are tied to solid rocks and cannot move.
poetry-fusha-0005: Imru al-Qays described his horse as a fetter for the awabid. What are awabid?
Awabid means wild animals. His horse is so fast it catches them and becomes like a fetter to them.
poetry-fusha-0007: In the line 'He has a gazelle's flanks, an ostrich's legs, the loping of a sirhan and the short stride of a tatful,' what is sirhan?
Sirhan means wolf, and irkha is a kind of its running. Tatful means a fox cub.
poetry-fusha-0008: Imru al-Qays likened his horse to a child's khudhruf. What is a khudhruf?
A pierced pebble spun by a child on a string
A small foal ridden by a boy
A short whip used on a horse
A small arrow shot by a boy
A khudhruf is a pierced pebble through which children pass a string and spin it above their heads. He likened his horse's speed to it.
poetry-fusha-0009: In the line 'A bay horse whose saddle felt slips from the smoothness of its back, as a safwa makes the descending traveler slip,' what is safwa?
Safwa, safwan and safa mean hard rock. Rain slips off it as saddle felt slips off the horse's back.
poetry-fusha-0010: In the line 'On the morning of al-bayn, when they departed, by the tribe's acacia trees I was like a man splitting bitter colocynth,' what does al-bayn mean?
Al-bayn here means separation: the day the loved ones departed.
poetry-fusha-0011: What are aram in Imru al-Qays's line 'You see the dung of aram in its courtyards and hollows, like peppercorns'?
Aram are pure white gazelles, singular ri'm, which live in sandy areas.
poetry-fusha-0012: In the line 'In Tayma it left no palm trunk, nor utum unless built up with stone,' what is an utum?
Utum means a palace or tall building, plural atam. The flood left only buildings made of stone.
poetry-fusha-0014: Who wrote: 'Days will reveal what you did not know, and news will come from someone you gave no provisions'?
The line is from Tarafah ibn al-Abd's Muallaqah, which begins with the words Li-Khawlata atlalun bi-burqati Thahmad.
poetry-fusha-0015: What does Tarafah mean by 'The injustice of relatives pains a person more than the stroke of a sharp Indian sword'?
Injustice vanishes through patience with relatives
Relatives wrong only those who wrong them
A sword blow is easier than friends' reproach
Relatives' injustice hurts the soul more than a sword blow
He says relatives' injustice arouses sorrow and anger more deeply than the stroke of a sharp sword.
poetry-fusha-0017: In Tarafah's words 'I see death yatamu the noble and selects them,' what does yatamu mean?
Itiyam means choosing: death chooses and selects the noble.
poetry-fusha-0018: In Tarafah's line 'When the people said, Who will be the man? I thought I was unitu, and did not grow lazy or dull,' what does unitu mean?
Unitu comes from ana, yani, meaning to intend. He thought they meant him, so he acted promptly.
poetry-fusha-0019: Tarafah boasted, 'I am the darb man you know.' What does darb mean?
A man who strikes often with a sword
Darb means a lean man. Arabs praised leanness because much flesh encourages laziness.
poetry-fusha-0020: In the line 'I see the grave of a nahham, stingy with his wealth, like that of a wayward man wasting it in idleness,' who is a nahham?
Someone intent on amassing and withholding wealth
Someone who spends lavishly on amusement
Nahham means someone intent on accumulating and withholding wealth. The miser's grave is like the squanderer's: after death there is no difference.
poetry-fusha-0021: Tarafah described his she-camel as awja mirqal. What does mirqal mean?
Mirqal is an intensive form from irqal, a swift gait between walking and running.
poetry-fusha-0022: In the line 'News will come from someone for whom you bought no batat and set no appointed time,' what is batat?
Batat means a traveler's clothing and equipment. News will come from someone for whom you bought no travel supplies.
poetry-fusha-0024: Zuhayr likened death to the random trampling of an ashwa. What is an ashwa?
A fierce wind on a dark night
A she-camel unable to see at night
An ashwa is a she-camel unable to see at night, striking blindly with its forelegs. Death likewise strikes indiscriminately.
poetry-fusha-0025: In the line 'Whoever does not accommodate others in many affairs is bitten by fangs and trampled by a mansim,' what is a camel's mansim?
The tip of its foot pad
A camel's mansim corresponds to a horse's hoof: the tip of the foot pad on which it steps.
poetry-fusha-0026: Who wrote: 'Whatever trait a person has, even if he thinks it hidden from people, it will be known'?
This is among Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma's wise sayings at the end of his Muallaqah.
poetry-fusha-0028: What does Zuhayr mean by 'An old man's foolishness has no forbearance after it, while a youth gains forbearance after foolishness'?
An old fool is unlikely to become forbearing, while a foolish youth may gain forbearance with time
A youth becomes forbearing only through keeping older men's company
An older man is always more forbearing than a youth
He says there is little hope of forbearance in a foolish old man, whereas age gives a youth forbearance and dignity.
poetry-fusha-0030: What does Zuhayr mean by 'Whoever fears the causes of death will be reached by them, even if he climbs the paths of heaven on a ladder'?
Fear of death cannot prevent it, even if one flees by ascending to heaven
All causes of death are in heaven
He says the causes of death will reach whoever fears them. Fear is of no use, even if one tries to climb to heaven to escape them.
poetry-fusha-0032: Zuhayr describes war as 'Grinding you like a mill with its thifal.' What is a mill's thifal?
Cloth or leather spread underneath to catch the flour
A mill's thifal is cloth or leather spread beneath it to catch the flour.
poetry-fusha-0033: In 'You two rescued Abs and Dhubyan after they had nearly annihilated each other and crushed Manshim's perfume between them,' who was Manshim?
A perfume seller whose perfume people dipped their hands in when making a pact
A famous horse in the Dahis and al-Ghabra war
A valley between Abs and Dhubyan

According to the best-known account, Manshim sold perfume. People dipped their hands in it to pledge an alliance, then fought until they perished. She became proverbial, though other origins are also given.
poetry-fusha-0034: What does shaki al-silah mean in Zuhayr's words 'Beside a lion, shaki al-silah, powerful in build'?
Shaki al-silah and shaik al-silah mean fully armed, from shawkah, meaning equipment and strength.
poetry-fusha-0035: Zuhayr said: 'I stood there after twenty hijjah, scarcely recognizing the dwelling after uncertainty.' What does hijjah mean?
Hijjah means year, plural hijaj. He stood by the dwelling twenty years after leaving it.
poetry-fusha-0036: In 'Her dwelling at al-Raqmatayn is like renewed tattoo marks on the nawashir of a wrist,' what does nawashir al-misam mean?
Nawashir al-misam means the wrist's veins. The wrist is where a bracelet sits. He likens the traces of the dwelling to renewed tattoos there.
poetry-fusha-0037: In 'War is only what you have known and tasted, and what is said of it is no hadith murajjam,' what is hadith murajjam?
Words based on conjecture rather than certainty
Hadith murajjam is talk based on conjecture. What he says of war is tested certainty, not guesswork.
poetry-fusha-0040: Labid says, 'Death's arrows never tatishu.' What does tatishu mean?
Taysh means veering or deviating. Death's arrows do not miss their target: there is no escape from it.
poetry-fusha-0041: In Labid's line 'The floods jala the ruins, like books whose pages the pens renew,' what does jala mean?
Jala means uncovered. The floods uncovered the traces of dwellings beneath the soil, making them look like newly written books.
poetry-fusha-0042: In 'I stood questioning them, but how can we question deaf, khawalid things whose words are unclear?' what does khawalid mean?
Khawalid means remaining. It describes the enduring, solid stones of the dwellings that do not answer the questioner.
poetry-fusha-0043: Who wrote 'From a people whose fathers set their traditions, and every people has a tradition and its leader'?
The line is from Labid ibn Rabiah's Muallaqah, in praise of his people.
poetry-fusha-0044: In Labid's words 'They are springtime for their neighbors and the murmilat when their year grows long,' who are the murmilat?
Women whose provisions have run out
Armala means to run out of provisions. His people are like springtime in their widespread benefit to neighbors and poor women.
poetry-fusha-0045: Whose Muallaqah opens with 'The dwellings have faded, both their temporary and permanent sites'?
Al-Zawzani states that the fourth Muallaqah is by Labid ibn Rabiah and begins with Afati al-diyaru mahalluha fa-muqamuha.
poetry-fusha-0047: In 'When the king imposes khasf on people, we refuse to accept humiliation among us,' what does khasf mean?
Khasf means humiliation. To impose khasf on someone is to burden them with something humiliating.
poetry-fusha-0048: What does Amr ibn Kulthum mean by 'Whenever we carry our mill to a people, they become flour for it in battle'?
We move our homes wherever we wish
Whenever we fight a people, we destroy them
We grind grain for guests from every people
We gather tribes around us for war
His mill is the mill of war. Whenever they fight a people, they kill them; flour is a metaphor for the slain.
poetry-fusha-0049: Who wrote 'We drink clear water when we reach it, while others drink mud and murky water'?
The line is from Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi's Muallaqah, boasting of his people.
poetry-fusha-0050: In 'Our spear-shaft, O Amr, defied enemies before you who tried to make it bend,' what does the spear-shaft symbolize?
Arabs use the spear-shaft as a metaphor for honor. Their honor refused to bend to enemies before him.
poetry-fusha-0051: Antarah opens his Muallaqah with 'Have poets left any mutaraddam?' What does mutaraddam mean?
A place to be repaired and patched
Mutaraddam is a place needing patching and repair. The poets have left no meaning unexpressed.
poetry-fusha-0052: In 'O dwelling of Ablah at al-Jiwa, speak! Good morning, dwelling of Ablah, and be safe,' what is al-Jiwa?
A particular place, with jaww originally meaning valley
Jaww means valley, plural jiwa. Al-Jiwa in the line is a particular place, as al-Zawzani says.
poetry-fusha-0053: Who wrote 'Praise me for what you know, for I am easy to deal with when I am not wronged'?
The line is from Antarah ibn Shaddad al-Absi's Muallaqah.
poetry-fusha-0054: In 'When I am wronged, my retaliation is basil, bitter to taste like colocynth,' what does basil mean here?
Basil here means hateful. Whoever wrongs him is punished in a way they hate, as they hate the taste of colocynth.
poetry-fusha-0055: Antarah describes his opponent as mudajjaj, whom champions dreaded facing. Who is mudajjaj?
Mudajjaj means fully armed. Champions dreaded facing him because of his might.
poetry-fusha-0056: In 'They call Antar as the spears are like a well's ashtan in the black horse's chest,' what are ashtan?
Shatan is a rope used to draw water, plural ashtan. He likens the long spears in his horse's chest to them.
poetry-fusha-0057: In 'He turned aside from spears striking his chest, complaining to me with tears and tahamhum,' what is tahamhum?
A horse falling to its knees
Tahamhum is a kind of whinny resembling a plaintive cry, to move the horse's owner to pity.
poetry-fusha-0059: In Antarah's words 'The horses plunge grimly through the khabar,' what is khabar?
Khabar is soft ground into which horses' legs sink.
poetry-fusha-0060: Al-Harith ibn Hillizah's Muallaqah begins 'Asma has announced her departure; many a resident's thawa grows tiresome.' What does thawa mean?
Thawa and thuwiyy mean staying. Many residents' stays become tiresome, but Asma is not among them.
poetry-fusha-0061: In al-Harith's line 'I see none of those I knew there, so today I weep bewildered, though weeping does not yuhiru,' what does yuhiru mean?
Iharah means bringing back. Weeping brings nothing back.
poetry-fusha-0062: In al-Harith ibn Hillizah's Muallaqah, 'Our brothers the Araqim go too far against us, pressing hard in their words,' who are the Araqim?
The Araqim are clans of Taghlib, named because their forefathers' eyes were likened to those of spotted snakes.
poetry-fusha-0064: Who wrote 'Small matters loom large in the eyes of the small, while great matters shrink in the eyes of the great'?
The line is from al-Mutanabbi's poem Ala Qadri Ahl al-Azm, praising Sayf al-Dawlah.
poetry-fusha-0068: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'Using generosity where the sword belongs harms greatness as much as using the sword where generosity belongs'?
Treat everyone as they deserve: do not honor those deserving punishment or punish those deserving gifts
Generosity is always better than war
The sword is suitable only for kings
Giving too much harms one's wealth
Al-Wahidi says everyone should be rewarded and treated as they deserve. Anyone acting otherwise harms their own greatness.
poetry-fusha-0071: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'What use is a person's eyesight if light and darkness are alike to him'?
Sight is a blessing people fail to appreciate
Night and day are alike to the wise
Sight that cannot distinguish light from darkness is useless, so the patron must distinguish the poet from others
The world is not worth looking at
Al-Wahidi says that if a sighted person cannot distinguish light from darkness, what use is their sight? The poet means: you must distinguish me from others.
poetry-fusha-0072: Who wrote 'I am the one whose literature the blind have seen, and whose words have made the deaf hear'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's. Al-Wahidi explains that his poetry became so famous that even the blind and deaf knew it.
poetry-fusha-0076: Who wrote 'The intelligent suffers through his intellect amid bliss, while the ignorant enjoys himself amid misery'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's and is among his proverbial sayings collected by al-Sahib ibn Abbad.
poetry-fusha-0079: Who wrote 'The taste of death in a trivial cause is like its taste in a great cause'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's, from Idha Ghamarta fi Sharafin Marum.
poetry-fusha-0086: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'Whoever spends his hours amassing money for fear of poverty has made poverty his very action'?
Amassing money out of fear of poverty is poverty itself, because the person withholds and deprives himself
Time is more valuable than money
The poor are happier than the rich
Poverty suddenly befalls those who do not save
Al-Wahidi says that collecting money for fear of poverty is itself poverty, because the collector withholds it.
poetry-fusha-0087: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'I thought the reports immense before meeting him, but when we met, experience made the reports seem small'?
The reports about his patron were exaggerated
He found his patron better than what he had heard
Khubr means direct experience. When he met the patron, he found him better than he had heard, so firsthand observation dwarfed the reports.
poetry-fusha-0088: What does al-Mutanabbi boast of in 'I grappled with disasters until I left them saying: Has death died, or has fear been frightened?'?
His ability to treat the sick
His repeated encounters with terrors without fear or destruction
Al-Wahidi says he repeatedly confronted disasters in travel and war until, if they could speak, they would marvel that he neither fears nor perishes.
poetry-fusha-0090: Who wrote 'When a person's deeds turn bad, his suspicions turn bad, and he believes his habitual imaginings'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's, from Firaqun wa-Man Faraqtu Ghayru Mudhammam.
poetry-fusha-0092: In 'If generosity is not freed from hurt, neither praise is gained nor wealth remains,' what does al-Mutanabbi mean about giving accompanied by reminders and hurt?
It is always better than withholding
It wastes wealth and gains no praise
Al-Wahidi says that if generosity is not free of reminders of favors, wealth is lost and praise is not gained: giving removes the wealth, while hurt cancels the praise.
poetry-fusha-0094: Who is the visitor in al-Mutanabbi's words 'My visitor seems bashful, for she visits only in darkness'?
Al-Wahidi says he means a fever that came at night, as if shy and visiting only in darkness.
poetry-fusha-0095: What does al-Mutanabbi advise in 'Ease for the eye the sights that burden it, for the eye's waking moments are like a dream'?
Sleep often to rest the eyes
Take distressing sights lightly, because they pass like dreams
Al-Wahidi says to ease the eye's burden of distressing sights. What it sees awake resembles a dream: it stays briefly, then passes.
poetry-fusha-0098: Al-Mutanabbi says, 'But the Arab youth there is a stranger in face, hand and tongue.' What place is he describing?
The poem describes Shib Bawwan in Persia, a place abundant in trees and water, as al-Wahidi says.
poetry-fusha-0099: Which famous poem opens 'Sound judgment protected me from folly, and the ornament of excellence adorned me when I lacked ornaments'?
This is the opening of al-Tughrai's Lamiyyat al-Ajam. Al-Damiri explained it in an abridgment of al-Safadi's commentary Al-Ghayth al-Musjam.
poetry-fusha-0100: Al-Tughrai says, 'Why stay in al-Zawra when neither my home nor my she-camel nor my camel is there?' Which city does he call al-Zawra?
Al-Zawra is Baghdad, named for the deviation of its qiblah (prayer direction), according to al-Damiri's commentary.
poetry-fusha-0102: What does al-Tughrai call a kingdom that need not fear harm and requires neither supporters nor servants?
The line says the kingdom of contentment need not fear harm and requires neither supporters nor servants. A contented person has no need of others.
poetry-fusha-0106: In the poem 'Even prayer niches weep though made of stone, even pulpits mourn though made of wood,' what does the poet lament?
The line is from Abu al-Baqa al-Rundi's Nuniyyah lamenting Andalusian cities such as Valencia, Murcia and Cordoba.
poetry-fusha-0109: What does al-Rundi mean in his Nuniyyah by 'All that was kingdom and king became like a drowsy sleeper's account of a passing vision'?
Kingship remains as long as the dream
Kingdoms and kings vanished until they became like a sleeper's tale of a dream
Kings dream of their rule lasting
He likens the disappearance of kingdoms and kings to a vision a drowsy sleeper sees and recounts, with nothing remaining of it.
poetry-fusha-0114: Ibn Durayd says, 'When overwhelming trouble burdens me, I am not one to say: The flood has reached the high ground.' What does he boast of?
Not panicking or complaining when hardship intensifies
The flood has reached the high ground is a proverb for a situation becoming severe. The poet denies being among those who panic and say it.
poetry-fusha-0118: Why did Kab ibn Zuhayr recite the poem beginning 'Suad has departed, and today my heart is love-stricken'?
To boast of the Muzaynah tribe
To apologize to and praise the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)
Kab recited it in apology to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) after being declared liable to death. It includes the line: The Messenger is a sword by whose light guidance is sought.
poetry-fusha-0121: Whom does the poet mourn in 'I thought of who would weep for me and found only the sword and the Rudayni spear weeping'?
The line is from Malik ibn al-Rayb's famous poem mourning himself as he lay dying in Khurasan.
poetry-fusha-0125: Abu Tammam's poem 'The sword is truer in its reports than books' praised Caliph al-Mutasim after the conquest of which city?
Abu Tammam composed it on the conquest of Amorium. It includes: O day of the battle of Amorium, wishes departed from you full-uddered, sweet of milk.
poetry-fusha-0128: Whom was Abu Firas al-Hamdani addressing in 'Does a captive laugh while a free one weeps, and a sorrowful one fall silent while a carefree one laments'?
A dove cooing nearby during his captivity
This is from Abu Firas's Rumiyyat. He wrote it while held captive by the Byzantines, after hearing a dove cooing nearby.
poetry-fusha-0133: Who is speaking in Hafiz Ibrahim's words 'I am the sea, with pearls hidden in my depths; have they asked the diver about my shells'?
The poem is titled Al-Lughah al-Arabiyyah Tana Hazzaha. Hafiz makes the language speak about itself.
poetry-fusha-0138: Jarir said, 'A man who lived building glory for ninety years, ascending to good deeds and honor.' Whom did he mourn in this poem?
The poem mourns al-Farazdaq. It includes: By my life, the death of al-Farazdaq has grieved Tamim and broken it amid the calamities of time.
poetry-fusha-0143: Who is described in 'A bearer of banners, a descender into valleys, an attender of gatherings, a leader of armies'?
The line is from al-Khansa's Raiyyah mourning her brother Sakhr.
poetry-fusha-0193: In 'Thabir amid the first downpours seemed like an elder wrapped in a bijad,' what is a bijad?
A bijad is a striped cloak. He likens Mount Thabir, wrapped in rain, to an old man wrapped in his cloak.
poetry-fusha-0194: Imru al-Qays mentioned ghutha in describing a flood. What is ghutha?
Grass, trees and soil carried by a flood
Ghutha is the grass, trees, herbage and soil brought by a flood. Its plural is aghtha.
poetry-fusha-0196: In Zuhayr's words 'There the wild cattle and white gazelles walk khilfah,' what does khilfah mean?
Khilfah means succeeding one another: when one herd passes, another comes.
poetry-fusha-0197: Zuhayr says, 'I swore by the House around which men who built it, from Quraysh and Jurhum, circumambulated.' What House does he swear by?
Al-Zawzani explains: I swore by the Kabah, around which its builders from Quraysh and Jurhum circumambulated.
poetry-fusha-0198: Zuhayr's Muallaqah praises two chiefs who reconciled Abs and Dhubyan. Who were they?
Harim ibn Sinan and al-Harith ibn Awf
Amr ibn Hind and al-Numan ibn al-Mundhir
Qays ibn Zuhayr and al-Rabi ibn Ziyad
Husayn ibn Damdam and Ward ibn Habis
The two chiefs are Harim ibn Sinan and al-Harith ibn Awf, who undertook to pay compensation for those killed.
poetry-fusha-0199: Who wrote 'Do not hide from Allah what is in your souls, hoping it will be concealed; whatever is hidden, Allah knows'?
The line is from Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma's Muallaqah. It is followed by: It is deferred, set in a book and stored for the Day of Reckoning.
poetry-fusha-0200: In 'We asked and you gave; we returned and you gave again, but whoever makes much tasal will one day be denied,' what is tasal?
Tasal means asking. Tafal is one of the verbal-noun patterns. Whoever asks too much will one day be denied.
poetry-fusha-0201: In Labid's words 'Traces of camps: since their inhabitants' time, years have tajarrama, with their lawful and sacred months,' what does tajarrama mean?
Tajarrum means completion and ending. Tajarramat al-sanah means the year completed its course.
poetry-fusha-0202: In 'It received the stars' spring rains and the wadq of thundering clouds, heavy and light,' what is wadq?
Wadq means rain. Wadaqat al-sama means the sky rained.
poetry-fusha-0203: Which poet's Muallaqah contains 'He built for us a house with a high roof, to which both old and young aspired'?
The line is from Labid's Muallaqah, boasting of his people. The house means the house of honor and glory.
poetry-fusha-0204: In 'We had long ghurr days, in which we refused the king's demand to submit,' what does ghurr mean?
Days means battles. Ghurr means famous, like horses with white forehead markings, which stand out.
poetry-fusha-0205: In 'Let no people think we have weakened and wanina,' what does wanina mean?
Wana means flagging. They are not among those broken or weakened in war.
poetry-fusha-0206: In 'Let none act with jahl toward us, lest we exceed the jahl of the foolish,' what does jahl mean?
It means: let none behave foolishly toward us, or we will exceed their foolishness. Jahl here is the opposite of forbearance.
poetry-fusha-0207: In Antarah's line 'Greetings, ruin of old, which aqwa and grew desolate after Umm al-Haytham,' what does aqwa mean?
Al-Zawzani explains aqwa and aqfara as becoming empty. The ruin lost its inhabitants after they departed.
poetry-fusha-0208: Antarah compared his she-camel's great size to a fadan. What is a fadan?
Fadan means palace, plural afdan. He likened the she-camel to it in size and bulk.
poetry-fusha-0209: In Antarah's words 'My rikab are docile, accompanying me wherever I wish,' what are rikab?
Rikab means camels and, according to most authorities, has no singular of the same form.
poetry-fusha-0210: In al-Harith ibn Hillizah's words 'They settled their plan at night, and in the morning there was dawda among them,' what is dawda?
poetry-fusha-0211: In 'From events and reports came a khatb that concerns and saddens us,' what does khatb mean?
Al-Zawzani says: from events and news came a grave matter that occupies and saddens us.
poetry-fusha-0213: What does Antarah boast of in 'Those who witnessed the battle will tell you that I plunge into war and refrain at the spoils'?
His courage in battle and restraint concerning spoils
He boasts of plunging into battle and then refraining from the spoils, combining courage and restraint.
poetry-fusha-0217: In Labid's line 'A person is like a flame and its light, yahuru to ash after shining,' what does yahuru mean?
Yahuru means becomes. He likens a person to a flame that shines and then becomes ash, as explained in the notes to Labid's Diwan.
poetry-fusha-0224: In al-Mutanabbi's line 'Let a madim not delight in fine clothing; does a fine shroud please the buried?' who is a madim?
Al-Wahidi says madim means a wronged person, and bizzah means clothing. Fine clothing does not please the oppressed, just as a fine shroud does not please the dead.
poetry-fusha-0225: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'I pray your discerning looks be spared from mistaking swelling for fat'?
Obesity is a sign of disease
The patron should look more at people's faces
Sayf al-Dawlah should distinguish a true poet from a pretender
Al-Wahidi says this is a comparison: do not assume every poet is truly a poet, just as swelling should not be mistaken for fat.
poetry-fusha-0226: In 'Heading to Kafur, leaving others, for whoever seeks the sea thinks little of the sawaqi,' what are sawaqi?
Saqiyah means a small river. He likens his patron to the sea and others to small rivers.
poetry-fusha-0227: In 'A man with a sick, bitter mouth finds clear water bitter,' what does al-Mutanabbi mean about those who envy him?
They criticize his poetry because of their own deficiency, not his
They are sick and need medicine
Al-Wahidi says they are like a sick person finding clear water bitter: they criticize him because of their own deficiency.
poetry-fusha-0228: Who wrote 'I returned with my pens saying to me: Glory belongs to the sword, not the pen'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's, from Hattama Nahnu Nusari al-Najma fi al-Zulam.
poetry-fusha-0233: Who wrote 'Being denied by a withholding hand does not hurt as much as being denied by a giving hand'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's and is among his proverbial sayings.
poetry-fusha-0235: What does al-Mutanabbi complain of in 'Time's children came to it in its youth and it delighted them; we came to it in old age'?
Coming late in time and not gaining what earlier people gained
He says earlier people came when time was young and it delighted them; we came when it had grown old and did not find what they found.
poetry-fusha-0245: In 'Ninety thousand, like lions of al-Shara: their skins were cooked before the figs and grapes ripened,' whom does Abu Tammam target with before the figs and grapes ripened?
Astrologers who claimed Amorium could not be conquered before figs and grapes ripened
The poem celebrates the conquest of Amorium and refutes astrologers who told al-Mutasim it could be conquered only when figs and grapes ripened.
poetry-fusha-0249: In 'Worries gathered at my saddle, so I directed my she-camel toward the white palace of al-Madain,' where did al-Buhturi go?
He directed his she-camel toward al-Madain to console himself with the faded Sasanian ruins.
poetry-fusha-0253: In 'Spear thrusts strike only their throats, and they do not shrink from the pools of death,' how does Kab describe the Prophet's Companions (peace and blessings be upon him)?
They thrust spears often in battle
They ward off spear thrusts with armor
They face the enemy, so are not stabbed in the back
They flee death when fighting intensifies
They do not turn their backs, so spear thrusts strike only their chests. They do not hang back from places of death.
poetry-fusha-0261: Ibn Durayd said, 'I have milked time in both its halves: sometimes it tasted bitter to me, sometimes sweet.' What does he mean?
He divided his wealth among his family
He experienced time's good and bad
He lived half his life in the desert
Milking time in both its halves is a proverb for experiencing affairs. He has tasted time's bitterness and sweetness.
poetry-fusha-0282: What is Abu al-Atahiyah discussing in 'Its sweetness is mixed with bitterness, and its comfort mixed with toil'?
The poem La-Amruka Ma al-Dunya bi-Dari Baqa criticizes worldly life and shows how its sweetness is mixed with bitterness.
poetry-fusha-0288: What does the poet urge in 'Do good, even if you receive no praise: what reward does pouring rain seek?'?
Doing good without expecting reward, like rain
He urges doing good without expecting anything in return, as rain falls without seeking reward.
poetry-fusha-0291: In 'Souls' desires are too small for people to become enemies and destroy one another over them,' what does al-Mutanabbi mean about worldly desires?
They are too great to gain without fighting
They are too trivial for people to fight and kill one another over
They can be gained only through enmity
He says what souls seek in this world is too small to justify enmity and mutual destruction.
poetry-fusha-0292: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'Every difficulty that has not happened is hard on souls, but easy once it happens'?
People find a matter hard before it happens, but easier once it occurs
Difficulties happen only to the weak
What the soul fears before it happens becomes easier once it occurs. The line is among his proverbial sayings.
poetry-fusha-0295: What does 'Whoever keeps the world company for long sees it change before his eyes until its truth seems a lie' mean?
The world changes for no one
Truthful people are not believed in the world
Long experience of the world reveals its apparent truth to be deception and delusion
Al-Wahidi says that long companionship with the world reveals its outer and inner nature: its truth is falsehood, and it is delusion and empty hopes.
poetry-fusha-0296: In 'Fear is only what a person fears, and safety only what he sees as safe,' how does al-Mutanabbi view fear and safety?
They depend on the army's size
They have no relation to people
They are judged by the soul according to its outlook
Al-Wahidi says fear is what a person fears: if one fears something harmless, it becomes fear; if one feels safe with something unsafe, one has already enjoyed a sense of safety.
poetry-fusha-0298: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'For one who becomes abased, humiliation is easy; a wound causes no pain to the dead'?
Someone who thinks little of himself bears humiliation like a corpse that feels no wound
Wounds hurt only the strong among the living
The dead are happier than the living
Al-Wahidi says that someone who considers himself low easily bears humiliation, like a dead person who feels no pain from wounds.
poetry-fusha-0302: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'If a wise man has tested people, I have eaten them while he has merely tasted'?
His knowledge of people exceeds an experienced man's as eating exceeds tasting
A wise man does not test people
Al-Wahidi says: my knowledge of people exceeds that of an experienced wise man, because I am like the eater while he is like the taster.
poetry-fusha-0308: In 'Swords, like people, have appointed lifetimes,' how does al-Mutanabbi describe his patron?
His blows are so powerful that they break the sword, as if killing it
Al-Wahidi says the excellence of his stroke kills both the victim and the weapon: it breaks the sword, which he describes as killing it.
poetry-fusha-0309: What does 'If courage does not bring you into the spear fight, no reproacher will bring you into it' mean?
A reproacher is braver than a fighter
A brave man needs someone to reproach him
Spear fighting is easier than reproach
Incitement and blame do not move a coward to fight
Al-Wahidi says that if courage does not take you into spear fighting, reproach will not either. Incitement does not move a coward.
poetry-fusha-0313: In 'You spend evening and morning on a mattress, while I sleep on the sarah of a bridled black horse,' what is sarah?
Sarah means the top of the back. She enjoys a soft bed while he spends the night on his horse's back.
poetry-fusha-0314: In 'If you tughdifi the veil before me, I am skilled at seizing an armored knight,' what does tughdifi mean?
Ighdaf means lowering. She conceals herself from him by lowering the veil.
poetry-fusha-0315: Antarah describes himself as tabb at seizing an armored knight. What does tabb mean here?
Tabb means skilled and knowledgeable. Mustalim means wearing armor, from lamah, meaning a coat of mail.
poetry-fusha-0316: In al-Harith's words 'After an ahd with her at Burqat Shamma, her nearest abode is al-Khalsa,' what does ahd mean?
Ahd means meeting. She resolved to leave them after he met her at Burqat Shamma.
poetry-fusha-0317: In al-Harith's Muallaqah, 'O speaker reporting about us before Amr, will this ever end?' who is Amr?
Al-Zawzani explains: O you who report about us to King Amr ibn Hind, will you not stop conveying false reports about us?
poetry-fusha-0318: In Labid's line 'People are like dwellings and their residents: inhabited one day, balaqi the next,' what does balaqi mean?
Balaqi means wastelands, as in the notes to Labid's Diwan. He likens people to dwellings that are populated and then empty.
poetry-fusha-0326: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'I keep my forbearance when it is generosity, but do not keep it when it is cowardice'?
He is forbearing toward enemies in every situation
He is forbearing when it is noble, but abandons it when it becomes cowardice
He considers forbearance and cowardice identical
He is forbearing as long as forbearance is a virtue, but abandons it when it becomes a means of humiliation.
poetry-fusha-0331: Who wrote 'If excellence does not spare you from thanking an inferior for a gift, excellence belongs to the one receiving thanks'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's, from Utainu Khaylan min Fawarisiha al-Dahr.
poetry-fusha-0346: Who is speaking in Hafiz Ibrahim's words 'I am the crown of glory on the brow of the East, whose pearls are the gems of my necklace'?
The line is from Hafiz Ibrahim's poem Misr Tatahaddathu an Nafsiha.
poetry-fusha-0364: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'If you leave a people who could have kept you from leaving, they are the ones who have departed'?
If they could honor you but force you to leave, they have chosen the separation
If people leave you, do not follow their traces or ask about them
A traveler seeking greatness is nobler than someone living comfortably among family
Whoever leaves his people regrets it all his life and finds no replacement
Al-Wahidi says that if you leave people who could have honored you, they are the ones choosing departure. The poet thus justifies leaving them.
poetry-fusha-0365: Who wrote 'Cowards see incapacity as wisdom: such is the deception of a base nature'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's. Al-Wahidi explains in his commentary that the coward's base nature makes incapacity look like wisdom.
poetry-fusha-0366: Al-Mutanabbi forbids complaining to people: 'Do not complain to another and delight him, like a wounded man complaining to crows and vultures.' Why choose crows and vultures?
They spread news and expose secrets
The wounded man finds no healer in the wilderness
They wait for the wounded man to die so they can eat him, without pity
Their cries increase his pain, sorrow and loneliness
Al-Wahidi says complaining to people is like a wounded man complaining to birds waiting for him to die so they can eat him.
poetry-fusha-0368: What does al-Mutanabbi claim for himself in 'I was made affectionate: were I to return to youth, I would leave my gray hair weeping with an aching heart'?
Strong longing for his youth and wishing its return
Fear of approaching death after his hair turned gray
Deep attachment to what accompanies him, even disliked gray hair
Al-Wahidi calls this line an outstanding expression of true attachment. Everyone wishes to part with gray hair, yet he would weep at leaving it because he is used to it.
poetry-fusha-0369: In al-Mutanabbi's words 'Live with honor or die noble, amid spear thrusts and fluttering bunud,' what are bunud?
Al-Wahidi says bunud is the plural of band, meaning a large banner.
poetry-fusha-0371: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'Whoever makes a lion his hunting hawk will himself be hunted by the lion among its prey'?
A lion hunts only what a hawk leaves
A skilled hunter catches lions with a trained hawk
Whoever accompanies the brave becomes brave
Whoever uses a lion to hunt will be hunted by that lion himself
Al-Wahidi says that someone using a lion as a hunter is attacked and hunted by it. The meaning is that the patron surpasses the person with whom he is associated.
poetry-fusha-0374: What does al-Mutanabbi mean by 'Thus have the days decreed among their people: one people's misfortunes are another people's benefits'?
Events that distress one people delight another
Hardships reveal character and refine souls
Time avenges the oppressed, however long it takes
Al-Wahidi says this is time's custom: one people's joy is another's sorrow. No event occurs without some rejoicing and others grieving.
poetry-fusha-0375: In 'Among the world's nakad for a free man is seeing an enemy whose friendship he cannot avoid,' how did al-Wahidi explain nakad?
Al-Wahidi says nakad means scarcity of good. One of the world's failings is forcing a free man to show friendship to his enemy.
poetry-fusha-0377: In one of his verses, whom does al-Mutanabbi call the most unjust of the unjust?
Someone betraying a person who entrusted him with secrets and money
Someone repaying sincere advice with harm and estrangement
Someone withholding a needy person's right despite being able to give it
Someone envying the person whose blessings he himself enjoys
The line says: The most unjust of the unjust is one who envies the person in whose blessings he luxuriates. Al-Wahidi says the worst injustice is envying your benefactor.
poetry-fusha-0378: In 'If forbearance is not in one's nature, an earlier birth will not make one forbearing,' what does al-Mutanabbi assert?
It is an inborn trait, not gained through age
It is learned by keeping company with sages and elders
It increases as a person ages
Al-Wahidi says that if a person is not endowed with innate forbearance, advanced age and earlier birth will not give it to him.
poetry-fusha-0379: Who wrote 'I knew the nights before what they did to us; when they struck me, they taught me nothing more about them'?
The line is al-Mutanabbi's. Al-Wahidi explains that he knew the nights and how they separate loved ones before they afflicted him.
poetry-fusha-0386: Which pre-Islamic poet's Mujamharah contains 'Those who ask people are denied, but one who asks Allah never fails'?
The line is from Abid ibn al-Abras's Aqfara min Ahlihi Malhub, his Mujamharah in Jamharat Ashar al-Arab.
poetry-fusha-0389: Whose poem opens 'Would that I knew whether I might spend a night beside the ghada trees, driving swift young she-camels'?
