This opens Malik ibn al-Rayb al-Tamimi's poem, included by Abu Zayd al-Qurashi in the elegies chapter of Al-Jamharah.
poetry-fusha-0391: Which poet mourned his brother Malik with 'We were like Jadhimah's two drinking companions for an age, until people said we would never part'?
The line is from Mutammim ibn Nuwayrah al-Yarbui's elegy for his brother Malik, in the elegies chapter of Jamharat Ashar al-Arab.
poetry-fusha-0392: Which Umayyad poet wrote 'The deliberate may attain part of his aim, while haste may bring error'?
The line is from al-Qutami's poem included by Abu Zayd al-Qurashi among the Mashubat in Al-Jamharah.
poetry-fusha-0393: Who wrote 'There is no good in forbearance without outbursts to protect its clarity from being muddied'?
The line is from the Raiyyah of the Nabighah of Banu Jadah, the first of the Mashubat in Jamharat Ashar al-Arab.
poetry-fusha-0395: In 'A people who, when evil bares its fangs, fly toward it in zurafat and alone,' what are zurafat?
Al-Tabrizi says zurafat means groups. The poet describes their courage and haste toward hardships, together and separately.
poetry-fusha-0396: In 'They do not ask their brother for proof of what he says when he yandubuhum in calamities,' what does yandubuhum mean?
Al-Tabrizi says yandubuhum means calls them. If someone calls for their support, they hurry without asking why.
poetry-fusha-0397: In the Hamasah line 'Some forbearance in the face of folly is idhan to humiliation,' what does idhan mean?
Al-Tabrizi says idhan means submission. Adhana li-kadha means submitted to it.
poetry-fusha-0399: In 'Then a hardy people would rise to support me at hafizah, when a weak man yielded,' how does al-Tabrizi explain hafizah?
Guarding the tribe's houses at night
Anger over something one must protect
Al-Tabrizi says hafizah is anger over something one must protect; lawthah means weakness.
poetry-fusha-0401: In Imru al-Qays's words 'I strive for muaththal glory, and those like me may attain it,' what does muaththal mean?
The Diwan's notes explain muaththal as deep-rooted and noble.
poetry-fusha-0403: In Labid's words 'Fear of our Lord is the best nafal, and by Allah's permission are my delay and haste,' what is nafal?
The notes to Labid's Diwan explain nafal as bounty and a gift, and rayth as deliberation and slowness.
poetry-fusha-0404: In Labid's words 'People are but two workers: one yutabbiru what he builds, another raises it,' what does yutabbiru mean?
The Diwan's notes explain yutabbiru as destroys and causes loss; the one who raises is the one who builds and erects.
poetry-fusha-0407: Who wrote 'How can they hope for my downfall now that white hair and baldness show on my head'?
The line is from Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil al-Yashkuri's Ayniyyah in his Diwan. He boasts that opponents cannot hope for his downfall now that he is gray-haired and experienced.
poetry-nabati-0044: Which poetic form dominated Sari al-Abd Allah's poetry?
Ataba dominated his poetry, and he became famous for it.
poetry-nabati-0056: Sulayman ibn Shuraym's Izzi li-Halak is among his most famous poems. Whom does he advise in it?
Among his most famous poems is Izzi li-Halak, in which he advises his son.
poetry-nabati-0077: Ousha al-Suwaidi retired from poetry in the late 1990s. On what theme did she continue to recite her poems?
Praising the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him)
After retiring, she continued reciting her poems praising the Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him).
poetry-nabati-0079: Which crisis in Kuwait did Fahd Bursali express in his poem Layt ha al-Naft al-Ghazir Yinqalib May Ghadir?
He composed it during Kuwait's water crisis in the 1950s.
poetry-nabati-0085: Muhsin al-Hazzani is considered an innovator in Nabati poetry for introducing which new meters?
He introduced the meters called Samri, which have two rhymes.
poetry-nabati-0086: On what occasion did Muhsin al-Hazzani compose his poem known as Al-Istighathah?
His town being besieged in war
Rain failing and drought setting in
His son's death in a raid
He composed it when rain failed and drought set in, supplicating to Allah and seeking rain.
poetry-nabati-0104: What kind of poetry is Mutlaq al-Thubayti's collection Andalusiyyat?
His works include Andalusiyyat, a collection of classical Arabic poetry, which earned him the title poet of Andalusiyyat.
poetry-nabati-0119: Which two old names for muhawarah poetry are associated with responding and improvisation?
Old names for muhawarah poetry include Raddiyyah and Mubadaah.
poetry-nabati-0120: What do practitioners of muhawarah poetry call its meters?
Muhawarah meters are called turuq or tawariq.
poetry-nabati-0121: In muhawarah poetry, what does fatl mean?
Responding to the other poet's verse
Ending the exchange with a supplication
The opening poet composing the first verse
The rows of performers repeating the verse aloud
Fatl means devising or composing the first verse; naqd is the reply to it.
poetry-nabati-0122: What term in muhawarah poetry means responding to the other poet's verse?
Naqd is the response to fatl and must reflect it.
poetry-nabati-0123: What does burying the meaning mean in muhawarah poetry?
Using double meanings and symbolism in the verse
Burying the meaning is a kind of double meaning or symbolism that adds depth to poetry.
poetry-nabati-0124: In which region did muhawarah poetry originate before spreading elsewhere?
Muhawarah poetry arose in the Hijaz and later spread to other regions.
poetry-nabati-0125: What is the origin of qaltah, a name for muhawarah poetry?
Aqlat, meaning come in or help yourself
Qaltah comes from aqlat, which means come in or help yourself.
poetry-nabati-0126: What other name is used for Nabati poetry in some sources?
Nabati poetry, also called qasid, is Arabic poetry composed in the dialects of the Arabian Peninsula.
poetry-nabati-0130: The Hilali cadence used in the oldest Nabati poems corresponds to which classical Arabic meter?
Most of the oldest examples use the Hilali cadence, corresponding to at-Tawil.
poetry-nabati-0131: What additional constraint do many later Nabati poems observe that classical poetry usually does not?
Beginning every poem with the basmalah
Using a single rhyme for the first half of every line too
Many later poems use one rhyme for the first half of each line too, rather than only the second half.
poetry-nabati-0133: Which meter does the Qatari poet Muhammad ibn Futays use in Ya Mumin al-Rifi?
Muhammad ibn Futays al-Marri's Ya Mumin al-Rifi is a well-known poem in the Hida meter.
poetry-nabati-0135: According to researcher Abd al-Jabbar Bajil, what is the name of Humayni poetry derived from?
The village of al-Humayniyyah near Hays
Bajil states it is named after al-Humayniyyah village, in the districts of al-Hudaydah near Hays.
poetry-nabati-0137: What bold idea did Saad al-Suwayyan propose in Al-Shir al-Nabati: Dhaiqat al-Shab wa-Sultat al-Nass?
Nabati poetry began in the twentieth century
Nabati poetry was borrowed from Persian
Nabati poetry descends from pre-Islamic poetry
He claimed Nabati poetry descends from pre-Islamic poetry, having undergone successive changes over time.
poetry-nabati-0141: The Qatari poet Khalid ibn Mujib al-Hajri excelled at descriptive poetry. What did he describe most often?
The sea, ships and pearl diving
He excelled at description, depicting she-camels, male camels, horses, wilderness and pastures because he spent his life in the desert.
poetry-nabati-0146: Which meter did Rashid al-Khalawi use for his long poems?
He used the Hilali meter and was known for long poems.
poetry-nabati-0147: Rashid ibn Juaythin compiled Al-Shajan, containing poets' responses to the poems of which poet?
Al-Shajan: Mujarayat Ashar Khalid al-Faysal includes around 120 poems by poets responding to Khalid al-Faysal's poems.
poetry-nabati-0171: Whose struggle and difficult life did poet Zayd al-Harb describe in his poems?
His poems described the struggle of Kuwaiti divers searching for pearls.
poetry-nabati-0177: The muhawarah poet Faysal al-Riyahi composed a thousand-line poem. What did the public call it?
He composed a poem of 1000 lines, which the public calls The Great Poetic Epic.
poetry-nabati-0191: What is the name Hajini derived from?
Hajini means singing or a quick rhythm and is derived from hujun, thoroughbred camels.
poetry-nabati-0192: In Hajini performed on camelback, what does the zarfal rhythm indicate?
Darhamah and zarfal indicate ordinary running and fast running, respectively.
poetry-nabati-0223: An early example of muhawarah is an exchange between Budaywi al-Waqdani and which poet from Hudhayl?
One example is the exchange between Muhammad al-Lihyani of Hudhayl and Budaywi al-Waqdani.
poetry-nabati-0228: Nuhmad Allah Jat ala Ma Tamanna was composed in 1389 AH for which event on Saudi Arabia's southern border?
The poet composed it for the al-Wadiah War in 1389 AH/1969 CE.
poetry-nabati-0246: What nickname was given to the Raiyyah of the knight and shaykh Mishan ibn Hadhdhal?
Mishan ibn Hadhdhal wrote the Raiyyah nicknamed Al-Shaykhah.
poetry-nabati-0247: How many parts make up a Zuhayri poem or piece?
Zuhayri poems consist of seven parts, with the seventh ending in the first rhyme.
poetry-nabati-0248: What is the name of the wordplay used in Zuhayri rhymes?
The first three parts of a Zuhayri share a rhyme using wordplay called shaqr.
poetry-nabati-0249: In which region did Zuhayri originate before spreading to Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar?
This form originated in southern Iraq, then spread to Kuwait, Bahrain and Qatar.
poetry-nabati-0263: What distinctive quality characterized the Emirati poet Rashid ibn Tannaf's poetry?
His poetry featured humor, sometimes bordering on satire, as well as wisdom and proverbs.
poetry-nabati-0273: What does the Kuwaiti researcher Ibrahim al-Khalidi's book Tawariq al-Nabat cover?
The rhythms and meters of popular poetry
His publications include Tawariq al-Nabat: Awzan wa-Buhur al-Shir al-Shabi.
poetry-nabati-0279: The word shilah, which Nabati poets use to ask about a poem's meter, is derived from which verb?
Al-Suwayyan states that shilah derives from shala, meaning raised, and expresses raising the voice in song.
poetry-nabati-0280: When a Nabati poet wants to check a line's meter, what does he ask about instead of the poem's bahr?
A Nabati poet asks about the poem's shilah or tarq rather than its bahr (meter).
poetry-nabati-0283: In Dughaym al-Zilmawi's famous coffee poem Ya Kulayb, who is Kulayb?
His servant who prepared coffee for guests
He had a servant named Kulayb whose task was preparing and serving coffee to guests.
poetry-nabati-0286: Which Nabati poet is credited with introducing rhetorical embellishments into Nabati poetry?
Muhsin al-Hazzani was known for love poetry and introduced rhetorical embellishments into Nabati poetry.
poetry-nabati-0292: In Nabati poetry, what is a mushakah?
A satirical poem exchanged between two tribes
A poem sent by one poet to another to complain about something
A poem composed in response to a famous poem
A poem improvised before an audience
A mushakah is a poem sent by one poet to another complaining about a problem; the response poem is called a mardah.
poetry-nabati-0293: What is the response to a mushakah in Nabati poetry called?
Al-mardah is the other poet's response, which follows the meter and rhyme of the first poem.
poetry-nabati-0297: Which Saudi researcher called for Nabati poetry to be named 'folkloric poetry'?
Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Aqil al-Zahiri
Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Aqil al-Zahiri advocates the possibility of calling it folkloric poetry.
poetry-nabati-0303: Which Nabati poetic meter spread in the nineteenth century and became the most famous?
That century saw the spread of al-mas-hub, which became the most famous Nabati meter.
poetry-nabati-0305: What are the song meters Muhammad ibn La'bun added to Nabati poetry called?
Ibn La'bun added song meters called al-funun al-La'buniyyah.
poetry-nabati-0307: Some connect the name 'Nabati' poetry to which people said to have been known for it?
Some trace the name Nabati poetry to the Nabataeans, one of several views on its origin.
poetry-nabati-0309: In qaltah poetic exchanges, what is the role of the two audience rows?
Writing down and recording the verses
Choosing the subject of the exchange
There are usually two rows of audience members to repeat the verses of the two poets.
poetry-nabati-0314: Sayyaf al-Harbi recounts a contest with another poet: 'When the qaf was halfway through.' What does qaf mean here?
In his account, qaf is explained as the poetic exchange.
poetry-nabati-0334: Nabati poetry was historically known by another name derived from an Arabian region. What was it?
Nabati was historically also known as Najdi.
poetry-nabati-0348: Khalaf ibn Hathal composed 'Zabnati' in King Fahd's voice, addressing whom?
The State of Kuwait and its emir
He recited 'Zabnati', composed in King Fahd's voice to address the State of Kuwait and its emir, Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad.
poetry-nabati-0351: In what year was the Janadriyah Festival, which hosted Nabati poetry evenings, established?
The National Festival for Heritage and Culture has been held since 1405 AH/1985 CE.
poetry-nabati-0352: Where does the name 'Janadriyah' come from?
A tribe that lived in the area
An old meadow northeast of Riyadh
Janadriyah is a meadow formerly called Rawdat Suways, 50 kilometers northeast of Riyadh.
fitness-health-0001: According to British NHS guidance, what is a simple sign that your physical activity is moderately intense?
You can sing loudly without any effort
You can say only a few broken words
You can talk but cannot sing
You breathe as slowly as when completely at rest
Moderate activity raises your heart rate and speeds up breathing; a sign is being able to talk but not sing.
fitness-health-0002: If you cannot say more than a few words without pausing for breath, what intensity of activity are you doing?
The NHS describes vigorous activity as making you breathe hard and fast, so you can say only a few words without pausing.
fitness-health-0003: What is training based on short bursts of maximum effort interspersed with rest periods called?
Very vigorous activity is performed in short bursts of maximum effort with rest in between, known as high-intensity interval training (HIIT).
fitness-health-0004: On at least how many days a week does the British NHS recommend that adults do exercises strengthening the major muscle groups?
The NHS recommends exercises strengthening the major muscle groups on at least two days a week.
fitness-health-0005: Vigorous activity offers similar health benefits to 150 minutes of moderate activity per week in a shorter time. Approximately how long?
The NHS states that 75 minutes of vigorous activity a week offers benefits similar to 150 minutes of moderate activity.
fitness-health-0006: At approximately how many miles per hour does the British NHS estimate brisk walking speed?
Brisk walking is about three miles per hour, faster than a leisurely stroll.
fitness-health-0007: Why does the British NHS suggest pool exercise classes for someone with joint problems who wants to become more active?
Because the pool replaces all other exercise
Because water increases the body's load on the knees
Because moving in water uses no muscles
Because water supports the joints during movement
Water carries some body weight, supporting the joints and helping strengthen muscles.
fitness-health-0008: The World Health Organization defines sedentary behavior as waking periods with low energy expenditure. Which is an example?
Climbing stairs to the second floor
Lying down to watch a screen
The organization gives sitting, reclining and lying down as examples of sedentary behavior.
fitness-health-0009: How does the World Health Organization define physical activity?
Any organized competitive sport practiced at a club under a qualified coach
Any bodily movement produced by skeletal muscles that requires energy expenditure
Any continuous exercise lasting more than a full hour daily
Only movement performed inside a gym
This is the organization's definition, covering movement during leisure, transport, work and household tasks.
fitness-health-0010: What average daily duration of moderate or vigorous physical activity is recommended for children and young people aged 5 to 18?
The British NHS recommends an average of at least 60 minutes daily across the week.
fitness-health-0011: Besides aerobic exercise, what other type of activity do children and young people need each week?
They need two types: aerobic exercise and exercises strengthening muscles and bones.
fitness-health-0013: In the sit-to-stand exercise, what does the British NHS advise using to stand up?
Pushing with the arms on the armrests
Leg strength rather than the arms
Leaning on a wall behind the chair
Looking at the floor and bending the back strongly
The instruction is to rise slowly using the legs rather than the arms, while looking ahead.
fitness-health-0014: What kind of chair does the British NHS recommend for seated exercises at home?
Firm and stable, without wheels or armrests
A swivel chair with wheels for easy movement
Very low so the knees bend deeply
Soft, deep and full of comfortable cushions
A solid, stable chair without wheels is recommended; chairs with armrests are avoided because they restrict movement.
fitness-health-0015: Seated ankle stretches improve flexibility. What other benefit does the British NHS mention?
Reducing the risk of a blood clot
The NHS states that this exercise improves ankle flexibility and reduces the risk of a blood clot.
fitness-health-0016: According to the British NHS, what is the main benefit of a seated chest stretch?
The NHS describes this exercise as good for posture.
fitness-health-0017: You place your right heel directly in front of your left toes and walk that way. What is the purpose?
Heel-to-toe walking is one of the balance exercises in the British NHS series.
fitness-health-0018: Slowly raising the heels off the floor while holding a chair back belongs to which group of British NHS home exercises?
Calf raises are listed under strength exercises.
fitness-health-0019: Sideways bending, sliding the arm down the side of the body, helps restore flexibility in which area?
The NHS states that sideways bending helps restore lower back flexibility.
fitness-health-0020: The British NHS lists stronger bones and a reduced risk of which disease among the benefits of running?
Running strengthens bones and reduces the risk of osteoporosis.
fitness-health-0021: In at least how many weeks can beginners complete the Couch to 5K running program?
The program can be completed in nine weeks or longer, depending on the trainee's ability.
fitness-health-0022: How does the beginners' running program called Couch to 5K start?
Running continuously for half an hour from day one
The program starts with one minute of running followed by a minute and a half of walking, then increases running week by week.
fitness-health-0026: According to the British NHS, by up to what percentage can exercise reduce the risk of early death?
The NHS states that exercise reduces the risk of early death by up to 30%.
fitness-health-0027: Which condition does the British NHS list among those whose risk is lower in people who are regularly physically active?
The list includes heart disease, type 2 diabetes, depression and dementia, including Alzheimer's disease.
fitness-health-0028: According to the WHO estimate published in 2024 using 2022 data, what proportion of the world's adults are insufficiently physically active?
The organization estimated that about 31% of adults (1.8 billion) are insufficiently physically active.
fitness-health-0029: According to the World Health Organization, how much higher is the risk of death among insufficiently active people compared with active people?
The organization states that the risk is between 20% and 30% higher.
fitness-health-0030: What principle do the World Health Organization's guidelines emphasize about the amount of physical activity?
Doing it once a month is enough
It has no benefit below two hours daily
Any amount is better than none
The guidelines emphasize that any amount of activity is better than none at all.
fitness-health-0031: Which vitamin helps vision in dim light?
One function of vitamin A (retinol) is helping vision in dim light.
fitness-health-0032: What substance gives carrots and mangoes their orange color and is converted by the body into vitamin A?
Beta-carotene gives yellow and orange fruits and vegetables their color and is converted into vitamin A in the body.
fitness-health-0033: Which food is so rich in vitamin A that the British NHS advises against eating too much of it?
Liver is very rich in vitamin A; eating too much may raise intake above what is needed.
fitness-health-0034: What is the scientific name for vitamin B1?
Thiamine is vitamin B1 and helps release energy from food and maintain a healthy nervous system.
fitness-health-0035: According to the British NHS, which helps the body produce oxygen-carrying hemoglobin?
One function of vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is helping the body produce hemoglobin.
fitness-health-0036: Which vitamin can bacteria living in the gut produce?
The NHS states that gut bacteria can make biotin (B7).
fitness-health-0037: Which vitamin helps reduce the risk of fetal neural tube defects such as spina bifida?
Folate (B9) and its manufactured form, folic acid, reduce the risk of neural tube defects.
fitness-health-0038: Which vitamin does not occur naturally in fruits, vegetables and grains, so vegans may not get enough of it?
Vitamin B12 comes from meat, fish, milk and eggs and does not occur naturally in plants.
fitness-health-0039: Which vitamin is not stored in large amounts by the body and therefore needs to be consumed regularly?
Vitamin C is water-soluble and is not stored in large amounts, unlike the fat-soluble vitamins A, E and K.
fitness-health-0040: Vitamin D deficiency can cause bone pain in adults due to a condition called:
Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults.
fitness-health-0041: What does the British NHS say about vitamin D overdose from sun exposure?
It cannot occur through sun exposure
It occurs after fifteen minutes of exposure
It affects everyone sitting in the shade
It occurs in winter but not summer
You cannot get too much vitamin D from sunlight, although skin needs protection from prolonged exposure.
fitness-health-0043: Which leafy vegetable is rich in calcium, although the body cannot digest all its calcium?
The NHS makes an exception for spinach because the body cannot digest all the calcium it contains.
fitness-health-0044: Why are canned sardines a good source of calcium?
Because they are caught in deep, cold waters
Because they are preserved in very salty water
Because their oil turns into calcium in the body
Because their soft bones are eaten with them
The NHS lists fish whose bones are eaten, such as sardines, among calcium sources.
fitness-health-0045: Iodine helps the body make hormones for which gland?
Iodine is involved in making thyroid hormones, which regulate metabolic rate.
fitness-health-0046: Which mineral helps regulate fluid balance and proper heart muscle function, and is found in bananas?
Potassium regulates fluid balance and supports the heart muscle; sources include bananas, pulses and nuts.
fitness-health-0047: Which nut does the British NHS mention as a good source of selenium?
Listed sources of selenium include Brazil nuts, fish, meat and eggs.
fitness-health-0048: Taking excessive zinc supplements reduces the body's absorption of which mineral?
High doses of zinc reduce copper absorption, which may cause anemia and weak bones.
fitness-health-0049: What does the British NHS suggest for flavoring food instead of adding salt while cooking?
The NHS advises reducing salt in cooking and using herbs and spices for flavor.
fitness-health-0050: Besides calcium, which mineral helps build strong bones and teeth and release energy from food?
Phosphorus builds bones and teeth and helps release energy from food.
fitness-health-0051: According to Britain's Eatwell Guide, what share of our daily food should fruit and vegetables make up?
The guide states that fruit and vegetables should make up just over one third of our daily food.
fitness-health-0052: Into how many main food groups does Britain's Eatwell Guide divide foods and drinks?
The guide divides food and drink into five main food groups.
fitness-health-0053: To which group does Britain's Eatwell Guide not apply because of different nutritional needs?
Vegetarians who do not eat meat
The guide does not apply to children under two; it applies to vegetarians and overweight people.
fitness-health-0054: Why does the British guide consider pulses such as lentils and beans good alternatives to meat?
They are the richest natural sources of vitamin B12
They contain no starches or natural sugars at all
They are low in fat and rich in fiber and protein
They provide large amounts of beneficial cholesterol
Pulses are low in fat and provide fiber and protein.
fitness-health-0055: Why does the British NHS advise drinking juice with meals rather than between them?
To speed up fat burning after meals
Because juice loses its color if left too long
Juicing releases fruit sugars, which damage teeth; drinking juice with meals reduces this.
fitness-health-0056: Why do potatoes not count toward the five daily portions of fruit and vegetables in British guidance?
Because they grow underground rather than above it
Because they lack essential vitamins and minerals
Because they are usually eaten instead of bread and rice
Because they contain no dietary fiber
Potatoes are a starchy food replacing bread, rice and pasta in a meal, so they do not count toward the five portions.
fitness-health-0057: Which counts toward the five daily portions of fruit and vegetables in British guidance?
Sweet potatoes count because they are eaten in addition to starchy foods; cassava, yams and plantains do not.
fitness-health-0058: However much lentils and chickpeas you eat, they count as only one of the five daily portions. Why?
Because they are always cooked with lots of salt
Because they contain no dietary fiber at all
Because they do not provide the same nutrient mix as fruit and vegetables, and variety is intended
Because the guidelines classify them as sweets
Pulses count as one portion in five-a-day guidance; they are nutrient-rich but do not provide the same nutrient mix as fruit and vegetables, so portions should be varied.
fitness-health-0059: What is the direct digestive benefit of eating enough dietary fiber?
Speeding up sugar absorption from the gut into the blood
Preventing a feeling of fullness after eating
The NHS states that fiber helps digestion and prevents constipation.
fitness-health-0060: According to the British NHS, where is dietary fiber found in plants?
In the juice extracted from green stems
In the cell walls of vegetables, fruit, pulses and grains
Only in oils pressed from seeds
In flower nectar and pollen carried by bees
Fiber is the name for a group of substances in the cell walls of vegetables, fruit, pulses and grains.
fitness-health-0061: Some fiber in oats, apples and pulses is partly digested. What possible effect does the British NHS mention?
This fiber may help reduce the amount of cholesterol in the blood.
fitness-health-0062: What does the British NHS warn against when eating potatoes?
Storing them in a cool, dark, dry place away from light
Eating their skins after boiling them thoroughly
Baking them with a little oil
Eating their green or sprouted parts
Green, damaged or sprouted parts may contain harmful toxins.
fitness-health-0063: What chemical forms when starchy foods such as potatoes and bread are cooked for a long time at high temperatures?
Acrylamide forms during prolonged baking, frying and roasting at high temperatures, and there is evidence that it is carcinogenic.
fitness-health-0064: To reduce acrylamide when roasting or frying starchy foods, what color is recommended?
Black and burnt at the edges
The Food Standards Agency advises aiming for golden yellow or lighter.
fitness-health-0065: What does the British NHS advise about cooked rice left at room temperature overnight?
Rinse it with cold water, then eat it
Throw it away and do not eat it
Mix it with fresh rice, then eat it
Reheat it thoroughly, then eat it
Some bacterial spores survive cooking and produce toxins that reheating does not remove, so rice left overnight is discarded.
fitness-health-0066: How many times can cooked rice be reheated according to the British NHS?
Without limit as long as it is refrigerated
Rice should not be reheated more than once; any excess is discarded.
fitness-health-0067: According to the British NHS, what type of wheat is usually used to make pasta dough?
Pasta is a dough made from durum wheat and water.
fitness-health-0068: Why do whole grains keep you feeling full longer than refined grains?
Because the body digests them more slowly
We digest wholegrain foods more slowly than refined foods, so they keep us feeling full longer.
fitness-health-0069: Which group of vitamins can the body absorb only with the help of fat?
Vitamins A, D and E are fat-soluble and need fat to be absorbed.
fitness-health-0070: Which vegetable oil is rich in saturated fat?
The NHS lists palm oil and coconut oil as plant sources of saturated fat.
fitness-health-0071: What is the function of 'good' high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol?
Turning excess blood sugar into fat
Carrying excess cholesterol to the liver for disposal
Producing vitamin D in sun-exposed skin
High-density lipoprotein carries cholesterol from places where there is too much to the liver for disposal.
fitness-health-0072: Where are manufactured trans fats mainly found?
In cold-pressed extra virgin olive oil
Trans fats occur in partially hydrogenated vegetable oils and raise cholesterol like saturated fats.
fitness-health-0073: What type of fat makes up most of the fat in olive oil and avocados?
The NHS lists olive oil, avocados and some nuts as sources of monounsaturated fats.
fitness-health-0074: Which is a plant source of omega-3 fatty acids suitable for vegetarians?
Plant sources of omega-3 include flaxseed oil, rapeseed oil and walnuts.
fitness-health-0075: Which fish do British guidelines not count as oily fish?
The NHS states that fresh and canned tuna do not count as oily fish.
fitness-health-0076: Cod and haddock are examples of what type of fish?
Cod, haddock and pollock are examples of low-fat white fish.
fitness-health-0077: Why are children under sixteen advised to avoid shark, swordfish and marlin?
These fish may contain more mercury than others, which affects children's nervous systems.
fitness-health-0078: According to the British NHS, which method of cooking fish is less healthy?
Steamed, baked or grilled fish is healthier than fried fish; batter frying increases its fat content.
fitness-health-0079: Lactose intolerance means that the body cannot digest:
Lactose is a type of sugar found mainly in milk and dairy products.
fitness-health-0080: Which enzyme is added to lactose-free dairy products to digest their milk sugar?
Lactase is added to digest lactose so symptoms do not occur.
fitness-health-0081: According to the British NHS, when can pasteurized cow's milk be a child's main drink?
Cow's milk is not given as a drink before age one because it does not provide the balance of nutrients an infant needs.
fitness-health-0082: For approximately how many months at the start of life is exclusive breastfeeding recommended?
Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for about the first six months, then continued alongside solid foods.
fitness-health-0083: Why is skimmed milk not given as a main drink to children under five?
Because it causes milk allergy in all children
Because it is the milk richest in harmful saturated fats
Because it does not provide enough energy and important nutrients
Because it is usually sold without pasteurization or sterilization
The NHS states that it does not contain enough calories and important nutrients for young children.
fitness-health-0084: What sign does the British NHS mention to show you are drinking enough fluids?
Not feeling hungry between main meals all day
A dry mouth in the morning
Drinking throughout the day is recommended so that urine is clear and pale yellow.
fitness-health-0087: Which is a sign of dehydration mentioned by the British NHS?
Dehydration symptoms include thirst, dark strong-smelling urine, less frequent urination and a dry mouth.
fitness-health-0088: Which food does the British NHS suggest for people who find drinking water difficult, because it has a high water content?
Water-rich foods mentioned by the NHS include soup, jelly and fruits such as melon.
fitness-health-0089: Which drinks does the British NHS advise avoiding in very hot weather?
Hot drinks and those containing caffeine
Drinking plenty of cold fluids and avoiding caffeine and hot drinks is advised.
fitness-health-0090: Between which hours does the British NHS especially advise staying in the shade during very hot weather?
Staying in the shade is advised especially between eleven in the morning and three in the afternoon.
fitness-health-0091: How does the British NHS advise keeping the home cool during heatwaves?
Opening windows and curtains during the day and closing them tightly at night
Closing windows and curtains when it is hotter outside, and opening windows safely when the outside air becomes cooler, such as at night
Keeping windows open all day and night
Raising curtains during the day to let sunlight in
Windows are closed when the outside air is hotter and opened safely when it becomes cooler; curtains block sunlight.
fitness-health-0092: According to the British NHS, electric fans help with cooling while the temperature is below how many degrees Celsius?
The NHS states that fans are useful if the temperature is below 35 degrees.
fitness-health-0094: What does the British NHS advise when serving dried fruits such as dates and raisins?
Soak them in juice before eating
Eat them with meals rather than between meals
Eat them on an empty stomach every morning
Dried fruits are sticky and can harm teeth, so they are best eaten with meals rather than as snacks between them.
fitness-health-0095: What does the British NHS think about eating potatoes with their skins on?
It makes no difference because all the fiber is in the flesh
It is worse because the skin has no nutritional value at all
It is forbidden because the skin always contains toxins
It is better because it retains more fiber and vitamins
Keeping the skins on when boiling or baking is recommended to retain fiber and vitamins.
fitness-health-0097: What is meant by oily fish such as salmon and sardines in British guidance?
Only fish preserved in oil in metal cans
Fish rich in long-chain omega-3 fatty acids
Fish always fried in oil before eating
White fish almost free of fat
Oily fish are rich in long-chain omega-3 and are a good source of vitamin D.
fitness-health-0098: What is the purpose of pasteurizing milk?
Turning milk sugar into lactic acid
Adding calcium and vitamins to milk before packaging
Separating fat from milk to make it lighter
Killing bacteria with heat to prevent food poisoning
Pasteurization is heat treatment to kill bacteria and prevent food poisoning.
fitness-health-0099: What are daily habits that help good sleep, such as regular times and relaxing before bed, called?
The British NHS calls these small habit changes sleep hygiene.
fitness-health-0100: Why is it recommended to put phones and computers aside about an hour before sleep?
Devices consume room oxygen at night
Screens greatly raise the room temperature
Blue light from screens makes sleeping harder
Notification sounds weaken hearing over time
Blue light emitted by screens makes falling asleep harder.
fitness-health-0106: For at least how many hours before bed does the British NHS insomnia page advise avoiding exercise?
Its advice includes avoiding exercise for at least four hours before bed.
fitness-health-0107: According to the British NHS, how many hours of sleep do adults need on average?
Adults need an average of 7 to 9 hours of sleep.
fitness-health-0108: According to the British NHS, how many hours of sleep per day do babies and young children need on average?
Babies and young children need an average of 12 to 17 hours.
fitness-health-0109: When is insomnia called long-term insomnia according to the British NHS?
When it recurs once every month
When it lasts three months or more
When it lasts two full weeks
When it lasts three consecutive nights
Insomnia lasting less than three months is short-term; three months or longer is long-term.
fitness-health-0110: After a bad night's sleep, what does the British NHS advise someone with insomnia?
Stay up until dawn the next night
Its advice includes not sleeping in after a bad night and keeping regular times.
fitness-health-0111: Which sleeping position does the British NHS advise to reduce snoring?
Sleeping on the back with legs raised
Sleeping on the back with a low pillow
The NHS advises sleeping on the side; sleeping on the back makes snoring more likely.
fitness-health-0112: According to the British NHS, what causes snoring?
Strong heart contractions during deep sleep
Teeth rubbing against each other all night
Vibration of the tongue, throat and nasal passages during breathing
These parts relax and narrow during sleep, vibrating as breath passes through.
fitness-health-0113: What condition temporarily blocks the airways during sleep and may cause snoring?
Sleep apnea involves a temporary blockage of the airways during sleep.
fitness-health-0114: What is the name of the condition in which someone suddenly falls asleep anywhere?
The NHS describes narcolepsy as suddenly falling asleep anywhere.
fitness-health-0115: According to the British NHS, caffeine's effects on the body can last up to how many hours?
Caffeine's effects may last up to seven hours, so people with poor sleep are advised to avoid it in the evening.
fitness-health-0116: What advice does the British NHS give someone who wants to quit caffeine completely?
Drink it all at once in the morning
Stopping suddenly may cause insomnia and headaches, so gradual reduction is advised.
fitness-health-0119: Tiredness can sometimes signal a simple problem remedied by a glass of water. What is it?
Mild dehydration alone can make you feel tired; a glass of water can suffice, especially after exercise.
fitness-health-0121: How many minutes should the warm-up routine suggested by the British NHS take at least?
The warm-up should take at least six minutes, and longer when needed.
fitness-health-0122: Which movement starts the warm-up routine in British NHS guidance?
The routine starts with three minutes of marching on the spot while moving the arms.
fitness-health-0123: What is the purpose of gentle stretches after a workout?
Replacing fluids lost by the body
Cooling the body down, slowing the pulse and improving flexibility
Raising the heart rate as high as possible
The post-exercise routine helps gradual relaxation, improves flexibility and slows the heart rate.
fitness-health-0124: For how many seconds is each post-exercise stretch held in the British NHS routine?
Each stretch in the routine is held for 15 to 20 seconds.
fitness-health-0125: You lie on your back, raise one straight leg and pull it toward you with your hands. Which muscles does this stretch target?
The muscles at the back of the thigh
The muscles at the front of the thigh
This is a hamstring stretch, targeting the muscles at the back of the thigh.
fitness-health-0126: According to the British NHS, which leg muscle is most commonly affected by cramps?
Cramps most commonly affect the calf at the back below the knee, and less often the foot and thigh.
fitness-health-0128: Approximately how many minutes should brushing your teeth take each time?
Brushing twice daily for about two minutes each time with fluoride toothpaste is recommended.
fitness-health-0129: What is the thin layer of bacteria covering teeth when they are not cleaned properly called?
Plaque is a film of bacteria that contributes to gum disease and tooth decay.
fitness-health-0130: Why does the British NHS advise against rinsing with water immediately after brushing?
Cold water causes immediate tooth decay
It removes the concentrated fluoride left by the toothpaste
Rinsing whitens teeth more than necessary
Water softens the bristles and quickly damages them
Rinsing dilutes the remaining fluoride and reduces its protective effect, so only excess toothpaste is spat out.
fitness-health-0133: According to the British NHS, when is flossing preferable?
The NHS states that it is best to floss before brushing.
fitness-health-0134: Why does the British NHS not recommend wooden toothpicks to remove food debris?
They whiten teeth more than necessary
They may injure gums and cause inflammation
They remove the entire fluoride layer
They cause bad breath every time
Wooden toothpicks may wound the gums and lead to infection.
fitness-health-0135: According to the British NHS, when should fluoride mouthwash be used?
Before bed as a complete substitute for brushing
At another time, such as after lunch, rather than after brushing
Using it immediately after brushing removes the concentrated fluoride from toothpaste, so another time is chosen.
fitness-health-0136: According to the British NHS, for how many minutes should eating and drinking be avoided after fluoride mouthwash?
The NHS advises no eating or drinking for 30 minutes after fluoride mouthwash.
fitness-health-0137: Until at least what age do children need help or supervision when brushing their teeth, according to the British NHS?
Children need help or supervision until at least age seven.
fitness-health-0138: According to the British NHS, how much toothpaste is suitable for a child aged three to six?
Enough to cover the entire brush head
A thin smear is used under age three, and a pea-sized amount from three to six.
fitness-health-0139: Bleeding gums when brushing or eating hard foods such as apples are signs of which problem?
Gum disease symptoms include bleeding, redness and swelling of the gums.
fitness-health-0140: After how many years without a dental checkup does the British NHS advise an adult to see a dentist?
Seeing a dentist is advised after two years without a checkup, or one year for those under 18.
fitness-health-0142: According to the British NHS, approximately how many seconds should washing hands with soap and water take?
Hands are washed for about twenty seconds, rubbing every part.
fitness-health-0143: After washing and drying your hands with a paper towel, what does the British NHS advise using to turn off the tap?
Leave it running for the next person
The final step is using the disposable towel to turn off the tap.
fitness-health-0144: If soap and water are not immediately available, what alternative does the British NHS suggest for cleaning hands?
When soap and water are unavailable, alcohol-based hand sanitizer is used if available.
fitness-health-0147: Who does the British NHS list among those more vulnerable to dehydration?
The NHS highlights babies, children and older people as more vulnerable to dehydration.
fitness-health-0149: In the WHO principles of a healthy diet, what does 'moderation' mean?
Limiting intake of things that may harm health
Including varied foods from each food group
Moderation means limiting nutrients and foods that may harm health; the other options define adequacy, balance and diversity.
fitness-health-0150: Which WHO healthy-diet principle means balancing total energy intake with energy expenditure?
Balance means matching energy intake to expenditure and balancing protein, fats and carbohydrates.
fitness-health-0151: Which does the World Health Organization give as an example of whole grains?
WHO examples of whole grains include unprocessed maize, millet, oats, wheat and brown rice.
fitness-health-0152: Which is an example of pulses mentioned by the World Health Organization?
WHO examples of pulses include lentils, chickpeas, beans and dried peas; maize, millet and oats are grains.
fitness-health-0153: Which does the World Health Organization include among 'free sugars' whose intake should be limited?
Sugar naturally present in honey and fruit juices
Milk sugar in plain unsweetened yogurt
Free sugars include those added to food and those naturally present in honey, syrups and fruit juices.
fitness-health-0154: What is the WHO position on using non-sugar sweeteners such as sucralose and stevia to reduce sugar intake?
It advises reducing free sugars without using them
It recommends them as permanent sugar substitutes for everyone
It recommends them especially for children rather than adults and older people
It considers them a type of free sugar
The organization recommends limiting free sugars without resorting to non-sugar sweeteners.
fitness-health-0155: According to the WHO, which two fatty acids can only be obtained from food?
The organization states that linoleic acid and alpha-linolenic acid can only be obtained from food.
fitness-health-0156: Which nutrient does the World Health Organization describe as the basic building blocks of muscles, hormones and enzymes?
Proteins are basic building blocks of structural body components such as muscles, and of hormones and enzymes.
fitness-health-0157: The WHO notes that excessive protein can place a metabolic burden on the body, particularly which organs?
Excessive protein intake can burden the body, especially the kidneys.
fitness-health-0158: According to the WHO, which mineral reduces the negative effects of excess sodium on blood pressure?
The organization states that potassium can reduce the effect of high sodium on blood pressure.
fitness-health-0159: According to the WHO, where does most of the salt people consume in many countries come from?
Fresh fruits and natural juices squeezed at home
Processed foods and frequently eaten foods such as bread
Most salt comes from processed foods such as ready meals and processed meats, and frequently eaten foods such as bread.
fitness-health-0160: How many essential vitamins does the WHO list among the micronutrients the body needs?
The organization mentions about 30 micronutrients, including 13 vitamins and 16 minerals.
fitness-health-0161: What does the WHO encourage using to avoid iodine deficiency?
The organization encourages iodized salt to avoid iodine deficiency.
fitness-health-0162: What does the WHO advise about adding salt and sugar to an infant's complementary foods?
Add small amounts of both daily
The organization states that salt and sugars should not be added to complementary foods.
fitness-health-0163: Until what age does the WHO recommend continued breastfeeding alongside complementary foods?
The organization recommends continued breastfeeding up to two years of age and beyond.
fitness-health-0165: According to 2021 Global Burden of Disease estimates cited by the WHO, what is the world's most common health condition?
The organization states that untreated tooth decay is the most common disease according to 2021 estimates.
fitness-health-0166: According to the WHO, how does tooth decay occur?
Excess calcium deposits inside the tooth and breaks it apart
Heavy chewing of hard foods such as nuts and bones wears teeth away
Plaque converts free sugars into acids that destroy the tooth
Plaque forms on a tooth and converts free sugars into acids that destroy it over time.
fitness-health-0168: Which drink does the WHO encourage as the main drink among measures to prevent oral diseases?
Preventive measures include a diet low in free sugars and choosing water as the main drink.
fitness-health-0169: Why does the WHO encourage protective equipment during sports and cycling as part of oral health?
To prevent dry mouth and lips
To reduce injuries to the face, mouth and teeth
To improve nasal breathing during exertion
Protective equipment reduces the likelihood of facial injuries, including trauma to the mouth and teeth.
fitness-health-0170: What reason does the WHO give for more than a billion young people being at risk of permanent hearing loss?
Staying up late with screens in dark rooms
More than a billion young people face avoidable permanent hearing loss because of unsafe listening practices.
fitness-health-0171: What hearing threshold does the WHO consider normal hearing in both ears?
The WHO considers hearing normal if the hearing threshold is 20 decibels or better in both ears.
fitness-health-0172: What is cerumen, whose impaction may cause hearing impairment according to the WHO?
Impacted cerumen, meaning impacted earwax, is a cause of hearing loss.
fitness-health-0173: What is the name of the WHO initiative to reduce noise-induced hearing loss in recreational settings?
Hearing Is a Right for Everyone Everywhere
The organization promotes safe listening through its Make Listening Safe initiative.
fitness-health-0174: According to the WHO, untreated hearing loss increases the risk of which condition?
Effects of untreated hearing loss include an increased risk of dementia and accelerated cognitive decline.
fitness-health-0175: What proportion of childhood hearing loss does the WHO attribute to preventable causes?
About 60% of childhood hearing loss is attributed to causes preventable through public health measures.
fitness-health-0176: According to the WHO, what are the two main causes of vision impairment and blindness worldwide?
The organization states that refractive errors and cataracts are the two main causes.
fitness-health-0177: According to the WHO, what is the main condition causing near-vision impairment?
Presbyopia is the main cause of near-vision impairment.
fitness-health-0178: According to the WHO, most people with vision impairment and blindness belong to which age group?
Vision loss affects all ages, but most affected people are over 50.
fitness-health-0179: What is a cataract, which chronic ultraviolet exposure may contribute to?
Increasing cloudiness of the eye's lens
Separation of the retina from the eye wall
Increased pressure of fluid inside the eye
A cataract is a disease in which the eye's lens gradually becomes cloudy, impairing vision.
fitness-health-0181: Why does ultraviolet radiation increase at high altitudes?
Thinner air absorbs less of it
The sun is much closer to mountaintops
Ozone concentrates over mountains and doubles it
As altitude increases, the air becomes thinner and absorbs less ultraviolet radiation.
fitness-health-0182: Which surface increases ultraviolet radiation levels by reflecting it?
Reflective surfaces such as water, sand and fresh snow increase ultraviolet radiation levels.
fitness-health-0183: According to the WHO, which statement about ultraviolet radiation on a cloudy day is correct?
It disappears completely as soon as any cloud appears
It is always double the level on a clear day
Its levels may remain high despite clouds
It all turns into infrared radiation
Levels are highest under clear skies, but may be high even with cloud cover.
fitness-health-0184: At what UV index value does the WHO recommend sun protection measures?
Protection is recommended when the index is 3 or above.
fitness-health-0185: According to the WHO, what provides the best protection from sunlight?
The organization states that the best protection is seeking shade and wearing clothing rather than relying on sunscreens.
fitness-health-0186: Why does the WHO recommend a wide-brimmed hat in the sun?
To protect the eyes, face, ears and neck
To increase vitamin D production in sun-exposed skin
A wide-brimmed hat protects the eyes, face, ears and neck.
fitness-health-0188: According to the WHO, what is the most dangerous life-threatening type of skin cancer?
The organization describes cutaneous melanoma as a life-threatening malignant cancer.
fitness-health-0189: What is pterygium, listed by the WHO among the effects of chronic ultraviolet exposure on the eye?
A fleshy tissue growth that may cover part of the cornea
Gradual clouding of the eye's lens
A severe reduction in tear secretion
Chronic redness and swelling of the lower eyelid margin
Pterygium is a fleshy tissue growth that can cover part of the cornea.
fitness-health-0190: What is the WHO position on tanning beds as a way to obtain vitamin D?
They should not be considered an option because they increase skin cancer risk
It considers them safer than direct sunlight
It recommends them for children who do not leave home
It recommends them in winter as a substitute for sunlight
The organization states that tanning beds increase skin cancer risk and are not an option for reaching sufficient vitamin D levels.
fitness-health-0191: At what time of day does the WHO advise limiting time in the sun?
Radiation increases as the sun rises higher; protection measures include reducing time in the sun at midday.
fitness-health-0192: According to the WHO, how do ultraviolet radiation levels change as we approach the equator?
Ultraviolet radiation levels rise as we get closer to the equator.
fitness-health-0193: According to the WHO, why is exposure to small amounts of ultraviolet radiation beneficial to health?
It enables vitamin D production in the body
It strengthens the eye's lens and protects it from cataracts
Small amounts of ultraviolet radiation are necessary for producing vitamin D, which strengthens bones.
fitness-health-0194: What does the WHO say about a safe level of tobacco exposure?
There is no safe level of exposure
A small amount daily is safe and harmless
The organization states that tobacco use is harmful in all forms and there is no safe level of exposure.
fitness-health-0196: According to the WHO, what is the most common form of tobacco use worldwide?
The organization states that cigarette smoking is the most common form of tobacco use.
fitness-health-0197: In its 2026 tobacco fact sheet, how many non-smokers does the WHO estimate die annually from second-hand smoke?
Second-hand smoke causes the premature death of more than 1.6 million people annually.
fitness-health-0198: According to the WHO, what is the most cost-effective way to reduce tobacco use?
The organization considers tobacco taxes the most cost-effective method, particularly among young people and those with low incomes.
fitness-health-0199: What is the WHO view of heated tobacco products?
An approved treatment to help smokers quit
They release toxic substances, and there is no evidence that they help with quitting
Completely safe because they do not burn tobacco at all
Entirely free of nicotine and harmful substances
Heated tobacco products release toxic substances and have not been proven to help smokers quit.
fitness-health-0200: According to the WHO, how do e-cigarettes work?
They heat a liquid to produce an inhaled aerosol
They release only pure water vapor
E-cigarettes heat a liquid inside them to produce an aerosol inhaled by the user; they are harmful and unsafe.
fitness-health-0201: Where are nicotine pouches, promoted as tobacco-free, placed?
They are burned and their smoke inhaled
They are stuck to the skin of the arm
They are dissolved in water and drunk
Nicotine pouches are intended for placement between the gum and lip, and their nicotine may be extracted from tobacco.
fitness-health-0202: In what year did WHO member states adopt the Framework Convention on Tobacco Control?
The Framework Convention was adopted in 2003 and entered into force in 2005.
fitness-health-0203: How many measures are in the WHO MPOWER tobacco-control policy package?
The package includes six measures: monitoring, protection, help with quitting, warnings, advertising bans and tax increases.
fitness-health-0204: According to the WHO, how is body mass index calculated?
Weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared
Height in centimeters divided by weight in kilograms
Weight in kilograms squared divided by height in meters
Weight in kilograms multiplied by height in meters
Body mass index = weight (kg) divided by height squared (m2).
fitness-health-0205: At what body mass index does the WHO classify an adult as having obesity?
For adults, overweight is 25 or more and obesity is 30 or more.
fitness-health-0206: Besides body mass index, which measurement does the WHO mention as helping diagnose obesity?
The organization mentions other measurements, such as waist circumference, that can help diagnose obesity.
fitness-health-0209: What is the coexistence of undernutrition and obesity in the same country, community or household called?
The organization calls this the double burden of malnutrition, which is common in low- and middle-income countries.
fitness-health-0211: According to the WHO, at what reading does high blood pressure begin?
According to the WHO, hypertension is diagnosed when systolic pressure is 140 or higher and/or diastolic pressure is 90 or higher on two different days.
fitness-health-0212: According to the WHO, what is the only way to know if someone has high blood pressure?
A person may have no symptoms, so checking blood pressure is the only way to know.
fitness-health-0213: What does the first, systolic number in a blood pressure reading represent?
Pressure in the vessels while the heart rests between beats
Pressure in the vessels while the heart contracts
The number of heartbeats per minute
The amount of blood the heart pumps per hour
The first number is the pressure during heart contraction; the second, diastolic number is during its rest between beats.
fitness-health-0214: According to the WHO, which risk factor for high blood pressure cannot be changed?
Unchangeable factors include family history, being over 65 and having other diseases such as diabetes.
fitness-health-0215: What is the leading environmental risk factor for high blood pressure mentioned by the WHO?
The organization lists environmental risk factors, most notably environmental pollution.
fitness-health-0216: According to the WHO, what do most people with high blood pressure feel?
Most people have no symptoms, so blood pressure needs to be measured.
fitness-health-0217: When high blood pressure causes arteries in the brain to burst or become blocked, what is the resulting condition called?
Rupture or blockage of arteries supplying the brain causes a stroke.
fitness-health-0223: What does the British NHS say about getting a suntan?
There is no safe way to get one, and it does not protect the skin
It is the best prevention against skin cancer
It fully protects the skin from sunburn
It can only be acquired on cloudy days
The NHS states that there is no safe or healthy way to tan and that a tan does not protect the skin.
fitness-health-0224: What does sun protection factor (SPF) in sunscreens measure?
The product's shelf life after first opening
The sunscreen's water and sweat resistance during swimming
SPF measures protection against ultraviolet B (UVB); protection against UVA is measured in stars.
fitness-health-0225: What minimum sun protection factor (SPF) does the British NHS recommend in sunscreen?
The NHS recommends at least SPF 30 and at least four-star UVA protection.
fitness-health-0226: What does the open-jar symbol with an M and a number on sunscreen packaging mean?
The sunscreen's water and sweat resistance
The number of months it remains usable after opening
The permitted number of daily applications
The symbol shows how many months the sunscreen remains usable after opening.
fitness-health-0227: How often does the British NHS advise reapplying sunscreen?
It is reapplied every two hours because sunlight dries it out, and immediately after leaving the water even if it is water-resistant.
fitness-health-0228: Who does the British NHS advise keeping completely out of strong direct sunlight?
The NHS states that babies under six months should be kept out of strong direct sunlight.
fitness-health-0229: What does the British NHS advise someone with lower back pain?
Stay in bed for many days until pain goes away
Stay active and continue daily activities
Stop walking entirely until the back heals completely
Sleep on a hard floor for two consecutive weeks
It advises staying active, continuing daily activities and avoiding prolonged bed rest.
fitness-health-0230: According to the British NHS, what is a common cause of back pain?
A common cause is an injury such as a muscle strain; fractures, infections and tumors are very rare.
fitness-health-0232: According to the British NHS, how many hours after quitting smoking does blood carbon monoxide return to a non-smoker's level?
After 8 hours it falls by half, and after 48 hours it reaches a non-smoker's level.
fitness-health-0234: What is the first improvement listed in the British NHS guide twenty minutes after quitting smoking?
The pulse starts returning to its normal rate
Lung cancer risk falls by half
After 20 minutes the pulse starts returning to normal.
fitness-health-0235: According to the British NHS, after 28 smoke-free days, how many times more likely is someone to quit for good?
Someone who reaches 28 days without smoking is five times more likely to quit for good.
fitness-health-0236: According to the British NHS, what does second-hand smoke consist of?
Exhaled smoke plus smoke from the burning end of a cigarette
Water vapor condensing on windows after smoking
Ash falling from a cigarette onto clothing and furniture
Smoke that stays in the smoker's lungs and does not leave
Second-hand smoke is exhaled smoke plus sidestream smoke from the cigarette's burning end.
fitness-health-0237: What does the British NHS say about opening windows while smoking indoors?
It protects children but not adults
It fully protects the household from smoke harm
It does not protect others because smoke remains in the air for hours
It is enough if a fan is running in the same room
Opening windows or smoking in another room does not protect others; smoke remains for hours and spreads through the home.
fitness-health-0238: According to the British NHS, which illness are children living with a smoker more likely to develop?
Children in homes with a smoker are more likely to have asthma, chest and ear infections, and coughs.
fitness-health-0239: According to the British NHS, how many irritating, toxic and carcinogenic substances does second-hand smoke contain?
Second-hand smoke is a deadly mixture of more than 5000 irritating, toxic and cancer-causing substances.
fitness-health-0240: On colored nutrition labels on the front of food packages, what does red mean?
The food is naturally organic and additive-free
The food is high in fat, sugar or salt
The food is very low in calories
The food contains no preservatives at all
Red means high, amber means medium and green means low.
fitness-health-0241: In what order are ingredients listed on packaged foods?
By ingredient price, starting with the most expensive
By increasing weight, starting with the least
By decreasing weight, starting with the most
Ingredients are listed in descending order by weight, so the main ingredient comes first.
fitness-health-0242: Under British guidance, how are allergens highlighted in a packaged food's ingredients list?
In smaller letters than other ingredients
Allergens are made distinctive in the ingredients list, most commonly through bold type.
fitness-health-0243: According to the British NHS, approximately how much of our salt comes from packaged and everyday foods we buy, such as bread?
About three quarters of salt comes from packaged and everyday foods such as bread, breakfast cereals and ready meals.
fitness-health-0247: According to the WHO, approximately how many different diseases can contaminated foods cause?
Foods contaminated with bacteria, viruses, parasites or chemicals may cause more than 200 diseases.
fitness-health-0248: According to the WHO, which foods most commonly cause Campylobacter outbreaks?
Cooked rice served hot immediately after cooking
Freshly toasted bread from the oven
The organization lists raw or undercooked poultry and raw milk as leading Campylobacter sources.
fitness-health-0249: Which foodborne bacteria does the WHO state can grow even at refrigeration temperatures?
Listeria occurs in unpasteurized dairy products and some ready-to-eat foods and grows at refrigeration temperatures.
fitness-health-0250: Which fungal toxin may occur in maize and peanuts, with long-term exposure linked to liver cancer?
Aflatoxin B1 is a carcinogenic fungal toxin whose long-term exposure is linked to liver cancer.
fitness-health-0251: According to the WHO, where does methylmercury in food mainly come from?
Whole grains such as wheat, barley, maize and oats
Methylmercury mainly comes from seafood, particularly predatory fish.
fitness-health-0252: Which is a source of lead exposure in food mentioned by the WHO?
Clear glass water bottles refilled at home
Sources include spices adulterated with lead chromate and lead leaching from recycled aluminum cookware.
fitness-health-0253: What is the name of WHO guidance to ensure food safety in homes, restaurants and markets?
Ten Rules for Healthy Cooking at Home and in Restaurants
The organization calls for following its Five Keys to Safer Food.
fitness-health-0254: Diabetes is a chronic disease occurring when which organ cannot produce enough insulin, or when the body cannot use it effectively?
Diabetes occurs when the pancreas cannot produce enough insulin or the body cannot use it effectively.
fitness-health-0255: According to the WHO, what proportion of people with diabetes have type 2?
More than 95% of people with diabetes have type 2.
fitness-health-0256: What does the WHO state about preventing type 1 diabetes?
It is completely prevented by exercise
It is prevented by avoiding white sugar
It is prevented by drinking plenty of water
The organization states that the causes of type 1 and its prevention methods are unknown.
fitness-health-0257: According to the WHO, which symptoms may indicate diabetes?
Symptoms include intense thirst, frequent urination, blurred vision, tiredness and unintentional weight loss.
fitness-health-0258: On what date is World Diabetes Day observed?
The organization mentions observing World Diabetes Day on 14 November.
fitness-health-0259: According to the WHO, why do many people with diabetes develop foot problems?
Nerve damage and poor blood flow
Nerve damage and poor circulation may cause foot ulcers and lead to amputation.
fitness-health-0261: According to the WHO, why has trans fat use in processed foods increased?
It protects the heart and strengthens artery walls
It is rich in fat-soluble vitamins
It is cheaper and stays solid at room temperature
Trans fats are cheaper than healthier fats and remain solid at room temperature; they have no known health benefits.
fitness-health-0262: According to the WHO, how are trans fats produced industrially?
By fermenting oil with beneficial bacteria for weeks
By cooling vegetable oil until it freezes into solid pieces
By partially hydrogenating vegetable oil into a more solid fat
By mixing oil with sugar and salt and heating it gently for a long time
They are produced by partial hydrogenation: adding hydrogen to vegetable oil.
fitness-health-0263: According to the WHO, what is the natural source of trans fats?
Meat and dairy products from ruminants
Ruminants such as cattle and sheep are the source of naturally occurring trans fats in meat and dairy.
fitness-health-0264: What daily duration of awake tummy time does the British NHS recommend for a baby not yet crawling?
At least half an hour of tummy time, spread throughout the day, is recommended.
fitness-health-0265: According to the British NHS, for at least how many minutes daily should children aged one to two be active?
Toddlers should be active for at least 180 minutes (3 hours) daily.
fitness-health-0267: Which activity does the British NHS consider light activity for older adults?
Examples of light activity include moving around the home, slow walking, cleaning and making the bed.
fitness-health-0268: On at least how many days a week does the British NHS recommend activities improving strength, balance and flexibility for older adults?
Older adults are advised to do strength, balance and flexibility activities on at least two days a week.
fitness-health-0270: Which exercise is an example of aerobic exercise?
Sprinting at maximum speed for ten seconds
Aerobic exercise examples include middle- and long-distance running, swimming, cycling and walking.
fitness-health-0271: What substance does anaerobic exercise cause to accumulate in muscles?
During intense exertion, lactic acid (lactate) production exceeds its removal rate, so it accumulates in muscles.
fitness-health-0272: How does anaerobic exercise generally differ from aerobic exercise?
It is always practiced in water
It is much less intense and lasts much longer
It requires virtually no muscular effort
It is more intense and shorter in duration
Anaerobic exercise is more intense but shorter in duration than aerobic exercise.
fitness-health-0273: In which swimming stroke do both legs move up and down together in the 'dolphin kick'?
In butterfly, the arms move symmetrically and the legs move together in a dolphin kick.
fitness-health-0274: Which swimming stroke resembles a frog's movement and is the slowest competitive stroke?
Breaststroke is sometimes called the frog stroke; it is the slowest competitive stroke and is thought to be the oldest.
fitness-health-0275: What is backstroke's advantage and disadvantage?
Clear view of the direction but difficulty breathing
Maximum speed but much splashing on the face
Easy breathing but inability to see the direction
Backstroke makes breathing easy, but the swimmer cannot see where they are going.
fitness-health-0276: Which swimming stroke is generally the fastest of the main strokes performed face down?
Front crawl is generally the fastest stroke, so it is used in freestyle races.
fitness-health-0277: Which main muscles do push-ups, raising and lowering the body with the arms, work?
Only the neck, jaw and upper back muscles
Push-ups mainly work the pectorals, triceps and anterior deltoids.
fitness-health-0278: What is muscle pain and stiffness that peaks one to three days after unfamiliar exercise called?
Delayed onset muscle soreness (DOMS) is most intense between 24 and 72 hours after exercise.
fitness-health-0279: What does VO2 max measure in physical fitness?
Top speed in a hundred-meter run
Maximum oxygen consumption rate during exertion
VO2 max is the maximum oxygen consumption rate achievable during physical exertion, reflecting heart and lung fitness.
fitness-health-0280: According to the American Heart Association, what is a normal adult resting heart rate?
The American Heart Association states that a normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute.
fitness-health-0281: What is a resting heart rate below 60 beats per minute called?
Bradycardia is a resting rate below 60; tachycardia is above 100.
fitness-health-0282: Which exercise lowers the hips from standing and then rises, and is fundamental to strengthening the lower body?
Squats strengthen the quadriceps, gluteals and lower body muscles.
fitness-health-0283: Which exercise holds the body still in a push-up-like position to strengthen the core?
The plank is a static (isometric) core-strengthening exercise in a position resembling a push-up.
fitness-health-0284: What is meant by isometric (static) exercise?
Exercise performed only with free weights
Muscle contraction without a visible change in joint angle
Rapid repeated joint movement in different directions
Isometric exercise is a static muscle contraction in which neither muscle length nor joint angle changes.
fitness-health-0285: In which exercise is one leg forward with the knee bent and foot flat, while the other extends behind?
The lunge position has one leg forward with a bent knee and foot on the ground, and the other behind.
fitness-health-0286: Which exercise combines squatting, pushing the feet back into a plank, then returning and standing?
The burpee is a full-body exercise in four steps: squat, plank, squat, stand.
fitness-health-0287: What is another name for the exercise involving jumping with the legs apart and hands raised overhead, then returning?
The jumping jack is also known as a star jump.
fitness-health-0288: Using body weight as resistance with little or no equipment
Practicing exclusively underwater in deep pools
Calisthenics is strength training using body weight as resistance, such as push-ups, pull-ups and sit-ups.
fitness-health-0289: Which exercise tool is a cast-iron ball with a handle on top, resembling a cannonball?
A kettlebell is a cast-iron or steel ball with a handle on top.
fitness-health-0290: Which device counts a person's steps by detecting hand or hip movement?
A pedometer counts each step by detecting hand or hip movement.
fitness-health-0291: Where did the popular goal of ten thousand steps a day originate?
Military instructions for soldiers in wars
A marketing campaign by a pedometer manufacturer
This goal originated in a pedometer manufacturer's marketing campaign; evidence indicates that most benefits occur at about 7000 steps.
fitness-health-0292: Which Swedish training method alternates faster and slower running on natural terrain?
Fartlek is a Swedish training method alternating faster and slower running over level and elevated terrain.
fitness-health-0293: In which two places is glycogen mainly stored in the human body?
Glycogen is the main storage form of glucose and is made and stored mainly in the liver and skeletal muscles.
fitness-health-0294: Which is the only part of a whole grain retained in refined grains?
A whole grain contains endosperm, germ and bran, while a refined grain retains only the endosperm.
fitness-health-0295: How many essential amino acids cannot be made by the human body and must come from food?
There are nine essential amino acids, including leucine, lysine and tryptophan.
fitness-health-0296: In which sleep stage are vivid dreams common and most body muscles relaxed?
Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep features rapid eye movements, relaxed muscles and vivid dreams.
fitness-health-0297: Approximately how long does one sleep cycle last in adults?
REM and non-REM sleep alternate in a cycle lasting about 90 minutes in adults.
fitness-health-0299: What are the main external influences regulating the body's circadian rhythm, or biological clock?
The circadian rhythm is internal but is regulated by external influences, principally light and temperature.
fitness-health-0300: Which hormone is secreted in the brain at night and plays a crucial role in regulating the sleep-wake cycle?
Melatonin is a hormone secreted at night by the pineal gland and regulates the sleep-wake cycle.
fitness-health-0302: What body mass index range is classified as normal weight for adults?
The common classification is underweight below 18.5, normal 18.5-24.9, overweight 25-29.9 and obesity 30 or above.
fitness-health-0303: Why may body mass index be misleading when applied to some individuals?
It relies on measuring head circumference and foot size together
It is calculated from age and sex alone
It requires a laboratory blood test
It does not distinguish muscle mass from fat
Its limitations include being less useful for people with high muscle mass, abdominal obesity or short stature.
fitness-health-0304: What is the main difference between soluble and insoluble dietary fiber?
Soluble fiber is in meat and insoluble fiber in plants
Soluble fiber dissolves in water and is fermented by colon bacteria
Insoluble fiber raises blood sugar very quickly
Insoluble fiber is completely digested by stomach enzymes
Soluble fiber dissolves in water and is usually fermented in the colon by bacteria.
fitness-health-0305: Which fiber in oats and barley has been shown to lower harmful cholesterol when consumed regularly?
Regular consumption of beta-glucan from oats or barley lowers low-density lipoprotein cholesterol.
fitness-health-0307: What is the amount of energy the body needs for vital functions at complete rest called?
Basal metabolic rate is the energy needed to keep the body functioning at rest: breathing, circulation and temperature regulation.
fitness-health-0309: What distinguishes Nordic walking, which originated in Finland?
Using two special poles resembling ski poles
Walking barefoot on snow in winter
Walking backward to strengthen the legs
Nordic walking is a form of walking that works the whole body using specially designed poles resembling ski poles.
fitness-health-0311: Which muscles are primarily targeted by sit-ups?
The sit-up is an endurance exercise to strengthen and tone abdominal muscles.
fitness-health-0312: Which exercise lifts a weight from the ground to hip level and then returns it to the ground?
The deadlift is a strength exercise lifting a weight from the ground to the hips and returning it.
fitness-health-0314: Wearing sunglasses indoors and in dark places
Vitamin K deficiency in the daily diet
Prolonged uninterrupted focus on nearby screens
It results from prolonged uninterrupted focus on a nearby screen, preventing the eye muscles from resting.
fitness-health-0315: From which tree is the well-known siwak (tooth-cleaning stick) taken?
The miswak is a tooth-cleaning stick taken from the arak tree (Salvadora persica).
fitness-health-0318: Before becoming exercise equipment, what was the treadmill used for historically?
Pumping fresh air into deep mines
Training soldiers to swim in flowing rivers
Harnessing human or animal power to grind grain
Treadmills were historically used to harness animal or human power, often for grinding grain.
fitness-health-0319: Which free-weight tool is often used in pairs, one in each hand?
A dumbbell is a free weight used singly or in pairs, one in each hand.
fitness-health-0320: What is the increase in skeletal muscle size through growth of its cells called?
Muscle hypertrophy is an increase in skeletal muscle size through enlargement of its cells, a focus of bodybuilding.
fitness-health-0321: In endurance sports such as long-distance running, how is 'hitting the wall' traditionally explained?
Increased vitamin C in the blood
The lungs suddenly filling with fluid
Depletion of the body's glycogen stores
A sharp drop in skin temperature from heavy sweating
Hitting the wall is traditionally thought to result from glycogen depletion; a second wind comes when fat becomes the energy source.
fitness-health-0322: What may result when long-distance runners drink more water than their kidneys excrete?
Excess water dilutes blood sodium, a condition called exercise-associated hyponatremia.
fitness-health-0323: How was physical fitness defined before the Industrial Revolution?
The ability to perform daily tasks without excessive fatigue
The ability to lift huge weights overhead
Tall stature and a large physique
It was formerly defined as the ability to carry out daily tasks without excessive fatigue or lethargy.
fitness-health-0326: According to the WHO, perceived temperatures in sunlight may exceed shade temperatures by approximately how many degrees Celsius?
The organization warns that perceived temperatures in sunlight may be 10 to 15 degrees Celsius higher.
fitness-health-0327: Above what temperature does the WHO advise against using electric fans because they increase body heat?
The organization states that fans should only be used if the temperature is below 40 degrees Celsius.
fitness-health-0328: What air-conditioner setting does the WHO suggest with a fan, making the room feel cooler and reducing electricity use?
