Setting the air conditioner to 27 degrees with a fan makes the room feel about 4 degrees cooler and saves electricity.
fitness-health-0329: What does the WHO warn against regarding children in hot weather?
Leaving them in parked vehicles even briefly
Dressing them in light, loose, pale clothing
Giving them water whenever they ask
Bathing them with cold water at midday
The organization warns against leaving children or animals in parked vehicles even briefly, because temperatures rise quickly.
fitness-health-0330: How many daytime hours does the WHO advise spending in a cool place during heatwaves?
The organization advises spending two to three daytime hours in a cool place.
fitness-health-0331: According to the WHO, what is the leading cause of weather-related deaths?
The organization states that heat stress is the leading cause of weather-related deaths.
fitness-health-0332: According to the WHO, what is the greatest risk to drinking-water safety?
Microbial contamination of drinking water from feces is the greatest risk to its safety.
fitness-health-0333: According to the WHO, what are the most important chemical hazards in drinking water?
The most important chemical hazards arise from arsenic, fluoride or nitrate.
fitness-health-0334: In what year did the UN General Assembly explicitly recognize the human right to water and sanitation?
The General Assembly explicitly recognized this right in 2010.
fitness-health-0337: According to the WHO, which disease can contaminated drinking water transmit?
Contaminated water may transmit diseases such as diarrhea, cholera, dysentery, typhoid and polio.
fitness-health-0338: According to the WHO, what is the leading cause of death worldwide?
The organization states that cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death worldwide.
fitness-health-0339: According to the WHO, what most commonly causes the blood-vessel blockage leading to heart attacks and strokes?
Air collecting in vessels after exertion
Fatty deposits building up on inner vessel walls
Calcium deposits in bones near the heart
Blood vessels contracting from drinking cold water
The most common cause is fatty deposits building up on the inner walls of vessels supplying the heart or brain.
fitness-health-0340: According to the WHO, what causes rheumatic heart disease?
Vitamin D deficiency in early childhood
Rheumatic fever resulting from streptococcal infection
It results from damage to heart valves and muscle due to rheumatic fever following streptococcal infection, often starting with a sore throat.
fitness-health-0341: According to the WHO, what does peripheral arterial disease affect?
Vessels supplying the arms and legs
Peripheral arterial disease affects vessels supplying the arms and legs.
fitness-health-0342: What is another name for noncommunicable diseases?
Noncommunicable diseases are also known as chronic diseases and usually last a long time.
fitness-health-0343: According to the WHO, what are the four main groups of noncommunicable diseases?
Influenza, diabetes, asthma, and skin, lung and blood cancers
Malaria, cancers, diabetes and cardiovascular diseases
Cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes
Tuberculosis, heart disease, diabetes and cancers of various types
The main types are cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes.
fitness-health-0344: According to the WHO, what is the leading metabolic risk factor for deaths from noncommunicable diseases worldwide?
High blood pressure is the leading factor, accounting for about 25% of noncommunicable disease deaths, followed by high blood sugar and then overweight.
fitness-health-0345: According to the WHO, what is the most important environmental risk factor for noncommunicable diseases?
Indoor and outdoor air pollution is the most important environmental risk factor.
fitness-health-0346: By how much does Sustainable Development Goal target 3.4 aim to reduce premature deaths from noncommunicable diseases by 2030?
Target 3.4 aims to reduce premature deaths from these diseases by one third by 2030.
fitness-health-0347: Which age group does the British NHS describe as the most sedentary, spending ten or more hours daily sitting or lying down?
The NHS states that people over 65 spend 10 or more hours daily sitting or lying down.
fitness-health-0348: After what age does the WHO state that physical inactivity increases in both men and women?
Physical inactivity increases in both sexes after age 60.
fitness-health-0349: Besides physical activity and sedentary behavior, what do WHO guidelines for children under five cover?
Guidelines for children under five address physical activity, sedentary behavior and sleep over 24 hours.
fitness-health-0352: Which of the two daily toothbrushing times does the British NHS especially emphasize?
The NHS specifies brushing last thing before sleep, as nighttime brushing is important, and once more during the day.
fitness-health-0354: According to the WHO, which groups are more exposed to extreme heat because of their work?
Office workers in air conditioning all day
The organization mentions outdoor workers, manual workers, athletes and civil protection staff.
fitness-health-0356: How does the WHO advise using night air during heatwaves?
Run ovens at night to dry out humidity
Close windows at night and open them at midday
Open windows after dark when it is cooler outside
Turn off all fans throughout the night
Windows are opened after dark when the outdoor temperature is lower than indoors.
fitness-health-0357: What degree of hearing loss in the better-hearing ear does the WHO consider disabling?
Disabling hearing loss is greater than 35 decibels in the better-hearing ear.
fitness-health-0358: Which two interventions does the WHO consider among the most cost-effective in eye care?
Colored contact lenses and dark sunglasses
Daily vitamin drops and eye movement exercises
Warm eyelid compresses and regular massage
Correcting refractive errors with glasses and cataract surgery are among the most cost-effective health interventions.
fitness-health-0359: What does the British NHS say about frozen fruit and vegetables when counting five daily portions?
They count just like fresh ones
They never count, regardless of quantity
They count as only half a portion each time
They count only for children, not adults
They do not need to be fresh; frozen produce and produce canned in water or natural juice also count.

arabic-language-0145: When kana and its sister verbs enter an Arabic nominal sentence, how do they affect it?
They put the subject in the genitive and predicate in the nominative
They put the subject in the accusative and predicate in the nominative
They put both subject and predicate in the accusative
They put the subject in the nominative and predicate in the accusative
Kana and its sister verbs are modifying verbs: they put the original subject, called their noun, in the nominative, and the predicate in the accusative.
arabic-language-0146: In 'inna al-ilma nurun' (indeed, knowledge is light), how is 'al-ilma' parsed?
Inna puts the original subject, called its noun, in the accusative, and the predicate in the nominative.
arabic-language-0147: In Arabic, zanna and its sister verbs put what in the accusative?
The subject, while making the predicate nominative
Two objects originally forming a subject and predicate
Zanna and its sister verbs enter a subject-predicate construction and put both in the accusative as their two objects.
arabic-language-0151: In 'kafa'a al-mudiru al-talibati' (the headteacher rewarded the female students), what marks the accusative of 'al-talibati'?
The sound feminine plural takes kasrah instead of fathah in the accusative.
arabic-language-0154: An Arabic diptote usually takes which genitive marker?
A diptote does not take nunation and takes fathah instead of kasrah in the genitive unless it is in a construct phrase or definite with al-.
arabic-language-0155: Which Arabic word is a diptote?
A word ending with the extended feminine alif, such as sahra', is a diptote.
arabic-language-0156: In 'waqaftu ihtiraman lil-mu'allim' (I stood out of respect for the teacher), how is 'ihtiraman' parsed?
An object of purpose is an accusative verbal noun stating why the action occurs.
arabic-language-0157: In 'safartu sabahan' (I traveled in the morning), how is 'sabahan' parsed?
An adverbial object is an accusative noun indicating the time or place of an action.
arabic-language-0159: What grammatical case does the subject of a verb take in Arabic?
The subject is a nominative noun indicating who performed the action.
arabic-language-0160: In 'kutiba al-darsu' (the lesson was written), how is 'al-darsu' parsed?
The passive subject replaces the omitted active subject and takes its nominative case with a passive verb.
arabic-language-0161: What is an Arabic word whose ending changes according to its position in the sentence called?
An inflected word changes its ending according to grammatical influences; an indeclinable word keeps one ending.
arabic-language-0164: Which Arabic demonstrative is used for the masculine dual in the nominative?
Hadhani is the masculine dual nominative form; hadhayni is accusative and genitive.
arabic-language-0165: A noun immediately following an Arabic preposition is:
Prepositions put the following noun in the genitive.
arabic-language-0166: In 'ja'a rajulun karimun' (a generous man came), how is 'karimun' parsed?
An adjective is a dependent word describing a noun and following its grammatical case.
arabic-language-0167: Which Arabic word is used for semantic emphasis?
Words of semantic emphasis include nafs, ayn, kull, jami', kila and kilta.
arabic-language-0168: Which is one of the two regular Arabic exclamation patterns?
The two regular exclamation patterns are ma af'alahu and af'il bihi.
arabic-language-0169: The Arabic verbal noun 'hayhata' has the meaning of which past-tense verb?
Hayhata is a word functioning as a past-tense verb meaning became far away.
arabic-language-0170: The Arabic word 'sah' functions as an imperative meaning:
Sah is a word functioning as an imperative meaning be quiet.
arabic-language-0171: In rhetoric, what is similarity in pronunciation between two words with different meanings called?
Paronomasia is when two words resemble each other in pronunciation but differ in meaning.
arabic-language-0172: What is combining a thing and its opposite in speech called?
Antithesis combines two opposites in speech.
arabic-language-0173: What is agreement in the final letter of two prose clauses called?
Rhymed prose is agreement in the final letter of prose clauses.
arabic-language-0174: How many components of a simile do rhetoricians identify?
A simile has four components: the thing compared, what it is compared to, the comparison marker and the point of resemblance.
arabic-language-0175: A metaphor is originally a simile in which:
One of the two compared elements is omitted
The point of resemblance is stated
There are several things being compared
A metaphor is a simile with one of its two compared elements omitted.
arabic-language-0176: Which Arabic relative pronoun is specific to the feminine singular?
Allatī is feminine singular, and alladhī is masculine singular.
arabic-language-0177: From a three-root-letter verb, the Arabic comparative or superlative is formed on which pattern?
The comparative or superlative is formed on the af'al pattern to indicate sharing a quality and exceeding in it.
arabic-language-0178: The active participle of an Arabic three-root-letter verb follows which pattern?
The active participle of a three-root-letter verb follows the fa'il pattern, as in katib.
arabic-language-0179: The passive participle of an Arabic three-root-letter verb follows which pattern?
The passive participle of a three-root-letter verb follows the maf'ul pattern, as in maktub.
arabic-language-0181: What is a verb that requires only a subject and no direct object called?
An intransitive verb does not extend to a direct object and requires only its subject.
arabic-language-0182: In Arabic, when is hamzat al-wasl pronounced?
At the start of speech, but dropped in connected speech
In connected speech, but dropped at the start
Hamzat al-wasl enables pronunciation before a consonant without a vowel; it is pronounced initially and dropped in connected speech.
arabic-language-0183: What is merging an unvoweled consonant into an identical voweled consonant to form one doubled consonant called?
Assimilation merges one consonant into another so they become one doubled consonant.
arabic-language-0185: In rhetoric, what is an expression intended to convey an implication of its meaning, while its literal meaning remains possible?
Kinayah conveys an implication while allowing the literal meaning; for example, saying someone has much ash indirectly describes generosity.
arabic-language-0186: In 'qara'tu al-kitaba' (I read the book), how is 'al-kitaba' parsed?
A direct object is an accusative noun receiving the subject's action.
arabic-language-0187: In 'tara'ra'a al-sabiyyu fi bayti ilm', what does tara'ra'a mean?
Tara'ra'a describes a boy developing, growing up and maturing.
arabic-language-0188: Wished for the same without him losing it
Envied him and wished he would lose it
Ghabt means wishing for a situation like another person's without wanting them to lose it.
arabic-language-0189: When describing a traveler, the Arabic verb 'qafala' means:
Qafala, yaqfilu, qufulan means returned from a journey; qafilah is a returning company of travelers.
arabic-language-0190: The Arabic phrase 'abaqa al-abdu' means the enslaved person:
Abaqa describes an enslaved person escaping from his master.
arabic-language-0191: The Arabic phrase 'wajama al-rajulu' means the man:
Laughed until his back teeth showed
Shouted at the top of his voice
Wajama means being unable to speak from intense anger or grief.
arabic-language-0192: To 'awjasa' fear within himself means he:
Awjasa fear within himself means he concealed it.
arabic-language-0193: The Arabic phrase 'azifa al-rahilu' means departure:
Azifa means drew near or approached; al-azifah is derived from it.
arabic-language-0194: The Arabic phrase 'afalati al-shamsu' means the sun:
Reached the middle of the sky
arabic-language-0195: What does 'tanassala' from a sin mean?
Tanassala from a sin means to disclaim it.
arabic-language-0196: Held it in his right hand
Ta'abbata an object means to place it under one's armpit.
arabic-language-0197: Sadala or asdala a garment means to let it hang down.
arabic-language-0198: Ayna'a means that fruit matured and ripened.
arabic-language-0199: Inbalaja of dawn means to become bright and radiant.
arabic-language-0200: Al-qahqara means going backward; taqahqara means to retreat.
arabic-language-0201: What does a horseman 'ardafa' his companion mean?
Went ahead of him on the road
Ardafahu means to seat someone behind oneself; a radif is a passenger behind the rider.
arabic-language-0202: What kind of man is described as 'al-alma'i'?
Al-alma'i is brilliant and quick-witted, making guesses that prove correct.
arabic-language-0203: What kind of man is an 'al-jihbidh'?
Al-jihbidh is a discerning expert in intricate matters.
arabic-language-0204: What kind of person is an 'al-nihrir'?
Al-nihrir is skilled, proficient, sensible and experienced.
arabic-language-0205: What kind of man is an 'al-sindid'?
arabic-language-0206: Al-ri'did is a coward who trembles in battle.
arabic-language-0207: Al-abkam means a person unable to speak.
arabic-language-0208: Someone whose hair has turned gray
Someone whose hand was cut off
arabic-language-0209: One who lived a long life
Thukl means losing a loved one, most commonly a woman losing her child.
arabic-language-0211: Al-shadin is a gazelle fawn that has grown strong and no longer needs its mother.
arabic-language-0212: Al-jarw means the young of dogs and beasts of prey.
arabic-language-0213: 'Al-huwar' is the young of which animal?
Al-huwar is a camel's calf at birth.
arabic-language-0216: 'Al-hijris' is the young of which animal?
arabic-language-0217: 'Al-jahsh' is the young of which animal?
arabic-language-0219: Which animal makes the sound called 'al-thugha'?
Al-thugha is the cry of sheep.
arabic-language-0220: Which bird makes the sound called 'al-na'ib'?
Na'aba of a crow means to cry or call.
arabic-language-0221: Which bird makes the sound called 'al-hadil'?
Al-hadil is the sound of pigeons.
arabic-language-0222: Which animal makes the sound called 'al-fahih'?
A snake's fahih is the sound from its mouth.
arabic-language-0223: Which animal makes the sound called 'al-rugha'?
Al-rugha is the sound made by padded-footed animals such as camels.
arabic-language-0224: Which animal makes the sound called 'al-sahil'?
arabic-language-0225: 'Al-kinas' is the shelter of which animal?
Al-kinas is a sheltered place into which wild gazelles and cattle retreat.
arabic-language-0227: 'Al-wijar' is the den of which animal?
Al-wijar is the den of a hyena, wolf or similar animal.
arabic-language-0228: What kind of person is described as 'al-harim'?
arabic-language-0229: What kind of man is described as 'al-hasif'?
Al-hasif has good judgment and sound intellect.
arabic-language-0230: Al-ashar means insolent arrogance, or, according to another definition, its extreme form.
arabic-language-0231: Al-mirqat is a step used to climb.
arabic-language-0232: What span of time is a 'hiqba'?
A hiqba is a period of unspecified duration; its plural is hiqab.
arabic-language-0233: On what was a 'hawdaj' passenger carriage placed?
A cart pulled by a donkey
A hawdaj is a carriage for women placed on a camel's back.
arabic-language-0234: What is the craft of an 'iskaf'?
arabic-language-0235: Someone unable to see at night
Someone who works with their left hand
Al-a'sar is a person who works with their left hand.
arabic-language-0236: What does 'al-ghill' in the heart mean?
Al-ghill is concealed resentment in the heart.
arabic-language-0238: Al-daydan means regular practice and habit.
arabic-language-0239: Meeting someone awwal wahla means at the very first moment.
arabic-language-0240: What does 'fayna' mean in 'bayna al-fayna wa-al-ukhra'?
Al-fayna means a time or moment.
arabic-language-0241: Al-jadhwa is a thick piece of wood containing fire; it is also defined as an ember.
arabic-language-0242: What is the 'dhubala' in a lamp?
Al-dhubala is the wick that is lit.
arabic-language-0243: What kind of vegetation is called 'hashim'?
arabic-language-0245: Al-bukra is early morning, the beginning of the day.
arabic-language-0246: Al-'ashiyy is the end of the day.
arabic-language-0249: What kind of wind is an 'i'sar'?
A cold wind from the north
One raising dust in a column
An i'sar is a wind that raises clouds or dust into the sky like a column.
arabic-language-0250: Al-wadq means rain of any intensity, heavy or light.
arabic-language-0251: What is the original meaning of 'al-ra'il', from which 'al-ra'il al-awwal' is derived?
Al-ra'il is the leading group of horses; it was then used figuratively for a pioneering group.
arabic-language-0252: A shield held in the hand
Al-mighfar is armor mail woven to fit the head.
arabic-language-0253: Al-kinana is a small leather quiver for arrows.
arabic-language-0254: The sea's lujja is its main body of water.
arabic-language-0255: Al-marfa is a place where ships dock.
arabic-language-0256: What is a 'shi'b' in the terrain?
Al-shi'b is a mountain path, also defined as a gap between two mountains.
arabic-language-0257: What is a 'fajj' in the terrain?
A broad passage between two mountains
Al-fajj is a broad passage between two mountains.
arabic-language-0258: What is a 'kathib' in the desert?
Al-kathib is sand accumulated into a mound.
arabic-language-0259: What part of a mountain is its 'qunna'?
The qunna of anything is its top, as with a mountain's summit.
arabic-language-0260: A pool left behind by a flood
Al-ghadir is a pool of water left behind by a flood.
arabic-language-0261: Ma' ma'in is visible water flowing over the earth's surface.
arabic-language-0262: Ujaj water is salty and bitter.
arabic-language-0265: What kind of rain is a 'dima'?
A dima is rain without thunder or lightning, lasting at least a third of a day or night.
arabic-language-0266: Nadra means beauty and freshness; nadir means beautiful and tender.
arabic-language-0267: Warif shade is broad and spreading.
arabic-language-0268: What is the original meaning of 'hadiqa'?
A hadiqa is a garden with trees, also defined as any land with fruit trees surrounded by a barrier.
arabic-language-0269: A ghusn branches off a tree's trunk; its plurals are aghsan and ghusun.
arabic-language-0270: What is the singular of 'nakhil' (palm trees)?
Nakhl and nakhil are collective forms; the singular is nakhla.
arabic-language-0271: Open space with nothing to hide behind
Al-'ara is open space with nothing to conceal a person.
arabic-language-0272: Al-qafr is empty land without water, people or pasture.
arabic-language-0275: What is a 'hadba' in the terrain?
A broad mountain spreading over the ground
Al-hadba is a mountain spreading broadly over the ground.
arabic-language-0277: Al-wa'r is the opposite of easy terrain: a hard, difficult place.
arabic-language-0279: What is the original meaning of 'al-khalij'?
Al-khalij is water branching off the main body, or an inlet of the sea.
arabic-language-0280: Al-dahdah is a small amount of water with a shallow bottom.
arabic-language-0281: Al-salsabil is a drink that passes easily down the throat.
arabic-language-0282: Al-tamy is mud carried by floodwater.
arabic-language-0283: What is the opposite of 'jahl' (ignorance) in dictionaries?
Ignorance is the opposite of knowledge.
arabic-language-0284: What is the opposite of war?
War is the opposite of peace.
arabic-language-0285: What is the opposite of nearness?
Nearness is the opposite of distance.
arabic-language-0286: What is the opposite of sweet?
Sweet is the opposite of bitter.
arabic-language-0287: What is the opposite of satiety?
Satiety is the opposite of hunger.
arabic-language-0288: What is the opposite of health?
Health is the opposite of illness.
arabic-language-0289: What is the opposite of truth?
Truth is the opposite of falsehood.
arabic-language-0290: What is the opposite of difficulty?
Ease is the opposite of difficulty.
arabic-language-0291: What is the opposite of light?
Darkness is the opposite of light.
arabic-language-0292: What is the opposite of spaciousness?
Narrowness is the opposite of spaciousness.
arabic-language-0293: What is the opposite of having one's thirst quenched?
Thirst is the opposite of having one's thirst quenched.
arabic-language-0294: What is the opposite of a docile animal?
Unruly is the opposite of docile.
arabic-language-0295: What is the opposite of sadness?
Joy is the opposite of sadness.
arabic-language-0296: What is the opposite of 'hija' (satirical invective)?
Praise is the opposite of satirical invective.
arabic-language-0297: What is the opposite of correctness?
Error is the opposite of correctness.
arabic-language-0298: What is the opposite of disparagement?
Praise is the opposite of disparagement.
arabic-language-0300: What is the opposite of new in dictionaries?
New is the opposite of khalaq, meaning worn out.
arabic-language-0301: What is the opposite of moist?
Moist is the opposite of dry.
arabic-language-0302: What is the opposite of giving?
Withholding is the opposite of giving.
arabic-language-0303: What is the opposite of fewness?
Abundance is the opposite of fewness.
arabic-language-0304: What is the opposite of prohibition?
Command is the opposite of prohibition.
arabic-language-0305: What is the opposite of corruption?
Soundness is the opposite of corruption.
arabic-language-0306: What is the opposite of sleep?
Wakefulness is the opposite of sleep.
arabic-language-0307: What is the opposite of clarity?
Turbidity is the opposite of clarity.
arabic-language-0309: Al-su'dud means honor, glory and leadership.
proverbs-0001: To whom do Arabs apply the proverb 'Sinimmar's reward'?
Someone who builds for others but nothing for himself
Someone who repays wrongdoing with kindness
Someone who repays kindness with harm
Someone who promises a gift then breaks his promise

It is related that Sinimmar built al-Khawarnaq for al-Nu'man, who threw him from its top after he finished so he could not build its like for another. Hence the proverb for repaying kindness with harm.
proverbs-0002: What was the occupation of Hunayn in the proverb 'He returned with Hunayn's two shoes'?
Abu 'Ubayd said Hunayn was a shoemaker from al-Hira. A Bedouin bargained with him over two shoes and they disagreed, so Hunayn tricked him by leaving the shoes along his route.
proverbs-0003: To whom did al-Maydani attribute 'The sword preceded the reproach', said when people blamed him for killing his son's killer in the sanctuary?
Al-Maydani stated that Dabba ibn Udd said it when people blamed him for killing his son's killer in the sanctuary.
proverbs-0004: Who was Shann in the proverb 'Shann matched Tabaqa'?
A chief of Quraysh before Islam
A shrewd and wise Arab man
Al-Sharqi ibn al-Qutami said Shann was a shrewd and wise Arab man who traveled until he found Tabaqa, a woman matching his intelligence.
proverbs-0006: Which woman was originally addressed by 'In summer you wasted the milk'?
Al-Maydani stated that Dakhtanus bint Laqit ibn Zurara was addressed with this proverb when she asked her first husband for a milking animal after leaving him.
proverbs-0007: What does the proverb 'Give the bow to its maker' mean?
Do not withhold gifts from someone who treated you well
Leave a matter to its owner when he becomes angry with it
Give everyone their due without delay
Seek help with your work from those knowledgeable and skilled in it
Al-Maydani said it means to seek help with one's work from those knowledgeable and skilled in it.
proverbs-0008: Who was Juhayza in the proverb 'Juhayza ended every speaker's speech'?
A she-camel that bolted and broke up a gathering
A slave woman who brought news making their speeches unnecessary
A soothsayer who settled disputes between tribes
A famous woman orator from Banu Tamim
People gathered to make speeches about reconciliation. A slave woman named Juhayza arrived with news that the killer had been killed, making their speeches unnecessary.
proverbs-0009: To whom is 'In our land, weak birds become eagles' applied?
The strong who lose their prestige in another land
A stranger honored away from his own land and people
Someone arrogant toward his people who is humiliated among them
The weak who become strong and the lowly who gain honor after humiliation

Al-bughath are weak birds inferior to the Egyptian vulture; istansara means to become eagle-like in strength. The proverb applies to the weak becoming strong and the lowly gaining honor after humiliation.
proverbs-0010: According to al-Maydani, to whom does 'Behind the hill lies what lies behind it' apply?
Someone revealing their own hidden affair
Someone seeking something in the wrong place
Someone so cautious that an opportunity passes
A slave woman arranged to meet her companion behind a hill, but her household detained her, so she said this. Al-Maydani says it applies to someone disclosing their own hidden affair.
proverbs-0012: What does 'yuflah' mean in 'Iron is yuflah by iron'?
Falh means splitting, hence fallah for a farmer who splits the earth. The saying means to tackle a difficult matter with something comparable and equally strong.
proverbs-0017: What does 'If your brother is harsh, be gentle' mean?
If your brother gains status, ask his help
If your brother is absent, safeguard his family
If your brother is insulted, personally defend him
If your companion treats you harshly, be gentle and accommodating
Abu 'Ubayd said accommodating a friend is not accepting oppression; it is good character. If he makes things difficult, make them easy.
proverbs-0018: To whom does 'Even a fine horse may stumble' apply?
Someone who errs so much that nothing can be entrusted to him
Someone who rushes a matter, fails and regrets it
Someone usually doing good who then makes a slip
Someone impoverished after wealth who can no longer be generous
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone who usually does good but then makes a slip.
proverbs-0019: According to Abu 'Ubayd, to whom does 'Even a habitual liar may tell the truth' apply?
Someone whose lies people believe for a long time
Someone usually doing wrong who then does a little good
Someone swearing often to convince others
Abu 'Ubayd said it applies to a man usually doing wrong who then does a little good.
proverbs-0021: What meaning did Abu 'Ubayd give to 'The staff comes from the little stick'?
A branch separates from its origin when grown
Abu 'Ubayd said it means a great thing begins small, as in their saying that a mature camel comes from a young camel.
proverbs-0022: What are 'al-zuba' in 'The flood has reached al-zuba'?
Pits dug on high ground to trap lions
Al-zuba is the plural of zubya, a lion-trapping pit dug on high ground beyond water's reach. A flood reaching it is overwhelming; the saying applies to something exceeding its limit.
proverbs-0023: When is 'The girth has passed the two teats' used?
When it is too late to act
A tuby in hoofed animals and beasts of prey corresponds to the teat of other animals. The saying is used when hardship reaches its utmost.
proverbs-0024: What are 'kana'in' in 'Before shooting, the kana'in are filled'?
Kana'in is the plural of kinana, an arrow quiver. The meaning is to prepare for a matter before it happens.
proverbs-0025: What is 'al-fara' in 'All game is in al-fara's belly'?
Ibn al-Sikkit said al-fara is the wild donkey. No larger animal was hunted by people, so it encompassed all other game.
proverbs-0026: What do Arabs mean by 'Until the two qaraz gatherers return'?
Waiting until an absent person returns
Al-Maydani said 'Until the two qaraz gatherers return' and 'Until the spiny-tailed lizard comes to water' both express something never happening.
proverbs-0028: To whom is 'Many a brother of yours was not born of your mother' attributed?
Al-Maydani said this proverb is attributed to Luqman ibn 'Ad and recounted its story.
proverbs-0029: To whom does 'She accused me of her own ailment and slipped away' apply?
Someone catching a disease and infecting another
Someone fleeing an argument they started
Someone accusing another without proof then apologizing
Someone reproaching a companion for a fault they themselves have
One of Ruhm bint al-Khazraj's co-wives said it when Ruhm reproached her for a fault Ruhm herself had. It applies to reproaching another for one's own fault.
proverbs-0030: What does 'shinshina' mean in 'A shinshina I recognize from Akhzam'?
Al-shinshina means nature and habit. Abu Akhzam al-Ta'i said it when his son Akhzam's sons mistreated him, resembling their father.
proverbs-0032: What does 'saqita' mean in 'Every saqita has someone to pick it up'?
An animal straying from its owner
Al-Asma'i said al-saqita is a word in which a person slips, and every word has someone to remember it. The proverb urges care in speech.
proverbs-0033: In 'More faithful than al-Samaw'al', what did al-Samaw'al refuse to surrender even at the cost of his son's life?
Imru' al-Qays entrusted armor to al-Samaw'al. When a king of al-Sham demanded it and took his son hostage, al-Samaw'al refused to surrender it out of faithfulness.
proverbs-0034: Arabs said 'More generous than the two captives of 'Anaza'; who were they?
Hatim al-Ta'i and Ka'b ibn Mama
Al-Ahnaf ibn Qays and Qays ibn 'Asim
Harim ibn Sinan and al-Harith ibn 'Awf
Al-Maydani said the two captives of 'Anaza were Hatim of Tayyi' and Ka'b ibn Mama.
proverbs-0035: What did Ka'b ibn Mama give his companion from al-Namir in preference to himself, becoming proverbial for generosity?
Travelers divided their water during a journey, and Ka'b kept giving the man from al-Namir his own share until Ka'b died of thirst.
proverbs-0037: What was the nickname of Habannaqa, proverbial for foolishness?
Habannaqa was Dhu al-Wada'at. His name was Yazid ibn Tharwan, from Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba.
proverbs-0038: From what did al-Kusa'i make the bow that caused his proverbial regret?
A nab' tree growing from a rock
Al-Kusa'i saw a nab' tree in a rock and admired it. He tended it until he cut it and made a bow, then regretted breaking it.
proverbs-0040: According to Muhammad ibn Habib's account, how far could Zarqa' al-Yamama see?
Muhammad ibn Habib said she was a woman from Jadis who could see something three days' journey away.
proverbs-0042: What escaped from Baqil when he tried to show its price with his hands and tongue?
Baqil bought a gazelle for eleven dirhams. Asked its price, he extended his hands and stuck out his tongue, and the gazelle escaped from under his armpit.
proverbs-0047: What is 'al-anuq', whose eggs Arabs proverbially describe as hard to obtain?
Al-anuq is the Egyptian vulture. Its eggs are hard to obtain because its nests are on mountaintops and in difficult, remote places.
proverbs-0048: Who was made proverbial for dutifulness to his mother in 'More dutiful than ...'?
Al-Maydani said 'More dutiful than al-'Amallas', a man who was dutiful to his mother and carried her on his shoulder.
proverbs-0049: Why did Arabs say 'Bolder than a fly'?
It attacks food before its owners touch it
It lands on a king's nose and a lion's eyelid, returning whenever driven off
It flies in intense heat without concern
It enters houses both day and night
Al-Maydani said it lands on a king's nose and a lion's eyelid and, despite being driven away, returns.
proverbs-0050: According to Abu 'Ubayd, what is 'safir' in 'More cowardly than a safir'?
A strong wind blowing at night
A wolf howling in the dark
A shepherd calling his flock by whistling
Abu 'Ubayd said al-safir means any whistling bird; whistling occurs among small birds and birds hunted as game.
proverbs-0052: Which bird did Arabs make proverbial for caution, saying 'More cautious than ...'?
Their sayings include 'More cautious than a crow'. They relate that a crow told its son to dodge when shot at. It replied, 'I dodge before being shot at.'
proverbs-0053: Which animal is proverbial for deep sleep in 'More sleepy than ...'?
Al-Maydani said the cheetah is the sleepiest creature and its sleep is profound, unlike a dog's.
proverbs-0054: According to al-Maydani, why did Arabs liken humiliation to a peg in flat ground?
It is pulled out when people leave
It cannot be seen from afar
It is left alone in the open
Al-Maydani explained 'More humiliated than a peg in flat ground' by saying that it is constantly hammered.
proverbs-0055: What is 'baydat al-balad', proverbial for lowliness?
A dove's egg fallen from its nest
A spiny-tailed lizard's egg buried in sand
An egg an ostrich abandons in the wilderness
A sandgrouse's egg on barren ground
Al-Maydani said it is an egg an ostrich leaves in the wilderness without returning to it.
proverbs-0056: Why did Arabs say 'More rash than a moth'?
It never stays long on one flower
Al-Maydani said 'More rash than a moth' because it throws itself into fire.
proverbs-0057: What is Thahlan, proverbial for heaviness?
Al-Maydani explained 'Heavier than Thahlan' by identifying it as a mountain in al-'Aliya.
proverbs-0058: What did Arabs make proverbial for spreading widely in 'More widely traveled than ...'?
'More widely traveled than poetry' refers to poetry reaching gatherings and entering tents, traveling the land without provisions.
proverbs-0059: What was the name of the qaraz gatherer of 'Anaza, proverbial for going astray?
Al-Maydani said the man in 'More lost than the qaraz gatherer of 'Anaza' was Yadhkur ibn 'Anaza, who went out gathering qaraz and never returned.
proverbs-0061: According to Abu 'Ubayd, what does 'Horses know their riders best' mean?
A horseman is known only on the battlefield
A person is known by their wealth
Rely on someone who knows the matter
A person can be judged only by their travel companion
Abu 'Ubayd said horses have tested their riders and know the poor rider from the others. The proverb means to rely on someone who knows the matter.
proverbs-0062: Who is credited with first saying 'It has been said, whether true or false'?
Al-Maydani stated that al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir al-Lakhmi first said it to al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad al-'Absi.
proverbs-0064: What is Umm 'Amir in 'Like the protector of Umm 'Amir'?
Umm 'Amir is a hyena. A Bedouin protected it from hunters and fed it, but it betrayed him while he slept.
proverbs-0065: What did 'Urqub promise his brother but withhold, making his promises proverbial?
The fruit of a palm tree
'Urqub told his brother that when the palm produced its first fruit, it would be his. He kept putting him off, then harvested it at night and gave him nothing.
proverbs-0067: He died in his bed and was not killed
He died far from his family
Al-Maydani said it means he died without being killed; its original sense is a man dying in his bed.
proverbs-0068: Who is credited with first saying 'I mean you; listen, neighbor'?
Al-Maydani said Sahl ibn Malik al-Fazari first said it when staying with some groups of Tayyi'.
proverbs-0069: What does 'li-nazirihi' mean in 'Tomorrow is near to its nazir'?
To one who sees it with his eyes
Al-Maydani said it means to one awaiting it; nazartuhu can mean I awaited him.
proverbs-0072: For what is 'Halima's day is no secret' used?
A secret its keeper preserves for ages
A war whose victor is unknown
Halima's day is among the best-known battle days of the Arabs. The saying applies to any widely known, famous matter.
proverbs-0073: Whose wife was Hadham, of the proverb 'The word is what Hadham said'?
Ibn al-Kalbi said the proverb belongs to Lujaym ibn Sa'b, father of Hanifa and 'Ijl, whose wife was Hadham.
proverbs-0075: What is 'al-jadad' in 'Whoever follows al-jadad is safe from stumbling'?
Al-Maydani said al-jadad means level ground. The saying concerns seeking safety.
proverbs-0076: A Bedouin reportedly asked al-Hasan al-Basri to teach him a moderate religion. Which reply became proverbial?
Patience is the key to relief
Religion is ease, so do not be harsh
Little that suffices is better than much that distracts
The best courses are the middle ones
Al-Maydani reported that al-Hasan al-Basri told the Bedouin, 'Well said; the best courses are the middle ones.' It urges adherence to moderation.
proverbs-0077: What are the 'two smallest parts' in 'A person is judged by his two smallest parts'?
Al-Maydani said they are the heart and tongue, called the two smallest because of their small size.
proverbs-0078: To whom does 'Hearing of al-Mu'aydi is better than seeing him' apply?
Someone absent from his people for a long time
Someone whose reputation is better than his appearance
Someone known by ancestry rather than deeds
Someone who talks much but does not act
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone whose reputation is better than his appearance. Al-Mundhir ibn Ma' al-Sama' first said it.
proverbs-0079: Which pre-Islamic poet first said 'The air is clear for you, so lay eggs and sing'?
Tarafa ibn al-'Abd said it as a boy after setting a trap for larks but catching nothing.
proverbs-0080: According to al-Maydani, what does 'Many a shot comes from no marksman' correctly mean?
An accurate shot from a normally inaccurate shooter
A shot with no shooter at all
An arrow rebounding and killing its owner
A shot missing its target and causing harm
Al-Maydani said it means an accurate shot may come from a normally inaccurate shooter, not a shot without any shooter, which is impossible.
proverbs-0081: Which pre-Islamic poet reportedly first said 'Many a striver works for one sitting idle'?
Al-Maydani said al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani reportedly first said it when al-Nu'man rewarded Shaqiq al-'Absi's family after his death.
proverbs-0082: What does 'A handful on a bundle' mean?
One affliction on top of another
An ibbala is a bundle of firewood and a dighth a handful of grass. Al-Maydani said the proverb means one affliction on top of another.
proverbs-0083: When is 'Set the dogs on the cattle' used?
When evildoers are set upon peaceful people in their homes
When a shepherd protects his livestock from wild beasts
When people are incited against each other without concern
When the strong are enlisted against the weak in war
Al-Maydani said it is used when people are incited against each other without concern: you suffer no harm, so leave them to it.
proverbs-0084: Al-jarid means choking distress and al-qarid poetry. The saying applies when something finally becomes possible too late to be useful.
proverbs-0085: What is 'al-sa'dan' in 'Pasture, but nothing like al-sa'dan'?
A plant among the best pasture grasses
Al-sa'dan is among the best pasture grasses for livestock. When animals graze on it, their milk thickens, becoming tastier and richer.
proverbs-0086: What is Sadda' in 'Water, but nothing like Sadda''?
Al-Mufaddal said Sadda' was a well whose water was sweeter than any other water they had.
proverbs-0087: Who said 'A young man, but none like Malik' while mourning his brother Malik?
Al-Maydani said Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said it of his brother Malik ibn Nuwayra, whom he elegized in poems.
proverbs-0088: To which Arab sage is 'The beginning of prudence is consultation' attributed?
Al-Maydani said the proverb belongs to Aktham ibn Sayfi.
proverbs-0089: To whom does 'Poor dates and short measure too?' apply?
Someone giving little then boasting of it
Someone buying what they do not need
Someone giving their worst possessions in charity
Hashaf is the worst kind of dates. The saying asks whether someone combines poor dates with short measure, applying to someone combining two undesirable traits.
proverbs-0091: Which pre-Islamic poet said 'Abu Mundhir, you have decimated us, so spare some of us; have mercy, some evils are easier than others'?
The verse belongs to Tarafa ibn al-'Abd; its second half became proverbial.
proverbs-0092: In 'The judge is approached in his home', which animal is the judge in the Arabs' animal fable?
Arabs related that a rabbit and fox brought their dispute to the spiny-tailed lizard, who said the judge is approached in his home.
proverbs-0094: What do Arabs mean by 'He brought a donkey's two horns'?
He brought something rare and precious
He brought something people laugh at
Al-Maydani said it means bringing lies and falsehood: a donkey has no horns, so it is as though he brought something impossible.
proverbs-0095: What was the man crossing the sea on in the story behind 'Your hands tied it and your mouth blew it up'?
A man tried crossing on a skin bag he had inflated but failed to tie properly. The air escaped and he drowned. The saying applies to bringing harm upon oneself.
proverbs-0097: Al-Mufaddal said a Muslim commander first said 'At dawn people praise the night journey' on his way to Iraq. Who was he?
Al-Mufaddal said Khalid ibn al-Walid first said it when Abu Bakr ordered him to march from al-Yamama to Iraq and he took the desert route.
proverbs-0098: What is a 'maghwat' in 'Whoever digs a maghwat falls into it'?
A well from which water is drawn
A covered pit for trapping hyenas and wolves
A ditch dug around a fortress
Shamir said a maghwat is dug and covered to trap a hyena or wolf, with a young goat placed inside.
proverbs-0100: What does 'Neither has your father been revived nor has the earth run out' concern?
A man wanted to put soil from where his father was killed on his head and was told this. It applies to seeking something futile.
proverbs-0102: What was 'Your rope is on your withers' a figurative expression for?
The gharib is the top of the camel's hump. Al-Maydani said the expression signifies divorce: go wherever you wish.
proverbs-0103: Who composed the proverbial verse 'I am Ibn Jala, climber of mountain passes; when I put down my turban, you will know me'?
Al-Maydani said it is by Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi; al-Hajjaj quoted it from the pulpit of al-Kufa.
proverbs-0105: When is 'The matter has returned to its proper place' said?
Of a prolonged illness with no hope of recovery
Of an absent person returning after a long absence
Of a dispute settled by fighting
Of a matter taken over by those properly responsible for it
Al-Maydani said it applies to a matter being handled by those properly responsible for it.
proverbs-0106: What does 'A tree begins with a seed' illustrate?
A small matter giving rise to a great one
Someone planting but not harvesting the fruit himself
Al-Maydani said it applies to a small matter giving rise to a great one.
proverbs-0107: What does 'He who warned has discharged his duty' mean?
Whoever apologizes after an error is no longer blameworthy
Whoever warns his people of war has fulfilled his covenant
Whoever warns you of what may befall you has an excuse in your eyes
Whoever warns first wins the spoils
Al-Maydani said someone warning you of what may befall you has discharged his duty toward you and has an excuse in your eyes.
proverbs-0108: To whom does 'Leave a man to what he has chosen' apply?
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone refusing your advice: leave him to his choice.
proverbs-0110: Who is Jidh' in 'Take from Jidh' what he gives you'?
He was Jidh' ibn 'Amr al-Ghassani. A tribute collector demanded two dinars, so he struck him with his sword and said, 'Take from Jidh' what he gives you.'
proverbs-0112: What does 'harf' mean in 'Do not tahrif about what you do not know'?
Al-harf means lavish praise. The saying applies to praising something excessively before fully knowing it.
proverbs-0113: What is 'al-haqin' in 'Al-haqin refutes the excuse'?
Al-haqin is stored milk. A man asked people for milk and they made excuses despite having stored milk; he said this to expose their lie.
proverbs-0114: To whom does 'This is not your nest, so move along' apply?
Someone raising himself above his station
Someone leaving home to live elsewhere
Someone leaving his people without reason
It means this is not a matter in which you have a right, so leave it. It applies to someone raising himself above his station.
proverbs-0117: What does 'Starve your dog and it will follow you' concern?
Associating with base people and how they should be treated
Al-Maydani said it concerns associating with base people and how they should be treated.
proverbs-0118: To whom does 'A clumsy woman found wool' apply?
Someone mastering work outside their trade
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone squandering their wealth.
proverbs-0120: What did a pre-Islamic caller mean by 'The dates are in the well'?
Water benefits people more than dates
Dates are stored in wells to preserve them
The well dries up when dates are abundant
Whoever waters his palms sees the result in his dates
When unripe dates matured, a caller would say 'The dates are in the well', meaning that one who waters sees the result in his dates.
proverbs-0123: To whom does 'Your brother is compelled, not a hero' apply?
Someone forced into something outside his usual conduct
Someone fighting to defend his brother
Someone praising himself for qualities he lacks
Al-Maydani said the person is forced into it, rather than naturally brave. It applies to someone compelled into something outside his usual conduct.
proverbs-0124: To whom does 'I hear the mill's clatter but see no flour' apply?
Someone frequently complaining of little provision
Someone raising his voice in an argument
Tihn means flour. Al-Maydani said the proverb applies to someone promising but not fulfilling.
proverbs-0125: To whom does 'The gazelle abandoned its shade' apply?
Someone going out in the heat to earn a living
Someone forgetting his home and family
Someone recoiling from something and leaving it never to return
Someone abandoning comfort in search of glory
The gazelle's shaded shelter is its kinas. If a hunter drives it out, it does not return. The proverb applies to leaving something in aversion and never returning.
proverbs-0126: Who is 'al-ra'id' in 'The scout does not lie to his people'?
The shepherd taking livestock to pasture
Someone preceding his people to find a campsite and water
The scout is sent ahead to seek a campsite or water. If he lies, his people perish. The saying concerns feared consequences of lying.
proverbs-0127: The deceased husband of a woman from 'Udhra
A beautiful slave girl from Banu Tamim
A fine horse of a king of al-Hira
Al-Mufaddal said Asma' bint 'Abd Allah al-'Udhriyya first said it. Her husband, a paternal kinsman named 'Arus, had died.
proverbs-0128: Who said 'Qasir cut off his nose for a purpose'?
Al-Maydani said al-Zabba' said it when she saw Qasir with his nose cut off.
proverbs-0129: What does 'He gave him a little from an overflow' mean?
Al-Maydani said it means a little from much, applying to someone giving a small amount from his abundance.
proverbs-0130: Who was Du'aymis al-Raml, proverbial for guidance in 'Better at finding the way than Du'aymis al-Raml'?
A camel that knows the roads
A star used for navigation at night
They said he was an exceptionally skilled guide who became known by this name. Calling someone the Du'aymis of a matter means he is knowledgeable about it.
proverbs-0131: Which outlaw poet was proverbial for running speed in 'Faster at running than ...'?
Their proverbs include 'Faster at running than al-Shanfara'. Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani recounted his raiding with Ta'abbata Sharran and 'Amr ibn Barraq.
proverbs-0132: Who was proverbial for knowledge of genealogy in 'More knowledgeable about lineage than ...'?
Al-Maydani said Daghfal was a man from Banu Dhuhl ibn Tha'laba, the foremost genealogist of his time.
proverbs-0133: In 'Healthier than Abu Sayyara's donkey', for how many years did Abu Sayyara lead people from al-Muzdalifa to Mina on his donkey?
Al-Maydani stated that Abu Sayyara al-'Adwani had a black donkey on which he led people from al-Muzdalifa to Mina for forty years.
proverbs-0134: Who was Mula'ib al-Asinna, proverbial for horsemanship?
Al-Maydani said the man in 'A finer horseman than Mula'ib al-Asinna' was Abu Bara' 'Amir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far ibn Kilab, the horseman of Qays.
proverbs-0135: In 'Aswad than al-Ahnaf', from what is 'aswad' derived?
Al-Maydani said aswad in this expression derives from siyada, leadership.
proverbs-0137: Which insect is proverbial for gathering and storing, as in 'More acquisitive than ...'?
Their proverbs include 'More acquisitive than an ant', also phrased with dharra, a tiny ant.
proverbs-0138: Why did Arabs say 'Sharper of hearing than a horse'?
It hears enemy footsteps long before its rider
It hears horses neighing a day's journey away
It obeys its owner's voice among other voices
It hears its own hair fall to the ground
Al-Maydani said a horse is reputed to hear a hair falling from its body to the ground.
proverbs-0140: What does 'wahy' mean in 'More enduring than wahy on stone'?
Al-Maydani said wahy means writing and also something written.
proverbs-0141: What is 'jana al-nahl' in 'Purer than jana al-nahl'?
Al-Maydani said it is honey, also called al-mazj, al-ary and al-darab.
proverbs-0142: What is a 'qutrub' in 'More wakeful than a qutrub'?
A small creature that does not sleep at night
A star staying awake until dawn
Al-Maydani said it is a small creature that does not sleep at night because it moves about so much, according to Abu 'Amr.
proverbs-0143: Why did Arabs say 'More bewildered than a spiny-tailed lizard'?
It digs a burrow with many entrances and exits
It eats its young when they hatch
It does not drink water and remains thirsty
Once it leaves its burrow, it cannot find its way back
Al-Maydani said it is because, once the spiny-tailed lizard leaves its burrow, it cannot find its way back.
proverbs-0144: Why was 'More revealing than dawn' said?
Al-Maydani said dawn tears away every veil and conceals nothing.
proverbs-0145: What is a 'sharif' in 'More yearning than a sharif'?
A ewe that has given birth
Al-Maydani said al-sharif is an old she-camel, whose yearning for her young is greater than that of others.
proverbs-0146: Why do Arabs say 'More truthful than a sandgrouse'?
Its call echoes its name and never changes
It always comes to water at the same time
It never loses its way to its nest, however far away
It warns people of an approaching enemy
Al-Maydani said it has one unchanging call, echoing its name: qata, qata. Arabs therefore call it the truthful bird.
proverbs-0147: Why did Arabs say 'More unjust than a snake'?
It bites someone who treated it well
It enters another animal's burrow and takes it over
Al-Maydani said a snake comes to another animal's burrow, enters it and takes it over.
proverbs-0148: What does 'He seized him as a spiny-tailed lizard seizes its young' mean?
He took him gently and affectionately
He seized him fiercely, intending to kill him
He seized him then let him go
Al-Maydani said it means seizing someone fiercely with intent to kill: the lizard mistakes its young for other ground creatures, seizes them and kills them.
proverbs-0150: A kind word said to an angry person
Cold water given to a thirsty person
Sour milk mixed with sweet milk
Rathi'a is sour milk mixed with sweet milk, and fath' means soothing. The saying concerns a gift creating harmony, however small.
proverbs-0153: What does ''alam' mean in 'Whenever we pass an 'alam, another appears'?
Al-Maydani said a mountain is called an 'alam. The saying means that whenever one matter is finished, another arises.
proverbs-0154: To whom does 'He is only like deceptive lightning' apply?
Someone promising then breaking his promise and not delivering
Barq al-khullab is lightning without rain, as though deceptive. The saying applies to someone promising then failing to deliver.
proverbs-0155: Which Companion said 'Indirect expressions provide an alternative to lying'?
Al-Maydani said these are the words of 'Imran ibn Husayn; manduha means ample room.
proverbs-0156: Maqdara means power and hafiza anger: when a man gains power over his adversary, his anger fades.
proverbs-0157: I inherited it from my forefathers
I was the first to enter it
Al-Maydani said it means I know it well. Having bajda of something means having knowledge of it.
proverbs-0158: What does 'If one wild donkey escapes, another is caught' concern?
Being content with what is present and leaving what is absent
Hastening to seek what is lost
Ribat is what an animal is tied with. The hunter is told that if one wild donkey escaped, he should be content with what the snare caught. The saying urges contentment with what is present.
proverbs-0161: What does 'aqwam' mean in 'Women are the counterparts of aqwam'?
Aqwam here means men. The saying means women are like men and were derived from them, having rights corresponding to their obligations.
proverbs-0162: Which outlaw said to a man kneeling on his chest, 'The night is long and you have moonlight'?
Al-Mufaddal said al-Sulayk ibn al-Sulaka al-Sa'di was asleep when a man knelt on his chest and demanded surrender, so he said this.
proverbs-0163: Who are 'those who make you cry' in 'Follow those who make you cry, not those who make you laugh'?
A girl's maternal aunts made her laugh when she visited, while her paternal aunts disciplined her. Her father told her to follow those who made her cry, meaning to adhere to their direction.
proverbs-0164: What does 'Humiliation is kindness to the base person' mean?
If you honor a base person, he obeys you
A base person never feels humiliation
If you humiliate a base person, it is as though you honored him
Humiliation reforms both noble and base people
Mar'ama means compassion and kindness. Honoring the base person makes him disdain you, while humiliating him is as though you honored him.
proverbs-0165: What does 'li-tahna' mean in 'You were named Hani' li-tahna'?
Hana'tu al-rajula means I gave the man something. The saying means you were given this name to bestow favors on people.
proverbs-0166: What does 'dhu shujun' mean in 'Conversation is dhu shujun'?
Al-Maydani said it means having many paths; the singular is shajn. It applies to conversation recalling another topic.
proverbs-0167: What is 'judhayl' in 'I am its well-rubbed judhayl'?
Diminutive of a wall built of clay
Diminutive of jidhl, a tree stump
Judhayl is the diminutive of jidhl, a tree stump. A muhakkak is a post erected where camels rest so mangy camels can rub against it.
proverbs-0168: Which animal did Arabs portray as saying 'How can I return to you when this is the mark of your axe?'
In the Arab tale underlying the proverb, it is spoken by a snake guarding a fertile valley.
proverbs-0170: According to al-Maydani, who first said 'Returning is more praiseworthy'?
Al-Maydani said Khidash ibn Habis al-Tamimi first said it.
proverbs-0171: What does 'He returned to his original track' concern?
A bad habit abandoned then resumed
A horse returning to its tethering place
A right returning to its owners
A traveler returning to his family
It means returning to one's original path and applies to a bad habit abandoned then resumed.
proverbs-0173: When is 'Of the spoils, I am content with returning' used?
Imru' al-Qays said it in a verse. Al-Maydani said it applies to being content with safety.
proverbs-0174: To whom does 'Like a camel driver with no camel' apply?
Someone pretending to possess what he does not own
Someone good at singing but not working
Someone leading his people to destruction
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone pretending to possess what he does not own.
proverbs-0175: What does 'You will not lack support from your cousin' mean?
A cousin has the strongest inheritance claim
Your relative is angered on your behalf when you are wronged, even if you oppose him
Al-Maydani said your close relative is angered on your behalf when he sees you wronged, even if you are hostile toward him.
proverbs-0176: To whom does 'If only a woman wearing a bracelet had slapped me' apply?
A woman angry at her husband
A noble person unable to bear being wronged by a lowly person
Someone struck who does not resist
Al-Maydani said it applies to a noble person unable to bear being wronged by a lowly person.
proverbs-0178: What does 'Of a necklace, enough is what encircles the neck' mean?
Do not burden yourself beyond your capacity
Be content with a little out of much
Al-Maydani said it means being content with a little out of much.
proverbs-0179: What does 'Every man is a child in his home' concern?
It means setting aside formality and being playful. The proverb concerns good companionship.
proverbs-0180: What does 'qadm' mean in 'Khadm may be reached through qadm'?
Eating with the tips of the teeth
Khadm is eating with the whole mouth, and qadm with the tips of the teeth. The saying means a distant goal may be reached through gentleness.
proverbs-0181: What does 'He told me truly the age of his young camel' concern?
A man bargained with another over a young camel. Its owner said 'hida'', a word used to quiet young camels, prompting the saying. It concerns truthfulness.
proverbs-0182: What does 'saqatta' mean in 'Upon an expert you have saqatta'?
Al-Maydani said saqatta means you came upon, using falling figuratively for encountering; the expert is someone knowledgeable.
proverbs-0183: According to al-Asma'i, with what did Ibn Bayd block the road?
Al-Asma'i said Ibn Bayd slaughtered a she-camel on a mountain pass, blocking the road and preventing people from using it.
proverbs-0184: What is 'al-khiyat' in 'I will not do that until a camel enters the eye of al-khiyat'?
Al-Maydani said a needle is called al-khiyat or al-mikhyat.
proverbs-0185: What is 'al-qatad' in 'Before that comes stripping al-qatad'?
A smooth rock that cannot be climbed
Khart is stripping leaves from a tree by hand. Al-qatad is a tree with needle-like thorns. The saying concerns a matter obstructed by a barrier.
proverbs-0186: What does 'Beware of weariness in pursuing matters' concern?
Forbidding company with the easily bored
It is attributed to Abjar ibn Jabir al-'Ijli in advice to his son. It encourages diligence in matters and avoiding negligence.
proverbs-0188: What does 'A man's place of death lies between his jaws' refer to?
Maqtal means the place of killing; the tongue is intended, meaning that killing can result from it.
proverbs-0193: A man said nothing was more hateful to him than dates and butter, and was told 'Many a blamed one has no fault'. In whose gathering did this occur?
Al-Maydani related that a man said this in al-Ahnaf ibn Qays's gathering, and al-Ahnaf replied, 'Many a blamed one has no fault.'
proverbs-0194: What does 'fa-khlub' mean in 'If you cannot overcome, fa-khlub'?
Khalaba means to deceive, and khilaba is deception. Deception in war is intended.
proverbs-0195: What does 'Quenching thirst does not require draining the vessel' concern?
Insisting on drinking all the water
Being content with some of what one needs
Tashaff means drinking everything in a vessel. The saying concerns being content with some of what one needs.
proverbs-0196: Who composed 'Leave aside plunder whose outskirts were raided', which became proverbial?
Al-Maydani said it is from a verse by Imru' al-Qays, spoken when his camels were raided. It applies to losing property and then losing something greater.
proverbs-0197: What does 'Every sheep will be hung by its own leg' mean?
Every offender is held accountable for his own offense
Every shepherd is responsible for his flock
Everyone is known by their ancestry
Nawt means hanging. Every offender is held accountable for his own offense; someone other than the offender should not be punished for it.
proverbs-0198: What does 'Let no one outside your party saddle your mount' mean?
Do not travel alone at night
Seek help only from people you trust
Do not leave your people in hardship
Do not carry someone else's belongings on your journey
Al-Maydani said it means seeking help only from people you trust.
proverbs-0200: To whom does 'Among the misses is a hitting arrow' apply?
A skilled archer who never misses
Someone making many mistakes then succeeding once
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone who misses many times then hits once, like the popular saying that a shot may come from no marksman.
proverbs-0201: What does 'Compete with an old camel or leave it' mean?
Seek help only from older, experienced people
Give up competition unless your wealth makes you strong
Use a staff for a long journey
Do not enter a crowd unarmed
Al-Maydani said it means seeking help only from people of age and experience in affairs.
proverbs-0202: According to Abu 'Ubayd, what does 'Take the edges, for you wear sandals' mean?
Undertake the difficult matter, for you are strong enough
Beware of thorns even while wearing sandals
Walk slowly, for the road is long and desolate
Return home before night overtakes you
Abu 'Ubayd said it means undertaking a difficult matter because you are capable. It originated with a man telling a shepherdess to take the valley's edges because she wore sandals.
proverbs-0203: What does 'You reminded me to thrust when I had forgotten' concern?
One thing reminding someone of another
A man charged another, who told him to drop his spear. Reminded of the spear in his hand, he stabbed him. It concerns one thing recalling another.
proverbs-0204: To whom does 'In the livestock's appearance you recognize its thriving' apply?
Someone whose good exterior indicates a good interior
Someone spending wealth improperly until impoverished
Someone whose growing wealth makes him arrogant
Someone guarding wealth without benefiting from it in life
Imra means growth and goodness. Al-Maydani said the proverb applies to someone whose good exterior indicates a good interior.
proverbs-0205: To whom does 'Whoever appoints a wolf as shepherd has wronged' apply?
Someone grazing sheep in predator territory
Someone abandoning caution toward an enemy
He wrongs the sheep, or the wolf by requiring what is contrary to its nature. The saying applies to appointing an untrustworthy person.
proverbs-0209: To whom does 'Every suitor has a date on his tongue' apply?
Someone promising gifts but giving none
Someone softening his speech when seeking a favor
Someone eating in others' homes but never feeding anyone
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone softening his speech when seeking a favor.
proverbs-0210: Who was Mujir al-Zu'un, proverbial for protection?
Al-Maydani said the man in 'More protective than Mujir al-Zu'un' was Rabi'a ibn Mukaddam al-Kinani, who protected the women travelers from Nubaysha al-Sulami.
proverbs-0211: What is 'al-ghuwayr' in 'Perhaps al-ghuwayr holds hardship'?
The name of a man from Lakhm
The name of a well in Iraq
Al-ghuwayr is the diminutive of ghar, a cave. Ab'us is the plural of bu's, hardship. The expression originated with al-Zabba'.
proverbs-0215: To whom does 'An eye recognized and shed tears' apply?
Someone weeping over lost good fortune
Someone seeing a matter and recognizing its reality
Someone saddened by separation from loved ones
Al-Maydani said it applies to someone seeing a matter and recognizing its reality.
proverbs-0216: In al-Maydani's account of al-Harith ibn Zalim's proverbial faithfulness, how did 'Iyad ibn Dayhath become entitled to his protection?
He spent a whole night as his guest
He ate his food and drank his drink
He joined his own well rope to al-Harith's and watered his camels
He sought his protection at the Ka'ba during the sacred month
'Iyad borrowed some of al-Harith's well ropes, joined them to his own and watered his camels. When they were raided, he cried out for his protector, and al-Harith acknowledged the protection.
proverbs-0217: Why did Arabs say 'More productive than a cheetah'?
Old cheetahs gather around a young one that hunts for them
It runs faster than any predator and no prey ever escapes
Hunters profited by catching and selling cheetahs in markets
It hunts more than it needs daily and hides the rest for itself
Al-Maydani said old cheetahs unable to hunt gather around a young cheetah that hunts enough to feed them daily.
proverbs-0218: Arabs said 'Rarer than red sulfur'; what was red sulfur said to mean?
Al-Maydani said it was identified as red gold, or alternatively as something existing only in speech.
proverbs-0219: Whom does the Kuwaiti proverb 'The hen dies with its eye on the bran' describe?
A mother spending her whole life raising her children
A poor person who never had a full meal in life
Someone devoted to work and earnings until his last day
A greedy person coveting what is not his until life's end
It describes a greedy person nearing death yet still coveting what is not his, like a hen dying with its eye on livestock feed.
proverbs-0220: What does the Kuwaiti proverb 'Whatever comes from Allah is welcome' express?
Contentment and submission to Allah's decree and predestination
Welcoming a guest returning from a long journey
Praying for a pilgrim returning home from Mecca
Thanking someone for a gift on special occasions
It means contentment and submission to the decree and predestination of Allah, exalted and majestic.
proverbs-0221: What is the point of the Kuwaiti proverb 'The appearance is impressive, but the substance is weak'?
Beautiful words do not satisfy hunger
The weak cannot be entrusted with anything
Do not be deceived by appearances
A great person's worth is known only through work
Outward appearance does not necessarily reflect a person's inner self, intentions and deeds. The point is not to be deceived by appearances.
proverbs-0223: In the Kuwaiti proverb 'Only their people can face al-salayib', what does 'al-salayib' mean?
Al-salayib is said to mean wars. The point is that hardships and ordeals are repelled only by the homeland's heroes and noble men.
proverbs-0224: In Kuwait, what does 'This is Sayfu and these are his old clothes' mean when said about a man?
He is ready to travel with all his belongings, weapons and clothes
He is as he always was; nothing has changed
He is poor and owns nothing but his clothes
He is brave and never parts with his weapon
The person is as he always was; his life and habits have not changed. Khalajin means clothes.
proverbs-0225: What does the Kuwaiti proverb 'If it were any good, the birds would not have rejected it' imply?
Provision comes to those who seek it
Birds know good food better than people
There is no good in discarded things
Good things do not stay long with their owner
The proverb implies there is no good in discarded things.
proverbs-0226: What does the Kuwaiti saying 'Envying a poor man for dying on Friday' indicate?
The most extreme degree of envy
The merit of dying on Friday over other days
People's mercy and kindness toward the poor
A poor person's contentment with his little
It indicates extreme envy: envying a poor man who owns nothing even for his death on Friday.
proverbs-0227: When is the Kuwaiti proverb 'Accusations come to you while you sleep' used?
Guests visiting during rest without warning
Provision coming to an idle person at home without effort
An unforeseen calamity befalling someone who had no part in it
It refers to an unforeseen problem or calamity affecting someone who had no part in it.
proverbs-0228: What advice does 'If your loved one is honey, do not eat it all' convey?
Do not exploit a kind, generous person's goodness
Eat sweets moderately to avoid illness
Give loved ones your finest food
If you accompany a kind and generous person, do not greedily exploit their goodness.
proverbs-0229: To whom is the Kuwaiti proverb 'The door is wide enough for a camel' said?
A generous household with wide doors
It is said to someone whose continued presence is unwanted.
proverbs-0230: Whom does the Kuwaiti maritime proverb 'He took us with sail and oar' describe?
Someone making many promises and never fulfilling any
Someone doing two hard jobs at once and mastering neither
Someone getting the better of others in conversation through wit and much talk
Someone often traveling by sea to provide for his family
It describes someone outtalking others through intelligence, shrewdness and abundant speech, like a ship moving with both sail and the sailors' rowing.
proverbs-0231: What does the Kuwaiti proverb 'The scoop empties the tank' indicate?
A small tool suffices for a large task when used well
Excessive use without replenishment hastens depletion
Water is a ship's most precious cargo on long voyages
A steady little is always better than an interrupted abundance
Extravagance and heavy consumption without replacement or additions cause something to run out sooner.
proverbs-0232: What does 'No wave rises unless wind drives it' mean?
Every event has a cause, like waves rising because of strong wind.
proverbs-0233: In 'If its tarij is submerged, patching is no use', what is the 'tarij'?
A piece of wood at the ship's top
The tarij is a piece of wood at the top of a ship. If water reaches it, sinking is inevitable. The saying expresses despair after many calamities.
proverbs-0234: Whom does the Kuwaiti proverb 'Cargo on deck' describe?
Someone bearing others' burdens without asking for anything
Someone boasting of possessions at every gathering
Someone bearing worries alone without complaint
It describes someone revealing private matters to the public, like a ship whose deck cargo everyone can see.
proverbs-0235: What does 'A flood that does not wet you does not concern you' mean?
A flood does not harm those living high above valleys
Do not fear heavy rain if you have shelter
A matter that neither affects nor harms you does not occupy you
Abundant water drowns crops rather than watering them like light rain
A flood that does not wet you does not concern you: do not occupy yourself with what does not involve or harm you.
proverbs-0236: In 'A creature of habit ma yiyuz 'an tab'ih', what does 'ma yiyuz' mean?
Tubay' is the diminutive of tab', disposition; ma yiyuz means does not abandon, originally ma yajuz. A habitual trait is difficult to change.
proverbs-0237: To whom does 'I thought my honor came from my ancestors' heritage; it turned out to come from what I possess' apply?
Someone boasting of ancestors but forgetting to work and earn
Someone living long under an illusion contrary to reality
Someone squandering ancestral inheritance on hospitality until poor
It means: I thought people honored me for my lineage, but it was actually for what I earned. It applies to living under an illusion.
proverbs-0238: When is 'When distress intensifies, expect relief' used?
When setting out on a journey
When relief seems slow in coming
Its meaning is clear; it is used when relief seems slow in coming.
proverbs-0239: In 'While you eat the dates, we count al-ta'am', what is 'al-ta'am'?
Al-ta'am is the plural of ta'ama, a date pit. The dates eaten are counted through the pits; the saying concerns precise accounting.
proverbs-0240: To whom does 'When lightning flashes, look at your bull's eye' apply?
Someone fearing winter rain, thunder and lightning
Someone caring for livestock in winter and fearing the cold
Someone among people some of whom cannot be trusted
Someone seizing an opportunity before it passes
It applies to someone among people some of whom cannot be trusted. Its story concerns a woman who saw in a lightning flash that the waterskin carrier was not a bull.
proverbs-0241: What does 'When cows make pilgrimage on their horns' express?
The stubbornness of someone rejecting advice
It means: I will fulfill my promise after cows make pilgrimage on their horns. Cows do not walk on their horns, so it expresses impossibility.
proverbs-0242: What does 'al-qatu' mean in 'When al-qatu is away, play, mouse'?
Al-qatu means the cat. The mouse plays freely in the cat's absence.
proverbs-0243: In 'When the camel tah, its knives multiply', what does 'tah' mean?
Tah means fell. When the camel falls, cowardly butchers pounce to finish it off.
proverbs-0244: When is the Kuwaiti saying 'News that even the witch can read' used?
When news has spread widely among people
When children learn reading and writing in traditional schools
When warning against sorcery and charlatans
When criticizing an ignorant pretender to knowledge
It is used when news has spread widely among people.
proverbs-0245: Who is Marhun in 'Marhun did not abandon his companions'?
A merchant pledging money with friends until returning from a long journey
A captain refusing to leave his ship in a storm and sinking with it
A faithful man who did not abandon friends during crises
A poet praising his people and friends at every gathering
Marhun was known for loyalty to his friends and did not abandon them during crises.
proverbs-0246: What does 'I love you, my benefactor, even if you are my enemy' mean?
It describes always loving and treating enemies well
It describes forgiving relatives who mistreat one
It describes not distinguishing friend from enemy
It describes putting self-interest above everything
It applies to someone putting self-interest above every other consideration.
proverbs-0247: To whom does 'At work he falls ill; at cooking he springs up' apply?
Someone good at cooking but no other housework
Someone falling ill from overeating then complaining
Someone feigning illness at work but rushing to eat
Someone blowing on a fire to cook for guests on cold nights
It describes someone feigning illness when assigned a task but rushing up when food is served.
proverbs-0248: In 'A mouthful of khabis comes with belittling', what is 'khabis'?
Thin bread baked on a griddle at home
A sweet made from dough, dates and flavorings
Rice cooked with meat in large pots
Khabis is a common traditional sweet made from dough, dates and flavorings such as cardamom and sugar.
proverbs-0249: Friday is a day for honoring guests and family
Strength and support come through community and numbers
Families gather only on special occasions
Large gatherings are never free of disagreement
It means strength and support are achieved through community and numbers.
proverbs-0251: Why is 'Whoever does not die today will die tomorrow' used?
To remind people that death comes sooner or later
To urge postponing tasks until tomorrow without laziness
To console people over someone dying far from home
To mock someone afraid of illness and often complaining
It reminds people that their appointed death will arrive sooner or later.
proverbs-0252: What does 'If you strike the nose, the eye sheds tears' express?
Striking the face creates lasting enmity
Deep closeness and affection between people
Illness in one organ spreads to the rest of the body
Interfering in others' affairs brings personal harm
It expresses deep affection and closeness, like the nose and eye: when one is hurt, the other is affected.
proverbs-0253: To what does 'Counted eggs in a tightly tied bag' apply?
Arguing over something plainly true, and a person with limited income
A merchant selling by number rather than weight or volume
Someone preserving people's secrets for years
Someone hiding money from family and counting it daily in fear
It applies to disputes over something whose truth is very clear, and to a person with limited income unable to spend more.
proverbs-0254: In 'A push of the mardi and an easterly wind', what is a 'mardi'?
A short oar used near the harbor
A thick rope securing sail to mast
A long pole used to push boats through shallow water
A heavy stone thrown into the sea to anchor a ship
A mardi is a long spear-like pole for pushing boats and small ships through shallow water.
proverbs-0255: When do people say 'A push of the mardi and an easterly wind'?
When a dusty, humid easterly wind blows
When ships set off at the start of pearl-diving season
When an unwelcome, tiresome person leaves
When bidding farewell to a traveler dear to family and neighbors
It concerns someone whose bad character makes a group find him burdensome. When he leaves, they sigh with relief and someone says this.
proverbs-0256: What does 'Spend what is in your pocket; what is unseen will come to you' mean?
Rely on Allah for provision, spend and do not be stingy
Save nothing because the future is unknown
Borrow from others and repayment money will come
Spend all your money before it is lost or stolen
Rely on Allah for provision, spend from what He has given you and do not be stingy; Allah will replace it.
proverbs-0258: To whom does 'If you see something, do not say anything' apply?
Someone seeing wrongdoing but keeping silent out of fear
Someone discovering something that should be concealed
Someone bearing false witness against another
It applies to someone discovering something that must be concealed. A supporting hadith is cited: ومن ستر مسلمًا ستره الله [Whoever covers a Muslim, Allah will cover him].
proverbs-0259: When is the Kuwaiti proverb 'None knows the unseen except Allah' said?
When afraid of traveling by sea
When something valuable is lost and its location unknown
When someone predicts something, as a rebuke to the predictor

It rebukes someone claiming certainty about future events known only to Allah. It derives from Allah's words in Surat al-Naml 65: «قل لا يعلم من في السماوات والأرض الغيب إلا الله» [Say, "None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except Allāh, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected."]
proverbs-0260: What does 'Whoever serves Allah is served' mean?
Allah helps those who obey Him and grants them acceptance among people
People honor someone working in a mosque
The children of someone serving people will serve him
A trustworthy servant becomes a master
Allah helps those who obey Him and provides people to assist them. It describes a righteous man respected by people.
proverbs-0261: To whom does 'Haste is from Satan' apply?
Someone quick to do good deeds
Someone rushing where deliberation is needed
It applies to someone rushing where deliberation is needed. In doing good deeds, however, one should hasten.
