proverbs-0262: In 'Whoever gets there first labaq', what does 'labaq' mean?
Obtained a place suitable for him
Labaq means obtaining a suitable place. The proverb concerns someone alert to opportunities who obtains the best of them.
proverbs-0263: To whom does 'Whoever is greedy taba'' apply?
Someone printing books and selling them in markets
A greedy person whose greed leads to ruin
Someone adopting others' manners to please them
Someone hoping for Allah's mercy and attaining what he wants
It applies to a greedy person whose greed leads to ruin or a bad reputation.
proverbs-0264: To whom does 'Whoever finds fault will be afflicted' apply?
Someone often mentioning people's faults and shortcomings
Someone correcting others' faults with private advice
Someone falling ill and being mocked by people
Someone criticizing food, refusing it and giving no thanks
It applies to someone whose talk consists of mentioning people's faults and publicizing their shortcomings.
proverbs-0265: What does 'The more his chatter, the less his standing' mean?
A person who talks excessively loses standing
A person who travels excessively loses wealth
A person who laughs excessively loses dignity
A person who eats excessively falls ill
It means that someone who talks excessively loses standing.
proverbs-0266: To whom does 'Where are you going? I am coming with you' apply?
Someone always enjoying travel with friends
Someone asking about everything and interfering
Someone welcoming guests at all times
Someone following others even to destruction
It applies to someone whose direction is determined by following others, even if they go to destruction.
proverbs-0267: For what purpose is 'Only the strong can perform Hajj' said?
Praising someone who performed Hajj on foot
Consoling someone wanting to perform Hajj but unable
Encouraging young people to perform Hajj early

It consoles someone wanting to perform Hajj (pilgrimage) but unable. Allah's words are cited in support: لا يكلف الله نفسًا إلا وسعها [Allāh does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] what [good] it has gained, and it will bear [the consequence of] what [evil] it has earned. "Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people."[111]]
proverbs-0268: To whom does 'A flowing spring, if you would come to drink' apply?
A generous person who never turns away a petitioner
A miser who closes his door
Someone going to a well in summer
It applies to a generous person who never turns away a petitioner.
proverbs-0269: To whom does 'The centerpiece of the necklace and the bead of the pendant' apply?
A child dear to both parents' hearts
It applies to a child dear to both parents' hearts.
proverbs-0271: To whom does ''Adhari spring waters the distant and leaves the near' apply?
Someone watering crops at night rather than day
Someone spending on himself but stingy toward others
Someone giving to and maintaining ties with the distant while neglecting the near
Someone traveling far and leaving family
It applies to giving to and maintaining ties with distant people while neglecting those nearby. 'Adhari spring in Bahrain watered distant orchards.
proverbs-0273: What does 'Sa'id is Mubarak's brother' express?
Two people alike in character and circumstances
Two brothers always loving one another
Someone blessed with two sons in one year
It describes two people alike in character and circumstances, usually disapprovingly.
proverbs-0274: What does 'Sa'id is a full moon in his mother's eyes' concern?
A mother's admiration for her child
A child dutiful to his mother
A child born on a full-moon night
It concerns a mother's admiration for her child, even if he is an enslaved person.
proverbs-0275: To whom does 'Happy is he whose helper is my Lord' apply?
Someone successful in his affairs through Allah's help
It applies to someone successful in his affairs: whoever Allah helps is happy and fortunate.
proverbs-0277: What does 'If the right hand does not rush to help the left, know that what trod on that one will tread on it' mean?
The weak cannot support the strong in hardship
What befalls another will befall you if you do not support him
Someone entering another's land without permission is expelled
The right hand is stronger than the left in every task
Wata derives from the formal Arabic wat', treading. What befalls another is bound to befall you if you do not support and help.
proverbs-0280: What does 'One hand does not clap' indicate?
A miser does not honor or welcome guests
Joy is complete only with family and neighbors together
The importance of solidarity and assistance
A man cannot work with one hand
It indicates the importance of solidarity and assistance in accomplishing and achieving things.
proverbs-0293: According to al-Maydani, what does 'Your brother is he who supports you' mean?
Your brother is someone sharing your lineage and blood
Your true brother puts you first and prefers you over himself
Your brother merely consoles you in calamity
Your brother visits you in illness
Al-Maydani said one's true brother puts one first and prefers one over himself. The proverb encourages care for one's brethren.
proverbs-0294: What is 'firar' in 'A fine horse's eye is its firar'?
A horse's speed in a long race
Examining an animal's teeth to determine its age
Holding a horse by the bridle when mounting
Firar means examining an animal's teeth to determine its age. The proverb applies to someone whose appearance reveals his inner qualities, making testing unnecessary.
proverbs-0296: Which scholar told an apologizing man 'I have excused you without an apology; excuses are tainted with lies'?
It is related that a man apologized to Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, who replied with these words.
proverbs-0297: What is 'ibsas' in 'Familiarizing comes before ibsas'?
Urging camels on at the watering place
Ibsas is gentling a she-camel during milking by saying 'bis, bis'. The proverb concerns tact when asking for something.
proverbs-0298: What does 'The first raid is clumsy' concern?
Abu 'Ubayd said it concerns lack of experience. The raid is described as clumsy because its participants are clumsy.
proverbs-0299: What does 'istanwaqa' mean in 'The male camel has istanwaqa'?
Al-Maydani said it means it became a she-camel. Tarafa reportedly said it when he heard a poet switch from describing a male camel to a she-camel.
proverbs-0300: What does 'Like one searching for the knife' concern?
Searching for a lost object in the wrong place
Seeking something that leads to one's own destruction
A man found game but had nothing to slaughter it with. The animal scratched the ground with its hooves, uncovering a blade with which it was slaughtered.
proverbs-0305: To whom is 'One date added to another makes a store of dates' attributed?
Uhayha ibn al-Julah said it when reproached for picking up a fallen date in his orchard. It concerns managing wealth well.
proverbs-0307: When is 'If you said a date, he would say an ember' used?
Al-Maydani said it is used when preferences differ.
kuwait-sea-heritage-0241: Which fish appears in the Kuwaiti proverb 'An 'uma is eaten yet disparaged'?
Al-'uma is the sardine, which people call inferior yet still eat.
kuwait-sea-heritage-0246: When is al-Sarayat season, known for sudden weather changes?
According to Kuwait's meteorological service, al-Sarayat season lasts from 9 April to 13 May.
kuwait-sea-heritage-0282: Beside which landmark is the shipwrights' diwaniya overlooking Arabian Gulf Street?
The emir ordered a diwaniya built for the shipwrights. Its building still stands facing the sea beside al-Seif Palace.
kuwait-sea-heritage-0319: What is 'fawh', used to prepare the huwayta sea snail for eating?
Huwayta flesh is eaten after fawh, meaning boiling it in hot water.
kuwait-old-life-0087: What is the small, poor-tasting fruit of the thorny wild lote tree called?
The wild lote tree has thorns, and its fruit, called al-dal, is small and poor-tasting.
kuwait-old-life-0088: Which tree in old Kuwaiti homes had broad leaves and yellow fruit containing a sticky liquid?
The bambar tree has many branches, broad leaves and yellow fruit containing a sticky liquid.
kuwait-old-life-0154: What are the dried desert plants eaten by sheep in summer called?
Plants become scarce in summer, and sheep eat them dried; they are then called hamis.
marine-life-0001: What is the approximate maximum depth of the Arabian Gulf?
The Arabian Gulf is shallow, with a maximum depth of about 90 meters.
marine-life-0002: At the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf water leaves along the bottom while ocean water enters at the surface. Why?
Monsoon winds push Gulf water downward
The strait's bottom is deeper than the Gulf of Oman's
Gulf water is warmer and therefore lighter than ocean water
Gulf water is saltier and therefore heavier and denser
The Gulf's high salinity makes its water denser, so it flows out in the lower layer while less saline ocean water enters above it.
marine-life-0003: For which marine animal is the Arabian Gulf the world's second most important habitat after Australia?
About 7500 dugongs live in Gulf waters, making it their second most important habitat after Australia.
marine-life-0004: What chiefly explains the scarcity of coral reefs in the northern Arabian Gulf compared with the Red Sea?
Sediment from Shatt al-Arab and fluctuations in temperature and salinity
Strong cold currents from the Indian Ocean
Great depths preventing sunlight from reaching the bottom
Frequent violent waves constantly breaking coral
Shatt al-Arab carries sediment that clouds the water and blocks light, and causes large temperature and salinity fluctuations unsuitable for coral.
marine-life-0008: The sabur fish migrates; where does it go to lay its eggs?
The distant depths of the Indian Ocean
Sabur is an anadromous fish, migrating from the sea into rivers to spawn, such as Shatt al-Arab in our region.
marine-life-0009: The sabur fish enjoyed in Kuwait and Iraq belongs to which fish family?
Sabur, or hilsa, belongs to the herring family.
marine-life-0010: What is the predominant body color of the Gulf's subayti fish?
Subayti is a sea bream with a silvery-gray body.
marine-life-0011: To which family does the popular Gulf fish subayti belong?
Subayti (Sparidentex hasta) belongs to Sparidae, the sea bream family.
marine-life-0012: Why is nuwaybi, familiar in Kuwait's markets, called a croaker in English?
It makes sounds using its swim bladder
It lives near frogs in estuaries
Fishers use a special call to gather it
It makes a sound by jumping above water
Croakers produce sounds by moving muscles around the swim bladder.
marine-life-0013: To which genus does the Gulf's sha'ri fish belong?
Sha'ri is an emperor fish of the genus Lethrinus.
marine-life-0014: To which family does kan'ad, common in the Gulf and Arabian Sea, belong?
Kan'ad (Scomberomorus commerson) is a Spanish mackerel in the family Scombridae.
marine-life-0015: What makes the dorsal spines of the Gulf's safi fish hazardous when handling it?
They are venomous and cause severe pain
They are coated with a sticky substance
They detach easily and remain embedded in skin
Safi fish, or rabbitfish, have venomous fin spines that cause a painful sting.
marine-life-0016: Safi is herbivorous; what is its main food?
Other fish's eggs and newly hatched young
Safi fish, or rabbitfish, graze on algae and seagrasses.
marine-life-0017: The spine venom of some safi species resembles that of which famously dangerous fish?
The spine venom of some safi species has been found to resemble stonefish venom.
marine-life-0018: Which shrimp species is most important in Kuwaiti and Gulf fisheries?
The green tiger prawn (Penaeus semisulcatus) is the Gulf's principal commercial species.
marine-life-0019: Which fish hops across coastal mudflats at low tide and can remain out of water for a long time?
A hermit crab in a borrowed shell
The mudskipper is an amphibious fish living on mudflats. It breathes out of water through its skin and mouth cavity.
marine-life-0021: Which tree forms mangrove forests along Arabian Gulf coasts?
The gray mangrove, Avicennia marina, known as shura, is the dominant species along Gulf coasts.
marine-life-0022: How do gray mangroves eliminate excess salt absorbed from seawater?
They convert it into sugar in their roots
They expel it with gum from their trunks
They excrete it through glands in their leaves
They store it in fruit then shed the fruit
Gray mangrove leaves have salt glands that secrete excess salt onto their surfaces.
marine-life-0024: On which plant does the dugong chiefly feed in shallow water?
The dugong is an herbivore grazing on seagrasses in shallow meadows.
marine-life-0025: How does a dugong's tail differ from a manatee's?
A dugong's is forked like a dolphin's, while a manatee's is paddle-shaped
A dugong's is long like a rope, while a manatee's is very short
A dugong's has spines, while a manatee's is smooth
A dugong's is round and paddle-shaped, while a manatee's is forked
A dugong's tail is split into a crescent like a dolphin's, while a manatee's is rounded like a paddle.
marine-life-0027: What is the hawksbill turtle known for eating on coral reefs?
The hawksbill turtle relies heavily on sponges for its food.
marine-life-0028: Where does the green turtle get its name?
Its constant residence in cloudy green water
The green turtle is named for the greenish fat beneath its shell, rather than the shell's color.
marine-life-0029: What is the adult green turtle's main food?
Crustaceans, shellfish and small bottom-dwelling crabs
The adult green turtle is herbivorous, feeding chiefly on seagrasses and algae.
marine-life-0030: What determines the sex of young sea turtles inside their eggs?
Temperature of the sand around the eggs
Sea turtles' sex is determined by incubation temperature; higher temperatures produce more females.
marine-life-0033: Which two rivers form Shatt al-Arab, which flows into the head of the Arabian Gulf?
The Syr Darya and Amu Darya
Shatt al-Arab forms at the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates at al-Qurna.
marine-life-0034: Which small southern Kuwaiti island is surrounded by coral reefs?
Kubbar is a small coral island south of Kuwait surrounded by reefs.
marine-life-0036: Which microscopic organisms usually cause red tides?
Shrimp larvae and decomposing fish eggs
Red tides are usually caused by species of dinoflagellates.
marine-life-0037: What is a place where fresh river water mixes with salty seawater called?
An estuary is a partially enclosed coastal body of water where fresh water mixes with seawater.
marine-life-0038: What describes water saltier than fresh water but less salty than seawater, as in estuaries?
Brackish water is intermediate between fresh and salt water and is common in estuaries.
marine-life-0039: Which coastal habitat in temperate regions is regularly flooded by tides and supports salt-tolerant grasses?
Salt marshes are coastal lands flooded by tides and supporting salt-tolerant vegetation.
marine-life-0040: Which sea lies between the Arabian Peninsula and the Indian subcontinent and connects to the Gulf through the Gulf of Oman?
The Arabian Sea is part of the Indian Ocean and connects through the Gulf of Oman to the Arabian Gulf.
marine-life-0041: What is the approximate area of the Arabian Gulf?
About one and a half million square kilometers
The Arabian Gulf covers about 251 thousand square kilometers.
marine-life-0042: Which predatory fish has a long cylindrical body and a projecting jaw full of sharp teeth?
The barracuda is a long-bodied predatory fish with a projecting jaw and sharp teeth.
marine-life-0043: How does a barracuda usually hunt its prey?
Creating a bubble trap around fish schools
The barracuda is an ambush predator that strikes its prey at great speed.
marine-life-0046: What is the moment when a tidal current stops before reversing direction called?
The moment when a tidal current stops is called slack water, usually near high or low tide.
marine-life-0047: In regions with semidiurnal tides, approximately how many times a day does the sea reach high tide?
Semidiurnal tides have approximately two high tides and two low tides each day.
marine-life-0048: Approximately how long separates successive high tides in a semidiurnal cycle?
The principal lunar tidal cycle is about 12 hours and 25 minutes, half a lunar day.
marine-life-0049: Why does high tide occur about fifty minutes later each day?
Ocean water needs fifty extra minutes daily to warm and expand in sunlight
The sun rises fifty minutes later daily throughout the year
Earth's rotation slows by fifty whole minutes each day
The moon returns to the same position in the sky about every 24 hours and 50 minutes
The moon orbits Earth in the same direction as Earth's rotation, returning to its sky position after about 24 hours and 50 minutes.
marine-life-0050: During which two lunar phases do neap tides reduce the difference between high and low water?
At the quarter phases, the sun and moon are at a 90-degree angle, so the sun's effect partly offsets the moon's.
marine-life-0051: Approximately how strong is the sun's tidal force relative to the moon's?
Despite the sun's enormous size, its distance makes its tidal force only about 46% of the moon's.
marine-life-0052: Who developed the first mathematical theory of tides based on universal gravitation?
Newton explained tides mathematically through gravity in his book al-Mabadi' (Principia).
marine-life-0053: Which body of water is known for predominantly diurnal tides, with one high and one low tide per day?
Diurnal tides predominate in the Gulf of Mexico and the South China Sea.
marine-life-0054: When does a perigean spring tide with a large tidal range occur?
When a full or new moon coincides with the moon's closest approach to Earth
When the sun is directly over the equator at the spring and autumn equinoxes
When the moon is at first quarter and farthest from Earth
When the moon is halfway between full and last quarter at its farthest point
A full or new moon coinciding with lunar perigee produces a perigean spring tide with the greatest tidal range.
marine-life-0055: Which scientist led the first systematic harmonic analysis of tidal records beginning in 1867?
George Darwin, son of Charles Darwin
Lord Kelvin began systematic harmonic analysis of tidal records in 1867.
marine-life-0056: Where is the world's greatest tidal range recorded, reaching about 16 meters?
The Bay of Fundy in Canada
The Bay of Bengal in India
The North Sea near the Netherlands
The Bay of Fundy is famous for the world's highest tidal range because of tidal resonance in its funnel-shaped basin.
marine-life-0059: Which river has the world's largest tidal bore, locally called the 'Silver Dragon'?
The Qiantang River and Hangzhou Bay experience the world's largest tidal bore, reaching up to 9 meters.
marine-life-0060: In which country did the world's first tidal power station open in 1966?
The Rance station in Brittany, France, opened in 1966 as the world's first tidal power station.
marine-life-0061: Where is the world's largest tidal power station, which surpassed Rance in 2011?
The Gulf of Cambay on India's west coast
The Bay of Fundy in Canada
South Korea's Sihwa Lake station, with a capacity of 254 megawatts, is the world's largest.
marine-life-0062: What is an ocean point where water height scarcely changes between high and low tide called?
The eye of a permanent major ocean whirlpool
An amphidromic point, or tidal node, has zero or near-zero tidal amplitude, with tidal lines rotating around it.
marine-life-0063: Who first discovered amphidromic points by tracing cotidal lines in the North Sea?
William Whewell discovered them by extending cotidal lines from North Sea coasts and finding that they met at a point.
marine-life-0066: What are seawater-filled hollows in coastal rocks after the tide recedes called?
Tide pools are rocky hollows retaining seawater at low tide and supporting many organisms.
marine-life-0067: What is the open distance of water over which wind blows without changing direction, creating waves?
Fetch is a major factor determining wave size, along with wind speed and duration.
marine-life-0068: What are waves called after leaving the wind region that generated them and traveling thousands of kilometers?
Waves moving away from their generating wind region are called swell and may travel thousands of kilometers.
marine-life-0069: What distance defines a sea wave's wavelength?
From one crest to the next
From the water surface to the seabed
From shore to the first wave
Wavelength is the distance between successive crests; height is measured from trough to crest.
marine-life-0070: What happens to wavelength as a wave enters shallow water near shore?
It doubles because of bottom friction
It shortens because wave speed decreases
It lengthens because the wave accelerates
When a wave interacts with the bottom, it slows and its crests come closer together, shortening its wavelength.
marine-life-0072: How do oceanographers define a rogue wave?
A wave always moving against the prevailing wind
A wave more than twice the significant wave height
A wave caused by an earthquake directly beneath the seabed
A wave forming only where tides meet river currents at major estuaries
A rogue wave exceeds twice the significant wave height, the mean height of the highest third of waves.
marine-life-0073: Which powerful Norwegian current is among the world's strongest tidal currents?
Saltstraumen near Bodo, Norway, is among the world's strongest tidal currents.
marine-life-0074: What long-term effect does tidal friction have on Earth's rotation?
It has absolutely no effect on Earth's rotation speed
It speeds Earth's rotation, shortening the day
It slows Earth's rotation, gradually lengthening the day
It reverses Earth's rotation every million years
Tidal acceleration gradually slows Earth's rotation and moves the moon farther away.
marine-life-0075: Approximately how far does the moon recede from Earth each year because of tidal interaction?
The moon recedes from Earth by about 3.8 centimeters annually through tidal acceleration.
marine-life-0076: What is the movement of sand along a beach by waves striking it at an angle called?
Longshore drift carries sediment parallel to the shore when waves arrive at an angle.
marine-life-0077: What is the slight rise and fall of land itself under the moon's and sun's gravity called?
Solid Earth tides are periodic displacements of the land surface that may reach tens of centimeters at the equator.
marine-life-0079: Which body of water is known for a small tidal amplitude?
Mediterranean tides have small amplitudes because the basin's oscillation patterns do not match the cycles of astronomical tidal forces.
marine-life-0080: Which forces chiefly cause ocean tides?
Tides arise chiefly from the moon's gravitational attraction, then the sun's, together with Earth's rotation.
marine-life-0082: Approximately how deep is Challenger Deep, the deepest point in the oceans?
Challenger Deep is about 10900 meters deep, approximately 11 kilometers below sea level.
marine-life-0083: Which craft carried Jacques Piccard and Don Walsh to Challenger Deep in 1960?
Piccard and Walsh descended in the bathyscaphe Trieste to Challenger Deep on 23 January 1960.
marine-life-0085: In which ocean is the Puerto Rico Trench, that ocean's deepest point?
The Puerto Rico Trench is the deepest location in the Atlantic Ocean.
marine-life-0086: Which trench contains the deepest point in the Indian Ocean?
The Sunda Trench, also called the Java Trench, is the deepest trench in the Indian Ocean.
marine-life-0087: Which is the world's only sea without land shores, bounded entirely by ocean currents?
The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is bounded by ocean currents rather than land.
marine-life-0088: After what is the Sargasso Sea named?
A tribe that lived on its islands
The Sargasso Sea is named for the brown Sargassum seaweed floating abundantly on its surface.
marine-life-0089: To which sea do European eels migrate to lay their eggs?
European eels travel thousands of kilometers to spawn in the Sargasso Sea.
marine-life-0091: Which ocean current transports the greatest volume of water in the world?
The Gulf Stream in the North Atlantic
The cold California Current off America's west coast
The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows around Antarctica and transports more water than any other ocean current.
marine-life-0093: What does the Japanese name 'Kuroshio' mean?
Kuroshio means black tide in Japanese, referring to its deep blue, almost black water.
marine-life-0094: What are large, wind-driven circular ocean-current systems called?
An ocean gyre is a vast circular current system driven by winds and the Coriolis force.
marine-life-0096: What is the decrease in ocean water's pH through absorbing atmospheric carbon dioxide called?
Carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater, forming carbonic acid and lowering pH.
marine-life-0097: Why does ocean acidification harm corals and shelled mollusks?
It heats the surrounding water to boiling point
It increases dissolved oxygen, poisoning cells and killing algae
It makes building calcium carbonate structures harder
Fewer carbonate ions in more acidic water hinder the formation of calcium carbonate structures.
marine-life-0098: What is the approximate average salinity of seawater?
About 35 grams of salts per liter
About 3 grams of salts per liter
Average seawater salinity is about 3.5%, approximately 35 grams of salts per liter.
marine-life-0099: Which two ions are most abundant among seawater's dissolved salts?
Chloride and sodium ions account for most seawater salts.
marine-life-0100: At approximately what temperature does seawater of normal salinity freeze?
Salts lower the freezing point, so seawater of normal salinity freezes at about two degrees below zero.
marine-life-0101: Which ocean-connected sea is the least salty because of the many rivers flowing into it?
The Baltic Sea is among the largest bodies of brackish water because of its many rivers and low evaporation.
marine-life-0102: Why is the Black Sea's deep water almost devoid of oxygen?
Dense algae consume all oxygen day and night at every depth
Its extreme cold prevents oxygen dissolving
A less saline surface layer prevents mixing with deep water
The Black Sea has layers of different densities, preventing deep saline water from mixing with surface water and making it oxygen-free.
marine-life-0103: Which toxic gas accumulates in the Black Sea's oxygen-free depths?
Bacteria in the oxygen-free depths produce hydrogen sulfide.
marine-life-0104: Why is the Red Sea among the saltiest seas connected to the ocean?
Salty ocean water flows into it from two directions
Numerous volcanoes dissolve salts on its bottom
Abundant red algae release much salt in summer
Intense evaporation, little rain and no major incoming rivers
Intense evaporation, low rainfall and the absence of major rivers raise the Red Sea's salinity.
marine-life-0106: In which country does the Mid-Atlantic Ridge clearly rise above sea level?
Iceland lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge where it rises above sea level.
marine-life-0107: What is the shallow seabed next to land, before the steep descent to the depths, called?
The continental shelf is a relatively shallow submerged extension of the land, followed by the continental slope.
marine-life-0109: What is a flat-topped seamount, leveled by waves before sinking, called?
A guyot is a flat-topped seamount eroded by waves when near the surface, then submerged.
marine-life-0110: Approximately how deep does sunlight sufficient for photosynthesis reach in clear seawater?
The photic zone extends from the surface to about 200 meters, where light suffices for photosynthesis.
marine-life-0111: What is the water layer where salinity changes rapidly with depth called?
The halocline is a layer where salt concentration changes sharply with depth.
marine-life-0112: Which deepest ocean zone lies in trenches below about 6000 meters?
The abyssal zone above the deep-sea plains
The hadal zone lies in deep trenches from about 6000 meters to the deepest seabed.
marine-life-0114: What is the main energy source for organisms around deep-ocean hydrothermal vents?
Green algae using faint light emitted by the vents
Heat organisms absorb directly from rocks
These environments depend on bacteria producing food through chemosynthesis from compounds such as hydrogen sulfide.
marine-life-0115: In what year were the first ocean-floor hydrothermal vents discovered near the Galapagos Islands?
Hydrothermal vents were discovered in 1977 at the Galapagos Rift.
marine-life-0116: What are hydrothermal vents that discharge hot, dark water laden with metal sulfides called?
Black smokers eject extremely hot water from which dark metal sulfides precipitate.
marine-life-0117: Which animal lives around hydrothermal vents without a mouth or digestive system, relying on bacteria inside its body?
The giant tube worm Riftia has no mouth; symbiotic bacteria in a special organ feed it.
marine-life-0119: What is the ocean surrounding Antarctica called?
The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica and is bounded by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current.
marine-life-0120: Approximately what percentage of Earth's surface do oceans cover?
The global ocean covers about 71% of Earth's surface.
marine-life-0121: Approximately how deep are the oceans on average?
The ocean's average depth is about 3.7 kilometers.
marine-life-0122: What phenomenon deflects surface water movement at an angle to the wind because of Earth's rotation?
The Coriolis force deflects the net movement of the surface layer by about 90 degrees from the wind direction; this is called Ekman transport.
marine-life-0123: Which British ship made a scientific voyage around the world between 1872 and 1876, establishing modern oceanography?
The Challenger expedition (1872-1876) was the first major scientific expedition to study the oceans.
marine-life-0126: Which microscopic algae live inside coral tissue and supply most of its food?
Diatoms floating in the open sea
Zooxanthellae are symbiotic algae that live in coral cells and provide products of photosynthesis.
marine-life-0127: What is the loss of coral color when it expels its symbiotic algae due to warmer water called?
Coral bleaching occurs when heat stress causes coral to expel the algae that color and feed it.
marine-life-0128: What material do coral polyps use to build the hard skeletons that form reefs?
Coral polyps secrete calcium carbonate skeletons that accumulate to build reefs.
marine-life-0129: What is the world's largest coral reef system?
The Belize Barrier Reef in the Caribbean
The Maldives reefs in the Indian Ocean
The Great Barrier Reef in Australia
The Great Barrier Reef off Queensland is the world's largest reef system.
marine-life-0130: Approximately how long is Australia's Great Barrier Reef?
The Great Barrier Reef extends more than 2300 kilometers.
marine-life-0131: Which type of coral reef grows directly beside the shore or very close to it?
Fringing reefs are the most common reef type and grow directly near the coast.
marine-life-0132: Which scientist proposed that atolls form from reefs around volcanic islands that gradually subside?
Darwin proposed that an atoll develops as a volcanic island subsides while the surrounding reef continues growing upward.
marine-life-0134: Which starfish is known for eating coral, with population outbreaks destroying areas of reef?
The crown-of-thorns starfish feeds on coral polyps, and outbreaks destroy reefs.
marine-life-0135: Which reef fish bites coral with its beaklike mouth and releases the remains as fine sand?
Parrotfish grind coral and algae, producing sand that helps form coral beaches.
marine-life-0136: What do some parrotfish species make around their bodies before sleeping at night?
Some parrotfish secrete a mucus covering around themselves during sleep; it has been shown to protect them from parasites.
marine-life-0137: Among which creature's stinging tentacles does the clownfish live without being harmed?
Clownfish live symbiotically among sea anemone tentacles, protected by a mucus layer.
marine-life-0138: What happens in a clownfish group if the dominant female dies?
The group joins another nearby group
The largest juvenile takes charge without changing
The entire group abandons the anemone
Clownfish are sequential hermaphrodites that change from male to female; the dominant male becomes female when she dies.
marine-life-0139: What service does the cleaner wrasse provide to large reef fish?
It guards their eggs against predators
It removes parasites and dead skin
It cleans sand around their burrows
Cleaner wrasses establish cleaning stations where they remove parasites from other fish.
marine-life-0140: Which reef fish has long striped fins and venomous spines and has invaded Atlantic and Caribbean waters?
Lionfish are predators with venomous spines, native to the Indian and Pacific oceans, that have invaded the Atlantic.
marine-life-0142: What potent toxin in pufferfish organs makes eating them dangerous?
Pufferfish contain tetrodotoxin, a deadly neurotoxin.
marine-life-0143: How does a pufferfish defend itself when a predator attacks?
It inflates its body by swallowing water
A pufferfish fills its flexible stomach with water, swelling into a ball that is difficult to swallow.
marine-life-0144: What is the world's largest bivalve, which lives on coral reefs?
The giant clam Tridacna gigas is the largest living bivalve and may weigh over 200 kilograms.
marine-life-0145: Where does the giant clam get much of its food?
By catching small fish with its shell
From symbiotic algae in its tissues
The giant clam hosts zooxanthellae in its outer tissue, which provide food.
marine-life-0146: Which marine creatures are among the simplest animals, lacking true tissues and letting water pass through pores in their bodies?
Sponges are simple animals without true tissues; water passes through their pores to filter food.
marine-life-0147: To which animal group does coral belong?
Coral belongs to the cnidarians, like jellyfish and sea anemones.
marine-life-0148: Why do most coral reefs grow in clear, shallow water?
Because deep water is extremely salty
Because their symbiotic algae need sunlight
Because predators cannot reach shallow water
Because waves in shallow water bring only oxygen
The symbiotic algae inside coral need light for photosynthesis, so reefs grow in clear, shallow water.
marine-life-0149: In which temperature range do reef-building corals usually thrive?
Below zero Celsius in polar waters
Most coral reefs thrive in warm water between about 23 and 29 degrees Celsius.
marine-life-0150: Which reefs are separated from the coast by a lagoon or relatively deep channel?
Barrier reefs run parallel to the coast, separated from it by a lagoon or channel.
marine-life-0151: What is the shallow body of water surrounded by a coral atoll called?
An atoll surrounds a shallow body of water called a lagoon.
marine-life-0152: Which small creature uses its large claw to release a bubble that makes a loud snap and stuns prey?
A pistol shrimp snaps its claw shut, creating a bubble that collapses with a loud sound and a shock that stuns prey.
marine-life-0154: What distinguishes mantis shrimp eyes from those of most animals?
They see only black and white
They have many types of color receptors
They are on the tail rather than the head like other crustaceans
Mantis shrimp eyes contain between 12 and 16 types of photoreceptors.
marine-life-0156: How does a sea urchin primarily protect itself from predators?
A sea urchin is covered with movable spines that protect it.
marine-life-0157: What unusual defense do some sea cucumbers use when attacked?
They expel internal organs or sticky threads
They deliver a powerful electric shock
They change shape and color to resemble a poisonous fish
They jump out of the water
Some sea cucumbers expel sticky tubes or their innards to distract an attacker, then regenerate them later.
marine-life-0158: What ability lets a starfish replace a severed arm?
Starfish can regenerate lost arms, and some species can regenerate an entire body from one arm.
marine-life-0159: How does a starfish eat a closed clam?
It breaks the shell with strong teeth
It swallows the entire clam with its shell
It extends its stomach through its mouth and digests prey outside its body
It injects a powerful venom that gradually dissolves the calcareous shell
A starfish opens the shell slightly, pushes its stomach inside, and digests the clam.
marine-life-0160: Why does a hermit crab carry an empty snail shell on its back?
It attracts females during mating season
A hermit crab has a soft, unarmored abdomen, so it shelters in an empty snail shell and replaces it as it grows.
marine-life-0161: Which animals attach themselves headfirst to rocks and ships and extend feathery legs to catch food?
Barnacles are crustaceans that attach themselves by their heads and catch food with feathery legs.
marine-life-0162: Which scientist spent eight years studying and classifying barnacles before publishing his famous theory?
Darwin studied barnacles for about eight years and wrote a detailed study of them.
marine-life-0166: Which predatory eel hides in reef crevices and has a second jaw inside its throat?
Moray eels have a second set of pharyngeal jaws that extend to pull prey into the throat.
marine-life-0167: Which colorful reef fish has a flat, disclike body and a dark eyespot near its tail?
Many butterflyfish have an eyespot near the tail to confuse predators.
marine-life-0169: What is the world's largest toothed whale?
The sperm whale is the largest toothed whale and the largest toothed predator.
marine-life-0170: What waxy substance fills the sperm whale's huge head and gives it its English name?
The sperm whale's head contains a spermaceti organ filled with a waxy substance, from which its English name derives.
marine-life-0171: What valuable waxy substance forms in the intestines of the largest toothed whales and is used in perfume-making?
Ambergris is a waxy substance that forms in the sperm whale's digestive tract and was historically used in perfumes.
marine-life-0172: Which whale is known for males singing long, complex songs during mating season?
Male humpback whales perform complex songs that repeat and change across seasons.
marine-life-0173: What feature of the humpback whale's body distinguishes it from other large whales?
A complete absence of horizontal tail flukes
The humpback whale's pectoral fins are very long, reaching up to a third of its body length.
marine-life-0175: What is the long spiral tusk projecting from a male narwhal's head?
The narwhal's tusk is an elongated, twisted canine tooth that pierces its upper lip.
marine-life-0176: To which family does the killer whale (orca) actually belong?
The orca is the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family.
marine-life-0177: Which white polar whale is nicknamed the 'sea canary' because of its many sounds?
The beluga is known as the sea canary for its whistles and varied sounds.
marine-life-0178: What fibrous plates hang from some whales' upper jaws instead of teeth to filter food?
Baleen consists of keratin plates that baleen whales use to filter krill and small fish.
marine-life-0179: What is the world's second-longest whale after the blue whale?
The fin whale is the second-longest cetacean after the blue whale and may exceed 26 meters.
marine-life-0180: Which whale makes one of the longest mammalian migrations, between Alaska and Mexico?
Gray whales migrate thousands of kilometers between northern feeding grounds and breeding grounds in Mexico.
marine-life-0181: Which whale is believed to be the longest-lived mammal and may live over two hundred years?
Studies indicate that bowhead whales may live more than 200 years.
marine-life-0182: How does a dolphin locate objects and prey in murky water?
By sensing the prey's electric field
By emitting clicks and listening to their echoes
With sharp night vision in its large eyes
Dolphins use echolocation by emitting clicks and analyzing their echoes.
marine-life-0184: What visible difference distinguishes a true seal from a sea lion?
Seals have long tusks and sea lions have none
Sea lions have external ear flaps and seals do not
Seals live in freshwater and sea lions in saltwater
Sea lions have white fur and seals have smooth skin
Sea lions have small external ears, whereas true seals lack ear flaps.
marine-life-0186: Which predatory Antarctic seal is known for hunting penguins?
The leopard seal is a major Antarctic predator that hunts penguins.
marine-life-0187: Which of these mammals is scientifically classified as a marine mammal because it relies on the sea for food?
The polar bear is considered a marine mammal because it relies on sea ice and hunting seals.
marine-life-0188: Which land animal is most closely related to dugongs and manatees?
Marine sirenians belong to a group whose closest living relatives are elephants.
marine-life-0189: Which is the only penguin that naturally lives north of the equator on some of its islands?
The Galapagos penguin lives on islands, some of which lie north of the equator.
marine-life-0190: What is the largest and heaviest penguin species?
The emperor penguin is the tallest and heaviest penguin.
marine-life-0191: Who incubates the emperor penguin's egg throughout the polar winter?
Only the female, in a burrow
Only the male, on his feet
No one; it is buried in snow
The father and mother alternate daily
The female lays the egg, and the male incubates it on his feet for about two months without food.
marine-life-0192: Which seabird has the longest wingspan of any living bird?
The wandering albatross has the longest wingspan of any living bird, which may exceed three meters.
marine-life-0193: What is the largest living turtle and the most widely distributed across the oceans?
The leatherback is the largest living turtle; its back is leathery rather than a hard shell.
marine-life-0194: What is the leatherback turtle's preferred food?
Leatherback turtles feed primarily on jellyfish.
marine-life-0196: How do sea snakes breathe when they spend most of their lives underwater?
Through gills beneath the lower jaw
Through a breathing tube extended above water
With a long lung, surfacing for air
Only by absorbing oxygen from water through the skin
Sea snakes are reptiles that breathe air with a large lung and can take in some oxygen through their skin.
marine-life-0197: What distinguishes sea otter fur from that of other animals?
It is the densest fur of any animal
It is thick white fur like a polar bear's
Sea otters have the densest fur in the animal kingdom instead of an insulating layer of blubber.
marine-life-0198: Which finned marine mammal feeds mainly on clams and mollusks on the Arctic seabed?
Walruses suck clams from the seabed in Arctic waters.
marine-life-0199: Which toothed whale holds the deepest known dive among mammals?
Cuvier's beaked whale has recorded the deepest and longest known dives among mammals.
marine-life-0200: Which animal underpins Southern Ocean food chains and feeds many whales?
Antarctic krill are tiny crustaceans in enormous numbers that underpin Southern Ocean food chains.
marine-life-0201: What group of marine mammals includes whales, dolphins, and porpoises?
Whales, dolphins, and porpoises form the order Cetacea.
marine-life-0202: How many chambers make up most whales' stomachs?
The cetacean stomach has three chambers.
marine-life-0203: Which living land animal is most closely related to whales?
Genetic studies show that hippopotamuses are the closest living animals to whales.
marine-life-0204: Which marine mammal group includes seals, sea lions, and walruses?
Pinnipeds are marine mammals with flipper-like limbs, including seals, sea lions, and walruses.
marine-life-0205: What is the world's largest living fish species?
The whale shark is the largest living fish and may exceed 18 meters in length.
marine-life-0206: What is the second-largest living fish, a shark that filters plankton with its mouth open near the surface?
The basking shark is the second-largest living fish after the whale shark and is a filter feeder.
marine-life-0208: Which vertebrate has the longest known lifespan and may live over 250 years?
The Greenland shark is the longest-lived known vertebrate, according to estimates from dating its eye lens.
marine-life-0209: Which shark can live in freshwater and travel long distances up rivers?
Bull sharks tolerate freshwater and travel up rivers such as the Amazon and Mississippi.
marine-life-0210: Which striped shark is known as the 'garbage can of the sea' because it eats almost anything?
Tiger sharks eat a wide range of food and even garbage, earning the nickname 'garbage can of the sea.'
marine-life-0211: Which small shark removes circular pieces of flesh from whales and large fish?
The cookiecutter shark attaches to prey and spins to cut out a round piece of flesh.
marine-life-0212: Which giant extinct shark was among the largest predatory fish in history?
Megalodon was an extinct shark that lived millions of years ago and was among the largest predators.
marine-life-0213: How does the great white shark keep its body warmer than the surrounding water?
Only by constantly swimming near the warm sunlit surface
With dense fur beneath its skin
With a thick blubber layer like whales
With a network of blood vessels retaining muscle heat
Countercurrent heat exchange in the great white shark's blood vessels raises its body temperature above the water temperature.
marine-life-0214: What is the world's largest ray, which feeds on plankton?
The giant manta is the largest ray and filter-feeds on plankton.
marine-life-0215: Which cartilaginous fish can deliver an electric shock to paralyze prey?
Electric rays have electrical organs that generate a shock to paralyze prey.
marine-life-0216: Where is a stingray's venomous defensive spine located?
On its back near the head
Stingrays have one or more tail spines that inject venom in defense.
marine-life-0217: Which cartilaginous fish has a long, flat snout lined with teeth on both sides?
Sawfish have a long, flat snout with two rows of sawlike teeth.
marine-life-0222: What is the world's longest bony fish, thought to have inspired tales of giant sea serpents?
Oarfish are the longest bony fish and have been associated with sea serpent tales.
marine-life-0223: Which fish was thought extinct for millions of years until discovered alive near South Africa in 1938?
The coelacanth was discovered alive in 1938 after previously being known only from fossils.
marine-life-0225: What does the deep-sea anglerfish use to attract prey?
A glowing lure dangling from its head
A loud sound made with its fins
A strong scent secreted by its glands
Bright changing colors on its tail and fins
Female anglerfish have a modified dorsal spine ending in a bacteria-lit lure that attracts prey.
marine-life-0226: In which fish does the male carry eggs in a special pouch until they hatch?
The female seahorse deposits eggs in the male's pouch, where he carries them until they hatch.
marine-life-0227: By hopping along the bottom with its tail
Horizontally, moving its tail from side to side
By forcefully expelling water from its mouth and gills
Upright, rapidly moving its dorsal fin
Seahorses swim upright, propelled by a rapidly fluttering dorsal fin.
marine-life-0228: Which bottom-dwelling fish are born with one eye on each side before one eye moves so both are on the same side?
Rock-dwelling fish such as stonefish and scorpionfish
Flatfish such as halibut and sole
One eye migrates during flatfish development, leaving both eyes on the same side.
marine-life-0229: Which fish migrates from the sea to the river where it hatched to lay eggs, often dying afterward?
Salmon return to their natal rivers to spawn, and many species die afterward.
marine-life-0230: Which large, fast, relatively warm-blooded fish crosses the Atlantic during migration?
Bluefin tuna maintain a body temperature above the surrounding water and cross the Atlantic.
marine-life-0232: Which jawless fish has a round sucking mouth, with some species parasitizing other fish?
Lampreys are jawless fish with toothed suction-disc mouths; some parasitize fish.
marine-life-0233: Sharks have no swim bladder; what helps them float instead?
A primitive lung filled with air
Cartilaginous fish have no swim bladder, and their oily liver helps with buoyancy.
marine-life-0234: Which small luminous fish is among the world's most numerous deep-sea fish?
Lanternfish are among the most abundant vertebrates and have light-producing organs on their bodies.
marine-life-0235: Which small fish lives in huge schools and is associated with the coast of Peru?
The anchovy fisheries off Peru are among the largest in the world.
marine-life-0236: Which fish supported North Atlantic fisheries for centuries before its fishery off Newfoundland collapsed in 1992?
The northern cod fishery off Newfoundland collapsed in 1992 due to overfishing.
marine-life-0237: Which deep-sea fish is named after a bird because its enormous mouth resembles the bird's beak and pouch?
The pelican eel is so named because its huge mouth resembles a pelican's.
marine-life-0238: Which animal has the largest eyes in the animal kingdom?
The blue whale in the oceans
The eagle-owl among nocturnal birds of prey
Giant and colossal squid have the largest eyes in the animal kingdom, reaching 27 centimeters.
marine-life-0239: What is the heaviest known living invertebrate?
The colossal squid is the heaviest known invertebrate.
marine-life-0241: What is the only living cephalopod with an external chambered shell?
The nautilus is the only living cephalopod with an external chambered shell.
marine-life-0242: Which fearsomely named cephalopod lives in oxygen-poor depths and feeds on marine snow?
Squid that fly above the water
Vampire squid feed on marine snow rather than blood and live in the oxygen minimum zone.
marine-life-0243: How does an octopus escape its enemies quickly?
It buries itself very deep in sand
It delivers a powerful electric charge that stuns and paralyzes the attacker
It flies above the water with its arms
It releases ink and jets away by expelling water through its funnel
An octopus releases an ink cloud and propels itself by expelling water through its siphon.
marine-life-0244: Where are most of an octopus's nerve cells located?
About two-thirds of an octopus's nerve cells are distributed in its arms.
marine-life-0246: What distinguishes box jellyfish eyes from those of most jellyfish?
They have complex eyes with lenses
They see only in total darkness
They never move or respond to any light
Box jellyfish have 24 eyes, some complex with lenses and corneas.
marine-life-0247: Which tiny jellyfish can return to the juvenile polyp stage after maturity, earning the name 'immortal jellyfish'?
This jellyfish can reverse its life cycle and repeatedly return to the polyp stage.
marine-life-0248: Why is the Portuguese man-of-war not a true jellyfish?
It is a marine plant resembling jellyfish
It is a colony of specialized organisms working together
It is a type of shelled mollusk
It lives in freshwater and inland lakes rather than the sea
The Portuguese man-of-war is a siphonophore, a colony of specialized individuals called zooids.
marine-life-0249: What helps the Portuguese man-of-war float and move with the wind on the sea surface?
Sticky air bubbles secreted beneath its body
A gas-filled sac resembling a sail
A floating gas sac acts as a sail, letting the wind propel it.
marine-life-0250: What living crustacean has the greatest leg span, reaching about four meters?
Red king crab in the Bering Sea
The Japanese spider crab has the longest leg span of any arthropod.
marine-life-0251: What is the largest land-dwelling arthropod, which begins life as a marine larva?
The coconut crab is the largest terrestrial arthropod, and its larvae develop in the sea.
marine-life-0252: Which marine creature is called a 'living fossil' and has blue blood used to test the safety of drugs and vaccines?
Hermit crab with its borrowed shell
A substance extracted from horseshoe crab blood detects bacterial contamination in medicines.
marine-life-0253: To which animals is the horseshoe crab more closely related than to true crabs?
The horseshoe crab is a chelicerate and is more closely related to spiders and scorpions.
marine-life-0254: Which large armored crustacean escapes danger by rapidly flexing its muscular tail to move backward?
Lobsters escape backward with rapid tail strokes.
marine-life-0255: Which group of tiny crustaceans is among the most numerous planktonic animals in the sea?
Copepods are tiny crustaceans forming a large proportion of zooplankton.
marine-life-0256: Which large woodlouse-like crustacean lives on the deep seabed and feeds on fallen carcasses?
Giant isopods are deep-sea scavengers that eat material falling to the bottom.
marine-life-0257: Which marine arthropods have long legs and bodies so small that their digestive organs extend into their legs?
The sea spider's body is so small that parts of its digestive system and organs extend into its legs.
marine-life-0259: Which enzyme catalyzes the light-producing reaction in luminous organisms?
marine-life-0260: Which microscopic organisms make beach waves glow blue at night when disturbed?
Many dinoflagellates emit light when water is disturbed, making waves glow at night.
marine-life-0261: Which of these marine animals are most closely related to starfish?
Starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers are all echinoderms.
marine-life-0262: Which part of a sea urchin is eaten as a delicacy in some cuisines?
Sea urchin gonads are eaten and are known in Japan as uni.
marine-life-0263: What is the sea urchin's mouth apparatus, consisting of five teeth, muscles, and plates, called?
Aristotle described the sea urchin's chewing apparatus, which was named Aristotle's lantern.
marine-life-0264: What material forms the needlelike skeleton of many glass sponges?
Glass sponge spicules consist of silica, whereas calcareous sponge spicules consist of calcium carbonate.
marine-life-0265: How does a stationary sea sponge feed?
It catches fish with stinging tentacles
It filters food particles from water pumped through its body
It makes food solely by photosynthesis through algae attached to its outer surface
It absorbs food from the rock it clings to
Sponges pump water through pores and channels, filtering out bacteria and food particles.
marine-life-0266: Which colorful shell-less marine mollusks are sometimes called sea slugs?
Nudibranchs are sea slugs that lose their shells as adults and are known for bright colors.
marine-life-0267: Which venomous sea snail hunts fish with a harpoon-like tooth that injects potent venom?
Cone snails fire a modified harpoon-like tooth that injects venom potentially fatal to humans.
marine-life-0269: What organisms drift with water currents because they cannot swim against them?
Plankton are carried by currents and cannot swim against them.
marine-life-0271: Which plankton group photosynthesizes and produces a large share of Earth's oxygen?
Phytoplankton photosynthesize and produce about half the oxygen generated by photosynthesis on Earth.
marine-life-0272: Which single-celled algae surround themselves with a glassy silica wall?
Diatoms are microscopic algae with silica walls called frustules.
marine-life-0274: Which huge brown algae grow in cold water, forming underwater 'forests'?
Kelp grows in cold, nutrient-rich waters, forming underwater forests.
marine-life-0275: What is the main difference between seagrasses and seaweeds?
Seagrasses are flowering plants with true roots
Seagrasses are flowering plants with roots, stems, and flowers, whereas seaweeds are not flowering plants.
marine-life-0276: Which tropical coastal habitat has trees growing in saltwater that protect coasts from erosion?
Mangroves tolerate salt, and their roots protect coasts from erosion and waves.
marine-life-0277: An extremely cold area where water freezes year-round
An area with many underwater volcanoes that keep its water boiling
An area so oxygen-poor that most organisms cannot live there
An area completely devoid of dissolved salts
Dead zones are oxygen-depleted waters, often caused by the decomposition of algal blooms resulting from nutrient pollution.
marine-life-0278: What commonly causes dead zones near large river mouths?
Cold water rising from the depths
Many large whales consuming dissolved oxygen
Runoff of fertilizers and nutrients causing algal blooms
Agricultural nutrients cause algal blooms, whose decomposition then consumes oxygen.
marine-life-0279: What is catching fish faster than they can reproduce and replenish their numbers called?
Overfishing depletes fish stocks faster than they can recover.
marine-life-0280: What is the unintended catching of marine creatures such as dolphins and turtles while fishing for another species called?
Bycatch consists of organisms unintentionally caught in nets.
marine-life-0281: What are lost or abandoned fishing nets that keep catching and killing marine creatures called?
Ghost nets are lost nets that remain in the sea and continue trapping creatures.
marine-life-0283: How many nautical miles does a coastal state's exclusive economic zone extend from its baseline?
Up to 200 nautical miles, subject to maritime boundary delimitation
The exclusive economic zone extends up to 200 nautical miles under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.
marine-life-0284: How wide may a coastal state's territorial sea be under the law of the sea?
The territorial sea extends up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline.
marine-life-0285: How many meters equal one international nautical mile?
A nautical mile equals 1852 meters by international definition.
marine-life-0286: What unit of ship speed equals one nautical mile per hour?
A knot is a speed unit equal to one nautical mile per hour.
marine-life-0288: Which French explorer co-invented the underwater breathing apparatus 'Aqua-Lung' in 1943?
Cousteau developed the Aqua-Lung with engineer Emile Gagnan in 1943.
marine-life-0290: Which technology uses sound waves to map the seabed and detect underwater objects?
Sonar sends sound pulses and receives their echoes to determine depths and locate objects.
marine-life-0292: Which American marine biologist was nicknamed 'Her Deepness' for her many dives and explorations?
Sylvia Earle is a marine biologist and explorer nicknamed 'Her Deepness.'
marine-life-0293: Which coastal instruments monitor sea-level rise worldwide alongside satellites?
Sea-level changes are measured by coastal tide gauges and satellite altimetry.
marine-life-0294: What are the two main causes of sea-level rise in recent decades?
Melting ice and thermal expansion of seawater
Increased rainfall and many new rivers
Sinking continents and a rising ocean floor due to tectonic plates
Sea level rises through melting glaciers and ice sheets and the thermal expansion of water.
marine-life-0296: Which islands' marine and land organisms inspired Darwin's studies and are known for marine iguanas?
Marine iguanas live only in the Galapagos Islands.
marine-life-0297: What are the microscopic and small marine animals that eat phytoplankton and provide food for fish called?
Zooplankton eat phytoplankton and transfer energy to fish and higher consumers.
marine-life-0298: What daily migration do many planktonic organisms and small ocean fish perform?
Moving from the sea to rivers every morning
Circling the entire ocean with currents once a day
Swimming from the pole to the equator every day
Rising to the surface at night and descending by day
Diel vertical migration is Earth's largest animal migration: organisms rise at night to feed and descend during the day.
marine-life-0299: Which Southern Ocean animal is among the animal species with the greatest biomass on Earth?
Antarctic krill have one of the greatest biomasses of any single animal species.
marine-life-0300: Which seabirds have a large skin pouch beneath their beaks for scooping up fish?
Pelicans have a broad skin pouch beneath the beak for scooping up fish and water.
marine-life-0301: Which seabird steals other birds' food and avoids landing on water because its feathers become waterlogged?
Frigatebirds steal other birds' food; limited gland oil means their feathers become waterlogged if they land on water.
marine-life-0302: Which seabird plunges into water like an arrow from a great height to catch fish?
Gannets plunge from great heights, diving like arrows to catch fish.
marine-life-0303: Which colorful-billed Arctic seabirds resemble penguins in shape but can fly?
Puffins are colorful-billed auks that fly and dive in the North Atlantic.
marine-life-0304: Which seabird makes the longest known annual migration between the Arctic and Antarctic?
Arctic terns migrate between northern breeding grounds and the Southern Ocean in the longest known migration.
marine-life-0305: Which black seabirds dive for fish and then stand on rocks with their wings spread to dry?
Cormorant feathers are not fully waterproof, so they stand with wings spread to dry them.
marine-life-0306: Which whale has had an isolated, nonmigratory population in the Arabian Sea near Oman for tens of thousands of years?
The Arabian Sea humpback population is isolated and nonmigratory; a study using Oman data (2000-2004) estimated about 80 individuals.
marine-life-0307: Which threatened seabird is endemic to the Arabian Gulf and southeastern Arabian coast and found nowhere else?
The Socotra cormorant is endemic to the Gulf and southeastern Arabian Peninsula.
marine-life-0308: Which Gulf islands have a large protected Socotra cormorant nesting colony and a large surrounding dugong population?
Bahrain's Hawar Islands have a large surrounding dugong population and a protected Socotra cormorant colony.
marine-life-0309: Which luminous microscopic organism causes green blooms in the Arabian Sea and Gulf of Oman and is known as 'sea sparkle'?
Noctiluca is a luminous dinoflagellate abundant in the Arabian Sea and Gulf of Oman.
marine-life-0310: Which inlet at the head of the Arabian Gulf overlooks Kuwait City?
Kuwait Bay is a small bay at the head of the Arabian Gulf, with Kuwait City on its shore.
marine-life-0312: Approximately what proportion of the ocean floor is covered by coral reefs?
Reefs cover less than 0.1% of the ocean floor but shelter about a quarter of marine species.
marine-life-0313: Approximately what proportion of marine species do coral reefs shelter despite their small area?
Coral reefs shelter about a quarter of marine species.
marine-life-0314: All dead coral falls to the bottom at once each year
Many colonies release their eggs on roughly the same night
All reefs move toward deeper water
Many coral colonies release their gametes together on particular nights timed to lunar and temperature conditions.
marine-life-0315: Which organisms secrete lime and form a pink crust that cements coral reef structures?
Red coralline algae secrete lime and cement reef structures.
marine-life-0316: How do some mangrove trees germinate their seeds before they fall into the water?
The seeds germinate while still on the parent tree
The seeds wait years on the bottom before germinating
Birds carry the seeds to distant land
The tree buries its seeds in mud using its roots
Many mangroves are viviparous: their seeds germinate on the parent tree, then fall as ready seedlings.
marine-life-0317: Approximately what proportion of an iceberg's volume is submerged below sea level?
Ice density is close to seawater density, so about nine-tenths of an iceberg remains underwater.
marine-life-0320: Which famous Atlantic hydrothermal field has vents building white carbonate chimneys?
Sea of Darkness field near the Azores
At the Lost City field near the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, alkaline vents build white carbonate chimneys.
marine-life-0321: What is unusual about male anglerfish behavior in some deep-sea species?
They fuse with the female's body and live parasitically on her
They build a sand nest for the female
They drive females out of their territory and live alone until death
They carry eggs in their mouths until they hatch
In some anglerfish species, the small male bites the female, fuses with her, and becomes dependent on her.
marine-life-0322: Which deep-sea fish has a transparent dome on its head through which its tubular eyes are visible?
Barreleyes have transparent heads and upward-facing tubular eyes.
marine-life-0323: Why does the blobfish look saggy and jellylike when brought to the surface?
Its body is adapted to enormous deep-sea pressure
It absorbs freshwater from rivers, swelling its tissues
It has no bones at all
The blobfish's gelatinous flesh suits extreme deep-sea pressure and sags outside those conditions.
marine-life-0325: Which white crustacean with densely hairy arms was discovered near hydrothermal vents in the South Pacific?
The yeti crab has hairy arms supporting bacteria and was discovered near hydrothermal vents.
marine-life-0326: How do dolphins sleep without drowning?
They close their blowholes and sleep on the bottom for hours
They beach themselves and sleep on sand
They never sleep, relying on slow swimming instead
One brain hemisphere sleeps while the other stays awake
Dolphins alternate sleeping brain hemispheres so the other can control breathing and movement.
marine-life-0327: How do tuna breathe while continuously swimming?
Only by absorbing oxygen through their skin
By keeping their mouths open so water passes over their gills
By storing air in their swim bladders and drawing on it when needed
Tuna rely on ram ventilation, swimming with open mouths to pass water over their gills.
marine-life-0329: What happens when a shark's teeth fall out or break?
It grows an entirely new jaw each year
It swallows them to use their calcium to build other teeth
New teeth from rows behind continually replace them
Sharks have rows of replacement teeth that advance to replace lost ones throughout life.
marine-life-0330: How does the loggerhead turtle navigate on long ocean migrations?
By tracking the scent of distant beaches
By observing water color and temperature along the way
Loggerhead turtles sense Earth's magnetic field and use it for navigation.
marine-life-0332: How do scientists estimate a bony fish's age?
By weighing its gills and heart immediately after capture
By counting annual rings in ear stones or scales
Ear stones (otoliths) and scales develop annual growth rings that are counted like tree rings.
marine-life-0333: What is the world's smallest and shallowest ocean?
The Arctic Ocean is the smallest and shallowest of the five oceans.
marine-life-0334: What is the world's second-largest ocean by area?
The Atlantic is the second-largest ocean after the Pacific.
marine-life-0335: Where does the Indian Ocean rank among the world's oceans by area?
The Indian Ocean is the world's third-largest ocean.
marine-life-0336: Approximately how much does water pressure increase for every ten meters descended in the sea?
Pressure does not change with depth
Only about one-tenth of an atmosphere
Water pressure increases by about one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth.
marine-life-0338: Which herbivorous marine mammal group includes dugongs and manatees?
The order Sirenia includes dugongs and manatees, which are herbivorous marine mammals.
marine-life-0339: Which huge sirenian became extinct in the eighteenth century only about 27 years after its discovery?
Steller's sea cow was discovered in 1741 and became extinct by 1768 due to hunting.
marine-life-0340: How many sea turtle species live in the world's oceans today?
There are seven living sea turtle species.
marine-life-0341: When does a female sea turtle usually come ashore to dig a nest and lay eggs?
Female sea turtles usually come ashore at night to nest.
marine-life-0343: Which Arctic seal gives birth to pups with brilliant white fur?
Harp seal pups are born with white fur that changes after a few weeks.
marine-life-0344: Which small silver fish forms huge schools in the North Atlantic and was the basis of an old European trade?
Herring are silvery schooling fish that were central to a major trade in northern Europe.
marine-life-0345: To which marine animal group do brittle stars with thin, flexible arms belong?
Brittle stars are echinoderms closely related to starfish.
marine-life-0346: Which mollusk has more than a hundred tiny eyes along the edges of its shell?
Edible oyster of the genus Ostrea
Scallops have rows of tiny eyes along their mantle edges, sometimes exceeding two hundred.
marine-life-0347: Unlike most bivalves, how does a scallop move through water?
It swims by rapidly opening and closing its shell
It crawls with a long muscular foot
It continually burrows in sand with its strong muscular foot
It only drifts with the current
Scallops swim by clapping their shells, expelling water for propulsion.
marine-life-0348: Which bristled marine annelid causes painful burning when touched?
Fireworms bear bristles that pierce skin and cause painful burning.
marine-life-0349: Which transparent gelatinous creatures move using rows of shimmering cilia and do not sting?
Comb jellies swim with eight rows of beating cilia, and most lack stinging cells.
marine-life-0354: Which cold current carries icebergs south from the Arctic toward Newfoundland?
The cold Labrador Current carries icebergs south from Baffin Bay toward Newfoundland.
marine-life-0355: What pattern decorates whale shark skin and distinguishes each individual?
Bright blue rings on the tail
Black transverse stripes like a tiger's
Whale sharks have pale spots and light lines with a pattern unique to each individual.
marine-life-0356: Approximately how long can a dugong live?
Dugongs may live about 70 years or more.
marine-life-0357: Which fish lays more eggs at once than any other known vertebrate, potentially reaching 300 million?
Female ocean sunfish produce more eggs than any other known vertebrate.
marine-life-0358: What is the largest known octopus species, found in the North Pacific?
The giant Pacific octopus is the largest and heaviest octopus species.
marine-life-0359: Approximately how deep can a leatherback turtle dive?
Leatherback turtles are among the deepest-diving reptiles and may descend beyond a thousand meters.
marine-life-0360: Which of these marine mammals is an apex predator that no other sea animal preys upon?
The killer whale is an apex predator at the top of the marine food chain and has no natural predator.
marine-life-0361: Which copper-containing protein carries oxygen in octopus blood instead of hemoglobin?
Hemocyanin carries oxygen using two copper atoms. First discovered in the common octopus in 1878, it turns blue when oxygenated.
marine-life-0362: In which ocean is Point Nemo, the sea location farthest from the nearest land?
Point Nemo lies in the South Pacific, about 2688 kilometers from the three nearest land areas.
marine-life-0363: Fire coral, painful for divers to touch, is not true stony coral. To which cnidarian class does it belong?
Fire coral belongs to Hydrozoa and is more closely related to hydras than to stony coral.
marine-life-0364: What tool does a sea otter use while floating on its back to open its prey's hard shells?
A kelp stalk wrapped around the shell
A fish bone to split the shell
A stone placed on its chest
A coral fragment to scrape the edge
A sea otter strikes a shell against a stone on its chest; it is among the few mammals that use tools.
marine-life-0365: What phenomenon occurs when winds push surface water away from the coast, replacing it with cold, nutrient-rich deep water and supporting rich fisheries such as Peru's?
Upwelling is wind-driven movement in which cold, nutrient-rich deep water replaces surface water, explaining Peru's rich fisheries.
marine-life-0366: What is the organic carbon captured by oceans and coastal ecosystems and stored in their plants and sediments called?
Blue carbon is organic carbon captured and stored by oceans and coastal ecosystems such as seagrass meadows and tidal marshes.
astronomy-0001: Which planet has the hottest surface in the Solar System despite not being closest to the Sun?
Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, making it the hottest planet even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
astronomy-0002: Which planet takes longer to rotate on its axis than to orbit the Sun?
Venus rotates on its axis in about 243 Earth days but completes an orbit of the Sun in about 225 days.
astronomy-0003: What causes the reddish color of Mars?
Sunlight reflecting off its polar ice
Its extreme proximity to the asteroid belt
Iron oxide spread through its soil and dust
Iron oxide (rust)-rich dust covers Mars's surface, making it look red.
astronomy-0004: One of the Solar System's tallest known volcanoes is on Mars. What is it called?
Olympus Mons is a shield volcano on Mars that rises more than 20 kilometers.
astronomy-0005: What are the names of Mars's two moons?
Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, discovered by astronomer Asaph Hall in 1877.
astronomy-0006: What is Jupiter's Great Red Spot actually?
The shadow of one of its large moons
The Great Red Spot is a giant anticyclone in Jupiter's atmosphere, larger than Earth and observed for over a century and a half.
astronomy-0007: What is the largest moon in the entire Solar System?
Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter, is the Solar System's largest moon and has a larger diameter than Mercury.
astronomy-0009: Which Solar System body is the most volcanically active?
Jupiter's moon Io is the most volcanically active Solar System body due to Jupiter's enormous tidal forces.
astronomy-0010: Why are scientists interested in Jupiter's moon Europa in the search for habitable environments?
Its surface has lakes of liquid methane
It is the Solar System moon closest to the Sun
Its atmosphere is dense and oxygen-rich
It likely has a liquid water ocean beneath its icy crust
Evidence suggests a saltwater ocean beneath Europa's icy crust.
astronomy-0011: Which planet's average density is lower than that of water?
Saturn's average density is about 0.69 grams per cubic centimeter, lower than water's.
astronomy-0012: Which is the only Solar System moon surrounded by a dense atmosphere?
Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere, mainly nitrogen.
astronomy-0013: On which Saturnian moon did Cassini discover jets of water vapor and ice from the south pole?
Cassini observed plumes of water vapor and ice erupting from Enceladus's south polar region.
astronomy-0014: Which planet's axis is tilted about 98 degrees, making it appear to orbit the Sun lying on its side?
Uranus's axis tilts about 98 degrees, so one pole faces the Sun near solstice, rather than throughout its orbit.
astronomy-0015: William Herschel discovered Uranus on 13 March 1781, making it the first planet discovered with a telescope.
astronomy-0016: Which planet's position was calculated mathematically before it was discovered as a planet with a telescope?
Le Verrier predicted Neptune's position from disturbances in Uranus's orbit, and Galle observed it near the predicted position in 1846.
astronomy-0017: What distinguishes the orbit of Triton, Neptune's largest moon, from those of other large moons?
It orbits opposite to its planet's rotation
Its orbit is perfectly circular with no inclination
It has the fastest known lunar orbit
It orbits the Sun rather than Neptune
Triton is the only large moon with a retrograde orbit, opposite Neptune's rotation, suggesting it was captured from the Kuiper belt.
astronomy-0018: Which planet has the fastest observed atmospheric winds?
Neptune's winds reach about 2100 kilometers per hour, the fastest in the Solar System.
astronomy-0020: Which American astronomer discovered Pluto in 1930?
Clyde Tombaugh discovered Pluto at Lowell Observatory in 1930.
astronomy-0022: Where is the main asteroid belt in the Solar System?
The main asteroid belt lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
astronomy-0023: What does the astronomical unit represent in distance measurement?
The average distance between Earth and the Sun
The radius of the Moon's orbit around Earth
The distance between the Sun and its nearest star
The distance light travels in one year
An astronomical unit is approximately the average Earth-Sun distance, about 150 million kilometers.
astronomy-0024: Approximately how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
The Sun is about 150 million kilometers away, a distance light covers in about 8 minutes and 20 seconds.
astronomy-0025: Which two Solar System planets have no natural moons?
Mercury and Venus are the only planets without natural moons.
astronomy-0026: Approximately what is the tilt of Earth's rotation axis?
Earth's axis tilts about 23.4 degrees from the perpendicular to its orbital plane, causing the seasons.
astronomy-0027: What is the main cause of Earth's four seasons?
Earth's changing distance from the Sun during the year
The tilt of Earth's axis as it orbits the Sun
Earth's axial tilt causes each hemisphere to receive sunlight at different angles during the year, producing seasons.
astronomy-0028: In which month does Earth reach the point in its orbit closest to the Sun?
Earth reaches perihelion in early January, so summer is not tied to proximity to the Sun.
astronomy-0029: Which planet has the shortest day, rotating on its axis in less than ten hours?
Jupiter rotates in about 9 hours and 56 minutes, the shortest day among the planets.
astronomy-0030: What are Saturn's rings mostly made of?
Saturn's rings consist mainly of water-ice particles with some rock and dust.
astronomy-0031: What is the broad gap separating Saturn's A and B rings called?
The Cassini Division is a gap about 4800 kilometers wide between rings A and B, discovered by Giovanni Cassini in 1675.
astronomy-0032: Which planet is popularly known as the 'morning star' and 'evening star'?
Venus is the brightest planet in the sky and appears shortly before sunrise or after sunset, hence these names.
astronomy-0033: Which planet has a day very close in length to Earth's?
A Martian day (sol) is about 24 hours and 39 minutes, very close to an Earth day.
astronomy-0034: Approximately how many Earth years does Neptune take to orbit the Sun once?
Neptune takes about 164.8 Earth years to orbit the Sun once.
astronomy-0035: Approximately how many times is Jupiter's mass greater than the combined mass of all other Solar System planets?
Jupiter's mass is about two and a half times the combined mass of all the other planets.
astronomy-0036: What is the giant canyon system extending over four thousand kilometers across Mars called?
Valles Marineris is a vast canyon on Mars stretching about 4000 kilometers, named after the Mariner 9 probe.
astronomy-0038: Which atmospheric gas gives Uranus its blue-green color?
Methane absorbs red light and reflects blue and green, making Uranus appear blue-green.
astronomy-0039: What is the belt beyond Neptune's orbit containing Pluto and many icy bodies called?
The Kuiper belt is a region beyond Neptune containing small icy bodies, including Pluto.
astronomy-0040: Which distant region is thought to be the source of long-period comets?
The Oort cloud is a theoretical cloud of icy bodies surrounding the Solar System, likely the source of long-period comets.
