human-body-0169: What chemicals does a nerve cell release at a synapse to transmit a signal to the next cell?
Neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine and dopamine are released into the synaptic cleft to transmit signals.
human-body-0170: What is the longest and thickest nerve in the human body?
The sciatic nerve extends from the lower back through the thigh to the lower leg and is the longest and widest nerve.
human-body-0171: How many pairs of cranial nerves do humans have?
Twelve pairs of cranial nerves emerge directly from the brain.
human-body-0172: How many pairs of nerves emerge from the spinal cord?
There are 31 pairs of spinal nerves emerging from the spinal cord.
human-body-0173: Which long cranial nerve travels from the brainstem to the heart, lungs, and digestive system?
The vagus nerve is the tenth cranial nerve and reaches the organs of the chest and abdomen.
human-body-0174: Which reflex does a doctor test by tapping below the patella with a small hammer?
Tapping the patellar tendon stretches the quadriceps, causing an involuntary contraction that makes the lower leg jerk.
human-body-0176: Which division of the autonomic nervous system becomes active in danger, speeding up the heart and dilating the pupil?
The sympathetic nervous system is responsible for the fight-or-flight response, increasing the pulse rate and dilating the pupils.
human-body-0177: Which division of the autonomic nervous system is most active during rest and digestion?
The parasympathetic system is known as the rest-and-digest system; it slows the heart and stimulates digestion.
human-body-0178: What two parts make up the central nervous system?
The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord; nerves outside these are peripheral.
human-body-0179: What stage of sleep involves rapid eye movements and frequent dreams?
The second stage of light sleep
During rapid eye movement sleep, the eyes move rapidly, dreams are more vivid, and the muscles are relaxed.
human-body-0181: What relay station in the brain do most sensory signals pass through before reaching the cortex?
The thalamus relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex.
human-body-0182: What is the convoluted outer gray layer of the cerebrum?
The cerebral cortex is a layer of gray matter covering the cerebrum; its folds increase its surface area.
human-body-0185: What non-neuronal cells support and nourish nerve cells in the nervous system?
Glial cells support, nourish, and insulate neurons and do not themselves transmit nerve impulses.
human-body-0186: Which Spanish scientist demonstrated that the nervous system consists of separate cells and received a Nobel Prize in 1906?
Ramon y Cajal developed the neuron doctrine and shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Golgi.
human-body-0187: At approximately which vertebral level does the spinal cord end in an adult?
The first or second lumbar vertebra
The middle of the thoracic vertebrae
In adults, the spinal cord ends near the first or second lumbar vertebra, with nerves descending beyond it.
human-body-0188: What small gland in the brain secretes melatonin, which regulates sleep?
The pineal gland secretes melatonin at night, helping regulate the sleep-wake cycle.
human-body-0189: What biological clock regulates sleep-wake cycles over approximately 24 hours?
The circadian rhythm is an internal cycle lasting about 24 hours that regulates sleep, hormones, and temperature.
human-body-0190: Which nerve carries images from the eye to the brain?
The optic nerve is the second cranial nerve and transmits visual signals from the retina to the brain.
human-body-0191: What is the scientific name for the fluid-filled cavities inside the brain?
The brain has four ventricles in which cerebrospinal fluid is produced and circulates.
human-body-0194: Which cranial nerve moves the tongue?
The hypoglossal nerve is the twelfth cranial nerve and supplies the tongue muscles.
human-body-0197: What is the ability to sense the position and movement of the limbs without looking at them?
Proprioception relies on receptors in muscles, tendons, and joints that inform the brain of the body's position.
human-body-0198: Which neurotransmitter is associated with reward and motivation and is affected in Parkinson's disease?
Dopamine is a neurotransmitter in reward and movement pathways. Its deficiency in the brain causes Parkinson's symptoms.
human-body-0199: Which neurotransmitter do motor nerves release to make skeletal muscles contract?
Acetylcholine is released at the neuromuscular junction, triggering muscle contraction.
human-body-0200: What is the transparent layer at the front of the eye through which light first enters?
The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye and provides most of the eye's light-refracting power.
human-body-0201: What is the colored part of the eye that controls pupil size?
The iris is a colored muscular ring that constricts and dilates the pupil to regulate the amount of light.
human-body-0202: What happens to the pupil when moving from a dark place into bright light?
In bright light, the pupil contracts and narrows to reduce the amount of light entering the eye.
human-body-0203: What is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the image forms?
The retina contains photoreceptor cells and converts the image into nerve signals.
human-body-0204: Which retinal cells are responsible for color vision?
Cones work in bright light and distinguish colors, while rods provide vision in dim light.
human-body-0205: Which retinal cells enable people to see in dim light?
Rods are highly sensitive to light and work in dim lighting, but they do not distinguish colors.
human-body-0206: How many types of cone cells are in the retina of a person with normal vision?
Humans have three types of cones, sensitive to short, medium, and long wavelengths.
human-body-0207: Why is there a blind spot in each eye's visual field?
Because the eyelid always covers part of the pupil
Because the point where the optic nerve leaves the retina has no photoreceptors
Because the lens does not refract light at its edges
Because the cornea is opaque in its center
There are no rods or cones at the optic disc, so an image falling there is not seen.
human-body-0208: What small area at the center of the retina provides the clearest, most detailed vision?
The fovea centralis is densely packed with cones, providing the highest visual acuity.
human-body-0210: Which vision defect allows a person to see nearby objects clearly while distant ones appear blurry?
In nearsightedness, images of distant objects focus in front of the retina and appear blurry.
human-body-0211: Which type of lens is used to correct nearsightedness?
A concave lens slightly diverges light rays, moving the image back onto the retina.
human-body-0213: Deficiency of which vitamin causes night blindness and poor vision in the dark?
Vitamin A is essential for forming rhodopsin pigment in rods, and its deficiency causes night blindness.
human-body-0214: Which eye condition makes the lens cloudy and opaque, often with aging?
A cataract is clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision. It is treated by removing the lens and implanting a replacement.
human-body-0215: Which disease involves increased eye pressure that gradually damages the optic nerve?
Glaucoma is a group of diseases that damage the optic nerve. Increased eye pressure is its main risk factor.
human-body-0216: Where is the lacrimal gland that secretes tears located?
Below the eye in the cheek
In the inner corner near the nose
In the upper outer part of the eye socket
The lacrimal gland is in the upper outer part of the orbit. Tears then drain through ducts near the nose.
human-body-0217: What thin transparent membrane covers the white of the eye and the inner surfaces of the eyelids?
The conjunctiva is a thin mucous membrane covering the sclera and the inner eyelids. Its inflammation is called conjunctivitis.
human-body-0218: What strong white layer forms the outer covering of most of the eyeball?
The sclera is a tough white fibrous coat that protects the eye and maintains its shape.
human-body-0219: What transparent gel fills the vitreous chamber behind the lens and in front of the retina?
The vitreous body is a transparent gel filling the space between the lens and retina and maintaining the eye's shape.
human-body-0220: How does the eye change its focus to see nearby objects clearly?
The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens
During accommodation, the ciliary muscle contracts, increasing the lens's curvature to see nearby objects.
human-body-0221: What is the light-sensitive pigment found in rod cells called?
Rhodopsin is a pigment in rods that breaks down in light, initiating a visual signal.
human-body-0222: What membrane separates the outer ear from the middle ear and vibrates with sound?
The eardrum is a thin membrane that vibrates with sound waves and transmits its vibrations to the ossicles.
human-body-0223: What are the three middle-ear ossicles, in order from the eardrum inward?
The malleus connects to the eardrum, followed by the incus and then the stapes, which transmits vibrations to the inner ear.
human-body-0224: What spiral-shaped part of the inner ear converts vibrations into nerve signals for hearing?
The cochlea is a fluid-filled spiral tube containing hair cells that convert vibrations into auditory signals.
human-body-0225: Which inner-ear structures sense balance and head movement?
The three semicircular canals contain fluid that moves as the head rotates, allowing balance to be sensed.
human-body-0226: What tube connects the middle ear to the pharynx and equalizes pressure on both sides of the eardrum?
The Eustachian tube opens during swallowing and yawning to equalize pressure, as happens on an airplane.
human-body-0227: What is the approximate range of sound frequencies a healthy young person can hear?
Humans normally hear sounds between about 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz.
human-body-0228: What waxy substance do glands in the external auditory canal secrete to protect it?
Earwax is a waxy substance that traps dust and germs and protects the skin of the canal.
human-body-0229: What unit measures sound intensity when discussing noise and its risk to hearing?
Sound intensity is measured in decibels. Prolonged exposure to high intensity damages hearing cells.
human-body-0231: Where are the olfactory receptors that detect odors located?
At the roof of the nasal cavity
At the front openings of the nostrils
The olfactory epithelium at the top of the nasal cavity contains odor-receptor nerve cells.
human-body-0233: What fifth taste was added to sweet, salty, sour, and bitter and is described as the savory taste of broth?
Umami is a taste the tongue detects from glutamate, found in broth, tomatoes, and cheese.
human-body-0235: Approximately how often are taste-bud cells renewed?
Taste-bud cells are short-lived and renew about every 10 days.
human-body-0236: Which sensory receptors in the skin resemble an onion and detect vibration and deep pressure?
Pacinian corpuscles have onion-like layers deep in the skin and detect vibration and pressure.
human-body-0237: Which touch receptors, abundant in the fingertips and lips, detect light touch?
Meissner corpuscles lie near the skin surface, are abundant in the fingertips and lips, and are sensitive to light touch.
human-body-0238: What are the sensory receptors that transmit pain sensations called?
Nociceptors are nerve endings that respond to harmful stimuli and transmit pain.
human-body-0239: What visible outer part of the ear collects sounds and directs them into the auditory canal?
The pinna is cartilage covered with skin that collects sound waves and directs them toward the canal.
human-body-0241: What reflex makes us automatically close our eyes when something approaches them or touches the cornea?
The blink reflex is involuntary closure of the eyelids that protects the eye from objects and irritants.
human-body-0242: Approximately how many times per minute does a person normally blink?
The average blink rate is about 17 times per minute and decreases greatly when concentrating on reading.
human-body-0243: How many external muscles move each eyeball within its socket?
Each eye has six external muscles: four rectus muscles and two oblique muscles.
human-body-0244: What condition occurs when both eyes do not point at the same spot at the same time?
Strabismus is misalignment of the eyes, with each looking in a different direction.
human-body-0245: What transparent fluid fills the anterior chamber of the eye between the cornea and iris?
Aqueous humor nourishes the cornea and lens. Impaired drainage raises eye pressure.
human-body-0246: Which senses are affected by damage to the vestibulocochlear nerve?
The vestibulocochlear nerve is the eighth cranial nerve and carries hearing and balance signals.
human-body-0247: What is the most numerous type of white blood cell in a healthy adult's blood?
Neutrophils make up about half or more of white blood cells and are the first to reach an infection site.
human-body-0248: What large immune cells engulf and digest germs and cell debris and reside in the lungs, liver, and spleen?
Macrophages are large cells that engulf foreign bodies and dead cells through phagocytosis.
human-body-0249: What is the process by which an immune cell engulfs and digests a germ called?
Phagocytosis is a process in which a cell surrounds a foreign particle, engulfs it, and then digests it.
human-body-0250: What proteins produced by B cells bind specifically to germs to neutralize them?
Antibodies are Y-shaped proteins that recognize and bind to a specific antigen.
human-body-0251: What is a foreign molecule that stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies called?
An antigen is a molecule recognized by the immune system, which responds by producing antibodies.
human-body-0252: What gland behind the breastbone is where T lymphocytes mature?
T cells mature in the thymus, which is why they are named with the letter T.
human-body-0253: Where do B lymphocytes mature in humans?
B cells form and mature in the bone marrow, then move to the lymphoid organs.
human-body-0254: Which lymphocytes kill virus-infected cells and some cancer cells without prior sensitization?
Natural killer cells are part of innate immunity and directly kill infected and tumor cells.
human-body-0255: What cells remain in the body after infection or vaccination and quickly recognize the germ if it returns?
Memory B and T cells retain a record of the antigen, making the second response faster and stronger.
human-body-0256: What substance do mast cells release during allergies, causing itching, sneezing, and a runny nose?
Histamine dilates blood vessels and increases their permeability, producing allergy symptoms.
human-body-0257: Which type of antibody is primarily associated with allergic reactions?
Immunoglobulin E binds to mast cells and triggers histamine release in allergies.
human-body-0258: Which antibody is most abundant in the blood and crosses the placenta to the fetus?
Immunoglobulin G is the most abundant antibody in the blood and the only one that crosses the placenta.
human-body-0259: Which antibody is abundant in secretions such as saliva, tears, and mucus?
Immunoglobulin A protects mucous membranes and is abundant in secretions.
human-body-0260: What antibacterial enzyme is found in tears and saliva?
Lysozyme breaks down the walls of some bacteria and is found in tears, saliva, and mucus.
human-body-0261: What are the four classic signs of inflammation described by ancient physicians?
Coldness, bluish discoloration, numbness, and tingling
The four signs of inflammation are redness, heat, swelling, and pain; loss of function was added later.
human-body-0262: What benefit does a rise in body temperature (fever) provide during infection?
It kills weak white blood cells
It increases saliva secretion to wash away germs
It helps the immune system and hinders the multiplication of some germs
It makes the body eliminate excess water
Fever improves the efficiency of some immune responses and makes conditions less favorable for some germs.
human-body-0265: What is the body's largest lymphoid organ, located in the upper left abdomen?
The spleen is the largest lymphoid organ. It filters blood and removes aging red blood cells.
human-body-0266: What two lymphoid masses on either side of the throat form a defense at the entrance to the respiratory and digestive systems?
The tonsils are lymphoid tissue in the throat that intercept germs entering with air and food.
human-body-0267: Which English physician developed a smallpox vaccine in 1796 using cowpox?
Edward Jenner demonstrated that inoculation with cowpox protects against smallpox, establishing the basis of vaccination.
human-body-0268: Which disease did the World Health Organization declare eradicated in 1980 thanks to vaccination?
Smallpox was the first human disease eradicated worldwide, as announced in 1980.
human-body-0269: What type of immunity does an infant receive from antibodies in its mother's milk?
Ready-made antibodies transferred to an infant provide temporary passive immunity.
human-body-0271: What proteins do virus-infected cells secrete to warn nearby cells and help them resist infection?
Infected cells release interferons, activating neighboring cells' defenses against the virus.
human-body-0272: What first line of defense prevents most germs from entering the body in the first place?
Intact skin and mucous membranes form a physical barrier that prevents most germs from entering.
human-body-0273: What type of immunity is present from birth and responds quickly and nonspecifically to any germ?
Innate immunity is a rapid, general defense present from birth that requires no previous exposure.
human-body-0274: What vessels return excess fluid from tissues to the bloodstream?
Lymphatic vessels collect excess interstitial fluid and return it to the blood.
human-body-0275: What antibiotic did Alexander Fleming discover in 1928 from a mold fungus?
Fleming observed that Penicillium mold killed surrounding bacteria, leading to the discovery of penicillin.
human-body-0277: Which lymphocytes does human immunodeficiency virus attack, weakening the immune system?
HIV infects CD4 helper T cells, reducing their numbers and weakening immunity.
human-body-0278: What immune cells carry antigens and present them to T cells and are named for their branching shape?
Dendritic cells are antigen-presenting cells that activate T cells and have branching projections.
human-body-0279: What is a rapid, severe allergic reaction that may threaten life called?
Anaphylaxis is an acute allergic reaction affecting multiple systems that may cause low blood pressure and breathing difficulty.
human-body-0281: What is the pus that collects in inflamed wounds?
Clear lymph fluid from the nodes
Fluid containing dead white blood cells and germ debris
Pus consists mainly of dead neutrophils and tissue and germ debris.
human-body-0282: Which type of white blood cell increases in number during allergies and parasitic infections?
Eosinophils participate in defense against parasites and in allergic reactions.
human-body-0283: Protection of nonimmune people when a large proportion of the community is immune
When most people are immune, infection spreads less easily, protecting those without immunity.
human-body-0284: What lymphoid patches are found in the small intestinal wall, especially the ileum?
Peyer patches are lymphoid clusters in the ileal wall that monitor germs in the intestine.
human-body-0285: What substance does a doctor use to stimulate immunity against a specific disease without making the person ill?
A vaccine contains weakened germs or parts of them, training the immune system without causing disease.
human-body-0286: For which disease did Louis Pasteur famously develop a vaccine in 1885?
Louis Pasteur developed a rabies vaccine and successfully tested it on a child in 1885.
human-body-0287: What precursor cells in the bone marrow give rise to all blood cells?
Hematopoietic stem cells in the bone marrow differentiate into red cells, white cells, and platelets.
human-body-0288: Which antibody appears first upon initial exposure to a germ and is the largest?
Immunoglobulin M is the first antibody produced in the primary response and is a large pentamer.
human-body-0289: What depigmentation disease causes white patches on the skin and is considered an autoimmune disease?
In vitiligo, areas of skin lose pigment cells. It is thought to be an autoimmune disease.
human-body-0290: What cells do B cells become to secrete large quantities of antibodies?
Activated B cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete abundant antibodies.
human-body-0291: Which white blood cells become macrophages when they leave the blood and enter tissues?
Monocytes are the largest white blood cells and differentiate into macrophages in tissues.
human-body-0292: What chronic respiratory disease narrows the airways, causing wheezing and shortness of breath?
Asthma is chronic inflammation of the airways that causes narrowing, wheezing, and shortness of breath.
human-body-0293: What small gland attached to the base of the brain produces hormones that regulate growth and thyroid activity?
The pituitary gland at the base of the brain secretes hormones that regulate the thyroid, adrenal glands, and others.
human-body-0294: What element does the thyroid gland need to make its hormones and is added to table salt?
The two thyroid hormones contain iodine. Its deficiency may cause enlargement of the gland, called goiter.
human-body-0295: What is the shape of the thyroid gland at the front of the neck?
The thyroid has two lobes connected by an isthmus, making it resemble a butterfly.
human-body-0296: Where are the two adrenal glands located?
The adrenal glands sit like caps above the kidneys and secrete adrenaline and cortisol.
human-body-0297: What hormone is released abundantly during fear and danger, speeding up the heartbeat?
The adrenal medulla releases adrenaline during the fight-or-flight response, speeding up the heart and breathing.
human-body-0298: What hormone lowers blood sugar by allowing it to enter cells?
Insulin from pancreatic beta cells allows cells to absorb glucose, lowering blood sugar.
human-body-0299: What pancreatic hormone raises blood sugar when it falls?
Glucagon stimulates the liver to convert glycogen into glucose, raising blood sugar.
human-body-0300: What insulin-secreting cell groups in the pancreas are named after their German discoverer?
The islets of Langerhans are endocrine cell clusters in the pancreas containing insulin-secreting beta cells.
human-body-0301: Which Canadian scientist helped discover insulin in 1921 and won a Nobel Prize?
Frederick Banting discovered insulin with Charles Best. Banting received the Nobel Prize in 1923.
human-body-0302: What hormone is called the stress hormone and is secreted by the adrenal cortex?
Cortisol rises during stress, raises blood sugar, and suppresses inflammation.
human-body-0305: What condition results from excess growth hormone production in childhood, causing greatly increased height?
Excess growth hormone before the growth plates close leads to gigantism and excessive height.
human-body-0306: What tiny functional unit in the kidney filters blood and forms urine?
The nephron is the basic unit for filtering blood and forming urine in the kidney.
human-body-0307: Approximately how many nephrons does one human kidney contain?
Each kidney contains about a million nephrons, with variation between individuals.
human-body-0308: What coiled network of blood capillaries at the start of the nephron is where blood filtration begins?
The glomerulus is a mass of capillaries from which blood is filtered into Bowman's capsule as urine formation begins.
human-body-0309: What two tubes carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder?
The ureters are two muscular tubes that propel urine from the renal pelvis to the bladder.
human-body-0310: What shape does the kidney have, to which many things are compared?
The kidney is a bean-shaped organ about 10 to 13 cm long.
human-body-0311: What is the main substance through which the kidney removes protein waste?
Urea is the main waste product of protein breakdown. It forms in the liver and is excreted by the kidney in urine.
human-body-0312: What medical procedure cleans the blood using an external machine when the kidneys fail?
Dialysis removes waste and excess fluid from the blood in place of diseased kidneys.
human-body-0313: What outer skin layer has cells that continually renew and shed?
The epidermis is the surface layer. Its cells are produced at its base, then rise and shed.
human-body-0314: What middle skin layer contains hair follicles, sweat glands, and blood vessels?
The dermis lies beneath the epidermis and contains blood vessels, nerves, hair follicles, and glands.
human-body-0315: What pigment gives skin and hair their color and protects against ultraviolet radiation?
Melanin is a pigment produced by pigment cells that absorbs ultraviolet radiation.
human-body-0316: What tough protein makes up hair, nails, and the outer skin layer?
Keratin is a strong fibrous protein forming hair, nails, and the stratum corneum.
human-body-0317: What is the most abundant protein in the human body, giving skin and tendons their strength?
Collagen is the most abundant protein in mammals and is found in skin, bones, and tendons.
human-body-0318: What vitamin does the skin produce when exposed to sunlight?
Ultraviolet radiation converts a substance in the skin into vitamin D.
human-body-0319: What skin glands secrete an oily substance that softens hair and skin?
Sebaceous glands secrete sebum through hair follicles, moisturizing skin and hair.
human-body-0320: How does sweat help cool the body?
By evaporating from the skin surface and taking heat with it
By constricting blood vessels in the skin
Sweat evaporation draws heat from the skin, lowering body temperature.
human-body-0321: What causes goosebumps during cold or fear?
Contraction of small muscles at the hair follicles
The arrector pili muscles contract, raising the hairs and producing bumps on the skin.
human-body-0322: During the first year of life
Fingerprint ridges form in the fetus and remain unchanged throughout life.
human-body-0323: Which grow faster: fingernails or toenails?
Both grow at exactly the same speed
Fingernails grow about two to three times faster than toenails.
human-body-0326: What is the approximate normal human body temperature?
Normal human body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius, with slight variation during the day.
human-body-0328: Approximately what percentage of an adult human body is water?
Water makes up about 60% of an adult man's body weight. The proportion decreases slightly with age.
human-body-0329: What is the most abundant chemical element in the human body by mass?
Oxygen accounts for about 65% of body mass, mostly in water.
human-body-0330: What is the most abundant metal in the human body?
Calcium is the most abundant metal in the human body, mostly in bones and teeth.
human-body-0331: How many chromosomes are in most human body cells?
Most human cells contain 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.
human-body-0334: What involuntary action involves opening the mouth and taking a deep breath when sleepy or bored?
Yawning is a reflex involving opening the mouth and taking a deep breath. It is common during sleepiness and boredom.
human-body-0335: What reflex forcefully expels air through the nose and mouth to remove irritants from the nasal passages?
Sneezing is a reflex that expels irritants from the nose with a strong burst of air.
human-body-0336: What is the function of the tiny cilia lining the trachea?
Moving mucus and dust toward the throat for removal
The cilia move rhythmically, pushing mucus laden with dust and germs upward.
human-body-0337: What waxy fatty substance is produced by the liver and used to build cell membranes and some hormones?
Cholesterol is an essential component of cell membranes and is used to make steroid hormones and vitamin D.
human-body-0338: In which part of the digestive system are vitamin B12 and bile salts mainly absorbed?
The ileum is the final part of the small intestine and specializes in absorbing vitamin B12 and bile salts.
human-body-0339: What middle part of the small intestine lies between the duodenum and ileum?
The jejunum is the middle part of the small intestine and absorbs much of the nutrients.
human-body-0340: What is the common name for hard crystals formed from urinary salts in the urinary tract?
Kidney stones are hard crystals formed from urinary salts and cause severe pain when passing.
human-body-0342: What disease involves uric acid accumulating in joints, often causing severe pain in the big toe?
Gout is joint inflammation caused by deposits of uric acid crystals, most famously in the big toe.
muslim-scientists-0001: Badi al-Zaman al-Jazari served as chief engineer at the palace of which ruling dynasty in Diyarbakir?
Al-Jazari served as chief engineer at the Artuqid court in Diyarbakir (Amid).
muslim-scientists-0002: How many mechanical devices did al-Jazari describe, with construction instructions, in his book Al-Jami bayn al-Ilm wa-al-Amal al-Nafi fi Sinaat al-Hiyal?
In his book of 1206 CE, al-Jazari described fifty mechanical devices with instructions for building them.
muslim-scientists-0004: What mechanical component did al-Jazari use in his twin-cylinder pump to convert rotary motion into linear reciprocating motion?
Al-Jazari described a crankshaft and connecting rod in his pump, converting continuous rotation into reciprocating motion.
muslim-scientists-0006: In one of his candle clocks, al-Jazari first used what fastening joint that is still used today?
Historian Donald Hill stated that al-Jazari's candle clock used the bayonet fitting for the first time.
muslim-scientists-0007: A water supply system powered by gears and water, developed by al-Jazari, was built in the thirteenth century to supply mosques and bimaristans (hospitals) in which city?
Al-Jazari described a water-raising machine driven by gears and water power. A similar machine was installed on the Yazid River in Damascus.
muslim-scientists-0010: How many volumes make up al-Zahrawi's Al-Tasrif li-man Ajiza an al-Talif?
Al-Tasrif is a medical encyclopedia in thirty volumes, the last devoted to surgery.
muslim-scientists-0011: Why did al-Zahrawi place surgery in the final volume of Al-Tasrif?
Because he wrote it late in life after retiring from medical practice in Cordoba
Because it is the highest level of medicine and should not be practiced before mastering its other branches
Because the caliph requested a separate book dedicated to him
Because it was the least important medical branch to physicians of his time
Al-Zahrawi stated that surgery is the highest form of medicine and should not be practiced before knowing its other branches.
muslim-scientists-0012: Approximately how many surgical instruments did al-Zahrawi present in his book with illustrations?
Al-Zahrawi presented over two hundred surgical instruments, including scalpels, forceps, specula, and cautery tools.
muslim-scientists-0013: What pioneering material did al-Zahrawi use for internal sutures that is still used in surgery?
Al-Zahrawi pioneered the use of catgut for internal sutures because it dissolves and is accepted by the body.
muslim-scientists-0015: Who translated al-Zahrawi's book on surgery into Latin in the twelfth century CE?
Gerard of Cremona translated it into Latin, making it a surgical reference in European universities for centuries.
muslim-scientists-0016: At the court of which Umayyad ruler in al-Andalus is al-Zahrawi commonly said to have worked as a physician?
Al-Zahrawi worked as a physician at the court of Caliph al-Hakam II (al-Mustansir Billah).
muslim-scientists-0017: Al-Zahrawi invented an instrument to break up stones without a surgical incision. Where were those stones located?
He used the al-mishaab instrument to break up a stone lodged in the urethra, the urinary passage, rather than inside the bladder.
muslim-scientists-0018: What did al-Zahrawi use to bind and stabilize loose teeth?
A paste of wax and gum
Al-Zahrawi used gold and silver wires to bind loose teeth and was a pioneer of dentistry.
muslim-scientists-0020: Ibn al-Haytham is known for attempting what engineering project in Egypt?
Building the great wall of Cairo
Regulating the flooding of the Nile
Building a new lighthouse for Alexandria
Digging a canal connecting the Nile to the Red Sea
Ibn al-Haytham was known for his knowledge of applied mathematics, including his attempt to regulate Nile flooding.
muslim-scientists-0021: What title did Abu al-Hasan al-Bayhaqi give Ibn al-Haytham?
Al-Bayhaqi called him the second Ptolemy because of his standing in mathematics and astronomy.
muslim-scientists-0022: Ibn al-Haytham primarily used the camera obscura to observe which phenomenon?
He observed the crescent image of the Sun during a partial eclipse as its light passed through a small round aperture.
muslim-scientists-0023: Which law of light did Ibn al-Haytham formulate fully in Kitab al-Manazir?
He was the first to formulate the complete law of reflection, stating that the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in one plane.
muslim-scientists-0024: The famous Alhazen's problem concerns finding a point on what surface?
A convex lens where light converges
A glass prism where light separates into its colors
A water surface where light refracts
A spherical mirror that reflects light to the eye
The problem asks: given a light source and a spherical mirror, where is the point from which light reflects into the observer's eye?
muslim-scientists-0025: How many treatises (parts) make up Ibn al-Haytham's Kitab al-Manazir?
Kitab al-Manazir consists of seven treatises, written between 1011 and 1021 CE.
muslim-scientists-0026: What did Ibn al-Haytham demonstrate experimentally about the path of light?
That it travels from the eye to visible objects
That it bends around opaque objects
That it travels at infinite speed
That it travels in straight lines
Ibn al-Haytham experimentally proved that light travels in straight lines and conducted experiments on lenses and mirrors.
muslim-scientists-0027: Ibn al-Haytham used the sum of fourth powers of numbers to calculate the volume of which solid?
Ibn al-Haytham derived a formula for the sum of fourth powers and used it to calculate the volume of a paraboloid.
muslim-scientists-0028: How did al-Biruni measure the Earth's radius?
By observing a lunar eclipse from two distant cities
By measuring a mountain's height and the dip of the horizon from its summit
By measuring the shadows of two poles in distant cities
By measuring the length of a degree of meridian in the Sinjar desert
Al-Biruni measured a mountain's height and then the angle of the horizon's dip from its summit, calculating the radius using trigonometry.
muslim-scientists-0029: Where did al-Biruni make his famous measurement of the Earth's radius?
Ghazni in what is now eastern Afghanistan
Nandana in what is now Pakistan
Al-Biruni performed his experiment at Nandana Fort in Pind Dadan Khan, in present-day Pakistan.
muslim-scientists-0030: What instrument did al-Biruni use to determine the density of metals and gemstones accurately?
Al-Biruni used a hydrostatic balance to measure the density of many materials accurately.
muslim-scientists-0031: Al-Biruni classified gemstones by physical properties such as specific gravity and hardness rather than the common classification of his time by what?
Al-Biruni departed from his era's practice of classifying gemstones by color and classified them by specific gravity and hardness.
muslim-scientists-0032: What do some historians believe al-Biruni considered likely in Al-Qanun al-Masudi based on his calculations of the Earth's size?
That the Moon is larger than Earth
That seas cover the entire Southern Hemisphere south of the equator
That Earth is half as large as Ptolemy's estimate
The existence of land in the ocean between Asia and Europe
He believed the known world occupied no more than two-fifths of the Earth's circumference and inferred that land likely existed in the ocean between Asia and Europe.
muslim-scientists-0033: What is the subject of al-Biruni's Al-Saydana fi al-Tibb?
Drug names and their synonyms in several languages
Methods of preparing compound medicines by distillation
Al-Saydana is a book on drugs giving synonyms for their names in Syriac, Persian, Greek, Indian languages, and others.
muslim-scientists-0034: Of al-Biruni's 146 books, how many did he devote to astronomy, mathematics, and related fields?
Al-Biruni wrote 146 books, including 95 on astronomy, mathematics, and mathematical geography.
muslim-scientists-0035: What is the main subject of al-Biruni's Al-Athar al-Baqiya an al-Qurun al-Khaliya?
Al-Athar al-Baqiya was his first major work and concerns calendars and chronological calculations among different nations.
muslim-scientists-0036: In Al-Qanun al-Masudi, al-Biruni disagreed with Ptolemy about what matter concerning the Sun?
That the Sun revolves around Earth
That the solar year is exactly 360 days
That the Sun is smaller than the Moon
That the Sun's apogee moves rather than remaining fixed
Unlike Ptolemy, al-Biruni observed that the Sun's apogee, the farthest point in its apparent orbit, moves rather than remaining fixed.
muslim-scientists-0038: What common computer science term derives from the name Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi?
His name was Latinized as Algoritmi, from which the word algorithm derives.
muslim-scientists-0039: Who translated al-Khwarizmi's book on algebra into Latin in 1145 CE?
Robert of Chester translated it in Segovia in 1145 CE, helping spread the word algebra.
muslim-scientists-0040: Al-Khwarizmi's Kitab Surat al-Ard revised and corrected a geography book written by whom?
In Kitab Surat al-Ard, al-Khwarizmi listed city coordinates based on Ptolemy's geography, improving their values.
muslim-scientists-0041: What numeral system did al-Khwarizmi's book on Indian arithmetic transmit to Europe?
The Latin translation of his book on Indian arithmetic introduced the West to the decimal place-value system.
muslim-scientists-0042: What was the original meaning of al-jabr for al-Khwarizmi?
For him, al-jabr meant completing an equation by adding the same quantity to both sides to eliminate subtraction. The word algebra derives from its name.
muslim-scientists-0043: To how many standard forms did al-Khwarizmi reduce linear and quadratic equations to solve them?
His method began by reducing an equation to one of six standard forms and then solving it.
muslim-scientists-0044: Among the practical applications in al-Khwarizmi's algebra book were problems in trade, surveying, and what?
Al-Khwarizmi included practical problems in trade, surveying, and dividing inheritances.
muslim-scientists-0047: Ibn Firnas invented a method for cutting what material that al-Andalus had previously sent to Egypt for cutting?
His method of cutting rock crystal (quartz) eliminated al-Andalus's need to send it to Egypt.
muslim-scientists-0049: Which astronomical tables did Abbas ibn Firnas introduce to al-Andalus?
Ibn Firnas introduced the Sindhind astronomical tables to al-Andalus.
muslim-scientists-0050: Approximately how many devices did the Banu Musa brothers describe in Kitab al-Hiyal?
In Kitab al-Hiyal (about 850 CE), the Banu Musa described around a hundred devices and how to use them.
muslim-scientists-0051: The three brothers known as the Banu Musa were Muhammad, Ahmad, and whom?
The three sons of Musa ibn Shakir were Muhammad, Ahmad, and al-Hasan.
muslim-scientists-0052: What did the Banu Musa measure to obtain a relatively accurate value for the Earth's circumference?
A mountain's height and the dip of the horizon from its summit
The length of one degree of latitude
The time between two lunar eclipses
A pole's shadow on the solstice
The Banu Musa surveyed the length of one degree of latitude and used it to derive the Earth's circumference.
muslim-scientists-0053: What distinguished the Banu Musa's devices from those of their Greek predecessors, such as Hero and Philo?
Their focus on automatic control, such as self-operating valves
Their reliance solely on wind power rather than water or weights
Their large size and numerous operators
Their construction from wood rather than metals
They were distinguished by their focus on automatic control: self-operating valves, timers, and delay systems.
muslim-scientists-0054: According to a story about Abu Bakr al-Razi choosing the site for a bimaristan (hospital) in Baghdad, what did he do?
He hung pieces of meat around the city and chose the place where they spoiled most slowly
He chose the city's highest spot because it was less humid
He chose the closest site to the Tigris River for its abundant water
He measured air temperature in each neighborhood and chose the coldest
Al-Razi hung pieces of fresh meat in different places and chose the hospital site where the meat took longest to spoil.
muslim-scientists-0055: Al-Razi wrote a book for poor people and travelers to treat common illnesses when no doctor was available. What was its title?
Man la Yahduruhu al-Tabib is a home treatment guide that al-Razi addressed to poor people, travelers, and the general public.
muslim-scientists-0056: To whom did al-Razi dedicate Al-Mansuri fi al-Tibb?
Mansur ibn Ishaq, governor of Rayy
Al-Razi dedicated Al-Tibb al-Ruhani and Al-Mansuri to Mansur ibn Ishaq, governor of Rayy.
muslim-scientists-0058: In treating meningitis, al-Razi compared the outcomes of patients given a particular treatment with those not given it. What was the treatment?
Al-Razi compared the outcomes of meningitis patients treated with bloodletting with those not bled, an early comparison between two groups.
muslim-scientists-0059: How did al-Razi handle questions in his teaching sessions?
He answered all of them himself before the lesson began
He wrote them down and answered in separate letters
They passed through successive circles of students, and he answered if they could not
He postponed them to a special session at the end of the week
A question was put to the first circle of students, then the second, and so on. If none could answer, al-Razi did.
muslim-scientists-0061: Ibn al-Nafis planned his encyclopedia Al-Shamil fi al-Tibb in three hundred volumes. How many did he complete before his death?
Ibn al-Nafis completed only eighty volumes of Al-Shamil, yet it is among the largest medical encyclopedias written by one person.
muslim-scientists-0062: Approximately how old was Ibn al-Nafis when he wrote Sharh Tashrih al-Qanun?
Ibn al-Nafis published Sharh Tashrih al-Qanun at the age of twenty-nine.
muslim-scientists-0063: At which bimaristan (hospital) did Ibn al-Nafis study medicine for more than ten years?
Ibn al-Nafis began studying medicine at sixteen at Al-Nuri Bimaristan, founded by Nur al-Din Zangi in Damascus.
muslim-scientists-0064: Ibn al-Nafis was appointed chief physician at Al-Nasiri Bimaristan (hospital) in Cairo. Who founded it?
Salah al-Din founded Al-Nasiri Bimaristan. Ibn al-Nafis headed its physicians and taught there for years.
muslim-scientists-0065: Which of these sultans had Ibn al-Nafis as his personal physician?
Ibn al-Nafis became Sultan al-Zahir Baybars's personal physician. The other three ruled before his lifetime or after his death.
muslim-scientists-0066: Before his death, to which institution did Ibn al-Nafis endow his house and library?
Ibn al-Nafis donated his house and library to Qalawun Bimaristan (Al-Mansuri) in Cairo.
muslim-scientists-0068: What is the subject of the fifth and final book of Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb?
The fifth book of Al-Qanun is devoted to compound medicines (al-aqrabadhin).
muslim-scientists-0069: Where was Al-Qanun fi al-Tibb translated from Arabic into Latin in the twelfth century?
Al-Qanun was translated into Latin in Toledo in the twelfth century and influenced European medicine for centuries.
muslim-scientists-0072: How many sectional maps did al-Idrisi's atlas Nuzhat al-Mushtaq fi Ikhtiraq al-Afaq contain?
The atlas contained seventy maps: seven regions, each divided into ten sections.
muslim-scientists-0073: On what was the world map al-Idrisi made for King Roger engraved?
A marble wall in the king's palace
A large sheet of red copper
A huge disc of pure silver
Parchment made from tanned gazelle hide
The map was engraved on a pure silver disc two meters in diameter.
muslim-scientists-0074: How were the maps in al-Idrisi's atlas oriented?
North at the top and south at the bottom
South at the top and north at the bottom
East at the top and west at the bottom
West at the top and east at the bottom
Al-Idrisi's maps were oriented with south at the top and north at the bottom.
muslim-scientists-0075: Into how many climatic regions did al-Idrisi divide the known world in his book?
Following Ptolemy's method, al-Idrisi divided the world into seven regions, each with ten sections.
muslim-scientists-0076: Approximately what value did al-Idrisi's atlas give for the Earth's circumference?
It estimated the circumference at about 37,000 kilometers, with an error of less than ten percent.
muslim-scientists-0078: In which city did al-Battani establish his own observatory?
Al-Battani lived most of his life in Raqqa on the Euphrates, where he established his observatory.
muslim-scientists-0079: How long did al-Battani estimate the solar year to be?
Al-Battani's value for the solar year differs from the accepted value by only 2 minutes and 22 seconds.
muslim-scientists-0080: What value did al-Battani obtain for the obliquity of the ecliptic (Earth's axial tilt)?
Al-Battani improved on Ptolemy's measurement, finding an obliquity of 23 degrees 35 minutes. The accepted value is about 23.44 degrees.
muslim-scientists-0081: What value did al-Battani obtain for the precession of the equinoxes?
From precise measurements of the equinoxes, al-Battani found a precession of 54.5 seconds per year, or one degree every 66 years.
muslim-scientists-0082: Al-Battani noticed that the Sun's distance from Earth varies during the year. This helped him understand which phenomenon?
Recognizing the changing distance between Earth and the Sun led al-Battani to understand the cause of annular eclipses.
muslim-scientists-0083: Al-Battani used trigonometry to formulate an equation for determining what?
Al-Battani used trigonometry to develop an equation for determining the qibla (direction of prayer). It remained in use until al-Biruni introduced more accurate methods.
muslim-scientists-0084: Al-Zij al-Sabi is among the most famous astronomical tables of the Abbasid era. Who compiled it?
Al-Zij al-Sabi is by al-Battani (around 900 CE). It was translated into Latin and printed in Nuremberg in 1537 CE.
muslim-scientists-0086: What method did al-Kindi present for deciphering encrypted messages when their language is known?
Replacing every letter with the following one
Counting each letter's frequency and comparing it with another text
Removing repeated letters and keeping the rest
Al-Kindi proposed frequency analysis: counting each letter's occurrences in a text of the same language and comparing them with the message.
muslim-scientists-0089: Which of these titles was the navigator Ahmad ibn Majid known by?
Ibn Majid was known as the Lion of the Sea and the Prince of the Arab Sea.
muslim-scientists-0090: What is Ahmad ibn Majid's most famous book on navigation?
Al-Fawaid fi Usul Ilm al-Bahr wa-al-Qawaid
Al-Fawaid fi Usul Ilm al-Bahr wa-al-Qawaid is among his most important books and was a reference for Arab sailors.
muslim-scientists-0091: Ibn Majid based his navigational calculations on lunar mansions and stellar akhnan (directions). How many were there?
He used lunar mansions and thirty-two stellar khann (directions) to determine ships' courses.
muslim-scientists-0092: What has modern research concluded about the story that Ibn Majid guided Vasco da Gama to India?
He drew a route map for him but did not accompany him
It is very unlikely that he ever met him
He accompanied him to India's coast and then returned
He guided him only to the Cape of Good Hope
The guide who directed Vasco da Gama was found to have been a man from Gujarat, making the story highly unlikely.
muslim-scientists-0093: Approximately how many works in verse and prose did Ahmad ibn Majid write?
Ibn Majid wrote about forty works in verse and prose, mostly on nautical sciences.
muslim-scientists-0094: Which European explorer used al-Farghani's calculations of the Earth's size but mistakenly treated the Arabic mile as a Roman mile?
Columbus relied on al-Farghani's calculations but interpreted the Arabic mile as the shorter Roman mile.
muslim-scientists-0095: What structure did astronomer Ahmad ibn Kathir al-Farghani supervise building on Rawda Island in Cairo?
Al-Farghani supervised construction of the new Nilometer on Rawda Island by order of al-Mutawakkil. It was completed in 861 CE.
muslim-scientists-0096: Al-Farghani's most famous astronomy book was an expanded summary of which Greek work?
His Jawami Ilm al-Nujum was an expanded summary of Al-Majisti with corrected and more precise data.
muslim-scientists-0097: What did al-Farghani help calculate with a team of scholars under Caliph al-Mamun's patronage?
The distance between Earth and the Moon
The depth of the Arabian Gulf
The height of the Lighthouse of Alexandria
The Earth's diameter by measuring the length of a meridian arc
Al-Farghani helped calculate the Earth's diameter by measuring the length of a meridian arc under al-Mamun's patronage.
muslim-scientists-0099: For which emir did Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi write his book on fixed stars?
Al-Sufi wrote his book in Shiraz for the Buyid emir Adud al-Dawla.
muslim-scientists-0100: What did Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi describe as a small cloudy patch in its earliest recorded observation?
In 964 CE, al-Sufi recorded the earliest known observation of the Andromeda Galaxy, describing it as a small cloud.
muslim-scientists-0101: What was al-Sufi among the first to attempt in the study of fixed stars?
Measuring the distance from Earth to each star
Dividing the sky into a hundred constellations
Matching Greek star names with their Arabic names
Al-Sufi was among the first to connect Greek star names with traditional Arabic names and constellations.
muslim-scientists-0102: Ibrahim ibn Yahya al-Zarqali (Arzachel in Europe) was nicknamed al-Naqqash. What does this nickname mean?
Al-Zarqali trained as a metalsmith and engraver and was nicknamed al-Naqqash. Arzachel is a modified form of al-Zarqali.
muslim-scientists-0103: What was al-Zarqali's al-Safiha al-Zarqaliyya, known in Europe as the Saphaea?
A table of salah (prayer) times in Toledo
An improved astrolabe usable at all latitudes
Al-Safiha al-Zarqaliyya was a sophisticated astrolabe he invented, used by navigators until the sixteenth century.
muslim-scientists-0104: Al-Zarqali corrected Ptolemy's estimate of the Mediterranean Sea's width (its end-to-end extent). To how many degrees did he correct it?
Al-Zarqali reduced Ptolemy's exaggerated estimate of 62 degrees to the correct value of 42 degrees.
muslim-scientists-0105: How much annual movement of the Sun's apogee relative to the fixed stars did al-Zarqali estimate?
He measured it at about 12.04 arcseconds per year, very close to the modern value of 11.77.
muslim-scientists-0106: Which astronomical tables, famous in medieval Europe, were based partly on al-Zarqali's work?
The Toledan Tables were completed around 1080 CE in Toledo and were based partly on al-Zarqali's work.
muslim-scientists-0107: When designing an instrument for Ptolemy's model of Mercury, how did al-Zarqali describe the path of the epicycle's center?
An oval shape resembling a pine nut
Al-Zarqali noticed that the path of Mercury's epicycle center was not circular but oval, resembling a pine nut.
muslim-scientists-0108: Where did the Fatimids establish an observatory for astronomer Ibn Yunus al-Misri?
On Rawda Island in the Nile
The Fatimids established an observatory for Ibn Yunus on Mount Muqattam near Fustat.
muslim-scientists-0109: After whom was Ibn Yunus's great astronomical table named al-Hakimi?
Ibn Yunus dedicated Al-Zij al-Kabir al-Hakimi to the Fatimid caliph al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah.
muslim-scientists-0110: How many lunar eclipses did Ibn Yunus describe in his observations, alongside forty planetary conjunctions?
Ibn Yunus described forty planetary conjunctions and thirty lunar eclipses. His observations were used centuries later.
muslim-scientists-0111: What is the truth about the common claim that Ibn Yunus used a pendulum to measure time?
Ibn Khallikan mentioned it in his biography in Wafayat al-Ayan
It is an error traced to an English scholar in 1684 CE
It is established in his Al-Zij al-Hakimi
Attributing the pendulum to him is unfounded and stems from an error by Edward Bernard, professor of astronomy at Oxford, in 1684 CE.
muslim-scientists-0112: One of Ibn Yunus's methods for finding time from the Sun's altitude is equivalent to a trigonometric identity that later paved the way for what?
His method is equivalent to the product-of-cosines formula (one of Werner's formulas), which was fundamental to the development of prosthaphaeresis and then logarithms.
muslim-scientists-0113: What position did Ibn al-Shatir hold at the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus?
Ibn al-Shatir was a muwaqqit (timekeeper) at the Umayyad Mosque, determining salah (prayer) times and the beginnings of months.
muslim-scientists-0114: On which minaret of the Umayyad Mosque did Ibn al-Shatir install his marble sundial?
Ibn al-Shatir installed his marble sundial on the al-Arus Minaret. The original was later moved to the Damascus Museum.
muslim-scientists-0116: Ibn al-Shatir invented an instrument called Sunduq al-Yawaqit li-Marifat al-Mawaqit. What does it combine?
A universal sundial and a magnetic compass
A balance and a gold measure
A small water clock and a spherical astrolabe
A telescope and a star map
Sunduq al-Yawaqit combines a universal sundial and a magnetic compass to determine salah (prayer) times and is kept in the Aleppo Museum.
muslim-scientists-0117: What is the title of Ibn al-Shatir's most important treatise on reforming astronomical models?
Nihayat al-Sul fi Tashih al-Usul is his most important book. In it, he corrected Ptolemy's models for the Sun, Moon, and planets.
muslim-scientists-0119: In 1551 CE, Taqi al-Din al-Rasid described a steam engine. What practical use did he give for it?
Taqi al-Din described a steam turbine whose practical use was turning a roasting spit.
muslim-scientists-0120: Under which Ottoman sultan was Taqi al-Din's Istanbul observatory established in 1577 CE?
Sultan Murad III funded the observatory at Taqi al-Din's request. It was completed in 1577 CE.
muslim-scientists-0122: Taqi al-Din estimated the annual movement of the Sun's apogee at 63 seconds, compared with today's known value of 61 seconds. What was Copernicus's value?
Copernicus's value was 24 seconds and Tycho Brahe's was 45 seconds, making Taqi al-Din more accurate than both.
muslim-scientists-0123: On which numerical system did Taqi al-Din base his trigonometric tables?
Taqi al-Din prepared trigonometric tables based on decimal fractions.
muslim-scientists-0124: How many people worked at Taqi al-Din's observatory in Istanbul?
The observatory had sixteen workers: eight observers, four scribes, and four assistants.
muslim-scientists-0125: To how many decimal places did Ghiyath al-Din al-Kashi calculate 2 pi in 1424 CE?
Al-Kashi calculated it to 16 decimal places. No one surpassed him until Ludolph van Ceulen 180 years later.
muslim-scientists-0126: Which trigonometric law is called al-Kashi's theorem in France?
In Miftah al-Hisab, al-Kashi explained solving a triangle given two sides and the included angle. Thus the law of cosines bears his name in France.
muslim-scientists-0127: What is the title of al-Kashi's arithmetic book completed in 1427 CE?
Miftah al-Hisab is among al-Kashi's most famous books and covers solving triangles and decimal fractions.
muslim-scientists-0128: Al-Kashi invented an analog calculating instrument called Tabaq al-Manatiq and another for finding the time of planetary conjunctions. What was the second called?
Al-Kashi invented Lawh al-Ittisalat to determine the time of planetary conjunctions and perform linear interpolation.
muslim-scientists-0129: What is the subject of al-Kashi's treatise Sullam al-Sama (1407 CE)?
The sizes and distances of celestial bodies
In Sullam al-Sama, al-Kashi addressed his predecessors' difficulties in determining the sizes and distances of Earth, the Moon, the Sun, and the stars.
muslim-scientists-0131: The astronomer-sultan Ulugh Beg was whose grandson?
Ulugh Beg was the son of Shah Rukh, son of Tamerlane, and was appointed ruler of Samarkand while young.
muslim-scientists-0133: In which Samarkand square did Ulugh Beg build his famous madrasa (school) between 1417 and 1420 CE?
Ulugh Beg built his madrasa (school) in Registan Square, and its building still stands.
muslim-scientists-0134: How many stars did Ulugh Beg remeasure through observation in Al-Zij al-Sultani?
He redetermined the positions of 992 stars and added 27 stars from al-Sufi's book that could not be seen from Samarkand.
muslim-scientists-0135: In what year were the remains of Ulugh Beg's observatory in Samarkand rediscovered?
The observatory fell into ruin some time after Ulugh Beg's death, and its remains were rediscovered in 1908 CE.
muslim-scientists-0136: How long did Ulugh Beg estimate the sidereal year to be in 1437 CE?
He estimated it at 365 days, 6 hours, 10 minutes, and 8 seconds, an error of only +58 seconds, using a sundial 50 meters high.
muslim-scientists-0137: How did Omar Khayyam provide a general solution to cubic equations?
Khayyam was the first to provide a general solution to cubic equations through the intersection of two conic sections.
muslim-scientists-0139: In which city was the observatory established where Omar Khayyam headed a calendar-reform team for Sultan Malikshah?
Khayyam was tasked with establishing an observatory in Isfahan in 1074 CE to reform the calendar.
muslim-scientists-0140: What geometric shape is sometimes associated with Omar Khayyam alongside the Italian Saccheri?
The Saccheri quadrilateral is sometimes called the Khayyam-Saccheri quadrilateral because Khayyam described it in his commentary on Euclid's postulates.
muslim-scientists-0141: What is the Tusi couple in astronomy?
Two planets orbiting one center in opposite directions at the same speed
Two parabolas meeting at one focus
Two facing mirrors that magnify star images
A small circle rotating inside a circle twice its size to generate straight-line motion
The Tusi couple is a small circle rolling inside a circle of twice its diameter, causing a point on it to move back and forth in a straight line.
muslim-scientists-0142: The Maragha Observatory, directed by Nasir al-Din al-Tusi, is in which region of present-day Iran?
The Maragha Observatory is in East Azerbaijan in present-day Iran and was directed by al-Tusi.
muslim-scientists-0143: Which observatory served as a model for Ulugh Beg's observatory in Samarkand and Taqi al-Din's in Istanbul?
Maragha Observatory was a model for later observatories in Samarkand, Istanbul, and Jaipur.
muslim-scientists-0145: Which mathematical discipline is al-Tusi credited with making an independent science rather than merely a tool for astronomy?
Al-Tusi's writings on trigonometry established it as a science independent of astronomy.
muslim-scientists-0146: What is the title of al-Khazini's encyclopedia on balances and density, written in 1121 CE?
Mizan al-Hikma is al-Khazini's encyclopedia on hydrostatic balances, density, and the specific gravity of metals and gemstones.
muslim-scientists-0147: According to modern studies, what accuracy did al-Khazini's comprehensive balance achieve?
Modern studies have confirmed his balance's accuracy of one part in sixty thousand.
muslim-scientists-0148: For which Seljuk sultan did al-Khazini write his astronomical tables in 1115 CE?
Al-Khazini wrote Al-Zij al-Sanjari under Sultan Sanjar's patronage.
muslim-scientists-0150: What enormous instrument did Abu Mahmud al-Khujandi build near Rayy in 994 CE?
Al-Khujandi built the first enormous mural sextant to measure Earth's axial tilt with high precision.
muslim-scientists-0151: What did al-Khujandi conclude by comparing his measurement of Earth's axial tilt with earlier measurements?
That the tilt is increasing rapidly
That the tilt was decreasing in his era
That Earth's axis has no tilt
He found his value of 23 degrees 32 minutes 19 seconds smaller than earlier values and concluded that the tilt was decreasing rather than constant.
muslim-scientists-0152: In which present-day country is Khujand, the city after which astronomer Abu Mahmud al-Khujandi is named?
Al-Khujandi was born in Khujand, now in Tajikistan.
muslim-scientists-0153: On what animal did Abu Marwan ibn Zuhr test tracheotomy before recommending it for humans?
Ibn Zuhr opened a goat's trachea and treated it until it recovered, demonstrating the procedure's safety before applying it to humans.
muslim-scientists-0155: Ibn Zuhr wrote Al-Taysir at a friend's request to complement that friend's Al-Kulliyyat. Who was he?
Ibn Zuhr wrote Al-Taysir at Ibn Rushd's request to complement Al-Kulliyyat fi al-Tibb. Both books were printed together in Latin.
muslim-scientists-0156: How many successive generations of physicians came from the Banu Zuhr family to which Abu Marwan ibn Zuhr belonged?
The Banu Zuhr family produced six successive generations of physicians in al-Andalus from the early tenth century.
muslim-scientists-0157: What is the subject of Ibn Zuhr's Al-Aghdhiya?
Foods and diet through the seasons
Al-Aghdhiya is a guide to foods and health regimens that classifies foods and recommends what suits each season.
muslim-scientists-0158: Approximately how many plant, food, and medicinal substances did Ibn al-Baytar's Al-Jami li-Mufradat al-Adwiya wa-al-Aghdhiya include?
Al-Jami lists about 1,400 plants, foods, and medicines in alphabetical order.
muslim-scientists-0159: What does the name Ibn al-Baytar, by which the Andalusian herbalist Diya al-Din al-Malaqi was known, mean?
His father was a baytar, meaning a veterinarian, so he became known as Ibn al-Baytar.
muslim-scientists-0161: What position did Ibn al-Baytar hold in the service of the Ayyubid sultan al-Malik al-Kamil?
Ibn al-Baytar entered al-Malik al-Kamil's service after 1224 CE and was appointed chief herbalist.
muslim-scientists-0162: What substance did Ibn al-Baytar call Chinese snow when discussing gunpowder?
Ibn al-Baytar called saltpeter (potassium nitrate) Chinese snow.
muslim-scientists-0163: Ammar al-Mawsili invented a hollow needle to draw opacity out of the eye. What condition did he treat with it?
Ammar al-Mawsili invented a hollow needle for extracting cataracts, a major cause of blindness.
muslim-scientists-0164: What is the title of the only book written by ophthalmologist Ammar al-Mawsili?
His only book, Al-Muntakhab fi Ilaj al-Ayn, was written for the Fatimid al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah.
muslim-scientists-0165: Who wrote Tadhkirat al-Kahhalin, the most comprehensive surviving medieval Arabic book on ophthalmology?
Tadhkirat al-Kahhalin is by Ali ibn Isa al-Kahhal and was the authoritative ophthalmology reference of his time.
muslim-scientists-0166: Which Arab ophthalmologist was known in medieval Europe as Jesu Oculist?
Jesu Oculist is a Latin rendering of the name Ali ibn Isa al-Kahhal.
muslim-scientists-0168: Who translated Ibn al-Jazzar's Zad al-Musafir wa-Qut al-Hadir into Latin?
Constantine the African translated Ibn al-Jazzar's books, including Zad al-Musafir, known as the Viaticum.
muslim-scientists-0169: Ibn al-Jazzar devoted one of his books to the health of which group?
Ibn al-Jazzar's works include Tibb al-Mashayikh wa-Hifz Sihhatihim, concerning older people's health.
muslim-scientists-0170: By what name was Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Majusi's Kamil al-Sinaa al-Tibbiyya famous?
Al-Majusi dedicated his book to Adud al-Dawla, and it became known as Al-Kitab al-Malaki (Liber Regalis).
muslim-scientists-0171: How did al-Majusi divide the twenty treatises of Kamil al-Sinaa al-Tibbiyya?
Ten on theory and ten on practice
Five on anatomy and fifteen on medicines
Ten on diseases and ten on surgery
All on simple and compound medicines
The book has twenty treatises: the first ten on theoretical medicine and the other ten on practical medicine.
muslim-scientists-0172: At which Baghdad hospital did Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Majusi work?
Al-Majusi worked at Al-Adudi Bimaristan (hospital), founded by Adud al-Dawla in Baghdad in 981 CE.
muslim-scientists-0173: What medical encyclopedia did Ali ibn Sahl Rabban al-Tabari write, one of the earliest Islamic medical encyclopedias?
Firdaws al-Hikma, written by Ali ibn Rabban al-Tabari, is among the earliest medical encyclopedias in Islam.
muslim-scientists-0174: Which physician do biographical works identify as a student of Ali ibn Sahl Rabban al-Tabari?
Abu Bakr al-Razi was Ali ibn Rabban al-Tabari's most famous student.
muslim-scientists-0176: What is the Arabic original of the medical book known in Europe as Colliget, which remained a textbook for centuries?
Colliget is a Latin modification of the title Al-Kulliyyat fi al-Tibb by Ibn Rushd.
muslim-scientists-0177: Which part of the eye did Ibn Rushd identify as the main organ for sensing light, contrary to the prevailing view of his time?
Ibn Rushd held that the retina, rather than the lens, was responsible for sensing light.
muslim-scientists-0178: In his medical writings, Ibn Rushd described symptoms of a condition now known as which neurological disease?
Ibn Rushd provided early descriptions of conditions resembling Parkinson's disease and a new theory of stroke.
muslim-scientists-0179: Egyptian physician and astronomer Ali ibn Ridwan is famous for a precise description of what celestial event in 1006 CE?
Ibn Ridwan provided the most precise description of SN 1006, the brightest stellar event in recorded history.
muslim-scientists-0181: What is another Arabic name for a bimaristan (hospital) in Islamic civilization?
A bimaristan, or maristan, is also called Dar al-Shifa in Arabic.
muslim-scientists-0182: Which Abbasid caliph ordered physicians to be examined in 931 CE and barred unlicensed practitioners from practicing medicine?
After a patient died due to a physician's error, al-Muqtadir ordered physicians to be examined. Their chief, Sinan ibn Thabit, examined them and licensed only those qualified.
muslim-scientists-0184: Approximately how many physicians worked at Al-Adudi Bimaristan (hospital) in Baghdad when it opened?
Al-Adudi Bimaristan began with twenty-five staff working in specialties from ophthalmology to surgery and was a teaching hospital.
muslim-scientists-0185: Abu Sad al-Ala ibn Sahl has been described as discovering which law of light centuries before Snell?
Ibn Sahl has been described as discovering the law of refraction known as Snell's law.
muslim-scientists-0186: What is the subject of Ibn Sahl's optical treatise written around 984 CE?
The anatomy of the eye's layers
His treatise Fi al-Alat al-Muhriqa discusses mirrors and lenses that concentrate light.
muslim-scientists-0188: What did Kamal al-Din al-Farisi use to represent a raindrop in his experiments?
A polished copper container filled with rainwater
A transparent glass sphere filled with water
He used a large glass sphere filled with water inside a dark room as a model of a raindrop.
muslim-scientists-0191: How many plants are described in the surviving parts of al-Dinawari's Kitab al-Nabat, covering the Arabic letters sin through ya?
The surviving parts of the book describe 637 plants from the Arabic letter sin through ya.
muslim-scientists-0192: What is the title of Kamal al-Din al-Damiri's encyclopedia of animals?
Hayat al-Hayawan al-Kubra is al-Damiri's encyclopedia arranged by animal names.
muslim-scientists-0193: Who wrote Ajaib al-Makhluqat wa-Gharaib al-Mawjudat?
Ajaib al-Makhluqat is Zakariyya al-Qazwini's most famous work on cosmography.
muslim-scientists-0194: What is the subject of al-Qazwini's Athar al-Bilad wa-Akhbar al-Ibad?
Biographies of scholars and physicians in the East
A geographical dictionary of lands and their peoples
Athar al-Bilad is a geographical dictionary collecting accounts of lands and their peoples.
muslim-scientists-0196: How many earlier authors did Ibn al-Awwam quote in Kitab al-Filaha?
Ibn al-Awwam quoted 112 earlier authors in his book.
muslim-scientists-0197: Who wrote Uyun al-Anba fi Tabaqat al-Atibba?
Uyun al-Anba is an encyclopedia of physicians' biographies written by Ibn Abi Usaybia of Damascus.
muslim-scientists-0198: How many biographies did the Andalusian Ibn Juljul's Tabaqat al-Atibba wa-al-Hukama contain?
Ibn Juljul's book contains 57 biographies of physicians and sages from Greece, the Islamic world, al-Andalus, and elsewhere.
muslim-scientists-0199: Ibn Juljul of Cordoba was the personal physician of which Umayyad caliph?
Ibn Juljul became Caliph Hisham II's personal physician and taught medicine.
muslim-scientists-0200: What is the title of geographer Ibn Hawqal's book written in 977 CE after his long travels?
Ibn Hawqal wrote Surat al-Ard in 977 CE, revising and expanding al-Istakhri's book.
muslim-scientists-0203: To which cartographic school did geographer al-Istakhri belong and help spread?
Al-Istakhri belonged to the Balkhi school, which focused on Islamic lands and their geographical description.
muslim-scientists-0207: Yaqut al-Hamawi gathered much of his book's material from libraries in two cities in Khorasan. In which one did he study for two years?
Yaqut benefited from the libraries of Merv, where he studied for two years, and those of Balkh.
muslim-scientists-0208: What is the title of Ibn Khordadbeh's book written around 870 CE?
Al-Masalik wa-al-Mamalik by Ibn Khordadbeh is among the earliest Arabic geography books.
muslim-scientists-0209: What official position did Ibn Khordadbeh hold that helped him describe routes and kingdoms?
Ibn Khordadbeh oversaw the caliphate's postal and intelligence service in the Jibal region, then in Samarra and Baghdad.
muslim-scientists-0210: Al-Bakri's Al-Masalik wa-al-Mamalik is considered one of the most important historical sources for which region?
West Africa and the Ghana Empire
Central Asia and the lands of the Turks and Khazars
Al-Bakri's book is a major source on West Africa, the Ghana Empire, and trans-Saharan trade.
muslim-scientists-0211: What is striking about the Andalusian geographer Abu Ubayd al-Bakri?
He drew his maps on silk
He traveled around the entire world on one ship with merchants
He wrote his book in Hebrew
He never traveled outside al-Andalus to the lands he described
Al-Bakri died in Cordoba without visiting the places he described. He based his book on sources and accounts from merchants and travelers.
muslim-scientists-0212: In which years did the Andalusian Ibn Jubayr make the journey to Mecca that he recorded in his book?
Ibn Jubayr traveled to Mecca between 1183 and 1185 CE and recorded his observations in Egypt, the Levant, and Sicily.
muslim-scientists-0214: Which island did Ibn Jubayr visit on his return journey, describing its mixed culture?
On his return, Ibn Jubayr passed through Sicily after its Norman conquest and described its diverse culture.
muslim-scientists-0215: To which king did Caliph al-Muqtadir send the embassy whose journey Ahmad ibn Fadlan recorded?
The king of the Volga Bulgars
Ibn Fadlan joined al-Muqtadir's embassy to the king of the Volga Bulgars and recorded its events in his Risala.
muslim-scientists-0216: What scholarly role did Ahmad ibn Fadlan hold at al-Muqtadir's court before his journey?
Ibn Fadlan was a faqih (Islamic jurist) at Caliph al-Muqtadir's court before departing with the embassy.
muslim-scientists-0217: What is the title of the nautical atlas written by the Ottoman admiral Piri Reis?
His nautical atlas is Kitab al-Bahriyya (Kitab-i Bahriye), alongside his famous world map of 1513 CE.
muslim-scientists-0218: When was Piri Reis's first world map rediscovered in Topkapi Palace?
His map was rediscovered in 1929 CE during restoration work at Topkapi Palace in Istanbul.
muslim-scientists-0220: By what title was the mathematician Abu Kamil Shuja ibn Aslam known?
Abu Kamil was known as the Egyptian calculator and was a leading algebraist after al-Khwarizmi.
muslim-scientists-0221: Abu Kamil is considered the first mathematician to systematically accept which type of numbers as solutions and coefficients of equations?
Abu Kamil was the first to systematically use and accept irrational numbers as solutions and coefficients.
muslim-scientists-0222: Which European mathematician adopted Abu Kamil's methods, thereby helping introduce algebra to Europe?
Fibonacci adopted many of Abu Kamil's methods, giving Abu Kamil an important role in transmitting algebra to Europe.
muslim-scientists-0223: Abu Bakr al-Karaji described an arrangement of numbers now named after a French scholar. What is it?
Al-Karaji presented an early formulation of binomial coefficients and an explicit description of what is known as Pascal's triangle.
muslim-scientists-0224: Which method of mathematical proof did al-Karaji introduce in a lost work quoted by al-Samaw'al?
Al-Karaji introduced the idea of proof by mathematical induction, which reached us through al-Samaw'al al-Maghribi.
muslim-scientists-0225: Besides mathematics, al-Karaji wrote one of the oldest surviving independent works in which field?
Mineralogy and refining metals by fire
Al-Karaji explained the principles of hydrology in Istinbat al-Miyah al-Khafiyya. His book has been described as the oldest surviving text in this field.
muslim-scientists-0227: What distinguishes Abu al-Hasan al-Uqlidisi's al-Fusul fi al-Hisab al-Hindi (952 CE)?
The first Arabic book solving all cubic equations
The first Arabic commentary on the Elements
The oldest surviving book using decimal fractions
Al-Uqlidisi's book is the oldest surviving book using decimal fractions with Indian numerals. It was written in Damascus in 952 CE.
muslim-scientists-0228: What method of calculation did al-Uqlidisi advocate instead of the method common in his time?
Calculating with letters instead of numerals
Calculating with finger joints instead of writing on paper
Calculating with pebbles instead of numerals
Calculating with pen and paper instead of a dust board
Al-Uqlidisi showed how to calculate with pen and paper instead of a dust board whose writing was erased.
muslim-scientists-0229: Why was Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Ibrahim called al-Uqlidisi?
He was the first to translate Euclid's book into Arabic
It was a title for sellers of copies of Euclid's book
He was born in a city called Euclid
He wrote a commentary on the entire Elements
The title al-Uqlidisi was commonly applied to people who sold manuscript copies of Euclid's Elements.
muslim-scientists-0231: Which of these arithmetic books was written by al-Qalasadi?
Al-Tabsira fi Ilm al-Hisab is by al-Qalasadi; the other works are by Ibn al-Banna, al-Kashi, and al-Karaji.
muslim-scientists-0232: Talkhis A'mal al-Hisab is a famous book by which Moroccan scholar?
Talkhis A'mal al-Hisab is by Ibn al-Banna al-Marrakushi. It covers fractions and sums of squares and cubes.
muslim-scientists-0235: Abu al-Wafa al-Buzjani's book on arithmetic for merchants contains the first use of which numbers in a medieval Islamic text?
His arithmetic book for merchants contains the first known use of negative numbers in a medieval Islamic text.
muslim-scientists-0237: Habash al-Hasib al-Marwazi is credited with discovering which two trigonometric ratios?
Habash al-Hasib discovered tangent and cotangent and compiled some of the earliest known tables for them.
muslim-scientists-0238: Ibn Mu'adh al-Jayyani's Majhulat Qisiyy al-Kura is considered the first book in which field?
Al-Jayyani's book has been described as the first treatise on spherical trigonometry.
muslim-scientists-0239: What was the perfect compass about which Abu Sahl al-Quhi wrote?
An instrument for measuring the altitude of stars
A magnetic compass for finding the qibla (prayer direction) while traveling
A compass with an adjustable leg for drawing conic sections
A balance for measuring the density of metals
The perfect compass has one variable-length leg and draws lines, circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
muslim-scientists-0240: In 988 CE, Abu Sahl al-Quhi headed the astronomers at a Baghdad observatory built by whom?
Al-Quhi headed the astronomers at the observatory built in Baghdad by the Buyid emir Sharaf al-Dawla.
muslim-scientists-0241: On what idea did Abu Sa'id al-Sijzi base the boat-shaped astrolabe admired by al-Biruni?
The Sun is the center of the universe
Planets orbit the Sun in elliptical orbits
Apparent motion is caused by Earth's rotation
The Moon receives its light from the Sun
Al-Biruni stated that the boat-shaped astrolabe was based on the idea that the motion we see comes from Earth's motion rather than the sky's.
muslim-scientists-0242: Abu Ja'far al-Khazin was the first to formulate and solve which problem in number theory?
Al-Khazin was the first to formulate and solve the congruum problem.
muslim-scientists-0243: Which problem of Archimedes did al-Mahani unsuccessfully attempt to solve?
Cutting a sphere with a plane into two volumes in a given ratio
Doubling a cube's volume using a ruler and compass
Al-Mahani attempted to divide a sphere into two volumes in a given ratio. Abu Ja'far al-Khazin later solved the problem.
muslim-scientists-0244: On which Greek book did al-Nayrizi write his famous commentary that was translated into Latin?
Al-Nayrizi commented on al-Hajjaj ibn Matar's translation of Euclid's Elements. Gerard of Cremona translated the commentary into Latin.
muslim-scientists-0245: Which astronomical tables did Maslama al-Majriti introduce to al-Andalus and improve?
Al-Majriti introduced and improved al-Khwarizmi's astronomical tables and improved translations of the Almagest.
muslim-scientists-0246: Through what achievement is Maslama al-Majriti regarded as initiating organized scientific research in al-Andalus?
Translating Greek medical books into Arabic
Establishing a school of astronomy and mathematics
Building the first observatory in Cordoba
Al-Majriti founded a school of astronomy and mathematics. Ibn al-Saffar was one of his students.
muslim-scientists-0247: An exoplanet was named after which Andalusian astronomer who studied under al-Majriti?
The planet Saffar (Upsilon Andromedae b) was named in honor of Ibn al-Saffar.
muslim-scientists-0248: What is the best-known work of the Andalusian astronomer Ibn al-Saffar?
Tables of lunar and solar motion
His best-known work is a treatise on using the astrolabe that remained in use until the fifteenth century.
muslim-scientists-0249: What is the title of Jabir ibn Aflah al-Ishbili's book criticizing the mathematical foundations of Ptolemy's work?
Islah al-Majisti by Jabir ibn Aflah was the first critique of the Almagest in the Islamic West.
muslim-scientists-0251: What is Nur al-Din al-Bitruji known for in astronomy?
Accurately measuring Earth's circumference by observing a lunar eclipse in two cities
A model of concentric spheres as an alternative to Ptolemy's
Al-Bitruji was the first to propose a model of concentric spheres as an alternative to Ptolemy's system.
