muslim-scientists-0252: Who taught the Andalusian astronomer Nur al-Din al-Bitruji?
Al-Bitruji was a student of Ibn Tufayl and a contemporary of Ibn Rushd.
muslim-scientists-0253: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Fazari is credited with making the first instrument of which type in the Islamic world?
Al-Fazari is credited with making the first astrolabe in the Islamic world.
muslim-scientists-0254: Al-Fazari helped translate an Indian astronomical book into Arabic that became known as al-Sindhind. Who was its original author?
Al-Fazari and Ya'qub ibn Tariq translated Brahmagupta's book, which became known as al-Sindhind.
muslim-scientists-0255: In which field did Hasan al-Rammah al-Shami excel during the Mamluk era?
Hasan al-Rammah studied types of gunpowder and explosives and devised new kinds of gunpowder and a new fuse.
muslim-scientists-0256: In which book did Ibn al-Haytham criticize Ptolemy's works and expose their contradictions?
In al-Shukuk ala Batlamyus (1025-1028 CE), Ibn al-Haytham identified contradictions in Ptolemy's Almagest, Planetary Hypotheses, and Optics.
muslim-scientists-0257: Ibn al-Haytham wrote as many as two hundred books. How many survive?
Ibn al-Haytham wrote about two hundred books, of which only 55 survive.
muslim-scientists-0258: Which optical phenomenon involving the Moon did Ibn al-Haytham explain?
The Moon appearing larger near the horizon
The Moon changing color during an eclipse
Always seeing one side of the Moon
A halo appearing around the Moon
Ibn al-Haytham explained the Moon illusion, its appearing larger near the horizon. His explanation reached Europe through Roger Bacon and others.
muslim-scientists-0259: When did Friedrich Risner print the Latin translation of Ibn al-Haytham's Kitab al-Manazir?
Risner printed it in 1572 CE under the title Opticae Thesaurus, together with Ibn al-Haytham's treatise on twilight.
muslim-scientists-0260: Besides a lunar crater bearing his name, how was Ibn al-Haytham honored in modern astronomy?
An asteroid was named after him
A galaxy was named after him
A comet was named after him
A binary star was named after him
A lunar crater and asteroid 59239 Alhazen were named after him.
muslim-scientists-0261: Ibn al-Haytham refuted the theory that rays emerge from the eye. Who were prominent earlier proponents?
Euclid and Ptolemy held that rays emerge from the eye toward the visible object. Ibn al-Haytham disproved this experimentally.
muslim-scientists-0262: Which language did al-Biruni learn, besides Arabic and Persian, to study Indian sciences from their original sources?
Al-Biruni mastered Sanskrit and translated Indian mathematics and sciences into Arabic.
muslim-scientists-0263: After whom was al-Biruni's major astronomical work al-Qanun al-Mas'udi named?
Al-Biruni dedicated the Qanun to Mas'ud, son of Sultan Mahmud al-Ghaznawi.
muslim-scientists-0265: With which contemporary scholar did al-Biruni exchange scientific letters that still survive?
Al-Biruni corresponded with Ibn Sina, and their correspondence on scientific matters survives.
muslim-scientists-0267: How old was Ibn Sina when he became physician to the Samanid emir Nuh ibn Mansur?
Ibn Sina became physician to Nuh II of the Samanids at the age of seventeen.
muslim-scientists-0268: Of Ibn Sina's approximately 240 surviving works, how many concern medicine?
About 240 of his works survive, including around 40 on medicine.
muslim-scientists-0269: What made al-Jazari's twin-piston pump a milestone in engineering history?
Its early use of suction pipes and the double-action principle
It was the first steam-powered pump
It was the first cast-iron pump
It was the first pump to lift water a hundred meters from the bottom of a well
His pump combined suction pipes and the double-action principle with conversion of rotary motion into reciprocating motion.
muslim-scientists-0272: How tall was the astronomical castle clock, al-Jazari's largest clock?
The castle clock was about 3.4 meters tall and displayed the zodiac and the paths of the Sun and Moon.
muslim-scientists-0273: What distinguished the elephant clock's measurement of time?
It used sand instead of water
It worked without water or weights, powered only by wind
The elephant clock recorded temporal hours whose length varied with the length of daylight throughout the year.
muslim-scientists-0274: In al-Jazari's elephant clock, how long did the perforated bowl take to fill and sink?
The bowl filled through a small hole in half an hour and sank. Its ropes then activated the mechanism announcing the half-hour or hour.
muslim-scientists-0275: Where is the oldest known manuscript of al-Jazari's book on mechanical devices (1206 CE) kept?
The Egyptian National Library in Cairo
The Topkapi Palace Library in Istanbul
The oldest known copy, Ahmed III 3472, is held in the Topkapi Palace Library.
muslim-scientists-0276: What is the Banu Musa's most important geometrical work, widely used by medieval mathematicians?
Al-Usul fi al-Handasa al-Mustawiya wa al-Mujassama
Their most important work is Kitab Ma'rifat Misahat al-Ashkal al-Basita wa al-Kuriyya.
muslim-scientists-0277: The Banu Musa wrote about twenty books. How many survive?
The Banu Musa wrote about twenty books, all but three of which were lost.
muslim-scientists-0278: Which two Greek engineers inspired some of the machines in the Banu Musa's Kitab al-Hiyal?
Archimedes of Sicily and Apollonius of Perga
Hero of Alexandria and Philo of Byzantium
Some of their machines drew inspiration from Hero of Alexandria and Philo of Byzantium, whom they then greatly surpassed.
muslim-scientists-0279: Which accurate mathematical tables did al-Khwarizmi contribute to trigonometry?
Al-Khwarizmi provided accurate sine and cosine tables.
muslim-scientists-0280: Al-Khwarizmi supervised a team of geographers making a world map for al-Ma'mun. How many geographers were there?
Al-Khwarizmi helped draw a world map for al-Ma'mun, supervising seventy geographers.
muslim-scientists-0281: Where is the unique Arabic copy of al-Khwarizmi's book on algebra kept?
Its unique Arabic copy is kept in Oxford. Rosen translated it into English in 1831 CE.
muslim-scientists-0283: Al-Zahrawi described a method for reducing a dislocated joint now attributed to the Swiss surgeon Kocher. Which joint?
Al-Tasrif described what later became known as Kocher's method for reducing a dislocated shoulder.
muslim-scientists-0284: Al-Zahrawi was the first to describe ligating which artery to treat migraine?
Al-Zahrawi described ligation of the temporal artery to treat migraine about six hundred years before Pare.
muslim-scientists-0286: In his commentary on Hippocrates' Epidemics, how did Ibn al-Nafis anticipate the English physician John Snow?
Describing locations of epidemic cases to trace the source
Isolating patients in quarantine sites outside city walls
Ibn al-Nafis described the locations of epidemic cases in Damascus to trace their source, an approach similar to John Snow's centuries later.
muslim-scientists-0287: Which famous European anatomist edited a Latin translation of al-Razi's al-Mansuri in the sixteenth century?
Gerard of Cremona translated it around 1180 CE, and Vesalius edited its Latin translation in the sixteenth century.
muslim-scientists-0289: Al-Kindi joined al-Khwarizmi in spreading which numerals in the Islamic world?
Al-Kindi and al-Khwarizmi played important roles in introducing Hindu-Arabic numerals to the Islamic world.
muslim-scientists-0290: Whose earlier linguistic work did al-Kindi build upon in cryptology?
Al-Kindi built upon al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Farahidi's work on cryptography.
muslim-scientists-0292: Who was among Ulugh Beg's most famous astronomy students?
His most famous astronomy student was Ali al-Qushji, whereas Qadi Zada was a leading teacher at his school.
muslim-scientists-0294: On which earlier tables was al-Kashi's Zij al-Khaqani based?
Al-Kashi based his Zij al-Khaqani on Nasir al-Din al-Tusi's Zij al-Ilkhani.
muslim-scientists-0295: In Risalat al-Watar wa al-Jayb, al-Kashi calculated which trigonometric value with accuracy unsurpassed until Taqi al-Din?
Al-Kashi calculated the sine of one degree with accuracy approaching that of his value for pi.
muslim-scientists-0296: Approximately how many books did Taqi al-Din al-Rasid write before his death in 1585 CE?
Taqi al-Din died in 1585 CE after writing more than ninety books.
muslim-scientists-0297: Where did Taqi al-Din continue his observations in Istanbul while his observatory was being completed?
Taqi al-Din continued his studies in Galata Tower until the new observatory was completed.
muslim-scientists-0298: In which book did Nasir al-Din al-Tusi first propose the Tusi couple in 1247 CE?
Al-Tusi first proposed it in Tahrir al-Majisti (1247 CE) to explain the motion of the inferior planets.
muslim-scientists-0299: In which year did construction of the Maragha Observatory begin?
Construction of the Maragha Observatory began in 1259 CE and took three to five years.
muslim-scientists-0300: What distinguished the abridged edition of al-Idrisi's book printed in Rome in 1592 CE?
It was the first book printed in Italian
It was the first book ever printed
It was among the earliest printed Arabic books
It was the first geographical atlas printed in color in Europe
The Rome edition of 1592 CE was among the earliest printed Arabic books.
muslim-scientists-0301: Al-Idrisi was among the first Arabs to write about which East Asian kingdom?
The kingdom of Bagan in Burma
The kingdom of Srivijaya in Sumatra
The kingdom of Silla in Korea
Al-Idrisi wrote about the Korean kingdom of Silla, encouraging Arab merchants to travel there.
muslim-scientists-0304: How many camels were needed to transport a single mobile bimaristan (hospital) under the Seljuk sultan Muhammad?
A single mobile hospital under Muhammad the Seljuk required forty camels to transport it.
muslim-scientists-0305: How many animal species are described in al-Jahiz's Kitab al-Hayawan?
Kitab al-Hayawan is a seven-volume encyclopedia describing more than 350 animal species.
muslim-scientists-0306: What is the title of the Toledan pharmacologist Ibn Wafid's principal book?
Ibn Wafid's most important book is al-Adwiya al-Mufrada, translated into Latin as De Medicamentis Simplicibus.
muslim-scientists-0308: In which European city was the Latin translation of al-Battani's astronomical tables printed in 1537 CE?
The Latin translation of al-Battani's astronomical tables was printed in Nuremberg in 1537 CE.
muslim-scientists-0310: Al-Battani established a criterion for sighting the crescent Moon. How long did he require the Moon to remain above the horizon after sunset?
His criterion included a minimum difference in longitude between the Moon and Sun and a moonset more than 43.2 minutes after sunset.
muslim-scientists-0311: Around 856 CE, al-Farghani wrote a treatise in Cairo on which instrument?
Al-Farghani wrote a treatise on the astrolabe in Cairo around 856 CE.
muslim-scientists-0312: Al-Zarqali wrote about making which instrument for calculating planetary positions, a work translated into Spanish by order of Alfonso X?
Al-Zarqali wrote about constructing an equatorium to calculate planetary positions. His work was translated as part of Alfonso X's Libros del Saber de Astronomia.
muslim-scientists-0313: For how many years did al-Zarqali observe the Sun, beginning in 1050 CE?
Al-Zarqali observed the Sun for twenty-five years beginning in 1050 CE.
muslim-scientists-0314: In which year did Ibn Yunus observe solar and lunar eclipses in Cairo?
Ibn Yunus observed solar and lunar eclipses in Cairo in 978 CE.
muslim-scientists-0315: For how many years did Ibn Yunus serve as an astronomer for the Fatimids in Cairo?
Ibn Yunus served as an astronomer for the Fatimids for twenty-six years, first under al-Aziz Billah and then al-Hakim.
muslim-scientists-0316: What was the name of the astrolabe made by Ibn al-Shatir?
Ibn al-Shatir named his astrolabe al-Ala al-Jami'a.
muslim-scientists-0317: Ibn al-Shatir made a small sundial (12 x 12 cm) to determine zuhr (noon prayer) and asr (afternoon prayer). What else did it indicate?
The start of the lunar month
The length of the solar year
His small sundial showed the local meridian and the direction of Mecca.
muslim-scientists-0319: What value did Taqi al-Din al-Rasid give for the obliquity of the ecliptic in his tables?
Taqi al-Din gave the obliquity as 23 degrees 28 minutes 40 seconds, closer to the correct value than his predecessors' values.
muslim-scientists-0320: In which other science did Taqi al-Din write and establish the law of reflection through observation?
Taqi al-Din wrote on optics, established the law of reflection through observation, and investigated refraction.
muslim-scientists-0321: How tall was the gnomon, or pillar, that Ulugh Beg used for his measurements over many years?
Ulugh Beg used a sundial with a pillar about 50 meters tall for his measurements.
muslim-scientists-0322: Who published the star catalog from Ulugh Beg's al-Zij al-Sultani in Oxford in 1665 CE?
Thomas Hyde published it in Oxford in 1665 CE.
muslim-scientists-0323: What did al-Kashi develop in algebra and numerical analysis that was not known in Europe until centuries later?
An iterative method for solving cubic equations
Al-Kashi developed an iterative method for solving cubic equations that was not discovered in Europe until centuries later.
muslim-scientists-0324: In which year did al-Kashi write his treatise describing astronomical observation instruments?
In 1416 CE, al-Kashi wrote a treatise on observational instruments, including al-Khujandi's sextant and the Fakhri sextant.
muslim-scientists-0325: Ibn Sahl used the law of refraction to derive the shapes of special lenses. What was their distinctive feature?
They focused light without geometric aberration
They split light into its colors
Ibn Sahl derived lens shapes that focused light without geometric aberration.
muslim-scientists-0326: Ibn Sahl is considered the first known Muslim scholar to study which Greek book?
Ibn Sahl was the first known Muslim scholar to study Ptolemy's Optics, preparing the way for Ibn al-Haytham's work.
muslim-scientists-0327: Which teacher advised Kamal al-Din al-Farisi to study Ibn al-Haytham's Kitab al-Manazir?
Al-Farisi studied under Qutb al-Din al-Shirazi, who in turn studied under Nasir al-Din al-Tusi.
muslim-scientists-0328: Al-Fakhri fi al-Jabr wa al-Muqabala is a surviving mathematical work by which scholar?
Al-Karaji's surviving books include al-Badi fi al-Hisab, al-Fakhri fi al-Jabr wa al-Muqabala, and al-Kafi fi al-Hisab.
muslim-scientists-0329: Up to which power of the unknown did Abu Kamil readily handle algebraic equations?
Abu Kamil was the first Muslim mathematician to readily handle powers beyond the square, up to the eighth power.
muslim-scientists-0330: Al-Khujandi stated a special case of Fermat's famous theorem. What was the exponent?
Al-Khujandi stated that the sum of two cubes cannot be a cube, the case with exponent 3, but his proof was incorrect.
muslim-scientists-0331: When was the sole manuscript of al-Uqlidisi's book on Indian arithmetic discovered?
The historian Ahmad Salim Saidan discovered it in 1960 CE.
muslim-scientists-0333: Habash al-Hasib devised a trigonometric algorithm for parallax problems. Which European scholar rediscovered it in 1609 CE?
Kepler rediscovered Habash's algorithm in 1609 CE. It is now known as Kepler's equation.
muslim-scientists-0334: What did al-Nayrizi use to prove the Pythagorean theorem?
Al-Nayrizi proved the Pythagorean theorem using a Pythagorean tiling of squares.
muslim-scientists-0336: Where did Abu Sa'id al-Sijzi make astronomical observations between 969 and 970 CE?
Al-Sijzi made observations in Shiraz between 969 and 970 CE.
muslim-scientists-0337: In the late eighth century, al-Fazari described which African country as the land of gold?
Al-Fazari mentioned Ghana and described it as the land of gold, one of the earliest Arabic references to it.
inventions-0001: Which French physician invented the stethoscope, used to listen to heartbeats, in 1816?
Rene Laennec invented the stethoscope in 1816 using a rolled paper tube and then a wooden one.
inventions-0002: How many dots make up the original cell in the raised writing system Louis Braille devised for blind people?
The original Braille cell is a rectangle with two columns of three dots each, making six dots.
inventions-0003: In which year did Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel patent dynamite?
Nobel patented dynamite in 1867 after mixing nitroglycerin with an absorbent material that made it safer to transport.
inventions-0004: Who devised a method in the 1860s for preserving liquid foods by heating them moderately to kill germs without boiling?
Louis Pasteur devised this method in the 1860s, and it was named pasteurization after him.
inventions-0005: Against which disease did Louis Pasteur test his vaccine on the child Joseph Meister in 1885?
Pasteur treated Joseph Meister after a rabid dog bit him. He became the first person to receive the rabies vaccine in 1885.
inventions-0006: Which type of radiation did German physicist Wilhelm Rontgen discover in 1895, opening the way for medical imaging?
Rontgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and called them X because their nature was unknown.
inventions-0007: Which Austrian scientist discovered the main blood groups in 1901?
Karl Landsteiner discovered blood groups in 1901, making blood transfusion safe. He received the Nobel Prize in 1930.
inventions-0008: At which university did Frederick Banting and Charles Best isolate insulin in 1921?
Banting and Best conducted their experiments at the University of Toronto in Canada in 1921. Insulin was then used to treat diabetes.
inventions-0009: In 1928, Alexander Fleming noticed that mold growing on a bacterial culture plate killed nearby bacteria. What substance did he discover?
Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 from Penicillium mold. After development into a medicine, it became one of the most important antibiotics.
inventions-0010: In 1882, Robert Koch announced the discovery of the bacterium responsible for which disease?
Koch announced the discovery of the tuberculosis bacillus in 1882. World Tuberculosis Day is observed on March 24 to commemorate it.
inventions-0011: Which British physician proved in 1897 that mosquitoes transmit the malaria parasite?
Ronald Ross proved the role of mosquitoes in transmitting the malaria parasite in 1897 and received the Nobel Prize in 1902.
inventions-0012: What substance did surgeon Joseph Lister use to disinfect wounds and surgical instruments in the 1860s?
Lister used carbolic acid, or phenol, as an antiseptic, greatly reducing surgical mortality.
inventions-0013: Which Hungarian physician urged doctors to wash their hands with a chlorine solution to reduce deaths from puerperal fever?
Semmelweis required handwashing with a chlorine solution at the Vienna hospital in 1847, causing deaths to fall sharply.
inventions-0014: Dutch physician Willem Einthoven received the Nobel Prize in 1924 for a practical device recording the electrical activity of which organ?
Einthoven's device was the electrocardiograph, for which he received the Nobel Prize in 1924.
inventions-0015: In 1747, naval surgeon James Lind conducted a trial on sailors with scurvy. What did he find cured them?
Lind found that sailors who ate oranges and lemons recovered quickly because of vitamin C.
inventions-0016: Which Polish biochemist coined the term vitamin in 1912?
Casimir Funk coined the word in 1912 from vital and amine, believing they were all amines.
inventions-0017: In a book published in 1628, English physician William Harvey fully described which process in the human body?
Blood circulating through the body, pumped by the heart
In his 1628 book, Harvey described blood circulating throughout the body through the heart's pumping action.
inventions-0018: Who first saw the capillaries connecting arteries and veins under a microscope in 1661?
Malpighi saw capillaries in a frog's lung under a microscope in 1661, completing what Harvey had begun.
inventions-0019: Which Dutch merchant made precise lenses by hand and was the first to see and describe bacteria?
Using his lenses, van Leeuwenhoek saw microorganisms and described them in letters to the Royal Society from 1676 onward.
inventions-0020: Robert Hooke used the word cell for what he saw under a microscope in a thin slice of which plant material?
In a slice of cork, Hooke saw cavities resembling monks' small rooms and called them cells. He published this in Micrographia in 1665.
inventions-0021: With whom did botanist Matthias Schleiden develop cell theory in 1838-1839?
Schleiden formulated cell theory for plants, and Theodor Schwann extended it to animals in 1839.
inventions-0022: Which part of the cell did Scottish botanist Robert Brown name in 1831?
Robert Brown observed, described, and named the nucleus in orchid cells in 1831.
inventions-0023: In 1869, Swiss scientist Friedrich Miescher isolated a substance he called nuclein from white blood cells. What is it known as today?
The substance Miescher isolated was nucleic acid, although its role in heredity was not understood until decades later.
inventions-0024: At which university were James Watson and Francis Crick working when they published their DNA double-helix model in 1953?
Watson and Crick built their model at the University of Cambridge's Cavendish Laboratory and published it in 1953.
inventions-0025: Who invented the polymerase chain reaction (PCR), which amplifies DNA fragments millions of times, in 1983?
American chemist Kary Mullis invented this technique in 1983 and received the Nobel Prize for it in 1993.
inventions-0026: Australian physicians Barry Marshall and Robin Warren proved that which bacterium causes stomach ulcers?
They discovered the role of Helicobacter pylori in ulcers and received the Nobel Prize in 2005.
inventions-0027: In which city did surgeon Christiaan Barnard perform the first human-to-human heart transplant in 1967?
Barnard performed the operation at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town on December 3, 1967.
inventions-0028: Which American surgeon performed the first successful kidney transplant between identical twins in 1954?
Joseph Murray successfully transplanted a kidney between identical twins in 1954 and received the Nobel Prize in 1990.
inventions-0029: During World War II, Dutch physician Willem Kolff built the first practical device for which treatment?
Kolff built the first practical dialysis machine, or artificial kidney, in the Netherlands in 1943.
inventions-0030: The iron lung developed by Philip Drinker and Louis Shaw in 1928 particularly saved patients with which disease?
The iron lung breathed for patients whose chest muscles had been paralyzed by polio.
inventions-0033: Which substance did Scottish physician James Young Simpson introduce for anesthesia in surgery and childbirth in 1847?
Simpson tested chloroform on himself and his companions in 1847 and then introduced it for anesthesia.
inventions-0034: The BCG vaccine developed by French scientists Albert Calmette and Camille Guerin protects against which disease?
Its name abbreviates Bacillus Calmette-Guerin. It is a tuberculosis vaccine used since 1921.
inventions-0035: Jonas Salk's vaccine was declared successful in 1955. Against which disease was it developed?
Salk's vaccine is an inactivated polio vaccine whose success was announced in 1955.
inventions-0037: Which British engineer developed the computed tomography scanner in the early 1970s?
Godfrey Hounsfield developed the scanner at EMI and shared the 1979 Nobel Prize with Allan Cormack.
inventions-0038: In the 1930s, German scientist Gerhard Domagk discovered the first widely used drug in which class?
Domagk discovered the antibacterial effect of Prontosil, the first sulfonamide, and received the Nobel Prize in 1939.
inventions-0041: In 1820, Danish physicist Hans Christian Oersted observed which effect of an electric current flowing through a wire?
It deflects a nearby compass needle
The compass needle's deflection near the wire showed that an electric current generates a magnetic field.
inventions-0042: Which phenomenon, on which electric generators depend, did Michael Faraday discover in 1831?
Faraday discovered that a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, a phenomenon called electromagnetic induction.
inventions-0043: Which German physicist first experimentally demonstrated electromagnetic waves in the late 1880s?
Hertz demonstrated the waves predicted by Maxwell. The unit of frequency was named after him.
inventions-0044: Which Italian scientist invented the mercury barometer for measuring atmospheric pressure in 1643?
Torricelli invented the mercury barometer in 1643. The pressure unit torr was named after him.
inventions-0045: Otto von Guericke demonstrated two metal hemispheres that horses could not pull apart after the air inside was removed. What did this prove?
The horses could not separate the hemispheres because external air pressure pressed them together after the air between them was removed.
inventions-0046: Which Dutch scientist first made an accurate pendulum clock in 1656?
Huygens made the pendulum clock in 1656, making it far more accurate than other clocks of its time.
inventions-0048: In which year did Swedish astronomer Anders Celsius propose his centigrade temperature scale?
Celsius proposed his scale in 1742. Its original form was reversed, with zero for boiling and one hundred for freezing.
inventions-0050: Who built the atmospheric piston steam engine that began pumping water out of mines in 1712?
Thomas Newcomen built the first atmospheric piston engine in 1712 to pump water out of mines.
inventions-0051: What was James Watt's most important improvement to the steam engine in 1765, greatly reducing fuel consumption?
Watt condensed steam in a separate chamber, so the cylinder no longer cooled and heated with every stroke, reducing wasted fuel.
inventions-0052: Who built the first steam locomotive to run on rails, tested in Wales in 1804?
Richard Trevithick's locomotive ran on the Penydarren railway in Wales in 1804.
inventions-0054: What was the name of the first public railway to use steam locomotives, opened in England in 1825?
The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in 1825 and was the first public railway to use steam locomotives.
inventions-0055: In which year did the world's first underground railway, London's Metropolitan line, open?
London's underground Metropolitan Railway opened in January 1863.
inventions-0056: In which year did Japan's first high-speed Shinkansen line open between Tokyo and Osaka?
The Tokaido Shinkansen opened in 1964, becoming the world's first high-speed railway line.
inventions-0057: How many wheels did the Benz Patent-Motorwagen, patented in 1886 and considered the first practical automobile, have?
Karl Benz's first car had three wheels and an internal combustion engine.
inventions-0058: In which year was the first successful four-stroke gas engine, using the Otto cycle, built?
Nikolaus Otto built the first successful four-stroke engine in 1876.
inventions-0059: What ignites fuel in a diesel engine instead of an electric spark plug?
A continuous flame from a small burner
The heat of highly compressed air
Air is compressed in the diesel engine's cylinder until it becomes very hot, igniting the fuel as soon as it is sprayed in.
inventions-0060: In which year did Henry Ford introduce the moving assembly line at his factory to produce the Model T?
Ford introduced the moving assembly line in 1913, greatly reducing the car's assembly time and price.
inventions-0061: American Mary Anderson received a patent in 1903 for which automobile device?
Mary Anderson noticed that drivers stopped their vehicles to clear snow from the glass, so she invented a wiper operated from inside.
inventions-0062: In which year did Swedish engineer Nils Bohlin introduce the three-point seat belt used in cars today?
Bohlin introduced the three-point seat belt in 1959, and his company made the patent freely available to everyone.
inventions-0063: Who invented the cat's-eye road reflectors used to guide drivers at night in 1934?
British inventor Percy Shaw patented cat's-eye reflectors in 1934.
inventions-0064: In which city were the world's first traffic lights installed in 1868?
The first traffic lights were installed in Parliament Square in London in December 1868 to regulate carriage traffic.
inventions-0065: In which city was the world's first parking meter installed in 1935?
The first parking meter was installed in Oklahoma City in the United States in July 1935.
inventions-0066: British engineer Edgar Hooley noticed that spilled tar bound the stones on a road. What paving material did he patent in 1902?
Hooley patented tarmac, a mixture of tar and gravel, in 1902.
inventions-0068: In which year did German inventor Karl Drais devise the wooden two-wheeled machine propelled by pushing against the ground, the ancestor of the bicycle?
Karl Drais introduced his machine, called the running machine, in 1817.
inventions-0069: Who built the hot-air balloon that carried humans on their first flight in 1783?
Brothers Joseph and Etienne Montgolfier built the hot-air balloon that carried the first human passengers in 1783.
inventions-0070: Which gas did Frenchman Jacques Charles use to fill his balloon that flew in 1783?
Jacques Charles used hydrogen, making his balloon the first gas balloon to carry humans.
inventions-0071: Who built the first steerable airship driven by a steam engine, which flew in 1852?
Henri Giffard's steam-powered airship flew about 27 kilometers in 1852.
inventions-0072: In which year did Count Ferdinand von Zeppelin's first rigid airship fly over Lake Constance?
The LZ 1 airship first flew over Lake Constance in July 1900.
inventions-0073: Which German aviator made more than two thousand successful glider flights in the 1890s?
Otto Lilienthal made more than two thousand flights in his gliders, benefiting later aviation pioneers.
inventions-0074: Which British engineer identified the four forces of flight, lift, drag, thrust, and weight, and is called the father of aviation?
Sir George Cayley identified the forces acting on an aircraft and designed gliders that carried a person.
inventions-0075: Which was the first jet airliner to enter commercial service in 1952?
The British Comet entered service in 1952 as the first jet airliner.
inventions-0076: Which was the first piloted aircraft to exceed the speed of sound in level flight in 1947?
The experimental Bell X-1 exceeded the speed of sound on October 14, 1947.
inventions-0077: The supersonic Concorde aircraft resulted from cooperation between Britain and which other country?
Concorde was developed under a treaty between Britain and France and first flew in 1969.
inventions-0078: The flight recorder known as the black box was invented in the 1950s by a scientist from which country?
Australian David Warren invented it following investigations into Comet aircraft crashes.
inventions-0079: In 1926, Robert Goddard launched the first rocket powered by which type of fuel?
Goddard launched the first liquid-fueled rocket in Massachusetts on March 16, 1926.
inventions-0080: Which British inventor developed the hovercraft, which travels over water and land on an air cushion, in the 1950s?
Christopher Cockerell invented the hovercraft and patented it in the 1950s.
inventions-0081: Whose Clermont, the first commercially successful passenger steamboat, sailed on the Hudson River in 1807?
Robert Fulton's steamboat sailed between New York and Albany in 1807, becoming the first commercially successful steamboat.
inventions-0082: Dutch inventor Cornelis Drebbel built the first submarine known to have successfully traveled underwater. In which river did he test it?
Drebbel tested his submarine in London's River Thames around 1620.
inventions-0083: The first nuclear power station to supply electricity to the public grid began operating in 1954 in which country?
The Obninsk station near Moscow began supplying electricity to the grid in 1954.
inventions-0084: Which engineer invented the modern steam turbine, used in most power stations, in 1884?
British engineer Charles Parsons invented the steam turbine in 1884.
inventions-0085: With which engineer did Jacques-Yves Cousteau develop the Aqua-Lung underwater breathing apparatus in 1943?
Cousteau and engineer Emile Gagnan developed the Aqua-Lung regulator in 1943.
inventions-0086: Which major maritime navigation problem did English clockmaker John Harrison solve in the eighteenth century?
Harrison built an accurate marine clock enabling sailors to calculate longitude by comparing local time with a reference time.
inventions-0087: Gerardus Mercator drew a world map in 1569 using the projection named after him. What advantage did it offer navigators?
It shows a constant-bearing course as a straight line
It shows the poles at their true size
It shows sea depths in colors
On a Mercator projection, a course at a constant bearing appears as a straight line, making routes easier for navigators to plot.
inventions-0088: The oldest surviving terrestrial globe, made by Martin Behaim in Nuremberg, dates to which year?
Behaim's globe, called the Earth Apple, was made between 1490 and 1492 and is the oldest surviving terrestrial globe.
inventions-0089: Which French physicist developed the lightweight stepped lens that increased the range of lighthouse beams?
Augustin Fresnel designed his lighthouse lens in the 1820s.
inventions-0090: What made the elevator Elisha Otis demonstrated in New York in 1854 safe for passengers?
A brake that stopped it if the rope broke
Otis demonstrated his elevator and ordered the rope cut. The safety brake stopped the platform from falling.
inventions-0091: Which American engineer designed the first modern air conditioner for a New York printing plant in 1902?
In 1902, Willis Carrier designed a device to control temperature and humidity in a Brooklyn printing plant.
inventions-0093: What inspired Swiss engineer George de Mestral to invent Velcro?
De Mestral noticed that burdock burrs clung to his clothes and his dog's fur with tiny hooks, which he imitated.
inventions-0094: American chemist Stephanie Kwolek invented Kevlar fibers in 1965. What distinguishes them?
Exceptional strength combined with low weight
Kevlar consists of very strong, lightweight fibers that are stronger than steel at the same weight.
inventions-0095: In 1938, chemist Roy Plunkett accidentally discovered which material used to coat nonstick cookware?
Plunkett discovered Teflon, or polytetrafluoroethylene, in DuPont's laboratories in 1938.
inventions-0096: Which chemist led the DuPont team that invented nylon in 1935?
Wallace Carothers made nylon in 1935, the first commercially successful fully synthetic fiber.
inventions-0097: In which year did Leo Baekeland invent Bakelite, the first fully synthetic plastic?
Baekeland made Bakelite from phenol and formaldehyde in 1907.
inventions-0098: Which British metallurgist discovered stainless steel in Sheffield in 1913?
In 1913, Harry Brearley produced chromium-rich steel resistant to rust.
inventions-0099: What made Henry Bessemer's 1856 process revolutionary in steelmaking?
Blowing air through molten iron burns away impurities quickly, making steel cheap and abundant.
inventions-0100: Which English builder patented Portland cement, the most widely used type of cement, in 1824?
Joseph Aspdin patented Portland cement in 1824, naming it for its resemblance to stone from the Isle of Portland.
inventions-0101: In 1867, French gardener Joseph Monier patented concrete flowerpots reinforced with what?
Monier reinforced his concrete pots with iron mesh and was a pioneer of reinforced concrete.
inventions-0102: Between which cities was the first official message sent over Samuel Morse's telegraph line in 1844?
The message was sent from Washington to Baltimore on an experimental line on May 24, 1844.
inventions-0104: The first transatlantic telegraph cable was laid in 1858. Approximately how long did it work before failing?
The 1858 cable worked for only about three weeks. A permanent cable succeeded in 1866.
inventions-0105: In 1843, Scottish clockmaker Alexander Bain patented a device transmitting images and writing over telegraph wires. It was the forerunner of which device?
Alexander Bain's 1843 patent is considered the origin of the fax machine.
inventions-0106: In which year did Englishman Isaac Pitman publish his shorthand system based on sounds rather than letters?
Isaac Pitman published his phonetic shorthand system in 1837. It spread throughout the English-speaking world.
inventions-0107: For which machine was the QWERTY keyboard layout originally developed?
Christopher Sholes developed this layout for the typewriter in the 1870s.
inventions-0108: What was the name of the device that first recorded and played back sound in 1877 using a cylinder wrapped in tin foil?
Edison invented the phonograph in 1877. It stored sound by inscribing grooves in tin foil.
inventions-0109: Which Frenchman took the oldest surviving landscape photograph, View from the Window at Le Gras, around 1826-1827?
Nicephore Niepce took the photograph from his home's window at Le Gras, using an exposure lasting hours or days.
inventions-0110: The daguerreotype process was announced in 1839. On what surface did its image appear?
A daguerreotype image appeared on a copper plate coated with silver polished to a mirror finish.
inventions-0111: What was the main advantage of Fox Talbot's calotype process over the daguerreotype?
Printing many copies from one negative
The calotype produced a paper negative from which many positive copies could be printed, unlike the unique daguerreotype.
inventions-0112: Who introduced the roll-film Kodak camera that made photography accessible to the public in 1888?
George Eastman introduced the Kodak camera with roll film in 1888, popularizing photography.
inventions-0113: Who invented the first instant camera, introduced in 1948, which produced a printed photograph in about a minute?
Edwin Land invented the instant camera, which his company Polaroid introduced in 1948.
inventions-0114: Which American lawyer and physicist invented dry document copying, the basis of modern photocopiers, in 1938?
Chester Carlson invented xerography in New York in 1938.
inventions-0115: Which Scottish scientist patented the kaleidoscope, whose colored patterns repeat through mirrors, in 1817?
David Brewster invented the kaleidoscope around 1815 during experiments on light polarization and patented it in 1817.
inventions-0116: Who first made movable type from fired clay in eleventh-century China?
Bi Sheng made ceramic movable type between 1039 and 1048 CE. Two centuries later, Wang Zhen introduced wooden type.
inventions-0117: The oldest surviving dated printed book, found in China's Dunhuang caves, dates to which year?
This book was printed using woodblocks in 868 CE and found in the Mogao Caves near Dunhuang.
inventions-0118: Which English pharmacist invented friction matches in 1826?
In 1826, pharmacist John Walker noticed that a dried mixture on a stick ignited when rubbed, leading him to make friction matches.
inventions-0120: Which American patented sweetened condensed milk in 1856?
Gail Borden patented condensed milk in 1856 by evaporating its water in a vacuum vessel.
inventions-0121: Where did Clarence Birdseye see fish freeze immediately after being caught in icy conditions, inspiring rapid food freezing?
In Labrador, Birdseye saw that fish rapidly frozen in extreme cold retained their flavor after thawing.
inventions-0122: In 1869, French chemist Hippolyte Mege-Mouries invented which cheap butter substitute in response to a competition announced by Napoleon III?
Mege-Mouries made margarine in 1869 after Napoleon III requested a cheap substitute for butter.
inventions-0124: Which French physicist invented the steam digester in 1679, which cooks food with steam trapped under pressure and is the ancestor of the pressure cooker?
Denis Papin invented the steam digester in 1679 and fitted it with a safety valve.
inventions-0125: Which chemist invented the double-walled vacuum vessel, the ancestor of the thermos flask, in 1892?
Sir James Dewar invented the vacuum vessel in 1892 to keep liquefied gases cold.
inventions-0126: English engineer Edwin Budding's 1830 cylinder lawn mower was inspired by a machine used for what?
Budding saw a machine with rotating blades trimming the nap of cloth in a textile factory and applied its principle to grass.
inventions-0127: Which British engineer built a large suction cleaning machine transported on a horse-drawn cart in 1901?
In 1901, Hubert Cecil Booth built a powered vacuum cleaner transported to homes on a cart.
inventions-0128: In which year did American inventor Josephine Cochrane invent the first practical dishwasher using water pressure?
Josephine Cochrane patented the dishwasher in 1886.
inventions-0130: For what purpose did American inventor Bette Nesmith Graham develop a white liquid in the 1950s?
She developed white correction fluid to cover typewriter errors. It later became known as Liquid Paper.
inventions-0131: In which year did American inventor Walter Hunt invent the safety pin?
Walter Hunt patented the safety pin in 1849.
inventions-0133: Who patented the rubber band in London in 1845?
Stephen Perry patented the rubber band in 1845 for holding papers and letters together.
inventions-0134: Which 3M engineer developed transparent adhesive tape in 1930?
Richard Drew developed transparent adhesive tape in 1930, following the masking tape he had invented earlier.
inventions-0135: Englishman William Addis made the first mass-produced toothbrush around 1780. Where is he said to have designed it?
Addis reportedly made his first brush from a bone and pig bristles in prison, then established a factory to produce it.
inventions-0136: Who patented the revolving door in the United States in 1888?
Theophilus Van Kannel patented the revolving door in Philadelphia in 1888.
inventions-0137: Which American store owner invented the wheeled shopping cart in 1937?
Sylvan Goldman invented the shopping cart in 1937 to encourage customers to buy more.
inventions-0138: In which city was the first cash-dispensing ATM installed at a bank branch in 1967?
The first ATM was installed at a Barclays branch in Enfield, north London, on June 27, 1967.
inventions-0139: What inspired Norman Woodland's idea for the barcode?
Woodland extended Morse code's dots and dashes in sand, turning them into thin and thick lines.
inventions-0140: The QR code was invented in Japan in 1994. What was its original purpose?
Denso Wave designed it to track car parts during manufacturing.
inventions-0141: Blaise Pascal built his mechanical calculator in 1642 to help his father with his work. What did his father do?
His father supervised tax collection in Rouen, so Pascal built the machine to simplify his lengthy calculations.
inventions-0142: In 1614, Scotsman John Napier published which mathematical invention that turns multiplication into addition?
Napier published logarithm tables in 1614, shortening astronomical and navigational calculations.
inventions-0143: Which Englishman invented the slide rule around 1622, used by engineers for centuries before calculators?
Around 1622, William Oughtred placed two logarithmic scales side by side to make the first slide rule.
inventions-0144: Which English engineer designed the Difference Engine to calculate mathematical tables automatically in the 1820s?
Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine and then the Analytical Engine, anticipating the computer.
inventions-0145: Herman Hollerith's tabulating machine was first used in 1890 to count what?
Hollerith's machines were used for the 1890 United States census, reducing the time it took by years.
inventions-0146: What controlled the Jacquard loom, introduced in 1804, to weave complex patterns?
The card holes determined which threads were raised, allowing the loom to weave the pattern automatically.
inventions-0148: Who invented the flying shuttle, which doubled weaving speed, in 1733?
John Kay invented the flying shuttle in 1733, allowing one weaver to weave wide cloth quickly.
inventions-0149: Who patented the power loom, driven by power rather than the weaver's hand, in 1785?
Edmund Cartwright patented the power loom in 1785 and improved it in later years.
inventions-0150: Which American invented the cotton gin, which rapidly separates seeds from fibers, in 1793?
Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin in 1793 and patented it in 1794.
inventions-0151: Which English farmer developed the seed drill in 1701 to plant seeds in regular rows at a consistent depth instead of scattering them by hand?
Jethro Tull developed the seed drill in 1701, reducing seed waste and increasing yields.
inventions-0152: Which American blacksmith made a steel plow in 1837 that cut sticky prairie soil without clogging?
In 1837, John Deere made a polished steel plow to which prairie soil did not stick.
inventions-0153: Which particle did Joseph John Thomson discover in 1897 while studying cathode rays?
In 1897, Thomson demonstrated that cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles smaller than atoms: electrons.
inventions-0154: Rutherford's team fired alpha particles at a very thin metal foil, revealing the atomic nucleus. Which metal was it?
Some alpha particles bouncing back from gold foil indicated a small, dense nucleus at the atom's center.
inventions-0155: Which British physicist discovered the neutron in 1932?
James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 and received the Nobel Prize in 1935.
inventions-0156: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 when salts of which element affected a covered photographic plate?
Becquerel found that uranium salts darkened a photographic plate even in darkness, discovering radioactivity.
inventions-0157: Marie Curie named one of the two elements she and her husband discovered in 1898 after her homeland. Which element?
Polonium was named after Poland, Marie Curie's homeland.
inventions-0158: In 1938, chemists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann discovered nuclear fission after bombarding which element with neutrons?
Hahn and Strassmann found barium among the products of bombarding uranium with neutrons, which was explained as nuclear fission.
inventions-0159: At which university was the first nuclear reactor to achieve a self-sustaining chain reaction built in 1942?
Chicago Pile-1 was built beneath stadium stands at the University of Chicago and reached criticality on December 2, 1942.
inventions-0160: Which physicist invented the cyclotron, a circular particle accelerator, at the University of California, Berkeley?
Ernest Lawrence invented the cyclotron in 1929-1930 and received the Nobel Prize for it in 1939.
inventions-0161: With whom did Hans Geiger develop the radiation counter named after its two inventors in 1928?
Geiger and his student Walther Muller developed the counter in 1928, giving it the name Geiger-Muller counter.
inventions-0162: Which Scottish physicist invented the cloud chamber, which reveals charged particle tracks as lines of mist?
Charles Thomson Rees Wilson invented the cloud chamber and received the Nobel Prize for it in 1927.
inventions-0163: Austrian physicist Victor Hess discovered cosmic rays in 1912 by measuring radiation where?
At the bottom of a lake
Hess ascended to a great height in a balloon and found that radiation increased with altitude, showing it came from space.
inventions-0164: In 1911, Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes discovered that which metal's electrical resistance vanished when cooled near absolute zero?
Onnes cooled mercury with liquid helium and its resistance vanished, leading to the discovery of superconductivity in 1911.
inventions-0165: Which English scientist identified hydrogen as a distinct gas in 1766 and called it inflammable air?
Henry Cavendish was the first to identify hydrogen as a distinct substance in 1766.
inventions-0166: In 1772, Scottish physician Daniel Rutherford isolated which gas, calling it noxious air?
Daniel Rutherford is credited with discovering nitrogen in 1772.
inventions-0167: In 1774, Swedish chemist Carl Scheele prepared which yellow-green gas without recognizing it as an element?
Scheele prepared chlorine in 1774. Humphry Davy demonstrated that it was an element in 1810.
inventions-0168: Which was the first noble gas discovered on Earth, found in air by Lord Rayleigh and William Ramsay in 1894?
Rayleigh and Ramsay discovered argon in 1894, making it the first noble gas discovered on Earth.
inventions-0169: What did chemist Humphry Davy use to first isolate potassium and sodium in 1807?
Davy passed an electric current through molten potash and soda, isolating the two metals in 1807.
inventions-0170: Whom was Humphry Davy's 1815 safety lamp designed to protect?
Davy's lamp prevented its flame from igniting methane gas accumulated in coal mines.
inventions-0171: In 1886, American Charles Hall and which other scientist independently discovered the electrolytic process for producing aluminum?
Hall and Heroult independently discovered the process in 1886. Named after both, it made aluminum cheaper.
inventions-0172: The industrial Haber-Bosch process transformed global agriculture by producing which compound from atmospheric nitrogen?
The Haber-Bosch process produces ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen. Most fertilizers are made from it.
inventions-0173: In 1828, German chemist Friedrich Wohler made which organic compound from inorganic substances?
Wohler prepared urea from ammonium cyanate in 1828, demonstrating that organic compounds could be made in a laboratory.
inventions-0175: What shape did German chemist August Kekule propose for the benzene molecule in 1865?
Kekule proposed that benzene's six carbon atoms were connected in a six-membered ring.
inventions-0176: Which Danish chemist introduced the pH scale for measuring acidity in 1909?
Soren Sorensen introduced the pH scale at the Carlsberg Laboratory in 1909.
inventions-0177: Russian scientist Mikhail Tsvet originally developed chromatography to separate what?
Tsvet separated plant pigments such as chlorophyll in a calcium carbonate column, where they appeared as colored bands.
inventions-0178: Which French chemist first isolated the highly reactive element fluorine in 1886?
Henri Moissan isolated fluorine by electrolysis in 1886 and received the Nobel Prize in 1906.
inventions-0179: Which English chemist developed the first modern atomic theory in the early nineteenth century and was among the first to describe color blindness scientifically?
John Dalton developed his atomic theory and described the color blindness he had, which came to be called Daltonism.
inventions-0180: What instrument did Charles Coulomb use in 1785 to measure the force between electric charges?
Coulomb measured the force between charges with a torsion balance and formulated his law in 1785.
inventions-0181: In 1676, Danish astronomer Ole Romer inferred that light has a finite speed by observing eclipses of what?
Romer observed that eclipses of Io occurred later when Earth was farther from Jupiter, concluding that light takes time to travel.
inventions-0182: Which British engineer invented the vacuum diode, the first electronic valve, in 1904?
John Ambrose Fleming invented the diode in 1904 to detect radio signals.
inventions-0184: Three Bell Laboratories scientists received the 1956 Nobel Prize for inventing the transistor: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain, and whom?
Bardeen, Brattain, and Shockley shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics for the transistor.
inventions-0185: Theodore Maiman operated the first working laser in 1960 using a crystal of what?
Maiman used a synthetic ruby rod illuminated by a flash lamp at Hughes Laboratories in 1960.
inventions-0187: Where was the first practical silicon solar cell, demonstrated in 1954, made?
Chapin, Fuller, and Pearson made the first practical silicon solar cell at Bell Laboratories in 1954.
inventions-0188: Which young French physicist first observed the photovoltaic effect, on which solar cells depend, in 1839?
In 1839, nineteen-year-old Edmond Becquerel observed that light generated a current in an electrochemical cell.
inventions-0190: Which French physicist invented the lead-acid battery, the first rechargeable battery, in 1859?
Gaston Plante invented the lead-acid battery in 1859. It is still used in cars.
inventions-0191: Three scientists received the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing which batteries?
Goodenough, Whittingham, and Yoshino received the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for lithium-ion batteries.
inventions-0192: Which French engineer first demonstrated colored neon lights for signs in Paris in 1910?
Georges Claude demonstrated neon lamps at the Paris Motor Show in 1910.
inventions-0193: Three scientists received the 2014 Nobel Prize in Physics for inventing an LED of which color, enabling energy-efficient white lighting?
The blue LED was the missing component needed to produce white light. Akasaki, Amano, and Nakamura received the 2014 Nobel Prize for it.
inventions-0196: In which country did Louis Essen build the first accurate atomic clock in 1955?
Louis Essen and Jack Parry built the clock at Britain's National Physical Laboratory in 1955.
inventions-0197: Which Chinese scientist built the earliest known earthquake detector in 132 CE, with eight dragons dropping balls into frogs below?
Zhang Heng built the earthquake detector in 132 CE during the Han dynasty.
inventions-0198: In 1814, German scientist Joseph Fraunhofer made which instrument to study dark lines in the solar spectrum?
Fraunhofer invented the spectroscope in 1814 and used it to describe dark lines in the solar spectrum that were named after him.
inventions-0200: In 1860, Bunsen and Kirchhoff used spectroscopy to discover which element, named for its blue spectral lines?
Bunsen and Kirchhoff discovered cesium in 1860. Its name comes from a Latin word meaning sky blue.
inventions-0201: Which French engineer invented the electric cell that became the basis of dry batteries in 1866?
Georges Leclanche invented his cell in 1866, from which the dry battery was developed.
inventions-0215: The archaeological site of Ugarit was accidentally discovered in 1928 when a farmer's plow struck an ancient tomb. In which country is it today?
Ugarit is at Ras Shamra, north of Latakia on the Syrian coast.
inventions-0216: Where is the ancient kingdom of Ebla, whose palace yielded an archive of about twenty thousand cuneiform tablets?
Ebla is at Tell Mardikh near Idlib in northwestern Syria, where about twenty thousand tablets were found.
inventions-0217: Mohenjo-daro, one of the largest cities of the Indus Valley civilization, is in which present-day country?
Mohenjo-daro is in Pakistan's Sindh province and was uncovered in the 1920s.
inventions-0218: Which Swiss traveler became the first European in modern times to reach Petra in 1812?
Burckhardt reached Petra in 1812 and introduced it to Europe.
inventions-0219: The Antikythera mechanism, the oldest known geared astronomical calculator, was recovered in 1901 from what?
The mechanism was recovered from a Roman shipwreck near the Greek island of Antikythera.
inventions-0220: Where is Gobekli Tepe, which contains the oldest known massive stone structures?
Gobekli Tepe lies near Sanliurfa in southeastern Turkey and dates to about 9500 BC.
inventions-0222: Which American explorer brought the Andean city of Machu Picchu to the world's attention in 1911?
Hiram Bingham visited the site in 1911 and brought it to the world's attention.
inventions-0224: Which Portuguese navigator reached India by sea around the Cape of Good Hope in 1498?
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in India in 1498, opening the sea route there from Europe.
inventions-0225: Which Portuguese sailor was the first European to round the Cape of Good Hope, in 1488?
Bartolomeu Dias rounded the southern tip of Africa in 1488.
inventions-0226: After Magellan was killed in the Philippines, which Spanish sailor completed the first voyage around the world in 1522?
Elcano captained the Victoria back to Spain in 1522, completing the first circumnavigation of Earth.
inventions-0227: Who was the first European to see the Pacific Ocean from the Americas in 1513 after crossing the Isthmus of Panama?
Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama in 1513 and saw the Pacific Ocean.
inventions-0228: Which Norwegian explorer was the first to reach the South Pole, in 1911?
Roald Amundsen reached the South Pole on 14 December 1911.
inventions-0229: New Zealander Edmund Hillary and whom first reached the summit of Everest in 1953?
Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit on 29 May 1953.
inventions-0230: Which lake did British explorer John Speke identify as the source of the Nile in 1858?
Speke reached Lake Victoria in 1858 and said it was the source of the Nile. It was later established as the main source of the White Nile.
inventions-0231: Which Scottish explorer reached Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River in 1855?
David Livingstone was the first European to see the falls in 1855.
inventions-0232: Who described the aeolipile, a rotating steam-powered sphere and the oldest known steam engine, in the first century AD?
Hero of Alexandria described the aeolipile, a sphere that rotates as steam escapes from two pipes.
inventions-0233: Which Alexandrian engineer is considered the father of pneumatics and developed the water clock and piston pump?
Ctesibius wrote the first works on pneumatics and improved the water clock.
inventions-0234: Eratosthenes measured Earth's circumference in the third century BC by comparing the Sun's shadow in Alexandria with which other Egyptian city?
Eratosthenes compared the Sun's angle in Alexandria with Aswan (Syene), where the Sun casts no shadow at noon on the summer solstice.
inventions-0235: Which Welsh mathematician invented the equals sign (=) in 1557?
Robert Recorde used two parallel lines in 1557 because nothing could be more equal than them.
inventions-0236: Which Englishman introduced the infinity symbol (∞) into mathematics in 1655?
John Wallis first used the infinity symbol in 1655.
inventions-0238: Which American developed the pin tumbler cylinder lock, the modern lock commonly used in doors, in the 1860s?
Linus Yale Jr. developed the pin tumbler cylinder lock and patented it in the 1860s.
inventions-0239: Which English inventor patented the hydraulic press, which multiplies force using liquids, in 1795?
Joseph Bramah patented the hydraulic press in 1795, which is why it is sometimes called the Bramah press.
inventions-0241: Which Englishman described a flushing toilet, considered one of the earliest models of the modern toilet, in 1596?
Sir John Harington described a flushing toilet in 1596 and installed one for his godmother, Queen Elizabeth I.
inventions-0242: Which British officer invented the first pressurized portable fire extinguisher in the 1810s?
In 1813 George William Manby invented a copper extinguisher containing a solution under air pressure.
inventions-0243: Which Polish pharmacist invented the modern kerosene lamp in 1853?
Ignacy Lukasiewicz invented the kerosene lamp in 1853 and later established one of the earliest oil refineries.
inventions-0244: In which state was the first mechanically drilled oil well for extracting oil in the United States sunk in 1859?
Edwin Drake drilled his well in Titusville, Pennsylvania, in 1859.
inventions-0246: In 1668 Isaac Newton built a telescope that collects light without a front lens. What does it use to collect it?
Newton's telescope used a concave mirror to collect light, eliminating the color distortion caused by lenses.
inventions-0247: Which invisible rays did astronomer William Herschel discover in 1800 by placing a thermometer beyond the red end of the Sun's spectrum?
The thermometer's temperature rose beyond the red end, leading Herschel to infer the existence of invisible infrared rays.
inventions-0248: In 1801 German scientist Johann Ritter discovered invisible rays by observing that they darkened which chemical beyond the violet end of the spectrum?
Ritter found that silver chloride darkened faster beyond violet, discovering ultraviolet rays.
inventions-0249: In 1852 French physicist Leon Foucault named an instrument the gyroscope. What did he use it to demonstrate?
Foucault named it from two Greek words meaning 'seeing rotation' because he used it to demonstrate Earth's rotation.
inventions-0250: In which year did Frenchman Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot build the first steam-powered road vehicle?
Cugnot built his steam carriage in 1769. It is considered the first self-propelled vehicle.
inventions-0255: Which dinosaur was the first to be described and given a scientific name, by William Buckland in 1824?
Buckland described Megalosaurus in 1824, followed by Mantell's description of Iguanodon in 1825.
inventions-0256: English fossil collector Mary Anning discovered the first two known skeletons of which extinct long-necked marine reptile on the Lyme Regis coast?
Mary Anning found the first two Plesiosaurus skeletons, contributing to the understanding of prehistoric life.
inventions-0257: In 1779 Dutch physician Jan Ingenhousz showed that plants release oxygen and purify air under which condition?
Ingenhousz showed that green parts of plants purify air only in light, pioneering the understanding of photosynthesis.
inventions-0258: Louis Pasteur's experiment with a swan-neck flask disproved which idea?
The broth in the curved-neck flask remained free of microbes, proving that they do not arise spontaneously.
inventions-0261: Near which city did Siemens open the first electric tram line serving passengers in 1881?
The Lichterfelde tram near Berlin opened in 1881 and was the first commercial electric tram.
inventions-0263: Which American invented compressed-air train brakes in 1869?
George Westinghouse patented air brakes in 1869, improving train safety.
inventions-0264: Which American engineer invented the electric car starter in 1911, removing the need to crank the engine by hand?
Charles Kettering invented the electric starter in 1911, and Cadillac fitted it to its cars in 1912.
inventions-0265: With whom did Gottlieb Daimler build the first gasoline-powered motorcycle in 1885?
Daimler and Wilhelm Maybach built the Reitwagen motorcycle in 1885.
inventions-0266: Which American built the first successful gasoline-powered farm tractor in 1892?
John Froelich built the first gasoline-powered tractor capable of moving forward and backward in Iowa in 1892.
inventions-0267: Cragside in England was the first house in the world lit by hydroelectricity. Which engineer owned it?
Lord William Armstrong lit his home, Cragside, with hydroelectricity in 1878.
inventions-0268: Which engineer designed the Thames Tunnel, opened in 1843 and the first known tunnel under a navigable river?
Marc Isambard Brunel designed the tunnel and invented a special tunneling shield. His son Isambard worked with him.
inventions-0269: In the late 1910s Ernest Rutherford established the existence of which positively charged particle in the nuclei of all atoms?
Rutherford found that hydrogen nuclei emerged from bombarded nitrogen nuclei and called them protons.
inventions-0270: Which British geologist developed the horizontal seismograph in Japan in 1880?
John Milne developed the horizontal seismograph in Japan in 1880.
inventions-0272: Which American patented the paper drinking straw in 1888?
Marvin Stone patented the paper straw in 1888. The bendable straw came later.
inventions-0273: Who patented the metal bottle cap with a toothed edge in 1892?
William Painter patented the crown cap in 1892.
inventions-0274: Who developed the safety razor with a thin disposable blade in the early twentieth century?
King Gillette developed the razor with a disposable blade and patented it in the early twentieth century.
inventions-0276: A professor of architecture from which country invented the Rubik's Cube in 1974?
Erno Rubik invented the cube in Budapest, Hungary, in 1974.
inventions-0277: British cartographer John Spilsbury made the first jigsaw puzzle in the 1760s to teach children what?
Spilsbury glued a map to a wooden board and cut it along national borders to teach geography.
inventions-0278: Which Canadian engineer proposed dividing the world into standard time zones in 1879?
Sandford Fleming proposed a worldwide system of 24 time zones in 1879.
inventions-0279: In which year did an international conference in Washington adopt the Greenwich meridian as the world's prime meridian?
The International Meridian Conference in Washington adopted the Greenwich meridian in 1884.
inventions-0280: In which country was the metric system of measurement first established in the late eighteenth century?
The metric system was established in France after its revolution, and the meter was defined in the 1790s.
inventions-0281: Which chemist developed soft contact lenses in the early 1960s?
Otto Wichterle developed a soft gel material from which he made the first soft contact lenses.
inventions-0282: Which French surgeon devised the 'flying ambulance' to transport the wounded quickly in light carriages in Napoleon's army?
Dominique Jean Larrey devised light ambulance carriages to transport wounded soldiers quickly for treatment.
inventions-0284: In London in 1854 English physician John Snow showed that cholera is transmitted through what?
Snow traced the cases to a contaminated water pump in Broad Street in 1854.
inventions-0285: In Tunisia in 1909 French physician Charles Nicolle discovered that typhus is transmitted by what?
Nicolle proved that lice transmit typhus and won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1928.
inventions-0286: Emil von Behring received the first Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1901 for his serum treatment for which disease?
Von Behring received the first Nobel Prize in Medicine for diphtheria antitoxin serum.
inventions-0287: James Joule measured the mechanical equivalent of heat in an experiment in which a falling weight turned what?
A coil in a magnetic field
Paddles in a vessel of water
A pendulum in a vessel of oil
A piston in an air cylinder
The falling weight turned paddles in water, raising its temperature, allowing Joule to measure the relationship between work and heat.
inventions-0288: In 1900 French chemist Paul Villard discovered a penetrating type of nuclear radiation later called what?
Villard discovered highly penetrating radiation from radium in 1900, which Rutherford named gamma rays.
inventions-0289: In 1932 American Carl Anderson discovered the first known antimatter particle. What was it?
Anderson observed the positron, the electron's positive counterpart, in a cloud chamber in 1932.
inventions-0290: In 1913 British chemist Frederick Soddy coined which term for atoms of the same element with different masses?
Soddy coined the term 'isotopes' in 1913 and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1921.
inventions-0291: On what basis did British physicist Henry Moseley arrange the elements in 1913?
Using X-rays, Moseley showed that atomic number is the correct basis for arranging the periodic table.
inventions-0293: Who invented the Linotype machine, which sets an entire line of type at once?
Ottmar Mergenthaler invented the Linotype in the 1880s, revolutionizing newspaper printing.
inventions-0294: Which German writer invented lithography in 1796?
Alois Senefelder invented lithography in 1796 to print his plays cheaply.
inventions-0295: Which was the first newspaper printed on a steam-powered press in 1814?
Friedrich Koenig's steam-powered press printed The Times of London in 1814.
inventions-0296: Who made the first parachute jump from a balloon over Paris in 1797?
Andre-Jacques Garnerin parachuted from a balloon at a great height over Paris in 1797.
inventions-0297: The strait separating Asia and North America bears the name of a Danish navigator who sailed through it in 1728 in the service of which country?
Vitus Bering was an officer in the Russian navy when he sailed through the strait in 1728.
inventions-0298: Which Dutch navigator was the first European to reach New Zealand, in 1642?
Abel Tasman reached New Zealand in 1642, and the island of Tasmania was named after him.
inventions-0299: American agronomist Norman Borlaug won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970 for developing high-yield varieties of what?
Borlaug developed short, disease-resistant wheat varieties and was a pioneer of the Green Revolution.
inventions-0300: In 1939 Swiss scientist Paul Muller discovered that DDT is effective at what?
Muller discovered DDT's effectiveness as an insecticide and won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1948.
inventions-0301: Which Chinese scientist is known as the father of hybrid rice?
Yuan Longping developed the first hybrid rice varieties in the 1970s, greatly increasing production.
inventions-0302: China's Tu Youyou won the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2015 for discovering artemisinin, a drug used to treat what?
Tu Youyou extracted artemisinin from sweet wormwood, saving millions of malaria patients.
inventions-0303: Which Japanese inventor invented instant noodles in 1958?
Momofuku Ando invented instant noodles in Japan in 1958.
inventions-0304: In 1908 Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda discovered the fifth taste, umami, in broth made from what?
Ikeda found that glutamic acid in seaweed (kombu) broth was the source of this taste.
inventions-0305: Which engineer established an optical telegraph system in France in the 1790s that sent messages using movable arms on successive towers?
Claude Chappe established France's optical telegraph network starting in 1792, transmitting messages in minutes.
inventions-0307: The scanning tunneling microscope, which revealed individual atoms, was invented in 1981 at an IBM laboratory near which city?
Gerd Binnig and Heinrich Rohrer invented it at IBM's Zurich laboratory in 1981 and won the Nobel Prize in 1986.
inventions-0308: Which element did German Hennig Brand discover in 1669 while searching for the philosopher's stone?
Hennig Brand extracted phosphorus in 1669. It was named 'light-bearer' because it glows in the dark.
inventions-0309: Which element did German chemist Martin Klaproth discover in 1789 and name after a planet discovered a few years earlier?
Klaproth named uranium after the planet Uranus, which Herschel discovered in 1781.
inventions-0310: Weeks after Volta announced his electric pile in 1800, Englishmen William Nicholson and Anthony Carlisle used it to decompose what?
Nicholson and Carlisle decomposed water electrically into hydrogen and oxygen in 1800.
inventions-0312: Polyethylene, the most widely used plastic, was discovered in practice in 1933 in the laboratories of which British company?
Eric Fawcett and Reginald Gibson discovered it at Imperial Chemical Industries (ICI) laboratories in 1933.
inventions-0314: In the float glass process, smooth, flat sheets are produced by floating molten glass on which molten metal?
Molten glass floats on a bath of molten tin, leveling its surface, in a process developed by Alastair Pilkington.
inventions-0315: French chemist Edouard Benedictus discovered laminated safety glass in 1903 when he dropped a flask coated inside with which substance?
The flask's fragments did not scatter because a dry layer of cellulose nitrate held them together, giving him the idea for laminated glass.
inventions-0316: Which German chemist devised the method of coating glass with a thin layer of silver to make modern mirrors in 1835?
Justus von Liebig devised the chemical deposition of silver on glass in 1835.
inventions-0317: Which Englishman built the safety bicycle with equal-sized wheels and a chain, the basis of the modern bicycle, in 1885?
John Kemp Starley built the Rover safety bicycle in 1885, which became the model for modern bicycles.
inventions-0318: Which Frenchman built the first seaplane to take off from water under its own power in 1910?
Henri Fabre took off in his seaplane from a lake near Marseille in March 1910.
inventions-0319: Which engineer invented the autogyro, a rotorcraft that preceded the helicopter, in 1923?
The autogyro designed by Juan de la Cierva flew successfully in 1923.
inventions-0320: Which American architect patented the lightweight geodesic dome made of interlocking triangles in 1954?
Richard Buckminster Fuller developed the geodesic dome and patented it in the United States in 1954.
inventions-0321: Which German invented the taximeter in 1891?
Wilhelm Bruhn invented the taximeter in 1891 to calculate fares by distance and time.
inventions-0322: Which French surgeon revived the use of thread to tie blood vessels to stop bleeding instead of cauterization in the sixteenth century?
Ambroise Pare revived tying blood vessels with thread to stop bleeding instead of painful cauterization.
inventions-0323: Who published 'De humani corporis fabrica', which corrected Galen's anatomical errors, in 1543?
Andreas Vesalius published his book in 1543, laying the foundations of modern anatomy.
inventions-0324: Which British surgeon developed modern hip replacement surgery in the 1960s?
Sir John Charnley developed the low-friction artificial hip joint in the 1960s.
inventions-0325: Which British ophthalmologist implanted the first intraocular lens after cataract removal in 1949?
Harold Ridley noticed that plastic fragments in pilots' eyes were not rejected and implanted the first intraocular lens in 1949.
inventions-0326: Which German physician made the first recording of electrical brain waves in humans in 1924?
Hans Berger recorded the first human electroencephalogram in 1924.
inventions-0327: Howard Florey and Ernst Chain turned penicillin into a practical medicine during World War II. At which university were they working?
Florey and Chain's team at Oxford University purified penicillin and tested it on patients in 1940-1941.
inventions-0328: Which American physicist invented the high-voltage electrostatic generator with a metal dome and a moving belt in 1929?
Robert Van de Graaff built his generator in 1929 to accelerate particles in nuclear physics experiments.
inventions-0330: The first permanent color photograph was displayed in 1861 using the three-color method proposed by which physicist?
In 1861 Maxwell displayed a color photograph of a fabric ribbon by combining three red, green, and blue images.
inventions-0331: Who described the oldest known vending machine, which dispensed a measure of water when a coin was inserted, in the first century AD?
Hero of Alexandria described a machine that dispensed water when a coin pressed a lever that opened a valve.
inventions-0332: American Garrett Morgan patented a traffic signal with a third warning position in 1923. Which invention had made him famous earlier?
Garrett Morgan invented a protective breathing mask used to rescue tunnel workers in 1916, then patented his traffic signal in 1923.
inventions-0333: Ernest Solvay developed the Solvay process for producing sodium carbonate from salt and limestone. Which country was he from?
Belgian Ernest Solvay developed his process in the 1860s.
inventions-0334: Which Englishman invented the slow-burning safety fuse that reduced mining accidents in 1831?
William Bickford invented the safety fuse in Cornwall in 1831 to protect miners.
inventions-0335: English chemist Alfred Bird invented baking powder in 1843 because his wife did what?
Was allergic to yeast and eggs
Bird invented baking powder and custard powder because his wife was allergic to eggs and yeast.
inventions-0336: Where was the first commercial oil discovery in the Middle East made in 1908?
Oil flowed at Masjed Soleyman in southwestern Iran in 1908, marking the region's first commercial discovery.
inventions-0337: In which year did Melvil Dewey first publish his Dewey Decimal Classification for library books?
Melvil Dewey published his classification system in 1876, and it is still used in many libraries.
inventions-0338: Which Frenchman invented the liquid-free aneroid barometer in 1844?
Lucien Vidi invented the aneroid barometer in 1844, making pressure measurement possible without mercury.
inventions-0339: Which Danish scientist developed the staining method that divides bacteria into positive and negative groups in 1884?
Hans Christian Gram developed his staining method in 1884, and it remains fundamental to bacterial classification.
palm-plants-0001: What is the scientific name of the date palm?
The date palm is Phoenix dactylifera of the palm family and is the type species of the genus Phoenix.
palm-plants-0004: How long is a date fruit usually?
The date fruit is oval-cylindrical, measuring 3 to 7 centimeters long and about 2.5 cm in diameter.
palm-plants-0005: Approximately how long is a fully grown date palm frond?
Date palm leaves are pinnate, measuring 4-6 meters long, with spines on the stalk.
palm-plants-0006: Approximately how many leaflets does a single date palm frond bear?
A date palm's pinnate frond bears about 150 leaflets, each about 30 cm long.
palm-plants-0007: Botanists describe the date palm as dioecious. What does this mean?
Male flowers grow on one tree and female flowers on another
It has two trunks growing from one root
It bears fruit twice in one year
It grows in both plains and rugged mountains at the same time
The date palm is dioecious: each sex has its own tree. The male tree bears male flowers and the female tree bears female flowers.
palm-plants-0008: If date palms are grown from seeds, approximately what percentage of the seedlings will be fruit-bearing females?
About half of seedlings grown from seed are fruit-bearing females, which is why propagation by offshoots is preferred.
palm-plants-0009: With hand pollination, approximately how many female date palms can one male palm serve?
With human assistance, one male palm can pollinate up to one hundred female palms.
palm-plants-0010: Date varieties are divided into soft, semi-dry, and dry. Which of these is an example of a dry date?
Medjool is an example of a soft date, Deglet Noor of a semi-dry date, and Thoory of a dry date.
palm-plants-0011: From which date variety was the first draft date palm genome published in 2011?
The draft genome was published in 2011 from the Khalas variety, followed by more complete assemblies in 2013 and 2019.
palm-plants-0013: When the dubas bug sucks sap from a palm, what visible damage results?
Root rot below the soil surface
Black sooty mold forms on the fronds
Long tunnels bore through the trunk to the palm's heart
The dubas bug (Ommatissus lybicus) sucks sap, resulting in black sooty mold.
palm-plants-0014: In the 1920s, how many healthy Medjool offshoots were taken from Morocco to the United States?
Eleven healthy Medjool palms were transported, of which nine survived. Their descendants were moved to Indio, California, in 1935.
palm-plants-0015: Approximately how many dates does a mature, fruit-bearing palm produce in one season?
A mature palm produces 70-140 kg of dates per season. They do not ripen all at once and are harvested in stages.
palm-plants-0016: At which Neolithic site in western Pakistan were date seeds found among the earliest evidence of familiarity with dates?
Ancient date seeds were found at Mehrgarh, a Neolithic site in western Pakistan, without establishing a definite date for their cultivation there.
palm-plants-0017: Which Andalusian scholar included a chapter on date palm cultivation in his twelfth-century agricultural book?
Ibn al-Awwam of Seville's twelfth-century Kitab al-Filaha includes a treatise on date palm cultivation.
