palm-plants-0018: Who introduced date palms to California by 1769 AD?
The Spanish introduced date palms to California, and they were present around the San Diego mission in 1769 AD.
palm-plants-0019: Mazafati is one of the world's best-known date varieties. Which country is it associated with?
Among the world's best-known varieties are Algerian Deglet Noor, Iraqi Zahidi and Halawi, Moroccan Medjool, and Iranian Mazafati.
palm-plants-0020: Halawi is one of the world's best-known date varieties. Where does it originate?
The source lists Zahidi and Halawi among Iraq's best-known dates.
palm-plants-0021: Dates are a good source of which mineral?
Dates are a good source of potassium, with the amount varying by variety.
palm-plants-0022: How are date pits used in some countries after roasting and grinding?
A red dye for wool and cotton
A coffee substitute or an addition to coffee
Fuel for lamps in old houses
The pits are ground and used like coffee beans or added to coffee.
palm-plants-0023: What is traditionally made from date clusters after their fruit has been stripped off?
Fruit clusters stripped of their dates are used as brooms.
palm-plants-0024: Which dangerous virus can pass from bats to humans through drinking raw palm sap?
Drinking raw palm sap is one route of Nipah virus transmission from bats to humans. Boiling inactivates it.
palm-plants-0025: Palm fiber is used to make ropes and coarse fabrics. From which part is this fiber taken?
The palm heart at the crown
The sheaths at the bases of fronds
Fiber extracted from the leaf sheaths at the bases of fronds is used to make ropes, coarse fabrics, and hats.
palm-plants-0026: Why is harvesting the palm heart for food a great loss?
It makes its fruit taste bitter
It turns a female palm into a male
It stops fruiting for one year
The terminal bud (heart) is edible, but removing it kills the palm because it has no other growing point.
palm-plants-0027: What did palm fronds symbolize in processions of Roman commanders returning from war?
Palm fronds, mostly from date palms, symbolized triumph in Roman victory processions.
palm-plants-0028: Which special type of roots does the date palm have?
The date palm has respiratory roots (pneumatodes) that help with air exchange.
palm-plants-0029: Why does a palm trunk not grow thicker with age like most trees?
Its roots are short and shallow
The fiber wrapped around it prevents the trunk from expanding
The palm is a monocot without a cylindrical cambium, so its trunk grows taller rather than thicker.
palm-plants-0030: After approximately how many years does a date palm grown from an offshoot begin bearing fruit?
A palm grown from an offshoot begins bearing fruit at about four years old, compared with 7-10 years for one grown from seed.
palm-plants-0031: What is the thin covering around a date pit that separates it from the flesh called?
The qitmir is a thin membranous covering around the pit and is the inner layer of the fruit wall.
palm-plants-0032: What is the small round depression on the back of a date pit that marks the embryo's position and from which germination begins called?
The naqir is a depression on the dorsal side of the pit that marks the embryo's position and from which germination begins.
palm-plants-0033: What is the thin strand of white tissue in the groove along the inner side of a date pit called?
The pit's groove contains a thin strand of white fleshy tissue called the fatil.
palm-plants-0034: What is the part that covers the base of a date fruit and attaches it to a strand of the fruit cluster called?
The qim' covers the fruit's base and attaches it to the strand. It consists of the dried remains of the calyx and corolla.
palm-plants-0035: Before opening, palm flowers are enclosed in a covering that splits when they mature. What is this covering called?
The kufurra is the covering of the palm's inflorescence, while the ighrid is the flower cluster inside it.
palm-plants-0036: How many separate carpels make up the date palm's female flower?
The female flower has three separate carpels, one of which grows if pollinated.
palm-plants-0037: How many stamens does a male date palm flower bear?
The male flower has six stamens that release pollen when the anthers mature.
palm-plants-0039: According to studies, what is the optimum temperature for date palm pollen germination?
The optimum pollen germination temperature is 35 degrees Celsius. Germination falls greatly at about 43 degrees.
palm-plants-0041: What is a palm fruit that sets without pollination, develops without a pit, and does not ripen called?
Parthenocarpic fruit set produces seedless fruits called shis or shisha'.
palm-plants-0043: What is the ideal age for separating an offshoot from its mother palm?
It is preferable to separate an offshoot at about three to five years, once its roots and size have developed, depending on the variety and care.
palm-plants-0044: Which ancient Mesopotamian law code referred to date palm pollination?
Cuneiform tablets and Hammurabi's stele indicate that artificial date palm pollination was practiced in ancient times.
palm-plants-0045: What is the ideal temperature range for date palm growth?
Temperatures between 32 and 38 degrees Celsius are ideal for palm growth, and the palm tolerates over 50 degrees.
palm-plants-0046: In which year did UNESCO inscribe 'Date palm: knowledge, skills, traditions and practices' on its intangible cultural heritage list?
In December 2019 UNESCO inscribed this joint Arab nomination on the Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
palm-plants-0047: Which Gulf country was called the land of a million palm trees because of its many palms?
Bahrain was called the land of a million palm trees because of its many palms.
palm-plants-0048: Why was Iraq formerly called Ard al-Sawad (the land of blackness)?
Its alluvial soil turned black after floods
Oil was abundant on its surface
Iraq was called Ard al-Sawad because its widespread palm groves looked dark from a distance.
palm-plants-0049: On which Emirati island were two charred date seeds found, the older dating to the sixth millennium BC?
Two charred date seeds were found on Dalma Island off Abu Dhabi. One was dated to about 5290-4940 BC and the other to about 4810-4540 BC.
palm-plants-0050: Which archaeological site in Kuwait is among the earliest sites of date palm use in the Gulf, dating to about 5000 BC?
The Al-Subiyah site in Kuwait, dating to about 5000 BC, provides some of the earliest evidence of palm use in the Gulf.
palm-plants-0051: How many pairs of chromosomes does the date palm genome contain?
The date palm genome is distributed over 18 pairs of chromosomes.
palm-plants-0052: Which stage immediately follows busr in date fruit development?
The fruit passes through tal', then khalal, then busr, then rutab, and finally tamr.
palm-plants-0054: How many ovaries does the female palm flower contain, one of which is fertilized while the others wither?
The female flower has three ovaries. One is fertilized and grows, while the other two wither.
palm-plants-0055: What does daqal mean in Classical Arabic?
Palms growing along rivers and springs
The poorest palms with the worst dates
In Classical Arabic, daqal refers to palms with the worst dates, although Deglet Noor is now one of the finest varieties.
palm-plants-0056: Which date variety is nicknamed 'fingers of light' and 'the lady of dates'?
Deglet Noor is nicknamed the lady of dates and fingers of light and is well known in Algeria and Tunisia.
palm-plants-0058: What increased the popularity of Deglet Noor dates in the United States during World War II?
Sugar rationing made them a substitute for candy
A ban on importing dried figs from Europe at the time
A shortage of flour in bakeries
Sugar rationing during World War II helped popularize Deglet Noor as a substitute for candy.
palm-plants-0060: In which Moroccan region did the Medjool variety originate?
The Medjool variety originates in Morocco's Tafilalt region and is still grown there.
palm-plants-0062: Barhi is among Iraq's best-known dates. From which Iraqi city does its palm originate?
Barhi is among Basra's best-known dates, and people from Unaizah brought it from there to Al-Qassim.
palm-plants-0063: Residents of which city in Al-Qassim brought the Barhi palm from Iraq to the Arabian Peninsula?
The Barhi palm originates in Basra and was brought to the Arabian Peninsula by people from Unaizah.
palm-plants-0064: What color is the Barhi fruit at the khalal stage?
Barhi is green at the jimri stage, yellow at khalal, and amber-brown at rutab.
palm-plants-0065: Which characteristic distinguishes Khalas dates from many varieties and makes them desirable in markets?
They retain their pleasant flavor during long storage
They are dark black at both the tamr and rutab stages
Their fruit is completely without a pit
They ripen twice in one season
Khalas is an excellent commercial variety because it retains its pleasant flavor during long storage.
palm-plants-0066: Into which product did researchers in the UAE convert Khalas date pits in their experiments?
Emirati researchers converted Khalas pits into biofuel, as oil can be extracted from about 10% of them.
palm-plants-0067: Which town in Al-Qassim is considered the home of the first Sukkari palm?
Sukkari became known and famous in Al-Qassim, and Huwaylan is the home of its first palm.
palm-plants-0068: Which date variety, famous in Al-Kharj Governorate, has both red and yellow on a single fruit?
Sagai is a date from Al-Kharj. Its cylindrical fruit combines red and yellow.
palm-plants-0069: In which region is the Naboot Saif date variety well known?
Naboot Saif is among the date varieties for which Najd, specifically Al-Qassim, is known.
palm-plants-0070: Ajwa has two types, one of which is the elongated Abu Dhira'. What is the other, round type called?
Ajwa has two types: the elongated Abu Dhira' and the round Mudardamah.
palm-plants-0071: According to Medina residents, where are the finest and best-known Ajwa dates grown?
In Yanbu on the Red Sea coast west of Medina
In Tabuk in the kingdom's northwest
In Upper Medina near Quba Mosque
Ajwa is grown throughout Medina, but the finest comes from the orchards of Upper Medina in the south, near Quba Mosque.
palm-plants-0072: Bayoud is one of the most dangerous date palm diseases. What causes it?
A fungus of the genus Fusarium
Bayoud is a fungal disease caused by Fusarium oxysporum f.sp. albedinis.
palm-plants-0073: Where does the name of the palm disease bayoud come from?
Eggs laid by the insect in the trunk
The name bayoud derives from the Arabic word for white, referring to the whitening of infected fronds.
palm-plants-0074: In which country was bayoud disease of palms first recorded in 1870 AD?
Bayoud disease was first recorded in Morocco in 1870 AD.
palm-plants-0075: How do red palm weevil larvae kill a palm?
They bore tunnels up to a meter long in the trunk
They suck sap from the fruit before it ripens
They gnaw the fine surface roots in moist soil
Weevil larvae bore holes up to a meter long in palm trunks, weakening the palms until they die.
palm-plants-0076: Where did the red palm weevil originate before spreading to the Middle East and Europe?
The red palm weevil originated in tropical Asia, then spread to Africa and Europe.
palm-plants-0077: What is the approximate area of Al-Ahsa Oasis, considered the world's largest oasis?
Al-Ahsa Oasis covers about 85.4 square kilometers and is the world's largest oasis.
palm-plants-0078: Approximately how many palm trees does Al-Ahsa Oasis contain?
More than two and a half million
About a quarter of a million
About ten and a half million
Al-Ahsa Oasis contains over 2.5 million palms, watered by more than 280 artesian springs.
palm-plants-0079: What is the old name of the Al-Ahsa region in Arabic sources?
Al-Ahsa is also known as Al-Hasa and Hajar.
palm-plants-0081: Which Spanish city has a palm grove on UNESCO's World Heritage List since 2000 AD?
UNESCO inscribed the Palmeral of Elche as a World Heritage Site in 2000 AD.
palm-plants-0083: Which traditional irrigation system is Al Ain Oasis in the UAE famous for?
Al Ain Oasis is famous for the falaj system, an underground channel that brings water to farms and palms.
palm-plants-0084: The UAE's Liwa Oasis, famous for its palms, lies on the northern edge of which desert?
Liwa Oasis lies southwest of Abu Dhabi on the northern edge of the Empty Quarter desert.
palm-plants-0085: The old Shali fortress in Egypt's Siwa Oasis was built from kershef and palm trunks. What is kershef?
White plaster mixed with crushed palm fiber
A mixture of salt and mud brick
Shali fortress was built from kershef, a mixture of salt and mud brick, and palm trunks.
palm-plants-0086: Which two crops is Egypt's Siwa Oasis famous for growing?
Siwa Oasis is based on the cultivation of thousands of date palms and olive trees.
palm-plants-0087: According to modern classifications, approximately how many genera does the palm family (Arecaceae) contain?
The palm family currently contains 181 genera and about 2600 species, mostly in tropical regions.
palm-plants-0088: Most palms have unbranched trunks. Which of these genera is known for its branching trunk?
Most palm leaves are borne on an unbranched stem, while the doum genus, Hyphaene, is known for its branching trunk.
palm-plants-0089: Which palm is the world's tallest monocotyledonous plant and Colombia's national tree?
The Quindio wax palm (Ceroxylon quindiuense) can reach 60 meters and is Colombia's national tree.
palm-plants-0090: Which plant bears the largest seed in the plant kingdom?
The coco de mer palm, Lodoicea maldivica, in the Seychelles bears the largest seed in the plant kingdom.
palm-plants-0091: The coco de mer palm (Lodoicea maldivica) grows wild only on which islands?
Lodoicea maldivica is endemic to Praslin and Curieuse in the Seychelles, although its scientific name refers to the Maldives.
palm-plants-0092: Which plant has the longest leaves in the plant kingdom, reaching about 25 meters?
Raffia palms (Raphia) have the largest leaves among plants, reaching 25 meters long.
palm-plants-0093: The talipot palm bears the world's largest branched inflorescence. What happens after it fruits?
It turns into a male palm
It loses its fronds and then regrows them
The talipot palm is monocarpic: it flowers once at an age of 30-80 years, then dies after fruiting.
palm-plants-0094: What was traditionally written on talipot palm leaves in South and Southeast Asia?
Talipot leaves were written on with an iron stylus to make palm-leaf manuscripts.
palm-plants-0095: Which is the only palm considered adapted to coastal mangrove environments?
The nipa palm (Nypa fruticans) is the only palm adapted to mangrove environments, and its trunk grows underground.
palm-plants-0096: The name rattan refers to about 600 species of palm characterized by what?
Growing no taller than a handspan
Growing in salt water on seacoasts
Climbing like ropes over other plants
Rattan comprises about 600 species of climbing palms in the Old World, used to make wicker furniture and baskets.
palm-plants-0097: From which part of the sago palm is sago starch extracted?
The sago palm is the main source of sago starch, which is extracted from its trunk by washing.
palm-plants-0098: Which Brazilian palm is called the tree of life because of its many uses and is a symbol of Ceara state?
The carnauba palm (Copernicia prunifera) is called the tree of life because of its many uses and is a symbol of Ceara state.
palm-plants-0099: Approximately how many times more oil does oil palm produce than soybeans over the same area?
Oil palm produces about nine times as much oil as soybeans per unit area.
palm-plants-0100: From which part of the African oil palm fruit is palm oil extracted?
Palm oil is extracted from the reddish pulp (mesocarp) of African oil palm fruit.
palm-plants-0101: With what are areca palm seeds traditionally chewed in South Asia?
The areca palm is grown for its seeds, which are chewed with betel leaves and slaked lime.
palm-plants-0102: The Canary Island date palm, a relative of the date palm, is a natural symbol of the Canary Islands alongside what?
The Canary Island date palm is a natural symbol of the Canary Islands along with the canary, Serinus canaria.
palm-plants-0103: Which is the only palm native to the southwestern United States, forming oases around water sources in its deserts?
Washingtonia filifera is the only palm species native to the southwestern United States.
palm-plants-0104: The royal palm (Roystonea regia) is the national tree of which country?
Roystonea regia is Cuba's national tree.
palm-plants-0106: What is the dried coconut flesh from which oil is extracted called?
Dried coconut flesh is called copra, and oil is extracted from it.
palm-plants-0107: What material is made from the fibrous husk of a coconut?
Activated charcoal made from the flesh
Coir is extracted from the fibrous husk, charcoal is made from the hard shell, and oil from the flesh.
palm-plants-0108: How many germination pores are there in a coconut's hard shell?
The hard shell has three germination pores, two closed and one functional, which are remnants of the flower's three carpels.
palm-plants-0109: Approximately how many years does a coco de mer (Lodoicea) fruit take to ripen?
A coco de mer fruit takes 6-7 years to ripen and another two years to germinate.
palm-plants-0110: Along which river is the doum palm (Hyphaene thebaica) common in Egypt and Sudan?
The doum palm grows where groundwater is present and is widespread along the Nile in Egypt and Sudan.
palm-plants-0111: What shape are doum palm leaves?
Doum leaves are fan-shaped, measuring about 120 by 180 cm, and cluster at the tips of branches.
palm-plants-0112: To which plant family does arfaj (Rhanterium epapposum) belong?
Arfaj belongs to Asteraceae and is a desert shrub found in the Arabian Peninsula.
palm-plants-0113: What color are arfaj flowers, which bloom in late spring?
Arfaj flowers are bright yellow, about 1.5 cm across, and bloom in April and May.
palm-plants-0115: What happens to arfaj in summer when the ground dries out?
It flowers abundantly and bears fruit
Its leaves fall, leaving bare branches
It dies completely and returns from seed in winter
In summer, arfaj leaves fall and its branches become bare and woody, then it grows again after rain.
palm-plants-0116: Ramth (Haloxylon salicornicum) is a desert shrub characterized by what?
Being nearly leafless and highly branched
Being aquatic and living in ponds
Ramth is a nearly leafless, highly branched shrub that tolerates salinity and drought.
palm-plants-0117: What is the Arabic name for white saxaul (Haloxylon persicum), a tree frequently mentioned in old Arabic poetry?
Haloxylon persicum is called ghada in Arabic and is frequently mentioned in Classical Arabic poetry.
palm-plants-0118: Why was ghada firewood well known in the past?
Its fragrant white smoke repels insects and vermin
It burns well and gives off intense heat
It is light and floats on water
Ghada wood is strong and heavy, burns well, and produces high heat, so it is used as fuel.
palm-plants-0119: Which genus includes a plant that parasitizes saxaul roots and is nicknamed desert ginseng in Chinese medicine?
Cistanche deserticola parasitizes saxaul roots and is nicknamed desert ginseng.
palm-plants-0120: What is the national tree of the United Arab Emirates?
Ghaf (Prosopis cineraria) is the UAE's national tree and is the subject of the 'Plant a Ghaf' campaign.
palm-plants-0121: What type of tree is the famous Tree of Life in Bahrain's desert?
Bahrain's Tree of Life is a ghaf about 400 years old, growing in a desert without a visible water source.
palm-plants-0122: Approximately how old is Bahrain's Tree of Life?
Bahrain's Tree of Life is a ghaf estimated to be about 400 years old.
palm-plants-0123: To which family does the ghaf belong?
Ghaf is a flowering tree in the legume family, Fabaceae, with bipinnate compound leaves.
palm-plants-0124: The presence of a ghaf tree in an arid desert usually indicates what?
Oil deposits close to the ground surface
Ghaf grows where rainfall is very low, but indicates the presence of a deep groundwater level.
palm-plants-0125: What distinguishes the thorns of the samar tree (Vachellia tortilis)?
It has no thorns at all
Fine, soft, hairlike thorns covering all branches
One long thorn at each leaf
A combination of long straight thorns and short hooked ones
Samar has long, straight, pale thorns and short, hooked, dark ones, which may occur together or separately.
palm-plants-0126: What shape are the samar tree's seed pods?
Flat and coiled like a spring
Samar pods are flat and coiled like a spring.
palm-plants-0127: What benefit does the samar tree provide to poor soil through its roots?
Fixing nitrogen with the help of symbiotic bacteria
Driving worms out of the soil
Dissolving limestone with acids released by fine roots
Samar fixes nitrogen in the soil in cooperation with symbiotic root bacteria, making it useful for land restoration.
palm-plants-0128: Sidr (Ziziphus spina-christi) is the national tree of which Gulf country?
Sidr, Ziziphus spina-christi, is Qatar's national tree.
palm-plants-0129: Where do sidr trees usually grow in desert environments?
On the tops of shifting sand dunes far from water
In wadis where groundwater is available
Sidr grows in deserts and semi-deserts, usually in wadis and along watercourses where groundwater is present.
palm-plants-0130: What do the green fruits of ushar (Calotropis procera) contain?
A light aromatic oil used for perfume and massage
The green fruits of ushar contain extremely bitter, poisonous milky sap with cardiac toxins.
palm-plants-0131: What name did ancient historians give the ushar fruit because it grew near the Dead Sea?
Ushar was called the Apple of Sodom because Josephus and Tacitus described it growing in the Sodom region near the Dead Sea.
palm-plants-0132: The markh shrub (Leptadenia pyrotechnica) contributes to desert planting projects because it does what?
Stabilizes sand dunes with its roots
Repels locust swarms from nearby farms
Markh is highly drought-tolerant and stabilizes soil, making it a pioneer species in dune stabilization.
palm-plants-0133: Approximately how deep can markh shrub roots extend into sand?
The long roots of markh reach 12 meters below the surface.
palm-plants-0134: For which animal is markh especially good fodder?
All livestock graze on markh, and it is especially good fodder for camels.
palm-plants-0135: The green branches of the desert shrub arta (Calligonum comosum) resemble what?
Arta's green branches spread from the stem like broom bristles.
palm-plants-0136: Which is a benefit of the arta shrub in the desert?
It provides smokeless firewood and indicates fresh water
It produces large fruits like watermelons
It is a source of natural rubber
Its fibers make expensive soft silk fabrics
Arta stabilizes dunes, provides livestock fodder and smokeless firewood, and indicates the presence of fresh water.
palm-plants-0137: Thumam (Panicum turgidum) is a desert grass whose hard, glossy stems resemble what?
Thumam stems have long internodes, are hard and glossy with few leaves, and resemble bamboo canes.
palm-plants-0138: How does thumam grass help samar trees regenerate in the Sahara?
It attracts birds that pollinate them
Its dense clumps protect seedlings from drought and grazing
Its roots release natural fertilizer to feed their small, weak roots
Thumam clumps act as nurse plants, protecting samar seedlings from drought and livestock grazing.
palm-plants-0139: The yusr or ban tree (Moringa peregrina) has seeds yielding oil with which unusual property?
Ban seeds contain a light aromatic oil that is highly resistant to rancidity and was formerly used as a perfume base.
palm-plants-0140: For which precision use was ban seed oil employed after Bedouins supplied the seeds to Cairo's markets?
Making medicinal soap for wounds and ulcers
Bedouins supplied ban seeds to Cairo to extract fine lubricating oil for mechanical watches.
palm-plants-0142: From which tree are traditional siwak (tooth-cleaning sticks) taken?
Siwak is taken from the roots and small branches of the arak tree (Salvadora persica).
palm-plants-0143: What do the arak tree's small red fruits taste like?
Arak fruits are small, red, edible, and juicy, but pungent and sharp.
palm-plants-0144: The arak tree's scientific name persica refers to what?
A type of peach resembling its fruit
Persia, where the type specimen was collected
The purple color of its flowers
A Persian botanist who discovered it in the eighteenth century
The arak type specimen was collected in Persia, so the species was named persica.
palm-plants-0145: In which two countries of the southern Arabian Peninsula is the frankincense tree (Boswellia sacra) native?
The frankincense tree (Boswellia sacra) is native to Oman and Yemen in southern Arabia, and Somalia in the Horn of Africa.
palm-plants-0146: On the slopes of which mountains are frankincense trees abundant in southern Arabia?
In Oman, frankincense trees are abundant on the steep slopes of the Dhofar Mountains.
palm-plants-0147: What is frankincense tree bark like?
Smooth, shiny, and slippery, making climbing difficult
Papery and easy to peel off
Frankincense tree bark has a papery texture and can be peeled off easily.
palm-plants-0149: Myrrh is an aromatic gum resin extracted from what?
Dried sap of the myrrh tree
Arak roots after grinding and soaking
Myrrh is a resin made from the dried sap of Commiphora myrrha.
palm-plants-0150: On which archipelago does the dragon's blood tree (Dracaena cinnabari) grow?
The dragon's blood tree is endemic to Yemen's Socotra archipelago in the Arabian Sea and is Yemen's national tree.
palm-plants-0151: What shape is the dragon's blood tree's crown?
Pointed and pyramidal like pine trees
The dragon's blood tree has a dense crown shaped like an inverted umbrella.
palm-plants-0152: What distinguishes the branching of the dragon's blood tree?
All branches emerge from one point
Its branches droop to the ground
Each branch repeatedly divides into two
The dragon's blood tree branches dichotomously, with each branch repeatedly dividing into two.
palm-plants-0153: Which Tamarix species is the tallest, reaching 18 meters?
Athel, Tamarix aphylla, is the largest species in the genus Tamarix and reaches 18 meters tall.
palm-plants-0154: How does the athel tamarisk dispose of excess salt?
It releases it with gum from the trunk
It stores it in swollen roots deep below the soil
It secretes salty water from glands on its leaves
It converts it into sugar in the fruit
Athel secretes salty water from leaf glands. The water evaporates, leaving a crust of crystals.
palm-plants-0155: Why is athel tamarisk often planted around farms in dry areas?
To extract oil from its many seeds
Athel has been used for decades as an agricultural windbreak and shade tree, especially in dry regions.
palm-plants-0156: What are the sand mounds that accumulate at the bases of gharqad shrubs (Nitraria retusa) in Moghra Oasis called?
Gharqad forms mounds called nebkhas, where windblown material accumulates at its base.
palm-plants-0157: The bitter apple plant (Citrullus colocynthis) and its leaves resemble what?
Bitter apple is a creeping plant resembling watermelon but bearing small, hard fruits with bitter pulp.
palm-plants-0158: What is the approximate diameter of a bitter apple fruit?
The bitter apple fruit is smooth and spherical, 5-10 cm in diameter, and extremely bitter.
palm-plants-0159: What do the branches of kaff Maryam (Anastatica hierochuntica) do when the plant dries out?
They fall off and are carried away by wind
They contract into a closed fist that protects the seeds
When dry, kaff Maryam's branches contract into a closed fist that protects the seeds, then open with moisture.
palm-plants-0160: Why is Anastatica not a true resurrection plant despite opening in water?
It opens in intense sunlight rather than rainwater
It grows only in humid regions
Its dead tissues do not become living and green again
Anastatica opens and closes with moisture, but its dead tissues do not revive or turn green, so it is not a true resurrection plant.
palm-plants-0161: White wormwood (Artemisia herba-alba) is called white grass because of what?
Its stems and leaves are white and woolly
Its roots are white as salt underground
Herba-alba means white grass because its stems and leaves are white and woolly.
palm-plants-0162: Awsaj (Lycium shawii) is a thorny desert shrub. What are its fruits like?
Large, black, and poisonous, eaten by no animal or bird
Yellow and winged, carried by the wind
Awsaj produces edible red berries the size of peas.
palm-plants-0163: Tarthuth (Cynomorium coccineum) is a red desert plant without chlorophyll. How does it obtain food?
It lives symbiotically with ants in nests beneath the sand
It is fully parasitic on the roots of a host plant
It absorbs dew from the air
It catches insects with sticky leaves
Tarthuth is a holoparasite, spending most of its life as an underground rhizome attached to the host plant's roots.
palm-plants-0164: Which insects pollinate the tarthuth inflorescence after being attracted by its smell?
Tarthuth is pollinated by flies attracted by its sweet, cabbage-like smell.
palm-plants-0165: What happens to the red tarthuth inflorescence after pollination?
It withers and disappears beneath the sand
After pollination, the tarthuth spike turns black.
palm-plants-0166: Desert truffles are not flowering plants. To which kingdom do they belong?
Desert truffles are fungi (of the genera Terfezia and Tirmania in the family Pezizaceae) that live symbiotically with the roots of plants such as rockroses.
palm-plants-0167: Desert truffles live symbiotically with the roots of plants from which genus?
Desert truffles form root symbioses with Helianthemum species and others.
palm-plants-0169: What were the white inflorescences of desert cotton (Aerva javanica) traditionally used for in the Arabian Peninsula?
The dense white inflorescences of Aerva javanica were harvested in the Arabian Peninsula to stuff pillows and saddle padding.
palm-plants-0170: A substance extracted from the leaves of senna (Senna italica) is used medically as what?
Senna species are grown for their leaves, which yield senna glycosides, the basis of laxatives.
palm-plants-0172: What color are the sweet fruits of the qardi shrub (Ochradenus baccatus)?
Qardi flowers are yellow, and its berries are white and sweet.
palm-plants-0174: The small, fleshy leaves of the haram shrub (Zygophyllum qatarense) primarily do what?
This shrub has small, succulent leaves that store water, with leaflets in pairs.
palm-plants-0175: Horwoodia dicksoniae is a wild herb in Kuwait and Najd. To whom does the species name dicksoniae refer?
The British botanist who first classified it
Violet Dickson, who collected its specimens
The species was named in honor of Violet Dickson for her work collecting specimens from the Arabian Peninsula.
palm-plants-0176: What distinguishes the leaves of the desert herb Horwoodia dicksoniae?
Horwoodia dicksoniae is an annual herb with aromatic leaves that grows in sands and wadis.
palm-plants-0177: Cistanche tubulosa is cultivated in the Taklamakan Desert and traditionally used for medicine and food in which country?
Cistanche tubulosa is cultivated in the Taklamakan Desert and traditionally used as medicine and food in China.
palm-plants-0178: Which is a notable characteristic of Rhazya stricta, an evergreen desert shrub in the Arabian Peninsula?
Rhazya stricta is a poisonous evergreen plant in the dogbane family.
palm-plants-0179: Which desert plant in southwestern Africa has only two leaves throughout its life, both of which keep growing?
Welwitschia has just two leaves emerging from a woody stem, which keep growing throughout its life.
palm-plants-0180: In which desert does Welwitschia mirabilis grow?
Welwitschia is endemic to the Namib Desert along the coasts of Angola and Namibia.
palm-plants-0181: How old are the oldest Welwitschia plants estimated to be?
Many Welwitschia plants are hundreds of years old, and the oldest may reach 2000 years.
palm-plants-0182: Welwitschia is classified as a gymnosperm. How does it reproduce?
Welwitschia is a gymnosperm that reproduces through cones, which secrete nectar attracting insects.
palm-plants-0183: How long does the giant saguaro cactus usually live?
The saguaro is slow-growing and usually lives 150 to 200 years.
palm-plants-0184: At approximately what age does a saguaro cactus grow its first side arm?
A saguaro usually develops its first side arm at 50-70 years old, though this may be delayed to about 100 years in dry sites. Some never grow arms.
palm-plants-0185: The saguaro cactus's scientific genus name, Carnegiea, honors whom?
The saguaro's scientific name, Carnegiea gigantea, honors Andrew Carnegie.
palm-plants-0186: The saguaro cactus flower is the official state wildflower of which US state?
The saguaro flower is Arizona's official state wildflower.
palm-plants-0187: The Joshua tree is a tree-like plant found mainly in which desert?
The Joshua tree (Yucca brevifolia) is largely restricted to the Mojave Desert.
palm-plants-0188: The American desert Joshua tree belongs to which genus?
The Joshua tree is Yucca brevifolia of the genus Yucca and is a monocotyledonous tree.
palm-plants-0189: The desert ocotillo looks dry and dead. When does it become covered with leaves?
Ocotillo renews its leaves after rain, quickly turning green and remaining so for weeks or months.
palm-plants-0191: Which birds pollinate ocotillo's scarlet flowers?
Ocotillo flowers are pollinated by hummingbirds and carpenter bees.
palm-plants-0192: The ring of creosote bush called King Clone in the Mojave Desert is estimated to be about how old?
The King Clone ring is among the oldest living organisms, estimated to be about 11,700 years old.
palm-plants-0193: What do residents of American deserts associate the scent of the creosote bush with?
The scent of resinous creosote leaves intensifies with rain, so people associate it with the smell of rain.
palm-plants-0194: Why is the American agave called the century plant?
It flowers once at the end of its long life
It lives exactly one hundred years, then reproduces by seed
It was discovered a century ago
It is called the century plant because it flowers once at the end of its life, then dies, although it usually lives only 10-30 years.
palm-plants-0195: How long does the American agave, or century plant, usually live?
Despite its name, the century plant usually lives only 10-30 years.
palm-plants-0196: What is the chemical nature of jojoba 'oil' extracted from its seeds?
Jojoba oil is actually a liquid wax ester extracted from the seeds and is valued in cosmetics manufacturing.
palm-plants-0197: What does the Greek name Lithops, for living stone plants, mean?
Lithops comes from the Greek lithos (stone) and ops (face), referring to their resemblance to pebbles.
palm-plants-0198: How do Lithops plants protect themselves from herbivores?
With sharp, poisonous spines covering their swollen leaves
By disguising themselves as small pebbles
Lithops avoid being eaten by camouflaging themselves as small stones.
palm-plants-0199: What is the function of the transparent window at the top of the soil-buried leaves of Lithops?
Protecting small seeds from intense sunlight
Letting light into the leaf for photosynthesis
Lithops leaves are mostly buried, with a transparent window at the top that lets light in for photosynthesis.
palm-plants-0200: What do the flowers of the desert plant Hoodia gordonii smell like?
Hoodia flowers smell like rotting meat and are pollinated by flies.
palm-plants-0201: What is the common name of Adenium obesum, a plant with a swollen stem that grows in the Arabian Peninsula and Africa?
Adenium obesum is known as desert rose and is a poisonous plant in the dogbane family.
palm-plants-0202: Where did the boojum tree (Fouquieria columnaris) in Baja California get its English name?
The sound of wind in its branches
The name of a local tribe
Godfrey Sykes named it Boojum after a word in Lewis Carroll's poem 'The Hunting of the Snark'.
palm-plants-0203: Approximately how many seeds can a Russian thistle (Salsola tragus) tumbleweed scatter as it rolls in the wind?
When the dry plant detaches and rolls in the wind, it can scatter about 200,000 seeds.
palm-plants-0204: In which desert does Selaginella lepidophylla grow, curling its stems into a ball when dry?
Selaginella lepidophylla is native to the Chihuahuan Desert in the United States and Mexico.
palm-plants-0205: What are desert plants that germinate, flower, and set seed quickly during short rainy periods called?
Desert ephemerals are adapted to take advantage of short periods of moisture in arid climates.
palm-plants-0207: The cactus genus Pereskia differs from most cacti in what way?
It has no spines at all
Pereskia is a cactus with conspicuous true leaves and non-succulent stems, unlike most cacti.
palm-plants-0208: In which type of soil does Syrian rue (Peganum harmala) usually grow?
Peganum harmala is a perennial herb that usually grows in saline soils in desert and Mediterranean regions.
palm-plants-0209: By which measure is California's General Sherman the world's largest living single-trunk tree?
General Sherman is a giant sequoia and the largest living single-trunk tree by volume.
palm-plants-0210: To which species does the famous General Sherman tree belong?
General Sherman is a giant sequoia, Sequoiadendron giganteum, in Sequoia National Park.
palm-plants-0211: Hyperion, the world's tallest known living tree, is of which species?
Hyperion is a coast redwood in California and the tallest known living tree.
palm-plants-0213: Methuselah, approximately 4858 years old and considered the oldest known non-clonal living organism, belongs to which species?
Methuselah is a Pinus longaeva pine, 4858 years old, and the oldest known non-clonal living organism.
palm-plants-0214: Pando in Utah is considered the world's heaviest living organism. What is it?
An entire forest of different oak species
A clonal aspen colony whose trunks share one root system
Pando is a quaking aspen colony with about 47 thousand genetically identical stems connected to one root system.
palm-plants-0215: Which plant bears the largest single flower on Earth?
Rafflesia arnoldii produces the largest single flower on Earth and is parasitic in the forests of Sumatra and Borneo.
palm-plants-0216: Why is the rafflesia called the corpse flower?
It is white like a shroud
It dies as soon as it opens
It grows in old cemeteries and around graves
It is called the corpse flower because it smells like decomposing meat.
palm-plants-0217: Rafflesia arnoldii is one of three national flowers of which country?
Rafflesia is one of Indonesia's three national flowers, along with white jasmine and the moon orchid.
palm-plants-0218: Titan arum (Amorphophallus titanum), with the world's largest unbranched inflorescence, is endemic to the forests of which island?
Amorphophallus titanum is endemic to rainforests on the Indonesian island of Sumatra.
palm-plants-0219: Where did titan arum first flower outside its native habitat in 1889 AD?
Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, in London
New York Botanical Garden in the Bronx
Titan arum first flowered in cultivation at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, in 1889 AD.
palm-plants-0220: Which aquatic plant genus includes the smallest flowering plants on Earth?
The genus Wolffia contains the smallest flowering plants, with grains resembling cornmeal floating on water.
palm-plants-0221: What do the tiny aquatic Wolffia plants lack?
Wolffia plants float without roots and have flowers that are rarely seen.
palm-plants-0222: How large is the diameter of the leaves of the giant Amazon water lily (Victoria amazonica)?
The floating leaves of Victoria amazonica can reach 3 meters in diameter.
palm-plants-0223: The giant water lily genus Victoria was named after whom or what?
John Lindley named the genus in 1837 after Queen Victoria, who had recently ascended the throne.
palm-plants-0224: To which plant family does bamboo belong?
Bamboo forms the subfamily Bambusoideae within the grass family, Poaceae.
palm-plants-0225: How tall can a giant bamboo stem of the species Dendrocalamus sinicus grow?
Dendrocalamus sinicus stems can reach 46 meters tall and 36 cm in diameter.
palm-plants-0226: How many species does the baobab genus (Adansonia) contain?
The genus Adansonia contains eight species native to Africa, Australia, and Madagascar.
palm-plants-0227: What is the baobab nicknamed because of its unusual shape?
The baobab is known as the upside-down tree because its bare branches resemble roots.
palm-plants-0228: Which French scientist is honored by the baobab genus name Adansonia?
The genus honors Michel Adanson, who gave the first detailed botanical description of the baobab.
palm-plants-0229: The main trunk of the Great Banyan near Kolkata, India, was removed in 1925 AD. How did it survive?
Through its many supporting trunks descending from its branches
By being grafted onto another nearby fig tree in the garden
By being moved into a greenhouse
After the main trunk was removed, the tree remained alive and continued spreading thanks to its many supporting trunks.
palm-plants-0230: What is the main product obtained from cork oak bark?
Cork oak is the main source of cork used in bottle stoppers and flooring.
palm-plants-0231: How often can cork oak bark be stripped without harming the tree?
Once the tree reaches 25 years old, its bark can be harvested every 9-12 years without harm.
palm-plants-0232: Where is the Brazilian rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis) originally native?
The rubber tree originates in the Amazon Basin and has been introduced across tropical regions.
palm-plants-0233: What is extracted from the rubber tree as the primary source of natural rubber?
The milky latex extracted from the tree is the primary source of natural rubber.
palm-plants-0234: Where was the olive tree first cultivated?
Olive was among the earliest domesticated fruit trees and was first cultivated in the eastern Mediterranean between 6000 and 4000 BC.
palm-plants-0235: The argan tree, from which argan oil is extracted, is mainly native to where?
The argan tree originates in Morocco's semi-desert Souss, Chiadma, and Haha regions.
palm-plants-0237: Approximately how long do argan trees live?
Argan trees reach 8-10 meters tall and live about 200 years.
palm-plants-0238: The henna plant's scientific name, Lawsonia inermis, honors whom?
Scottish physician Isaac Lawson, a friend of Linnaeus
An English traveler who visited India in the seventeenth century
The town of Lawson in Egypt
The species was named after Scottish physician Isaac Lawson, a friend of Linnaeus.
palm-plants-0239: In which temperature range does the henna shrub produce the most dye?
Henna produces the most dye when grown at temperatures between 35 and 45 degrees Celsius.
palm-plants-0240: How does valuable oud (agarwood) form in Aquilaria trees?
The wood is soaked in oil for a long time
Buried wood fossilizes for thousands of years until it becomes aromatic
The tree secretes a defensive resin after infection by a type of mold
It forms spontaneously in the roots
Oud forms in the heartwood of Aquilaria trees when they secrete defensive resin to resist a fungal infection.
palm-plants-0241: What is Aquilaria wood like before the fungal infection that turns it into oud?
Shiny red with a pungent smell like sandalwood
Before infection, the heartwood is light, pale, and almost odorless. It then becomes heavier, darkens, and becomes saturated with resin.
palm-plants-0242: Which country produces about 80% of the world's gum arabic?
Sudan produces eighty percent of the world's gum arabic from the hashab tree.
palm-plants-0243: What is the local Sudanese name for the finest gum arabic extracted from Senegalia senegal?
The finest gum arabic is known locally as hashab gum, in contrast to lower-quality talh gum.
palm-plants-0244: Approximately how much gum arabic does one hashab tree yield?
Gum is collected from cuts in the bark, and one tree yields 200-300 grams.
palm-plants-0245: What is the cross-sectional shape of a papyrus stem?
Papyrus produces green stems with triangular cross sections, emerging from thick woody rhizomes.
palm-plants-0246: Besides paper, what did the ancient Egyptians make from buoyant papyrus stems?
Papyrus stems are highly buoyant and can be used to make boats. The plant is also the source of papyrus paper.
palm-plants-0247: What do Mimosa pudica leaves do when touched?
The sensitive plant's leaves quickly fold and droop when touched, then reopen after a few minutes.
palm-plants-0248: What does the Latin word pudica in the scientific name Mimosa pudica mean?
Pudica is Latin for shy or shrinking, referring to its contraction when touched.
palm-plants-0249: Where is the insect-eating Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) originally native?
The marshes of North and South Carolina
The Himalayan Mountains of northern India and Nepal
The Venus flytrap is an insect-eating plant native to wetlands in North and South Carolina.
palm-plants-0250: When does a Venus flytrap close on an insect?
At the first touch of any of its tiny sensitive hairs
When its sensitive hairs are touched a second time within about twenty seconds
The first touch primes the trap. It closes only after a second touch within about 20 seconds, to the same hair or another one.
palm-plants-0251: Why are insect-eating Nepenthes plants called monkey cups?
They grow on tall trees inhabited by monkeys
Monkeys were thought to drink rainwater from their pitchers
They were called monkey cups because monkeys were thought to drink rainwater from their pitchers.
palm-plants-0252: The parasitic dodder plant (Cuscuta) obtains food from its host through what?
Deep soil roots that absorb water and minerals
Haustoria that penetrate the host's tissues
Dodder has little chlorophyll and extracts food and water from its host's vascular system through haustoria.
palm-plants-0253: How do dodder seedlings locate a host plant?
By waiting for birds to carry and drop their seeds on it
By sensing volatile organic compounds from it
By growing randomly until they touch it
Dodder seedlings find their hosts by sensing volatile organic compounds.
palm-plants-0254: Why is ginkgo (Ginkgo biloba) described as a living fossil?
It is the last living species of an order that appeared over 290 million years ago
It fossilizes immediately after death and remains standing for millions of years
It was discovered inside an ancient cave
Ginkgo is the last living species of the order Ginkgoales, which appeared over 290 million years ago.
palm-plants-0255: Which exceptional event did some ginkgo trees in Japan survive?
The great Tokyo fires following the Kanto earthquake
Some ginkgo trees survived extreme events such as the atomic bombing of Hiroshima.
palm-plants-0257: Which country supplies about 95% or more of commercial balsa wood?
Balsa is grown in dense stands, and Ecuador supplies 95% or more of commercial balsa.
palm-plants-0258: The hard, dense lignum vitae tree (Guaiacum) is the national tree of which country?
Lignum vitae is the national tree of the Bahamas and the national flower of Jamaica.
palm-plants-0260: How did desert dwellers describe arfaj in terms of its uses?
Camels do not graze it and it is unsuitable as fuel
One of the best desert plants for camels and best fuels
Useful only as an eye medicine
One of the worst and most poisonous plants for livestock
Arfaj is among the best desert plants as camel forage and firewood. Excessive cutting by people made it scarce.
palm-plants-0261: To which plant family does the ramth genus (Haloxylon) belong?
Haloxylon belongs to the amaranth family, and its species include Persian saxaul (ghada).
palm-plants-0262: What does the common expression 'embers of ghada' describe?
The smell of the first rain
The expression 'embers of ghada' commonly describes intense heat because ghada embers burn fiercely and last a long time.
palm-plants-0264: To which family does the arta genus (Calligonum) belong?
Calligonum is a genus in the knotweed family containing about 80 shrub species.
palm-plants-0265: The grass genus Panicum belongs to the grass family. Which are among its most important cultivated species?
Panicum contains about 450 species, the most important of which include some millets.
palm-plants-0266: What is the red head of the tarthuth plant called, as in the expression 'as red as ...'?
The head of tarthuth is called nak'ah. An Arab expression for a very red-faced man is 'as red as a nak'ah'.
palm-plants-0267: Why did Bedouins traditionally gather tarthuth for trade?
To make ropes from its fibers
To use it as palm fertilizer
Bedouins gathered tarthuth to extract red dye and used it to mark their livestock.
palm-plants-0268: What did Arabs call bitter apple seeds eaten after soaking to remove their bitterness?
Arabs ate bitter apple seeds and called them habid after soaking them in water and salt until their bitterness disappeared.
palm-plants-0269: To which plant family does bitter apple belong?
Bitter apple is a creeping annual species in the genus Citrullus of the gourd family.
palm-plants-0270: Tamarisk is mentioned once in the Quran. In which surah?
Tamarisk appears in verse 16 of Surah Saba: «ذَوَاتَيْ أُكُلٍ خَمْطٍ وَأَثْلٍ وَشَيْءٍ مِنْ سِدْرٍ قَلِيلٍ» [of bitter fruit, tamarisks and something of sparse lote trees.] (QuranEnc, 34:16).
palm-plants-0271: Why were athel tamarisk stems used in shipbuilding?
They are flexible and bend easily without breaking in the waves
Their wood is hard and they grow near seas and wadis
They are hollow and float on water
Athel stems yield hardwood and are used to make ships, especially because they grow near seas and valleys.
palm-plants-0272: What is the arak tree fruit eaten by people and birds called?
Arak fruit is called barir, and its ripe fruit is called kabath. It is red, then turns black as it ripens.
palm-plants-0273: What effect does livestock grazing on arak have on its milk?
It gives it a pleasant scent
Camels graze on arak branches, and the milk of livestock that eat it acquires a pleasant scent.
palm-plants-0274: To which family does the rockrose genus (Helianthemum) belong?
Helianthemum is a plant genus in the family Cistaceae and contains 73 accepted species.
palm-plants-0275: At approximately what depth were American mesquite roots (of the genus Prosopis) found in copper mines near Tucson, USA?
American mesquite roots were found at a depth of about 53 meters in copper mines near Tucson.
palm-plants-0276: What do residents of some Central and South American countries make from ground mesquite pods (of the genus Prosopis)?
In some American countries, pods of American mesquite species are ground and made into sweet-tasting bread.
palm-plants-0277: To which plant family does sidr belong?
Sidr, Ziziphus spina-christi, belongs to the genus Ziziphus in the buckthorn family, which also includes jujube.
palm-plants-0278: Which familiar fruit tree belongs to the same genus, Ziziphus, as sidr?
The genus Ziziphus includes sidr and jujube.
palm-plants-0279: What distinguishes the two thorns at the base of a sidr leaf?
Both are long, straight, and point upward
There are no thorns at the leaf base
One is straight and the other curved
Sidr has two stipular thorns, one straight and the other curved.
palm-plants-0281: To which plant family does the wormwood genus belong?
Wormwood is a genus of wild perennial herbaceous plants in the aster family.
palm-plants-0283: What does the scientific term halophyte mean in botany?
A plant that feeds on insects
A plant that lives in shade
A halophyte is a salt-tolerant plant. The word comes from the Greek halas (salt) and phyton (plant).
palm-plants-0284: Approximately what percentage of all plant species are salt-tolerant plants (halophytes)?
Salt-tolerant plants are uncommon, perhaps only 2% of plant species.
palm-plants-0285: In desert plants with crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM), when do stomata open to take in carbon dioxide?
In CAM plants, stomata remain closed during the day to reduce transpiration and open at night to collect carbon dioxide.
palm-plants-0286: Which structure is characteristic of all cacti and produces spines and flowers?
All cacti have areoles, highly reduced branches from which spines and flowers emerge.
palm-plants-0287: All cacti originate in the Americas except one species also found in Africa and Sri Lanka. Which is it?
Cacti are native to the Americas except Rhipsalis baccifera, which is also found in Africa and Sri Lanka.
palm-plants-0288: When was prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) domesticated in central Mexico?
Prickly pear was domesticated in central Mexico 8000-9000 years ago.
palm-plants-0289: What are the tiny hairlike spines on prickly pear pads that easily lodge in the skin called?
Prickly pear has large fixed spines and tiny hairlike spines called glochids that lodge in the skin.
palm-plants-0290: According to studies, where did Aloe vera originate?
Aloe vera originated in the Arabian Peninsula and is genetically close to Aloe perryi, endemic to Yemen.
palm-plants-0293: Which common nickname of the African baobab refers to monkeys?
Common baobab names include monkey bread tree and upside-down tree.
palm-plants-0294: What is the world's tallest flowering plant?
Eucalyptus regnans is the tallest flowering plant. Its tallest living specimen, Centurion, is about 100 meters tall in Tasmania.
palm-plants-0295: What are the oldest known lotus seeds that successfully germinated?
1300-year-old seeds from a dry lake bed in China
10-thousand-year-old seeds from pharaonic tombs in Egypt
The oldest recorded lotus germination was from 1300-year-old seeds from a dry lake bed in northeastern China.
palm-plants-0296: The Indian lotus (Nelumbo nucifera) is the national flower of which country?
The lotus is India's national flower and, unofficially, Vietnam's national flower.
palm-plants-0297: Where does the name of the insect-eating sundew (Drosera) come from?
Its growth in dry places exposed to sunlight
Drops of sticky material that shine like dew
Drosera comes from the Greek drosos, meaning dew, referring to the shiny mucilage drops on its glandular hairs.
palm-plants-0298: On which continent does the insect-eating sundew (Drosera) not grow?
Drosera species occur on every continent except Antarctica.
palm-plants-0299: What is the function of the respiratory aerial roots of gray mangrove (Avicennia marina)?
Taking oxygen from the air to aerate roots in oxygen-poor mud
Absorbing salt from humid air above the sea
Mangrove has respiratory aerial roots projecting about 20 cm above the mud. They take oxygen from the air to aerate its roots in oxygen-poor mud.
palm-plants-0300: What color is the underside of gray mangrove (Avicennia marina) leaves?
Silvery white or gray with fine hairs
Mangrove leaves are glossy green above and silvery white or gray with fine hairs beneath.
palm-plants-0301: Why is the sycamore fig (Ficus sycomorus) called the mulberry fig?
It always grows beside mulberry trees in orchards
Its fruits are black like mulberries
It is called the mulberry fig because its leaves resemble mulberry leaves.
palm-plants-0302: Why is Moringa oleifera called the drumstick tree?
The sound of its branches in the wind
Its lightweight wood is used to make drums in India
It is called the drumstick tree because of its long, thin, triangular seed pods.
palm-plants-0303: How does a strangler fig begin life before wrapping around its host tree?
It germinates in water and then climbs
Its seed germinates in crevices high in another tree
It sprouts from the host tree's root
It germinates in soil in the tree's shade, then wraps around its trunk
Birds carry strangler fig seeds, which germinate in crevices high in trees. Their roots then descend and surround the host.
palm-plants-0304: What is jute nicknamed in Bangladesh because of its value and color?
Jute is called golden fiber in Bangladesh because of its color and monetary value.
palm-plants-0305: From which language did European botanists borrow the name luffa in the seventeenth century?
European botanists borrowed the name luffa from the Arabic name luf.
palm-plants-0307: From which part of the indigo plant (Indigofera tinctoria) is blue dye extracted?
Indigo dye is extracted from the plant's leaves by soaking them in water and fermenting them.
palm-plants-0308: What is the nutritional mode of white sandalwood (Santalum album)?
It catches insects with its leaves
It lives on bare rocks without true roots
It partially parasitizes other trees' roots
Sandalwood parasitizes other trees' roots through haustoria on its own roots, without greatly harming them.
palm-plants-0309: The forests of which country contain about half of the world's naturally occurring teak trees?
Myanmar's teak forests account for about half of the world's naturally occurring teak.
palm-plants-0311: How many species does Phoenix, the genus to which the date palm belongs, contain?
The genus Phoenix contains 14 palm species, ranging from the Canary Islands in the west to southern China and Malaysia in the east.
palm-plants-0312: How does the palm genus Phoenix differ from most members of its subfamily?
Its leaves are feather-shaped rather than fan-shaped
Phoenix is unusual in its subfamily, Coryphoideae, because its leaves are pinnate rather than palmate and fan-shaped.
palm-plants-0314: The Cretan date palm was named theophrasti in honor of Theophrastus, who is known as what?
The name was chosen because Theophrastus, the father of botany, described palm species including a palm from Crete.
palm-plants-0316: The European fan palm (Chamaerops humilis) is known for what?
Being among the most cold-tolerant palms
Chamaerops humilis is among the most cold-tolerant palm species and is grown in temperate regions.
palm-plants-0317: What does the Latin name flabellifer in the palmyra palm's name (Borassus flabellifer) mean?
Flabellifer is Latin for fan-bearing, referring to its large fan-shaped leaves.
palm-plants-0318: The palmyra palm genus name Borassus derives from a Greek word meaning what?
The Greek borassos means the immature date palm inflorescence, which the palmyra inflorescence resembles.
palm-plants-0319: The leaves of which two palms were used to make palm-leaf manuscripts in South Asia?
Dried and smoke-treated palmyra and talipot leaves have been used as writing material since the fifth century BC.
palm-plants-0320: How was writing inscribed on palm-leaf manuscripts?
With a knife stylus that cut the letters, followed by rubbing pigments over them
Directly with a quill and ink
Letters were cut into the treated leaves with a knife stylus, then pigments were applied and wiped off, leaving ink in the grooves.
horses-camels-falcons-0001: What do Arabic language scholars call a camel calf that has entered its second year?
In Al-Tha'alibi's sequence of camel ages, a camel in its second year is ibn makhad.
horses-camels-falcons-0002: A camel calf has reached its third year. By which name is it known?
A camel in its third year is ibn labun.
horses-camels-falcons-0003: Why is a camel in its fourth year called hiqq?
It is entitled to graze alone
It has become fit to carry loads
Its mother is entitled to be milked
Its milk teeth are due to fall out
Al-Tha'alibi said that when a camel is in its fourth year and has become fit to carry loads, it is hiqq.
horses-camels-falcons-0004: What is a camel in its fifth year called in the age sequence?
In its fifth year it is jadha', followed by thani in its sixth.
horses-camels-falcons-0005: Which name applies to a camel in its sixth year?
In its sixth year, when it sheds its central incisor, it is thani.
horses-camels-falcons-0006: What is a camel that has entered its seventh year called?
In its seventh year, when it sheds its lateral incisor, it is raba'.
horses-camels-falcons-0007: What is a camel in its eighth year called?
In Al-Tha'alibi's sequence, a camel in its eighth year is sadis.
horses-camels-falcons-0008: When a camel's canine tooth erupts in its ninth year, what do Arabs call it?
In its ninth year, when its canine tooth erupts, it is bazil.
horses-camels-falcons-0009: What is a camel in its tenth year called?
In its tenth year it is mukhlif, followed by mukhlif of one year, then mukhlif of two years.
horses-camels-falcons-0010: What is a camel calf called after it completes one year and is separated from its mother?
After it completes one year and is separated from its mother, it is fasil.
horses-camels-falcons-0011: What is a camel calf called at the moment its mother gives birth to it?
Al-Tha'alibi said that a camel calf at birth is salil, then saqb and huwar.
horses-camels-falcons-0012: A camel described as awd is one that is what?
Nearly senile but still has some strength
A camel nearing senility but retaining some strength is awd.
horses-camels-falcons-0013: What is a black camel whose blackness is mixed with white like ramth smoke called?
In camel colors, a black camel mixed with white like ramth smoke is awraq.
horses-camels-falcons-0014: What is a very black camel called in camel color terminology?
A camel that is intensely black is jawn.
horses-camels-falcons-0015: When Arabs describe a camel as adam, what do they mean?
In camel colors, a white camel is adam. Udm refers to white camels, unlike the term as applied to people.
horses-camels-falcons-0016: What is a white camel with a reddish tinge called?
If redness is mixed into its whiteness, it is ashab.
horses-camels-falcons-0017: If a camel's whiteness has a blond tinge, what do Arabs call it?
If a blond tinge is mixed into its whiteness, it is a'yas, from which the term 'is derives.
horses-camels-falcons-0018: What is a red camel whose redness is mixed with black called?
A camel with unmixed redness is ahmar, but if black is mixed with it, it is armak.
horses-camels-falcons-0019: What is a group of three to ten camels called?
A group of between three and ten camels is dhawd.
horses-camels-falcons-0020: What is a group of ten to forty camels called?
A group of between ten and forty camels is sirmah.
horses-camels-falcons-0022: Hunaydah is a name for how many camels?
When camels reach one hundred, they are hunaydah.
horses-camels-falcons-0023: What do Arabs call a group of one thousand camels?
When camels reach one thousand, they are khatar.
horses-camels-falcons-0024: In Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl's sequence of camel gaits, which is the first degree?
The first camel gait is dabib, then tazayyud, then dhamil, then rasim.
horses-camels-falcons-0025: Which is the final and fastest camel gait in Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl's sequence?
Al-Nadr's sequence ends with ratakan, then ijmar, then irqal.
horses-camels-falcons-0026: What is dhamil in camel gaits?
horses-camels-falcons-0027: What does wakhdan describe in a female camel's gait?
Moving in every direction out of liveliness
Throwing its legs forward like an ostrich's walk
Twisting right and left as it walks
Wakhdan is throwing the legs forward like an ostrich's walk.
horses-camels-falcons-0028: What is it called when camels visit water one day and skip the next?
Going to water every other day is ghibb.
horses-camels-falcons-0029: If camels visit water once every day, what is this watering schedule called?
Visiting water once every day is zahirah.
horses-camels-falcons-0030: The Arabic verb ahdara describes a horse running. Which verb describes a camel running?
In the classification of running: ahdara for a horse, arqala for a camel, khaffa for an ostrich, asala for a wolf, and maza'a for a gazelle.
horses-camels-falcons-0031: Which Arabic verb specifically describes a camel sitting down?
A person jalasa, a camel baraka, a sheep rabadat, a beast of prey aq'a, and a bird jathama.
horses-camels-falcons-0032: If a female camel produces a sound from her throat without opening her mouth, which Arabic verb describes it?
Al-Tha'alibi said that if a female camel produces a sound from her throat without opening her mouth, it is said arzamat.
horses-camels-falcons-0033: If a female camel cries with longing after her calf, what is she said to do?
If she cries with longing after her calf, it is said hannat. If she prolongs the longing cry, it is said sajarat.
horses-camels-falcons-0034: What is the sound of a male camel called when he voices it clearly?
If the male camel voices its roar clearly, it is said hadara. If his voice becomes clear, it is said qarqara.
horses-camels-falcons-0035: In the classification of different sounds, sarif is the sound of what?
In his list of sounds, Al-Tha'alibi mentions the sarif of a camel's canine tooth.
horses-camels-falcons-0036: In Arabic usage, 'matiyya' is a general term for:
Matiyya is a general term for any camel used for riding.
horses-camels-falcons-0037: What is a she-camel selected as a mount for her excellence, sound build, and fine appearance called?
A she-camel selected as a mount for her excellence and sound build is a rahila. The hadith says: «الناس كإبل مئة لا تكاد تجد فيها راحلة» [People.].
horses-camels-falcons-0038: A camel used by its owner to carry loads is a zamila.
horses-camels-falcons-0039: A she-camel is called 'ushara' when her pregnancy reaches:

At ten months of pregnancy, a she-camel is called ushara, as in: «وإذا العشار عُطّلت» [And when full-term she-camels[1865] are neglected]. Quran 81:4 (QuranEnc) [1865] Those ten months pregnant and nearing delivery. This verse alludes to distraction from the most valued of possessions.
horses-camels-falcons-0040: What term describes a she-camel whose calf walks alongside her?
When her calf walks alongside her, she is called mutfil.
horses-camels-falcons-0041: Has lost her calf through death or slaughter
Sniffs a calf but does not give it milk
Shows affection and care for another camel's calf
If she takes affectionately to another camel's calf and cares for it, she is ra'im.
horses-camels-falcons-0042: What is a camel used to draw water called?
A camel used to draw water is a nadih.
horses-camels-falcons-0043: What is a male camel selected from the herd for breeding called?
A male selected to mate with the she-camels is a qari'.
horses-camels-falcons-0044: A tendency to become thirsty quickly
A she-camel with a tall hump is kawma.
horses-camels-falcons-0045: What is the item placed in a camel's nose called when made of hair?
The item in a camel's nose is a khishash if wooden, a bura if brass, and a khizama if made of hair.
horses-camels-falcons-0046: What is the rope used to bind a camel's knee called?
The iqal is the rope used to bind a camel's knee.
horses-camels-falcons-0047: The gharz of a camel corresponds to which item for a horse?
By analogy, a camel's gharz corresponds to a horse's stirrup.
horses-camels-falcons-0048: A camel's 'mansim' corresponds to which human feature?
A camel's mansim corresponds to a human nail, a hoofed animal's hoof, and a bird's claw.
horses-camels-falcons-0049: A camel's 'lugham' is comparable to which human secretion?
A camel's lugham is comparable to human saliva.
horses-camels-falcons-0050: According to al-Mubarrad, a 'qalus' among camels corresponds to:
According to al-Mubarrad, a bakr corresponds to a young man, a qalus to a young woman, and a jamal to an adult man.
horses-camels-falcons-0051: What is a young horse called when it completes one year?
A horse is called muhr at birth, then filw; after completing a year, it is hawli.
horses-camels-falcons-0052: After being called muhr at birth, what is a young horse called before completing its first year?
At birth it is a muhr, then a filw.
horses-camels-falcons-0057: A 'qarih' among horses corresponds to which camel age term?
By analogy, a qarih horse corresponds to a bazil camel.
horses-camels-falcons-0058: What is a white mark on a horse's forehead the size of a dirham called?
A dirham-sized white forehead mark is a qurha; when larger, it is a ghurra.
horses-camels-falcons-0059: What is a white mark on a horse's forehead called when it exceeds the size of a dirham?
A dirham-sized mark is a qurha; when larger, it is a ghurra.
horses-camels-falcons-0060: What is a white facial mark covering the nose but not reaching the lip called?
When it covers the nose without reaching the lip, it is a shimrakh.
horses-camels-falcons-0061: What is a white mark filling a horse's forehead without reaching its eyes called?
When it fills the forehead without reaching the eyes, it is a shadikha.
horses-camels-falcons-0062: What describes a horse with white over its entire face but dark areas around its eyes?
If the white mark covers its whole face while its eyes remain surrounded by dark areas, it is mubarqa'.
horses-camels-falcons-0063: What is a horse with white on its upper lip called?
White on the upper lip makes it artham; on the lower lip, almaz.
horses-camels-falcons-0064: What is a horse called when its white facial mark extends down one side to a cheek?
If its facial mark extends down one side to a cheek, it is latim.
horses-camels-falcons-0065: When can a horse properly be described as 'muhajjal'?
When white occurs only on its forehead
When white occurs on all four legs or three of them
When white occurs on just one foreleg
Al-Tha'alibi said a horse is called muhajjal only when white occurs on all four legs or on three of them.
horses-camels-falcons-0066: What describes a horse with white on its forelegs but not its hind legs?
If white occurs on its forelegs but not its hind legs, it is a'sam.
horses-camels-falcons-0067: Can only be ridden with someone walking beside it
Has white on one hind leg
If white occurs on one hind leg, it is arjal.
horses-camels-falcons-0068: What is 'shikal', a marking the Arabs disliked in horses?
A facial mark leaning toward one cheek
White on a foreleg and the opposite hind leg
White on a foreleg and the opposite hind leg is shikal, which was disliked.
horses-camels-falcons-0069: What describes a horse with a white tail?
A horse with a white tail is ash'al.
horses-camels-falcons-0073: What describes a gray horse whose white color is clear and free of black?
When its white color is clear and free of black, it is ashhab qirtasi.
horses-camels-falcons-0074: What is a horse whose red color is mixed with black called?
When its red color is mixed with black, it is kumayt.
horses-camels-falcons-0075: What is a red horse with no black mixed into its red color called?
If it is red without black, it is ashqar.
horses-camels-falcons-0076: What horse color lies between ashqar and kumayt?
A horse whose color lies between ashqar and kumayt is ward.
horses-camels-falcons-0077: What describes a horse with white spots and spots of another color?
A horse with white spots and spots of any other color is abrash.
horses-camels-falcons-0078: In al-Tha'alibi's ordering of a horse's running gaits, which comes first?
The order is khabab, taqrib, imjaj, ihdar, irkha', ihdhab, then ihmaj.
horses-camels-falcons-0079: What is the highest stage of a horse's running, when it exerts its utmost effort, called?
Ihmaj is when a horse exerts its utmost running effort; it is the final stage in the sequence.
horses-camels-falcons-0080: In a horse's gait, 'taqrib' means that it:
Raises and sets down both forelegs together
Taqrib means a horse raises and sets down both forelegs together.
horses-camels-falcons-0081: What does 'hamlaja' mean in an animal's gait?
Taking wide strides and extending its run
Hamlaja means a horse takes quick, closely spaced steps.
horses-camels-falcons-0082: In a horse's running, 'anaq' means that it:
Turns its hoof toward its upper foreleg
Pounds the ground with its hooves
Spaces its strides widely and extends its run
Anaq means a horse spaces its strides widely and extends its run.
horses-camels-falcons-0083: In the terminology of leaping, which verb is used for a horse's leap?
A human tafara, a horse dabara, a camel wathaba, a boy qafaza, and a sparrow naqaza.
horses-camels-falcons-0084: The sound of its breathing when running
Its sound when asking for fodder

Dabh is the sound of a horse's breathing when running. It appears in the Quran: «والعاديات ضبحًا» [By the racers, panting,[1967]]. Quran 100:1 (QuranEnc) [1967] i.e., the horses bearing riders as they race to attack the enemy.
horses-camels-falcons-0085: What is the sound a horse makes when asking for fodder or greeting its owner affectionately called?
Hamhama is a horse's sound when asking for fodder or greeting its owner affectionately.
horses-camels-falcons-0086: What describes a horse with no mixed-breed ancestry?
According to al-Kisa'i, a horse with no mixed-breed ancestry is mu'rib.
horses-camels-falcons-0087: What is a horse called when it is tethered close to its owner and honored for its value and excellence?
According to Abu Ubayda, a horse tethered close by and honored for its value and excellence is muqarrab.
horses-camels-falcons-0088: What describes a horse with a fully developed, beautiful build?
A horse with a fully developed, beautiful build is mutahham.
horses-camels-falcons-0089: A long neck and long legs
A horse with a long neck and long legs is salhab.
horses-camels-falcons-0090: What is a horse with a long tail called?
A horse with a long tail is dhayyal or rifall.
horses-camels-falcons-0091: What describes a horse whose hooves do not become sore from much walking?
A horse whose hooves do not become sore is rajil.
horses-camels-falcons-0092: Calling a fast-running horse 'ya'bub' compares it to:
A fast-running horse is ya'bub, compared to a ya'bub, a fast-flowing stream.
horses-camels-falcons-0093: According to al-Tha'alibi, who first described a horse with tireless running as 'bahr' (sea)?
The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him
Al-Tha'alibi said a horse with tireless running is bahr, and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, first used this description for a horse he rode.
horses-camels-falcons-0094: Which horse of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recorded in biographies bears a name describing a light, fast horse likened to flowing water?
In Fiqh al-Lugha, al-Tha'alibi calls a light, fast horse sakb, likening it to pouring water. Al-Sakb is one of the Prophet's horses named in biographies.
horses-camels-falcons-0095: What is a horse that stops walking and refuses to move even when struck called?
A horse that stops and refuses to move even when struck is harun.
horses-camels-falcons-0096: What is a horse that refuses to let anyone mount it called?
A horse that refuses to be mounted is shamus.
horses-camels-falcons-0097: What describes a horse that kicks with its hind legs?
A horse that kicks with its hind legs is ramuh.
horses-camels-falcons-0098: 'Jamuh' has two meanings when describing a horse; one is a fault. What is its favorable meaning?
The second meaning of jamuh is lively and fast, a favorable description, as in Imru' al-Qays's phrase 'jamuhan maruhan'.
horses-camels-falcons-0099: What is a horse whose thick forelock covers its eyes called?
A horse with a forelock so thick it covers the eyes is aghamm; one with a sparse forelock is asfa.
horses-camels-falcons-0100: According to al-Jahiz, how many leading racehorses did the Arabs recognize?
Al-Jahiz said the Arabs recognized eight leading racehorses and gave no share to those beyond them.
horses-camels-falcons-0101: What is the horse finishing second behind the winner in a race called?
The leading horses are ordered: al-Sabiq, then al-Musalli, then al-Muqaffi, then al-Tali.
horses-camels-falcons-0102: The 'sukayt' in a race is the horse that:
The sukayt is the last horse to arrive at the end of the race.
horses-camels-falcons-0103: What does 'kura'' refer to in the expression 'al-kura' wa-al-silah'?
Al-Tha'alibi states that kura' refers to horses.
horses-camels-falcons-0104: A camel's 'khila'' corresponds to which fault in a horse?
By analogy, a camel's khila' corresponds to a horse's balking.
horses-camels-falcons-0105: The Arabian camel's scientific name 'dromedarius' comes from a Greek word meaning:
The Greek word dromas means running or runner, used in 'running camel' to denote the Arabian camel.
horses-camels-falcons-0106: Which of the three camel species is tallest at the shoulder?
The Arabian camel is tallest of the three species. The Bactrian is heaviest but shorter at the shoulder.
horses-camels-falcons-0107: The two-humped camel is called Bactrian after:
The Bakhtiari tribe in the Zagros Mountains
The Bakhtaran desert extending across northern India
The city of Bukhara in Transoxiana
The historical region of Bactria in Central Asia
The Bactrian camel's name comes from the ancient historical region of Bactria in Central Asia.
horses-camels-falcons-0108: What is the relationship between the wild two-humped camel and the domestic Bactrian camel?
The wild camel is a Bactrian breed that became feral
The wild camel is the ancestor from which the Bactrian was domesticated
The wild camel is a separate species, not the domestic camel's ancestor
The wild camel is a hybrid of Bactrian and Arabian camels
Genetic studies show the wild camel is a separate species that diverged from the Bactrian about a million years ago, rather than its ancestor.
horses-camels-falcons-0109: What rare ability among large mammals distinguishes the wild two-humped camel?
Living on water saltier than seawater
Going without sleep for weeks without harm
The wild camel can live on water saltier than seawater, which even the domestic Bactrian cannot tolerate.
horses-camels-falcons-0111: What is the swollen pink organ a male Arabian camel protrudes from its mouth during mating season called?
The male Arabian camel has a throat organ called the shiqshiqa, which protrudes from its mouth during mating season like a swollen pink tongue.
horses-camels-falcons-0112: How do camel red blood cells differ from those of most mammals?
They are oval rather than round
They retain a nucleus throughout their lifespan
Camel red blood cells are oval, facilitating flow during dehydration and preventing rupture when large amounts of water are drunk.
horses-camels-falcons-0113: Which organ is absent in both Arabian camels and horses?
The Arabian camel has no gallbladder, as is also the case with horses.
horses-camels-falcons-0114: How many permanent teeth does an Arabian camel have after losing its milk teeth?
An Arabian camel has 22 milk teeth, replaced by 34 permanent teeth.
horses-camels-falcons-0115: The 'rete mirabile' in a camel's head is a network of arteries and veins whose function is:
Warming the eyes on cold desert nights
Cooling blood flowing to the brain
The rete mirabile uses countercurrent blood flow to cool blood flowing to the brain and regulate its temperature.
horses-camels-falcons-0116: How does the Arabian camel conserve water that would otherwise be lost through daytime sweating?
It closes all its skin pores
It allows its body temperature to rise during the day
It stores sweat in its hump
It sleeps throughout the hot hours until sunset
The camel reduces sweating by allowing its body temperature to fluctuate during the day from about 34 to 41 degrees Celsius.
horses-camels-falcons-0117: What is the maximum amount of water an Arabian camel can drink in one session?
According to the FAO, a thirsty camel can drink quickly in hot weather, consuming up to about 200 liters in one session.
horses-camels-falcons-0118: What proportion of its body water can an Arabian camel withstand losing, a level fatal to most mammals?
An Arabian camel can withstand losing more than 30% of its body water, something most mammals cannot do.
horses-camels-falcons-0119: How does a camel's way of walking resemble a giraffe's?
It advances both hind legs before its forelegs
