It jumps with all four legs together
It moves both legs on one side together
It walks on the tips of its hooves
Like the giraffe, the Arabian camel moves both legs on the same side of its body at once.
horses-camels-falcons-0120: What material actually makes up a camel's hump?
Fat held together by fibrous tissue
A hollow cartilaginous bone filled with air
The hump consists of fat held together by fibrous tissue; it is not a water store as commonly claimed.
horses-camels-falcons-0121: Which continent has more than 80% of the world's Arabian camels?
Africa has the vast majority of the world's Arabian camels, mainly in the Horn of Africa.
horses-camels-falcons-0122: In the Gulf region, camels are locally classified as majahim, humr, sufr, zurq, and shu'l based on:
Gulf camels are divided into breeds including majahim, humr, sufr, zurq, and shu'l according to coat color.
horses-camels-falcons-0123: What are riding camels in the Sahara locally known as?
Riding camels are called dhalul in Arabia, hajin in Egypt, and mahari in the Sahara.
horses-camels-falcons-0124: Which country has the world's largest herds of feral camels?
Australia has the most feral camels, descended from camels brought for transport in the nineteenth century.
horses-camels-falcons-0125: Australia's famous train 'The Ghan' was named in honor of:
An English explorer who crossed Australia's great desert
The Afghan cameleers who pioneered the route
The Ghan is short for 'The Afghan Express'. Its emblem is a camel and rider, honoring the Afghan cameleers who opened the route.
horses-camels-falcons-0126: At which battle was the first military use of camels in history recorded?
The first recorded use of camels as military animals was by the Qedarite king Gindibu, with a thousand camels at Qarqar in 853 BC.
horses-camels-falcons-0127: Why did Cyrus place camels in front of the Lydian cavalry at the Battle of Thymbra?
Their horses were frightened by the camels' smell and appearance
Camels are faster than horses on plains
Camels carry heavier armor and withstand spear thrusts
Cyrus knew Lydian horses feared camels, so he put the baggage camels in front, where their smell and appearance frightened the Lydian cavalry.
horses-camels-falcons-0128: A camel-herding tribe in northern Sudan and Chad
Caravan traders between Egypt and the Levant
French camel-riding units in the Sahara
In 1912, France established camel-riding units known as Meharists within the Army of Africa in the Sahara.
horses-camels-falcons-0129: How many living species belong to the camel family?
The camel family includes seven species: three true camels and four South American camelids.
horses-camels-falcons-0130: What does 'Tylopoda', the name of the suborder containing camelids, mean?
Tylopoda is a Greek word meaning 'padded foot', referring to camelids' foot pads.
horses-camels-falcons-0131: How many chambers does a camelid's stomach have?
Camelids have three stomach chambers, rather than four as in ruminants.
horses-camels-falcons-0132: They form only in the hump
They consist only of heavy chains
They consist only of light chains
Camelids have unique antibodies lacking light chains, which are being studied for drug development.
horses-camels-falcons-0133: Genetic studies show that the domesticated llama descends from:
DNA analysis confirmed the guanaco as the llama's wild ancestor and the vicuna as the alpaca's ancestor.
horses-camels-falcons-0134: Which wild camelid is considered the ancestor of the domesticated alpaca?
Genetic studies indicate the vicuna is the alpaca's wild ancestor.
horses-camels-falcons-0135: Which camelid is Peru's national animal and appears on its coat of arms?
The vicuna is Peru's national animal and appears on its coat of arms. Wearing its wool was once restricted to Inca royalty.
horses-camels-falcons-0136: Why is vicuna wool so expensive?
It is shorn once every ten years in a royal ceremony
Vicunas are wild and shorn only every two or three years
Its wool is gathered from its feathers
Vicuna wool is extremely fine and scarce. Wild animals are gathered for shearing and then released, and are shorn only every two or three years.
horses-camels-falcons-0137: Where did the earliest camelids originate before moving to Asia across the Beringia land bridge?
Camelids originated in North America, and the ancestor of modern camels later migrated to Asia across the Beringia land bridge.
horses-camels-falcons-0138: Protylopus was among the earliest known camels. About how large was it?
The size of a modern camel
Protylopus lived in North America 40-50 million years ago and was about the size of a rabbit.
horses-camels-falcons-0139: A pure Arabian racing breed descended from ancient majahim
An extinct wild camel from Iran
A mountain breed of Bactrian camel
A hybrid of an Arabian and a two-humped camel
The Khorasani camel is a hybrid of an Arabian camel and a two-humped camel.
horses-camels-falcons-0140: Why was making cheese from camel milk difficult for a long time?
Traditional rennet coagulates its proteins slowly and produces a weak curd
It lacks proteins and fats capable of coagulation
Traditional rennet coagulates camel milk slowly and produces a weak curd. Researchers commissioned by the FAO improved cheesemaking by adding calcium phosphate and a suitable coagulating enzyme.
horses-camels-falcons-0142: From which camel is most hair used in textile production collected?
Camel hair used in textiles is collected from the Bactrian camel found across Asia.
horses-camels-falcons-0143: What water source does the Bactrian camel rely on during winter in its cold homeland?
The Bactrian camel is one of the few animals that regularly eat snow to meet their water needs.
horses-camels-falcons-0144: The Bactrian camel was famously the main transport animal on which historical trade route?
The Bactrian camel was the main transport animal on the Silk Road because it tolerates cold, dryness, and high altitudes.
horses-camels-falcons-0145: What is the 'zawr' on an Arabian camel's body?
A small bone at the base of the tail supporting the spine
A thick pad over the breastbone
The zawr is a thick tissue pad over the breastbone that raises the camel's body above the hot ground when it kneels.
horses-camels-falcons-0146: How does a camel remove sand from its eyes?
By rubbing its eye with a leg
A camel removes sand from its eye with its transparent third eyelid, known as the nictitating membrane.
horses-camels-falcons-0147: Camel dung is so dry that it:
Turns into white salt when dried in the sun
Can be used as fuel without drying
Camel dung is so dry it needs no drying before being used as fuel for a fire.
horses-camels-falcons-0148: The camel disease 'jufar' is caused by:
The parasite Trypanosoma evansi causes jufar in camels.
horses-camels-falcons-0149: The discovery of life-size camel rock reliefs, among the oldest animal reliefs of their kind, was published in 2018. Where were they found?
The oldest known camel reliefs were discovered in Saudi Arabia in 2018 and estimated to be 7000-8000 years old.
horses-camels-falcons-0150: What happens to a Bactrian camel's humps when food is scarce?
They shrink and lean to one side
They join to form one hump
A well-fed Bactrian camel has full, upright humps; when food is scarce, they shrink and lean to one side.
horses-camels-falcons-0151: According to a genetic study published in 2016, where did Arabian camel domestication probably begin?
Iranian Plateau in the foothills of the Zagros Mountains
A 2016 study suggested camel domestication began in the southeastern Arabian Peninsula, while the Bactrian camel was domesticated later in Central Asia.
horses-camels-falcons-0152: How can a horse doze while standing without falling?
By resting its head against the stable wall
By distributing its weight over only two legs
By closing one eye and keeping the other open
Through a special stay apparatus in its legs
A horse can enter light sleep while standing using a stay apparatus in its legs that prevents it from collapsing.
horses-camels-falcons-0153: What does a horse need to reach rapid eye movement sleep?
To sleep in a dark stable
A horse can doze standing, but reaches rapid eye movement sleep only while lying down.
horses-camels-falcons-0154: What is the usual average lifespan of a domestic horse?
A domestic horse lives an average of 25 to 30 years, depending on breed and care.
horses-camels-falcons-0155: A mare's pregnancy lasts an average of about:
A mare's pregnancy lasts about 340 days, roughly 11 months, and she usually gives birth to one foal.
horses-camels-falcons-0156: From which point is a horse's height measured?
A horse's height is measured at the highest point of the withers, where the neck meets the back, because it is a fixed point.
horses-camels-falcons-0157: A 'hand', used to measure horse height in English-speaking countries, equals:
horses-camels-falcons-0158: What is the traditional height boundary between a horse and a pony?
The traditional standard is 14.2 hands, meaning 14 hands and two inches (about 147 cm); below it is a pony and above it a horse.
horses-camels-falcons-0159: How do pedigree registries classify the miniature Falabella breed?
Hybrid donkeys of ancient Spanish origin
Although a Falabella may stand no more than 76 cm tall, its registries consider it a miniature horse rather than a pony.
horses-camels-falcons-0160: How many chromosomes do domestic horse cells contain?
The horse has 64 chromosomes; its genome was sequenced in 2007.
horses-camels-falcons-0161: How does the wild Przewalski's horse differ genetically from the domestic horse?
It has 33 chromosome pairs rather than 32
They do not differ in chromosomes or genome
Przewalski's horse has 33 chromosome pairs, while the domestic horse has 32.
horses-camels-falcons-0162: Where was the wild Przewalski's horse reintroduced after becoming extinct in the wild?
Since the 1990s it has been released again in its Mongolian homeland, in Hustai National Park and elsewhere.
horses-camels-falcons-0164: Which statement about albino horses with pink skin and red eyes is correct?
They are born that way but their color later changes
They occur only in the Arabian breed
Horses fitting this description do not exist
There are no albino horses in the sense of having pink skin and red eyes.
horses-camels-falcons-0165: A dun horse is usually distinguished by which primitive marking?
A dark stripe along the back
An entirely white tail from root to tip
The dun gene lightens body color but not the extremities, retaining primitive markings such as a dark dorsal stripe.
horses-camels-falcons-0166: How does a roan horse differ from a young gray despite their similar mixed coats?
A roan does not turn white with age
A roan is born entirely white
A roan always has blue eyes
Roan occurs only in mules and miniature horses
A roan has mixed light and dark hairs like a young gray, but unlike a gray it does not turn white with age.
horses-camels-falcons-0167: Which bone is absent from a horse's skeleton compared with a human's?
A major difference is that horses lack collarbones; their forelegs are attached to the trunk by muscles, tendons, and ligaments.
horses-camels-falcons-0168: The 'knee' of a horse's foreleg corresponds to which human joint?
A horse's front knee consists of carpal bones corresponding to the human wrist.
horses-camels-falcons-0169: What is virtually absent from a horse's lower legs below the knees and hocks?
There are no muscle bellies below a horse's knees and hocks; tendons and ligaments transmit movement.
horses-camels-falcons-0170: The outer hoof wall is made from the same material as:
The hoof wall and sole consist of keratin, the same material as human nails.
horses-camels-falcons-0171: How often do a domestic horse's hooves usually need trimming?
Hooves grow continuously, and most domestic horses need trimming and reshoeing every 5 to 8 weeks.
horses-camels-falcons-0172: The frog is a V-shaped part of the hoof. Its functions include:
Absorbing shock and helping pump blood
Secreting sweat to cool the legs during long runs
The frog is rubbery, absorbs shock, improves grip, and acts as a pump returning blood to the heart.
horses-camels-falcons-0173: If a horse stands for long periods in constantly wet surroundings, its hoof frog may develop a bacterial infection called:
A frog constantly exposed to damp conditions can develop a bacterial infection known as thrush.
horses-camels-falcons-0174: Where is a horseshoe nail driven into the hoof?
Into the coronet at the hairline above the hoof
At the outer edge of the white line
Into the center of the frog
Nails are driven at an angle, entering the wall at the outer edge of the white line and exiting through the wall's surface.
horses-camels-falcons-0175: How many incisors does an adult horse have?
An adult horse has 12 front incisors for cutting grass and 24 chewing teeth toward the rear.
horses-camels-falcons-0176: The four canine teeth behind the incisors are usually found in:
Stallions and geldings usually have four additional canine teeth behind the incisors, called tushes.
horses-camels-falcons-0177: Why are a horse's small 'wolf teeth' often removed?
They may interfere with the bit
Wolf teeth are small vestigial teeth in front of the cheek teeth, usually removed because they may interfere with the bridle's bit.
horses-camels-falcons-0178: Where does a bridle's bit rest in a horse's mouth?
Above the tongue beside the molars
On the gums in the gap between incisors and cheek teeth
Between the lips in front of the incisors
Behind the last molars near the throat and esophagus entrance
A horse has a gap between incisors and cheek teeth where the bit rests on the gums.
horses-camels-falcons-0179: How can a horse's age be roughly estimated?
By comparing withers height with leg length
A horse's teeth keep erupting and wear down through grazing, so its incisors provide a rough estimate of age.
horses-camels-falcons-0180: Why are digestive disorders known as colic dangerous to horses?
A horse has extremely short intestines
Horses cannot vomit, so digestive problems can quickly cause colic, a leading cause of death in horses.
horses-camels-falcons-0181: Where does cellulose fermentation occur in a horse's digestive system?
In the cecum and large intestine
A horse is not a ruminant; it digests cellulose through fermentation in the cecum and large intestine.
horses-camels-falcons-0182: With its eyes on the sides of its head, how wide is a horse's field of vision?
Only 90 degrees in front of the head
A horse's eyes are on the sides of its head, giving it a field of vision of about 350 degrees.
horses-camels-falcons-0183: What kind of color vision do horses have?
They see red more clearly than all other colors
They cannot see colors at all
Horses have dichromatic vision, resembling human red-green color blindness.
horses-camels-falcons-0184: Through how many degrees can a horse rotate each outer ear?
Each outer ear rotates up to 180 degrees, enabling hearing in all directions without turning the head.
horses-camels-falcons-0185: How many beats does a horse's trot have?
The walk has four beats, the trot two, and the intermediate running gait, the canter, three.
horses-camels-falcons-0186: How many beats does a horse's canter have?
The canter is a three-beat gait with a speed of 19 to 24 km per hour.
horses-camels-falcons-0188: A horse's pace is which kind of gait?
A four-beat gait with a suspended leap
A one-beat gait with all legs jumping together
The pace is a two-beat lateral gait in which the horse moves both legs on the same side together.
horses-camels-falcons-0189: Who usually leads a herd of horses?
Horses are herd animals with a clear hierarchy, led by a dominant individual that is usually a mare.
horses-camels-falcons-0190: In classification by temperament, which group does the Arabian horse belong to?
Eastern horses such as Arabians, Akhal-Tekes, and Barbs belong to the lively, fast hotblood group.
horses-camels-falcons-0191: What does 'coldblood' mean in classification of horses by temperament?
Wild horses that have never been domesticated
Coldbloods are heavy, muscular draft horses with calm temperaments, nicknamed gentle giants.
horses-camels-falcons-0192: How many toes did Hyracotherium, an early member of the horse family, have on each front foot?
Hyracotherium had four toes on each front foot and three on each hind foot.
horses-camels-falcons-0193: What remnants of ancient side toes remain in modern horses' legs?
Small splint bones below the knee
Only small vestigial bones below the knee, called splint bones, remain of the modern horse's side toes.
horses-camels-falcons-0194: Which two animals share the order of odd-toed ungulates with horses today?
Only three families of odd-toed ungulates remain: horses, tapirs, and rhinoceroses.
horses-camels-falcons-0195: A male horse and a female zebra
A male donkey and a mare
A male horse and a female donkey
A mule is a hybrid of a male donkey and a female horse, more common than the hinny.
horses-camels-falcons-0196: A hinny is a less common hybrid than a mule. It results from:
A zebra and a female donkey
A male donkey and a mare
A male horse and a female donkey
A hinny results from a male horse and a female donkey; it is smaller than a mule and has shorter ears.
horses-camels-falcons-0197: How much did a mule cost among the Hittites compared with a good horse?
The Hittites valued mules above their finest horses; a mule cost three times as much as a good horse.
horses-camels-falcons-0198: The earliest known evidence attributed to horse domestication is associated with which Central Asian culture?
The earliest known archaeological evidence of horse domestication is attributed to the Botai culture around 3500 BC, a matter of scientific debate.
horses-camels-falcons-0199: Where is a horse's white facial marking called a snip located?
On the muzzle between the nostrils
Only on the lower lip, not the upper lip
A snip is a white mark on the muzzle between the nostrils, while a star is a mark between or above the eyes.
horses-camels-falcons-0200: What characterizes white markings on a horse's body over its lifetime?
They appear after the third year
They are present from birth and do not change
They disappear after weaning and are replaced by others
White markings are present at birth and remain unchanged throughout a horse's life, so they are used for identification.
horses-camels-falcons-0201: According to modern genetic analysis, where is the homeland of modern domestic horses?
The Tibetan Plateau and Himalayan foothills
The western Eurasian steppes around the Volga and Don
Genetic evidence points to the western Eurasian steppes in the lower Volga-Don region as the homeland of modern domestic horses.
horses-camels-falcons-0202: What do Bedouins call the slight bulge between an Arabian horse's eyes, thought to increase sinus capacity?
Bedouins call the forehead bulge between the eyes jibbah, and it is thought to have helped Arabian horses adapt to the dry desert climate.
horses-camels-falcons-0203: What did Bedouins call the junction of the head and arched neck in Arabian horses, preferring it to be long?
Bedouins called the Arabian horse's poll and throatlatch structure mitbah; the longer it was, the more highly the horse was regarded.
horses-camels-falcons-0204: What is the facial profile of most Arabian horses?
Most Arabian horses have a distinctive concave profile known as a dished face.
horses-camels-falcons-0205: Which skeletal difference occurs in some Arabian horses?
7 lumbar vertebrae and 19 pairs of ribs
5 lumbar vertebrae and 17 pairs of ribs
Some Arabian horses have 5 lumbar vertebrae rather than the usual 6, and 17 pairs of ribs rather than 18.
horses-camels-falcons-0206: In Bedouin folklore, what title was given to the first Arabian horse?
One Bedouin tale says the first Arabian horse was nicknamed Drinker of the Wind.
horses-camels-falcons-0207: What did Bedouins feed their horses when pasture and water were unavailable?
Where there was no pasture or water, Bedouins fed their horses dates and camel milk.
horses-camels-falcons-0208: Through which line did Bedouins trace Arabian horse strains?
Bedouins developed Arabian horse strains with distinct traits, traced through the maternal line alone.
horses-camels-falcons-0209: Which is one of the five principal Arabian horse strains?
The five principal strains are Kuhaylan, Saqlawi, Ubayyan, Hamdani, and Hadban.
horses-camels-falcons-0210: In the legend of Arabian horse origins, 'Al Khamsa' refers to:
Al Khamsa refers to a legendary group of foundation mares of the Arabian breed.
horses-camels-falcons-0212: In which equestrian sport do Arabian horses particularly excel?
High show jumping in indoor arenas
Arabian horses dominate endurance riding because of their stamina and endurance.
horses-camels-falcons-0213: The three founders of the Thoroughbred breed are the Darley Arabian, the Godolphin Arabian, and:
The three foundation stallions of the Thoroughbred are the Darley Arabian, the Godolphin Arabian, and the Byerley Turk.
horses-camels-falcons-0214: In which city was the Darley Arabian purchased in 1704 before being shipped to England?
Thomas Darley bought this stallion in Aleppo in 1704 and sent it as a gift to his brother in England.
horses-camels-falcons-0215: To which stallion can the Y chromosome of about 95% of modern Thoroughbreds be traced?
The Y chromosome in about 95% of modern male Thoroughbreds traces to the Darley Arabian, usually through his descendant Eclipse.
horses-camels-falcons-0216: Who gave the Godolphin Arabian to King Louis XV of France?
The horse was exported while young to the Bey of Tunis's stable, then presented to Louis XV in 1730.
horses-camels-falcons-0217: A carriage horse for the King of England
A royal postal horse in Northern Ireland
The Byerley Turk was Captain Robert Byerley's warhorse during the Williamite wars in Ireland.
horses-camels-falcons-0219: Which estate near Cairo did the Blunts maintain to facilitate importing Arabian horses?
The Blunts maintained the Sheykh Obeyd estate near Cairo alongside their farm in England.
horses-camels-falcons-0221: Marengo, one of Europe's most famous Arabian stallions, was the warhorse ridden by:
Marengo was one of Europe's most famous Arabian stallions and Napoleon Bonaparte's warhorse.
horses-camels-falcons-0222: What was the Arabian horse breeding station established by Egypt's Royal Agricultural Society in 1928 in the Ain Shams desert called?
The society bought 60 feddans in the Ain Shams desert in 1928, and the farm was named Al-Zahraa Station.
horses-camels-falcons-0223: Which Mamluk sultan established the Al-Nasiri stud to import and breed Arabian horses in Egypt?
Records refer to the Al-Nasiri stud established by Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun.
horses-camels-falcons-0224: Turkmen Akhal-Teke horses are nicknamed golden horses because of:
The distinctive metallic sheen of their coats
Akhal-Tekes are famous for their distinctive metallic coat sheen, earning the nickname golden horses.
horses-camels-falcons-0226: The first recorded use of the horse name 'Barb' appeared in a translation of which book?
Muruj al-Dhahab wa-Ma'adin al-Jawhar by al-Mas'udi
The name Barb first appeared in a translation of Wasf Afriqiya by al-Hasan al-Wazzan, known as Leo Africanus.
horses-camels-falcons-0227: What is the other official name for the Andalusian horse?
The Andalusian is also known as the Purebred Spanish Horse, Pura Raza Espanola.
horses-camels-falcons-0228: The Friesian breed, known for its solid black color, originated in:
The Friesian originated in Friesland in the northern Netherlands and is known for its solid black color and long leg feathering.
horses-camels-falcons-0229: Which traditional task were huge English Shire horses known for?
Classical dressage displays in royal schools
Shires were used for farm work, towing canal boats, and pulling road transport wagons.
horses-camels-falcons-0230: Clydesdale draft horses take their name from a region in:
The Clydesdale originated in the seventeenth century and takes its name from the Clydesdale region of Scotland.
horses-camels-falcons-0231: Which breed's blood was added to the French Percheron draft breed in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries?
Arabian blood was added to the Percheron in the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries.
horses-camels-falcons-0232: Feral mustangs in the western United States descend from horses brought by:
Mustangs are feral horses descended from horses brought to the Americas by Spanish conquistadors.
horses-camels-falcons-0233: Lipizzan horses were named after the village of Lipica, now located in:
The breed takes its name from Lipica, formerly in the Habsburg Empire and now in Slovenia.
horses-camels-falcons-0234: With which riding school in Vienna are Lipizzan horses closely associated?
Lipizzans are associated with Vienna's Spanish Riding School, where they perform advanced classical dressage movements.
horses-camels-falcons-0235: For which work were small Shetland ponies used in Britain and the United States?
Shetland ponies were used in farm work and later in coal mines in Britain and America.
horses-camels-falcons-0236: The Falabella, one of the world's smallest horse breeds, originated in:
The Falabella is a small Argentine breed, standing between 63 and 86 cm tall.
horses-camels-falcons-0237: The American Appaloosa breed is famous for:
Its extremely short tail from birth
The Appaloosa is an American breed famous for its colorful spotted coat pattern, developed by the Nez Perce people.
horses-camels-falcons-0238: What distinguishes the ears of India's Marwari horse?
They are very short and rounded
They curve inward until their tips meet
Their tips have a conspicuous natural split
Marwari ears curve inward until their tips nearly meet.
horses-camels-falcons-0241: What is the consistent color of Austrian Haflinger horses?
Chestnut with a flaxen mane and tail
Solid black without any white marking
The Haflinger is always chestnut with a flaxen mane and tail.
horses-camels-falcons-0242: For which gait are German Trakehner horses known?
The Trakehner is known for its floating trot, full of impulsion and suspension.
horses-camels-falcons-0243: According to historical sources, in which civilization were paired stirrups invented?
Pharaonic Egypt during the New Kingdom
Stirrups were invented in China under the Jin dynasty in the fourth century, then spread to Europe through Eurasian nomadic peoples.
horses-camels-falcons-0244: What is the earliest rigid foot support known in the history of riding?
A double leather strap in ancient Rome
The earliest rigid foot support was a big-toe loop that appeared in India in the late second century BC.
horses-camels-falcons-0245: The stirrup is described as the third revolutionary step in horse equipment after:
Metal armor and the long spear
The stirrup is considered the third revolutionary step in horse equipment after the chariot and saddle.
horses-camels-falcons-0246: What was the 'hipposandal' used by Romans to protect horses' hooves?
A rigid sole attached with straps
The Romans tried to protect horses' hooves with a rigid sole fastened by straps, called a hipposandal.
horses-camels-falcons-0248: A farrier who trims hooves and fits horseshoes combines the skills of:
A herder, groom, and horse trainer
A farrier combines a blacksmith's skills in shaping horseshoes with a veterinarian's knowledge of leg anatomy.
horses-camels-falcons-0249: What distinguishes a curb bit from a simple snaffle?
It uses leverage to apply pressure to the poll and chin
It is placed outside the mouth
It is not attached to the bridle
It is made of braided ropes instead of metal
A simple snaffle applies direct mouth pressure, whereas a curb uses leverage to apply pressure to the mouth, poll, nose, and chin groove.
horses-camels-falcons-0250: The wool pad placed beneath the saddle
The frame on which the saddle is built
The strap fastening it around the belly
The saddle tree is its foundation, usually wooden, on which it is built; it distributes the rider's weight.
horses-camels-falcons-0251: The Arabic word 'baytar' comes from a Greek word meaning:
Baytar comes from the Greek hippiatros, meaning horse doctor.
horses-camels-falcons-0252: Who wrote the first known Arabic treatise on horsemanship and veterinary medicine?
The first known Arabic treatise on horsemanship was by Ibn Akhi Hizam, manager of Caliph al-Mu'tadid's stable, titled Kitab al-Furusiyya wa-al-Baytara.
horses-camels-falcons-0253: In Al-Furusiyya, Ibn Qayyim al-Jawziyya added which fourth branch to the three branches of horsemanship?
The three branches were riding, shooting from horseback, and lance fighting; Ibn al-Qayyim added sword dueling.
horses-camels-falcons-0254: In 2005, researcher Ken Franklin recorded a peregrine falcon diving at approximately:
Ken Franklin documented a peregrine falcon diving at 389 km per hour, making it the fastest animal in a dive.
horses-camels-falcons-0255: The peregrine falcon's scientific and English name means:
The royal falcon reserved for kings
Both names mean wandering falcon, referring to the migratory habits of many northern populations.
horses-camels-falcons-0256: From which major ice-free land area is the peregrine entirely absent?
The peregrine is the world's most widespread raptor, entirely absent only from New Zealand among major ice-free land areas.
horses-camels-falcons-0257: What caused the sharp decline in peregrine numbers in the mid-twentieth century?
DDT pesticide, which thinned its eggshells
Nest collapses caused by earthquakes and rockfalls
DDT thinned peregrine eggshells, reducing hatching success. Numbers recovered after it was banned in the 1970s.
horses-camels-falcons-0258: Where does a peregrine usually lay its eggs?
In a twig nest in a tree
In a shallow scrape on a cliff ledge
Peregrines nest in a shallow scrape made by the female, usually on cliff ledges or, more recently, tall buildings.
horses-camels-falcons-0259: For approximately how many days are peregrine eggs incubated?
Peregrine eggs are incubated for 29 to 33 days, mostly by the female.
horses-camels-falcons-0260: Which English term do falconers use for a male peregrine?
A male peregrine is called a tiercel, a female a falcon, and the young eyases.
horses-camels-falcons-0261: What is the function of the notch near the tip of a peregrine's upper beak?
Severing the spinal cord in the prey's neck
Picking small insects from still water
A notch near the upper beak's tip enables falcons to kill prey by severing the spinal cord at the neck.
horses-camels-falcons-0262: According to a 2021 study, what is the benefit of the black 'mustache' below a peregrine's eye?
Camouflage among dark rocks when approaching prey
Reducing sun glare and improving vision
The study found larger mustaches in sunny regions and concluded they reduce glare and improve vision.
horses-camels-falcons-0263: What helps a peregrine breathe during its rapid dive despite intense air pressure?
Small bony projections in its nostrils
An air sac in its chest
Holding its breath until catching prey and landing
Small bony projections in a falcon's nostrils are thought to redirect the strong airflow, making breathing easier during a dive.
horses-camels-falcons-0264: How does a peregrine protect its eyes from dust during a dive while retaining vision?
Tilting its head back and closing one eye
Its third eyelid, the nictitating membrane
Falcons use nictitating membranes to spread tears and clear debris from the eyes while retaining vision.
horses-camels-falcons-0265: The Latin 'falco', from which the falcon's name derives, is related to a word meaning:
Falco is related to falx, meaning sickle, referring to the shape of a falcon's long, pointed wings in flight.
horses-camels-falcons-0266: By what name is the peregrine known among people of the Arabian Peninsula?
The peregrine is known as shihana among people of the Arabian Peninsula and many Jordanians.
horses-camels-falcons-0267: Falconers distinguish four classes of young peregrines. Which is strongest and most desirable?
Falconers rank the young as nadir, strongest and most desirable, then laziz, mahqura, and taba'.
horses-camels-falcons-0268: In falconers' usage, a 'taba'' among young peregrines is one that:
Is born in captivity and hand-reared
Is the strongest and most expensive
Is usually male and less desirable to them
The taba' is usually male, smaller and less desirable to falconers than females.
horses-camels-falcons-0269: On what basis do hunters divide peregrines into 'mountain' and 'sea' types?
Mountain peregrines nest in mountains, while sea peregrines nest on cliffs near the sea; they are not separate species.
horses-camels-falcons-0270: For what purpose were peregrines used in World War II?
Peregrines were used in World War II to hunt carrier pigeons transporting military messages.
horses-camels-falcons-0272: The saker falcon is the national bird of several countries, including:
The saker falcon is a national bird of Hungary, Mongolia, the United Arab Emirates, and several Arab countries.
horses-camels-falcons-0274: How does the saker falcon's hunting style usually differ from the peregrine's?
It eats carrion more often than hunting live prey
It pursues prey horizontally instead of diving from above
The saker often hunts by horizontal pursuit rather than the peregrine's dive from height.
horses-camels-falcons-0275: Which is an Arabic name for the saker falcon (Falco cherrug)?
The saker is also called sharq (plural shuruq) or turmudi, and in some regions hurr.
horses-camels-falcons-0276: What is the world's largest falcon species?
The gyrfalcon is the largest member of the falcon family, reaching 65 cm in length.
horses-camels-falcons-0277: Which falcon is considered Iceland's national symbol?
The gyrfalcon is a prized hunting bird valued by Vikings and is Iceland's national symbol.
horses-camels-falcons-0278: The gyrfalcon is a high-latitude bird breeding on Arctic coasts, tundra, and islands of North America and Siberia.
horses-camels-falcons-0279: One of two falcons was probably sacred to the ancient Egyptians: the peregrine and the:
The ancient Egyptian sacred falcon was probably a lanner or peregrine; Horus was depicted with a lanner's head.
horses-camels-falcons-0281: What is the Barbary falcon's status in modern classification?
The Barbary falcon is a nonmigratory peregrine subspecies ranging from the Canary Islands across North Africa to the Middle East.
horses-camels-falcons-0282: Approximately how many species belong to the genus Falco?
The genus Falco contains about 40 species distributed across every continent except Antarctica.
horses-camels-falcons-0283: Unlike sparrowhawks and eagles, how do falcons kill their prey?
By dropping it from great heights onto rocks
With their beaks, aided by a tooth on the side
Falcons kill prey with their beaks, using a tooth on the beak's side, unlike sparrowhawks and eagles, which use their feet.
horses-camels-falcons-0284: Which of these falcons is smallest?
The smallest falcon is the Seychelles kestrel, measuring between 15 and 24 cm long.
horses-camels-falcons-0285: The falcon family probably originated in:
The falcon family probably originated in South America during the Paleocene.
horses-camels-falcons-0286: Which of these birds belongs to the falcon family alongside falcons?
The falcon family includes falcons and caracaras, whereas eagles and sparrowhawks belong to the hawk family.
horses-camels-falcons-0288: The most distinctive feature of kestrel hunting is that they:
Chase birds in flight for long periods
Hover at low altitude, then dive onto ground prey
Hunt in large groups surrounding prey on the ground
Kestrels hover 10 to 20 meters above open ground, then dive onto terrestrial prey.
horses-camels-falcons-0290: An old English name for the kestrel is 'windhover'. Why?
Its shrill call resembles wind whistling among rocks
It flaps its wings while stationary, facing the wind
An old name is windhover because it flaps its wings while remaining stationary in the air facing the wind.
horses-camels-falcons-0291: Where does the sooty falcon winter after breeding on Gulf islands and cliffs?
Central Asia and the Kazakh steppes
The sooty falcon breeds from northeastern Africa to the southern Gulf and winters in East Africa and Madagascar.
horses-camels-falcons-0292: One reason for the laggar falcon's decline in the Indian subcontinent is:
Interbreeding with other species until its distinctive traits disappeared
Its use as bait to catch large falcons
Major threats include pesticides and its use as bait to catch large falcons.
horses-camels-falcons-0293: The prairie falcon is the only large falcon found exclusively in:
The prairie falcon is the only large falcon native exclusively to North America.
horses-camels-falcons-0295: How much larger than a male can a female peregrine sometimes be?
Peregrines show clear sexual dimorphism; the female may be up to 30% larger than the male.
horses-camels-falcons-0296: What characterizes the peregrine's breeding partnership?
The female always raises the young alone
It lives alone and does not mate
Peregrines mature in their first year and mate for life.
horses-camels-falcons-0297: Approximately how long does a peregrine live in the wild?
Peregrines in the wild usually live up to about 15 years; some have exceeded 19 years, and they may reach 25 in captivity.
horses-camels-falcons-0298: What distinctive flight technique does the Barbary falcon use?
It flaps only the outer portions of its wings
It flies upside down when approaching prey
Only the outer portions of the Barbary falcon's wings flap during flight.
horses-camels-falcons-0299: Approximately how large is the genetic difference between the Barbary falcon and peregrine?
Mitochondrial DNA studies estimated a difference of about 0.6-0.8% between Barbary falcons and peregrines; many specialists consider it a subspecies.
horses-camels-falcons-0300: Which Arabic name for training falcons to hunt is used alongside 'siqara'?
Falconry is also called biyaza, miqnas, and bazdara; its practitioner is a saqqar or bazdar.
horses-camels-falcons-0301: A falconer who raises birds of prey and hunts with them
A spice seller in the market
A falconry practitioner is called a saqqar, bazdar, bayzar, or bayyaz.
horses-camels-falcons-0302: What leather item covers a falcon's head and eyes when it is not flying?
A falconer uses a leather hood to cover a falcon's head and eyes when it stops flying.
horses-camels-falcons-0303: A broad-topped wooden perch planted in sand
A leather cover for a falcon's head
A glove worn by the falconer
The wooden wakr serves as the bird's perch: a broad, flat surface attached to a stick planted in sand.
horses-camels-falcons-0305: Which country was among the eleven that nominated falconry for UNESCO's list in 2010?
Falconry was nominated by Belgium, Czechia, France, South Korea, Mongolia, Morocco, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Syria, and the United Arab Emirates.
horses-camels-falcons-0306: According to the evidence, where did falconry probably begin?
Evidence suggests falconry may have begun in Mesopotamia, with the earliest accounts dating to about 2000 BC.
horses-camels-falcons-0308: Which falcon has traditionally been used most in western Asia to hunt houbara bustards?
The saker is the species most traditionally used in western Asia to hunt houbara bustards, sandgrouse, curlews, and hares.
horses-camels-falcons-0309: Why did hybrid falcons become popular among Arabian Peninsula falconers?
They are large, bold hunters of houbara and resist aspergillosis
They live twenty years longer than wild falcons
Hybrids spread to meet demand for large, bold females that hunt houbara and tolerate aspergillosis in desert conditions.
horses-camels-falcons-0310: The first hybrid falcons produced in captivity resulted from mating:
A male kestrel and female merlin
A male gyrfalcon and female lanner
A male saker and female peregrine
A male peregrine and female eagle
Falconers Ronald Stevens and John Morris put a male saker and female peregrine together in western Ireland, and they mated.
horses-camels-falcons-0312: Historians believe Frederick II gained firsthand knowledge of Arab falconry during:
His campaign in the East between 1228 and 1229
He is thought to have gained firsthand knowledge of Arab falconry during his wars in the region between June 1228 and June 1229.
horses-camels-falcons-0313: At Frederick II's court, Theodore of Antioch translated into Latin a falconry treatise by which Arab falconer?
The falconer known by the Latin name Moamyn
Around the 1240s, the Arab falconer Moamyn's treatise was translated into Latin as De Scientia Venandi per Aves.
horses-camels-falcons-0314: The fourth book of Frederick II's The Art of Hunting with Birds is devoted to hunting cranes with:
The fourth book covers hunting cranes with gyrfalcons, and the fifth hunting herons with saker falcons.
horses-camels-falcons-0316: Why does repairing a falcon's broken feather by imping not hurt it?
It is done while the bird sleeps
Imping the broken mature part of a feather is painless because mature feathers are dead keratin structures, like human hair and nails.
horses-camels-falcons-0317: What is a 'jess' in falconry equipment?
A thin leather strap attached to a falcon's leg
A jess is a thin leather strap used to tether and control a trained falcon on a glove or perch.
horses-camels-falcons-0318: Which twentieth-century innovation reduced the loss of falconers' birds during hunting?
Modern veterinary medicine and radio tracking with transmitters on birds increased their lifespan and reduced losses.
first-aid-0002: St John Ambulance distinguishes a burn from a scald. What causes a scald?
Touching an exposed electrical wire at home
Contact with dry heat such as an iron or flame
Spilling a chemical such as bleach on a hand
Contact with moist heat such as steam or a cup of hot tea
Scalds result from moist heat such as steam and hot liquids, while burns result from dry heat such as fire and irons.
first-aid-0003: After thoroughly cooling a burn, what does the British Red Cross recommend covering it lightly with?
A broad adhesive dressing secured tightly over all the skin
Medical cotton placed directly on the burn
Cling film or a clean plastic bag
A fluffy towel moistened with warm water
Cling film or a clean plastic bag does not stick to the burn, keeps it clean to help prevent infection, and reduces pain by keeping air off its surface.
first-aid-0004: Why does the British Red Cross advise against putting an adhesive dressing on a burn?
It prevents blisters that aid healing
It quickly raises the burned skin's temperature
It contains substances that poison the skin
It sticks to the skin and may cause further damage
Adhesive dressings stick to burned skin and may cause further damage; cling film or a clean bag is an alternative.
first-aid-0005: Why should butter or oily creams not be applied to a burn?
They cool the skin excessively until it freezes
Their oils trap heat in the skin
They conceal pain, making the person think they have healed
They attract insects to the exposed burn
Butter and creams contain oils that retain heat, the opposite of the intended goal of cooling the burn.
first-aid-0006: Many toothpastes contain menthol. What is the problem with putting toothpaste on a burn?
It gives a superficial cooling sensation without treating the burn
It contains sugar that infects the burn
It dissolves the top layer of burned skin
It traps water under the skin, causing large painful blisters
Menthol gives an apparent cooling sensation but does not actually cool the burn; removing toothpaste in hospital may hurt and cause further damage.
first-aid-0007: If cool running water is unavailable for a burn, what alternative does the British Red Cross mention?
Putting ice cubes directly on the skin
Applying cold vegetable oil from the refrigerator
Pouring other cool liquids such as milk over the burn
Sprinkling flour or starch on the burn
If running water is unavailable, other cool liquids such as milk or soft drinks can be poured over the burn to cool it.
first-aid-0008: When cooling a burn with a shower, why avoid putting the person's whole body under cold water or in a cold bath?
It spreads the burn to healthy skin
It suddenly raises the person's blood pressure
It may cause severe allergic shock
Cool water is directed only at the burn because cooling the whole body may cause hypothermia.
first-aid-0009: What should be done with clothing stuck to a burn?
Pull it off quickly in one sharp movement
Leave it and do not try to remove it
Moisten it with oil, then gently pull it from the skin
Cut it away along with the attached skin
Do not try to remove anything stuck to the burn because that may worsen damage. Nearby clothing that is not stuck can be removed.
first-aid-0010: In which case does the British Red Cross always recommend medical advice after a burn, however small?
When the casualty is a baby or child
When pain completely disappears after cooling
When the burn is on the forearm or shoulder
When there is mild redness without blisters
Even small burns can threaten a baby or child's life, so medical advice is always sought after cooling the burn.
first-aid-0011: When does the British Red Cross advise a burned adult to seek medical advice immediately?
When pain subsides after twenty minutes
When mild redness appears on a finger
When scalded by a cup of water
When the face or genital area is burned
Seek medical help immediately for burns to the face or genital area, or when in doubt about severity.
first-aid-0012: When does St John Ambulance recommend removing rings and clothing that is not stuck to a burn?
Only after the ambulance team arrives
Before the area begins to swell
Jewelry and clothing that is not stuck are removed early, before swelling makes removal difficult.
first-aid-0013: Why is cling film laid lengthwise over a burn rather than wrapped around the limb?
The area needs room to swell
Wrapping makes the film stick to the skin
Laying it lengthwise cools the burn more
Wrapping prevents air from reaching the burn
St John Ambulance advises against wrapping film around the burn because the area needs room to swell.
first-aid-0014: What should be done with blisters that may appear on a burn?
Leave them intact to avoid infection
Open them with a sterile needle to drain the fluid
Apply toothpaste to dry them quickly
Opening blisters may cause infection, so they are left intact.
first-aid-0015: For a burn on a hand or foot, what does St John Ambulance suggest covering it with after cooling?
A hand or foot burn can be covered with a clean plastic bag instead of cling film.
first-aid-0016: When covering a severe burn using a roll of cling film, what is done with the first two turns?
Place them directly on the burn
Wrap them tightly around the limb
Moisten them with warm water before use
Discard them, then take a fresh piece
St John Ambulance recommends discarding the first two turns and laying a fresh piece lengthwise over the burn.
first-aid-0017: Which burn type affects all skin layers and may damage nerves, muscles, and blood vessels?
A full-thickness burn affects all skin layers and may extend to nerves, tissues, muscles, and blood vessels.
first-aid-0018: A burn affects the epidermis and part of the dermis, leaving red, raw skin and blisters. How is it classified?
A partial-thickness burn affects the epidermis and part of the dermis, with redness, raw skin, and blisters. A superficial burn affects only the epidermis, causing redness and pain without blisters.
first-aid-0019: When cooling a severe burn, why keep the burned area from touching the ground?
The first aider helps the casualty sit or lie down, keeping the burned area off the ground to keep it clean.
first-aid-0020: Excessive cooling of a large burn may dangerously lower body temperature. Who is at greatest risk?
St John Ambulance warns that hypothermia from excessive cooling is more dangerous for babies and older adults.
first-aid-0021: If the chemical causing a burn is a dry powder, how is it removed first?
Brush or pat it off the skin
Leave it on the skin until the ambulance arrives
Wipe it with a vinegar-soaked cloth
Apply vegetable oil until it holds together
Chemical powder is brushed or patted off the skin, then the burn is flooded with water.
first-aid-0022: What does St John Ambulance warn against when treating an acid or alkali burn?
Wearing protective gloves before touching the casualty
Flooding the burn with running water for a long time
Trying to neutralize the chemical without training
An untrained person should not try to neutralize acid or alkali burns; instead, flood the burn with running water.
first-aid-0023: When flooding a chemical burn with water, where should the runoff be directed?
Away from the first aider to prevent chemical splashes
Toward the casualty's chest to cover as much burned skin as possible
Toward the casualty's face to cool the whole body quickly
Into a small container for reuse in washing
Water is poured away from the first aider to avoid chemical splashes, while preventing contaminated water from collecting near the casualty.
first-aid-0024: What does St John Ambulance say about searching for an antidote before washing a chemical burn?
It must be found before any water washing
Do not delay treatment while searching for it
Mix it with water and wash with it
St John Ambulance states that treatment should not be delayed by searching for an antidote; flooding the burn with water takes priority.
first-aid-0026: What must a first aider check before approaching someone with an electrical burn?
That the electricity supply has been disconnected
That the burn has no blisters
That the burn has cooled completely
That the casualty is speaking clearly
Do not approach the casualty before ensuring the electricity supply is disconnected, to keep the first aider safe.
first-aid-0027: Why should someone with a small electrical burn be examined by a health professional?
It may conceal major internal injuries
It inevitably becomes inflamed within an hour
It always leaves a large visible scar
It requires stitches in every case
The American Red Cross warns that a small electrical burn may indicate major internal injuries; electricity may affect the heart and breathing.
first-aid-0028: According to a physician on the American Red Cross Scientific Advisory Council, what burn size warrants emergency care?
The size of a small coin
Covering a quarter of the body or more
Larger than half an arm's area
Larger than the palm of the hand
The physician says burns requiring emergency care include burns to the face, hands, and genitals, and any burn larger than the palm of the hand.
first-aid-0029: To prevent burns, what maximum water-heater setting does the American Red Cross recommend?
Prevention advice includes setting the water heater to 120 Fahrenheit or less, and lower for children and older adults.
first-aid-0030: To prevent children's kitchen burns, which way should pot and pan handles point?
Toward the door for easy carrying
Toward the back, out of children's reach
Toward the side wall of the stove in every case
The American Red Cross recommends using rear burners and turning handles toward the back, away from children.
first-aid-0031: What clothing does the American Red Cross recommend avoiding while cooking?
Loose clothing can come near flames and catch fire, so it should be avoided while cooking.
first-aid-0032: Why does the World Health Organization advise against applying ice to a burn?
It melts quickly and is useless
It increases the depth of injury
The organization states that ice should not be applied because it deepens burn injury.
first-aid-0033: Which traditional substance does the World Health Organization explicitly list among things not to put on burns?
The organization advises against applying pastes, oils, turmeric, or raw cotton to burns.
first-aid-0034: Which method does the World Health Organization mention for extinguishing flames on a person's clothing?
Running toward the nearest water source
Pulling off burning clothing by hand
Methods of extinguishing flames include rolling on the ground, covering the person with a blanket, or using water.
first-aid-0035: According to the World Health Organization, where do burns mainly occur?
At home and in the workplace
The organization states that burns mainly occur at home and in the workplace.
first-aid-0036: The World Health Organization defines a burn as an injury caused primarily by heat, or by radiation, electricity, or chemicals. What other cause does it mention?
The organization's definition includes burns caused by heat, radiation, radioactivity, electricity, friction, and chemicals.
first-aid-0037: If someone's clothing catches fire, what three steps does the American Red Cross teach?
The familiar rule is to stop what you are doing, drop to the ground while covering your face, and roll until the fire goes out.
first-aid-0038: Why should someone whose clothing is on fire not run?
They might trip and break a bone
Running makes the fire burn faster
Running suddenly raises blood pressure and causes fainting
It makes them harder for rescuers to see
The American Red Cross warns that running makes the fire burn faster.
first-aid-0039: When dropping to the ground to extinguish burning clothing, what should be covered if possible?
The person is told to drop to the ground, cover the face if possible, and roll until the fire goes out.
first-aid-0040: For how many minutes does St John Ambulance recommend cooling sunburned skin with cool water?
First aid for sunburn includes cooling the skin with cool water for 10 minutes and moving the person out of the sun.
first-aid-0041: When does St John Ambulance advise someone with sunburn to consult a health professional?
If they feel thirsty after an hour
If their skin becomes slightly red
If their skin peels after a week
Blistering in sunburn calls for consultation with a health professional.
first-aid-0042: Besides sunlight, what causes of sunburn does St John Ambulance mention?
Sunburn results from excessive exposure to the sun, sunlamps, or sunbeds.
first-aid-0043: According to St John Ambulance, what causes the heat rash popularly called 'hamw al-Nil'?
Blocked sweat glands during excessive sweating
Heat rash occurs when sweat glands become blocked because the person is sweating more than usual.
first-aid-0044: What clothing does St John Ambulance recommend for someone with heat rash?
Tight synthetic clothing against the body
Loose cotton clothing does not trap heat as synthetic fibers do.
first-aid-0045: When bathing to cool skin with heat rash, what does St John Ambulance recommend avoiding?
Perfumed products such as shower gels and creams may irritate the skin, so they are avoided.
first-aid-0046: According to the British Red Cross, what does early cooling of a burn with running water reduce?
Pain, swelling, and the risk of scarring
The risk of fever and vomiting after the burn
Cooling reduces pain, swelling, and the risk of scarring; the sooner and longer it is done, the less the injury's impact.
first-aid-0047: If a serious burn needs twenty minutes of cooling, what should the first aider do according to the British Red Cross?
Stop cooling and take the casualty to hospital
Apply ice to shorten the time
Cool it for two minutes, cover it, and leave
Call an ambulance while continuing to cool the burn
Begin cooling immediately, call an ambulance during cooling if needed, and continue cooling until it arrives.
first-aid-0048: According to the American Red Cross, what is left in place when cooling a burn?
A ring around the burned finger
A tight belt over the burn
Remove clothing and jewelry from the burn area except items stuck to it, which are left in place.
first-aid-0049: Which home-burn prevention measure does the World Health Organization suggest?
Using candles instead of lights at night
Putting the stove on the floor for easier cooking
Reducing water temperature at hot-water taps
Storing fuel near the kitchen for easy access
The organization's burn-prevention recommendations include reducing tap-water temperature and promoting safety education and smoke detectors.
first-aid-0050: An adult is choking and cannot speak or cough. Which part of the hand is used for back blows?
Give firm back blows with the heel of the hand between the shoulder blades, creating vibration and pressure that may dislodge the obstruction.
first-aid-0051: How many back blows does a first aider give a choking adult before moving to abdominal thrusts?
Give up to five back blows; if the obstruction remains, give up to five abdominal thrusts.
first-aid-0052: When giving a choking adult abdominal thrusts, where is the fist placed and in which direction is it pulled?
Above the navel, pulling inward and upward
Below the navel, pulling firmly downward
On the left side, pushing inward
Stand behind the person, place your fist above the navel, and pull firmly inward and upward up to five times.
first-aid-0053: Below what age must abdominal thrusts not be given to a choking child?
Do not give abdominal thrusts to a baby under one year because the internal organs are delicate; use chest thrusts instead.
first-aid-0054: How is a choking baby held to give back blows?
Lying on its back on a table
Face down on the thigh, with the head below the bottom
Upright on the shoulder, with the head raised
Hanging by the feet, head downward
Place the baby face down on the first aider's thigh, with its head lower than its bottom and its head supported.
first-aid-0055: Why is a choking baby's head kept lower than its bottom during back blows?
It increases blood pressure in the brain to wake the baby
Babies often choke on fluids, so gravity helps drain them
It makes the blows gentler on the baby's small back
A lowered head prevents the baby from crying during first aid
Babies often choke on mucus or curdled milk, and lowering the head helps fluid drain by gravity.
first-aid-0056: If back blows do not clear the obstruction from a baby's throat, what does the first aider give?
A little water to swallow the object
A finger sweep of the mouth
Turn the baby onto its back and give up to five thrusts on the breastbone in the center of the chest using both thumbs with hands encircling the chest, according to Resuscitation Council UK 2025.
first-aid-0057: Where does a first aider press on a choking baby's chest to give chest thrusts?
At the top of the chest just below the neck
On the left side between the ribs
On the lower abdomen just above the navel
In the center of the chest below the nipple line
Press on the lower half of the breastbone in the center of the chest below the nipple line, using both thumbs with hands encircling the chest, up to five times.
first-aid-0058: What does the British Red Cross say about hanging a choking child upside down by the feet?
It is the most effective method for young children
It helps if preceded by five back blows
It is ineffective and may push the object deeper or injure the child
It helps only if the blockage is liquid
Hanging a child by the feet is ineffective, risks dropping and injuring the child, and may push the object deeper into the throat.
first-aid-0059: When may a first aider remove an object from a child's mouth with their fingers?
In all cases before back blows
Only if the child is unconscious
When it is clearly visible and can be safely grasped
When it is not visible but its presence is suspected
Do not insert fingers into the mouth if the object cannot be seen, as this may push it deeper. If clearly visible, it can be carefully grasped.
first-aid-0060: Should a choking child be given a glass of water or a mouthful of food to push the obstruction down?
No; it will not clear the blockage and may worsen it
Yes, if the object is soft food
Yes; water pushes the object into the stomach
No, unless the child is older than six
The British Red Cross states this does not clear the blockage and may cause an additional obstruction.
first-aid-0061: What happens if an object goes down into a child's lung instead of coming out of the mouth?
Give plenty of water to dissolve it in the lung
Continue abdominal thrusts until it comes out of the mouth
It is treated in hospital; the important thing is that the airway is open
Force the child to vomit to remove it from the lung
The British Red Cross explains that this is not ideal but can be treated in hospital; the important thing is that the child is breathing.
first-aid-0062: What question does St John Ambulance recommend asking first when someone appears to be choking?
Ask: Are you choking? If the person can speak or cough, encourage coughing.
first-aid-0063: Which children does St John Ambulance advise should be seen at hospital even after the obstruction clears?
Every child who choked on water
Every child who cried after choking
St John Ambulance states that every child who received abdominal thrusts must be examined in hospital even if the obstruction clears.
first-aid-0064: A visibly pregnant woman appears to be choking and back blows have not helped. What does the American Red Cross recommend instead of abdominal thrusts?
A finger sweep of the mouth
For a visibly pregnant person or someone too large to encircle, give chest thrusts instead of abdominal thrusts.
first-aid-0065: If you choke while alone, what does the American Red Cross recommend after calling emergency services?
Drinking plenty of water to push the obstruction down
Lying on your back and waiting for help
Pressing your abdomen against a chair back or fixed object
Trying to vomit by putting a finger down your throat
You can give yourself abdominal thrusts with your hands or by bending over and pressing your abdomen against a chair back or fixed barrier without a sharp edge.
first-aid-0066: Which eating behavior does the American Red Cross list as a choking risk factor?
Drinking water after finishing a meal
Eating while seated at a table
Talking or laughing with a full mouth
Risk factors include talking or laughing with a full mouth, eating quickly, and poorly fitting dentures.
first-aid-0067: According to the American Red Cross, what sound may a choking person make while trying to breathe?
A sharp, high-pitched squeak may be heard during attempts to breathe, or no sound if the blockage is complete.
first-aid-0068: How deep are chest thrusts for a choking baby in American Red Cross guidance?
About one and a half inches
About two and a half inches
Give the baby five quick chest thrusts in the center of the chest, about one and a half inches deep, one-third of the chest's depth.
first-aid-0069: According to St John Ambulance, at what rate are adult chest compressions given during resuscitation?
Compress the chest at 100 to 120 compressions per minute, about two per second.
first-aid-0070: According to St John Ambulance, approximately how deeply is an adult's chest compressed during cardiopulmonary resuscitation?
With straight arms, compress about 5 to 6 cm, then allow the chest to rise fully.
first-aid-0071: What is the ratio of chest compressions to rescue breaths in the resuscitation St John Ambulance teaches the public?
Alternate 30 chest compressions with two breaths (30:2) until help arrives or signs of life appear.
first-aid-0072: For at most how many seconds does a first aider check normal breathing in an unresponsive person?
Open the airway and look, listen, and feel for breathing for no more than 10 seconds.
first-aid-0073: What are the agonal gasps St John Ambulance warns about in the first minutes of cardiac arrest?
Strong coughing showing an object has been expelled
Slow, intermittent gasps that are not normal breathing
About half of people in cardiac arrest make slow, sometimes noisy gasps. This is not normal breathing, but a sign of cardiac arrest.
first-aid-0074: Why does a first aider tilt an unresponsive person's head back before checking breathing?
It prevents vomit leaving the stomach
It draws the tongue forward and opens the airway
It directly increases blood flow to the brain
It wakes the person from unconsciousness
When a person becomes unresponsive, muscles relax and the tongue may block the airway; tilting the head back draws the tongue forward.
first-aid-0075: According to the British Red Cross, what should a lone first aider do first for an unresponsive adult who is not breathing?
Give compressions for a full minute before calling
Call emergency services before starting chest compressions
Give five breaths and wait for help
For an adult, a lone first aider calls emergency services before starting chest compressions.
first-aid-0078: Why does St John Ambulance emphasize rescue breaths in resuscitating a baby?
Compressions alone suffice for adults but not babies
Cardiac arrest in babies is usually caused by a breathing problem
A baby's chest can never tolerate compressions
Cardiac arrest in babies and children is usually caused by a breathing problem, so rescue breaths are essential.
first-aid-0079: According to Resuscitation Council UK 2025, what is used to compress a baby's chest during resuscitation?
Both thumbs with hands encircling the chest
Use both thumbs with hands encircling the chest for a baby, one or both hands for a child, and both hands for an adult.
first-aid-0080: How does a first aider give a rescue breath to a baby under one year?
Mouth over the baby's mouth while pinching its nose
Mouth over the baby's nose only
Mouth over both the baby's mouth and nose
Blowing air near the baby's face
Because the baby's face is small, seal your mouth over both its mouth and nose and blow gently until the chest rises.
first-aid-0081: According to St John Ambulance, how deeply is a child's chest compressed during resuscitation?
Compress the child's chest with one or both hands to one-third of its depth, not exceeding 6 cm, then let it rise fully.
first-aid-0082: If several first aiders are performing resuscitation, how often should they switch chest compressions according to the British Red Cross?
Switch every minute or two with as little interruption as possible, because fatigue reduces compression quality.
first-aid-0083: If a first aider fears breaking a rib during chest compressions, what is the British Red Cross's response?
Continue; a rib can heal, and blood circulation takes priority
Stop compressions immediately and give only rescue breaths
Reduce pressure until the chest no longer moves
Compress the abdomen instead of the chest
A rib may break, but maintaining blood circulation takes priority. Ribs heal, while stopping compressions greatly reduces survival chances.
first-aid-0084: According to the British Red Cross, how likely are chest compressions alone to restart the heart?
Unlikely; compressions maintain blood flow, and the device determines whether a shock is appropriate
Almost guaranteed for a healthy young athlete
Guaranteed if compressions continue for ten minutes
Compressions maintain blood circulation; the defibrillator analyzes the rhythm to determine whether a shock is appropriate. Not all cardiac arrests are shockable.
first-aid-0085: According to the British Red Cross, who may use an automated external defibrillator (AED) in public places?
Staff of the place housing the device
Anyone can use the device; it gives voice instructions and delivers a shock only when needed.
first-aid-0086: Can an automated defibrillator shock a healthy heart?
Yes, if the shock button is pressed by mistake
No; it only delivers a shock when needed
Yes, if the pads are reversed on the chest
No, unless the casualty is a child
The device analyzes heart rhythm and shocks only when needed; it never shocks a healthy heart.
first-aid-0088: According to St John Ambulance, where is the first defibrillator pad placed on an adult's chest?
On the upper right side below the collarbone
On the upper left side directly over the heart
On the back between the shoulder blades
In the center of the abdomen above the navel
Place the first pad on the upper right side below the collarbone and the second on the left side below the armpit.
first-aid-0090: For a child aged one to eight, if pediatric defibrillator pads are unavailable, how are standard pads placed?
One in the center of the chest and the other in the center of the back
Side by side on the back between the shoulder blades
One on the abdomen and the other on the thigh
Side by side on the chest over the heart
The British Red Cross recommends placing one pad in the center of the child's chest and the other in the center of the back.
first-aid-0091: A person in cardiac arrest is lying in water. What does the American Red Cross recommend before using a defibrillator?
Placing the pads over wet clothes
Removing the person from the water first
Spraying water on the chest to improve conduction
Delaying use until the person is completely dry
Remove the person from the water before using the device, although it may be used in rain or snow.
first-aid-0092: A casualty has a pacemaker visible under the skin. How is a defibrillator pad placed?
Away from the device, not over it
A defibrillator must never be used on them
Directly over the device to deliver current to it
Only on the back in every case
A defibrillator may be used with a pacemaker, but the pad should not be placed directly over it, as that may weaken the shock.
first-aid-0093: According to the British Red Cross, what is a heart attack and how does it differ from cardiac arrest?
A sudden blockage of blood supply to the heart muscle that may lead to cardiac arrest
An electrical heart disturbance unrelated to blood supply
A sudden blood pressure rise that resolves with rest
A complete heart stoppage causing immediate unconsciousness and cessation of breathing
In a heart attack, blood flow to the heart muscle is blocked. It may lead to cardiac arrest, in which the person becomes unresponsive and stops breathing.
first-aid-0094: An unresponsive person is breathing normally, with no suspected back or neck injury. In what position are they placed?
On their back with legs raised
On their stomach with their face toward the ground
On their side with the head tilted back
Place them on their side with the head tilted back, the recovery position, to keep the airway open and let vomit or blood drain.
first-aid-0095: If a casualty remains in the recovery position for 30 minutes, what does St John Ambulance recommend?
Sit them up and give water
Turn them into the recovery position on the other side
Leave them unmoved until the ambulance team arrives
Turn them onto their back and raise their legs
Turn the casualty onto the other side after 30 minutes in the recovery position.
first-aid-0096: According to St John Ambulance, what is removed first when placing someone in the recovery position?
Glasses and bulky objects in their pockets
Remove glasses and bulky objects from pockets; do not search pockets for small items.
first-aid-0098: Should a first aider speak to an unresponsive person who is breathing?
Yes, loudly to force them to wake quickly
Yes; they may hear what is happening around them
Reassure the person by speaking, as they may hear what is happening even without responding.
first-aid-0099: According to the British Red Cross, what is the first thing to do for someone bleeding severely?
Wash the wound thoroughly with soap and water
Raise the injured limb and leave it uncovered
Find a pressure bandage before anything else
Press on the wound with anything available
The first step is pressure on the wound with whatever is available to stop or slow bleeding; pressure helps blood clot.
first-aid-0101: A bleeding wound contains an embedded object such as glass. What is the correct action?
Remove the object immediately, then press on the wound
Push the object deeper to block bleeding
Leave the object and press around it, not on it
Wash the wound until the object comes out
Do not remove an embedded object because it plugs the wound and removal may greatly increase bleeding; press around it.
first-aid-0102: Should a severely bleeding wound be washed?
No, unless it is on the face
Yes, with soap and water to prevent infection
Yes, with running water before applying pressure
Do not wash a severely bleeding wound, as this may increase bleeding; minor cuts and grazes are washed.
first-aid-0103: For an animal bite that is not bleeding severely, what does the British Red Cross recommend?
Minor wounds are washed to remove dirt; animal bites without severe bleeding are washed with soap and water.
first-aid-0104: A bleeding casualty has become pale, cold, and dizzy. What does this warn of?
Shock due to insufficient circulating blood
Dehydration from drinking too little before the injury
An allergy to the wound dressing
Low blood sugar from not eating for hours
These are signs of shock, meaning insufficient circulating blood, a potentially life-threatening condition distinct from psychological shock.
first-aid-0105: How is a bleeding casualty positioned if shock is suspected?
Seated with the head between the knees
Lying down, with legs raised if no injury or breathing difficulty prevents it
On the stomach with the head below the rest of the body
Lay the person down, control bleeding, and seek help. The legs may be raised if no injury or breathing difficulty prevents it.
first-aid-0106: A first aider fears infection from blood and has no gloves. What does the British Red Cross suggest?
Cleaning hands with alcohol before touching
Pressing on the wound with an elbow instead of a hand
Leaving the casualty until gloves arrive
Using a plastic bag as a barrier
A plastic bag can serve as a barrier, or the casualty can press their own hand on the wound.
first-aid-0107: What does a public access trauma (PAcT) first aid kit usually contain?
Painkillers in different doses for adults and children
Tourniquets and special dressings that help clotting
The kit contains protective items such as gloves, special dressings including clot-promoting ones, tourniquets, and clear instructions.
first-aid-0108: How does a first aider check that a wound bandage is not too tight?
Press a nail beyond the bandage for five seconds and watch the color return
Raise the limb and see whether the bandage moves
Compare the neck pulse before and after bandaging
Ask whether the bandage feels comfortable
Press a nail or skin beyond the bandage for five seconds until pale. If color does not return within two seconds, the bandage is too tight.
first-aid-0109: How often does a first aider recheck circulation after bandaging?
St John Ambulance recommends checking circulation beyond the bandage every 10 minutes.
first-aid-0110: According to St John Ambulance, where is a tourniquet placed on a bleeding limb?
Below the wound, farther from the heart
Above and close to the wound, not over a joint
On the nearest joint for stability
Place the tourniquet around the limb above and close to the injury, preferably below the elbow or knee, and never over a joint.
first-aid-0112: After applying a tourniquet and stopping the bleeding, should it be loosened periodically?
Yes, if the casualty complains of pain
No, except after a full hour
Yes, every ten minutes to let blood through
St John Ambulance states that an applied tourniquet must not be loosened because bleeding will resume.
first-aid-0113: What is recorded after applying a tourniquet if it has a designated field?
Record the tourniquet application time in the designated field if present, and monitor the casualty until the ambulance arrives.
first-aid-0115: If a ready-made tourniquet is unavailable, what does St John Ambulance say can be improvised?
A thin metal wire tightened around the limb
A thin elastic band such as a hair tie
A triangular bandage or scarf with a pen for twisting
A single turn of adhesive tape
A tourniquet can be improvised from a triangular bandage, scarf, or tie with a pen or fork as a twisting rod; a belt can also be used.
first-aid-0116: According to the American Red Cross, what blood loss quantity can be life-threatening?
About half a soft-drink can may threaten life, and less may suffice for a small child
A few drops showing on clothing
Enough to wet one paper tissue
Losing about half a drink can of blood may threaten life, and less may suffice for a small child; this is not a safe threshold for ongoing bleeding.
first-aid-0117: If a first aider must apply a tourniquet to a limb with an embedded object, where does the American Red Cross say to place it?
Do not remove the embedded object; if a tourniquet is needed, place it above the object.
first-aid-0118: In American Red Cross classification, what is a wound in which skin and possibly underlying tissue are partially or completely torn away?
An avulsion involves skin and possibly underlying tissue being partially or completely torn away.
first-aid-0119: What is a wound caused by something rough rubbing and damaging the skin's surface, such as falling on asphalt?
An abrasion or graze damages the skin surface through friction and is sometimes called road rash or carpet burn.
first-aid-0120: Which wound occurs when a nail or animal tooth penetrates the skin and may not bleed much?
A puncture wound is caused by an object piercing the skin, such as a nail or tooth, and may not bleed much unless a blood vessel is injured.
first-aid-0121: According to St John Ambulance, how does a cut differ from a graze?
Cuts affect children and grazes affect adults
A cut always affects bone, while a graze affects only the skin's surface
A cut breaks fully through the skin, while a graze scrapes only its upper layers
A cut always bleeds and a graze never does
In a cut, the skin is broken fully through; in a graze, only its upper layers are scraped.
first-aid-0122: According to St John Ambulance, to what level is an injured hand raised when treating a cut?
Raise and support the wounded part above heart level.
first-aid-0123: When cleaning around a wound with soap and water, in which direction is it wiped?
Back and forth across the wound
Wipe around the wound away from it, using a clean piece for each wipe.
first-aid-0124: Which situation does St John Ambulance list as requiring medical help for a minor wound?
The wound is a small, clean superficial graze
The casualty is unsure about tetanus vaccination
The wound is on the knee of a child who fell
Seek medical help if bleeding does not stop, an object is embedded, the wound is a bite, infection is suspected, or tetanus vaccination status is uncertain.
first-aid-0125: How should someone with a nosebleed sit?
Sit leaning forward and pinch the soft part of the nose; tilting the head back makes blood run into the throat.
first-aid-0126: Why should the head not be tilted backward during a nosebleed?
It immediately causes dizziness and fainting
It greatly raises blood pressure in the head
It completely prevents clotting in the nose, prolonging bleeding
Blood may run into the throat, blocking the airway or being swallowed
Tilting the head back makes blood run into the throat, where it may block the airway or reach the stomach and cause nausea.
first-aid-0127: Which part of the nose is pinched to stop a nosebleed?
The soft part of the nose
The hard bone at the top of the nose
Pinch the soft part of the nose while breathing through the mouth.
first-aid-0128: According to St John Ambulance, for how many minutes is pressure first maintained during a nosebleed?
Maintain pressure for ten minutes, then release. If bleeding continues, repeat for two more periods of ten minutes each.
first-aid-0129: According to St John Ambulance, when does a nosebleed require calling emergency services?
If it lasts more than two consecutive minutes
If it lasts more than 30 minutes
If a few drops come out
