Call emergency services if bleeding is severe or lasts more than 30 minutes.
first-aid-0130: After a child's nosebleed stops, what advice helps prevent renewed bleeding?
Blow the nose forcefully to clean it
Blowing the nose after a nosebleed may restart bleeding, so the child is advised not to do so.
first-aid-0131: Which nontraumatic nosebleed cause does the American Red Cross mention?
Drinking large amounts of cold water
Sleeping a lot during the day
Sitting in the shade for a long time
Nontraumatic causes include dry air and altitude changes; some conditions and medicines may increase susceptibility.
first-aid-0132: According to St John Ambulance, what is shock in first aid?
A psychological state of fear after an accident
A life-threatening condition caused by too little oxygen reaching the brain and organs
A sudden rise in body temperature after injury with heavy sweating and shivering
Muscle spasm caused by extreme cold
Shock differs from psychological shock: it is a life-threatening condition in which the body does not get enough oxygen to the brain and vital organs.
first-aid-0133: When treating shock, what is done with tight clothing around the neck, chest, and waist?
Tighten it further to warm the body
Loosen it so it does not obstruct blood flow
Wet it with cold water to cool the body
Loosen tight clothing so it does not obstruct blood flow, and cover the casualty to keep them warm.
first-aid-0134: Why does a first aider reassure and calm someone in shock?
Fear and pain increase the body's oxygen demand and worsen shock
The casualty allows first aid only when completely calm and reassured
Fear and pain increase the body's oxygen demand and worsen shock, so reassurance is part of first aid.
first-aid-0135: Which cause of shock does St John Ambulance mention?
Sitting for a long time at a screen in a closed room
Fluid loss through diarrhea, vomiting, or burns
Causes of shock include severe bleeding, heart problems, fluid loss through dehydration, diarrhea, vomiting, or burns, and severe allergy.
first-aid-0136: According to St John Ambulance, for at most how many minutes is a cold compress applied to a bruise?
Apply a cold compress or a bag of frozen vegetables wrapped in a towel for no more than 20 minutes.
first-aid-0137: When does St John Ambulance recommend seeing a doctor about a bruise?
If it turns blue on the first day
If it has not disappeared after three weeks
If it appears hours after the injury
Most bruises disappear in about two weeks; a bruise still present after three weeks should be checked.
first-aid-0138: Why should a friction blister not be burst?
Its fluid causes a skin allergy
It disappears by itself within an hour
Bursting it may increase infection risk
Bursting a blister increases infection risk. Cover it with a dressing whose pad is larger than the blister.
first-aid-0139: According to St John Ambulance, how is a wooden splinter pulled from the skin with tweezers?
Straight out at the same angle it entered
Perpendicular to the skin regardless of its angle
By pushing it forward until it exits the other side
By twisting it back and forth until loose
Grasp the splinter close to the skin and pull it straight out at the same angle it entered.
first-aid-0140: If a splinter is deep in the skin and difficult to remove, what does St John Ambulance recommend?
Leave it in place and seek medical help
Cut the skin with a needle to remove it
Apply oil until it comes out by itself after two days
Heat it to soften it and make it come out
A deep splinter is difficult to remove, so leave it in place and advise the casualty to seek medical help.
first-aid-0141: After removing a splinter, why is the wound gently squeezed?
To make the skin edges join and heal quickly
To reduce pain at the splinter site
To release a little blood that helps remove dirt
Gently squeeze the wound to release a little blood that helps flush out dirt, then clean and cover it.
first-aid-0142: What three main bandage types does St John Ambulance mention?
The three main types are roller bandages for limb support and securing dressings, tubular bandages for joints and fingers, and triangular bandages for slings and large wounds.
first-aid-0143: Which knot does St John Ambulance recommend for a triangular bandage?
Tie a triangular bandage with a reef knot: right over left and under, then left over right and under.
first-aid-0144: Why are fingers or toes left exposed when bandaging a limb?
To let the casualty move freely during transport
To let the bandage dry faster
Leave fingers or toes exposed so blood flow can be checked after bandaging.
first-aid-0145: What is the purpose of an elevation sling in which the casualty's fingertips touch the opposite shoulder?
Helping stop bleeding and reduce forearm or hand swelling
Supporting the neck after a spinal injury
Immobilizing a thighbone fracture during transport
Warming the arm during severe hypothermia
An elevation sling supports the forearm and hand in a raised position, helping stop bleeding and reduce swelling.
first-aid-0146: How far should an arm sling support the arm?
To about the middle of the forearm
To the tip of the little finger
Adjust the sling to support the arm as far as the little fingertip.
first-aid-0147: When applying a figure-eight bandage to a hand, how much of the previous turn should each turn cover?
Each turn covers two-thirds of the previous turn, covering a new third of skin with each turn.
first-aid-0148: Why should adhesive tape not be wrapped completely around an injured limb when securing a dressing?
It sticks to hair and hurts
It does not secure the dressing well
Do not wrap tape completely around the limb because it may reduce blood flow; use a roller bandage if pressure is needed.
first-aid-0149: According to the British Red Cross, where should a suspected limb fracture be supported if possible?
Only below the injury at the joint
At the point farthest from the injury
Support the limb above and below the injury to prevent unnecessary movement, ease pain, and prevent further damage.
first-aid-0150: A joint appears dislocated. Should a first aider try to put it back?
Yes, by gently pulling the limb until it returns
Yes, if the casualty is in severe pain
No; this may cause further damage
Never try to put a dislocation back, as this may worsen damage; leave it to professionals.
first-aid-0151: According to the British Red Cross, which is the usual way to confirm a broken bone?
The casualty's ability to move the limb
The bruise color around the injury
The severity of pain when touched
A bone may be broken even if the casualty can move the limb; a fracture is usually confirmed with an X-ray.
first-aid-0152: According to the British Red Cross, why can fractures in children sometimes be difficult to identify?
Bruises do not appear on their bodies
Children do not feel fracture pain
Their soft bones may bend or split
Babies' and children's bones are soft and may bend or split, making fractures hard to identify without X-rays.
first-aid-0153: According to St John Ambulance, what is an open fracture?
A fracture affecting only skull bones
A fracture with a wound or cut in nearby skin
A fracture invisible on standard X-rays however often repeated
A fracture that heals without any treatment
An open fracture has a skin wound near the broken bone, whereas the skin around a closed fracture is intact.
first-aid-0154: When an arm fracture is suspected, what is removed from the injured limb as soon as possible?
Rings, watches, and anything encircling it
Remove rings, watches, and anything encircling the limb early, because swelling may make them restrict blood flow.
first-aid-0155: Where is pressure applied to control bleeding from an open fracture?
No pressure is ever applied to an open fracture
On the joint above the fracture
Around the wound, not over the protruding bone
Cover the wound with a sterile dressing and press around it, not over protruding bone or the fracture site.
first-aid-0156: A casualty has a suspected leg fracture and may develop shock. What does St John Ambulance warn against?
When treating shock, do not raise the legs if a leg fracture or pelvic or hip injury is suspected.
first-aid-0157: St John Ambulance particularly warns of shock signs after fractures of which bones?
Fractures of the thighbone, hip, or pelvis may cause internal bleeding and signs of shock.
first-aid-0158: According to St John Ambulance, what immobilizes an upper-limb fracture before transport?
Immobilize an upper-limb fracture with a sling and a lower-limb fracture with broad bandages.
first-aid-0159: According to the British Red Cross, what is the difference between a strain and a sprain?
A strain affects a joint and a sprain a muscle
A strain affects bone and a sprain skin
A strain affects a muscle and a sprain a joint
They are two names for the same injury
A strain is a muscle injury, while a sprain is an injury to a joint such as the knee, ankle, or wrist.
first-aid-0160: The abbreviation RICE is used in first aid for sprains and strains. What does E stand for?
RICE means rest, ice, comfortable support, and elevating the injured part.
first-aid-0162: What is the British Red Cross's view of warm compresses or alternating hot and cold for a sprain?
Not recommended; ice is more effective at reducing swelling
Always used for children instead of ice
Better than ice in the first hours
Used immediately after the first ten minutes of cooling
Warm treatments are not recommended first aid, and an ice pack is more effective at reducing swelling.
first-aid-0163: According to the British Red Cross, how is a sprain bandaged after cooling?
Very tightly so the joint cannot move
Over clothing rather than directly on skin
Without pulling tight, ensuring it is not constricting
After warming the joint with hot water
Support the part in a raised position, then apply the bandage without tightening excessively, ensuring it does not become constricting.
first-aid-0164: Which joints does St John Ambulance list among common dislocations?
Common dislocations include the knee, jaw, ankle, fingers, and thumb.
first-aid-0165: What supports the arm when a shoulder or elbow dislocation is suspected?
Support the arm with a sling and a broad bandage around the chest and sling for added comfort and stability.
first-aid-0166: Which possible spinal injury cause does St John Ambulance mention?
Diving headfirst into a shallow pool and striking the bottom
Sitting a long time in a comfortable chair
Walking quickly on level ground for a long time
Causes include falls from height, diving into shallow water and striking the bottom with the head, and sudden vehicle stops.
first-aid-0167: A conscious casualty has a suspected spinal injury. What is the most important action until an ambulance arrives?
Support the head to keep the head, neck, and spine aligned
Have them walk a little to check they are unharmed
Sit them up on a high pillow and ask them to move their neck slowly
Turn them onto their stomach to rest their back
Do not move the casualty. Support the head in a neutral position to keep the head, neck, and spine in a straight line.
first-aid-0168: Why does a first aider spread their fingers when supporting a spinal injury casualty's head, leaving the ears uncovered?
The ears usually bleed after this injury
The casualty needs to hear the first aider
The ear is where the pulse is checked
Spread the fingers to avoid covering the ears, because the casualty needs to hear the first aider.
first-aid-0170: According to the British Red Cross, for how many minutes is a cold item applied after a blow to the head?
Apply something cold, such as frozen vegetables wrapped in a towel, for up to 20 minutes to reduce swelling and pain.
first-aid-0171: A player sustains a blow to the head during a match. According to the British Red Cross, when may they return to play?
After examination by a medical professional
After fifteen minutes if the headache stops
In the next half if they feel better
Do not return to sport until examined by a medical professional.
first-aid-0172: According to the British Red Cross, which sign after a head injury calls for emergency services?
Clear fluid or blood coming from an ear or the nose
Mild pain when touching the area
A small swelling appearing minutes after the blow
Clear fluid or blood from an ear or the nose is a sign of serious head injury requiring emergency help.
first-aid-0173: According to the British Red Cross, what is a concussion?
The brain being shaken inside the skull by a blow to the head
A nosebleed after falling on the face
A skull fracture visible on X-rays after falling from height
Swelling of the scalp where the blow landed
A concussion occurs when a blow to the head shakes the brain inside the skull; most affected people recover fully.
first-aid-0174: According to the British Red Cross, which group should always seek medical advice after a head injury?
People taking medicines that prevent blood clotting
People with no headache or dizziness after the blow
Advice is recommended for those over 65, with previous brain injury, taking blood thinners, who have drunk alcohol, or who have nobody to care for them.
first-aid-0175: According to the British Red Cross, may a child sleep after a head injury?
Yes, if it is their normal bedtime and there are no signs of serious injury
No, unless six hours have passed
Yes, in all cases, even with unusual severe drowsiness immediately after injury
No; they must be kept awake all night
Let the child sleep if it is their normal bedtime with no signs of serious injury; unusual drowsiness requires urgent attention.
first-aid-0176: In the AVPU scale used by St John Ambulance to assess responsiveness, what does V mean?
Is the pulse regular and strong?
Does the person respond to voice when spoken to?
Can the person see surrounding objects clearly?
Does the person vomit after the injury?
AVPU means Alert, responds to Voice, responds to Pain, Unresponsive.
first-aid-0177: Which eye sign does St John Ambulance list as indicating serious head injury?
Mild redness in the white of the eye
Signs of serious head injury include unequal pupil sizes, blood or fluid from an ear or the nose, and declining responsiveness.
first-aid-0179: What increases the risk of complications from concussion, according to the American Red Cross?
Being a fit athlete who exercises daily
Someone who has had a concussion is at greater risk of complications from subsequent concussions.
first-aid-0181: When rinsing an eye exposed to a chemical, how should the person's head be tilted, according to the American Red Cross?
With the affected eye higher than the unaffected eye
Forward with the face toward the ground
Fully backward with the face upward
With the affected eye lower than the unaffected eye
Keep the affected eye lower so contaminated water does not enter the unaffected eye.
first-aid-0182: A large object is embedded in someone's eye. What is the correct response?
Gently remove it with tweezers, then rinse the eye
Leave it in place, cover the eye, and call emergency services
Rinse the eye with water until the object comes out
Ask the person to rub the eye gently to dislodge it
Do not attempt to remove a large object embedded in the eye. Cover the eye with a clean dressing and seek medical help.
first-aid-0183: What does St John Ambulance advise someone with dust or a small object in their eye?
Close it tightly for a full hour to produce plenty of tears
Do not rub it, as this may make it worse
Rub it vigorously to remove the object
Put a drop of warm oil in it
Advise the person not to rub their eye, then try rinsing the small object out with clean water.
first-aid-0184: According to St John Ambulance, where should water be poured to rinse a small object visible on the eye's surface?
From the inner corner of the eye
From the outer corner of the eye
The person tilts their head back, and clean water is poured from the inner corner of the eye.
first-aid-0185: What is the eye condition called a flash burn, mentioned by St John Ambulance?
An eye wound from a metal fragment at work
Eye inflammation from a pollen allergy
Damage to the eye's surface from ultraviolet radiation, such as welding glare or snow glare
An eye burn from a household chemical such as bleach or strong oven cleaner
A flash burn occurs when ultraviolet radiation damages the eye's surface, such as sunlight reflected off snow or an unprotected exposure to a welding flash.
first-aid-0186: A permanent tooth has been completely knocked out. By which part should it be picked up, according to the American Red Cross?
With a tissue wrapped tightly around the entire tooth
Pick up a permanent tooth by its crown, not its root, and preserve it for a dentist to replant. A baby tooth should not be replanted.
first-aid-0187: If no special storage solution is available for a knocked-out permanent tooth, what should it be stored in, according to the American Red Cross?
In a cup of tap water
Store it in cow's milk or the person's saliva in a container, not in tap water, and go to a dentist immediately.
first-aid-0188: Within how many minutes should a knocked-out permanent tooth ideally be replanted, according to the American Red Cross?
The sooner a permanent tooth is replanted, the greater its chance of survival, ideally within 30 minutes. A baby tooth should not be replanted.
first-aid-0189: A child has put a bead in their nose. What does St John Ambulance recommend?
Try removing it with tweezers at home
Go to the emergency department without trying to remove it
Push it inward so the child swallows it
Block the other nostril and blow forcefully through the nose
Do not try to remove a foreign object from the nose or ear, as this could push it deeper. Go to the emergency department.
first-aid-0190: An insect has entered a child's ear. What does St John Ambulance suggest?
Drip hot oil into the ear
Shake the child's head forcefully downward with the affected ear facing the ground until it falls out
Position the affected ear upward and gently flood it with lukewarm water
Insert a cotton bud to remove it

Support the head with the affected ear upward and gently pour in lukewarm water to float the insect out, unless there is severe pain, bleeding, discharge, or ventilation tubes in the ear. In those cases, seek medical attention.
first-aid-0191: On arriving at a road collision, what should a first aider ensure first, according to St John Ambulance?
The scene is safe for them, the casualties, and other road users
The casualties are removed from the vehicles immediately
The damaged vehicles are moved to the roadside to let traffic pass
The collision is photographed to send to the police
Check that the scene is safe before helping casualties, to protect the first aider, casualties, and road users.
first-aid-0192: According to St John Ambulance, what should a first aider assume about everyone involved in a road collision?
They are uninjured as long as they can speak
They may have a neck or spinal injury
Assume that everyone involved may have a neck or spinal injury, and support their head and neck.
first-aid-0193: What should a first aider switch off in damaged vehicles to make them safe, according to St John Ambulance?
Switch off the engines of all damaged and nearby vehicles, and disconnect the battery if possible.
first-aid-0194: What should a first aider prohibit near a road collision, according to St John Ambulance?
Using a phone to call emergency services
Do not allow anyone to smoke near the scene because fuel may have spilled.
first-aid-0195: How should a road collision scene be protected from approaching traffic, according to St John Ambulance?
The first aider stands in the middle of the road and waves at vehicles
The road is blocked by moving casualties into its middle
The damaged vehicles are left without any warning signs, and everyone simply waits for police
Ask two drivers to stop some distance away in each direction with their hazard lights on
Ask two drivers to protect the scene by stopping some distance away in each direction with hazard lights on. Use warning triangles if available.
first-aid-0196: Someone with heat exhaustion appears to recover after rest and water. What does the British Red Cross recommend?
Return to work in the sun immediately
Nothing further is needed after recovery
Give them a fizzy energy drink
Seek medical advice even if they appear to have fully recovered, and call emergency services if they deteriorate.
first-aid-0197: Which drinks does the British Red Cross mention for replacing salts lost through sweating in heat exhaustion?
Fizzy energy drinks high in sugar and caffeine
Water replaces fluids, while isotonic sports drinks replace salts lost through sweating.
first-aid-0198: How does the skin of someone with heat exhaustion usually appear, according to the British Red Cross?
Shiny yellow, extremely hot, and completely dry without sweat
Sweaty, cooler to the touch, and paler than usual
In heat exhaustion, the person sweats and their skin is cooler to the touch and paler. In heatstroke, the skin is hot and may be dry or sweaty, with altered consciousness.
first-aid-0199: What is the main difference between heatstroke and heat exhaustion, according to the British Red Cross?
Heatstroke occurs only in direct sunlight, while heat exhaustion occurs only indoors
Heatstroke is milder and does not need emergency care
Heatstroke affects only children, while heat exhaustion affects only adults
Heatstroke disrupts the brain's temperature regulator; heat exhaustion involves loss of salts and fluids

Heatstroke is a failure of temperature regulation: temperature rises greatly, consciousness is altered, and the skin is hot and may be dry or sweaty. In heat exhaustion, the body struggles with salt and fluid loss, and the skin is pale and clammy.
first-aid-0200: Above what body temperature do British Red Cross guidelines list a sign of heatstroke?
Signs include a body temperature above 40 degrees Celsius with altered consciousness. The skin is hot and may be dry or sweaty.
first-aid-0202: What method does the British Red Cross describe for cooling someone with heatstroke?
Cover them with a thick blanket until an ambulance arrives
Give them a hot drink so they sweat heavily and cool themselves
Wrap them in a cold wet sheet and continually pour cold water over it
Leave them in the sun with a small fan
Move them to a cool place, remove their outer clothing, and wrap them in a cold wet sheet over which cold water is poured.
first-aid-0203: According to the British Red Cross, what is the difference between sunstroke and heatstroke?
There is no difference: heatstroke is another name for heat exhaustion
Sunstroke results from excessive sun exposure, while heatstroke can occur in a hot room
Sunstroke affects only the skin and never raises internal body temperature, however long the exposure
Sunstroke is always more dangerous and has completely different symptoms
Their symptoms are the same, but sunstroke results from excessive sun exposure, while heatstroke can occur in a room without cool air.
first-aid-0204: Where does St John Ambulance suggest placing cold packs, if available, to cool someone with heatstroke?
Only on the soles and palms
Under the armpits and around the neck
If cold packs are available, place them under the armpits and around the neck while wrapping the person in a cold wet sheet.
first-aid-0205: What is the preferred method for cooling exertional heatstroke in American Red Cross guidelines?
Run a small fan near the person
Put a cold pack only on the forehead while covering the body
Immerse the body up to the neck in cold water
Give the person ice-cold water to drink
The preferred method is immersion up to the neck in cold water for 15 minutes or until the confusion resolves.
first-aid-0206: In American Red Cross heatwave guidelines, what must not be given to someone with heatstroke after calling emergency services?
Cool the body using wet cloths, spraying, fanning, or a cold bath, and give the person nothing to drink.
first-aid-0207: What are heat cramps, according to the American Red Cross?
Itchy skin and small blisters caused by blocked sweat glands
A headache from sleeping in a hot room
Muscle spasms caused by losing a lot of salt and water
Heat cramps are muscle spasms and pain caused by losing large amounts of salt and water through heavy sweating.
first-aid-0208: How can someone check that they are drinking enough water in hot weather, according to the American Red Cross?
By measuring their pulse every hour
By observing urine color: dark yellow may indicate insufficient drinking
By counting sweating episodes each day and comparing them with cold days
By weighing themselves morning and evening
Urine color is an indicator: dark yellow may mean you are not drinking enough.
first-aid-0209: Which drinks does the American Red Cross advise avoiding during heatwaves?
Water with a salty snack after sweating
Avoid sugary, caffeinated, and alcoholic drinks, and replace salts with snacks or sports drinks.
first-aid-0210: What is the difference between a WATCH and a WARNING in weather alerts, as explained by the American Red Cross?
A watch means prepare; a warning means act
A watch means act; a warning means prepare
Both a watch and a warning mean evacuate the home immediately
A watch is for daytime and a warning for nighttime
WATCH means be prepared, while WARNING means take action.
first-aid-0212: How should someone with heat exhaustion be positioned, according to St John Ambulance?
Sitting in the sun while drinking water
Lying in a cool shaded place with their legs raised
Lying on their stomach in a closed room without ventilation
Standing and walking slowly to stimulate circulation
Help them lie down in a cool shaded place with their legs raised, and give them plenty of water.
first-aid-0213: Which sign of dehydration in young infants does the British Red Cross mention?
Hot red cheeks with excessive drooling
A sunken fontanelle (the soft spot on top of the head)
Young infants may have a sunken fontanelle; children may have pale skin and sunken eyes.
first-aid-0214: Which drinks does the British Red Cross exclude when giving someone with dehydration plenty of fluids?
Give plenty of fluids that are not energy drinks, fizzy drinks, or alcohol.
first-aid-0215: What sign of dehydration in young children when crying does St John Ambulance mention?
Signs in young children include no tears when crying, fewer wet nappies, and sunken eyes.
first-aid-0217: Why should water be boiled and then cooled before giving it to a child with vomiting and diarrhea, according to the British Red Cross?
To increase its beneficial mineral salts
To make the child vomit their stomach contents
To kill germs and then allow the child to drink without being burned
Boil the water to kill germs, then cool it so the child can drink without being burned.
first-aid-0218: What should an infant under six months with vomiting and diarrhea be given, according to the British Red Cross?
Give an infant under six months their usual milk instead of boiled water, and seek medical advice because they are more prone to dehydration.
first-aid-0219: Below what body temperature is hypothermia defined, according to St John Ambulance?
Hypothermia occurs when body temperature drops below 35 degrees Celsius; normal temperature is about 37.
first-aid-0220: Someone has hypothermia outdoors. Why does St John Ambulance tell the first aider not to give them their own clothes?
The person needs a little cold
The first aider needs to stay warm too
Extra clothing raises temperature dangerously quickly
The first aider's clothes may be contaminated
The first aider should not give away their own clothing, because they must stay warm themselves. Use available coverings instead.
first-aid-0221: What should not be given to someone with hypothermia to warm them up?
Alcohol worsens hypothermia, while warm drinks and energy-rich foods are helpful.
first-aid-0222: When treating hypothermia indoors, to approximately what temperature does St John Ambulance recommend warming the room?
Cover the person with layers of blankets and warm the room to about 25 degrees Celsius.
first-aid-0223: Why should a hot-water bottle not be placed against someone with hypothermia, according to St John Ambulance?
It cools too quickly to help
It causes sweating followed by chilling
Do not place direct heat, such as a hot-water bottle or fire, near the person because it may cause burns.
first-aid-0224: In a remote area where emergency services cannot be contacted, how should help be sought for someone with hypothermia, according to St John Ambulance?
Make the person walk to the nearest village
The first aider goes alone for help, leaving the person wrapped in a blanket
Leave the person asleep until morning
Send two people together for help and do not leave the casualty alone
Never leave the casualty alone. In remote areas, send two people together to seek help.
first-aid-0225: How should a frostbitten body part be warmed, according to St John Ambulance?
In warm, not hot, water at about 40 degrees Celsius
By holding it directly near a heater
By rubbing the skin vigorously with snow
In boiling water to melt the ice on the skin quickly
Place the affected part in warm, not hot, water at about 40 degrees Celsius. Do not rub it or expose it to direct heat.
first-aid-0226: Why should frostbitten skin not be rubbed?
Rubbing may damage frozen skin, so warm it gently instead.
first-aid-0227: When should a first aider not try to thaw a frostbitten body part, according to the British Red Cross?
If the toes or ear tips are affected
If there is a chance it could freeze again
If the person is shivering severely
If the person is a young child
Do not try to thaw the affected part if there is any chance it could refreeze.
first-aid-0228: How does the British Red Cross describe chest pain in a heart attack?
Chest pain that always disappears after a few minutes of rest
A brief mild prickling that disappears when sitting position changes
Heartburn that disappears immediately after drinking water
A vice-like crushing pain that does not ease with rest and may spread to the arms and jaw
Heart attack pain is persistent and vice-like. It may spread to the arms, neck, jaw, back, and abdomen, and does not ease with rest.
first-aid-0229: Why does the British Red Cross advise sitting someone with a suspected heart attack on the floor, supported by a chair or wall?
It makes their pulse easier to measure
The cold floor cools their body and makes them comfortable
Sitting reduces strain on the heart and limits injury if they collapse
Sitting on the floor immediately stops chest pain and restores a normal pulse
Sitting reduces strain on the heart, and being on the floor reduces the risk of injury if they collapse.
first-aid-0230: What is angina, and how do its symptoms differ from a heart attack, according to the British Red Cross?
A sudden complete artery blockage causing severe pain that does not ease with rest or medication
Narrowed arteries causing pain that eases with rest and prescribed medication
Lung inflammation causing cough and fever
In angina, narrowed arteries reduce blood reaching the heart. Unlike a heart attack, its symptoms ease with rest and prescribed medication.
first-aid-0231: What unusual feeling does St John Ambulance list among heart attack symptoms?
Signs include crushing chest pain, breathlessness, heavy sweating, and a sense of impending doom.
first-aid-0232: In the FAST test for recognizing a stroke, what does A stand for?
Attention: can they remember what just happened?
Arms: can they raise both arms?
FAST stands for Face, Arms, Speech, and Time to call emergency services.
first-aid-0233: Why should someone with a suspected stroke not be given food or drink, according to St John Ambulance?
Water increases bleeding in the brain
Someone having a stroke may have difficulty swallowing, so give them nothing to eat or drink.
first-aid-0234: What causes a stroke, according to St John Ambulance?
A blockage or bleeding in the brain's blood vessels
Inner ear inflammation causing severe dizziness
A stroke occurs when the brain's blood supply is interrupted, depriving it of oxygen because of a blockage or bleeding in its vessels.
first-aid-0235: During an epileptic seizure, what must a first aider not do?
Restrain the person or put anything in their mouth
Place a soft cushion under their head
Move sharp objects and hot drinks away
Do not restrain the person or put anything in their mouth. Protect their head and remove objects that could injure them.
first-aid-0236: When does an epileptic seizure require calling emergency services, according to the British Red Cross?
If it lasts more than five minutes
If it lasts less than a minute
If the person has known epilepsy and recovers quickly
Call emergency services if it is their first seizure, lasts more than five minutes, causes injury, or has an unknown cause.
first-aid-0237: After an epileptic seizure ends, how should the person be positioned if they are breathing?
On their side with their head tilted back
Standing and walking around the room to regain energy
On their back with a high pillow
After the seizure, help them lie on their side with their head tilted back to keep them breathing.
first-aid-0238: Why does St John Ambulance advise filming a seizure on a phone if possible, after making the person safe?
An ambulance will not come without a video
To publish it and raise awareness of epilepsy
The recording may help with diagnosis later
So the person knows how they looked and is not embarrassed
After calling for help and making the person safe, a video of the seizure may help doctors diagnose it.
first-aid-0239: How long may full recovery from an epileptic seizure take, according to St John Ambulance?
Full recovery from a seizure may take 15 to 30 minutes.
first-aid-0240: What causes febrile seizures in children?
A light blow to the head during play

Febrile seizures are caused by fever and raised temperature. Protect the child from injury, time the seizure, and call emergency services when needed, then place them in the recovery position afterward.
first-aid-0241: At what age are febrile seizures most common, according to the British Red Cross?
Only in the first weeks after birth
Febrile seizures usually affect infants and children aged six months to three years.
first-aid-0242: Should a child having a febrile seizure be placed in a cold bath to cool them?
Yes, a cold bath is the fastest cooling method
No, put them in hot water to make them sleep
Yes, if the seizure continues for more than one minute
No, cold water is distressing and may cause hypothermia
Do not put the child in a cold bath or shower or try to cool them during the seizure. Protect them from injury and call emergency services when needed.
first-aid-0243: Approximately what is normal body temperature, according to the British Red Cross?
Normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius. A child's temperature is considered high at 38 degrees or above.
first-aid-0244: Should a feverish child be sponged with water to cool them, according to the British Red Cross?
Yes, with ice water to lower the temperature quickly before anything else
No, cover them with heavy blankets instead
It is not recommended; the key is not to cool them rapidly
Yes, with alcohol instead of water
Sponging and cold baths are not recommended. Avoid rapid cooling; remove excess clothing and give fluids instead.
first-aid-0245: What happens to the airways during an asthma attack, according to the British Red Cross?
They narrow, making inhaling and exhaling difficult
They widen, allowing too much air in
They fill with water, causing coughing
They suddenly become blocked by a foreign object
During an asthma attack, the tubes carrying air into and out of the lungs narrow, making breathing difficult.
first-aid-0246: What color is an asthma reliever inhaler usually, according to the British Red Cross?
Reliever inhalers are usually blue, while preventer inhalers may be brown or white.
first-aid-0247: What is a spacer used with an asthma inhaler?
An electronic device that measures the severity of an asthma attack
A small oxygen mask placed on the face until the attack ends completely
A mask that prevents dust from entering the nose
A hollow cylinder attached to the inhaler to deliver medicine more effectively
A spacer is a hollow cylinder attached to an inhaler. Medicine collects in it and is inhaled slowly. It is used especially with children.
first-aid-0248: Should a first aider leave someone having an asthma attack to seek help?
Yes, after they use their inhaler
No, the attack may worsen quickly
Yes, if the attack is mild
No, unless the person is an adult
Do not leave the person alone because the attack may worsen quickly. Ask someone else to call emergency services if needed.
first-aid-0249: Which position can help a child breathe after using their inhaler during an asthma attack, according to the British Red Cross?
Lying completely flat on their back
Sitting upright and leaning slightly forward may ease breathing. Encourage slow, deep breaths.
first-aid-0250: Which sign does St John Ambulance mention as indicating low oxygen during an asthma attack?
A gray-blue color in the lips, earlobes, and nail beds
Intense redness of the face and neck
Heavy cold sweating of the palms and soles with facial redness
Yellowing of the whites of the eyes
Signs of low oxygen include a gray-blue color in the lips, earlobes, and nail beds.
first-aid-0251: In which asthma situation should a first aider call emergency services, according to the British Red Cross?
The person improves after using the inhaler
The person has their inhaler and spacer
This is the person's first attack
The attack is mild and resolves quickly
Call emergency services if this is the first attack, the inhaler does not help, no medication is available, or the person worsens or becomes exhausted.
first-aid-0252: How quickly can anaphylactic shock develop after contact with a trigger, according to the British Red Cross?
Anaphylactic shock develops within seconds or minutes of contact with the trigger and is an emergency.
first-aid-0253: Which foods does the British Red Cross mention as common causes of allergic reactions?
Nuts, shellfish, eggs, and dairy products
White bread, water, salt, and sugar
Common triggers include pollen, stings, latex, and foods such as nuts, shellfish, eggs, and dairy products.
first-aid-0254: What does the auto-injector carried by someone at risk of anaphylaxis contain, according to St John Ambulance?
An auto-injector is a prefilled device containing adrenaline, which helps relieve the allergic reaction.
first-aid-0255: After using an auto-injector for someone with anaphylaxis, what should be done with it, according to the British Red Cross?
Return it to its case for reuse
Throw it in a bin immediately
Hand it to the ambulance team when they arrive
Break it so nobody can use it
Give the used injector to the ambulance crew when they arrive.
first-aid-0256: Someone with anaphylaxis is having difficulty breathing. How should they be positioned, according to St John Ambulance?
Lay the person down with their legs raised, unless they have difficulty breathing, in which case sit them up.
first-aid-0257: Where should an anaphylaxis auto-injector be administered, according to American Red Cross guidelines?
In the abdomen around the navel
In the arm above the elbow
In the middle of the outer thigh
Choose the middle of the outer side of one thigh for the injection, and hold the device in place for the time stated in its instructions.
first-aid-0258: What signs of low blood sugar in someone with diabetes does the British Red Cross mention?
Hot dry skin and fruity-smelling breath
Cool clammy skin, sweating, drowsiness, and confusion
Itchy skin and a red rash
Signs of low blood sugar include cool clammy skin, sweating, drowsiness, confusion, and feeling faint.
first-aid-0259: Why should someone with diabetes and low blood sugar not be given a diet fizzy drink?
It contains no sugar, so it will not help
It raises blood sugar dangerously quickly
Diet drinks contain no sugar, so they do not help raise low blood sugar.
first-aid-0260: If it is unclear whether a conscious person's blood sugar is low or high, would giving sugary food usually harm them if it is high, according to the British Red Cross?
It usually would not harm them
When in doubt, give sugar to a conscious person who can swallow. If their blood sugar is high, this usually will not harm them. Call emergency services if they do not improve.
first-aid-0261: Which sign of high blood sugar does St John Ambulance mention?
Sweet fruity breath and extreme thirst
Signs of high blood sugar include warm dry skin, rapid pulse and breathing, sweet fruity breath, extreme thirst, and drowsiness.
first-aid-0262: Which organ secretes insulin to regulate blood sugar, according to St John Ambulance?
Insulin is a substance secreted by the pancreas, which lies behind the stomach, and regulates blood sugar levels.
first-aid-0263: Someone with diabetes appears to have low blood sugar but is not fully alert. Why should they not be given food or drink, according to St John Ambulance?
Sugar is harmful in this situation
If the person is not fully alert, do not give food or drink because they could choke.
first-aid-0264: What causes fainting (a brief loss of consciousness), according to the British Red Cross?
A temporary reduction in blood flow to the brain
A sudden rise in blood sugar
Fainting is caused by a temporary reduction in blood flow to the brain and may involve a brief loss of consciousness.
first-aid-0265: Someone feels they are about to faint. What does the British Red Cross suggest?
Lie on their back and raise their legs
Lying on their back with their legs raised improves blood flow to the brain.
first-aid-0266: After someone who fainted regains consciousness and improves, how should they be helped to sit up, according to St John Ambulance?
After drinking plenty of cold water
After lying down for a full hour
Reassure the person and, once they improve, help them sit up slowly over a few minutes.
first-aid-0267: Someone feels the signs of fainting. Which preventive measure does the American Red Cross mention?
Hold their breath for a long time
Cross their legs or tense their leg muscles
Ways to prevent fainting include lying on the back, crossing the legs or tensing their muscles, and loosening tight clothing.
first-aid-0268: Why does St John Ambulance advise against having someone who is hyperventilating (breathing rapidly and deeply) breathe into a paper bag?
A plastic bag is needed instead
The person might tear the bag
It may make their condition worse
Breathing into a paper bag is not recommended because it may worsen the condition. Reassure the person and move them somewhere quiet instead.
first-aid-0269: A child is breathing very rapidly. What does St John Ambulance say about hyperventilation in children?
It happens every day after play
It is very common and needs no action
It is rare, so other causes should be considered
It is treated by breathing into a paper bag
Hyperventilation is rare in children, so other causes of their rapid breathing should be considered.
first-aid-0271: Should a first aider wait for a rash before calling emergency services when meningitis is suspected?
Yes, if the person is an adult
Yes, a rash is the only definite sign
No, the rash appears late and may never appear
No, unless their temperature is normal
Do not wait for a rash. It usually appears in later stages and may not appear at all, and the person may deteriorate rapidly.
first-aid-0272: Which sign on an infant's head does the British Red Cross mention among meningitis symptoms?
The fontanelle, the soft spot on top of an infant's head, may become bulging or firm, with high-pitched crying and floppiness.
first-aid-0273: What is sepsis, according to St John Ambulance?
A superficial skin infection that clears by itself
High blood pressure from anxiety and severe chronic stress after illness
An excessive bodily response to infection that may cause organ failure
Sepsis is a life-threatening condition in which the immune system goes into overdrive fighting infection, reducing blood supply to vital organs.
first-aid-0274: Which urinary sign does St John Ambulance list among adult sepsis symptoms?
Urine changes color after eating beetroot
No urination in the past 24 hours
Large amounts of clear urine after drinking water
Signs of sepsis include difficulty urinating or no urination in 24 hours.
first-aid-0275: What is croup in children, according to the British Red Cross?
A blocked nose caused by a cold
A middle ear infection causing pain, fever, and a mild cough at bedtime
Swelling of the voice box and airway causing a barking cough
A skin allergy causing a red rash
Croup is swelling of the voice box and airway that makes breathing difficult and causes a short barking cough.
first-aid-0276: When are croup attacks most common in children, according to the British Red Cross?
Croup symptoms often worsen at night. Sitting up and reassurance help breathing. Seek medical advice because the child may need treatment.
first-aid-0277: Should someone who has swallowed a harmful substance be made to vomit?
No, unless the substance is medicine or cough syrup
Yes, if they have no symptoms
Yes, to expel the substance quickly
No, it could damage the throat or block the airway
Do not induce vomiting: it may injure the throat or block the airway, and a corrosive substance burns the throat again on the way out.
first-aid-0278: Why should someone who swallowed a harmful substance not be given anything to drink, according to the British Red Cross?
Water dilutes the substance so it cannot be detected in later medical tests
The liquid may speed up absorption of the substance into the body
It completely stops the substance from acting
Liquid enters the stomach and breaks down the harmful substance, which may then be absorbed into the body faster.
first-aid-0279: A child swallowed something harmful but seems completely well. What does the British Red Cross recommend?
Give milk to dilute the substance
Give salty water to induce vomiting
Call emergency services even if there are no symptoms, because some symptoms may be delayed.
first-aid-0280: What information should a first aider try to obtain from someone who swallowed a harmful substance?
Their parents' names and home address
When and how long they slept
What they swallowed, when, and how much
Ask about the substance, the time it was swallowed, and the amount, because emergency services need this information.
first-aid-0281: Why should a first aider keep the substance's container or a sample of the person's vomit, according to St John Ambulance?
To help professionals identify the poison
To return it to the pharmacy
To document the incident for the police
Containers, labels, and a vomit sample may help healthcare professionals identify the poisonous substance.
first-aid-0282: Which group is most at risk of poisoning, according to the American Red Cross?
Young adults aged twenty to thirty
Most poisoning occurs at home. Children under five, especially those who crawl, are most at risk.
first-aid-0283: What poisoning prevention advice does the American Red Cross give regarding medicines and children?
Do not call medicine candy to persuade a child to take it
Store medicine in candy containers so it is easy to find
Leave medicines on the table where adults can see them
Do not call medicine candy even if it tastes sweet. Keep medicines in their original containers in a locked location.
first-aid-0284: Why is carbon monoxide difficult to detect, according to St John Ambulance?
It has no taste or smell
Carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas with no taste or smell, making it difficult to detect.
first-aid-0285: Someone has carbon monoxide poisoning in a room full of fumes. What does St John Ambulance warn the first aider against?
Helping the person get outside into fresh air
Staying with the person until help arrives
Help the person get outside into fresh air, but do not enter the fume-filled area yourself.
first-aid-0286: What does the American Red Cross call carbon monoxide?
Carbon monoxide is called the invisible killer because it cannot be seen, smelled, or heard.
first-aid-0287: How many rapid beeps does a carbon monoxide alarm usually sound at a dangerous gas level, according to the American Red Cross?
A smoke alarm usually sounds three rapid beeps, while a carbon monoxide alarm sounds four rapid beeps.
first-aid-0288: At least how many feet from a home should a portable generator be operated, according to the American Red Cross?
Operate generators and all engine-powered machines at least 20 feet from the home to avoid carbon monoxide.
first-aid-0289: Which action does the American Red Cross advise against to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning?
Using a gas oven to heat the home
Do not use a gas oven or stove to heat the home, or a barbecue indoors or in a garage.
first-aid-0290: Can a carbon monoxide alarm replace a smoke alarm, according to the American Red Cross?
Yes, if the home is small
No, a smoke alarm replaces it instead
Do not use a carbon monoxide alarm instead of a smoke alarm. Each has its own function, and both are needed.
first-aid-0291: After the last episode of diarrhea or vomiting due to food poisoning, how many hours does St John Ambulance recommend staying away from work or school?
Stay away from work or school for at least 48 hours after the last episode.
first-aid-0292: To prevent the spread of food poisoning infection, what does St John Ambulance recommend for washing hands?
Soap and water rather than alcohol hand sanitizer
Wash hands regularly with soap and water rather than hand sanitizer.
first-aid-0293: When comforting someone distressed after an incident, why does the British Red Cross caution against saying 'Everything will be all right'?
It prevents them from seeking help from professionals and family
It may be untrue and may seem to minimize their feelings
The statement may not always be true and may seem to minimize their feelings. It is better to show that you are listening and offer support.
first-aid-0294: According to the British Red Cross, do most people who help casualties after accidents experience psychological trauma?
Yes, if the casualty is a stranger
No, most do not and are glad they tried to help
No, because they feel nothing during first aid and remember nothing afterward
Yes, all need lengthy psychological treatment
Most people do not experience psychological trauma after helping others. Anyone who feels distressed should talk to someone they trust.
first-aid-0295: If a home catches fire, the family may have very little time to escape. How long does the American Red Cross estimate?
You may have only two minutes to escape a home fire, so working smoke alarms and a practiced escape plan are essential.
first-aid-0296: How often does the American Red Cross recommend testing home smoke alarms?
Test smoke alarms once a month and replace their batteries if they do not work.
first-aid-0297: How often each year does the American Red Cross recommend practicing a home fire escape plan?
Only once when moving into the home
Practice the escape plan at least twice a year so everyone can get out in under two minutes.
first-aid-0298: What rule does the American Red Cross teach for a home fire?
Hide in the bathroom until firefighters arrive
Get out, stay out, and call for help
Put out the fire yourself first, then leave
Get out, stay out, and call for help. Do not go back inside for anything or anyone.
first-aid-0299: If you must escape through smoke, how should you move, according to the American Red Cross?
Cover your head with a dry blanket and walk upright
Stand upright and run as fast as possible
Get low and move under the smoke toward the exit
Hold your breath and walk slowly upright
Get low and move under the smoke toward the exit, closing doors behind you.
first-aid-0300: You find a hot door handle while escaping a fire. What should you do, according to the American Red Cross?
Kick it open to get out
Do not open it; use your second escape route
Wet it with water, then open it
Open it quickly and go through
Do not open doors that are hot to the touch. Use the second exit.
first-aid-0301: If smoke and fire trap you in a room, what does the American Red Cross recommend?
Jump from the window regardless of the floor's height
Hide under the bed until firefighters arrive
Stay inside with the door closed, place a wet towel beneath it, and signal from the window
Open the door and run down the hallway at full speed
Stay in the room with the door closed, place a wet towel under the door, call the fire service, and signal from the window with bright fabric or a flashlight.
first-aid-0302: How should you get down during a fire in a building with elevators, according to the American Red Cross?
Use the stairs to escape a fire in a building with elevators.
first-aid-0303: Oil in a frying pan catches fire on the stove. What is the correct response, according to the American Red Cross?
Blow on it to extinguish it
Cover it with a lid and turn off the stove
Carry it quickly to the sink
Slide a lid over the pan, turn off the stove, and leave the lid in place until it cools completely. Never pour water on an oil fire.
first-aid-0304: Where do most home fires start, according to the American Red Cross?
In gardens because of the sun
In the kitchen while cooking on the stove
In bathrooms because of water heaters
Most home fires start in the kitchen while cooking, usually on the stovetop rather than in the oven.
first-aid-0305: At least how many feet should flammable materials be kept from heaters and anything that produces heat, according to the American Red Cross?
Keep anything that can burn at least three feet from anything that gets hot, such as heaters.
first-aid-0306: Which appliance's lint filter should be cleaned after every use to prevent fire?
Clean the clothes dryer's lint filter after every use, because lint buildup is a leading cause of dryer fires.
first-aid-0307: How often does the American Red Cross recommend replacing smoke alarms?
Replace smoke alarms every 10 years because they lose sensitivity over time.
first-aid-0308: In the PASS method of using a fire extinguisher, where should the nozzle be aimed?
At the ceiling above the fire
At the top of the flames
At the base of the fire
PASS: Pull the pin, Aim at the base of the fire, Squeeze the handle, and Sweep the nozzle from side to side.
first-aid-0309: What fire extinguisher rating does the American Red Cross recommend for homes?
An A-B-C rated extinguisher is recommended for homes.
first-aid-0311: Before trying to put out a small fire with an extinguisher, where should your back face, according to the American Red Cross?
Toward the fire to protect your face
Toward an exit you can reach quickly
Toward the wall farthest from the door
Everyone must already be outside, the fire service must have been called, the fire must be small, and your back must face a nearby exit.
first-aid-0312: What does the American Red Cross advise using instead of candles during a power outage?
Use flashlights rather than candles during power outages, and never leave a burning candle unattended.
first-aid-0313: How many escape routes from each room should family members know, according to the American Red Cross?
All family members should know two ways out of each room and the meeting place outside the home.
first-aid-0314: If a smoke alarm bothers you while cooking, what does the American Red Cross recommend?
Remove its battery until cooking is finished
Cover it with a plastic bag
Use the silence button rather than disabling the alarm
Permanently disconnect the alarm from the kitchen
Never disable a smoke alarm. Use its silence button, and consider another type if nuisance alarms recur.
first-aid-0315: Which use of electrical extension cords does the American Red Cross advise against to prevent fire?
Fire prevention advice includes checking cords and sockets, using extension cords to reach distant outlets, and avoiding running cords under carpets.
first-aid-0316: What safe alternative to ordinary candles does the American Red Cross suggest for homes with children?
Flameless candles with a light bulb
Flameless candles use a light bulb instead of a flame, so there is no danger if a child knocks them over.
money-economy-0001: How is the Bahraini dinar subdivided?
The Bahraini dinar is divided into one thousand fils, like the Kuwaiti dinar.
money-economy-0002: What is the name of the smaller unit into which the Omani rial is divided?
The Omani rial is divided into one thousand baisa.
money-economy-0003: The Saudi riyal is divided into one hundred units. What is each unit called?
The halala is the smaller unit of the Saudi riyal. One riyal equals one hundred halalas.
money-economy-0004: Into how many millimes is the Tunisian dinar divided?
One Tunisian dinar equals one thousand millimes.
money-economy-0005: What is the smaller unit of the Qatari riyal?
The Qatari riyal is divided into one hundred dirhams.
money-economy-0006: How many fils are in one UAE dirham?
The UAE dirham is divided into one hundred fils.
money-economy-0007: The Egyptian pound is divided into one hundred units. What is each called?
One Egyptian pound equals one hundred piastres, and one piastre equals ten milliemes.
money-economy-0008: How is the Libyan dinar subdivided?
The Libyan dinar is divided into one thousand dirhams.
money-economy-0009: What is the smaller unit of the Moroccan dirham called?
The Moroccan dirham is divided into one hundred centimes.
money-economy-0010: The yen is Japan's official currency.
money-economy-0011: The won is South Korea's currency. What is its international code under ISO 4217?
The ISO 4217 code for the South Korean won is KRW.
money-economy-0012: The ringgit is Malaysia's official currency.
money-economy-0013: Which of these is Thailand's currency?
The baht is Thailand's official currency.
money-economy-0014: The dong is the official currency of which country?
money-economy-0015: What is Indonesia's official currency called?
The Indonesian rupiah is Indonesia's currency.
money-economy-0016: What is Brazil's official currency called?
The Brazilian real is Brazil's currency.
money-economy-0017: The sol is the official currency of which South American country?
The sol is Peru's currency, and its name means sun in Spanish.
money-economy-0018: Venezuela's currency bears the name of a South American independence leader. What is it called?
The bolivar was named after Simon Bolivar.
money-economy-0019: The guarani is the currency of which country?
The guarani is Paraguay's currency and bears the name of the Guarani people.
money-economy-0020: Guatemala's currency bears the name of its national bird. What is it called?
The quetzal is Guatemala's currency and the name of its national bird.
money-economy-0021: Costa Rica's currency, the colon, was named after:
The colon is named after Columbus, whose Spanish name is Colon.
money-economy-0022: The name of South Africa's currency, the rand, comes from:
The founder of the first bank in Cape Town
A large river flowing through Johannesburg
A type of antelope found in the country
The rand is named after the Witwatersrand ridge, where most of the country's gold was discovered.
money-economy-0023: The naira is the official currency of which country?
money-economy-0024: The name of Ghana's currency, the cedi, means what in a local language?
Cowrie shells were once used as money, and the name cedi comes from them.
money-economy-0025: The Kenyan shilling is Kenya's currency.
money-economy-0026: The birr is the official currency of which African country?
money-economy-0027: What does kwacha, the name of Zambia's currency, mean in a local language?
Kwacha means dawn, symbolizing the dawn of independence.
money-economy-0028: The Turkish lira is divided into one hundred units called:
One Turkish lira equals one hundred kurus.
money-economy-0029: What is Afghanistan's official currency called?
money-economy-0030: The taka is the official currency of which country?
money-economy-0032: The Russian ruble is divided into one hundred units. What is each called?
One ruble equals one hundred kopecks.
money-economy-0033: What does zloty, the name of Poland's currency, mean?
Zloty is a Polish word meaning golden.
money-economy-0034: The name of Hungary's currency, the forint, comes from the currency of which Italian city?
Forint comes from the gold florin minted in Florence.
money-economy-0035: Why is the Swiss franc represented by CHF?
CH is the first two letters of Zurich's name
CH abbreviates the name of the first Swiss bank
CH abbreviates the German word for franc
CH stands for Confoederatio Helvetica, Switzerland's Latin name.
money-economy-0036: Before the pound sterling was decimalized in 1971, how many pence was it worth?
A pound equaled twenty shillings, and a shilling twelve pence, making 240 pence.
money-economy-0037: The Indian rupee is divided into one hundred units. What is each called?
One Indian rupee equals one hundred paise.
money-economy-0038: What is the basic unit of China's currency, the renminbi?
Renminbi is the currency's name, and the yuan is its basic unit.
money-economy-0039: What does renminbi, the name of China's currency, mean?
Renminbi literally means the people's currency.
money-economy-0040: In which year did euro banknotes and coins enter circulation?
The euro was introduced as an accounting currency in 1999, and its notes and coins entered circulation on 1 January 2002.
money-economy-0041: The euro symbol, ?, was inspired by which letter?
The euro symbol was inspired by the Greek letter epsilon and the first letter of Europe.
money-economy-0042: A dime equals ten cents, or one tenth of a dollar.
money-economy-0043: The word dollar derives from which old European silver coin?
Dollar derives from the thaler, which was minted in Bohemia.
money-economy-0044: The word dinar derives from the name of which coin?
Dinar derives from the Roman denarius.
money-economy-0047: The word fils derives from which coin?
A Persian coin called the daniq
A Byzantine coin called the follis
A Greek coin called the obol
An Indian coin called the anna
Fils comes from the Byzantine copper follis.
money-economy-0048: The word rupee comes from a Sanskrit word meaning:
Rupee comes from a Sanskrit word related to silver.
money-economy-0049: What does the Spanish word peso, used to name many currencies, mean?
money-economy-0050: How many piastres are in one Jordanian dinar?
One Jordanian dinar equals ten dirhams, one hundred piastres, or one thousand fils.
money-economy-0051: What is the economic term for a sustained general rise in the price level?
Inflation is a sustained general rise in prices that weakens money's purchasing power.
money-economy-0052: A general decline in the prices of goods and services is called:
Deflation is a general fall in the price level and is the opposite of inflation.
money-economy-0053: Inflation combined with economic stagnation and rising unemployment is called:
Stagflation combines rising prices with weak growth and increased unemployment.
money-economy-0054: Which country experienced the famous hyperinflation of 1923, when banknotes were carried in carts?
Germany experienced hyperinflation during the Weimar Republic, peaking in 1923.
money-economy-0055: Which country's currency experienced the highest known monthly inflation in history in 1946?
The Hungarian pengo experienced the highest recorded inflation in history in 1946.
money-economy-0056: The market value of all final goods and services produced within a country over a given period is called:
This is the definition of gross domestic product (GDP).
money-economy-0057: The value of the best alternative forgone when choosing something else is called:
Opportunity cost is what you lose from the best alternative you forgo.
money-economy-0058: The basic economic problem is that resources are limited while wants are many. What is this called?
Scarcity is the limitation of resources relative to people's wants and is the foundation of economics.
money-economy-0059: A market with a single seller offering a product with no close substitute is called:
A monopoly occurs when one seller alone controls the market.
money-economy-0060: A market with only one buyer and many sellers is called:
A monopsony is a market with a single buyer.
money-economy-0061: A market dominated by a few large sellers is called:
An oligopoly is a market dominated by a small number of producers.
money-economy-0062: An agreement among competing companies to fix prices or divide the market is called:
A cartel is a group of independent producers that agree on prices or output.
money-economy-0063: The theory of comparative advantage in international trade is primarily attributed to:
David Ricardo formulated comparative advantage theory in his 1817 book.
money-economy-0064: In which year was Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations published?
The Wealth of Nations was published in 1776.
money-economy-0065: The phrase 'invisible hand,' describing the market's self-regulation, is associated with:
Adam Smith used the expression 'invisible hand' in his books.
money-economy-0066: Who wrote The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money, published in 1936?
Keynes wrote the book, which formed the basis of Keynesian economics.
money-economy-0067: Who proposed that population grows geometrically (exponentially) while food supply grows arithmetically?
This summarizes Malthus's theory of population.
money-economy-0068: The law stating that bad money drives good money out of circulation is attributed to:
This is Gresham's law, named after Thomas Gresham.
money-economy-0069: Engel's law states that as a family's income increases:
The proportion of income spent on food falls
The proportion of income spent on food rises
Total spending on all needs falls
The proportion of income spent on food stays constant
Engel observed that food's share of income falls as income rises, even if the amount spent increases.
money-economy-0070: Increasing one production input while keeping the others fixed raises output by progressively smaller amounts beyond a certain point. What is this law called?
This is the law of diminishing returns.
money-economy-0071: The statement 'supply creates its own demand' is known as whose law?
This summarizes Say's law, attributed to Jean-Baptiste Say.
money-economy-0072: The Pareto principle states that roughly 80% of results often come from approximately:
This is the Pareto principle, or the 80/20 rule.
money-economy-0073: The Laffer curve describes the relationship between:
The Laffer curve shows that raising tax rates does not always increase tax revenue.
money-economy-0074: Which two variables does the Phillips curve relate?
The Phillips curve describes an inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment in the short run.
money-economy-0075: The measure of how much quantity demanded changes when a product's price changes is called:
Price elasticity of demand measures how quantity demanded responds to a price change.
money-economy-0076: A good for which demand increases when its price rises, contrary to the usual law of demand, is called:
A Giffen good is an exception to the law of demand.
money-economy-0077: Two goods consumed together, such as a car and its fuel, are called:
Demand for one complementary good is linked to demand for the other.
money-economy-0078: If the price of tea rises and demand for coffee increases, the two goods are:
Substitute goods replace one another, so demand for one increases when the other becomes more expensive.
money-economy-0079: A lighthouse that guides all ships and whose benefits cannot be withheld from anyone is a famous example of:
A public good is non-excludable, and one person's use does not reduce its availability to others.
money-economy-0080: Pollution affecting a neighborhood because of a nearby factory is an economic example of:
An externality is harm or benefit affecting a party not involved in the activity.
money-economy-0081: Who wrote the famous 1968 article The Tragedy of the Commons?
Ecologist Garrett Hardin published the article in Science in 1968.
money-economy-0082: The difference between the value of a country's goods exports and imports is called:
The trade balance equals exports minus imports.
money-economy-0083: If the value of a country's exports exceeds its imports, it has:
Exports exceeding imports create a trade surplus; the reverse is a deficit.
money-economy-0084: A tax imposed by a country on imported goods is called:
Customs duties, or tariffs, are imposed on imports.
money-economy-0085: Selling a product in a foreign market for less than its domestic price or below cost is called:
Dumping is pricing that harms producers in the importing country. Countries counter it with anti-dumping duties.
money-economy-0086: A policy of restricting imports through tariffs and quotas to protect domestic industries is called:
Protectionism protects domestic producers from foreign competition.
money-economy-0087: Government use of public spending and taxes to influence the economy is called:
Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxes.
money-economy-0088: Which institution usually conducts a country's monetary policy?
The central bank manages the money supply and monetary policy.
money-economy-0089: When government expenditure exceeds revenue in a fiscal year, this is called:
Expenditure exceeding revenue creates a budget deficit.
money-economy-0090: An official government decision to lower its currency's value against other currencies is called:
Devaluation is an official measure under a fixed exchange rate system.
money-economy-0091: The Gini coefficient is an economic indicator that measures:
The Gini coefficient measures inequality in income or wealth distribution.
money-economy-0092: A basket of goods and services whose prices are regularly monitored to measure inflation forms the basis of which index?
The consumer price index measures the average price change of a fixed basket of goods and services.
money-economy-0093: The branch of economics studying individuals, firms, and individual markets is called:
Microeconomics studies small units, while macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole.
money-economy-0094: Which French economic school considered land and agriculture the true source of wealth?
The physiocrats, led by Francois Quesnay, regarded agriculture as the source of wealth.
money-economy-0095: Which economic doctrine viewed national wealth as the accumulation of gold and silver through exports exceeding imports?
Mercantilism dominated Europe between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries.
money-economy-0096: Adam Smith used a pin factory to illustrate the benefit of:
Smith showed that dividing pin-making stages among workers multiplies production.
money-economy-0097: Which economist is associated with the theory of creative destruction in innovation?
Schumpeter was known for creative destruction: new innovation displaces the old.
money-economy-0098: What was the global economic crisis that began with the New York stock market crash of 1929 called?
The Great Depression began in the United States in 1929 and spread worldwide.
money-economy-0099: What is 29 October 1929, the day the New York stock market crashed, known as?
It is known as Black Tuesday and was one of the worst days of the crash.
money-economy-0100: The prices of which flower's bulbs reached extraordinary levels in the Netherlands before crashing in 1637?
The event is known as tulip mania and is considered one of the earliest recorded economic bubbles.
money-economy-0102: What metal were the earliest Lydian coins made from?
Electrum, a natural mixture of gold and silver
The earliest Lydian coins were made from electrum, a natural alloy of gold and silver.
money-economy-0103: Which Lydian king is credited with minting the first pure gold coins?
Croesus, king of Lydia, is credited with the first minting of pure gold and pure silver coins.
money-economy-0104: The first government-issued paper money in history appeared in:
Jiaozi paper money appeared in China under the Song dynasty.
money-economy-0105: The first European bank to issue banknotes was in:
Stockholms Banco issued the first European banknotes in 1661.
money-economy-0106: Which is considered the world's oldest surviving central bank?
Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, was founded in 1668.
money-economy-0107: In which year was the Bank of England founded?
The Bank of England was founded in 1694.
money-economy-0108: The Federal Reserve System, the US central bank, was founded in:
The Federal Reserve was established by an act in 1913.
money-economy-0109: In which year was the Bretton Woods conference, which established a global monetary system after World War II, held?
The conference was held in July 1944.
money-economy-0110: In which US state is Bretton Woods, the location of the famous monetary conference?
The conference took place at the Mount Washington Hotel in Bretton Woods, New Hampshire.
money-economy-0111: Which US president suspended the dollar's convertibility into gold in 1971?
The decision became known as the Nixon shock.
money-economy-0112: A monetary system in which a currency's value is tied to a fixed quantity of gold is called:
Under the gold standard, a monetary unit equals a specified weight of gold.
money-economy-0113: Money whose value comes from government decree rather than backing by a precious metal is called:
Fiat money has no commodity backing, and its value rests on the force of law.
money-economy-0114: Directly exchanging one good for another without using money is called:
Barter is the direct exchange of goods and services without money.
money-economy-0115: The main difficulty with barter is that both parties must simultaneously have exactly what the other wants. This is called:
The law of supply and demand
The requirement for a double coincidence of wants made money an easier medium of exchange.
money-economy-0116: When you say a book costs three dinars, you are using money as:
As a unit of account, money measures and compares the values of things.
money-economy-0118: Which small seashells were used as money for centuries in Africa and Asia?
Cowrie shells are among history's best-known forms of commodity money.
money-economy-0119: Large stone discs called rai were used as money on which island?
Rai stones were used as money by the people of Yap in the Pacific Ocean.
money-economy-0120: Why was the Spanish silver dollar known as a piece of eight?
It was minted in eight cities
It equaled eight Spanish reales, hence the name piece of eight.
money-economy-0121: Which Austrian silver coin circulated for a long time in Yemen, the Arabian Peninsula, and East Africa?
The Maria Theresa thaler remained in circulation in the region until the twentieth century.
money-economy-0122: Approximately how many grams does the Islamic gold dinar (one mithqal) weigh?
A dinar is one mithqal and weighs about 4.25 grams.
money-economy-0123: Ten dirhams of the Sharia weight standard equal how many mithqals?
The established ratio is that every ten dirhams weigh seven mithqals.
money-economy-0124: Which Egyptian historian wrote Ighathat al-Umma bi-Kashf al-Ghumma about the causes of high prices and debased money?
Al-Maqrizi's Ighathat al-Umma is among the best-known works on high prices and money.
money-economy-0125: Which scholar discussed earnings, prices, and civilization in his Muqaddima, leading many to regard him as a pioneer of economics?
In the Muqaddima, Ibn Khaldun discussed labor, value, prices, and taxes.
money-economy-0126: Judge Abu Yusuf wrote Kitab al-Kharaj at the request of which caliph?
Abu Yusuf wrote Kitab al-Kharaj for al-Rashid about the state's financial resources.
money-economy-0127: Who wrote Kitab al-Amwal, one of the earliest works on Islamic public finance?
Kitab al-Amwal was written by Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam (d. 224 AH).
money-economy-0128: The institution responsible for the Islamic state's funds in earlier times was called:
Bayt al-mal (public treasury) was the treasury of the Islamic state.
money-economy-0129: Which official supervised markets, weights, and measures in Islamic cities?
The muhtasib (market and public conduct inspector)
The muhtasib held the office of hisba (oversight of public conduct), which included supervising markets.
money-economy-0130: What was the document used by Abbasid merchants instead of carrying cash, redeemable in another country, called?
A suftaja (bill of exchange) allowed money to be redeemed in another country, sparing merchants the burden and risks of carrying cash.
money-economy-0132: Which German geographer coined the term Silk Road in the nineteenth century?
money-economy-0133: Which medieval trading alliance of northern European cities had Lubeck as a leading center?
The Hanseatic League included trading cities around the North Sea and Baltic Sea.
money-economy-0134: Which company, founded in 1602, was among the first to offer shares to the public?
The Dutch East India Company (VOC) issued shares to the public from its founding.
money-economy-0135: In which city did the exchange considered the oldest modern securities market originate?
The Amsterdam stock exchange is considered the world's oldest modern securities market.
money-economy-0137: The Buttonwood Agreement, signed under a tree in New York in 1792, formed the basis of:
Brokers signed the agreement that became the basis of the New York Stock Exchange.
money-economy-0138: New York's Wall Street was named after:
An old stone bridge at its end
The first bank established on the street
A wall built by Dutch settlers
A wall built by Dutch settlers in the seventeenth century stood at the site.
money-economy-0139: In which year was the Dow Jones Industrial Average first published?
The index was first published on 26 May 1896.
money-economy-0140: A financial market in which prices decline for a long period and pessimism prevails is called:
A bear market refers to falling prices, and a bull market to rising prices.
money-economy-0141: Which US program aimed to rebuild Western Europe's economy after World War II?
The Marshall Plan provided extensive aid to Western Europe beginning in 1948.
money-economy-0142: The famous South Sea Bubble of 1720 occurred in:
Shares in Britain's South Sea Company collapsed in 1720.
money-economy-0143: Which Scottish economist was associated with the Mississippi Company bubble in France?
John Law took charge of the Mississippi Company (Company of the West) in 1717 and its financial system, which collapsed in 1720.
money-economy-0144: In 1995, the World Trade Organization replaced an earlier international agreement abbreviated as:
The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) preceded the World Trade Organization.
money-economy-0145: Where is the World Trade Organization headquartered?
The organization's headquarters are in Geneva, Switzerland.
money-economy-0146: In which city was the 1960 conference founding the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) held?
OPEC was founded at the Baghdad conference in September 1960.
money-economy-0147: Which American economist led the monetarist school and won the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1976?
Milton Friedman was a leading monetarist and won the Nobel Prize in 1976.
money-economy-0148: In which year was the first Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences awarded?
Sweden's central bank established the prize, which was first awarded in 1969.
money-economy-0149: Which book did Alfred Marshall publish in 1890 that became a fundamental economics reference?
