Marshall's Principles of Economics was published in 1890.
money-economy-0150: Selling a product at its purchase cost plus a known profit agreed by buyer and seller is called:
Murabaha (cost-plus sale) is a sale at cost plus a disclosed, known profit.
money-economy-0151: A partnership in which one party provides capital, the other provides labor, and profit is shared in an agreed ratio is called:
Mudaraba (capital-and-labor partnership) is a partnership between a capital provider and a working partner, with profit shared as agreed.
money-economy-0152: A contract in which each partner contributes capital and they share profit and loss is called:
Musharaka (joint partnership) is a partnership in capital, profit, and loss.
money-economy-0153: A sale in which the price is paid at the contract session and specified goods owed by the seller are delivered at a known future date is called:
Salam (advance-payment sale) is the reverse of installments: payment is immediate and the goods are deferred.
money-economy-0154: A contract in which a buyer asks a manufacturer to make a specified item, such as furniture, with materials and labor provided by the manufacturer is called:
Istisna (manufacturing contract) is a contract to manufacture an item owed by the manufacturer according to specified requirements.
money-economy-0155: A contract for using something for a known period in return for payment, such as renting a house, is called:
Ijara (lease) transfers a benefit, rather than ownership of the asset.
money-economy-0156: What are Islamic financial certificates representing undivided ownership shares in assets or projects called?
Sukuk (asset ownership certificates) represent ownership in real assets rather than interest-bearing debt.
money-economy-0157: Insurance based on cooperation and donations among participants to cover losses suffered by one of them is known as:
Takaful (cooperative insurance) is cooperative coverage in which participants donate to a common fund.
money-economy-0158: One prohibited form of riba (usury) is exchanging gold for gold or dates for dates with an excess on one side. What is this type called?
Riba al-fadl (usury through unequal exchange) is inequality when exchanging a ribawi commodity for the same kind. It is named for the excess in one of the countervalues.
money-economy-0159: An increase in a debt in exchange for extending its due date, the pre-Islamic riba (usury) prohibited by the Quran, is called:
Riba al-nasi'a (usury through deferment) derives from the expression meaning to defer a debt; the increase is in exchange for extra time.
money-economy-0160: Hadiths mention six commodities subject to riba (usury) rules: gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, and...
The six commodities mentioned in the hadith are gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates, and salt.
money-economy-0161: In which surah does Allah say: «وَأَحَلَّ اللَّهُ الْبَيْعَ وَحَرَّمَ الرِّبَا» [But Allāh has permitted trade and has forbidden interest.]? (QuranEnc, 2:275)
money-economy-0162: A sale involving uncertainty and ambiguity that lead to disputes, such as selling fish still in water, is called by jurists:
Gharar (excessive uncertainty) is uncertainty and risk in a contract, and it has been prohibited.
money-economy-0163: Raising the bid for an item without intending to buy it, to deceive others, is called:
Najsh (shill bidding) is raising an item's price without intending to buy it. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, prohibited it.
money-economy-0164: The right of buyer and seller to confirm or cancel a sale while they remain together at the place of contracting is called:
Khiyar al-majlis (option while together) is supported by the hadith: «البيعان بالخيار ما لم يتفرقا» [The buyer and seller retain the option until they part.]
money-economy-0165: In Islamic jurisprudence, making a financial asset security for a debt, recoverable from it if repayment fails, is called:
This is the jurists' definition of rahn (pledge).
money-economy-0166: A loan given to someone in need and repaid with its equivalent, without any stipulated increase, seeking divine reward, is called:
Qard hasan (benevolent loan) is a charitable loan without any interest.
money-economy-0167: A trader sells an item on deferred payment, then buys it back for less in cash from the same buyer as a device to obtain riba (usury). What is this called?
Bay' al-ina (sale and buyback) is a device for obtaining a loan with an increase; the item is merely a means to that end.
money-economy-0168: Retaining an asset's principal while dedicating its benefits to charitable causes is called:
Waqf (charitable endowment) retains the principal and dedicates its benefits.
money-economy-0170: Which Quranic word means prohibited gambling?
Maysir (gambling) means games of chance and is prohibited in Surah Al-Ma'ida.
money-economy-0171: Where is the Islamic Development Bank headquartered?
The Islamic Development Bank is headquartered in Jeddah.
money-economy-0172: The savings bank founded by economist Ahmad al-Najjar in Mit Ghamr in 1963 was an early Islamic banking experiment in:
The Mit Ghamr Savings Bank in Egypt operated without interest.
money-economy-0173: Dubai Islamic Bank, one of the earliest modern commercial Islamic banks, was founded in:
Dubai Islamic Bank was founded in 1975.
money-economy-0174: Where is the Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial Institutions (AAOIFI) headquartered?
The organization is headquartered in Manama, Bahrain.
money-economy-0175: The Arab Monetary Fund is headquartered in:
The Arab Monetary Fund was founded in 1976 and is headquartered in Abu Dhabi.
money-economy-0177: The Organization of Arab Petroleum Exporting Countries (OAPEC) is headquartered in:
OAPEC was founded in 1968 and is headquartered in Kuwait.
money-economy-0178: OPEC has its permanent headquarters in:
OPEC's headquarters moved to Vienna in 1965.
money-economy-0179: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in:
The IMF is headquartered in Washington, DC.
money-economy-0180: The two international institutions born from the Bretton Woods conference were the International Monetary Fund and:
The World Bank and IMF were established at the Bretton Woods conference in 1944.
money-economy-0181: The Bank for International Settlements, described as the central banks' bank, is headquartered in:
It has been headquartered in Basel, Switzerland, since its founding in 1930.
money-economy-0182: The European Central Bank is headquartered in:
The European Central Bank is headquartered in Frankfurt, Germany.
money-economy-0183: Which Muslim scholar did American economist Arthur Laffer cite as having anticipated the idea behind his famous curve?
Laffer stated that Ibn Khaldun anticipated his curve's idea in the Muqaddima.
money-economy-0184: The tax formerly levied on conquered agricultural land in the Islamic state was called:
Kharaj (land tax) is a tax on land.
money-economy-0185: Preserving wealth is one of the five necessities in maqasid al-Sharia (the objectives of Islamic law). Which is another?
The five necessities are religion, life, intellect, lineage, and wealth.
money-economy-0186: In the hadith «البيّعان بالخيار ما لم يتفرّقا» [The buyer and seller retain the option until they part.], what does al-bayyi'an mean?
The two witnesses to the sale
Al-bayyi'an means the two parties to the sale: seller and buyer.
money-economy-0187: If a buyer discovers a pre-existing defect that was not disclosed, what is their right called?
Khiyar al-ayb (option for a defect) is established for the buyer when a defect concealed by the seller is discovered.
money-economy-0189: The technology underlying Bitcoin, which records transactions in a sequential distributed ledger, is called:
Blockchain is a decentralized ledger whose blocks are linked cryptographically.
money-economy-0190: Bitcoin's smallest unit, one hundred-millionth of a bitcoin, is called:
money-economy-0191: Which Italian scholar published the first printed explanation of double-entry bookkeeping in 1494?
Pacioli explained double-entry bookkeeping in his 1494 printed book and became known as the father of accounting.
money-economy-0192: In double-entry bookkeeping, each financial transaction is recorded in two accounts: one as a debit and the other as a:
Each entry has two equal sides: debit and credit.
money-economy-0193: Which financial statement shows a company's assets, liabilities, and owners' equity at a specific date?
The balance sheet is a snapshot of financial position at a particular moment.
money-economy-0194: Which financial statement presents a company's revenue, expenses, and net profit over a given period?
The income statement summarizes revenue, expenses, and the resulting profit or loss during a period.
money-economy-0195: The basic accounting equation is: Assets = Liabilities + ...
money-economy-0196: Allocating the cost of a fixed asset, such as a machine or vehicle, over its useful life is called:
Depreciation allocates an asset's cost over its useful life.
money-economy-0197: Which of these is usually a fixed cost that does not vary with production volume?
Rent is paid whether production rises or falls, so it is a fixed cost.
money-economy-0198: The point at which total revenue equals total costs, with neither profit nor loss, is called:
At the break-even point, there is neither profit nor loss.
money-economy-0199: The difference between sales revenue and the cost of goods sold is called:
Gross profit equals sales minus the cost of goods sold, before deducting other expenses.
money-economy-0200: The ease of converting an asset quickly into cash without a major loss in value is called:
Liquidity is an asset's ability to be converted quickly into cash at a price close to its value.
money-economy-0201: An independent examination of an entity's books and financial statements to verify their accuracy is called:
Auditing is an independent examination of financial information.
money-economy-0202: The document a seller sends a buyer listing goods, quantities, prices, and the amount due is:
An invoice requests the amount due and details the sale.
money-economy-0203: Selling goods in large quantities to traders for resale is called:
A wholesaler sells to traders, while a retailer sells to consumers.
money-economy-0204: A company granting another party the right to operate under its brand name and methods in return for fees is called:
A franchise licenses the use of a brand and business system.
money-economy-0205: The exclusive right granted by a state to an inventor to exploit an invention for a limited period is called:
A patent gives its owner a temporary exclusive right in exchange for disclosing the invention.
money-economy-0206: A company whose capital is divided into equal, tradable shares is called:
A joint-stock company's capital is divided into shares.
money-economy-0207: A business owned by one person who is solely responsible for all its debts is called:
A sole proprietorship is owned by one person who is liable for its debts with all their assets.
money-economy-0208: The part of a company's profit distributed to shareholders is called:
Dividends are shareholders' share of distributed profit.
money-economy-0209: In financial markets, an initial public offering means:
A board of directors' first meeting
A company's first sale of shares to the public
A company's first distribution of profits
An initial public offering (IPO) is the first offering of a company's shares to public investors.
money-economy-0210: The Nikkei 225 measures stock performance on which exchange?
The Nikkei 225 is a Tokyo stock exchange index.
money-economy-0211: The well-known DAX index measures the performance of major companies in:
The DAX is an index of Germany's Frankfurt stock exchange.
money-economy-0212: A company's share price multiplied by the number of its outstanding shares is called:
Market capitalization equals share price multiplied by the number of shares.
money-economy-0213: A debtor's inability to repay debts and the resulting legal proceedings are called:
Bankruptcy is a legal status declaring a debtor unable to repay debts.
money-economy-0214: The tax collected on the difference between the sale price and input cost at each stage of production and distribution is:
Value-added tax is imposed on the value added at each stage.
money-economy-0215: Which of these is a direct tax?
Income tax is paid directly by the taxpayer, while consumption taxes are indirect.
money-economy-0216: A tax whose rate increases as a person's income rises is called:
Under a progressive tax, the rate increases with income.
money-economy-0217: The four elements of the marketing mix are product, price, place, and...
The marketing mix's 4Ps are Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
money-economy-0218: In SWOT analysis, the letters stand for strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and...
SWOT stands for Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats.
money-economy-0219: The FIFO inventory valuation method assumes the goods issued first are:
FIFO stands for First In, First Out.
money-economy-0220: Pricing a product at 9.99 instead of 10 to make it seem cheaper to the buyer is called:
Psychological pricing uses the effect of the first digit on price perception.
money-economy-0221: A product sold at a very low price, possibly below cost, to attract customers to buy other products is called:
It is called a loss leader, and its purpose is to attract customers.
money-economy-0222: An auction that starts at a high price and gradually decreases until a buyer accepts is called:
A Dutch auction uses a descending price.
money-economy-0223: What does the Latin trading phrase Caveat emptor mean?
It means the buyer should check the goods before purchasing.
money-economy-0224: A trader bought an item for 400 dinars and sold it for 500 dinars. What is the profit as a percentage of cost?
Profit is 100 dinars; as a share of cost, 100 / 400 = 25%.
money-economy-0225: A decrease in unit cost as production volume increases is called:
Economies of scale are cost advantages gained by a business through expansion.
money-economy-0226: Assigning some company tasks to a specialized external provider rather than doing them internally is called:
Outsourcing means contracting with an external party.
money-economy-0227: In a limited liability company, a partner is liable for company debts only up to:
Limited liability restricts a partner's obligation to their contribution.
money-economy-0228: Which index measures the performance of the largest hundred companies on the London Stock Exchange?
The FTSE 100 is a London Stock Exchange index.
money-economy-0229: Which financial statement shows cash entering and leaving a company through its various activities over a period?
The statement of changes in equity
The cash flow statement tracks cash movements in operating, investing, and financing activities.
money-economy-0230: Assets bought for use over many years rather than resale, such as buildings and machinery, are called:
Fixed assets are long-term assets used in operations.
money-economy-0231: Which is an example of an intangible asset?
Intangible assets have no physical form, such as trademarks and patents.
money-economy-0232: The term describing one company buying and taking control of another is:
An acquisition occurs when a company buys a controlling stake in another.
money-economy-0233: Transferring ownership or management of a government enterprise to the private sector is called:
Privatization transfers public-sector ownership to the private sector. Nationalization is the reverse.
money-economy-0234: Transferring ownership of a private company to the state is called:
Nationalization transfers a private enterprise into state ownership.
money-economy-0235: In which year was the first product scanned using a barcode in a US store?
A pack of chewing gum was scanned in an Ohio store in 1974.
money-economy-0236: A card that deducts the purchase amount directly from its holder's bank account is called:
A debit card withdraws directly from the account balance.
money-economy-0237: The automated teller machine, allowing cash withdrawals without a teller, first appeared in 1967 in which city?
Barclays opened the first ATM in London in 1967.
money-economy-0238: A written plan estimating expected income and expenses for a future period is called:
A budget is a financial plan for income and spending over a future period.
money-economy-0239: Money set aside for emergencies such as job loss or a sudden car breakdown is called:
An emergency fund is a safety net for unexpected expenses that avoids the need to borrow.
money-economy-0240: An unplanned purchase made suddenly on the spur of the moment is called:
Impulse buying is a sudden, unplanned decision and a major reason for poor saving.
money-economy-0241: Designing products to fail or become outdated after a specified period so consumers must buy replacements is called:
Planned obsolescence is a policy of deliberately shortening a product's life.
money-economy-0242: A scheme based on recruiting new members whose fees benefit earlier members until it collapses is called:
A pyramid scheme is fraud based on recruitment rather than genuine sales, and it inevitably collapses.
money-economy-0243: A fraudulent scheme that pays existing investors 'profits' from new investors' money is named after which fraudster?
The Ponzi scheme is named after Charles Ponzi, who became known for it in the 1920s.
money-economy-0244: The image or mark visible in a banknote when held up to the light is called:
A watermark is made within the paper itself and appears in transmitted light.
money-economy-0246: US dollar banknotes are primarily made from:
They consist of 75% cotton and 25% linen.
money-economy-0247: Grooves on the edges of some precious-metal coins were originally introduced to prevent:
Clipping the edges to remove some metal
A grooved edge revealed anyone filing the edges of gold or silver coins.
money-economy-0248: The study and collection of coins and their history is called:
Numismatics is the study of coins and currency.
money-economy-0249: A troy ounce, used to weigh gold and silver, is approximately:
A troy ounce equals 31.1035 grams and differs from an ordinary ounce.
money-economy-0250: What percentage of 18-karat gold is pure gold?
Gold purity is measured out of 24, so 18 karat = 18 / 24 = 75%.
money-economy-0251: What is the gold content of 21-karat gold, common in Gulf markets?
money-economy-0252: Sterling silver used in jewelry contains what percentage of silver?
Sterling silver contains 925 parts per thousand of silver.
money-economy-0253: The carat used to weigh gemstones equals:
The metric carat is 200 milligrams, or 0.2 grams.
money-economy-0254: The word carat originally refers to the seeds of which tree, once used as weights?
The word is connected to carob seeds, which have similar weights.
money-economy-0255: The official stamp placed on gold and silver articles to indicate purity is called:
A hallmark guarantees a precious metal's purity.
money-economy-0256: Fort Knox in the United States is famous as:
The Fort Knox depository holds a large part of US gold reserves.
money-economy-0257: A coin with an outer ring and an inner core made of two different metals is called:
Bimetallic coins are difficult for counterfeiters.
money-economy-0258: The issuer's profit from the difference between money's face value and its issuance cost is called:
money-economy-0259: Money that the law obliges a creditor to accept in repayment of a debt is called:
Legal tender may not be refused in payment of a debt.
money-economy-0260: Tying a currency's value to another currency or a basket of currencies at a fixed rate is called:
Under a fixed exchange rate system, the rate is fixed and defended by the central bank.
money-economy-0261: An exchange rate system in which a currency's value is determined by market supply and demand is called:
A floating exchange rate is determined by the market.
money-economy-0262: The international reserve unit created by the IMF in 1969 is called:
Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) are a reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969.
money-economy-0263: Money sent by workers abroad to their families in their home countries is called:
Remittances are an important income source for many countries.
money-economy-0264: A commitment by an importer's bank to pay an exporter when the required documents are submitted is called:
A documentary credit assures the exporter of payment and the importer of the documents.
money-economy-0265: The document issued by a carrier acknowledging receipt of goods for shipment and establishing ownership is called:
A bill of lading is a receipt, contract of carriage, and document of title.
money-economy-0266: In international trade terminology, what does FOB mean?
FOB stands for Free On Board: responsibility transfers when the goods are loaded aboard the ship.
money-economy-0267: An agreement between countries to remove tariffs among themselves and adopt a common tariff toward the outside world is called:
A customs union goes beyond a free trade area by having a common external tariff.
money-economy-0268: A sale in which goods are delivered immediately and the price is paid in known installments on specified dates is:
In an installment sale, goods are delivered immediately and the price is deferred in installments.
money-economy-0269: How much zakat (obligatory alms) is due on money that reaches the nisab (minimum threshold) and has been held for a hawl (lunar year)?
Zakat (obligatory alms) on gold, silver, and money is one quarter of one tenth, or 2.5%.
money-economy-0270: In which surah does Allah say: «وَلَا تُبَذِّرْ تَبْذِيرًا» [and do not spend wastefully.[737]]? (QuranEnc, 17:26)

money-economy-0272: A check drawn by a bank itself and guaranteed because its value has been reserved from the customer's account is called:
A cashier's check is drawn on and guaranteed by the bank.
money-economy-0273: Which payment documents were sold to travelers and replaced if lost, but are less commonly used today?
Traveler's checks were designed to protect travelers from losing money.
money-economy-0274: An official currency issued digitally by a central bank is abbreviated as:
CBDC stands for Central Bank Digital Currency.
money-economy-0275: The standardized international bank account number used in cross-border transfers is known as:
IBAN stands for International Bank Account Number.
money-economy-0276: The international network headquartered in Belgium through which banks exchange financial transfer messages is called:
SWIFT is a cooperative association headquartered in Belgium.
money-economy-0277: The short secret numerical code entered by a cardholder when withdrawing cash is called:
PIN stands for Personal Identification Number.
money-economy-0278: Paying by holding a card or phone near a payment terminal without inserting it is called:
Contactless payment relies on near-field communication technology.
money-economy-0279: A document sent by a seller before a sale, showing prices and terms for the buyer to review, is called:
A quotation is sent before purchase to state the price.

money-economy-0283: The peso is the official currency of which Asian country?
The Philippine peso remains a legacy of Spanish rule.
money-economy-0284: The rufiyaa is the official currency of:
The rufiyaa is the Maldives' currency.
money-economy-0285: The som is the official currency of which of these countries?
The som is Uzbekistan's currency. Tajikistan uses the somoni, while Turkmenistan and Azerbaijan use the manat.
money-economy-0286: The manat is Azerbaijan's currency and also the currency of which other country?
Manat is the name of both Azerbaijan's and Turkmenistan's currencies.

money-economy-0290: Albania's currency, the lek, is named as a shortened form of whose name?
Lek is a shortened form of Alexander of Macedon's name in Albanian.
money-economy-0291: In which year did Croatia replace its currency, the kuna, with the euro?
Croatia adopted the euro on 1 January 2023.
money-economy-0292: Many researchers believe the dollar sign $ originated as an abbreviation for:
The most common view is that it evolved from ps, an abbreviation for peso.
money-economy-0293: The L in the pound sterling symbol ? stands for which Latin word?
Libra was a Roman unit of weight, the pound.
money-economy-0294: In which year was the Indian rupee symbol ? adopted?
The symbol was officially adopted in 2010.
money-economy-0295: How many countries adopted the euro when it was introduced as an accounting currency in 1999?
The euro was introduced in 11 countries, with Greece joining in 2001.
money-economy-0296: Which European accounting unit preceded the euro and was replaced by it at a one-to-one ratio?
The European Currency Unit (ECU) was replaced by the euro in 1999.
money-economy-0297: Which South American country adopted the US dollar as its official currency in 2000?
Ecuador abandoned the sucre and adopted the dollar in 2000.
money-economy-0298: The CFA franc is a shared currency used by countries in:
The CFA franc is used in two monetary unions in West and Central Africa.
money-economy-0299: The akce was the principal silver currency of which state?
The akce was a small Ottoman silver coin.
money-economy-0300: The name of the old Spanish currency, the maravedi, derives from which Islamic dynasty?
Maravedi derives from the Almoravid dinar.
money-economy-0301: Which eighth-century English king minted a gold coin imitating the Abbasid dinar, with Arabic writing?
Offa of Mercia minted a gold dinar copied from an Abbasid dinar.
money-economy-0302: Which magazine created the Big Mac Index to compare currencies' purchasing power?
money-economy-0303: The economic concept comparing currencies by their ability to buy the same basket of goods is called:
Purchasing power parity (PPP) compares the cost of the same basket across countries.

It began with the floating and collapse of the Thai baht in July 1997.

money-economy-0307: In economics, services such as education, tourism, and banking belong to which sector?
The primary sector concerns resources, the secondary sector industry, and the tertiary sector services.
riddles-logic-0007: 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, ... Each term is the sum of the previous two. What comes next?
These are Lucas numbers. The next is 7+11=18. Meanwhile, 22 is twice 11, and neither 15 nor 17 equals the sum of the last two terms.
riddles-logic-0010: 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, ... Which term follows 42 in these Catalan numbers?
The Catalan rule is: next term = current term x 2(2n+1)/(n+2). For n=5, 42x22/7=132. The other choices do not satisfy it.
riddles-logic-0011: 1, 5, 12, 22, 35, ... What is the next of these pentagonal numbers?
The differences 4, 7, 10, and 13 increase by 3 each time. The next difference is 16, and 35+16=51. No other choice gives a difference of 16.
riddles-logic-0013: 0, 1, 2, 5, 12, 29, ... Each term is twice the preceding term plus the term before that. What comes next?
These are Pell numbers: each term = 2 x the preceding term + the term before that. The next is 2x29+12=70. The choice 58 only doubles 29 and omits 12.
riddles-logic-0014: 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, ... What comes next if each term is the sum of the previous three?
This is a Tribonacci sequence. The next is 4+7+13=24. The choice 20 adds only two terms (7+13), while 26 doubles 13.
riddles-logic-0016: 3, 7, 31, 127, ... These are the first Mersenne primes. Which comes next?
They are 2^n-1 for n=2,3,5,7. The number 2047 (n=11) is not prime because it is 23x89. Both 511 and 4095 are also composite, so the next is 8191 (n=13).
riddles-logic-0017: 1, 11, 21, 1211, 111221, ... What comes next in the look-and-say sequence?
Each term describes the previous one: 111221 has three 1s, two 2s, and one 1, written 31 22 11, or 312211.
riddles-logic-0018: 7, 22, 11, 34, 17, ... In the Collatz sequence, halve an even number; multiply an odd number by 3 and add 1. What comes next?
17 is odd, so the next term is 3x17+1=52. The other choices do not follow the rule.
riddles-logic-0020: 1, 6, 15, 28, 45, ... What is the sixth of these hexagonal numbers?
The rule is n(2n-1), so the sixth is 6x11=66. The differences 5,9,13,17, then 21 also give 45+21=66.
riddles-logic-0021: 1, 13, 37, 73, ... What is the next of these star numbers?
The differences 12, 24, and 36 are multiples of 12. The next difference is 48, giving 73+48=121, also obtained from 6n(n-1)+1 at n=5.
riddles-logic-0026: 3, 5, 17, 257, ... Fermat numbers have the form 2^(2^n)+1. What comes next?
The terms are 2^1+1, 2^2+1, 2^4+1, and 2^8+1, so the next is 2^16+1=65537. The choice 65536 omits 1, while the exponents in 1025 and 4097 are not powers of 2.
riddles-logic-0029: 0, 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 13, ... In Recaman's sequence, subtract the step number if the result is positive and new; otherwise add it. What comes next?
At step seven, 13-7=6 has already appeared, so it is rejected. Instead, 13+7=20. Neither 19 nor 21 results from using 7.
riddles-logic-0030: 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, ... Each term adds the two terms immediately before its predecessor. What comes next?
In the Padovan sequence, the next term is the second-to-last plus the third-to-last: 7+5=12. The choice 16 adds the last two terms, which is the Fibonacci rule, not Padovan's.
riddles-logic-0031: 2, 3, 7, 43, ... Each term equals the product of all preceding terms plus 1. What comes next?
2x3x7x43=1806; adding 1 gives 1807 (Sylvester's sequence). The choice 1806 omits 1, and 1849=43^2.
riddles-logic-0032: 0, 1, 1, 3, 5, 11, 21, ... Each term equals the preceding term plus twice the term before that. What comes next?
These are Jacobsthal numbers: 21+2x11=43. The choice 42 only doubles 21, and 32 adds 21+11 without doubling.
riddles-logic-0033: Squaring the number made of four 1s produces digits rising from 1 to 4 and then falling: 1234321. Direct multiplication verifies it; the other choices differ from the result.
riddles-logic-0035: 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, 28, ... Two fixed operations alternate. What comes next?
The rule alternates multiplication by 2 and subtraction of 2 (5 to 10 to 8 to 16 to 14 to 28). It is now subtraction's turn, giving 28-2=26.
riddles-logic-0040: 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 14, 15, ... These are the composite numbers in order. What comes next?
A composite number has a divisor other than 1 and itself. The first composite number after 15 is 16=4x4, while 13, 17, and 19 are prime.
riddles-logic-0041: (3, 5), (5, 7), (11, 13), (17, 19), ... What is the next pair of twin primes?
Twin primes are two primes differing by 2. Since 25, 27, and 33 are composite, the next pair is (29, 31).
riddles-logic-0043: Which number is happy, meaning that repeatedly summing the squares of its digits eventually reaches 1?
7 to 49 to 97 to 130 to 10 to 1, so it is happy. The number 4 enters a cycle that never reaches 1; 16 goes to 37 to 58 to 89 and eventually 4, while 20 also goes to 4.
riddles-logic-0044: Arrange a four-digit number's digits in descending and ascending order, subtract the smaller from the larger, and repeat, retaining four digits with leading zeros. Which number is always reached if the digits are not all identical?
This is Kaprekar's constant. The process reaches 6174 within at most seven steps, and 7641-1467=6174, so it repeats itself.
riddles-logic-0045: Choose a three-digit number whose first digit exceeds its last by at least two, reverse it, and subtract the smaller from the larger. Reverse the result and add the two. What is the result always?
For example, 532-235=297 and 297+792=1089. The result is constant for every number satisfying the condition, rather than 999 or 1098.
riddles-logic-0046: When 142857 is multiplied by 3, its digits reappear in a cyclic arrangement. What is the result?
142857x3=428571, the same digits in cyclic order. The other choices are non-cyclic rearrangements and do not equal the product.
riddles-logic-0047: Which number equals the sum of the cubes of its digits?
1^3+5^3+3^3=1+125+27=153. The other three numbers also have a digit-cube sum of 153, so none equals its own sum.
riddles-logic-0048: The number 220 has a partner such that each number's proper divisors sum to the other. What is it?
The proper divisors of 220 sum to 284, and those of 284 (1+2+4+71+142) sum to 220. They are the smallest amicable pair.
riddles-logic-0057: Muharram, Rabi al-Awwal, Jumada al-Ula, Rajab, ... Skipping one Hijri month each time, which comes next?
These are months 1, 3, 5, and 7, so the next is the ninth, Ramadan. Sha'ban is eighth and Shawwal tenth.
riddles-logic-0058: If the Hijri month after next is Shawwal, which month preceded the current month?
Shawwal is the tenth month, so the current month is the eighth, Sha'ban, and the preceding month is the seventh, Rajab.
riddles-logic-0061: January, April, July, ... Advancing three Gregorian months each time, which month comes next?
The month numbers are 1, 4, and 7, increasing by three. The next is the tenth, October.
riddles-logic-0062: If the Gregorian month five months from now is February, what is the current month?
Counting five months from September gives October, November, December, January, February. From August, five months reaches only January.
riddles-logic-0063: If the day after tomorrow is Friday, what day was yesterday?
If the day after tomorrow is Friday, today is Wednesday and yesterday was Tuesday.
riddles-logic-0064: If the day before yesterday was Saturday, what day will the day after tomorrow be?
If the day before yesterday was Saturday, today is Monday and the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.
riddles-logic-0065: If today is Sunday, what day of the week will it be in 100 days?
100 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 2 (100=14x7+2). Two days after Sunday is Tuesday.
riddles-logic-0066: A 31-day month began on Thursday. What weekday is its final day?
Day 31 is 30 days after day 1. Since 30 divided by 7 leaves a remainder of 2, it is two days after Thursday: Saturday.
riddles-logic-0067: A 30-day month began on Monday. How many Mondays does it contain?
Mondays fall on the 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th: five in total. There is no sixth because day 36 is beyond the month.
riddles-logic-0068: If three days before yesterday was Thursday, what day will tomorrow be?
Three days before yesterday is four days before today. Thus today is Monday and tomorrow is Tuesday.
riddles-logic-0069: A common Gregorian year of 365 days began on Friday. On what day will the next year begin?
365=52x7+1. A common year exceeds 52 weeks by one day, so the next year begins on Saturday.
riddles-logic-0070: A leap year began on Sunday. On what day will the following year begin?
366=52x7+2, so the weekday advances by two days, from Sunday to Tuesday.
riddles-logic-0071: Which of these Gregorian years is a leap year?
A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400. Of these years, only 2000 is.
riddles-logic-0072: How many leap years are there from 2001 through 2100, inclusive?
There are 25 years divisible by 4 from 2004 through 2100, but 2100 is not divisible by 400 and is not a leap year, leaving 24.
riddles-logic-0073: A child was born on 29 February 2004. How many times did that date recur after their birth through the end of 2024?
29 February occurs only in leap years: 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024, making five times.
riddles-logic-0074: What is the value of the Roman numeral MCMXCIV?
M=1000, CM=900, XC=90, and IV=4, totaling 1994.
riddles-logic-0075: How is 49 written in standard Roman numerals?
49=40+9, with XL for forty and IX for nine, giving XLIX. Meanwhile, XLIV=44, LIX=59, and XXXIX=39.
riddles-logic-0076: I, V, X, L, C, ... What is the next basic Roman numeral symbol in this ascending sequence?
The values 1, 5, 10, 50, and 100 alternate multiplication by 5 and by 2. The next is 500, or D. M is 1000 and comes afterward.
riddles-logic-0077: How many times does X appear when 1999 is written in Roman numerals?
1999 = M CM XC IX. X appears in XC and IX, twice in total.
riddles-logic-0078: Which number requires the most symbols when written in Roman numerals?
88=LXXXVIII (eight symbols), 99=XCIX (four), and 50=L and 100=C each require one symbol.
riddles-logic-0079: What is the smaller angle between the clock hands at quarter past three?
The minute hand is at 90 degrees, and the hour hand is at 97.5 degrees after moving a quarter of the distance from 3 to 4. The difference is 7.5 degrees.
riddles-logic-0080: What is the angle between the clock hands at half past two?
The hour hand is at 2.5*30=75 degrees and the minute hand at 180 degrees, giving a difference of 105 degrees.
riddles-logic-0081: How many degrees is the smaller angle between the clock hands at 9:45?
The minute hand is at 270 degrees and the hour hand at 9.75*30=292.5 degrees. The difference is 22.5 degrees.
riddles-logic-0082: How many times do the hour and minute hands coincide in twelve hours?
They coincide every 12/11 hours, so this happens 11 times in 12 hours, not 12: the coincidence at 12 is counted only once.
riddles-logic-0083: How many times are the clock hands perpendicular in a full 24-hour day?
They are perpendicular twice per relative revolution. There are 22 relative revolutions per day (11 per 12 hours), giving 44.
riddles-logic-0084: When do the clock hands first coincide after three o'clock?
The minute hand catches the hour hand after 60*3/11=180/11=16 and 4/11 minutes.
riddles-logic-0085: A wall clock loses two minutes every hour and is set correctly at noon. What does it show when the correct time is 6 p.m.?
Six hours have passed, so it has lost 6*2=12 minutes and shows 5:48.
riddles-logic-0086: How many degrees does the hour hand move in twenty minutes?
The hour hand moves 30 degrees per hour, or half a degree per minute, so it moves 10 degrees in 20 minutes. The minute hand moves 120 degrees.
riddles-logic-0087: How many degrees does the minute hand move in seven minutes?
The minute hand moves 360 degrees in 60 minutes, or 6 degrees per minute, so it moves 7*6=42 degrees.
riddles-logic-0089: What is the total number of dots on the six faces of a standard die?
1+2+3+4+5+6=21. There are also three pairs of opposite faces, each totaling 7.
riddles-logic-0092: How many squares of all sizes are there on an 8x8 chessboard?
The number of squares is 1^2+2^2+...+8^2=204; 64 counts only the smallest squares.
riddles-logic-0093: How many trailing zeros are there in 25! (25 factorial)?
The number of zeros is [25/5]+[25/25]=5+1=6, since 25 contains two factors of 5.
riddles-logic-0094: How many trailing zeros are there in 100! (100 factorial)?
The number of zeros is [100/5]+[100/25]=20+4=24. Forgetting the multiples of 25 gives 20.
riddles-logic-0095: What is the digital root of 98765, found by repeatedly adding its digits until one digit remains?
9+8+7+6+5=35, then 3+5=8, so the digital root is 8.
riddles-logic-0096: In the Tower of Hanoi puzzle, what is the minimum number of moves needed to transfer three disks to another peg?
The minimum for n disks is 2^n-1. For three disks, 2^3-1=7; fewer moves are impossible.
riddles-logic-0097: A Tower of Hanoi has five disks. What is the minimum number of moves needed to transfer it completely?
The rule is 2^n-1, so five disks require 2^5-1=31. The value 63 applies to six disks, while 32 is one too many.
riddles-logic-0098: If transferring a six-disk Tower of Hanoi takes at least 63 moves, how many does a seven-disk tower require?
Each additional disk doubles the count and adds one: 2*63+1=127, or 2^7-1.
riddles-logic-0099: A farmer crosses a river in a boat that can carry only one of a wolf, a goat, and a cabbage with him. The wolf cannot be left with the goat, nor the goat with the cabbage. What does he take first?
Taking the wolf leaves the goat to eat the cabbage; taking the cabbage leaves the wolf to eat the goat. Crossing alone leaves both dangers. Only taking the goat first works.
riddles-logic-0100: In the wolf, goat, and cabbage puzzle, what is the minimum number of crossings, in both directions, needed to transport all three safely?
The optimal sequence is: goat, return, wolf, return with goat, cabbage, return, goat. This takes seven crossings; fewer are impossible.
riddles-logic-0102: You have 6-liter and 9-liter jugs and an unlimited water supply. Which quantity cannot be measured exactly in either jug or in their combined contents?
Every measurable quantity is a multiple of the greatest common divisor of 6 and 9, which is 3. The quantities 3, 12, and 15 are multiples of 3; 4 is not.
riddles-logic-0103: In the Monty Hall problem, a prize is behind one of three doors. You choose a door. The host, who knows the prize location, always opens an empty alternative door and offers a switch. What is your chance of winning if you switch?
Your initial choice is correct with probability 1/3. The remaining probability of 2/3 transfers entirely to the other closed door after the host reveals an empty one.
riddles-logic-0104: Assuming 365 equally likely birthdays, what is the smallest group size for which the probability that two people share a birthday exceeds one half?
Calculating the probability of no match shows that the chance of a match exceeds 50% at 23 people (about 50.7%); at 22 it is below half.
riddles-logic-0105: Ignoring February 29, how many people are needed to guarantee that two share a birthday?
There are 365 days. Each of 365 people could have a different birthday, but person 366 must share with someone, by the pigeonhole principle.
riddles-logic-0106: Ten people numbered 1 to 10 stand in a circle. Every second person is removed, starting with number 2, until one remains. What is that person's number?
For the Josephus problem with step 2, write 10=8+2. The survivor is 2*2+1=5.
riddles-logic-0107: In the Josephus problem, 41 people stand in a circle and every second person is removed, starting with the second. Which position survives?
41=32+9, so the survivor is 2*9+1=19 using the step-2 formula.
riddles-logic-0109: What is the greatest number of queens that can be placed on an 8x8 chessboard without attacking one another?
Each row can contain at most one queen, and there are eight rows. The eight-queens puzzle proves eight can be placed; a ninth is impossible.
riddles-logic-0110: One grain of wheat is placed on the first square of a chessboard, with the amount doubled on each subsequent square. How many grains are on the sixty-fourth square?
Square n contains 2^(n-1) grains, so square 64 contains 2^63. The expression 2^64-1 is the total for the entire board.
riddles-logic-0111: In the wheat and chessboard problem, starting with one grain and doubling on each square, how many grains are on the first ten squares combined?
The total is 1+2+4+...+512=2^10-1=1023. The value 512 is for the tenth square alone.
riddles-logic-0112: Two diagonally opposite corner squares are removed from a chessboard. Can the remaining 62 squares be covered by 31 dominoes, each covering two adjacent squares?
No, because 62 is not divisible by 2
No, because the removed squares have the same color
Each domino covers one white and one black square. Removing two of the same color leaves 32 of one color and 30 of the other, making coverage impossible. The number 62 is divisible by 2.
riddles-logic-0113: Why is it impossible to cross each of the seven bridges of Konigsberg exactly once?
Because the number of bridges is odd
Because the river splits into two branches
Because each of the four land areas has an odd number of bridges
Because no bridge joins two of the islands
Euler proved that a route crossing every bridge once requires no more than two land areas with an odd number of bridges. Konigsberg has four.
riddles-logic-0114: Each of three houses must be connected to three utilities (water, gas, and electricity) by lines on a flat surface. What is the minimum unavoidable number of line crossings?
The graph K3,3 is nonplanar and cannot be drawn without a crossing. Its minimum crossing number is just one.
riddles-logic-0116: Of Diophantus it was said: he spent a sixth of his life as a boy; his beard grew after another half-sixth; after another seventh he married; five years later he had a son, who lived half his father's lifespan; the father died four years after him. How long did he live?
x/6+x/12+x/7+5+x/2+4=x gives 75x/84+9=x, hence x=84. The other numbers do not satisfy the equation.
riddles-logic-0117: In the riddle of the Sphinx, what walks on four legs in the morning, two at noon, and three in the evening?
A human crawls as a baby, walks on two feet when young, and uses a cane in old age. This does not apply to the others.
riddles-logic-0118: In the Chinese hundred-birds problem, a rooster costs five coins, a hen three, and three chicks one coin. One hundred birds were bought for 100 coins, including 4 roosters. How many hens were there?
With 4 roosters, hens and chicks total 96. Then 3h+c/3=80, or 9h+c=240, giving h=18 and c=78. Check: 20+54+26=100.
riddles-logic-0119: On an island where everyone always tells the truth or always lies, Ahmad says: 'Khalid and I are both liars.' What are they?
Ahmad is a liar and Khalid is truthful
Ahmad is truthful and Khalid is a liar
If Ahmad were truthful, his statement would make him a liar. Thus he lies. His false statement means they are not both liars, so Khalid is truthful.
riddles-logic-0120: On an island of truth-tellers and liars, Saad says: 'Fahd is a liar.' Fahd says: 'Saad and I are the same type.' What are they?
Saad is a liar and Fahd is truthful
Saad is truthful and Fahd is a liar
If Saad were a liar, Fahd would be truthful, making Fahd's claim that they are the same type true: a contradiction. Therefore Saad is truthful and Fahd is a liar, whose statement is indeed false.
riddles-logic-0121: On an island of truth-tellers and liars, Zayd says about himself and Amr: 'At least one of us is a liar.' What are they?
Zayd is truthful and Amr is a liar
Zayd is a liar and Amr is truthful
If Zayd were a liar his statement would be true, a contradiction. He is truthful, and his statement requires a liar, who must be Amr.
riddles-logic-0122: On an island inhabited only by people who always tell the truth or always lie, which statement can none of them make?
A truth-teller cannot say 'I am a liar' because it is false. A liar cannot say it because it would be true. The other statements can be made by one of the two types.
riddles-logic-0123: Nine balls look identical, but one is slightly heavier. What is the minimum number of weighings on a balance scale needed to identify it with certainty?
Divide them into three groups of three. The first weighing identifies the heavier group, and the second identifies its heavier ball. One weighing distinguishes only three possibilities.
riddles-logic-0124: Among twelve coins, one is counterfeit, and it is unknown whether it is heavier or lighter. What is the minimum number of balance-scale weighings needed to identify it and determine which it is?
There are 24 possibilities (12 coins times heavier or lighter). Two weighings distinguish only 9 outcomes, while three distinguish up to 27. A three-weighing solution is known.
riddles-logic-0125: Using a balance scale and only three weighings, what is the largest number of balls among which you can find the single heavier ball?
Each weighing has three outcomes, so three weighings distinguish 3^3=27 possibilities. The number 81 requires four weighings.
riddles-logic-0126: A dark drawer contains many black and white socks. What is the minimum number you must draw to guarantee a pair of the same color?
There are two colors. The first two may differ, but the third must match one of them. Two are insufficient.
riddles-logic-0127: A dark box contains 10 black and 10 white socks. What is the minimum number you must draw to guarantee two white socks?
In the worst case, all ten black socks come out first, followed by the two white ones needed: 10+2=12.
riddles-logic-0128: A dark cupboard contains 5 pairs of black gloves and 5 pairs of brown gloves, each pair having a left and a right. What is the minimum number you must draw to guarantee a matching pair of the same color?
You might draw all ten left gloves first. The eleventh must be a right glove matching the color of one of them.
riddles-logic-0129: At a gathering of ten people, everyone shakes hands with everyone else once. How many handshakes occur?
Each handshake involves two people, so the count is 10*9/2=45. The value 90 counts each handshake twice.
riddles-logic-0130: There were 28 handshakes at a gathering where everyone shook hands with everyone else once. How many people attended?
The number of handshakes is n(n-1)/2, and 8*7/2=28. Seven people give only 21 handshakes.
riddles-logic-0131: What is the minimum number of people that guarantees either three mutual acquaintances or three mutual strangers?
The friends and strangers theorem says six always suffice. Five do not, as their relationships can form a pentagon containing neither kind of triple.
riddles-logic-0132: What is the minimum number of colors that always suffices to color any planar map so that neighboring regions have different colors?
The four-color theorem proves that four always suffice, and some maps cannot be colored with three.
riddles-logic-0133: In a 3x3 magic square containing the numbers 1 to 9, what is the sum of each row?
The numbers 1 to 9 total 45, divided equally among three rows, so each row totals 15.
riddles-logic-0134: Which number is at the center of the Lo Shu magic square containing the numbers 1 to 9?
The center belongs to four lines each totaling 15. This is possible only when the center is 15/3=5.
riddles-logic-0135: In a 4x4 magic square containing the numbers 1 to 16, what is the sum of each row?
The numbers 1 to 16 total 136, divided among four rows, so each row totals 34.
riddles-logic-0136: When finding primes up to 100 using the sieve of Eratosthenes, what is the largest prime whose multiples must be crossed out?
It suffices to cross out multiples up to the square root of 100, which is 10, so the last required prime is 7. The first multiple of 11 not already crossed out is 121.
riddles-logic-0137: A straight fence is 100 meters long, with a post every 10 meters including both ends. How many posts are needed?
There are ten intervals. On a straight line, the number of posts is one greater than the number of intervals, giving 11.
riddles-logic-0138: A 10-meter piece of wood is cut into one-meter pieces. Each cut takes one minute, and pieces cannot be stacked. How many minutes are needed?
Ten pieces require only nine cuts, because the last piece separates with the ninth cut.
riddles-logic-0139: How many Platonic solids are there: convex solids whose faces are identical regular polygons, with the same number of faces meeting at each vertex?
There are only five: the tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron.
riddles-logic-0140: A convex solid has 12 vertices and 30 edges. How many faces does it have?
Euler's formula is vertices - edges + faces = 2. Thus 12-30+f=2 gives 20 faces.
riddles-logic-0141: A cube is painted on the outside, then cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
Cubes with two painted faces are at the middle of each edge. A cube has 12 edges, each with one such small cube.
riddles-logic-0142: A cube is painted on the outside, then cut into 64 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have no paint?
The interior cubes form a cube with side length 4-2=2, so there are 2^3=8.
riddles-logic-0143: A bat and a ball cost 110 fils together. The bat costs 100 fils more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
If the ball costs b, the bat costs b+100, so 2b+100=110 and b=5. A ball costing 10 would make the total 120.
riddles-logic-0144: If 5 machines make 5 items in 5 minutes, how many minutes do 100 machines need to make 100 items?
Each machine makes one item in 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 items in the same five minutes.
riddles-logic-0145: A patch of plants on a lake doubles in size daily and covers the whole lake in 48 days. When did it cover half?
Since it doubles daily, it covers half the lake on the day before full coverage: day 47.
riddles-logic-0146: What is always ahead of you but cannot be seen?
The future is always ahead and has not yet arrived, so it cannot be seen. The past, yesterday, and memories are behind you.
riddles-logic-0147: What is tall when young and grows shorter as it ages?
A candle starts tall and becomes shorter as it melts while burning. A tree grows taller with age; rivers and mountains do not fit the description.
riddles-logic-0148: What follows you wherever you go and copies every movement, but cannot be touched?
Your shadow follows you, mirrors your movements, and cannot be touched. Your name, age, and breath do not copy your movements.
riddles-logic-0149: I disappear as soon as you say my name. What am I?
Any speech ends silence, including saying its name. A secret, darkness, and sleep do not disappear merely when named.
riddles-logic-0150: What has many teeth but never bites?
A comb has teeth but does not bite. A spoon, scissors, and a needle have no teeth.
riddles-logic-0151: What goes up and down but never moves from its place?
People go up and down stairs while the stairs remain fixed. Elevators, airplanes, and swings all move.
riddles-logic-0152: What belongs to you but is used by others more than by you?
Your name is yours, but others call you and mention it more than you say it yourself. The owner generally uses their house, money, and pen most.
riddles-logic-0153: What has blades but is not used for cutting?
Fan blades move air rather than cut. Scissors, knives, and sickles are cutting tools.
riddles-logic-0155: What has seas without water, mountains without earth, and countries without inhabitants?
A map depicts seas, mountains, and countries rather than containing them. A desert, ship, or city does not combine these features.
riddles-logic-0156: A man shaves many times a day, yet his beard stays the same. Who is he?
A barber shaves other people's beards, leaving his own unchanged. Bakers, carpenters, and blacksmiths do not shave as their work.
riddles-logic-0157: Turn me on my side and I become the infinity symbol. Cut me in half horizontally and I become two zeros. Which digit am I?
The digit 8 on its side resembles the infinity symbol, and its halves are circles like zeros. The other digits do not do this.
riddles-logic-0158: If you have me, you want to tell someone else. Once you tell them, you no longer have me. What am I?
Once disclosed, a secret is no longer a secret. Money, food, and books can remain owned even when shared.
riddles-logic-0159: What do you buy for eating but never eat?
A plate is bought to eat from, not to eat. Bread, dates, and fruit are eaten.
riddles-logic-0160: What has no real wings but flies and has a tail?
A kite flies in the wind and has a tail but no wings. Butterflies, doves, and bees have real wings.
riddles-logic-0161: What must you break before you can use it?
An egg's shell is broken before cooking it. Apples, bread, and honey can be used without breaking.
riddles-logic-0163: What is full of holes yet holds water?
A sponge is porous and absorbs and holds water. Water passes through sieves, strainers, and nets.
riddles-logic-0164: Which question cannot truthfully be answered 'yes'?
A sleeping person cannot give a conscious answer. Anyone answering consciously is awake, making 'yes' untrue. The other questions may be answered yes.
riddles-logic-0166: What always increases and never decreases?
Age increases each day and never goes backward. Money, water, and weight can increase and decrease.
riddles-logic-0167: A man walked in the rain without an umbrella or hat, yet not one hair on his head got wet. Why?
No hair got wet because he had none on his head. Speed, light rain, and height do not prevent hair from getting wet.
riddles-logic-0168: What goes all the way around an orchard without moving?
The wall surrounds the orchard on all sides and remains fixed. The guard moves, and the gate is in one location.
riddles-logic-0169: Jawad's parents have three sons: Rami, Mazen, and who?
The question says they are Jawad's parents, so Jawad himself is the third son.
riddles-logic-0170: What is black when clean and white when dirty?
A blackboard becomes dirty with white chalk. Paper and clothing become dirty with dark marks.
riddles-logic-0171: What gets bigger the more you take from it?
Removing soil from a hole makes it larger. A pile, jar, or basket diminishes or empties as things are taken from it.
riddles-logic-0172: In a race, you overtake the runner immediately behind the leader. What position are you now in?
You take the place of the runner who was second. The leader is still ahead, so you are second.
riddles-logic-0173: When Ali was eight, his brother was half his age. Ali is now 14. How old is his brother?
His brother was four. Their age difference remains four years, so he is now 14-4=10, not half of 14.
riddles-logic-0174: What fills a whole room without taking up any space?
Light spreads through a room without occupying space. Water, furniture, and sand take up space.
riddles-logic-0175: What has a neck but no head?
A bottle has a narrow neck but no head. Cups, plates, and spoons have no neck.
riddles-logic-0180: Born of water, I melt and disappear when returned to water. What am I?
Ice is frozen water and melts when placed in water. Fish live in water, while rock and wood do not dissolve.
riddles-logic-0181: Sarah has four daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many children does Sarah have?
The four daughters share the same brother, so there are four daughters and one son: five children.
riddles-logic-0182: Three consecutive integers total 333. What are they?
The middle number is 333/3=111, so the numbers are 110, 111, and 112. The other options total 330, 336, and 339.
riddles-logic-0183: How can you obtain 10 using the digit 9 three times?
Nine times nine, then divide by nine
Nine plus nine divided by nine
Nine plus nine, then subtract nine
The sum of nine and nine divided by nine
9+9/9=9+1=10, with division before addition. Both 9*9/9 and 9+9-9 equal 9, while (9+9)/9=2.
riddles-logic-0184: Which number remains itself when multiplied by any other number?
Zero times any number equals zero. One gives the other number rather than itself.
riddles-logic-0186: All birds have feathers, and an ostrich is a bird. What necessarily follows?
Everything with feathers is a bird
This is a valid syllogism: a property of the whole class applies to an individual, so an ostrich must have feathers. Flight was not mentioned in the premises.
riddles-logic-0188: If it rains, the ground gets wet. The ground is not wet now. What can we conclude?
This is modus tollens: denying the consequence (wet ground) denies its sufficient condition (rain).
riddles-logic-0189: If a metal is gold, it shines. This piece shines. Which conclusion is correct?
Concluding it is gold is the fallacy of affirming the consequent: things other than gold may shine. There is also no evidence that it is not gold.
riddles-logic-0190: 'If a number is divisible by 4, it is even.' Which statement is logically equivalent?
If a number is even, it is divisible by 4
If a number is not even, it is not divisible by 4
If a number is not divisible by 4, it is not even
If a number is odd, it is divisible by 4
The contrapositive is always equivalent to the original statement. The converse and inverse are false: 6 is even but not divisible by 4.
riddles-logic-0191: Four cards show 3, 8, red, and brown. The rule is: 'If one side has an even number, the reverse is red.' Which cards must be turned over to test it?
Turn over 8 to check that its reverse is red, and brown to check that its number is not even. Neither 3 nor red can violate the rule, whatever is on the other side.
riddles-logic-0192: Khalid is older than Saad, Badr is older than Saad, Khalid is older than Badr, and Saad is older than Majid. Who is youngest?
The order is Khalid, Badr, Saad, Majid. Saad is younger than Khalid and Badr but older than Majid.
riddles-logic-0193: In a race, Ahmad finishes before Badr. Jasim finishes after Badr but before Dawud. Iyad finishes before Ahmad. Who finishes third?
The order is Iyad, Ahmad, Badr, Jasim, Dawud. Badr is third.
riddles-logic-0194: Of 30 students, 18 like mathematics, 15 like science, and 5 like neither. How many like both subjects?
There are 25 who like at least one subject. Thus 18+15-x=25, giving x=8.
riddles-logic-0195: A club has 40 members: 25 swim, 20 run, and 10 do both. How many do neither?
Those doing at least one total 25+20-10=35. The remainder is 40-35=5.
riddles-logic-0196: A father is now three times his son's age. In 12 years he will be twice his age. How old is the son now?
If the son is x, then 3x+12=2(x+12), giving x=12. The father is 36; in 12 years they will be 48 and 24.
riddles-logic-0197: Two brothers' ages total 30 years, with a difference of 6 years. How old is the elder?
The elder is (30+6)/2=18 and the younger 12. Their sum is 30 and difference 6; no other option satisfies this.
riddles-logic-0198: A mother is 40 and her daughter is 10. In how many years will the mother be twice her daughter's age?
40+n=2(10+n) gives n=20. The mother will be 60 and her daughter 30.
riddles-logic-0199: Five years ago, Saad was twice his brother's age. In five years, he will be one and a half times his brother's age. How old is Saad now?
From s-5=2(b-5) and s+5=1.5(b+5), we get b=15 and s=25. Five years ago they were 20 and 10; in five years they will be 30 and 20.
riddles-logic-0200: A pen contains chickens and rabbits with 20 heads and 56 legs. How many rabbits are there?
If all were chickens, there would be 40 legs. The extra 16 legs come from rabbits, each adding two, so there are 8 rabbits.
riddles-logic-0201: One worker digs a hole in 6 hours, and another in 3 hours. How many hours do they need working together?
Their combined rate is 1/6+1/3=1/2 hole per hour, so they need two hours.
riddles-logic-0202: A tap fills a tank in 4 hours, and a hole in the bottom drains it in 6 hours. If both are opened with the tank empty, when will it fill?
The net filling rate is 1/4-1/6=1/12 tank per hour, so it fills in 12 hours.
riddles-logic-0203: A man drives to a city at 60 km/h and returns along the same road at 40 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole trip?
For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean: 2*60*40/(60+40)=48, not 50.
riddles-logic-0204: Two trains 300 km apart travel toward each other at 70 and 80 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
They close the gap at 70+80=150 km/h, and 300/150=2 hours.
riddles-logic-0205: A car travels at a constant 90 km/h. How many meters does it cover in one second?
90 km/h = 90000 meters / 3600 seconds = 25 meters per second.
riddles-logic-0206: An item's price rises by 10%, then its new price is reduced by 10%. What is the final change?
100 becomes 110, then 110-11=99. The price falls 1% because the reduction is calculated on a larger amount.
riddles-logic-0207: A number increased by 25% becomes 100. What was the original number?
The number times 1.25 equals 100, so it is 80. Increasing 75 by 25% gives 93.75.
riddles-logic-0208: Five numbers have an average of 20. Adding a sixth number raises the average to 21. What is the sixth number?
The first five total 100, and the six total 126, so the sixth is 126-100=26.
riddles-logic-0209: Four siblings have an average age of 10. Including their father raises the average to 16. How old is the father?
The siblings total 40, and all five total 5*16=80, so the father is 40.
riddles-logic-0210: A number is divisible by 9 if its digit sum is. The sums are 18 for 4518, 17 for 4517, 17 for 4508, and 19 for 4528. Only 4518 qualifies.
riddles-logic-0211: The rule for 11 is that the difference between the sums of digits in alternating positions is a multiple of 11. For 2728: (8+7)-(2+2)=11, and 2728=11*248.
riddles-logic-0212: What is the smallest digit that can replace the blank in 7_2 to make it divisible by 3?
The known digits total 7+2=9, divisible by 3, so zero works (702=3*234) and is the smallest digit.
riddles-logic-0213: A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. Only 16 qualifies among 10, 14, 16, and 18.
riddles-logic-0214: What is always true of the sum of seven odd numbers?
It can be odd or even
Each pair of odd numbers totals an even number. Three pairs give an even total, and the remaining odd number makes it odd. The example 1+1+1+1+1+1+3=9 disproves divisibility by 7.
riddles-logic-0215: Can plus and minus signs be placed between the numbers 1, 2, 3, through 10 to give zero?
No, because their sum is odd
No, because there is an even number of numbers
Their sum is 55, which is odd. Changing any number's sign changes the total by an even amount, so it remains odd and cannot be zero.
riddles-logic-0216: Ropes 48 and 72 meters long are cut into equal pieces of the greatest possible length with no remainder. How long is each piece?
The greatest common length is the greatest common divisor of 48 and 72, which is 24. The number 36 does not divide 48.
riddles-logic-0217: Two buses depart together at 6:00. One departs every 12 minutes and the other every 18. When will they next depart together?
The least common multiple of 12 and 18 is 36, so they coincide after 36 minutes, at 6:36.
riddles-logic-0218: What is the smallest positive number divisible by all of 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6?
The least common multiple is 2^2*3*5=60. The number 30 is not divisible by 4.
riddles-logic-0219: What is the smallest number that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6, and is divisible by 7?
The number has the form 60k+1. Testing gives 61, 121, 181, and 241, none divisible by 7. The first is 301=7*43.
riddles-logic-0220: Two dice are rolled together. What is the probability their sum is 7?
There are 36 outcomes. Six give 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), and their reverses. Thus 6/36=1/6.
riddles-logic-0221: A fair coin is tossed five times and shows heads every time. What is the probability of heads on the sixth toss?
Tosses are independent, so each has a 1/2 probability of heads regardless of previous results. Believing otherwise is the gambler's fallacy.
riddles-logic-0222: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least one head?
The four outcomes are equally likely. Only one has no heads (tails, tails), so the probability is 3/4.
riddles-logic-0223: Three boxes contain two gold coins, two silver coins, and one gold and one silver coin respectively. You draw a gold coin from a randomly chosen box. What is the probability its other coin is also gold?
The three gold coins are equally likely to be drawn, and two belong to the all-gold box. The probability is 2/3, not 1/2: Bertrand's box paradox.
riddles-logic-0224: A 5-meter ladder leans against a wall with its base 3 meters from the wall. How high does its top reach?
By Pythagoras, height squared = 5^2-3^2=16, so the height is 4 meters.
riddles-logic-0225: Which triple can be the side lengths of a right triangle?
25+144=169=13^2. The other sums, 25+121=146, 36+64=100, and 49+576=625, do not equal the square of the longest side in their options.
riddles-logic-0226: How many diagonals does a ten-sided polygon have?
The number of diagonals is n(n-3)/2 = 10*7/2 = 35. The value 45 includes sides as well as diagonals.
riddles-logic-0227: What is the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon?
The sum is (n-2)*180 degrees. For a hexagon, 4*180=720 degrees.
riddles-logic-0228: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 140 degrees. How many sides does it have?
Each exterior angle is 180-140=40 degrees. Exterior angles total 360 degrees, so the number of sides is 360/40=9.
riddles-logic-0229: If a square's side length doubles, by what factor does its area increase?
Area is the square of the side length. If the side becomes 2s, the area becomes 4s^2, four times as large.
riddles-logic-0230: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and area 24 square cm. What is its length?
Length and width sum to 10 and have product 24, so they are 6 and 4. The length is 6 cm.
riddles-logic-0231: What is the decimal value of the binary number 1011?
riddles-logic-0232: How many binary digits are needed to write the number 100 in binary?
100 is 1100100 in binary, seven digits, since 64 <= 100 < 128.
riddles-logic-0233: You have one weight each of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 grams, placed on one pan. What is the greatest weight you can measure?
The weights total 1+2+4+8+16=31, and every integer up to 31 has a binary representation using these weights.
riddles-logic-0234: Using only coins of denominations 3 and 5, what is the greatest integer amount that cannot be formed?
For coprime denominations a and b, the largest impossible amount is a*b-a-b = 15-8 = 7. Also, 8=3+5 and 11=3+3+5.
riddles-logic-0235: Using only coins of denominations 4 and 7, what is the greatest integer amount that cannot be formed?
The formula gives 4*7-4-7=17. The amounts 19=12+7 and 21=3*7 are possible. The amount 13 is impossible but not the greatest.
riddles-logic-0237: What is the sum of the integers from 1 to 100?
Gauss's method gives 50 pairs each totaling 101, so the sum is 100*101/2=5050.
riddles-logic-0238: What is the sum of the odd numbers from 1 to 19?
The sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2. There are ten here, so the sum is 100.
riddles-logic-0239: What is half of a third of a quarter of 240?
A quarter of 240 is 60, a third of that is 20, and half of that is 10.
riddles-logic-0240: As the Fibonacci sequence progresses, the ratio of each term to the preceding term approaches which number?
The ratio approaches the golden ratio (1+sqrt(5))/2, approximately 1.618. The value 1.414 is sqrt(2), 1.732 is sqrt(3), and 2.718 is e.
riddles-logic-0242: Which of these numbers is not prime?
51=3*17, so it is composite. The numbers 53, 59, and 61 have no divisors other than one and themselves.
riddles-logic-0243: Which number is not a perfect square?
144=12^2, 169=13^2, and 225=15^2. The number 186 lies between 13^2 and 14^2 (196), so it is not a square.
riddles-logic-0244: Which number is not a perfect cube?
343=7^3, 512=8^3, and 729=9^3. The number 625 is 5^4 and lies between 8^3 and 9^3.
riddles-logic-0245: Which is a triangular number: a sum of consecutive integers starting at 1?
45=1+2+...+9=9*10/2. Nearby triangular numbers are 36, 45, and 55, so none of the others qualifies.
riddles-logic-0246: Which number is a term in the Fibonacci sequence?
The sequence includes ...34, 55, 89, 144. Thus 89=34+55, while the others do not occur in it.
riddles-logic-0247: Each term is three times its predecessor: 6*3=18 and 18*3=54. No other choice satisfies multiplication by 3 on both sides.
riddles-logic-0250: One term in the sequence 2, 4, 8, 16, 30, 64 is wrong. Which?
Each term doubles the preceding one, so 16 should be followed by 32, not 30. The other terms follow the rule.
riddles-logic-0251: Which term does not fit the sequence 1, 4, 9, 15, 25, 36?
The terms are squares from 1^2 to 6^2. The fourth should be 16, not 15.
riddles-logic-0252: Which term is wrong in the Fibonacci sequence 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 20, 34?
Each term is the sum of the preceding two. After 8 and 13 comes 21, not 20, confirmed by 13+21=34.
riddles-logic-0253: Each term is a square plus one (1^2+1, 2^2+1, ...), so the next is 6^2+1=37. The differences 3, 5, 7, 9, then 11 confirm this.
riddles-logic-0254: The rule is: multiply the term by 3 and subtract 1 (2*3-1=5, 5*3-1=14, 14*3-1=41). The next is 41*3-1=122.
riddles-logic-0257: 1, 4, 27, 256, ... Each term is its position number raised to itself. What is the fifth term?
The terms are 1^1, 2^2, 3^3, and 4^4. The fifth is 5^5=3125. Also, 625=5^4 and 1024=4^5.
riddles-logic-0258: 1, 2, 4, 7, 28, 33, 198, ... Addition and multiplication by increasing numbers alternate. What comes next?
The operations are +1, *2, +3, *4, +5, *6. Next is +7: 198+7=205. The value 1386 comes from multiplying by 7.
riddles-logic-0262: Each term is a prime plus one: 2+1, 3+1, 5+1, 7+1, 11+1, 13+1, 17+1. The next prime is 19, giving 20.
riddles-logic-0263: These are squares of the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11. Next is 13^2=169. The numbers 144=12^2, 196=14^2, and 225=15^2 are not squares of primes.
riddles-logic-0264: This counts from 1 to 6 in binary. Next is 7, written 111. Binary does not use the digit 2.
riddles-logic-0265: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 23, 28, 38, 49, ... Each term is increased by its digit sum. What comes next?
riddles-logic-0266: What is the next palindrome after 1991, reading the same in both directions?
After 1991 there is no palindrome beginning with 1. The first beginning with 2 is 2002. Neither 1999 nor 2020 is a palindrome.
riddles-logic-0267: What is the smallest three-digit palindrome divisible by 7?
In order, 101, 111, 121, 131, 141, and 151 are not divisible by 7. Then 161=7*23. The number 252 is divisible by 7 but larger.
riddles-logic-0268: Which number is divisible by the sum of its digits?
The digits of 18 sum to 9, and 18/9=2. The numbers 19 (sum 10), 23 (sum 5), and 29 (sum 11) are not divisible by their digit sums.
riddles-logic-0269: What is the smallest abundant number, whose proper divisors sum to more than the number itself?
The proper divisors of 12 total 1+2+3+4+6=16 > 12, making it the first abundant number. Both 18 and 20 are abundant but larger. The proper divisors of 10 total 8.
riddles-logic-0270: Which number has the most divisors?
The number 60 has twelve divisors, 64 has seven, 50 has six, and 58 has four.
riddles-logic-0271: Which number is the product of exactly two primes?
35=5*7. The others have more than two prime factors: 27=3*3*3, 36=2*2*3*3, and 45=3*3*5.
riddles-logic-0272: The row 1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1 belongs to Pascal's triangle. What is its sum?
Row n in Pascal's triangle sums to 2^n. This is row five, counting from zero, so its sum is 2^5=32.
riddles-logic-0273: A row in Pascal's triangle is 1, 6, _, 20, _, 6, 1. What number fills each blank?
Each entry is the sum of the two above it in the row 1, 5, 10, 10, 5, 1: 5+10=15.
riddles-logic-0274: 1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 25, ... Each term is the sum of the preceding two plus one. What comes next?
These are Leonardo numbers: 15+25+1=41. The value 40 follows the Fibonacci rule without adding one.
riddles-logic-0275: The differences are 5, 13, 25, 41; their differences 8, 12, 16 increase by 4. Next are 20, then 61, giving 85+61=146.
riddles-logic-0276: These are powers of 11, so the next is 1331*11=14641. Its digits form the Pascal's triangle row 1 4 6 4 1.
riddles-logic-0277: In the look-and-say sequence, what follows the term 3112?
Read 3112 as one three, two ones, and one two: 13 21 12, giving 132112.
riddles-logic-0278: How many steps does 6 need to reach 1 in the Collatz sequence?
riddles-logic-0280: Applying Kaprekar's operation to three-digit numbers whose digits are not all identical, preserving leading zeros, which number is eventually reached?
With three digits the process reaches 495, since 954-459=495. The number 6174 applies to four-digit numbers.
riddles-logic-0282: What is the smallest perfect number, equal to the sum of its proper divisors?
6=1+2+3 is the smallest perfect number. The number 28 is perfect but larger, while the proper divisors of 12 sum to 16.
riddles-logic-0283: Which number forms an amicable pair with 1184?
The pair (1184, 1210) is amicable: the proper divisors of each sum to the other number.
riddles-logic-0287: 18=9*2, so the result is twice 111111111, which is 222222222.
riddles-logic-0288: In the famous alphametic SEND + MORE = MONEY, each letter represents a different digit. What is M?
The sum of two four-digit numbers is less than 20000. The fifth digit produced by carrying must therefore be 1, and a number cannot start with zero.
riddles-logic-0292: In a complete knight's tour on an 8x8 board, the knight visits each square once without returning to the starting square. How many moves does it make?
It starts on one square and visits 63 others. Each new visit is one move, so it makes 63 moves, not 64.
riddles-logic-0293: From a corner of a chessboard, how many squares can a knight move to?
A knight moves in an L shape. From a corner, only two of its eight possible destinations are within the board.
riddles-logic-0294: In a solved standard Sudoku, how many times does the digit 5 appear in the entire grid?
Each of the nine rows contains each digit from 1 to 9 once, so 5 appears nine times.
riddles-logic-0295: In the missing-square puzzle, rearranging the same pieces leaves a gap of one square. Why?
The shapes are not true triangles because the hypotenuse bends slightly
The gap is only an optical illusion
The small triangles have different slopes, so the apparent hypotenuse is not straight. The area difference between the two shapes is exactly one square.
riddles-logic-0296: If January 1 in a non-leap year is a Tuesday, what day is March 1?
The dates are 31+28=59 days apart. Dividing 59 by 7 leaves 3, so it is three days after Tuesday: Friday.
riddles-logic-0297: How many days are there from March 1 through May 31, inclusive?
March has 31 days, April 30, and May 31, totaling 92 days.
riddles-logic-0298: What time is it 1000 minutes after midnight?
1000 minutes is 16 hours and 40 minutes: 16:40, or 4:40 p.m.
riddles-logic-0299: A wall clock chimes the number of the hour. Three chimes take 6 seconds. How many seconds do six chimes take?
Three chimes have two intervals of 3 seconds each. Six chimes have five intervals, so they take 15 seconds.
riddles-logic-0300: You plant a seedling every half hour, starting with the first immediately, and have three seedlings. After how many minutes do you plant the last?
Three seedlings have only two intervals between them, each 30 minutes, so the last is planted after 60 minutes.
riddles-logic-0301: A man climbs from the ground floor to the second floor in 20 seconds. At the same speed, how many seconds does he need from the ground floor to the fourth?
The second floor is two flights above ground, each taking 10 seconds. The fourth is four flights above ground, taking 40 seconds.
riddles-logic-0302: A snail at the bottom of a 10-meter well climbs 3 meters by day and slips 2 meters at night. On which day does it escape?
Its net gain each full day is one meter. After seven days it is at 7 meters, and on the eighth day it climbs 3 to reach 10 and escapes before slipping.
riddles-logic-0303: A 200-meter train passes through a 400-meter tunnel at 20 m/s. How many seconds pass between its front entering and its rear leaving?
The train covers the tunnel's length plus its own: 400+200=600 meters. Then 600/20=30 seconds.
riddles-logic-0304: Ahmad sets off walking at 4 km/h. An hour later his brother follows at 6 km/h. How many hours after setting off does his brother catch him?
Ahmad has a 4 km lead. His brother closes the gap at 6-4=2 km/h, so catches him after 4/2=2 hours.
riddles-logic-0305: At a school, 80% of students pass mathematics and 70% pass science. What is the smallest possible percentage passing both?
The minimum overlap is 80%+70%-100%=50%. The value 56% is the product if the subjects are independent, not the minimum.
riddles-logic-0306: A merchant sells two items for 120 dinars each, making a 20% profit on the first and a 20% loss on the second. What is the overall result?
The first cost 100 (120/1.2) and the second 150 (120/0.8). Total cost is 250 and revenue 240, so the loss is 10 dinars.
riddles-logic-0307: Ten liters of juice contain 20% sugar. How many liters of water must be added to make the concentration 10%?
The sugar stays at two liters. For that to be 10%, total volume must be 20 liters, requiring 10 liters of added water.
