riddles-logic-0308: Equal cups contain water and juice. A spoonful of juice is added to the water and mixed, then a spoonful of the mixture is returned to the juice. Which is greater now?
It depends on the spoon size
After both transfers, each cup has its original volume. The juice transferred to the water cup exactly equals the water transferred to the juice cup.
riddles-logic-0309: Bacteria in a container double every minute, filling it after 60 minutes. When was it one-quarter full?
It was half full one minute before filling and one-quarter full two minutes before, after 58 minutes.
riddles-logic-0310: A sheet of paper 0.1 mm thick is folded in half 10 times. Approximately how thick does it become?
Each fold doubles the thickness, giving 0.1*2^10=0.1*1024, about 102 mm or 10 cm.
riddles-logic-0311: A knockout tournament has 64 competitors, with the loser eliminated from each match. How many matches determine the winner?
Each match eliminates one competitor. To leave one winner, 63 must be eliminated, requiring 63 matches.
riddles-logic-0312: If yesterday was Thursday, what day is ten days after tomorrow?
Today is Friday and tomorrow Saturday. Ten days after Saturday (10=7+3) is Tuesday.
tech-computing-0001: Which computer component fetches instructions, decodes them, and then executes them?
The central processing unit performs the fetch-decode-execute cycle for program instructions.
tech-computing-0002: Inside a processor, which unit performs arithmetic operations and logical comparisons?
The arithmetic logic unit (ALU) is a digital circuit that performs arithmetic and logical operations on binary numbers.
tech-computing-0003: What happens to the contents of random-access memory (RAM) when a computer loses power?
They are automatically copied to the processor
Common RAM is volatile: it loses its data when power is cut.
tech-computing-0004: What is the common abbreviation for memory whose data is written at the factory and is not lost when power is cut?
ROM is nonvolatile read-only memory that retains its data without power.
tech-computing-0005: What is the small, extremely fast memory near the processor that stores frequently used data to reduce access time?
Processor cache is smaller and faster than main memory and stores copies of frequently used data.
tech-computing-0006: What is the electronic board on which computer components such as the processor and memory are mounted and interconnected?
The motherboard is the main printed circuit board that holds and connects the essential components.
tech-computing-0007: Which processor was originally designed to accelerate image creation and display?
A graphics processor is a specialized circuit designed to speed up image generation and output to the screen.
tech-computing-0008: A desktop computer's power supply converts alternating current from the outlet into what type of current?
The power supply converts mains alternating current into regulated direct current at low voltages suitable for the components.
tech-computing-0009: How does a solid-state drive (SSD) differ from a traditional hard drive in its storage method?
It stores data on rotating magnetic disks in a sealed enclosure
It stores data in memory chips without moving parts
It uses a laser on a reflective surface
It stores data on magnetic tape wound inside it
An SSD uses integrated circuits, usually flash memory, to store data and has no moving parts.
tech-computing-0010: What principle does a traditional hard disk drive (HDD) use to store data?
Laser engraving on a reflective surface
A hard disk stores data magnetically on rigid rotating disks.
tech-computing-0011: What does an optical disk drive use to read data from a disk's surface?
An optical disk drive reads data using a laser beam reflected from the disk surface.
tech-computing-0012: In older personal computers, which firmware runs first at startup, initializes the hardware, and begins loading the operating system?
BIOS is firmware that initializes hardware during startup, then hands control to the operating system loader.
tech-computing-0013: What is the process of starting a computer and loading its operating system into memory called?
Booting is the process of starting the computer until the operating system is ready to work.
tech-computing-0014: A scanner inputs images and documents into the computer. The others are output devices.
tech-computing-0015: A printer outputs computer data onto paper. The others are input devices.
tech-computing-0016: Which American inventor created the computer mouse in the 1960s?
Douglas Engelbart created the first computer mouse in the 1960s.
tech-computing-0017: The common English keyboard layout is named after the first six letters of its top letter row. What is it called?
The QWERTY layout is named after the first six letters in the top row of an English keyboard.
tech-computing-0018: What is the smallest element of a digital image or screen whose color can be controlled individually?
A pixel is the smallest addressable element of a raster image or display.
tech-computing-0019: Screens create colors by mixing which three primary colors of light?
The additive RGB model mixes red, green, and blue light to produce screen colors.
tech-computing-0020: Which color model do color printers generally use?
CMYK is a subtractive model using cyan, magenta, yellow, and black for color printing.
tech-computing-0021: What does a screen resolution of 1920x1080 mean?
Screen length and width in millimeters
Display resolution is stated as the number of pixels across the width, then the height.
tech-computing-0022: What unit measures a screen's refresh rate?
Refresh rate is the number of times the image is redrawn each second, measured in hertz.
tech-computing-0023: Which unit normally measures a modern processor's clock speed?
Modern processor clock frequency is measured in gigahertz, billions of cycles per second.
tech-computing-0024: What does 'quad-core' mean for a processor?
It runs at four times the clock speed
It contains four independent processing units
It connects to four screens simultaneously
It contains four separate main memories
A multicore processor contains several independent processing units on one chip; a quad-core has four.
tech-computing-0025: What is the function of the heat sink mounted on a processor?
To transfer heat away from the processor
To strengthen the wireless network signal
A heat sink is a heat exchanger that transfers heat from the component to the surrounding air.
tech-computing-0026: In which year was the transistor, the basis of modern electronics and computers, invented?
The first practical transistor was invented at Bell Laboratories in 1947.
tech-computing-0027: Which engineer received the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics for his role in inventing the integrated circuit?
Jack Kilby received the 2000 Nobel Prize in Physics in recognition of his role in inventing the integrated circuit.
tech-computing-0028: Moore's law states that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit doubles approximately every...?
Gordon Moore observed that the number of transistors in an integrated circuit doubles approximately every two years.
tech-computing-0029: Who designed the Analytical Engine in the nineteenth century, considered the first concept of a general-purpose programmable computer?
Charles Babbage designed the Analytical Engine around 1837, the first design for a general-purpose mechanical computer.
tech-computing-0030: Who is considered the first person to publish an algorithm intended for execution by a calculating machine?
Ada Lovelace wrote an algorithm for calculating Bernoulli numbers on the Analytical Engine and is considered the first programmer.
tech-computing-0031: Which American computer scientist is associated with early compiler development and the COBOL programming language?
Grace Hopper pioneered compilers, and her ideas contributed greatly to COBOL.
tech-computing-0033: What does the Turing test, proposed in 1950, assess?
A machine's ability to imitate a human in conversation
Data integrity after transmission over distant networks
The Turing test assesses a machine's ability to show intelligent behavior indistinguishable from human behavior in conversation.
tech-computing-0034: Which huge American electronic computer was unveiled in 1946 at the University of Pennsylvania?
ENIAC was unveiled in 1946 and built at the University of Pennsylvania's Moore School of Electrical Engineering.
tech-computing-0035: Which electronic component underpinned first-generation computers in the 1940s and 1950s?
Early electronic computers relied on vacuum tubes before transistors replaced them.
tech-computing-0036: Which architecture stores program instructions and data together in the same memory?
Von Neumann architecture is a stored-program architecture in which instructions and data share the same memory.
tech-computing-0037: Combining processor and screen in one piece
Separating instruction memory from data memory
Using vacuum tubes instead of transistors
Harvard architecture gives program instructions separate memory and pathways from data memory.
tech-computing-0038: In which year was the first commercial single-chip microprocessor released?
The first commercial single-chip microprocessor was released in 1971.
tech-computing-0039: Punched cards were used to process the 1890 United States census. Who created the machine?
Herman Hollerith developed the punched-card tabulating machine used in the 1890 census.
tech-computing-0040: Which early nineteenth-century machine used punched cards to control patterns, inspiring the idea of programming?
The Jacquard loom (1804) controlled weaving patterns with punched cards and inspired the idea of storing instructions.
tech-computing-0041: Which mathematician gave his name to the algebra of true and false values underlying logic circuits?
George Boole introduced logical algebra in his books of 1847 and 1854, so it was named after him.
tech-computing-0042: Which American scientist is known as the father of information theory?
Claude Shannon laid the foundations of information theory in his 1948 paper, earning this title.
tech-computing-0043: What does the initial U in USB stand for?
USB stands for Universal Serial Bus.
tech-computing-0044: What does an HDMI cable carry between a device and a display?
HDMI is a digital interface carrying video and audio through one cable.
tech-computing-0045: Which German philosopher and mathematician published a paper in 1703 on binary arithmetic using 0 and 1?
Leibniz published his paper on binary arithmetic in 1703. It forms the basis of computer arithmetic.
tech-computing-0046: Which German engineer built the programmable Z3 computer in 1941?
Konrad Zuse built the Z3 in 1941, the first working programmable digital computer.
tech-computing-0047: Which British electronic computer was used during World War II to analyze encrypted messages?
Colossus computers were built in Britain between 1943 and 1945 to assist codebreakers.
tech-computing-0048: What is the smallest unit of computer information, taking only one of two values, 0 or 1?
The bit is the simplest information unit and represents one of two possible logical states.
tech-computing-0049: How many bits does one byte contain according to today's standard convention?
A byte in modern usage contains eight bits.
tech-computing-0050: What is a group of four bits, or half a byte, called?
A nibble is a group of four bits, half a byte.
tech-computing-0051: How many bytes are in a kibibyte (KiB), using binary prefixes?
A kibibyte equals 2 to the tenth power, or 1024 bytes.
tech-computing-0052: What is the base of the binary number system used by computers?
Binary is a base-2 number system using only the digits 0 and 1.
tech-computing-0053: In hexadecimal, which symbol represents decimal 15?
Hexadecimal uses A through F for values 10 through 15, so F equals 15.
tech-computing-0054: Exactly how many bits does one hexadecimal digit represent?
Each hexadecimal digit represents four bits, so a byte is written with two hexadecimal digits.
tech-computing-0055: How many characters are in the original ASCII encoding table?
Original ASCII is a seven-bit encoding containing 128 characters.
tech-computing-0056: What is the main purpose of the Unicode encoding standard?
To speed up data transfer between devices
To compress large text files to reduce disk space
To represent characters from most world languages with standardized numbers
Unicode is a unified text encoding standard for most of the world's writing systems.
tech-computing-0057: In UTF-8, what is the maximum number of bytes a single character can occupy?
UTF-8 encodes a character in one to four bytes, depending on its code point.
tech-computing-0058: Which logic gate outputs 1 only if both inputs are 1?
An AND gate outputs 1 only when all its inputs are 1.
tech-computing-0059: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs differ?
XOR, or exclusive OR, outputs 1 when exactly one input is 1.
tech-computing-0060: Which logic gate has one input and reverses its value?
The NOT gate, or inverter, outputs the opposite of its single input.
tech-computing-0061: Which logic gate is called universal because any logic circuit can be built using it alone?
NAND is a universal gate: any logical function can be built using it alone.
tech-computing-0062: What is the most common way computers represent negative integers?
Two's complement is the most common representation of signed integers in computers.
tech-computing-0063: What is the common standard for representing floating-point numbers in computers?
IEEE 754 is a technical standard for floating-point arithmetic established in 1985.
tech-computing-0064: What is the error called when an arithmetic result exceeds the largest value an integer variable can hold?
Integer overflow occurs when an operation produces a value outside the range representable by the available digits.
tech-computing-0065: What is compression called if decompression restores the file exactly, bit for bit?
Lossless compression allows the original data to be reconstructed exactly from the compressed data.
tech-computing-0066: What type of compression is normally used by JPEG images?
JPEG is a common method of lossy compression for digital images.
tech-computing-0067: What distinguishes vector graphics from raster images?
They store each pixel's color separately
They cannot be printed on paper
They can be enlarged without losing sharpness
Vector graphics are defined by mathematical geometric shapes, allowing enlargement without loss of quality.
tech-computing-0068: Converting analog sound to digital requires reading signal values at regular time intervals. What is this process called?
Sampling converts a continuous signal into a sequence of values at spaced points in time.
tech-computing-0069: According to the Nyquist-Shannon theorem, the sampling rate must exceed how many times the signal's highest frequency?
The theorem requires a sampling rate greater than twice the highest frequency to reconstruct the signal without distortion.
tech-computing-0070: What is the function of a parity bit added to transmitted data?
Numbering packets to restore their order
Compressing data to reduce its size
A parity bit is the simplest error-detection code and detects a change in an odd number of bits.
tech-computing-0071: In hexadecimal web colors, what color does #FFFFFF represent?
FFFFFF means maximum red, green, and blue intensity together, producing white.
tech-computing-0072: Which data type has only two values, true and false?
The Boolean type has only two values, representing true and false.
tech-computing-0073: What data type represents a sequence of characters, such as words and sentences?
A string in programming is a sequence of characters.
tech-computing-0074: What does a filename extension such as .txt or .png indicate?
A filename extension is a suffix indicating a property of the file, most commonly its content type and format.
tech-computing-0075: What was the main purpose of the PDF file format?
Compressing audio files to reduce size
Displaying a document with the same appearance on any device
Running executable programs on any operating system
PDF displays documents independently of software, hardware, and operating systems.
tech-computing-0076: In little-endian order, which byte of a number is stored first in memory?
Little-endian stores the least significant byte at the lowest address.
tech-computing-0077: What is the main purpose of combining files into a compressed ZIP archive?
Converting written text into audible audio files
Reducing size and combining several files into one
ZIP is an archive format supporting lossless compression and can contain multiple files and folders.
tech-computing-0078: How does a QR code differ from a traditional barcode?
It is one-dimensional with parallel lines
It is read magnetically rather than optically
It is a two-dimensional matrix code
A QR code is a two-dimensional matrix code that holds more data than a linear barcode.
tech-computing-0079: In which country was the QR code invented in 1994?
The QR code was invented in Japan in 1994 to track automotive parts.
tech-computing-0080: In the RGB color model, what color results when all three components have zero intensity?
RGB is additive: the absence of all red, green, and blue light produces black.
tech-computing-0081: A megapixel in digital camera specifications equals how many pixels?
A megapixel is one million pixels and describes the number of elements in a camera sensor.
tech-computing-0082: What unit normally measures network data transfer speed?
Data transfer rate is measured by the number of bits transmitted per second.
tech-computing-0084: How many different values can one byte, eight bits, represent?
Eight bits give 2 to the eighth power, or 256 values, from 0 to 255.
tech-computing-0085: What is the idea behind run-length encoding compression?
Encrypting repeated data with a shared secret key
Permanently deleting all repeated data from a file
Replacing consecutive repeated values with the value and its repetition count
Moving repeated data into a separate file
Run-length encoding stores a consecutive sequence of the same value as one value together with its count.
tech-computing-0086: What is a word in processor architecture?
A variable's name in a program
The natural unit of data processed by the processor at once
Any text written in a programming language
One full line of source code before translation into machine language
A word is the natural data unit handled by a processor's design, with its length determining register size.
tech-computing-0087: What does the zero-valued NUL character signify in C?
The start of a new line
Strings in C terminate with the zero-valued NUL character.
tech-computing-0088: Which network began operating in 1969 and is considered the original nucleus of the internet?
ARPANET was the first wide-area packet-switching network. It began operating in 1969 and formed the basis of the internet.
tech-computing-0089: Which British scientist invented the World Wide Web (WWW)?
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.
tech-computing-0090: At which scientific institution did the idea of the World Wide Web originate in 1989?
Tim Berners-Lee proposed the web in 1989 while working at CERN near Geneva.
tech-computing-0091: What is the correct relationship between the internet and the web?
The web is two decades older than the internet
They are synonymous names for exactly the same thing
The web is an information service running over the internet
The internet is a small part of the web
The web is an information system available through the internet. The internet is the network supporting it and other services such as email.
tech-computing-0092: Vint Cerf and Robert Kahn are called the fathers of the internet for designing what?
Cerf and Kahn designed the TCP/IP protocols on which the internet is based.
tech-computing-0093: Who first used @ in email addresses in 1971?
Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, using @ to separate the username from the machine name.
tech-computing-0094: What is the main markup language for describing web page structure and elements?
HTML is the standard markup language for documents intended for display in a web browser.
tech-computing-0095: What does CSS do in web pages?
Encrypt communication between browser and remote server
Transfer the page from server to browser
Style the page's appearance, such as colors and fonts
Store user data on the server
CSS is a style sheet language describing how a document written in a markup language is presented.
tech-computing-0096: What do HT stand for in HTTP?
HTTP stands for Hypertext Transfer Protocol.
tech-computing-0097: What does HTTPS add to HTTP?
Saving a full copy of the page in device memory
HTTPS is HTTP over an encrypted TLS connection.
tech-computing-0098: What is the default port for HTTPS?
HTTPS uses port 443 by default, while HTTP uses port 80.
tech-computing-0099: What is the function of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
Translating website names into IP addresses
DNS translates memorable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
tech-computing-0100: Which port does DNS usually use?
DNS servers operate on port 53 over UDP and TCP.
tech-computing-0101: What is the default port for the SSH secure remote access protocol?
The standard port for SSH servers is 22.
tech-computing-0102: Why did SSH replace Telnet for remote device administration?
Because Telnet supports only graphical commands
Because Telnet works only on wireless networks
Because Telnet connects to only one computer
Because Telnet sends passwords as unencrypted text
Telnet transmits data, including passwords, without encryption, so encrypted SSH replaced it.
tech-computing-0103: Which protocol sends email and transfers it between servers?
SMTP is the standard internet protocol for transferring email.
tech-computing-0104: Which protocol retrieves mailbox messages while keeping them synchronized on the server?
IMAP retrieves messages from a mail server while leaving them there.
tech-computing-0105: Setting the time on connected devices
Transferring files between devices over a network
Translating domain names into their numerical addresses
FTP is a standard protocol for transferring files from a server to a client over a network.
tech-computing-0106: Which protocol automatically gives devices IP addresses when they join a network?
DHCP automatically distributes IP addresses and network settings to devices.
tech-computing-0107: Which protocol synchronizes device clocks over a network?
NTP synchronizes clocks between computer systems over networks.
tech-computing-0108: How many bits long is an IPv4 address?
tech-computing-0109: How many bits does an IPv6 address contain?
IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long to address the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses.
tech-computing-0110: Which address has a valid IPv4 format?
An IPv4 address has four numbers from 0 to 255 separated by dots. The number 300 exceeds 255.
tech-computing-0111: The address range 192.168.x.x is reserved for what kind of network?
The 192.168.0.0/16 range is a private address range reserved for internal networks.
tech-computing-0112: What does IPv4 address 127.0.0.1 refer to?
127.0.0.1 is the loopback address referring to the device itself.
tech-computing-0113: How many bits long is the MAC address that physically identifies a network card usually?
Common MAC addresses are 48 bits long and written as six hexadecimal pairs.
tech-computing-0114: Which technology allows several devices on a home network to share one public IP address?
NAT rewrites addresses in packets, allowing an entire private network to use one public address.
tech-computing-0115: Which protocol finds the MAC address corresponding to an IPv4 address within a local network?
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) maps a network-layer address to a MAC address.
tech-computing-0116: Which protocol does the ping command use to test whether a device is reachable?
Ping sends ICMP echo request messages and waits for replies.
tech-computing-0117: It is faster because it does not check delivery
It carries only text, not images or files
It works only on local wireless networks
It ensures ordered delivery and retransmits missing data
TCP provides reliable, ordered, error-checked delivery, unlike UDP.
tech-computing-0118: Why is UDP preferred for live streaming and internet voice calls?
It has lower delay and does not wait for retransmission
It guarantees every packet arrives without loss, duplication, or delay
UDP suits time-sensitive applications, where dropping a packet is preferable to waiting for its retransmission.
tech-computing-0119: How many layers are in the OSI reference model for network communication?
OSI divides communication into seven layers, from physical to application.
tech-computing-0120: What is the top, seventh layer of the OSI model?
The seventh OSI layer is the application layer, closest to the user.
tech-computing-0121: At which OSI layer does a router primarily operate?
A router forwards packets by IP address, a function of layer three, the network layer.
tech-computing-0122: How does a switch improve on a hub in a local network?
It always sends data to all connected devices
It converts electrical signals into light
It sends data only to the intended device
A switch forwards data only to the port leading to the intended device. A hub repeats it to all ports.
tech-computing-0123: What does LAN mean in networking?
A wide-area network linking countries and continents
A communications network linking stations by satellite
A local network within a limited area such as a building or home
A LAN connects computers within a limited area such as a home, school, or building.
tech-computing-0124: Which IEEE standards group covers wireless local networks (Wi-Fi)?
IEEE 802.11 comprises the standards underlying Wi-Fi.
tech-computing-0125: What is the most common wired local networking technology, standardized as IEEE 802.3?
Ethernet is a family of wired networking technologies standardized in IEEE 802.3.
tech-computing-0126: Bluetooth wireless technology was named after whom?
A tenth-century king of Denmark and Norway
The name comes from King Harald Bluetooth, who ruled Denmark and Norway in the tenth century.
tech-computing-0127: What carries data inside fiber-optic cables?
Optical fibers carry data as light through glass or plastic fibers.
tech-computing-0128: Delay between sending data and its arrival
Proportion of packets lost along the way
Latency is the time delay between a cause and its effect; in networks, between transmission and arrival.
tech-computing-0129: What is a complete web resource address, such as https://example.com/page, called?
URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, a reference identifying a resource's location on a network.
tech-computing-0130: In example.org, what is the .org part called?
A top-level domain is the final part of a domain name, such as .org or .com.
tech-computing-0131: What is Kuwait's country-code top-level domain?
tech-computing-0132: Software extensions users install to speed up browsing and save time
Malicious programs that secretly steal passwords
Thumbnails of pages the user visited
Small pieces of data a website stores in the user's browser
A cookie is a small block of data created by a server and stored by the browser on the user's device.
tech-computing-0133: What does HTTP status code 404 mean when opening a web page?
The requested page is not on the server
The page was successfully moved permanently to a new address
Code 404 means the server could not find the requested resource.
tech-computing-0134: What method does the internet use to transfer data in small units that each follow their own route?
Packet switching divides data into packets, each transmitted independently across the network.
tech-computing-0135: Which port does unencrypted HTTP use by default?
The default port for HTTP servers is 80.
tech-computing-0136: What is the scam in which an attacker impersonates a trusted organization in a message to lure a victim into revealing a password?
Phishing is social engineering in which an attacker tricks a victim into revealing sensitive information.
tech-computing-0137: What is malicious software that encrypts a victim's files and demands money to decrypt them called?
Ransomware blocks access to a victim's data by encrypting it and demands a ransom.
tech-computing-0138: What distinguishes a worm from a computer virus?

It spreads independently over a network without a host file
A worm is a standalone program that copies itself and spreads over a network. A virus requires a host program.
tech-computing-0139: Why is a Trojan horse in malware called that?
It was the first virus discovered in Greece
It spreads very quickly between devices
It disguises itself as useful software
A Trojan deceives users about its nature by hiding in apparently useful software, like the wooden horse in the ancient story.
tech-computing-0140: Which malicious software secretly gathers user information and sends it to another party?
Spyware collects information about a person or device and sends it elsewhere without their knowledge.
tech-computing-0141: Which program secretly records keystrokes to steal passwords?
Keystroke logging secretly records keys pressed without the user's knowledge.
tech-computing-0142: What does a network firewall do?

Monitor and filter data traffic according to security rules
Cool servers in large data centers
A firewall is a security system that monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and controls it using defined rules.
tech-computing-0143: What is two-factor authentication at login?
Entering two consecutive passwords of the same type
Logging in from two devices simultaneously
Proving identity with two different factors, such as a password and a temporary code
Sharing one account between two people
Multifactor authentication requires two or more different types of evidence, such as something you know and something you possess.
tech-computing-0144: What attack tries possible passwords one after another until it finds the correct one?
A brute-force attack tries many passwords in the hope of eventually finding the correct one.
tech-computing-0145: Which password is strongest against guessing?
Password strength increases with length, randomness, and symbol variety. The others are common and easy to guess.

In a man-in-the-middle attack, the attacker secretly stands between parties who think they are communicating directly, relaying and potentially altering their messages.
tech-computing-0147: What is the aim of a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack?

Secretly changing website content without owners or visitors knowing
Encrypting a victim's files and demanding a ransom
Flooding a server with requests until users cannot access it
A denial-of-service attack overwhelms its target with excessive requests, preventing legitimate users from accessing it.
tech-computing-0148: What is a network of compromised devices remotely controlled by an attacker called?
A botnet is a group of internet-connected devices infected with malware that allows an attacker to control them.

Cross-site scripting lets an attacker inject scripts into pages viewed by other users.
tech-computing-0151: What is the flaw called when a program writes data beyond the bounds of its allocated memory space?
A buffer overflow is an anomaly in which a program writes data outside a buffer's bounds into adjacent memory.
tech-computing-0152: What does a zero-day vulnerability mean in computer security?

A vulnerability discovered and fixed on the same day
A vulnerability appearing only on the first day of each calendar month
An old vulnerability harmless to systems
A zero-day vulnerability has no official security patch available, whether the vendor has just learned of it or is not yet aware of it.
tech-computing-0153: What term describes psychologically deceiving people into revealing secrets rather than technically breaking into systems?
In information security, social engineering is psychological manipulation to make people act or disclose confidential information.
tech-computing-0154: In symmetric encryption, how many keys are used for encryption and decryption?

Two keys, one public and one private
Symmetric-key algorithms use the same key to encrypt and decrypt text.

RSA security relies on the difficulty of factoring the product of two large primes.
tech-computing-0157: Which symmetric encryption standard did the US government adopt in 2001 to replace DES?
The US National Institute of Standards and Technology adopted AES in 2001 to replace DES.
tech-computing-0158: What is the essential property of a cryptographic hash function?

It compresses a file so it can later be fully restored

A cryptographic hash function produces a fixed-length value from any input and is practically impossible to reverse to recover the input.
tech-computing-0159: Why is a salt added to a password before hashing it?

To shorten passwords for easier memorization
To allow recovery of the original password
A salt is random data added before hashing. It gives identical passwords different hashes and defeats precomputed tables.

Shifting three positions forward turns A into D.
tech-computing-0161: What is the main purpose of a digital signature on a message or file?

Compressing the message to reduce its size
A digital signature is a mathematical scheme for verifying a message's authenticity and that it has not been altered.
tech-computing-0162: Which entity issues digital certificates to establish website identity?
A certificate authority issues digital certificates establishing ownership of a public key.

tech-computing-0164: Under the 3-2-1 backup rule, how many copies should be kept off-site?

tech-computing-0165: What does a virtual private network (VPN) provide for a user?

A VPN extends a private network across a public one through a tunnel, usually with encryption.
tech-computing-0166: What do traditional antivirus programs rely on to detect known malware?

Signature-based detection compares files against distinctive patterns of known malware.
tech-computing-0167: What is a sandbox in software security?

A barrier that cuts off internet access entirely
An isolated environment for running suspicious programs without harming the system

A sandbox isolates running programs to prevent faults or vulnerabilities from spreading to the system.
tech-computing-0168: Why is installing operating system security updates as soon as they are released recommended?

A software patch is an update that fixes bugs, including security vulnerabilities.
tech-computing-0169: What is the purpose of a website CAPTCHA?

Least privilege requires each user or program to access only what is needed for its legitimate purpose.
tech-computing-0171: What are the three pillars of information security abbreviated CIA?
The information security triad comprises confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

A honeypot is a security mechanism that looks like a legitimate target but is isolated and monitored to detect attackers.

Spam consists of unsolicited messages sent in large quantities, mostly commercial.

A password manager stores passwords encrypted and can generate different strong passwords for each account.

Running a computer on solar power without electricity

tech-computing-0257: Who coined the term hypertext in the 1960s?
Ted Nelson coined the terms hypertext and hypermedia in 1963.

tech-computing-0264: What pioneering conversational program did Joseph Weizenbaum write in the 1960s?
Joseph Weizenbaum wrote ELIZA between 1964 and 1967 at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
tech-computing-0265: What is an expert system in artificial intelligence?

tech-computing-0266: Which field aims to enable computers to understand and process human languages?
Natural language processing concerns computers' ability to process data written in human languages.

tech-computing-0283: If a connection's speed is 8 megabits per second, approximately how many megabytes does it transfer per second?
A byte consists of eight bits, so eight megabits equal one megabyte.
tech-computing-0284: Which device converts digital signals to analog and back to transmit data over telephone lines?
A modem modulates a carrier signal to encode digital data and demodulates it on reception.
tech-computing-0285: What is a repeater's function in a network?
Translating private network addresses into public addresses
Encrypting data before it leaves the network
Assigning IP addresses to new devices
Strengthening a signal and retransmitting it over a greater distance
A repeater receives a signal and retransmits it to cover a longer distance.
tech-computing-0286: What are the two best-known frequency bands used by home Wi-Fi networks?
Wi-Fi commonly operates in the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands.
tech-computing-0287: What does the SSID identify in a wireless network?
The password required to connect to the network
The network name displayed when searching for it
The network's maximum speed in megabits
SSID stands for service set identifier, the wireless network name users see.
tech-computing-0288: Which of these Wi-Fi security protocols is the oldest and weakest, to the point of being insecure?
WEP is the oldest Wi-Fi security algorithm; its weaknesses led to its replacement by WPA and later protocols.
tech-computing-0289: What is dividing a local network into mutually isolated logical networks at the data link layer called?
A VLAN is a broadcast domain virtually partitioned and isolated within a local network at layer two.
tech-computing-0290: In the email address name@example.com, what does the part after @ represent?
An email address consists of a local part before @ and a domain after it.
tech-computing-0291: Which program reads screen content aloud to help blind people use a computer?
A screen reader is assistive technology that converts screen content into speech or Braille for blind and visually impaired people.
tech-computing-0292: Which technology converts images of printed or handwritten text into editable digital text?
Optical character recognition converts images of text into machine-encoded text.
tech-computing-0293: In spreadsheet software, what is the intersection of a row and column called?
A spreadsheet consists of cells arranged in rows and columns; each cell is the intersection of a row and a column.
tech-computing-0294: In spreadsheets, what does the $ symbol do in a reference such as $A$1?
Hides the cell from the user
Converts the cell value into currency
Sums all values in the column
Keeps the reference fixed when copying the formula
The $ sign makes a reference absolute, so it does not change when the formula is copied to other cells.
tech-computing-0295: Deleting old data to save space
Compressing data to speed up transmission
Saving a copy of data to restore it if the original is lost
A backup is a copy of data stored elsewhere for recovery after data loss.
tech-computing-0296: What does formatting a storage medium usually do?
Prepares it for use by creating a new file system
Copies its contents to another medium
Encrypts all files stored on it
Disk formatting prepares a disk for initial use and includes creating a new file system that erases its previous indexes.
tech-computing-0297: What is the main function of a computer's file system?
Protecting the device against viruses and various malicious programs
Speeding up the processor when running large programs
Organizing how files are stored, named, and retrieved
Connecting the computer to the local wireless network
A file system determines how data is stored and retrieved and how files are named and organized.
tech-computing-0298: Which unit expresses a printer's or scanner's resolution?
Printing and scanning resolution is measured by the number of dots per inch.
tech-computing-0299: Game software that can never be updated
A free trial version of commercial software
Software embedded in hardware that controls its basic operation
Firmware is software providing low-level control of a particular device's hardware.
tech-computing-0300: What is the difference between computer hardware and software?
Hardware is system programs, while software is user programs
Hardware is old-fashioned, while software is modern
Hardware is physical components, while software is instructions that operate them
Hardware is for networks, while software is for storage
Hardware consists of the computer's physical parts; software consists of instructions telling it what to do.
tech-computing-0301: What is descriptive information accompanying a file, such as creation date, author, and image dimensions, called?
Metadata is data providing information about other data.
islamic-architecture-0001: What is the recessed niche in the qibla (direction of prayer) wall that shows worshippers the direction of the Kaaba called?
The mihrab (prayer niche) is a recess in the qibla (direction of prayer) wall indicating the direction of Mecca, near which the imam (prayer leader) stands.
islamic-architecture-0002: What are the stepped architectural decorations resembling honeycombs or stalactites, used in the transition between a wall and a dome, called?
Muqarnas is a decorative structural element made of small overlapping recesses like honeycombs, adorning domes, entrances, and the tops of walls.
islamic-architecture-0003: What is the architectural term for a vaulted hall enclosed on three sides and completely open on one side to a courtyard?
An iwan is a rectangular vaulted space with walls on three sides and a facade fully open to the courtyard.
islamic-architecture-0004: In a traditional congregational mosque, what is the open courtyard usually surrounded by arcades called?
The sahn is the mosque's open courtyard, surrounded by roofed arcades in most congregational mosques.
islamic-architecture-0006: What is the screened or enclosed space near the mihrab (prayer niche) where a ruler prayed in some congregational mosques for security?
The maqsura is an enclosed space near the mihrab (prayer niche), reserved for the ruler and his guards in a number of early congregational mosques.
islamic-architecture-0007: Which structural element in the corners of a square converts it into an octagon to support a circular-based dome?
A squinch, or corner muqarnas, is an arch or recess at the corner of a square that makes its base octagonal to support a dome.
islamic-architecture-0008: Which type of arch is characteristic of Andalusian and Maghrebi architecture, widening above its springing points before closing?
The horseshoe arch extends beyond a semicircle, widening above its springing points; it became characteristic of Andalusian and Maghrebi architecture.
islamic-architecture-0009: What is the name of the construction style using alternating courses of light and dark stone in Levantine and Egyptian architecture?
Ablaq alternates light and dark stones in courses or arch voussoirs and was common in Mamluk architecture.
islamic-architecture-0010: What material is zellij, used to cover walls and floors in Morocco and al-Andalus, made of?
Colored glass pieces set in lead
Zellij is a mosaic of hand-cut glazed ceramic pieces assembled into geometric patterns.
islamic-architecture-0011: What are the perforated wooden windows projecting from traditional house facades that allow viewing and ventilation while preserving privacy called?
A mashrabiyya is a projecting wooden lattice covering windows, admitting air and light while shielding the interior from passersby's view.
islamic-architecture-0012: What is the main function of a malqaf or barjeel in traditional architecture in the Gulf and Iran?
Watching for arrivals from far away
Cooling the house by directing airflow
A barjeel (windcatcher) is a tower that catches wind and directs it into the house to cool it without power.
islamic-architecture-0013: What are the underground water channels known in Iran as qanats, which carry groundwater by natural gravity?
Stone channels raised on rows of columns
Underground tunnels with vertical ventilation shafts
A qanat is a gently sloping tunnel carrying water from an aquifer, with vertical shafts for excavation and ventilation.
islamic-architecture-0014: What is the Iranian garden layout that divides a garden into four parts with perpendicular paths or water channels called?
Chahar bagh (four gardens) is a four-part layout divided by perpendicular paths and water channels, which spread from Iran to India and al-Andalus.
islamic-architecture-0015: What waqf (charitable endowment) structure provided free drinking water to passersby in Islamic cities and often had a children's school above it?
A sabil is a charitable structure providing water to passersby. In Cairo it was combined with a kuttab (elementary school) on the upper floor, known as a sabil-kuttab.
islamic-architecture-0016: What is the Ottoman term for a complex surrounding a mosque and containing schools, a charitable kitchen, a bathhouse, and a hospital?
A kulliye is an integrated Ottoman complex around a mosque, including schools, an imaret (charitable kitchen), a bathhouse, a hospital, and other facilities.
islamic-architecture-0020: Which architectural style arose in areas conquered by Christian kingdoms in al-Andalus, where Muslim craftsmen built using their own architectural methods?
Mudejar architecture was produced by Muslim craftsmen who remained under Christian rule, using brick and Andalusian decoration.
islamic-architecture-0021: Which Arabic script with sharp angles and geometric forms predominated in mosque inscriptions in the early centuries?
Kufic is a geometric, angular script and the earliest script used to decorate Islamic architecture, as at the Dome of the Rock.
islamic-architecture-0023: What are the Ottoman ceramic tiles famous for blue and coral-red colors, covering the walls of many Istanbul mosques, called?
Iznik ceramics were produced in Iznik in Anatolia, peaked in the sixteenth century, and decorated Istanbul's mosques.
islamic-architecture-0024: What is the main material used to build traditional African Sahel mosques such as the Great Mosque of Djenne in Mali?
Sudano-Sahelian mosques are built of mudbrick and coated in earthen plaster that is renewed periodically.
islamic-architecture-0025: What are the wooden poles projecting from the walls of Sahelian earthen mosques, used as permanent scaffolding for renewing the mud coating, called?
Toron are bundles of palm wood embedded in the wall, serving as permanent scaffolding for annual repairs to the earthen coating.
islamic-architecture-0026: What is the open platform surrounding a minaret's shaft where the muezzin (caller to prayer) stands called?
The balcony is a circular platform around the minaret's shaft where the muezzin (caller to prayer) stands; the number of balconies varies with the mosque's importance.
islamic-architecture-0027: What shape do classical Ottoman minarets, such as those of Istanbul's major mosques, have?
Short square towers with an octagonal pavilion on top
An Ottoman minaret is a slender cylinder or polygon topped with a pointed conical cap, resembling a pencil.
islamic-architecture-0028: What shape predominated in traditional Maghrebi and Andalusian minarets, such as those of the mosques of Kairouan, Marrakesh, and Seville?
Spiral with an external winding staircase
The Maghrebi-Andalusian minaret is a square-section tower topped by a smaller pavilion, as in the Kutubiyya and Giralda.
islamic-architecture-0031: What is the historical name of the institution housing Sufis and ascetics in Mamluk cities?
A khanqah is a building for Sufis' residence and worship and was widespread in Mamluk Cairo.
islamic-architecture-0032: What is the coastal fortress where Muslims were stationed to guard frontiers, with famous examples in Sousse and Monastir, Tunisia?
A ribat is a frontier fortress where defenders lived for guarding and worship; famous examples include the ribats of Sousse and Monastir.
islamic-architecture-0033: What does kasbah mean in Maghrebi architecture?
A citadel or fortified district within a city
A covered market for fabrics and silk
In Morocco and Algeria, a kasbah is a citadel or fortified district within a city, serving as the ruler's or garrison's headquarters.
islamic-architecture-0034: What is an earthen fortified village with walls and towers in southern Morocco, famously exemplified by Ait Benhaddou, called?
A ksar, called ighrem in Amazigh, is an earthen fortified village surrounded by walls and towers; Ait Benhaddou is its best-known example.
islamic-architecture-0035: What does riad mean in traditional Moroccan housing?
A house around an internal garden courtyard
A monumental gate in the old city wall
A riad is a traditional Moroccan house opening onto a planted interior courtyard, often with a central fountain.
islamic-architecture-0037: What is the Persian name for a traditional underground reservoir keeping drinking water cool in cities such as Yazd, topped by a dome and windcatchers?
An ab anbar is a domed underground water reservoir surrounded by windcatchers that keep water cool in Iranian desert cities.
islamic-architecture-0038: What is the purpose of the old earthen building with a high conical dome known in Iran as a yakhchal?
A yakhchal is an ancient building with a conical dome and thick walls that preserves ice throughout summer in a desert environment.
islamic-architecture-0039: What is the raised stairway beside the mihrab (prayer niche) that the preacher ascends on Friday called?
The minbar (pulpit) is a raised stairway beside the mihrab (prayer niche) ascended by the preacher; inlaid wooden examples such as the Kairouan mosque's minbar are famous.
islamic-architecture-0041: What is the monumental projecting rectangular portal framing the entrance arch of mosques in Iran, Central Asia, and India called?
A pishtaq is a monumental projecting rectangular entrance facade surrounding an iwan arch or gateway, common in Iranian, Timurid, and Mughal architecture.
islamic-architecture-0042: What are the decorated projecting wooden windows and balconies on historic Jeddah house facades called in the Hejaz?
A rawshan is an enclosed projecting wooden balcony characteristic of historic Jeddah houses and similar to a mashrabiyya.
islamic-architecture-0043: What does jami mean in Islamic architectural terminology?
A large mosque where Friday prayers are held
A mosque attached to a school or khanqah
A jami, or congregational mosque, is a large mosque where Jumuah (Friday congregational prayer) and its khutbah (sermon) are held.
islamic-architecture-0044: What is the mosque wall that worshippers face and that contains the mihrab (prayer niche) called?
The qibla (direction of prayer) wall faces the Kaaba and contains the mihrab (prayer niche); worshippers face it.
islamic-architecture-0045: What is the Persian name for geometric ornament of interlacing lines forming overlapping stars and polygons on walls and doors?
Girih is geometric decoration of interlacing lines forming stars and polygons, widespread in Islamic architecture.
islamic-architecture-0046: The Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun in Cairo has a minaret with an external spiral staircase; which city's minaret probably influenced it?
Ahmad ibn Tulun grew up in Samarra, and his mosque's spiral minaret imitates the Malwiya of the Great Mosque of Samarra.
islamic-architecture-0047: What was the main material used to build the Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun, unlike most later stone mosques in Cairo?
Ibn Tulun's mosque was built of red brick coated with carved plaster, following Iraqi architectural practice.
islamic-architecture-0048: Which Cairo mosque is the oldest to survive largely in its original form?
Ibn Tulun's mosque, from the third Hijri century, is Cairo's oldest mosque surviving with its original layout; the Mosque of Amr was repeatedly rebuilt.
islamic-architecture-0049: Which Fatimid mosque in Cairo adjoins the city's northern wall near Bab al-Futuh?
The northern side of the Mosque of al-Hakim bi-Amr Allah was incorporated into the northern wall when Badr al-Jamali rebuilt it, adjoining the wall between Bab al-Futuh and Bab al-Nasr.
islamic-architecture-0050: What is the Fatimid al-Aqmar Mosque on al-Muizz Street in Cairo famous for?
Being Cairo's largest mosque by area
Its decorated stone facade facing the street
Being the first mosque built of mudbrick
Al-Aqmar Mosque (519 AH) was Cairo's first mosque with a decorated stone street facade; its facade is angled to follow the street line.
islamic-architecture-0051: What other name is the Mosque of Muhammad Ali in the Cairo Citadel known by, after the stone covering its walls?
It is called the Alabaster Mosque because its interior walls and lower exterior walls are covered with alabaster.
islamic-architecture-0052: In which architectural style was the Mosque of Muhammad Ali in the Cairo Citadel built?
The Mosque of Muhammad Ali was designed in the Ottoman style, with a central dome, semi-domes, and two slender minarets, influenced by Istanbul's mosques.
islamic-architecture-0053: How many stepped tiers make up the minaret of the Mosque of Uqba ibn Nafi in Kairouan?
The Kairouan mosque minaret is a square tower with three tiers decreasing in size upward and is among the oldest surviving minarets.
islamic-architecture-0054: The Great Mosque of Kairouan contains what is considered the oldest minbar (pulpit) surviving in its original location; what wood is it made of?
The Kairouan mosque's third-Hijri-century minbar (pulpit) is made of carved teak and is the oldest preserved in its original location.
islamic-architecture-0055: Which great mosque in the Tunis medina was associated with one of the Islamic world's oldest centers of learning?
Al-Zaytuna is the largest and oldest mosque in the Tunis medina and was a longstanding scholarly center that educated many scholars.
islamic-architecture-0056: Which small mosque in Kairouan is famous for its carved facade and named after the number of entrances in it?
The Mosque of the Three Doors, from the third Hijri century, has a facade with three arched entrances and Kufic inscriptions.
islamic-architecture-0057: What was the Kutubiyya Mosque in Marrakesh named after?
The military unit that guarded it
The sultan's library attached to the mosque
The many Quranic verses inscribed on its walls
The name Kutubiyya comes from the market of booksellers and manuscript sellers that surrounded the mosque.
islamic-architecture-0058: Approximately how tall is the minaret of the Kutubiyya Mosque in Marrakesh?
The Almohad Kutubiyya minaret rises about 77 meters, including its finial.
islamic-architecture-0059: The famous Giralda in Seville is now the cathedral's bell tower; what was it originally?
Minaret of the great Almohad mosque
A tower in the kasbah wall
The Giralda was originally the minaret of Seville's Almohad mosque; a bell tower was added on top after the mosque became a cathedral.
islamic-architecture-0060: The Hassan Tower in Rabat is the minaret of an unfinished mosque; which Almohad sultan ordered its construction?
The Almohad Yaqub al-Mansur began building the mosque and minaret in the late sixth Hijri century, and work stopped upon his death.
islamic-architecture-0061: The Great Mosque of Algiers has a minaret considered the world's tallest when completed; approximately how tall is it?
The Great Mosque of Algiers minaret rises about 265 meters, surpassing the Hassan II Mosque's 210-meter minaret.
islamic-architecture-0062: What is the striking structural feature of the prayer hall roof at the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca?
It is made entirely of glass
It is covered with gold sheets
It has no supporting columns at all
The Hassan II Mosque's prayer hall has a retractable roof that opens automatically to admit air and light.
islamic-architecture-0063: Which French architect designed the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca?
French architect Michel Pinseau designed the mosque, and thousands of Moroccan craftsmen built it.
islamic-architecture-0064: Architect Vedat Dalokay based the design of the King Faisal Mosque in Islamabad on the shape of what?
The Faisal Mosque has no traditional dome, and its eight sloping roof surfaces resemble a desert Bedouin tent.
islamic-architecture-0066: How many domes crown the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi?
The Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque has 82 domes of different sizes covered with white marble.
islamic-architecture-0067: In which country was the huge handmade carpet covering the main prayer hall of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque woven?
Craftsmen in Iran designed and handwove the carpet, which is among the world's largest hand-knotted carpets.
islamic-architecture-0068: In which city is the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque?
The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque is Oman's principal mosque and is located in the capital, Muscat.
islamic-architecture-0069: What is the name of the minaret at the southeastern corner of the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus?
The Umayyad Mosque has three minarets: al-Arus in the north, Isa in the southeast, and Qaytbay in the southwest.
islamic-architecture-0070: What is the small dome raised on columns in the Umayyad Mosque's courtyard in Damascus, where the mosque's funds were kept?
The Dome of the Treasury is an octagonal structure raised on columns in the western courtyard, formerly holding the mosque's funds and waqf (endowment) assets.
islamic-architecture-0071: What is the great dome above the transverse aisle in the Umayyad Mosque's prayer hall in Damascus called?
The central dome above the aisle crossing the prayer hall is called the Dome of the Eagle, likening the aisle to a bird's body and wings.
islamic-architecture-0072: Which Abbasid mosque did al-Mutawakkil build north of his capital, with a smaller spiral minaret modeled on the Malwiya?
Al-Mutawakkil built the Abu Dulaf Mosque north of Samarra, with a spiral minaret modeled on, but smaller than, the Malwiya.
islamic-architecture-0073: What nickname was given to the minaret of the Great Mosque of al-Nuri in Mosul because of its pronounced lean?
The al-Nuri Mosque's minaret was known as al-Hadba because of its lean, and the nickname came to refer to Mosul itself.
islamic-architecture-0074: In which Yemeni city is the towering earthen minaret of al-Mihdhar Mosque?
Al-Mihdhar Mosque is in Tarim in Wadi Hadramawt; its earthen minaret is among the tallest minarets built of earth.
islamic-architecture-0075: In which city is Qutb Minar, considered the world's tallest brick minaret?
Qutb Minar stands in Delhi's Qutb complex, rises about 73 meters, and is the tallest brick minaret.
islamic-architecture-0076: In which country is the Ghurid Minaret of Jam, a World Heritage site?
The Minaret of Jam is in Ghor Province in western Afghanistan; the Ghurids built it in the sixth Hijri century to a height of about 65 meters.
islamic-architecture-0077: Which famous Bukhara minaret is said to have been spared from destruction by Genghis Khan because he admired it?
The sixth-Hijri-century Kalyan Minaret is a symbol of Bukhara; a famous but undocumented account says Genghis Khan spared it while destroying its surroundings.
islamic-architecture-0078: Which Mughal emperor ordered the construction of the great congregational mosque in Old Delhi?
Shah Jahan built Delhi's Jama Masjid between 1644 and 1656 CE; it is among India's largest mosques.
islamic-architecture-0079: Which Mughal emperor built the great Badshahi Mosque in Lahore?
Aurangzeb ordered the construction of Lahore's Badshahi Mosque, completed in 1673 CE.
islamic-architecture-0080: On which historic square in Isfahan is the Shah Mosque (Imam Mosque) located?
The Shah Mosque stands on the southern side of Naqsh-e Jahan Square, created by Shah Abbas I.
islamic-architecture-0081: Why does the Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque in Isfahan have no minarets?
It was a private prayer hall for the Safavid court
An earthquake destroyed its old minaret
Its soft ground cannot support tall buildings
It was built before minarets appeared in Iran
The Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque was built as a private prayer hall for Shah Abbas's court rather than a public mosque, so it was small and had no minarets.
islamic-architecture-0082: Which Iranian mosque is among the earliest examples of the four-iwan layout and became a World Heritage site in 2012?
The Jameh Mosque of Isfahan was the first mosque to use a four-iwan layout around a courtyard and became a World Heritage site in 2012.
islamic-architecture-0083: Which mosque in Shiraz is nicknamed the Pink Mosque because of its many pink tiles and stained-glass windows?
The nineteenth-century Nasir al-Mulk Mosque in Shiraz is called the Pink Mosque; its windows cast colored light on its floor in the morning.
islamic-architecture-0084: Which of Mimar Sinan's mosques did he himself consider his masterwork and greatest achievement?
Sinan considered the Selimiye Mosque in Edirne his masterwork, completing it in 1575 CE with a dome about 31 meters in diameter.
islamic-architecture-0085: Which mosque did Sinan build in Istanbul to commemorate Prince Mehmed, the son of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent, after his death?
Suleiman ordered the Sehzade (Prince's) Mosque in memory of his son Mehmed; Sinan completed it in 1548 CE and considered it his apprenticeship work.
islamic-architecture-0086: Which small Istanbul mosque designed by Sinan is famous for its exceptionally extensive Iznik tile wall covering?
The Rustem Pasha Mosque near the Spice Bazaar is covered inside with an exceptional quantity of Iznik tiles in varied designs.
islamic-architecture-0087: Which architect designed the Sultan Ahmed Mosque in Istanbul?
Sedefkar Mehmed Agha, a pupil of Mimar Sinan, designed the mosque, which was built between 1609 and 1616 CE.
islamic-architecture-0088: How many domes crown the Great Mosque (Ulu Cami) in Bursa, Turkey?
Bursa's Ulu Cami is a multidomed mosque with twenty domes in four rows of five.
islamic-architecture-0089: Which Anatolian complex has an adjoining mosque and hospital, is famous for its carved stone portals, and became a World Heritage site in 1985?
Great Mosque and Hospital of Divrigi
The mosque and hospital in Divrigi were built in 1228 CE, became famous for their carved stone portals, and were listed as World Heritage in 1985.
islamic-architecture-0092: Which architectural character predominates in the Great Mosque of Xi'an, China?
Traditional Chinese temple and palace style
Indian Mughal style with onion domes and gardens
Ottoman style with domes and minarets
The Great Mosque of Xi'an follows traditional Chinese architecture, with courtyards, pavilions, and tiled roofs without domes.
islamic-architecture-0093: Huaisheng Mosque in Guangzhou is among China's oldest mosques; what else was its minaret used for?
A tower for observing stars and crescent moons
A tower guarding the city wall
The Huaisheng Mosque's minaret served as a lighthouse guiding ships in Guangzhou's port, hence its name, the Lighthouse Mosque.
islamic-architecture-0094: What is Indonesia's national mosque in the capital, Jakarta, called?
Istiqlal Mosque in Jakarta is Indonesia's national mosque and opened in 1978 CE.
islamic-architecture-0095: What is the likely origin of the name Alhambra in Granada?
The name of the princess it was built for
The reddish color of its walls
The red roses in its gardens
The gemstone inlaid in its domes
The name Alhambra derives from the reddish color of the fortress walls, built of rammed earth.
islamic-architecture-0096: Which Andalusian dynasty built most of the Alhambra palaces surviving in Granada today?
The Nasrid sultans built most of the Alhambra palaces in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries CE.
islamic-architecture-0097: Which phrase appears repeatedly in the Alhambra palace inscriptions and served as the Nasrid motto?
Sovereignty belongs to Allah, the One, al-Qahhar (the All-Subduer)
There is no deity but Allah
There is no victor but Allah
The Nasrid motto, There is no victor but Allah, is inscribed in countless places on the Alhambra's walls.
islamic-architecture-0098: What is the summer palace with gardens and water channels beside the Alhambra on a neighboring hill called?
The Generalife is a Nasrid summer palace famous for its gardens and pools, on the Hill of the Sun near the Alhambra.
islamic-architecture-0099: What is the courtyard of the Alhambra's Comares Palace with a long rectangular pool bordered by green shrubs called?
The Court of the Myrtles is the courtyard of Comares Palace, with a central rectangular pool bordered by myrtle shrubs.
islamic-architecture-0100: Near which Andalusian city are the ruins of Madinat al-Zahra, built by Abd al-Rahman al-Nasir as a caliphal palace city?
The ruins of Madinat al-Zahra lie on a mountainside west of Cordoba and became a World Heritage site in 2018.
islamic-architecture-0101: In which Spanish city is the fortified Islamic Aljaferia Palace, built during the Taifa period?
The Aljaferia Palace was built in Zaragoza in the eleventh century CE and is among the most prominent monuments of the Taifa period.
islamic-architecture-0102: Why did the Almohads build the Torre del Oro on the Guadalquivir riverbank in Seville?
To monitor the river and control its entrance
To store treasury gold and the caliphs' jewels
To house the city's governor and his entourage
To issue the call to prayer for the city's mosque
The Torre del Oro is an Almohad military tower built to monitor the river; a chain stretched from it to prevent ships entering.
islamic-architecture-0103: Which Ottoman sultan ordered the construction of Topkapi Palace in Istanbul?
Mehmed the Conqueror ordered Topkapi Palace built after the conquest of Constantinople, and it remained the sultans' residence for about four centuries.
islamic-architecture-0104: What does the name Topkapi Palace in Istanbul mean?
Topkapi means Cannon Gate in Turkish, after a gate near the palace.
islamic-architecture-0105: Which fortress did Mehmed the Conqueror build on the European shore of the Bosporus in 1452 CE in preparation for conquering Constantinople?
Mehmed the Conqueror built Rumeli Hisari in a few months in 1452 CE to control the Bosporus Strait.
islamic-architecture-0106: Which Ottoman sultan built Anadolu Hisari on the Asian shore of the Bosporus?
Bayezid I built Anadolu Hisari in the late fourteenth century; Mehmed the Conqueror later built Rumeli Hisari opposite it.
islamic-architecture-0107: In which eastern Turkish province is the Ottoman Ishak Pasha Palace?
Ishak Pasha Palace is in Dogubayazit district in Agri Province in eastern Turkey.
islamic-architecture-0108: Which Ottoman governor built al-Azm Palace in old Damascus as his residence?
Damascus governor Asad Pasha al-Azm built the palace in 1749 CE; it is now a museum of popular traditions.
islamic-architecture-0109: The Saadian sultan Ahmad al-Mansur built El Badi Palace in Marrakesh to celebrate victory in which battle?
Ahmad al-Mansur began building El Badi Palace in 1578 CE after the Moroccan victory over the Portuguese at Wadi al-Makhazin (the Battle of the Three Kings).
islamic-architecture-0110: Which museum holds the carved stone facade of the Umayyad Mshatta Palace from the Jordanian desert?
The Mshatta facade was given to Germany in 1903 CE and belongs to the Museum of Islamic Art in Berlin's Pergamon building.
islamic-architecture-0111: The facade of the Umayyad Qasr al-Hayr al-Gharbi was reassembled as the entrance to which museum?
The gateway of Qasr al-Hayr al-Gharbi was moved and reassembled as the entrance to the National Museum of Damascus.
islamic-architecture-0112: In which country's desert is the fortified Abbasid al-Ukhaidir Palace?
Al-Ukhaidir Palace is a huge Abbasid fortress in the Iraqi desert about 50 kilometers south of Karbala.
islamic-architecture-0113: Chehel Sotoun Palace in Isfahan is called the Palace of Forty Columns although it has twenty; what is the best-known explanation?
It was built in forty days
Half its original columns were destroyed by an ancient earthquake
The columns' reflections in the pool in front of it
The palace portico rests on twenty wooden columns reflected in the long pool in front, making them appear to be forty.
islamic-architecture-0115: What stone gives Delhi's Red Fort walls their name?
The Red Fort is named for its massive red sandstone walls and was built by Shah Jahan.
islamic-architecture-0116: Emperor Akbar built the monumental Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri to celebrate the conquest of which region?
Buland Darwaza (the High Gate) was built to commemorate Akbar's victory in Gujarat.
islamic-architecture-0117: What is the hall covered with thousands of small mirror pieces in Lahore Fort called?
Shah Jahan built the Sheesh Mahal (Palace of Mirrors) in Lahore Fort; its walls and ceilings are covered with mirror pieces.
islamic-architecture-0118: Which Fatimid gate of Cairo is topped by the two minarets of the Mamluk Mosque of al-Muayyad Shaykh?
Sultan al-Muayyad Shaykh built his mosque beside Bab Zuwayla and placed its minarets on the gate's two towers.
islamic-architecture-0119: Which Fatimid vizier rebuilt Cairo's gates and walls in stone in the late eleventh century CE?
Vizier Badr al-Jamali renewed Cairo's walls and built its stone gates, including Bab al-Futuh and Bab al-Nasr, in 1087 CE.
islamic-architecture-0120: The monumental Bab Mansur al-Alj is one of the best-known landmarks of which Moroccan city?
Bab Mansur is a gate of Ismaili Meknes, completed during the reign of Sultan Moulay Abd Allah ibn Ismail.
islamic-architecture-0121: What color predominates in the zellij on the outer facade of Bab Bou Jeloud in Fez?
Blue zellij covers Bab Bou Jeloud's outer facade, while green predominates on its inner facade.
islamic-architecture-0122: The carved stone Bab Agnaou is the main entrance to which part of Marrakesh?
Bab Agnaou is a twelfth-century Almohad gate that served as the main entrance to Marrakesh's royal kasbah.
islamic-architecture-0123: In which corner of old Damascus is its historic citadel?
The Citadel of Damascus is at the northwestern edge of the old city and was rebuilt by the Ayyubid al-Malik al-Adil.
islamic-architecture-0124: Which Roman monument was enclosed by the Islamic Citadel of Bosra, preserving it from destruction?
The Ayyubids and earlier Muslims surrounded Bosra's Roman theater with fortifications, turning it into a citadel and preserving it.
islamic-architecture-0125: What distinguishes Oman's Nizwa Fort from most Omani fortresses?
Nizwa Fort is famous for its enormous cylindrical tower, built in the seventeenth century CE during the Yaruba dynasty.
islamic-architecture-0126: Oman's historic Jabrin Castle was built by an imam of which dynasty?
Imam Bilarab ibn Sultan al-Yarubi built Jabrin Castle in the late seventeenth century CE.
islamic-architecture-0127: The historic al-Jalali and al-Mirani forts guard which city's harbor?
Al-Jalali and al-Mirani stand on two rocky outcrops at the entrance to old Muscat's harbor.
islamic-architecture-0128: The earthen al-Masmak Fort is among the most famous historic landmarks of which city?
Al-Masmak is an earthen and mudbrick fortress in central old Riyadh, built in the nineteenth century CE.
islamic-architecture-0129: What is the old fortified city overlooking the sea in Algiers, listed as a World Heritage site, called?
The Kasbah of Algiers is an old city terraced on a hill overlooking the sea and became a World Heritage site in 1992.
islamic-architecture-0130: In which country is the archaeological World Heritage site Qala of Beni Hammad?
Qala of Beni Hammad was the first Hammadid capital; its ruins are in Algeria's Msila Province.
islamic-architecture-0131: What is the massive earthen fortress that served as the rulers of Bukhara's seat for centuries called?
The Ark of Bukhara is a massive earthen fortress on an artificial hill, serving as the rulers' seat until the early twentieth century.
islamic-architecture-0132: What is the walled inner city of Khiva, Uzbekistan, the country's first World Heritage site, called?
Itchan Kala is Khiva's walled inner city and was listed in 1990 as Uzbekistan's first World Heritage site.
islamic-architecture-0133: What is the short Kalta Minor minaret, covered in colored ceramics in Khiva, famous for?
Leaning like the Tower of Pisa
Construction of Kalta Minor began in 1851 CE to make it Central Asia's tallest minaret, but work stopped and it remained short.
islamic-architecture-0134: The ancient Bam Citadel in southeastern Iran was famous as one of the world's largest structures built of what?
Arg-e Bam is the world's largest mudbrick structure and was severely damaged in the 2003 earthquake.
islamic-architecture-0135: On which elevated landform does the Citadel of Salah al-Din in Cairo stand?
The Citadel of the Mountain was built on a spur of the Muqattam Plateau overlooking Cairo.
islamic-architecture-0136: What geometric shape was used in Baghdad's plan when Abu Jafar al-Mansur built it?
Al-Mansur built Madinat al-Salam (Baghdad) as a round city with circular walls, his palace and the congregational mosque at its center.
islamic-architecture-0137: How many gates were in the outer wall of al-Mansur's Round City of Baghdad?
The Round City had four opposing gates: Kufa Gate, Basra Gate, Khurasan Gate, and Syria Gate.
islamic-architecture-0138: What shape was used in the plan of the Abbasid city of al-Rafiqa beside Raqqa?
Al-Mansur built al-Rafiqa in 772 CE with a horseshoe-shaped wall, modeled on his city of Baghdad.
islamic-architecture-0139: Which Umayyad city in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley was planned with two main streets crossing at right angles in the Roman manner?
Anjar is an early-eighth-century Umayyad city divided into four quarters by two perpendicular streets and listed as World Heritage.
islamic-architecture-0140: Which Palestinian city did Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik found as the administrative seat of Jund Filastin?
Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik founded Ramla in the early eighth century CE and made it the capital of Jund Filastin.
islamic-architecture-0141: Old Fez el-Bali is among the world's largest urban areas free of what?
Fez el-Bali's narrow winding alleys cannot admit cars, making it one of the world's largest car-free urban areas.
islamic-architecture-0142: Which Moroccan dynasty founded Marrakesh in the eleventh century CE?
The Almoravids founded Marrakesh around 1070 CE and made it their capital.
islamic-architecture-0143: What is Marrakesh nicknamed after the color of its walls and buildings?
Marrakesh is nicknamed the Red City because its walls and buildings are painted the color of red earth.
islamic-architecture-0144: Which Moroccan mountain city is famous for painting the houses of its old town blue?
Chefchaouen in the Rif Mountains is famous for alleys and houses painted in shades of blue.
islamic-architecture-0145: Which Moroccan city is nicknamed Daughter of Granada because Andalusian migrants rebuilt it and gave its architecture an Andalusian character?
Ali al-Mandari and fellow Granadans rebuilt Tetouan in the late fifteenth century, giving it the nickname Daughter of Granada.
islamic-architecture-0146: Which Alaouite sultan ordered the planning of Essaouira in Morocco in the eighteenth century?
Sultan Muhammad ibn Abd Allah (Muhammad III) founded Essaouira around 1760 CE and commissioned a French engineer to plan its fortifications.
islamic-architecture-0147: Which ancient Libyan desert city is nicknamed the Pearl of the Desert and has covered passages between its houses?
Ghadames is an ancient oasis city in western Libya nicknamed the Pearl of the Desert; its covered alleys provide protection from the heat.
islamic-architecture-0148: In which country is the Mzab Valley, with fortified towns centered on mosques atop hills?
The Mzab Valley in Algeria's Ghardaia Province contains fortified ksour (towns) from the eleventh century and is listed as World Heritage.
islamic-architecture-0149: Which Yemeni city is nicknamed the Manhattan of the Desert for its closely packed earthen towers?
Shibam in Hadramawt is a walled city of tall earthen buildings, earning it the nickname Manhattan of the Desert.
islamic-architecture-0150: In which country is the historic walled city of Harar, known for its many mosques?
Harar Jugol is a historic walled Islamic city in eastern Ethiopia, listed as a World Heritage site in 2006.
islamic-architecture-0151: Which city on Kenya's coast is the oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement?
Lamu Old Town is the oldest continuously inhabited Swahili settlement and is listed as World Heritage.
islamic-architecture-0152: Which architectural feature is Zanzibar's Stone Town famous for?
Zanzibar's Stone Town is famous for its massive wooden doors carved with decoration and fitted with brass studs.
islamic-architecture-0153: What material was used to build the Great Mosque of Kilwa on Tanzania's coast?
The Great Mosque of Kilwa was built of coral stone blocks and is among the oldest surviving mosques on the East African coast.
islamic-architecture-0154: In which country is Agadez, with its mosque's towering earthen minaret?
Agadez is in northern Niger, and its mosque's minaret is among the world's tallest earthen buildings.
islamic-architecture-0156: What material was used for most old houses in historic Jeddah?
Jeddah's residents built their houses from manqabi stone extracted from al-Arbain Lagoon, together with imported timber.
islamic-architecture-0157: In which Saudi region is the heritage village of Rijal Alma, with its multistory stone houses?
Rijal Alma is in Asir in southwestern Saudi Arabia and is famous for its decorated stone houses.
islamic-architecture-0159: Which Iranian city was historically called Nesf-e Jahan, meaning Half the World, for its many monuments?
Isfahan was nicknamed Half the World in the Safavid period because of its mosques, palaces, and bridges.
islamic-architecture-0160: Which Iranian desert city is famous for its many windcatchers and had its historic city listed as World Heritage in 2017?
Historic Yazd became a World Heritage site in 2017 and is famous for its earthen architecture and many windcatchers.
islamic-architecture-0161: How many madrasas (schools) surround Samarkand's famous Registan Square?
Three madrasas (schools) surround Registan Square: Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor, and Tilya-Kori.
islamic-architecture-0162: The oldest madrasa (school) on Registan Square in Samarkand bears whose name?
The Ulugh Beg Madrasa (school) in Registan was built around 1417-1420 CE and is the oldest of the square's three schools.
islamic-architecture-0163: Which ruler ordered the construction of the huge Bibi-Khanym Mosque in Samarkand?
Timur ordered the Bibi-Khanym Mosque built after his Indian campaign in 1399 CE; it was one of the largest mosques of its time.
islamic-architecture-0165: What is the famous square in Bukhara centered on an old pool and surrounded by a madrasa (school) and khanqah (Sufi lodge) called?
Lyabi-Hauz (by the pool) is a square in Bukhara around a seventeenth-century pool, surrounded by the Kukeldash Madrasa (school) and a khanqah (Sufi lodge).
islamic-architecture-0166: Which Turkish town became a World Heritage site for preserving traditional Ottoman houses?
Safranbolu was listed as World Heritage in 1994 for its preserved Ottoman houses and markets.
islamic-architecture-0167: Which river does the Ottoman-built Old Bridge of Mostar cross in Bosnia and Herzegovina?
Mostar's Old Bridge (Stari Most) crosses the Neretva River and was completed in 1566 CE.
islamic-architecture-0168: Which Ottoman architect built Mostar's Old Bridge in the sixteenth century?
Ottoman architect Hayreddin, a pupil of Mimar Sinan, designed the bridge, completed in 1566 CE.
