islamic-architecture-0169: Which architect designed the Mehmed Pasha Sokolovic Bridge over the Drina in Visegrad?
Mimar Sinan designed the Visegrad bridge at the request of Grand Vizier Mehmed Pasha Sokolovic; it was completed in 1577 CE.
islamic-architecture-0170: How many arches does Isfahan's Si-o-se-pol have, as indicated by its name?
The bridge's Persian name means the Bridge of Thirty-Three Arches; it was built during Shah Abbas I's reign.
islamic-architecture-0171: Isfahan's Khaju Bridge combines crossing the river with which other function?
A small mosque for travelers and merchants
Khaju Bridge has gates beneath its arches that allow it to act as a dam, retaining and regulating water in the Zayandeh Rud.
islamic-architecture-0172: What is the purpose of the Abbasid Nilometer on Rawda Island in Cairo?
Observing crescents to determine the start of months
Measuring the Nile's water level during floods
The Nilometer is a graduated column in a well connected to the Nile, used to measure water height to assess flooding and kharaj (land tax).
islamic-architecture-0173: What is the purpose of the huge circular Aghlabid Basins in Kairouan?
The Aghlabid Basins are circular reservoirs built in the ninth century CE to collect and store water for Kairouan's residents.
islamic-architecture-0174: What is the Syrian city of Hama on the Orontes River famous for?
Hama's norias are huge wooden wheels lifting water from the Orontes; some date to the Ayyubid period.
islamic-architecture-0175: Which Marinid madrasa (school) in Fez also served as a congregational mosque, holding Friday prayers and having a prominent minaret?
Marinid Sultan Abu Inan built the Bou Inania Madrasa (school), combining a school and congregational mosque; it is among the few Moroccan madrasas with a prominent minaret.
islamic-architecture-0176: What was the Marinid al-Attarin Madrasa (school) in Fez named after?
The scent of cedarwood in its ceiling
A family of prominent perfumers who endowed it
The medical students who studied there
The spice and perfume market beside it
The al-Attarin Madrasa (school) is near al-Qarawiyyin Mosque by the market of spice and perfume sellers, from which it takes its name.
islamic-architecture-0177: What is Morocco's largest historic madrasa (school), located in Marrakesh?
The Ibn Yusuf Madrasa (school) in Marrakesh, renovated by the Saadians in the sixteenth century, is Morocco's largest.
islamic-architecture-0178: Which woman founded the Ayyubid al-Firdaws Madrasa (school) in Aleppo?
Dayfa Khatun, Aleppo's regent, founded the al-Firdaws Madrasa (school) in 1235 CE; it is among the finest Ayyubid buildings.
islamic-architecture-0179: What does the Seljuk Karatay Madrasa (school) in Konya house today?
A home for orphans and widows
The Karatay Madrasa (school), built in 1251 CE and famous for its tiled dome, became a ceramics and tile museum.
islamic-architecture-0180: What is the Seljuk Ince Minareli Madrasa (school) in Konya famous for?
The Ince Minareli Madrasa (school) is famous for its stone portal carved with interlaced decoration and inscriptions; it is now a museum of stone and wood carving.
islamic-architecture-0181: Why was the Seljuk Cifte Minareli Madrasa (school) in Erzurum given this name?
It was commissioned by two sisters
It lies in a valley between two facing mountains
It has twin minarets above its entrance
Cifte Minareli means having two minarets, as two matching minarets rise above its entrance.
islamic-architecture-0182: What is the largest Seljuk roadside caravanserai in Anatolia, located near Aksaray?
Sultan Ala al-Din Kayqubad I built Sultan Han near Aksaray in 1229 CE; it is the largest Seljuk caravanserai.
islamic-architecture-0183: What is the largest caravanserai in old Damascus, with multiple domes above its courtyard?
Khan Asad Pasha, built in 1752 CE, is old Damascus's largest caravanserai and has several domes over its courtyard.
islamic-architecture-0184: Cairo's Khan al-Khalili market is named after which Mamluk emir?
Emir Jaharkas al-Khalili, master of the stables under Sultan Barquq, established a caravanserai on the site, giving the market his name.
islamic-architecture-0185: Which Ottoman sultan began building the core of Istanbul's covered Grand Bazaar?
Construction of the Grand Bazaar began under Mehmed the Conqueror a few years after the conquest; it expanded into one of the world's largest covered markets.
islamic-architecture-0186: What is the best-known explanation for Istanbul's historic Spice Bazaar being called the Egyptian Bazaar?
Its first merchants came from Alexandria and Damietta
It was built in the style of Cairo's markets
It was built using tax revenues from Ottoman Egypt
It is said to have been built with tax revenues from Ottoman Egypt; another explanation is that most of its goods came from Egypt.
islamic-architecture-0187: At which landmark does the covered al-Hamidiyya Souq in old Damascus end?
Al-Hamidiyya Souq extends from near the citadel to the old gate of the Temple of Jupiter in front of the Umayyad Mosque.
islamic-architecture-0188: Which Iranian covered bazaar became a World Heritage site in 2010 as one of the world's largest covered markets?
The historic Tabriz Bazaar was listed as World Heritage in 2010 and is among the oldest and largest covered markets.
islamic-architecture-0189: At whose request did Mimar Sinan design Istanbul's Cemberlitas Bath?
The Cemberlitas Bath was established in 1584 CE on the commission of Nurbanu Sultan, wife of Sultan Selim II.
islamic-architecture-0190: In a Turkish bath, what is the heated marble platform in the center of the hot room on which bathers lie called?
A heated marble platform called gobek tasi, meaning navel stone, occupies the center of a Turkish bath's hot room.
islamic-architecture-0191: Which Mamluk hospital in Aleppo was famous for treating psychiatric patients?
The Arghun Hospital in Mamluk Aleppo was famous for caring for psychiatric patients with abundant light, fresh air, and running water.
islamic-architecture-0192: Which Damascus hospital dates to the twelfth century CE and now houses the Museum of Arab Medicine and Science?
Nur al-Din Zangi founded al-Nuri Hospital in Damascus in 1154 CE; it is now a museum of medicine and science.
islamic-architecture-0193: How many minarets does the Suleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul have?
The Suleymaniye Mosque has four minarets and is one of Mimar Sinan's works for Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.
islamic-architecture-0194: Approximately what is the diameter of the Selimiye Mosque's dome in Edirne?
The Selimiye Mosque's dome is about 31.28 meters in diameter and was among the largest domes of its time.
islamic-architecture-0195: Which Ottoman mosque overlooking Istanbul's Eminonu harbor was completed by Turhan Hatice Sultan in 1665 CE?
The New Mosque (Yeni Cami) was begun by Safiye Sultan, work stopped, and Turhan Hatice Sultan completed it in 1665 CE.
islamic-architecture-0196: What happened to Istanbul's original Fatih Mosque in 1766 CE, leading to its reconstruction with a different design?
The 1766 earthquake destroyed the original Fatih Mosque, which was rebuilt with a new plan under Sultan Mustafa III.
islamic-architecture-0197: Mimar Sinan built two Istanbul mosques bearing the name of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's daughter; what was her name?
Sinan built the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque in Uskudar and another at Edirnekapi, named after Suleiman's daughter Mihrimah.
islamic-architecture-0198: Which Ottoman sultan built the Green Mosque in Bursa?
Sultan Mehmed I (Celebi) built Bursa's Green Mosque, named for its bluish-green tiles.
islamic-architecture-0199: The Uc Serefeli Mosque in Edirne is named after one of its minarets having what?
Uc Serefeli means having three balconies, as the mosque's tallest minaret has three balconies for muezzins (callers to prayer).
islamic-architecture-0200: What is the main historic street of Fatimid Cairo, extending from Bab al-Futuh in the north to Bab Zuwayla in the south?
Al-Muizz Street is Fatimid Cairo's main thoroughfare, extending between Bab al-Futuh and Bab Zuwayla and lined with many Mamluk and Fatimid monuments.
islamic-architecture-0201: Bayt al-Suhaymi is among the most famous historic houses with mashrabiyyas (wooden window screens) in which city?
Bayt al-Suhaymi is an Ottoman-style house in al-Darb al-Asfar alley in Fatimid Cairo, with mashrabiyyas (wooden window screens) and decorated halls.
islamic-architecture-0202: The Gayer-Anderson Museum in Cairo occupies two historic houses adjoining which mosque?
The Gayer-Anderson Museum occupies Bayt al-Kritliyya and the house of Amna bint Salim beside Ibn Tulun's mosque.
islamic-architecture-0204: Which dynasty built the Great Mosque of Algiers in the late eleventh century CE?
The Almoravids built the Great Mosque of Algiers around 1097 CE; it is among the city's oldest mosques.
islamic-architecture-0205: In which Moroccan mountain range is the historic Almohad Tinmel Mosque?
Tinmel Mosque is in Tinmel village in the High Atlas, built during the Almohad period at the birthplace of their movement.
islamic-architecture-0206: What does the name Tilya-Kori Madrasa (school) in Samarkand's Registan Square mean?
Tilya-Kori means gilded, referring to the abundant gilding in the decoration of its interior mosque.
islamic-architecture-0207: What is the Wazir Khan Mosque in Lahore famous for?
The Wazir Khan Mosque, dating to around 1641 CE, is famous for the colored ceramic tile decoration (kashi kari) covering its walls.
islamic-architecture-0208: What is the famous monument with four minarets in central Hyderabad, India?
Charminar (four minarets) was built in 1591 CE in the heart of Hyderabad and became the city's symbol.
islamic-architecture-0209: What distinguishes the double arches supporting the prayer hall roof in the Great Mosque of Cordoba?
They are entirely made of black marble
They are pierced with stained-glass windows
Alternating red brick and white stone voussoirs
They are clad in gleaming gilded copper sheets
The arches of the Great Mosque of Cordoba have two tiers, with alternating red brick and white stone voussoirs.
islamic-architecture-0210: Under which Andalusian Umayyad caliph was the mosaic-decorated mihrab (prayer niche) added to the Great Mosque of Cordoba?
Al-Hakam II al-Mustansir expanded the Great Mosque of Cordoba in the tenth century CE and built its new mosaic-decorated mihrab (prayer niche).
islamic-architecture-0211: Where were the skilled artisan and mosaic tesserae brought from to decorate the mihrab (prayer niche) of the Great Mosque of Cordoba in the tenth century CE?
Al-Hakam II requested a skilled mosaic artisan from the Byzantine emperor, who sent one along with mosaic tesserae.
islamic-architecture-0212: What was built in the middle of the Great Mosque of Cordoba in the sixteenth century CE?
A bell tower over the prayer niche
A Renaissance-style cathedral nave was built in the heart of the Great Mosque of Cordoba's prayer hall in the sixteenth century.
islamic-architecture-0213: In which Spanish city is the small Bab al-Mardum Mosque, preserved since 999 CE?
Bab al-Mardum Mosque in Toledo was built in 999 CE and later became a church known as Cristo de la Luz.
islamic-architecture-0214: Malaga's Andalusian Alcazaba is linked by a walled passage to a higher castle on a hill called:
Malaga's Alcazaba is connected to the Gibralfaro Castle above it by a fortified passage between two walls.
islamic-architecture-0215: Which Castilian king built the famous Mudejar wing in Seville's Alcazar?
King Pedro I had Muslim artisans build a Mudejar palace inside the Alcazar in the fourteenth century.
islamic-architecture-0216: Which old Andalusian quarter faces the Alhambra in Granada and is listed with it as a World Heritage Site?
The Albaicin quarter, on the hill facing the Alhambra, preserves Andalusian Granada's lanes and houses and is listed with the Alhambra as World Heritage.
islamic-architecture-0217: What is the largest hall in the Alhambra palaces, which served as the throne room in the Comares Tower?
The Hall of Ambassadors in the Comares Tower is the Alhambra's largest hall and housed the throne of Granada's sultan.
islamic-architecture-0218: For what purpose was the huge Heri es-Souani complex in Meknes built under Moulay Ismail?
Stables for the sultan's horses and mules
Heri es-Souani is a vast thick-walled complex built by Moulay Ismail to store grain and provisions, beside a large water basin.
islamic-architecture-0219: Beside which river valley in southern Morocco does the fortified earthen ksar of Ait Ben Haddou stand on a hillside?
Ait Ben Haddou stands on a hillside beside the Ounila Valley, on the old caravan route between the Sahara and Marrakesh.
islamic-architecture-0220: What is the purpose of the slight slope in the courtyard floor of the Great Mosque of Kairouan?
Collecting rainwater and draining it into a cistern
Keeping windblown sand out of the prayer hall
The Great Mosque of Kairouan's courtyard slopes toward its center to collect rainwater and channel it into an underground cistern.
islamic-architecture-0221: Near which Algerian city is the tall surviving minaret of Mansoura, a Marinid siege town?
The Marinid Mansoura Mosque was completed in 701 AH near Tlemcen. Only three sides remain of its square minaret, about 38 meters high.
islamic-architecture-0222: What is the geometric plan of the Dome of the Rock in Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, Palestine?
The Dome of the Rock is an octagonal building topped by a dome on a cylindrical drum, with octagonal arcades surrounding the rock.
islamic-architecture-0223: Which small open-sided dome supported by columns stands directly east of the Dome of the Rock in Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem?
Qubbat al-Silsila is a small open-sided Umayyad structure supported by columns, east of the Dome of the Rock.
islamic-architecture-0224: Which Ottoman sultan built the walls of Jerusalem's Old City in Palestine that stand today?
Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent ordered Jerusalem's walls rebuilt between approximately 1537 and 1541 CE.
islamic-architecture-0225: What is the Arabic name of Damascus Gate, the largest and best-known gate in the Old City walls of Jerusalem, Palestine?
Jerusalem's residents call Damascus Gate Bab al-Amud, after an ancient Roman column that once stood in its square.
islamic-architecture-0226: How many movable domes slide across the roof of the King Fahd expansion of the Prophet's Mosque in Medina?
The roof of the King Fahd expansion of the Prophet's Mosque has 27 sliding domes that open and close above square bases.
islamic-architecture-0227: Which Egyptian architect designed the current Quba Mosque when it was rebuilt in the 1980s?
Abdel-Wahed El-Wakil, a student of Hassan Fathy, designed the current Quba Mosque, rebuilt in 1986 CE.
islamic-architecture-0228: Which building material did Egyptian architect Hassan Fathy famously revive in New Gourna village?
Hassan Fathy revived mud-brick architecture with traditional domes and vaults in New Gourna, Luxor.
islamic-architecture-0229: What is the title of Hassan Fathy's famous book recounting the building of New Gourna?
Hassan Fathy's Imarat al-Fuqara recounts the New Gourna project and has been translated into many languages.
islamic-architecture-0230: Which Iraqi architect designed the Grand Mosque in Kuwait City?
Iraqi architect Mohamed Makiya, a pioneer of modern Arab architecture, designed Kuwait's Grand Mosque.
islamic-architecture-0231: What made the dome of Ahmed Al-Fateh Grand Mosque in Manama, Bahrain, famous?
It is covered in gold sheets
It is the world's largest fiberglass dome
It opens and closes automatically with the sun's movement
It is built from clay and coral stone taken from the sea
The Al-Fateh Mosque dome weighs about 54 tons and is made entirely of fiberglass. It was considered the largest dome of its kind in the world.
islamic-architecture-0232: In which Emirati city is the historic Al Jahili Fort?
Al Jahili Fort, one of the largest forts in the UAE, is in Al Ain and was built in the late nineteenth century.
islamic-architecture-0233: Under which ruler was the historic Murabba Palace in Riyadh built?
King Abdulaziz built Murabba Palace outside Riyadh's old walls in the 1930s as his seat of government.
islamic-architecture-0234: Near which Yemeni city is Dar al-Hajar Palace, built on a high rock in Wadi Dhahr?
Dar al-Hajar is a multistory palace atop a rock in Wadi Dhahr, northwest of Sanaa.
islamic-architecture-0235: What is the name of the famous main gateway in the walls of Old Sanaa?
Bab al-Yemen is the best-known surviving gate in Old Sanaa's walls and stands in the south of the city.
islamic-architecture-0236: In which Iraqi city is the historic Khan Marjan with its high vaulted roof?
Amin al-Din Marjan built Khan Marjan in Baghdad in the fourteenth century CE. Its roof is vaulted with high brick arches.
islamic-architecture-0237: Under which dynasty was the minaret of Aleppo's Great Umayyad Mosque built in the late eleventh century CE?
The minaret of Aleppo's Great Mosque was built around 1090 CE during Seljuk rule.
islamic-architecture-0238: Which Ottoman architect designed the Sulaymaniyya Takiyya in Damascus?
Mimar Sinan designed the Sulaymaniyya Takiyya in Damascus on Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent's orders. It includes a mosque and a school.
islamic-architecture-0239: On which site in Amman is the historic Umayyad Palace?
The Umayyad Palace is at the Amman Citadel site on Jabal al-Qala, overlooking the city center.
islamic-architecture-0240: Under which dynasty was the Great Mansuri Mosque in Tripoli, in the Levant, built?
The Great Mansuri Mosque in Tripoli was built in the late thirteenth century CE under Mamluk rule.
islamic-architecture-0241: What distinguishes Sultan al-Ghuri's minaret at Al-Azhar Mosque?
It is spiral with an external staircase
It is covered in blue tiles
In 1509 CE Sultan Qansuh al-Ghuri built a minaret at Al-Azhar whose summit ends in twin finials.
islamic-architecture-0242: What hangs from the center of the main prayer hall dome in Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque?
A huge crystal chandelier hangs in the prayer hall. When the mosque opened, it was among the largest chandeliers in the world.
islamic-architecture-0244: What does the main roof of Malaysia's National Mosque in Kuala Lumpur resemble?
The roof of Malaysia's National Mosque resembles an open umbrella, and the top of its minaret resembles a folded umbrella, symbolizing the tropical climate.
islamic-architecture-0245: What color of granite predominates on the dome of Putra Mosque in Putrajaya, Malaysia?
Putra Mosque's dome is clad in pink granite, earning it the name Pink Mosque.
islamic-architecture-0246: What distinguishes the roof of the Great Mosque of Demak on Indonesia's Java island?
A tiered pyramidal roof without a dome
Many small domes covered in green ceramics
Demak Mosque has a three-tiered pyramidal roof in traditional Javanese style instead of a dome.
islamic-architecture-0247: In what style was the minaret of Menara Kudus Mosque on Indonesia's Java island built?
Javanese Majapahit style in red brick
Moroccan square minaret style with an upper pavilion
The Kudus minaret preserves pre-Islamic architectural elements, including red-brick construction in the style of the Majapahit kingdom.
islamic-architecture-0248: What is the oldest and largest mosque in China's capital, Beijing?
Niujie Mosque is Beijing's oldest and largest mosque. Its origins date to the tenth century CE, and it was built in Chinese style.
islamic-architecture-0249: What is the largest historic Ottoman mosque in Sarajevo?
The sixteenth-century Gazi Husrev-beg Mosque is the largest historic mosque in Bosnia and Herzegovina, built by the Ottoman governor Husrev-beg.
islamic-architecture-0250: The Alai Darwaza gateway in Delhi's Qutb complex is India's oldest surviving building with:
Alai Darwaza, built by Alauddin Khalji in 1311 CE, contains India's oldest complete surviving true dome.
islamic-architecture-0251: What is Shah Jahan Mosque in Thatta, Pakistan, known for?
Being built entirely of white marble
Its location on a river island
Shah Jahan Mosque in Thatta has 93 domes, more than any other building in Pakistan.
islamic-architecture-0252: The Shat Gombuj Mosque in Bagerhat, Bangladesh, is called the Sixty Dome Mosque. How many domes actually cover its main hall?
The main hall has 77 domes. Including the four tower domes brings the total to 81, while there are sixty pillars.
islamic-architecture-0253: In which capital's old city is the historic Palace of the Shirvanshahs?
The fifteenth-century Palace of the Shirvanshahs is in the old city of Baku, Azerbaijan, and is listed as World Heritage.
islamic-architecture-0254: In which Iranian city is the World Heritage-listed Golestan Palace?
Golestan Palace in Tehran is one of its oldest landmarks and was the Qajar seat of government. It was listed as World Heritage in 2013.
islamic-architecture-0255: The historic Fin Garden is one of the oldest surviving Persian gardens. In which city is it?
Fin Garden in Kashan is one of the oldest surviving Persian gardens and is part of the Persian Garden World Heritage property.
islamic-architecture-0256: What distinguishes the two minarets above the entrance to the Jameh Mosque of Yazd?
They are among Iran's tallest minarets
They are made of unfired clay
Two Safavid minarets, about 52 meters high, rise above the entrance to the Jameh Mosque of Yazd and are among Iran's tallest.
islamic-architecture-0257: Which ruler is associated with the historic Vakil Bazaar in Shiraz?
Karim Khan Zand built Vakil Bazaar in Shiraz in the eighteenth century CE when he made the city his capital.
islamic-architecture-0259: Which elegant cursive Arabic script was commonly used in mosque inscriptions and Quran surah (chapter) headings?
Thuluth is an elegant cursive script used in mosque decoration since medieval times and in writing surah (chapter) titles.
islamic-architecture-0260: Which script is arranged in brick or square tiles in a geometric grid on Iranian building walls and is called bannai?
Square Kufic, or bannai, is a geometric script with right angles, widely used in tilework and covering entire buildings in Iran.
islamic-architecture-0261: What is the Persian name, meaning 'seven colors,' for the tile technique in which multicolored designs are painted on a tile before firing?
Haft rang, meaning seven colors, is a ceramic tile technique in which colored designs are painted beneath the glaze.
islamic-architecture-0262: Where did most of the marble and granite columns in the Great Mosque of Kairouan's prayer hall come from?
Nearby marble quarries, carved specifically for it
Roman and Byzantine archaeological sites such as Carthage
The columns in the Great Mosque of Kairouan's prayer hall came from ancient sites in the country, such as Carthage, Sbeitla, and Hadrumetum (Sousse).
islamic-architecture-0263: What is the name of the fountain often placed in mosque and caravanserai courtyards to provide drinking water and water for wudu (ablution)?
A shadirwan is a fountain built in a mosque courtyard or near its entrance so several people can perform wudu (ablution) at once.
islamic-architecture-0265: What is the raised platform inside a mosque on which the muezzin or relay caller stands to repeat the imam's takbir (saying Allahu akbar)?
The dikka is a raised mosque platform where the muezzin repeats the imam's takbir (saying Allahu akbar) and gives the iqama (call to begin prayer).
islamic-architecture-0266: What is the walled outer courtyard surrounding the Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun to separate it from city noise called?
The ziyada is an outer courtyard surrounding the mosque on three sides within an outer wall, separating the prayer space from the surrounding city.
islamic-architecture-0267: Which type of arch is drawn from four centers and became widespread in Islamic architecture, especially in Iran?
The four-centered arch, or Persian arch, was used by the Abbasids and then the Fatimids and became widespread in Iranian iwans and gateways.
islamic-architecture-0268: What is the secure roofed building at the center of an Ottoman market where valuable goods such as gold and jewelry are kept called?
A bedesten is a fortified domed building in the heart of an Ottoman market where valuable goods are stored and sold.
islamic-architecture-0269: What is the public charitable dining establishment in Ottoman complexes that provided free food to the poor and students called?
An imaret is a public charitable kitchen built throughout the Ottoman Empire to provide free food to specified groups.
islamic-architecture-0270: What is a historic merchants' inn in Maghreb cities such as Fez and Tetouan called?
In the Maghreb, funduq refers to historic urban caravanserais: multistory buildings around a courtyard.
islamic-architecture-0271: What is the fortified communal store where Amazigh tribes keep grain and belongings in southern Morocco called?
An agadir, plural igoudar, is a fortified communal store on a rocky height where grain and valuable possessions are kept.
islamic-architecture-0272: What does the name of the Safavid Hasht Behesht Palace in Isfahan mean?
Hasht Behesht means eight paradises. Its plan consists of a central hall surrounded by eight rooms.
islamic-architecture-0273: How many Iranian gardens were jointly listed as World Heritage under the name 'The Persian Garden' in 2011?
Nine historic gardens in Iran were jointly listed as World Heritage in 2011 as The Persian Garden.
islamic-architecture-0274: What is the small column-supported domed pavilion decorating the roofs of Mughal buildings in India called?
A chhatri is a raised, partly open pavilion topped by a dome, common in Mughal Indian architecture and elsewhere.
islamic-architecture-0275: What is a stone or marble screen pierced with geometric designs in Indian and Mughal architecture called?
A jali, meaning lattice, is a stone screen pierced or latticed with geometric or calligraphic designs.
islamic-architecture-0276: What was the art of inlaying marble with polished colored stones called in Mughal India?
The art of colored stone inlay was known in Mughal India as parchin kari, corresponding to Italy's pietra dura.
islamic-architecture-0277: Across how many successive terraces are the Mughal Shalimar Gardens in Lahore laid out?
Lahore's Shalimar Gardens consist of three successive terraces, each rising 4 to 5 meters above the preceding one.
islamic-architecture-0278: Sultan Murad IV built the Baghdad Kiosk in Topkapi Palace to celebrate:
The arrival of Baghdad merchants at the palace
The visit of Baghdad's governor to Istanbul
The Baghdad Kiosk was built in 1638-1639 CE to celebrate the Ottoman victory in Baghdad during Murad IV's reign.
islamic-architecture-0279: What was structurally distinctive about the Fatimid Mosque of al-Salih Talai in Cairo?
It was Cairo's first mosque with a stone dome
It was built on a bridge over the canal
It was the first elevated mosque raised above a row of shops
The Mosque of al-Salih Talai was built on a raised platform above shops that provided income for it, making it Cairo's first elevated mosque.
islamic-architecture-0280: In which African country is the earthen Larabanga Mosque, considered the country's oldest mosque?
Larabanga Mosque in northern Ghana is built in Sudano-Sahelian style. It is Ghana's oldest mosque and one of the oldest in West Africa.
islamic-architecture-0281: In which country is the earthen Great Mosque of Bobo-Dioulasso?
The earthen Great Mosque is in Bobo-Dioulasso in Houet Province, Burkina Faso.
islamic-architecture-0282: What is the name of the vast palace built by Kilwa's Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulayman in the fourteenth century on Tanzania's coast?
Husuni Kubwa, the Great Palace, is a palace and trading complex built outside Kilwa by Sultan al-Hasan ibn Sulayman in the early fourteenth century.
islamic-architecture-0283: For the kings of which dynasty did Arab artisans build Al-Aziza (La Zisa) Palace in Palermo, Sicily, in the twelfth century?
Arab artisans began building Al-Aziza Palace around 1165 CE under the Norman king William I as a summer residence for Norman kings.
islamic-architecture-0284: What wood was used for the tall columns in the Great Mosque of Srinagar in Kashmir?
Parts of Srinagar's Great Mosque rest on tall deodar columns. Deodar is Himalayan cedar.
islamic-architecture-0285: What is the Juma Mosque in Khiva, Uzbekistan, famous for?
Its more than two hundred wooden columns
Being built over the Amu Darya River
Khiva's Juma Mosque is a single-story building with a flat roof supported by 212 wooden columns in 17 rows.
islamic-architecture-0286: In which Iranian city is the Safavid Ganjali Khan complex with its square, bathhouse, and bazaar?
Ganjali Khan, governor of Kerman under Shah Abbas I, built this complex in the center of Kerman's old city.
islamic-architecture-0287: Which Saudi city does historic Marid Castle overlook?
Marid Castle stands on a hill overlooking Dumat al-Jandal from the west in Al Jawf Region.
islamic-architecture-0288: In which Bahraini city is the historic fort of Sheikh Salman bin Ahmad Al-Fateh?
Riffa Fort stands on a cliff overlooking the valley between East and West Riffa. Sheikh Salman bin Ahmad Al-Fateh rebuilt it in 1812 CE.
islamic-architecture-0289: Besides guarding, Qatar's historic Barzan Towers were formerly used for:
Barzan Towers were watchtowers, and Qatar's residents also used them to sight the Ramadan crescent.
islamic-architecture-0290: In which emirate is Al Bidya Mosque, considered the oldest standing mosque in the UAE?
Al Bidya Mosque is in Al Bidya village in Fujairah and is believed to have been built around 1446 CE.
islamic-architecture-0291: To which dynasty does the domed Amiriya Madrasa in Rada, Yemen, date?
Sultan Amir ibn Abd al-Wahhab of the Tahirid dynasty built the Amiriya Madrasa in 1504 CE.
islamic-architecture-0292: In which Yemeni city is the Mosque of Queen Arwa bint Ahmad al-Sulayhi?
Queen Arwa's Mosque is in Jibla. She converted Dar al-Izz Palace into a mosque after moving there in 1087 CE.
islamic-architecture-0293: What is the Arabic name of the sealed Golden Gate in the eastern wall of Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem, Palestine?
Muslims call the Golden Gate Bab al-Rahma. It is a double gateway in the eastern wall, built in the early Islamic period.
islamic-architecture-0294: What lighting objects for mosques were Mamluk glass workshops famous for?
Mamluk workshops were renowned for luxurious mosque lamps made of enameled and gilded glass.
islamic-architecture-0295: Where was the famous minbar (pulpit) of the Koutoubia Mosque, now preserved in El Badi Palace in Marrakesh, made?
The minbar (pulpit) was made in a Cordoba workshop in the early twelfth century on the orders of the Almoravid Ali ibn Yusuf, then transported in pieces to Marrakesh.
islamic-architecture-0296: Which Mamluk mosque stands inside Cairo's Citadel and was used by sultans for Friday prayer?
Mosque of al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun
The Mosque of al-Nasir Muhammad ibn Qalawun in the Citadel was completed in 1318 CE and was the royal mosque where sultans performed Friday prayer.
islamic-architecture-0297: France's King Louis Philippe gave the tower clock overlooking the courtyard of Muhammad Ali Mosque in the Citadel in exchange for:
The clock was given to Muhammad Ali around 1846 CE in exchange for the Luxor Obelisk, now in the Place de la Concorde in Paris.
islamic-architecture-0298: The largest surviving mosaic panel in the western arcade of the Umayyad Mosque in Damascus is named after which river?
The Barada panel is a large mosaic extending about 34.5 meters along the western arcade, depicting landscapes and buildings, some associated with the Barada River.
islamic-architecture-0299: Which governor of Medina introduced the first concave mihrab (prayer niche) in the Prophet's Mosque during al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik's rebuilding?
While governor of Medina under al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz ordered a recess marking the qibla (prayer direction) wall, creating the first concave mihrab (prayer niche).
islamic-architecture-0300: What is meant by a double dome in Seljuk, Timurid, and Ottoman architecture?
Two adjacent domes of equal size
A dome half stone and half wood
A dome with two shells, one above the other
A dome resting on two rows of columns
A double dome has inner and outer shells that may differ in shape, allowing a taller exterior without raising the interior ceiling.
islamic-architecture-0303: Under how many Ottoman sultans did Mimar Sinan serve as chief architect?
Sinan was chief imperial architect under Suleiman the Magnificent, Selim II, and Murad III, for about fifty years.
islamic-architecture-0304: Who succeeded Mimar Sinan as chief architect of the Ottoman Empire?
Davud Agha, one of the architects who had worked under Sinan, succeeded him as chief imperial architect.
islamic-architecture-0306: What was the first madrasa (school) built by the Marinids in Fez in 1271 CE?
Saffarin Madrasa (school) was completed in 1271 CE and was the first madrasa built by the Marinids.
islamic-architecture-0307: Which Marinid sultan founded the library of Al-Qarawiyyin Mosque in Fez in 1349 CE?
Sultan Abu Inan Faris founded the Al-Qarawiyyin library in 1349 CE, as an inscription above its door indicates. It is among the oldest operating libraries.
islamic-architecture-0308: Approximately how many columns support the arches of the Great Mosque of Kairouan's prayer hall?
The prayer hall arches of the Great Mosque of Kairouan rest on 414 marble, granite, and porphyry columns, out of more than 500 columns in the entire mosque.
islamic-architecture-0309: Which German Muslim architect designed the sliding domes and folding umbrellas at the Prophet's Mosque?
Mahmoud Bodo Rasch and his firm designed the sliding domes and folding umbrellas at the Prophet's Mosque.
islamic-architecture-0310: Which Moroccan grand vizier expanded Bahia Palace in Marrakesh in the late nineteenth century?
Ba Ahmad ibn Musa, grand vizier under Sultan Moulay Abd al-Aziz, expanded Bahia Palace between 1894 and 1900 CE.
islamic-architecture-0311: Around which feature are the historic Menara Gardens in Marrakesh arranged?
A small mosque with a minaret
A large water basin beside a pavilion
The Menara Gardens are arranged around a large water basin and reservoir beside a leisure pavilion, surrounded by an extensive orchard.
islamic-architecture-0312: Which Almohad ruler established the Menara Gardens in Marrakesh around 1157 CE?
Abd al-Mumin ibn Ali, the first Almohad caliph, established the Menara Gardens around 1157 CE.
islamic-architecture-0313: Which two colors are the houses of Sidi Bou Said village overlooking the Gulf of Tunis famous for?
Sidi Bou Said is famous for its white architecture with blue doors and windows.
islamic-architecture-0314: The Mosque of Sultan al-Muayyad Shaykh in Fatimid Cairo was built on the site of:
A prison in which al-Muayyad had been held
The mosque replaced a prison where al-Muayyad had been held before becoming sultan. He vowed that if he gained power, he would turn it into a place of learning.
islamic-architecture-0315: The historic Koza Han in Bursa, Turkey, is associated with the trade in:
Koza Han means the cocoon inn and was a center for trading silk and silkworm cocoons in Bursa.
islamic-architecture-0316: In which country is the historic Sultan Mosque in the Kampong Glam neighborhood?

Sultan Mosque is in Singapore's Kampong Glam neighborhood. Hussein Shah, Sultan of Johor, requested its construction in 1823 CE. The original was built in 1824-1826 CE, and it was rebuilt in the twentieth century.
islamic-architecture-0317: The Sheikh Karimul Makhdum Mosque, described in local accounts as the country's oldest mosque, is in:
The mosque is on Simunul Island in Tawi-Tawi, Philippines. Traditional accounts date its foundation to 1380 CE.
islamic-architecture-0318: What material was used to build the Old Friday Mosque in Male, capital of the Maldives?
Male's Old Friday Mosque was built from interlocking coral stone blocks and is considered one of the world's finest coral buildings.
islamic-architecture-0319: What is Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque in Colombo, Sri Lanka, famous for?
Jami Ul-Alfar, known as the Red Mosque, is a two-story building with alternating red and white stripes.
islamic-architecture-0320: In which city is Auwal Mosque, considered the first mosque established in South Africa?
Auwal Mosque was completed in 1794 CE in Cape Town's Bo-Kaap neighborhood and is South Africa's first mosque.
sahaba-0001: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) described a Companion as «أمين هذه الأمة» [trustworthy man of this Ummah]. Who was he?

Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Anas that the Prophet said: «إن لكل أمة أمينًا، وإن أميننا أيتها الأمة أبو عبيدة بن الجراح» [Every nation has an extremely trustworthy man, and the most trustworthy man of this Ummah is Abu ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrāh.] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0002: To the people of which place did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say «لأبعثن إليكم أمينًا حق أمين» [I will certainly send you a truly trustworthy man], then send Abu Ubayda?
Al-Bukhari narrated from Hudhayfa that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said this to the people of Najran and sent Abu Ubayda, may Allah be pleased with him.
sahaba-0003: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «إن لكل نبي حواريًّا، وإن حواريَّ...» [Every prophet had a disciple and my disciple...]. Whose name completes the hadith?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports: «إن لكل نبي حواريًّا وإن حواريَّ الزبير بن العوام» [Every prophet had a disciple and my disciple is Az-Zubayr.] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0004: Qays ibn Abi Hazim said he saw a Companion's hand, with which he had shielded the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), paralyzed. Whose hand did he mean?
Al-Bukhari narrated from Qays: «رأيت يد طلحة التي وقى بها النبي ﷺ قد شلّت» [I saw Talha's hand, with which he had shielded the Prophet, paralyzed.].
sahaba-0005: Which Companion said «إني لأول العرب رمى بسهم في سبيل الله» [I was the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allah's cause]?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Sad, may Allah be pleased with him: «إني لأول العرب رمى بسهم في سبيل الله» [I was the first Arab to shoot an arrow in Allah's cause.].
sahaba-0007: Sad ibn Abi Waqqas belonged to which Quraysh clan, the clan of the Prophet's maternal uncles?
Al-Bukhari gave the chapter heading: 'The merits of Sad ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri; Banu Zuhra are the Prophet's maternal uncles.'
sahaba-0008: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) praised a son-in-law from Banu Abd Shams, saying «حدثني فصدقني ووعدني فوفى لي» [He spoke truthfully to me and kept his promise to me]. Who was he?
Sahih al-Bukhari mentions him in the chapter on the Prophet's sons-in-law, including Abu al-As ibn al-Rabi, who belonged to Banu Abd Shams.
sahaba-0009: When some people criticized Usama ibn Zayd's appointment as commander, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said they had previously criticized another man's command. Who was he?

Al-Bukhari reports: «إن تطعنوا في إمارته فقد كنتم تطعنون في إمارة أبيه من قبل، وايم الله إن كان لخليقًا للإمارة» [If you criticize his appointment as commander, you previously criticized his father's command. By Allah, he was indeed worthy of command.].
sahaba-0011: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) told Hafsa «إن عبد الله رجل صالح» [Abdullah is a righteous man]. Which Abdullah did he mean?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Hafsa that the Prophet told her: «إن عبد الله رجل صالح» [Abdullah is a righteous man], meaning her brother Ibn Umar.
sahaba-0012: In Ibn Umar's dream when he was a young unmarried man sleeping in the mosque, where did the two angels take him?
To Paradise, where he saw a golden palace
To the Fire, which was enclosed like a well
To a green meadow containing a pillar and a handhold
To Bayt al-Maqdis, where he prayed two rakahs (prayer units)

Al-Bukhari narrated from Ibn Umar: «فرأيت في المنام كأن ملكين أخذاني فذهبا بي إلى النار فإذا هي مطوية كطي البئر» [I saw in a dream two angels take me to the Fire, which was enclosed like the walls of a well.].
sahaba-0014: Which Companion did Abu al-Darda describe as the one whom Allah had protected from Satan through His Prophet's words?

Sahih al-Bukhari reports: «أليس فيكم الذي أجاره الله على لسان نبيه ﷺ، يعني من الشيطان، يعني عمارًا» [Is there not among you the one whom Allah protected through His Prophet's words, meaning from Satan, and meaning Ammar?].
sahaba-0015: Umar used to say «أبو بكر سيدنا وأعتق سيدنا» [Abu Bakr is our master and freed our master]. Who is the second 'our master'?
Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa
Al-Bukhari narrated from Jabir that Umar used to say this, meaning Bilal, whom Abu Bakr freed.
sahaba-0016: Which Companion told Abu Bakr «إن كنت إنما اشتريتني لنفسك فأمسكني، وإن كنت اشتريتني لله فدعني وعمل الله» [If you bought me for yourself, keep me; if you bought me for Allah, let me go and work for Allah]?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports that Bilal said this to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both.
sahaba-0017: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said «استقرئوا القرآن من أربعة» [Learn the Quran from four people], naming one first. Whom did he name first?

Al-Bukhari reports: «خذوا القرآن من أربعة: من عبد الله بن مسعود فبدأ به، وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة، ومعاذ، وأبي» [Learn the Quran from four: Abdullah ibn Masud, whom he named first; Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa; Muadh; and Ubayy.].
sahaba-0018: Which of these freedmen was among the four from whom the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) instructed people to learn the Quran?
Thawban, freedman of the Messenger of Allah
Abu Rafi, freedman of the Messenger of Allah
Amir ibn Fuhayra, freedman of Abu Bakr
The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) included Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, among the four from whom the Quran should be learned, as recorded in al-Bukhari.
sahaba-0019: Abu Musa said: I and my brother arrived from Yemen, and for some time we thought this man belonged to the Prophet's household. Whom did he mean?
Al-Bukhari reports this from Abu Musa, who saw how frequently Ibn Masud and his mother visited the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him).
sahaba-0020: About whom did Hudhayfa say: «ما أعرف أحدًا أقرب سمتًا وهديًا ودلًّا بالنبي ﷺ من ابن أم عبد» [I know no one whose bearing, conduct and manner more closely resemble the Prophet's than Ibn Umm Abd's]?
Sahih al-Bukhari records this statement by Hudhayfa. Ibn Umm Abd is Abd Allah ibn Masud.
sahaba-0021: Anas said that four Ansar (Helpers), including Abu Zayd, had memorized the Quran during the Prophet's lifetime. He called Abu Zayd «أحد عمومتي» [one of my paternal uncles]. Who were the other three?
Ubayy, Muadh ibn Jabal and Zayd ibn Thabit
Ubayy, Sad ibn Ubada and Usayd ibn Hudayr
Muadh ibn Jabal, Abu Ayyub and Sad ibn Muadh
Zayd ibn Thabit, Hassan ibn Thabit and Abu Talha

Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Anas: «جمع القرآن على عهد النبي ﷺ أربعة كلهم من الأنصار: أبي، ومعاذ بن جبل، وأبو زيد، وزيد بن ثابت» [Four men, all of them Ansar (Helpers), memorized the Quran during the Prophet's lifetime: Ubayy, Muadh ibn Jabal, Abu Zayd and Zayd ibn Thabit].
sahaba-0022: Which surah did Allah command His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to recite to Ubayy ibn Kab, making Ubayy weep?
«تبارك الذي بيده الملك» [Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion] (al-Mulk)
«سبح اسم ربك الأعلى» [Exalt the name of your Lord, the Most High,] (al-Ala)
«إذا جاء نصر الله والفتح» [When the victory of Allāh has come and the conquest,[2005]] (al-Nasr)

In al-Bukhari, the Prophet said to Ubayy: «إن الله أمرني أن أقرأ عليك: لم يكن الذين كفروا» [Allah has commanded me to recite to you: Those who disbelieved]. Ubayy asked: Did He mention me by name? He said: Yes. Ubayy wept. Quran opening (QuranEnc). Footnote [2005]: The conquest of Makkah.
sahaba-0023: About which Companion did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) say: «اهتز عرش الرحمن لموت ...» [The Throne of al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) shook at the death of ...]?
Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram
Al-Bukhari reports that Jabir heard the Prophet say: «اهتز عرش الرحمن لموت سعد بن معاذ» [The Throne of al-Rahman (the Most Merciful) shook at the death of Sad ibn Muadh].
sahaba-0024: Two Companions left the Prophet on a dark night, and a light appeared before them. One was Usayd ibn Hudayr; who was the other?
Al-Bukhari included a chapter entitled «منقبة أسيد بن حضير وعباد بن بشر» [A virtue of Usayd ibn Hudayr and Abbad ibn Bishr] and related the account of the light before them.
sahaba-0025: Which Companion described the day of Uhud by saying: «كان أبو طلحة رجلًا راميًا شديد القِدّ، يكسر يومئذ قوسين أو ثلاثًا» [Abu Talha was a powerfully built archer; that day he broke two or three bows]?
The hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari is narrated by Anas ibn Malik. Abu Talha was his mother's husband.
sahaba-0026: Sad ibn Abi Waqqas said: «ما سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول لأحد يمشي على الأرض إنه من أهل الجنة إلا ل...» [I never heard the Prophet say of anyone walking on earth that he was among the people of Paradise except ...]. Who was he?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Sad: «إلا لعبد الله بن سلام» [except Abd Allah ibn Salam].
sahaba-0027: Jarir ibn Abd Allah al-Bajali said: «ما حجبني رسول الله ﷺ منذ أسلمت، ولا رآني إلا ...» [The Messenger of Allah never denied me access to him after I embraced Islam, and whenever he saw me, he ...]. How does the statement end?

Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Jarir: «ما حجبني رسول الله ﷺ منذ أسلمت ولا رآني إلا ضحك» [The Messenger of Allah never denied me access to him after I embraced Islam, and whenever he saw me, he smiled].
sahaba-0028: What was the name of the shrine known in the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic era) as the Yemeni Kaaba, which Jarir ibn Abd Allah rid the Prophet of?

Al-Bukhari reports from Jarir: «كان في الجاهلية بيت يقال له ذو الخلصة، وكان يقال له الكعبة اليمانية» [In the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic era), there was a shrine called Dhu al-Khalasa, also known as the Yemeni Kaaba].
sahaba-0029: Which Companion's father was mistakenly killed by Muslims on the day of Uhud, whereupon he said: «غفر الله لكم» [May Allah forgive you]?
Al-Bukhari reports from Aisha that Hudhayfa called out: «أبي أبي» [My father! My father!], but they did not stop before killing him. Hudhayfa said: «غفر الله لكم» [May Allah forgive you].
sahaba-0030: The Prophet established brotherhood between Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and an Ansari (Helper) who offered to share his wealth with him. Who was this Ansari?

Sahih al-Bukhari states: «آخى رسول الله ﷺ بين عبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن الربيع» [The Messenger of Allah established brotherhood between Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sad ibn al-Rabi]. He offered him half his wealth.
sahaba-0031: Of which battle in the Jahiliyya (pre-Islamic era) did Aisha say that Allah had prepared it for His Messenger, facilitating the Ansar's subsequent acceptance of Islam?
Al-Bukhari reports from Aisha: «كان يوم بعاث يومًا قدّمه الله لرسوله ﷺ ... في دخولهم في الإسلام» [The day of Buath was a day Allah had prepared for His Messenger ... in their acceptance of Islam].
sahaba-0032: The Prophet invited the Ansar (Helpers) to receive a land grant. They said they would accept only if their Muhajirun (Emigrant) brothers received an equivalent grant. Which land was it?

Al-Bukhari reports from Anas: «دعا النبي ﷺ الأنصار إلى أن يقطع لهم البحرين، فقالوا: لا إلا أن تقطع لإخواننا من المهاجرين مثلها» [The Prophet invited the Ansar (Helpers) to receive al-Bahrayn as a land grant. They said: No, unless you grant our Muhajirun (Emigrant) brothers its equivalent].
sahaba-0033: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah's words ﴿ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة﴾ [but give [them] preference over themselves, even though they are in privation.] describe an act by:
An Emigrant who left his trade to join the Prophet
An Emigrant who gave half his wealth in charity at Tabuk
A Helper who hosted the Prophet's guest with his children's food
A Helper who freed all his slaves on the day of the conquest
Under this verse, al-Bukhari relates the story of the Ansari (Helper) who told his wife to honor the Messenger of Allah's guest, although they had only their children's food (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0034: Which Companion said: «لقد رأيتني وإن عمر لموثقي على الإسلام قبل أن يسلم عمر» [I remember when Umar bound me because of my Islam, before Umar himself embraced Islam]?
Al-Bukhari reports this statement from Said ibn Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl in the mosque of Kufa.
sahaba-0035: Ammar ibn Yasir said that he saw the Messenger of Allah accompanied only by five male slaves, two women and whom else?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Ammar: «رأيت رسول الله ﷺ وما معه إلا خمسة أعبد وامرأتان وأبو بكر» [I saw the Messenger of Allah with only five male slaves, two women and Abu Bakr accompanying him].
sahaba-0036: Why was Asma bint Abi Bakr called Dhat al-Nitaqayn (the woman of the two waistbands)?
She wore two waistbands during Hajj and Umra
She used her waistband to bandage Muslims' wounds at al-Yarmuk
She split her waistband to tie up provisions for the Prophet and Abu Bakr
She gave her waistband to the Prophet on the day of the Hijra

In al-Bukhari, she said: «صنعت سفرة للنبي ﷺ وأبي بكر ... فقلت لأبي: ما أجد شيئًا أربطه إلا نطاقي، قال: فشقيه، ففعلت فسُمّيت ذات النطاقين» [I prepared provisions for the Prophet and Abu Bakr ... I told my father: I can find nothing to tie them with except my waistband. He said: Split it. I did so and was called Dhat al-Nitaqayn (the woman of the two waistbands)].
sahaba-0037: Who was the first child born to the Muhajirun (Emigrants) after the Hijra (migration) to Medina, whose palate the Prophet rubbed with a date, as Aisha related?
Al-Bukhari reports from Aisha: «أول مولود وُلد في الإسلام عبد الله بن الزبير» [The first child born in Islam was Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr].
sahaba-0038: A man pursued the Prophet and Abu Bakr during the Hijra (migration). The Prophet prayed against him, and his horse sank into the ground. Who was he?

Sahih al-Bukhari reports from al-Bara: «تبعه سراقة بن مالك بن جعشم فدعا عليه النبي ﷺ فساخت به فرسه» [Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Jushum pursued him, and the Prophet prayed against him, whereupon his horse sank into the ground].
sahaba-0039: Al-Bara said that the first people to arrive in Medina were Musab ibn Umayr and another man, both of whom taught people the Quran. Who was the other man?

Sahih al-Bukhari reports from al-Bara: «أول من قدم علينا مصعب بن عمير وابن أم مكتوم وكانا يقرئان الناس» [The first to arrive among us were Musab ibn Umayr and Ibn Umm Maktum, who taught people the Quran].
sahaba-0040: According to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, what was Musab ibn Umayr shrouded in on the day of Uhud?
A striped cloth that left his feet exposed when it covered his head
Two white garments belonging to the Ansar
A red cloak the Prophet had given him
The clothes he was killed in, together with idhkhir grass

Al-Bukhari reports from Khabbab: «قتل يوم أحد فلم نجد شيئًا نكفنه فيه إلا نمرة، كنا إذا غطينا بها رأسه خرجت رجلاه» [He was killed on the day of Uhud, and we could find nothing to shroud him in except a striped cloth. When we covered his head with it, his feet were exposed].
sahaba-0041: Umar allotted four thousand to the earliest Muhajirun (Emigrants), but three thousand five hundred to his son Abd Allah. What reason did he give?
He was his son, so he disliked favoring him
He embraced Islam after the conquest of Mecca
He was considered too young at Badr and Uhud
His parents took him on the migration; he did not migrate independently
In Sahih al-Bukhari, Umar said: «إنما هاجر به أبواه، يقول: ليس هو كمن هاجر بنفسه» [His parents merely took him on the migration, meaning that he was not like someone who migrated independently].
sahaba-0042: When the Negus died, the Prophet said: «مات اليوم رجل صالح فقوموا فصلوا على أخيكم...» [A righteous man died today, so stand and offer the funeral prayer for your brother ...]. What was the Negus's name?
Sahih al-Bukhari states: «فقوموا فصلوا على أخيكم أصحمة» [So stand and offer the funeral prayer for your brother Ashama].
sahaba-0043: Which girl came from Abyssinia and was given a patterned cloak by the Prophet, who said: «سناه سناه» [Beautiful, beautiful]?
Umm Khalid bint Khalid ibn Said

Al-Bukhari reports from Umm Khalid bint Khalid: «قدمت من أرض الحبشة وأنا جويرية فكساني رسول الله ﷺ خميصة لها أعلام» [I came from Abyssinia as a little girl, and the Messenger of Allah clothed me in a cloak with patterned markings].
sahaba-0044: Through which Companion did Umar seek rain during drought, saying: «اللهم إنا نتوسل إليك بعم نبينا فاسقنا» [O Allah, we seek to draw near to You through our Prophet's uncle, so grant us rain]?
Sahih al-Bukhari reports from Anas that, during drought, Umar sought rain through al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. pronunciation: Allahumma inna natawassalu ilayka bi-ammi nabiyyina fasqina.
sahaba-0045: Whom did Abu Hurayra describe as «أخير الناس للمسكين» [the best of people to the poor], taking them home and feeding them whatever he had?
Al-Bukhari reports from Abu Hurayra: «وكان أخير الناس للمسكين جعفر بن أبي طالب» [Jafar ibn Abi Talib was the best of people to the poor].
sahaba-0047: After the verse of tayammum (dry ablution) was revealed, which Companion said to Aisha: «جزاك الله خيرًا، فوالله ما نزل بك أمر قط إلا جعل الله لك منه مخرجًا» [May Allah reward you with good. By Allah, no difficulty has ever befallen you without Allah providing you a way out]?

Sahih al-Bukhari states: «فنزلت آية التيمم، فقال أسيد بن حضير: جزاك الله خيرًا...» [Then the verse of tayammum (dry ablution) was revealed, and Usayd ibn Hudayr said: May Allah reward you with good ...].
sahaba-0048: Of which night did Kab ibn Malik say: «وما أحب أن لي بها مشهد بدر وإن كانت بدر أذكر في الناس منها» [It would not please me to have attended the battle of Badr instead of the ‘Aqabah pledge, although Badr is more notable than it among the people.]?

In al-Bukhari, Kab said: «ولقد شهدت مع النبي ﷺ ليلة العقبة حين تواثقنا على الإسلام، وما أحب أن لي بها مشهد بدر» [I witnessed the night of the ‘Aqabah pledge of allegiance with the Prophet (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) when we jointly agreed to support Islam with all our efforts. It would not please me to have attended the battle of Badr instead of the ‘Aqabah pledge] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0049: Which Companion said: «إني من النقباء الذين بايعوا رسول الله ﷺ» [I am one of the representatives who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah], and mentioned pledging not to associate anything with Allah?
Al-Bukhari reports from Ubada ibn al-Samit: «إني من النقباء الذين بايعوا رسول الله ﷺ» [I am one of the representatives who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah].
sahaba-0052: A Companion's mother swore not to speak to him, eat or drink until he renounced his faith. About him was revealed: ﴿وإن جاهداك على أن تشرك بي﴾ [But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me]. Who was he?
Muslim reports from Sad that his mother swore not to speak to him until he renounced his religion, and Allah revealed that verse (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0053: The words ﴿ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي﴾ [And do not send away those who call upon their Lord morning and afternoon] were revealed concerning six Companions. Who said that he and Ibn Masud were among them?

Sahih Muslim reports from Sad: «فيّ نزلت ﴿ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم﴾، نزلت في ستة أنا وابن مسعود منهم» [It was concerning me that the words 'And do not send away those who call upon their Lord' were revealed. They were revealed concerning six people, including me and Ibn Masud] (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0054: Aisha told Urwa: «أبواك والله من الذين استجابوا لله والرسول من بعد ما أصابهم القرح» [By Allah, your two fathers were among the people described as: Those [believers] who responded to Allāh and the Messenger after injury had struck them.]. She meant Abu Bakr and whom?

Sahih Muslim reports from Aisha, with one narration explaining: «تعني أبا بكر والزبير» [She meant Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr]. They were Urwa's maternal grandfather and father. The Quran wording embedded in Aisha's statement follows the unchanged matching excerpt of (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0055: By what name did the Companions call Zayd ibn Haritha until the revelation of ﴿ادعوهم لآبائهم﴾ [Call them[1181] by [the names of] their fathers]?

Muslim reports from Ibn Umar: «ما كنا ندعو زيد بن حارثة إلا زيد بن محمد حتى نزل في القرآن: ادعوهم لآبائهم» [We used to call Zayd ibn Haritha only Zayd ibn Muhammad, until the Quran revealed: Call them[1181] by [the names of] their fathers] (QuranEnc). Footnote [1181]: Those children under your care.
sahaba-0056: Umm Salama saw Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, speaking to the Prophet and mistook him for a Companion. Whom did she think he was?
Sahih Muslim records Umm Salama saying: «هذا دحية» [That is Dihya]. She later learned that it was Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him.
sahaba-0057: After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr told Umar to join him in visiting a woman whom the Messenger of Allah used to visit. Who was she?

Sahih Muslim reports from Anas: «انطلق بنا إلى أم أيمن نزورها كما كان رسول الله ﷺ يزورها» [Let us visit Umm Ayman, just as the Messenger of Allah (may Allah's peace and blessings be upon him) used to visit her.] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0058: The Prophet did not visit women other than his wives and one female Companion, saying: «إني أرحمها، قُتل أخوها معي» [I feel compassion for her; her brother was killed while with me]. Who was she?

Muslim reports from Anas: «إلا أم سليم، فإنه كان يدخل عليها ... فقال: إني أرحمها، قتل أخوها معي» [Except Umm Sulaym, whom he used to visit ... He said: I feel compassion for her; her brother was killed while with me].
sahaba-0059: Which female Companion, when her son died, told her family not to tell Abu Talha about his son until she herself told him?

Sahih Muslim reports from Anas: «مات ابن لأبي طلحة من أم سليم فقالت لأهلها: لا تحدثوا أبا طلحة بابنه حتى أكون أنا أحدثه» [Abu Talha’s son from Umm Sulaym died. She asked family members not to tell Abu Talha about his son, as she would inform him herself.] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0060: When ﴿ليس على الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات جناح فيما طعموا﴾ [There is not upon those who believe and do righteousness [any] blame concerning what they have eaten [in the past]] was revealed, to which Companion did the Prophet say: «قيل لي: أنت منهم» [I was told: You are among them]?
Muslim relates the hadith in the chapter on the virtues of Abd Allah ibn Masud: «قال لي رسول الله ﷺ: قيل لي: أنت منهم» [The Messenger of Allah told me: I was told: You are among them] (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0061: How many surahs did Ibn Masud say he had recited to the Messenger of Allah?
In Sahih Muslim, Ibn Masud said: «فلقد قرأت على رسول الله ﷺ بضعًا وسبعين سورة» [I recited seventy-odd surahs to the Messenger of Allah].
sahaba-0062: When the Companions admired the softness of a silk garment given to the Prophet, he said: «لمناديل ... في الجنة خير منها وألين» [The handkerchiefs of ... in Paradise are better and softer than it]. Whose handkerchiefs?

Muslim reports from al-Bara: «أتعجبون من لين هذه؟ لمناديل سعد بن معاذ في الجنة خير منها وألين» [Do you marvel at its softness? The handkerchiefs of Sad ibn Muadh in Paradise are better and softer than it].
sahaba-0063: On the day of Uhud, the Prophet held up a sword and asked: «من يأخذه بحقه؟» [Who will take it and fulfill its due?]. Everyone hesitated except one man, who took it and split the polytheists' heads with it. Who was he?

Sahih Muslim states: «فقال سماك بن خرشة أبو دجانة: أنا آخذه بحقه، فأخذه ففلق به هام المشركين» [Simak ibn Kharasha, Abu Dujana, said: I will take it and fulfill its due. He took it and split the polytheists' heads with it].
sahaba-0064: Of which Companion killed at Uhud did the Prophet say: «ما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها حتى رفعتموه» [The angels kept shading him with their wings until you lifted him away]?
Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram, Jabir's father
Hanzala ibn Abi Amir, washed by the angels
Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib, the Prophet's uncle

In the chapter on the virtues of Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn Haram, Jabir's father, Muslim reports the Prophet's words: «ما زالت الملائكة تظله بأجنحتها» [The angels continue to shade him with their wings.].
sahaba-0065: After an expedition, a Companion was found beside seven men he had killed before they killed him. The Prophet said: «هذا مني وأنا منه» [He is of me, and I am of him]. Who was he?
Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Barza: «لكني أفقد جليبيبًا ... قتل سبعة ثم قتلوه، هذا مني وأنا منه» [But I am missing Julaybib ... He killed seven before they killed him. He is of me, and I am of him].
sahaba-0066: When Abu Dharr heard that the Prophet had been sent, whom did he send to Mecca to bring him news?

Sahih Muslim reports from Ibn Abbas: «لما بلغ أبا ذر مبعث النبي ﷺ بمكة قال لأخيه: اركب إلى هذا الوادي فاعلم لي علم هذا الرجل» [When Abu Dharr heard that the Prophet had been sent in Mecca, he told his brother: Travel to this valley and find out about this man for me].
sahaba-0067: Which Companion complained to the Prophet that he could not sit firmly on horseback, whereupon the Prophet struck his chest and said: «اللهم ثبته واجعله هاديًا مهديًّا» [O Allah, make him firm and make him a guide who is rightly guided]?

Muslim reports from Jarir: «شكوت إليه أني لا أثبت على الخيل فضرب بيده في صدري وقال: اللهم ثبته واجعله هاديًا مهديًّا» [I complained to him that I could not sit firmly on horseback. He struck my chest with his hand and said: O Allah, make him firm and make him a guide who is rightly guided]. supplication pronunciation: Allahumma thabbit-hu wajalhu hadiyan mahdiyya.
sahaba-0068: Ibn Abbas placed water for the Prophet to perform wudu (ablution) when he went to relieve himself. Upon learning who had put it there, what supplication did the Prophet make for him?
«اللهم بارك له في ماله» [O Allah, bless his wealth]
«اللهم أطل عمره» [O Allah, prolong his life]
«اللهم اجعله من الصالحين» [O Allah, make him one of the righteous]

Sahih Muslim states: «من وضع هذا؟ قالوا: ابن عباس، قال: اللهم فقهه» [Who put this here? They said: Ibn Abbas. He said: O Allah, grant him understanding]. Supplication pronunciations in choice order: Allahumma barik lahu fi malih; Allahumma atil umrah; Allahumma faqqih-h; Allahumma ijalhu min al-salihin.
sahaba-0069: The Prophet entrusted Anas with a secret that he told no one, even when someone very close to him asked about it. Who asked him?

Muslim reports from Anas: «أسرّ إليّ نبي الله ﷺ سرًّا فما أخبرت به أحدًا بعد، ولقد سألتني عنه أم سليم فما أخبرتها به» [Allah's Prophet entrusted me with a secret, and I have told no one of it since. Umm Sulaym asked me about it, but I did not tell her].
sahaba-0070: A Companion dreamed of a pillar in a green garden with a handhold at its top. He climbed it and took hold of it. The Prophet said he would die holding fast to the firmest handhold. Who was he?

In the chapter on the virtues of Abd Allah ibn Salam, Sahih Muslim relates his dream and the Prophet's words: «يموت عبد الله وهو آخذ بالعروة الوثقى» [Abd Allah will die holding fast to the firmest handhold].
sahaba-0071: For whom did the Prophet pray: «اللهم أيّده بروح القدس» [O Allah, aid him with the Holy Spirit (Jibrīl)]?

In Sahih Muslim, Abu Hurayra testified that he heard the Prophet say to Hassan: «أجب عني، اللهم أيده بروح القدس» [(Hassān) answer on my behalf. O Allah, aid him with the Holy Spirit (Jibrīl).] (HadeethEnc) Supplication pronunciation: Allahumma ayyidhu bi-ruh al-qudus.
sahaba-0072: Hassan asked the Prophet's permission to satirize Abu Sufyan. The Prophet asked: «كيف بقرابتي منه؟» [What about my kinship with him?]. How did Hassan answer?
I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn from dough
I will leave Quraysh alone and satirize their allies
I will satirize them without mentioning their ancestry
I will leave it until you give me permission again
Muslim reports that Hassan said: «والذي أكرمك لأسلنك منهم كما تسل الشعرة من الخمير» [By the One who honored you, I will draw you out from among them as a hair is drawn from dough].
sahaba-0073: When the Prophet wished Quraysh to be satirized, whom did he first send for, whose satire did not satisfy him?

Sahih Muslim states: «فأرسل إلى ابن رواحة فقال: اهجهم فهجاهم فلم يرض، فأرسل إلى كعب بن مالك، ثم أرسل إلى حسان بن ثابت» [He sent for Ibn Rawaha and said: Satirize them. He did so, but it did not satisfy him. He then sent for Kab ibn Malik, then Hassan ibn Thabit].
sahaba-0074: For which Companion's polytheist mother did the Prophet pray for guidance, after which the Companion returned to find that she had bathed and embraced Islam?

Muslim reports from Abu Hurayra: «كنت أدعو أمي إلى الإسلام وهي مشركة ... فادع الله أن يهدي أم أبي هريرة» [I used to invite my mother to Islam while she was a polytheist ... So pray to Allah to guide Abu Hurayra's mother].
sahaba-0075: What did Abu Hurayra do when the Prophet said: «من يبسط ثوبه فلن ينسى شيئًا سمعه مني» [Whoever spreads out his garment will not forget anything he hears from me]?
He wrote the hadith on a piece of writing material
He repeated the hadith three times
He spread out his garment, then gathered it to himself
He put his hand on his chest

Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Hurayra: «فبسطت ثوبي حتى قضى حديثه، ثم ضممته إليّ فما نسيت شيئًا سمعته منه» [I spread out my garment until he finished speaking, then gathered it to myself, and I never forgot anything I heard from him].
sahaba-0076: Where did the Prophet send Ali, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad to take a letter from a woman traveling in a howdah?

Muslim reports from Ali: «بعثنا رسول الله ﷺ أنا والزبير والمقداد فقال: ائتوا روضة خاخ فإن بها ظعينة معها كتاب» [The Messenger of Allah sent me, al-Zubayr and al-Miqdad, saying: Go to Rawdat Khakh, where there is a woman traveling in a howdah with a letter].
sahaba-0077: A slave complained about his master to the Prophet, saying that his master would certainly enter the Fire. The Prophet replied: «كذبت لا يدخلها، فإنه شهد بدرًا والحديبية» [You are wrong; he will not enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyya]. Who was the master?
Sahih Muslim reports from Jabir that a slave belonging to Hatib came to complain about him, and the Prophet gave that reply.
sahaba-0078: After Hunayn, the Prophet sent an army to Awtas whose commander was struck in the knee by an arrow. Who was the commander?
Muslim reports from Abu Musa: «بعث أبا عامر على جيش إلى أوطاس ... فرمي أبو عامر في ركبته» [He sent Abu Amir in command of an army to Awtas ... Abu Amir was struck in the knee by an arrow].
sahaba-0079: The Prophet said: «إني لأعرف أصوات رفقة ... بالقرآن حين يدخلون بالليل» [I recognize the voices of the group of ... reciting the Quran when they come in at night]. Whose voices?
Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Musa: «إني لأعرف أصوات رفقة الأشعريين بالقرآن حين يدخلون بالليل» [I recognize the voices of the group of Asharis reciting the Quran when they come in at night].
sahaba-0080: Which people gathered what food they had into one cloth and shared it equally when supplies ran low, prompting the Prophet to say: «فهم مني وأنا منهم» [Thus they are from me and I am from them.]?

Muslim reports: «إن الأشعريين إذا أرملوا في الغزو ... جمعوا ما كان عندهم في ثوب واحد ... فهم مني وأنا منهم» [The Ash‘aris, if they ran short of provisions while on a military expedition ... they would gather everything they had in one piece of cloth ... Thus they are from me and I am from them.] (HadeethEnc)
sahaba-0081: Abu Musa al-Ashari left Yemen aboard a ship as an emigrant. Where did the ship take them?
To the coast of Jeddah near Mecca
To Yanbu on the route to Medina

Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Musa: «فركبنا سفينة فألقتنا سفينتنا إلى النجاشي بالحبشة فوافقنا جعفر بن أبي طالب» [We boarded a ship, which took us to the Negus in Abyssinia, where we met Jafar ibn Abi Talib].
sahaba-0083: Jabir said: The words ﴿إذ همّت طائفتان منكم أن تفشلا﴾ [When two parties among you were about to lose courage] were revealed concerning us. Who were the two parties?
Banu Abd al-Ashhal and Banu Zafar

Sahih Muslim reports from Jabir: «فينا نزلت ... بنو سلمة وبنو حارثة، وما نحب أنها لم تنزل لقول الله: والله وليهما» [It was revealed concerning us ... Banu Salama and Banu Haritha. We would not wish it had not been revealed, because Allah says: but Allāh was their ally] (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0084: The Prophet said: «خير دور الأنصار ...» [The best clans of the Ansar (Helpers) are ...]. Which clan did he name first?

Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Usayd: «خير دور الأنصار بنو النجار، ثم بنو عبد الأشهل، ثم بنو الحارث بن الخزرج، ثم بنو ساعدة» [The best clans of the Ansar (Helpers) are Banu al-Najjar, then Banu Abd al-Ashhal, then Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj, then Banu Saida].
sahaba-0085: The Prophet said: «غفار غفر الله لها، و... سالمها الله» [[The tribe of] Ghifār, Allah forgave them. [The tribe of] ... Allah had peace with them.]. Which was the second tribe?

Muslim reports from Abu Dharr: «غفار غفر الله لها، وأسلم سالمها الله» [[The tribe of] Ghifār, Allah forgave them. [The tribe of] Aslam, Allah had peace with them.] (HadeethEnc) Pronunciation: Ghifar, ghafara Allahu laha; wa-Aslam, salamaha Allah.
sahaba-0086: Umar told Adi ibn Hatim: «إن أول صدقة بيّضت وجه رسول الله ﷺ ووجوه أصحابه صدقة ...» [The first charitable payment that brought joy to the faces of the Messenger of Allah and his Companions was that of ...]. Whose payment?

Sahih Muslim states: «إن أول صدقة بيضت وجه رسول الله ﷺ ووجوه أصحابه صدقة طيئ جئت بها» [The first charitable payment that brought joy to the faces of the Messenger of Allah and his Companions was the payment from Tayy that you brought].
sahaba-0087: Al-Tufayl ibn Amr came and said that his people had disbelieved and refused Islam, asking the Prophet to pray against them. Instead, the Prophet said: «اللهم اهدِ ... وائتِ بهم» [O Allah, guide ... and bring them]. Who were his people?

Muslim reports from Abu Hurayra: «قدم الطفيل وأصحابه فقالوا: إن دوسًا قد كفرت وأبت ... فقال: اللهم اهد دوسًا وائت بهم» [Al-Tufayl and his companions came and said: Daws have disbelieved and refused ... He said: O Allah, guide Daws and bring them]. supplication pronunciation: Allahumma ihdi Dawsan wati bihim.
sahaba-0088: Abu Hurayra said he would always love a tribe because of three things he heard the Messenger of Allah say about them, including that they were «أشد أمتي على الدجال» [the fiercest of my community against al-Dajjal (the False Messiah)]. Which tribe?

Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Hurayra: «لا أزال أحب بني تميم من ثلاث ... هم أشد أمتي على الدجال» [I will always love Banu Tamim because of three things ... They are the fiercest of my community against al-Dajjal (the False Messiah)].
sahaba-0090: When asked about ﴿وآخرين منهم لما يلحقوا بهم﴾ [And [to] others of them who have not yet joined them.], the Prophet placed his hand on a Companion and said: «لو كان الإيمان عند الثريا لناله رجال من هؤلاء» [If faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these people would attain it]. Who was the Companion?

Sahih Muslim reports from Abu Hurayra: «فوضع النبي ﷺ يده على سلمان ثم قال: لو كان الإيمان عند الثريا لناله رجال من هؤلاء» [The Prophet placed his hand on Salman, then said: If faith were at the Pleiades, men from among these people would attain it] (QuranEnc).
sahaba-0091: What was the actual name of the noble Companion Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Jarrah ... al-Qurashi al-Fihri al-Makki.
sahaba-0092: Which ancestor did Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah share with the Prophet?
In his biography of Abu Ubayda, al-Dhahabi says that his lineage and the Prophet's meet at Fihr.
sahaba-0093: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam's mother was the Messenger of Allah's paternal aunt. What was her name?
Al-Dhahabi calls al-Zubayr the devoted supporter of the Messenger of Allah and the son of his paternal aunt Safiyya bint Abd al-Muttalib.
sahaba-0094: Which of the ten promised Paradise did al-Dhahabi describe as the first to draw his sword in Allah's cause?
In Siyar Alam al-Nubala, al-Zubayr is described as one of the six members of the shura (consultative council) and the first to draw his sword in Allah's cause.
sahaba-0095: What was the kunya (name beginning with Abu) of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may Allah be pleased with him?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf ... ibn Zuhra ... Abu Muhammad, one of the ten promised Paradise.
sahaba-0096: What was the name of Abu Waqqas, the father of Sad ibn Abi Waqqas?
Al-Dhahabi says: Sad ibn Abi Waqqas; Abu Waqqas's name was Malik ibn Uhayb ibn Abd Manaf ibn Zuhra.
sahaba-0097: What was the kunya (name beginning with Abu) of Sad ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as the commander Abu Ishaq al-Qurashi al-Zuhri al-Makki, one of the ten promised Paradise.
sahaba-0098: Who was the first Muslim deputy governor of Damascus after its conquest, appointed by Abu Ubayda?
Al-Dhahabi says that Said ibn Zayd witnessed the siege and conquest of Damascus, and Abu Ubayda appointed him over it, making him the first Muslim to hold the deputy governorship of Damascus.
sahaba-0099: What was the kunya (name beginning with Abu) of Said ibn Zayd, one of the ten promised Paradise?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Said ibn Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl ... Abu al-Awar al-Qurashi al-Adawi.
sahaba-0100: To which clan of Quraysh did Musab ibn Umayr belong?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Musab ibn Umayr ibn Hashim ibn Abd Manaf ibn Abd al-Dar ... al-Qurashi al-Abdari.
sahaba-0101: Which early Muslim Companion was the Prophet's milk-brother and the son of his paternal aunt Barra bint Abd al-Muttalib, and whose widow the Prophet married?
Al-Dhahabi describes Abu Salama as the Messenger of Allah's milk-brother and the son of his paternal aunt Barra bint Abd al-Muttalib.
sahaba-0102: What was the kunya (name beginning with Abu) of Uthman ibn Mazun, may Allah be pleased with him?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Uthman ibn Mazun ibn Habib ... al-Jumahi, Abu al-Saib.
sahaba-0103: Salim, the freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, originally came from which Persian city?
Al-Dhahabi quotes Musa ibn Uqba: He was Salim ibn Maqil, originally from Istakhr.
sahaba-0106: Which Companion embraced Islam and was chained by his father, then escaped, hobbling in his chains, on the day of the treaty of al-Hudaybiyya while his father was present to draw up the treaty?
Al-Dhahabi says that Abu Jandal embraced Islam, and his father imprisoned and chained him. On the day of the treaty of al-Hudaybiyya, he escaped, hobbling in his chains, while his father was present.
sahaba-0107: Who went to Badr with his father while concealing his faith, then joined the Muslims when the two armies met, fought with them, and was counted among the participants at Badr?
Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn Amr
Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq
Abd Allah ibn Suhayl ibn Amr

Al-Dhahabi says that Abd Allah ibn Suhayl went to Badr with his father while concealing his faith. When the armies met, he joined the Muslims and fought, and was counted among the participants at Badr.
sahaba-0109: Which descendant of Abd al-Muttalib supplied the Messenger of Allah with three thousand spears on the day of Hunayn?
Al-Dhahabi says that Nawfal ibn al-Harith witnessed the pledge of al-Ridwan and supplied the Messenger of Allah with three thousand spears on the day of Hunayn.
sahaba-0110: Which cousin of the Prophet was initially turned away because of the harm he had caused him, then became a good Muslim and stayed with al-Abbas beside the Prophet at Hunayn when others fled?
Al-Dhahabi says of Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith that he then became a good Muslim and, together with al-Abbas, stayed beside the Messenger of Allah at Hunayn when others fled.
sahaba-0111: How many years older was Jafar ibn Abi Talib than his brother Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both?
Al-Dhahabi says that Jafar was Ali ibn Abi Talib's brother and ten years older than him.
sahaba-0112: Of which Companion did Ibn Ishaq say that he was the first in Islam to hamstring his mount, because he hamstrung his chestnut horse on the day he was martyred?
Al-Siyar recounts that he dismounted from a chestnut horse, hamstrung it, then fought until he was killed. Ibn Ishaq said that he was the first in Islam to hamstring his mount.
sahaba-0114: Abd Allah ibn Rawaha, the poet and representative at al-Aqaba, was the maternal uncle of which well-known Companion?
Al-Dhahabi says that Abd Allah ibn Rawaha was al-Numan ibn Bashir's maternal uncle and one of the scribes of the Ansar (Helpers).
sahaba-0115: Which Companion did al-Dhahabi describe as the first to establish the practice of praying before execution, after he prayed before the polytheists crucified him in Mecca?

Khubayb's biography states that he prayed, then said: «والله لولا أن تظنوا إنما طولت جزعًا من القتل لاستكثرت من الصلاة» [By Allah, were it not that you might think I prolonged my prayer out of fear of being killed, I would have prayed more]. He was the first to establish the practice of praying before execution.
sahaba-0117: What was the name of the Companion known by the kunya (name beginning with Abu) Abu Dujana?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Abu Dujana al-Ansari, Simak ibn Kharasha ibn Lawdhan ... al-Saidi.
sahaba-0118: Who dueled with the leader of the polytheists at Badr, exchanged blows with him, was carried away by Ali and Hamza, and later died at al-Safra?
Al-Dhahabi says that Ubayda ibn al-Harith dueled with the leader of the polytheists at Badr, exchanged blows with him ... and later died at al-Safra.
sahaba-0119: Who was ten years older than the Messenger of Allah and one of the earliest Muslims from Banu al-Muttalib?
Al-Dhahabi says that Ubayda ibn al-Harith al-Muttalibi was ten years older than the Messenger of Allah.
sahaba-0120: Who was appointed governor of al-Bahrayn by the Messenger of Allah, then served there under Abu Bakr and Umar, and whose brother was associated with Bir Maymun in upper Mecca?
Al-Dhahabi says that the Messenger of Allah appointed al-Ala ibn al-Hadrami governor of al-Bahrayn, and he later governed it for Abu Bakr and Umar.
sahaba-0122: Which Companion who had fought at Badr ate some of the poisoned sheep with the Prophet at Khaybar and suffered its effects?
Al-Dhahabi says that Bishr ibn al-Bara ate some of the poisoned sheep with the Prophet at Khaybar and suffered its effects.
sahaba-0123: Whom did al-Dhahabi call the representative and chief of al-Khazraj, whose kunya (name beginning with Abu) was Abu Qays?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Sad ibn Ubada ... the eminent and noble leader Abu Qays al-Ansari al-Khazraji al-Saidi al-Madani, the representative and chief of al-Khazraj.
sahaba-0124: Which brother of Umar ibn al-Khattab was older than him, embraced Islam before him, and carried the Muslims' standard at al-Yamama?
Al-Dhahabi describes Zayd ibn al-Khattab as the brother of Amir al-Muminin (Commander of the Believers) Umar. He was older, embraced Islam before Umar, and carried the Muslims' standard at al-Yamama.
sahaba-0126: Which Companion laid out and founded Basra and was the seventh person to embrace Islam?
Al-Dhahabi says that Utba ibn Ghazwan was the seventh person to embrace Islam and the one who laid out and founded Basra.
sahaba-0127: Which Companion was known as Khatib al-Ansar (the orator of the Helpers)?
Al-Dhahabi identifies him as Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas ... Khatib al-Ansar (the orator of the Helpers).
sahaba-0128: Whose name was al-Hubab, after whom his hypocrite father took his kunya (name beginning with Abu), before the Prophet renamed him Abd Allah?
Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Ubayy
Abd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As
