He says: 'Give nasal resonance to mim, then nun, when doubled; call each a letter of evident nasal resonance.'
tajweed-0026: How many rules govern mim sakinah (unvowelled mim) when followed by an alphabet letter?
Al-Jamzuri says: 'Its rules are three for whoever masters them: concealment, assimilation, and clear pronunciation only.'
tajweed-0027: What is the rule when ba follows mim sakinah (unvowelled mim)?
Tuhfat al-Atfal says: 'The first is concealment before ba; call it labial for the reciters.'
tajweed-0028: What does Tuhfat al-Atfal call the assimilation of mim sakinah (unvowelled mim) into a following vowelled mim?
Assimilation of letters with the same articulation point
Assimilation of letters with nearby articulation points
Al-Jamzuri says: 'The second is assimilation when its like follows; call it minor assimilation, young man.'
tajweed-0029: Before which two letters must izhar shafawi (clear labial pronunciation) of mim sakinah (unvowelled mim) be especially clear?
Mim must be especially clear before waw because they share an articulation point, and before fa because their articulation points are close.
tajweed-0032: Before how many letters is mim sakinah (unvowelled mim) pronounced clearly?
Mim sakinah is pronounced clearly before the remaining twenty-six letters, excluding ba and mim.
tajweed-0033: Before how many letters is the lam of the definite article al pronounced clearly, as a lunar lam?
Al-Jamzuri says: 'Before four plus ten; learn them from ibgh hajjak wa khaf 'aqimah.'
tajweed-0038: What mark in the written mushaf (Quran codex) identifies a solar lam?
A small mim above the lam
A doubling mark on the following letter
A sukun mark on the lam
A lengthening mark above the following letter
A solar lam is indicated by a shaddah (doubling mark) on the letter after it; a lunar lam lacks this doubling mark.
tajweed-0040: In tajweed (Quranic recitation) terminology, what are mutajanisan (homorganic letters)?
Letters close in articulation point or quality
Letters sharing an articulation point but differing in quality
Letters distant in articulation point and quality
Letters sharing both articulation point and qualities
Mutajanisan share an articulation point but differ in qualities, such as dal and ta in «قد تبين» [The right course has become distinct]. Quran 2:256 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0053: How many ways may a reciter begin a surah with isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) and basmalah (saying Bismillah)?
With the isti'adhah, basmalah, and surah there are four ways: connect all three; separate all three; connect the isti'adhah to the basmalah; or connect the basmalah to the surah.
tajweed-0054: Which way of using the basmalah (saying Bismillah) between two surahs is prohibited?
Separating all parts from one another
Connecting the previous surah's ending, basmalah, and next surah
Separating the previous surah's ending and connecting the basmalah to the next surah
Connecting the basmalah to the previous surah's ending and separating it from the next
All prohibit connecting the basmalah to the first surah's ending while separating it from the next, because this suggests it belongs to the preceding surah.
tajweed-0055: In which situation is saying the isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) aloud before Quran recitation recommended?
Saying it aloud is recommended when reciting at gatherings or teaching. It is said quietly in prayer, during quiet recitation, and when alone.
tajweed-0056: How many obligatory sakt (brief pauses without breathing) locations are distinctive to Hafs through the Shatibiyyah transmission?
Hafs has four obligatory pauses: at 'iwaja in al-Kahf, marqadina in Ya-Sin, man raq in al-Qiyamah, and bal ran in al-Mutaffifin.
tajweed-0057: In which surah does Hafs make a brief pause at the word 'iwaja in «ولم يجعل له عوجا» [and has not made therein any deviance.[779]]?

Hafs's first sakt (brief pause without breathing) is at the beginning of al-Kahf: «ولم يجعل له عوجا * قيما» [and has not made therein any deviance.[779] / [He has made it] straight]. Quran 18:1-2 (QuranEnc) [779] From the truth or the straight path.
tajweed-0059: In which surah is «وقيل من راق» [And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"], where Hafs pauses at nun?
Hafs's third sakt (brief pause without breathing) is in al-Qiyamah, on the nun of man in «وقيل من راق» [And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"]. Quran 75:27 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0062: Between which two surahs is a sakt (brief pause without breathing) optional rather than obligatory for Hafs?
Hafs has two optional pauses: between al-Anfal and at-Tawbah, and between the words maliyah and halak in al-Haqqah.
tajweed-0074: What is the rule for pronominal ha between two vowelled letters when not followed by hamzah, as in «إنه كان» [Indeed He is ever]?
Link it with six counts of lengthening
Make it unvowelled both when connecting and stopping
Link it with a lengthening letter lasting two counts
When pronominal ha occurs between two vowelled letters, it is linked with a waw or ya lengthened for two counts, except in specified exceptions. Quran example: 17:30 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0075: For Hafs, what is the rule for pronominal ha after an unvowelled letter and before a vowelled letter, as in «فيه هدى» [a guidance]?
For Hafs, ha after an unvowelled letter and before a vowelled letter is not lengthened, except in the words fihi muhana. Quran example: 2:2 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0076: Madd of the pronominal ha is called silah kubra (major linking lengthening) when which letter follows it?
A vowelled letter other than hamzah
Major linking lengthening occurs when an independent hamzah follows pronominal ha, as in «ماله أخلده» [his wealth will make him immortal.]. Quran 104:3 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0077: Madd as-silah al-kubra (major pronoun-linking lengthening) follows which lengthening rule and duration?
Major pronoun-linking lengthening follows madd ja'iz munfasil (permitted separate lengthening) in its ruling.
tajweed-0079: When is ya a madd (lengthening) letter?
When doubled after a kasrah vowel
When unvowelled and preceded by a kasrah vowel
When unvowelled and preceded by a fathah vowel
Tuhfat al-Atfal says: 'Kasrah before ya and dammah before waw are conditions; fathah before alif must be observed.'
tajweed-0080: In tajweed (Quranic recitation) terminology, which are the two lin (soft) letters?
Unvowelled waw and ya after dammah and kasrah
Unvowelled waw and ya after fathah
Al-Jamzuri says: 'The soft letters are unvowelled ya and waw when an opening vowel is pronounced before each.'
tajweed-0081: Which three rulings of madd (lengthening) does al-Jamzuri mention in his Tuhfah?
Heavy pronunciation, light pronunciation, and vowel inclination
Linking, making unvowelled, and vowel reduction
He says: 'Lengthening has three enduring rulings: obligation, permissibility, and necessity.'
tajweed-0082: When is lengthening called madd wajib muttasil (obligatory connected lengthening)?
When hamzah follows the lengthening letter in the next word
When hamzah follows the lengthening letter in the same word
When an original unvowelled letter follows the lengthening letter
When hamzah precedes the lengthening letter
Tuhfat al-Atfal says: 'It is obligatory if hamzah follows a lengthening letter in one word; this is counted as connected.'
tajweed-0083: What is the duration of madd muttasil (connected lengthening) in Hafs's narration through the Shatibiyyah transmission?
Obligatory connected lengthening lasts five or four counts.
tajweed-0084: Why is madd muttasil (connected lengthening) called obligatory?
Because its cause is an unvowelled letter retained both when connecting and stopping
Because it occurs only at a verse ending
Because reciters unanimously require lengthening it
Because all reciters lengthen it for six counts
It is obligatory because reciters unanimously require lengthening it, although they differ on its duration. None transmitted shortening it.
tajweed-0085: When is lengthening called madd badal (substitution lengthening)?
When hamzah precedes the lengthening letter
When hamzah follows the lengthening letter in the same word
When a doubled letter follows the lengthening letter
When a temporarily unvowelled letter follows the lengthening letter
Tuhfat al-Atfal says: 'Or hamzah precedes the lengthening letter: this is substitution, as in amanu and imana.'
tajweed-0086: What is the duration of madd badal (substitution lengthening) in Hafs's narration?
Substitution lengthening, as in Adam, utu, and imana, lasts two counts, like natural lengthening.
tajweed-0088: Which durations are permitted for madd 'arid lis-sukun (lengthening caused by a temporary unvowelled ending) when stopping?
If stopping causes a letter after a lengthening letter to become unvowelled, the reciter has three options: short, medium, and full lengthening.
tajweed-0090: When is a lin (soft) letter lengthened, as in «خوف» [fear] and «البيت» [the House]?
When connecting the word to what follows

The two soft letters are not lengthened in connected recitation. When stopping, their ruling follows madd 'arid lis-sukun (lengthening due to a temporary unvowelled ending). Quran word examples: 106:4 and 2:125 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0094: What is the duration of all four kinds of madd lazim (necessary lengthening)?
All reciters require six counts for every kind of necessary lengthening.
tajweed-0097: How many disconnected letters at surah openings are collected in the mnemonic silhu suhayran man qata'ak?
Al-Jamzuri says: 'The fourteen opening letters are collected in silhu suhayran man qata'ak, as is well known.'
tajweed-0099: According to Ibn al-Jazari's chosen position, how many articulation points do the letters have?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'The letters' articulation points are seventeen, according to the choice of one who has examined them.'
tajweed-0100: Why did Sibawayh and his followers count sixteen articulation points?
They excluded the nasal cavity from the articulation points
They assigned the cavity alif and hamzah to one articulation point
They combined the lips and nasal cavity as one articulation point
They assigned lam, nun, and ra to one articulation point
Sibawayh and his followers counted sixteen because they assigned the cavity alif and hamzah to one point. Al-Farra assigned lam, nun, and ra to one point.
tajweed-0101: How many general regions contain the letters' articulation points?
There are five regions: the oral cavity, throat, tongue, lips, and nasal cavity.
tajweed-0102: Which letters are articulated from the cavity?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'The cavity alif and its two sisters are lengthening letters whose sound ends in the air.'
tajweed-0103: Which two letters come from the deepest part of the throat?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Then, from the deepest throat: hamzah and ha.'
tajweed-0104: Where are the undotted letters 'ayn and ha articulated?
The part of the throat nearest the mouth
The deepest part of the throat
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Then, from its middle: 'ayn and ha.'
tajweed-0105: Which two letters are articulated in the upper throat, nearest the mouth?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Its nearest part: ghayn and kha.'
tajweed-0106: The tongue's side against the upper molars
The back of the tongue against the corresponding upper palate
The middle of the tongue against the middle of the upper palate
The tongue tip against the incisor roots
Qaf comes from the back of the tongue, toward the throat, against the back of the upper palate. Kaf's articulation point follows it.
tajweed-0107: Where are jim, shin, and non-lengthening ya articulated?
The tongue's side against the molars
The middle of the tongue against the middle of the upper palate
The tongue tip against the roots of the upper incisors
The back of the tongue against the back of the palate
Jim, shin, and ya come from the middle of the tongue against the middle of the upper palate.
tajweed-0108: Which letter is articulated from either side of the tongue against the adjoining upper molars?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Dad comes from its side beside the molars, on its left or right.'
tajweed-0109: How do tajweed (Quranic recitation) scholars describe dad's articulation point?
The first point from the chest
Dad comes from the tongue's side against the adjoining molars. Its articulation point is the most difficult.
tajweed-0110: Which letter has the broadest articulation point?
Lam's point is the front edge of the tongue against the corresponding teeth. It is the broadest articulation point.
tajweed-0111: Where are ta (emphatic), dal, and ta (non-emphatic) articulated?
The tongue tip against the tips of the upper incisors
The tongue tip against the roots of the upper incisors
The inside of the lower lip against the incisors
The middle of the tongue against the upper palate
Ta (emphatic), dal, and ta (non-emphatic) come from the upper surface of the tongue tip pressed against the roots of the upper incisors.
tajweed-0112: Where are za (emphatic interdental), dhal, and tha articulated?
The tongue's side against the molars
The tongue tip against the tips of the upper incisors
The tongue tip against the roots of the upper incisors
They come from the upper surface of the tongue tip pressed against the tips of the upper incisors: za with tongue elevation, and dhal and tha without it.
tajweed-0113: Which letter is articulated from the inside of the lower lip against the tips of the upper incisors?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'From the inside of the lip comes fa, against the projecting tips of the incisors.'
tajweed-0114: Which letters are articulated with both lips?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'For the two lips: waw, ba, mim.'
tajweed-0115: According to Ibn al-Jazari, where does ghunnah (nasal resonance) originate?
The deepest part of the throat
He says in al-Muqaddimah: 'Nasal resonance has its articulation point in the nasal cavity.'
tajweed-0116: Qaf and kaf are called uvular letters in reference to what?
They are called uvular because their articulation points are near the uvula.
tajweed-0117: Which letters are called shajriyyah (mid-mouth letters)?
The three shajriyyah letters are jim, shin, and ya, named for their origin in the middle opening of the mouth.
tajweed-0118: Which are the asaliyyah letters, named after the tongue's tapered tip?
The three asaliyyah letters are sad, sin, and zay, named after their articulation point at the tongue's tapered tip.
tajweed-0119: What are ta (emphatic), dal, and ta (non-emphatic) called?
They are called nit'iyyah (anterior-palate letters) in reference to the front of the upper palate.
tajweed-0120: Which are the lithawiyyah (gum letters), named for the proximity of their articulation point to the gums?
The three lithawiyyah letters are za, dhal, and tha.
tajweed-0121: What are lam, ra, and nun called in tajweed (Quranic recitation) books?
They are called dhalaqiyyah or dhawlaqiyyah, in reference to the tongue tip.
tajweed-0122: How many central incisors, frequently mentioned when discussing articulation points, are in the human mouth?
There are four central incisors, two in each jaw. Next come the lateral incisors, then the canines.
tajweed-0123: What do tajweed (Quranic recitation) scholars mean by nawajidh?
The first molars after the canines
The teeth next to the central incisors
The nawajidh are the rearmost molars. There are four, two in each jaw.
tajweed-0124: How many letter qualities did Ibn al-Jazari limit himself to in his versified al-Muqaddimah?
Ibn al-Jazari mentioned thirty-four qualities in at-Tamhid, but limited himself to seventeen in al-Muqaddimah.
tajweed-0129: Which four letters have itbaq (tongue-to-palate compression)?
Sad, dad, ta (emphatic), and za (emphatic interdental)
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Sad, dad, ta, and za are compressed letters.'
tajweed-0131: Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Their whistling letters are sad, zay, and sin.'
tajweed-0133: Which single letter has the quality of takrir (repetition)?
Repetition belongs to one letter, ra. Excessive repetition must be avoided.
tajweed-0134: Which letter uniquely has tafashshi (spreading), the spread of air in the mouth during pronunciation?
Tafashshi literally means spreading and is a quality of shin.
tajweed-0135: Istitalah belongs to the dotted letter dad. It is the extension of sound along its articulation point, from the beginning to the end of the tongue's side.
tajweed-0136: Which two letters have inhiraf (deviation) in al-Muqaddimah al-Jazariyyah?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Deviation is established in lam and ra.'
tajweed-0137: Which is the strongest letter overall, combining six strong qualities and no weak quality?
The strongest letter overall is undotted ta (emphatic), because it combines six strong qualities and none of the weak qualities.
tajweed-0138: Which qualities distinguish ta (emphatic) from ta (non-emphatic), despite their shared articulation point?
Ta (emphatic) has itbaq (tongue-to-palate compression) and isti'la (tongue elevation), unlike ta (non-emphatic). They also differ in breath restraint, breath flow, and echoing.
tajweed-0139: Which two letters with shiddah (complete sound blockage) are also considered mahmus (having breath flow)?
Most letters with complete sound blockage have restrained breath, except ta (non-emphatic) and kaf, which are considered letters with breath flow.
tajweed-0140: In tajweed (Quranic recitation) terminology, what does hams mean?
Breath flowing during pronunciation of a letter
The tongue rising toward the upper palate
Breath being restrained during pronunciation of a letter
Sound being blocked at the articulation point
Hams is breath flow at a letter's articulation point during pronunciation, due to weak pressure there. Its opposite is jahr (breath restraint).
tajweed-0141: What is isti'la (tongue elevation) in tajweed (Quranic recitation)?
Raising most of the tongue during pronunciation
Sound flowing with the letter due to weak pressure
Lowering the tongue away from the palate during pronunciation
A letter emerging easily from the tongue tip
Isti'la is raising a large part or most of the tongue during pronunciation. Its letters are collected in khuss daghtin qiz.
tajweed-0142: Qalqalah literally means movement and vibration. Technically, it is releasing the articulation point and sound with movement after their compression.
tajweed-0144: Ibn al-Jazari says, 'Pronounce the lowered letters lightly.' What ruling does he mean for letters of istifal (tongue lowering)?

The basic rule for letters of istifal is tarqiq (light pronunciation). Exceptions are ra and the lam of Allah's name in cases requiring heavy pronunciation. Alif follows the preceding letter. Ibn al-Jazari then warns against pronouncing alif heavily.
tajweed-0145: When is a vowelled ra pronounced lightly?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Pronounce ra lightly when it carries kasrah.'
tajweed-0149: In how many Quranic words is an unvowelled ra preceded by an original kasrah and followed in the same word by a tongue-elevation letter carrying fathah?
There are five such words: qirtas, firqah, irsada, mirsada, and labil-mirsad.
tajweed-0152: When is the lam of Allah's name pronounced heavily?
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Pronounce the lam in Allah's name heavily after fathah or dammah, as in 'Abdullah.'
tajweed-0154: Which madd (lengthening) is strongest in Shaykh Ibrahim as-Samanudi's versified hierarchy?
Lengthening due to a temporary unvowelled ending
As-Samanudi says: 'The strongest lengthening is necessary, then connected, then temporary, then separate, then substitution.'
tajweed-0155: Which comes last when types of madd (lengthening) are ranked from strongest to weakest?
Lengthening due to a temporary unvowelled ending
Substitution comes last because its cause precedes it, and because its lengthening letter usually replaces a hamzah.
tajweed-0156: If two causes for madd (lengthening) coincide, one strong and one weak, what should the reciter do?
Apply the stronger and disregard the weaker
Apply the weaker and disregard the stronger
Combine them by increasing the lengthening
When two lengthening causes coincide, the stronger is applied and the weaker disregarded. As-Samanudi says: 'Then the stronger of the two causes acts alone.'
tajweed-0157: When two separate lengthenings occur, as in «بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك» [what has been revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], and what was revealed before you], what must the reciter do?
Shorten the first and lengthen the second
Lengthen the first and shorten the second
Make the second longer than the first
When two lengthenings of the same type occur, their durations must be equal. Ibn al-Jazari says: 'A word is treated like its counterpart.' Quran 2:4 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0158: What is the basic rule when stopping at word endings?
Pure sukun (absence of a vowel) has no vowel sound. It is the basic stopping method because it is easier and allows a fuller rest.
tajweed-0159: What is rawm (vowel reduction) when stopping?
Rounding the lips silently after removing the vowel
Pronouncing part of the vowel with a faint sound
Some define it as pronouncing one-third of the vowel so that someone nearby can hear it but someone far away cannot.
tajweed-0160: What is meant by ishmaam (silent lip-rounding) when stopping?
Pronouncing one-third of a vowel faintly
Rounding the lips silently immediately after making the letter unvowelled
Ishmaam is rounding the lips immediately after making the letter unvowelled, without delay, while leaving a gap for breath to escape.
tajweed-0161: Ishmaam (silent lip-rounding) when stopping is possible only when the word ends in what?
An unvowelled letter during connected recitation
A dammah vowel or a nominative ending
A kasrah vowel or a genitive ending
A fathah vowel or an accusative ending
Ishmaam when stopping applies only to dammah and nominative endings.
tajweed-0163: Which stopping methods are permitted for a word ending in kasrah during connected recitation, such as «الرحيم» [the Especially Merciful]?
Absence of a vowel and silent lip-rounding
Pure absence of a vowel only
Absence of a vowel and a reduced vowel

A word with final kasrah during connected recitation may be stopped on using sukun (absence of a vowel) or rawm (a reduced vowel) only. Ishmaam (silent lip-rounding) is not permitted. Quran word example: 1:3 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0164: How does one stop at a word whose final vowel is fathah without nunation, such as «الذين» [Who]?
With pure absence of a vowel only
With a reduced vowel and silent lip-rounding
With absence of a vowel and a reduced vowel
With absence of a vowel and silent lip-rounding

A word with final fathah without nunation during connected recitation allows neither rawm (a reduced vowel) nor ishmaam (silent lip-rounding), because fathah is light. Quran word example: 2:3 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0165: Why are rawm (a reduced vowel) and ishmaam (silent lip-rounding) excluded when a feminine ending is stopped on as ha, as in «الجنة» [Paradise]?
It can only be stopped on with ta
Ha is an unvowelled throat letter
The word can only be accusative
Ha replaces the ta that carried the vowel
The feminine ha replaces ta, and ta is absent when stopping. This differs from words stopped on with ta in accordance with their written form. Quran word example: 2:35 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0166: How does one stop on plural mim whose vowel is added during connected recitation to resolve adjacent unvowelled letters, as in «وأنتم الأعلون» [and you will be superior]?
With a reduced vowel or silent lip-rounding
With pure absence of a vowel

Neither rawm (a reduced vowel) nor ishmaam (silent lip-rounding) applies to a temporary vowel added to resolve adjacent unvowelled letters, including plural mim. The vowel disappears when its cause disappears on stopping. Quran 3:139 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0167: When two unvowelled letters meet across two words, which vowel does Hafs normally give the first?
Hafs normally uses kasrah to resolve two adjacent unvowelled letters, as in «قل ادعوا الله» [Say, "Call upon Allāh]. Quran 17:110 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0168: Why is the nun of the preposition min given fathah to resolve adjacent unvowelled letters, as in «من الشاهدين» [among the witnesses]?
Because a lunar lam follows it
To avoid two successive kasrah vowels in a frequently used expression
Because fathah is nun's original vowel
Because nun is a nasal-resonance letter
The nun of the preposition min is given fathah before an unvowelled lam to avoid two successive kasrah vowels in a frequently used expression. Quran example: 3:81 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0172: How are two adjacent unvowelled letters within one word handled, both in connected recitation and when stopping, as in «الصاخة» [the Deafening Blast[1862]]?
Pause at the first unvowelled letter
Give the first unvowelled letter kasrah

The two adjacent unvowelled letters must be resolved by full lengthening for six counts. This is madd lazim (necessary lengthening). Quran 80:33 (QuranEnc) [1862] The piercing blast of the Horn which signals resurrection. Aṣ-Ṣākhkhah is also a name for the Day of Resurrection.
tajweed-0174: What is the slight lengthening used to separate two waw letters in «آمنوا وعملوا» [believe and do righteous deeds] to avoid assimilation?
Enabling lengthening is a slight lengthening of two counts used to separate two waw letters or two ya letters to avoid assimilation or omission. Quran example: 2:25 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0175: Why is lengthening the alif substituted for connecting hamzah in «آلذكرين» [Is it the two males] called madd al-farq (distinguishing lengthening)?
It distinguishes connected recitation from stopping
It distinguishes a question from a statement

Distinguishing lengthening replaces connecting hamzah in al-dhakarayn, Allahu when interrogative, and al-ana. It is named for distinguishing a question from a statement. Quran word example: 6:143 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0176: Through which transmission alone may Hafs use madd at-ta'zim (magnifying lengthening), as in «لا إله إلا أنت» [There is no deity except You]?
For those who shorten separate lengthening, magnifying lengthening is permitted for Hafs only through Tayyibat an-Nashr. Quran excerpt: 21:87 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0179: Why is madd tabi'i (natural lengthening) given this name?
A person with sound natural disposition neither shortens nor exceeds it
Its cause is a following hamzah or unvowelled letter
It lasts six counts for every reciter
It is called natural because a person with sound natural disposition neither reduces nor exceeds its proper duration of two counts.
tajweed-0180: What is another name for madd tabi'i (natural lengthening)?
Natural lengthening is also called primary lengthening and lengthening of the form, because it is inherent in the letter.
tajweed-0181: What are the two phonetic causes of madd far'i (secondary lengthening)?
An unvowelled letter and nasal resonance
There are two phonetic causes of lengthening: hamzah and an unvowelled letter. Each includes different types.
tajweed-0182: In Quran reciters' terminology, what is waqf (stopping)?
Making a word's final letter unvowelled without interrupting the sound
Interrupting the sound briefly without breathing
Interrupting the sound long enough to breathe, intending to resume recitation
Waqf interrupts the sound at a word for a period in which one normally breathes, with the intention of resuming recitation.
tajweed-0183: In Quran reciters' terminology, what is sakt (pausing)?
Interrupting the sound for less time than a stop, without breathing
Stopping at a verse ending while breathing
Interrupting the sound for a long time while breathing
Sakt interrupts the sound for less time than a waqf (stop), without breathing. Hafs's pause is brief.
tajweed-0184: What do tajweed (Quranic recitation) scholars mean by qat' (ending recitation)?
Stopping at a word with a complete meaning
Separating two surahs with the basmalah
Qat' means leaving and finishing recitation, including turning to an unrelated activity.
tajweed-0185: What should someone do when returning to recitation after ending it?
Repeat the surah from its beginning
After ending recitation, one should seek refuge in Allah when resuming. Seeking refuge is not required after an ordinary stop.
tajweed-0187: A waqf tamm (complete stop) occurs at speech that has what relationship to what follows?
A semantic relationship but no grammatical relationship
A grammatical and semantic relationship, despite conveying a meaning
Neither a grammatical nor a semantic relationship
A complete stop has no grammatical or semantic relationship between what precedes and what follows.
tajweed-0188: A waqf kafi (sufficient stop) occurs where the meaning is complete and what further condition holds?
Its meaning is incomplete without what follows
It has neither a grammatical nor a semantic relationship to what follows
It has a semantic but no grammatical relationship to what follows
It has both a grammatical and a semantic relationship to what follows
A sufficient stop occurs where the meaning is complete and there is a semantic, but no grammatical, relationship to what follows.
tajweed-0189: What kind of stop is stopping after «الحمد لله» [[All] praise is [due] to Allāh] before «رب العالمين» [Lord[4] of the worlds]?

Stopping after «الحمد لله» [[All] praise is [due] to Allāh] is hasan (good), because it is a meaningful sentence. However, beginning with «رب العالمين» [Lord[4] of the worlds] is unsuitable because it is a description connected to what precedes. Quran 1:2 (QuranEnc) [4] When referring to Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) , the Arabic term "rabb" (translated as "Lord") includes all of the following meanings: "owner, master, ruler, controller, sustainer, provider, guardian and caretaker."
tajweed-0190: What kind of stop is stopping at al-muflihun in «وأولئك هم المفلحون» [and it is those who are the successful] near the beginning of al-Baqarah?
This ends the discussion of believers. What follows begins a new discussion of disbelievers, so the stop is tamm (complete). Quran 2:5 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0195: What do repeated groups of three dots at two nearby locations in a verse indicate?
Three dots indicate waqf al-muraqabah or al-mu'anaqah (paired alternative stops): one stops at one of the two locations, but not both.
tajweed-0197: What kind of stop is stopping at 'anhum in «فتول عنهم يوم يدع الداع» [So leave them, [O Muḥammad]. The Day the Caller[1579] calls]?

Stopping at 'anhum is obligatory, because connecting the words suggests that the adverb yawm modifies the imperative fatawalla, distorting the meaning. Quran 54:6 (QuranEnc) [1579] Said to be an angel announcing the account and judgement.
tajweed-0198: Ibn al-Jazari says, 'No stop in the Quran is obligatory or forbidden except for a reason.' What does he mean?
No stop is obligatory or forbidden unless a reason requires it
Stopping is obligatory at every verse ending
Stopping is obligatory at every mushaf sign
Stopping within verses is categorically forbidden
The verse establishes that no Quranic stop is obligatory such that omitting it is sinful, or forbidden such that making it is sinful, unless there is a reason requiring that ruling.
tajweed-0199: When beginning a verb, when is hamzat al-wasl (connecting hamzah) pronounced with dammah?
When the verb's third letter carries fathah
When the verb's third letter carries an inherent dammah
When the verb's first letter carries dammah
When the verb's third letter carries kasrah
Ibn al-Jazari says: 'Begin a verb's connecting hamzah with dammah if the verb's third letter has dammah.'
tajweed-0201: With which vowel does one begin a connecting hamzah before the lam of the definite article, as in «الحمد» [[All] praise]?
Connecting hamzah before the lam of the definite article is always begun with fathah. Quran word example: 1:2 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0202: How many Quranic nouns have a connecting hamzah conventionally pronounced with kasrah when starting, such as ibn, ibnah, and imru'?
There are seven words: ibn, ibnah, imru', ithnan, imra'ah, ism, and ithnatan.
tajweed-0204: If interrogative hamzah precedes a verb's connecting hamzah, as in «أصطفى البنات» [Has He chosen daughters], what happens to the connecting hamzah?
It becomes an alif with full lengthening
It is omitted, leaving interrogative hamzah with fathah
It is softened between hamzah and alif
It is retained in pronunciation alongside interrogative hamzah
When interrogative hamzah precedes connecting hamzah, connecting hamzah is omitted and interrogative hamzah carries fathah. Quran 37:153 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0207: From which teacher, whom he described as 'possessing perfection,' did al-Jamzuri take the content of his poem?
Al-Jamzuri says: 'I named it Tuhfat al-Atfal, from our teacher al-Mihi, possessing perfection.'
tajweed-0213: Which is Ibn al-Jazari's most famous work on Quranic readings, including the seven readings and adding three?
Ibn al-Jazari wrote many books. His most famous is An-Nashr fi al-Qira'at al-'Ashr, including the seven readings and adding those of Abu Ja'far, Ya'qub, and Khalaf.
tajweed-0214: What title did its author give the poem known as ash-Shatibiyyah?
Ash-Shatibiyyah is a poem rhyming in lam that ash-Shatibi titled Hirz al-Amani wa Wajh at-Tahani, versifying the seven readings.
tajweed-0215: How many verses did Imam ash-Shatibi use to versify the seven readings in ash-Shatibiyyah?
Ash-Shatibi versified the seven mass-transmitted readings in one thousand and seventy-three verses.
tajweed-0217: Which imam is called 'the one who established the seven' because he was the first to limit a book to the seven reciters?
Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid was the first to select the seven reciters and limit his book to them, in the fourth century. He is therefore called the one who established the seven.
tajweed-0218: Who wrote At-Taysir fi al-Qira'at as-Sab', which became a main reference for later reciters?
Abu 'Amr 'Uthman ibn Sa'id ad-Dani, author of At-Taysir, became renowned in the fifth century. He died in 444 AH.
tajweed-0219: Who wrote ar-Ri'ayah, a famous work devoted to letter articulation points and qualities?
Among the most famous books devoted to articulation points and qualities is ar-Ri'ayah by Makki ibn Abi Talib al-Qaysi al-Qayrawani.
tajweed-0220: Whose poem is considered the earliest versified text on tajweed (Quranic recitation)?
Versification on tajweed began with the poem of Abu Muzahim al-Khaqani, who died in 325 AH. It is the earliest versified text on the subject.
tajweed-0225: 'Asim learned from Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami the reading he taught Hafs. To which Companion does its transmission chain lead?
'Asim told Hafs: 'I taught you what Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami taught me from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.'
tajweed-0226: The two most famous transmitters from Imam 'Asim are Hafs ibn Sulayman and whom?
Hafs ibn Sulayman and Abu Bakr Shu'bah ibn 'Ayyash transmitted 'Asim's reading. They are his most famous transmitters.
tajweed-0228: What did Yahya ibn Ma'in say about Hafs ibn Sulayman's transmission?
It is the most famous transmission of the people of Madinah
It is the authentic transmission related from 'Asim
It is a transmission that may not be recited in prayer
It is the earliest transmission from Nafi'
Yahya ibn Ma'in said: 'The authentic transmission related from 'Asim is that of Hafs ibn Sulayman.'
tajweed-0229: In which city was 'Asim ibn Abi an-Najud the leading Quran-reading teacher?
'Asim ibn Abi an-Najud al-Asadi, their freedman, was Kufa's leading Quran-reading teacher and one of the Successors.
tajweed-0231: When Imam Ahmad was asked which readings he preferred, he said the reading of the people of Madinah; if unavailable, whose reading?
'Abdullah ibn Ahmad related that his father said: 'The reading of the people of Madinah; if unavailable, then 'Asim's reading.'
tajweed-0232: A valid Quranic reading has three pillars: conformity to Arabic in at least one respect, conformity to the 'Uthmanic script even by possibility, and what?
A large number of people reciting it
Its inclusion in the two Sahih collections

The third pillar is an authentic chain transmitted through numerous independent routes from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Ibn al-Jazari points to it: 'And its chain is authentic: that is the Quran.'
tajweed-0233: If one of the three pillars of a valid reading is absent, how is the reading described?
If one of the three pillars is absent, the reading is shadhdh (anomalous), and reciting it is not permitted.
tajweed-0234: What term refers to a transmission attributed to someone conveying from a narrator, however far down the chain, as in 'Warsh's narration through al-Azraq'?
A tariq is attributed to someone conveying from the narrator, however far down the chain. A riwayah is attributed to the imam's narrator, and a qira'ah to the imam.
tajweed-0235: What is the technical term for a choice attributed to one of the ten imams, as in ''Asim's reading'?
Qira'ah means a choice in the manner of reciting attributed to one of the ten imams.
tajweed-0236: What is the intermediate recitation speed between tahqiq (deliberate recitation) and hadr (rapid recitation)?
Tadwir is an intermediate pace between tahqiq and hadr.
tajweed-0237: In Quran reciters' terminology, what is hadr?
Rapid, flowing recitation while observing the rules
A middle pace between slow and fast
Deliberate recitation with fully sustained lengthening
Hadr is rapid, flowing recitation while observing tajweed (Quranic recitation) rules.
tajweed-0238: Which recitation pace is recommended for teaching because it is more deliberate and composed?
Some tajweed (Quranic recitation) scholars mention tahqiq, a pace more deliberate than tartil (measured recitation), recommended for teaching.
tajweed-0239: What is lahn jali (obvious recitation error)?
An error when stopping at verse endings
An error impairing full mastery that only experts recognize
An error affecting word structure that reciters and ordinary people recognize
An error in precise lengthening durations
An obvious error affects a word's structure in a plainly apparent way recognized by both recitation scholars and ordinary people.
tajweed-0242: Tajweed literally means improvement. Technically, it means giving each letter its inherent and resulting due qualities.
tajweed-0243: For the Muslim community, what is the ruling on learning theoretical tajweed (Quranic recitation) rules?
Theoretical knowledge of tajweed rules is fard kifayah (a communal obligation). Correct Quranic pronunciation is obligatory for every reciter.
tajweed-0249: How does Hafs stop on a feminine ending written as open ta in the mushaf (Quran codex), as in «رحمت الله» [the mercy of Allāh]?
With ha, following the underlying rule
With ta, following the written form
Reciters differ in stopping on these words. Hafs is among those who stop with open ta in accordance with the written form. Quran example: 7:56 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0250: How does one stop on a verb's unvowelled feminine ta, as in «وقالت» [She said] and «ودت» [wish]?
There is agreement that a verb's feminine ta is written as open ta, and it can only be stopped on with ta. Quran word examples: 27:44 and 3:69 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0257: For which two letters does Ibn al-Jazari urge care to preserve shiddah (complete sound blockage) and jahr (breath restraint)?
After giving examples of ba, he says: 'Take care to preserve complete sound blockage and breath restraint in it and in jim, as in hubb, as-sabr, rabwah, and ujtuththat.'
tajweed-0276: What determines whether a doubled ra is pronounced heavily or lightly?
The rule for the first, unvowelled ra
The rule for the second, vowelled ra
A doubled ra consists of two ra letters, the first unvowelled and the second vowelled. Its ruling follows the second ra.
tajweed-0277: Ibn al-Jazari says of ra, 'Conceal its repetition when doubled.' What does he mean?
Make the doubled ra's repetition evident
Ra has the quality of takrir (repetition), and concealing that repetition is especially important when it is doubled.
tajweed-0279: What does Ibn al-Jazari emphasize by saying, 'And the hamzah of al-hamd, a'udhu, ihdina, Allah'?
Taking care to pronounce hamzah lightly
Softening hamzah to an intermediate sound
This follows his words, 'Pronounce the lowered letters lightly,' and emphasizes tarqiq (light pronunciation) of hamzah in these words.
tajweed-0280: The lam in «سلطان» [authorization] is an original part of the noun. What is its rule?
A noun's lam forms part of its structure and is always pronounced clearly, as in «ألسنتكم» [your languages] and «سلطان» [authorization]. Quran word examples: 30:22 and 4:91 (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0281: What is the rule for imperative lam before a present-tense verb, as in «وليكتب» [And let a scribe write]?
Imperative lam is added to the word's structure and precedes a present-tense verb. It is always pronounced clearly. Quran example: 2:282.' (QuranEnc)
tajweed-0285: Which two qualities do all qalqalah (echoing) letters share?
Complete sound blockage and breath restraint
All echoing letters have shiddah (complete sound blockage) and jahr (breath restraint), because the sound and breath must be restrained before the echoing release.
tajweed-0286: In an unvowelled letter within a word
In an unvowelled letter at which one stops
Echoing is strongest in an unvowelled letter when stopping on it. In a vowelled letter, it is concealed within the vowel.
tajweed-0287: Which two letters have ghunnah (nasal resonance)?
Nasal resonance belongs to nun and mim. It becomes evident in assimilation, concealment, and doubling.
tajweed-0289: When beginning Surah Bara'ah after the isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah), two options are allowed. What do both omit?
One beginning Bara'ah may either stop after seeking refuge or connect it to the surah's opening. Both options omit the basmalah (saying Bismillah).
tajweed-0291: Isti'adhah literally means seeking refuge, protection, and shelter. Technically, it is an expression by which one seeks refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed.
tajweed-0292: Is the formula of isti'adhah (seeking refuge), 'I seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed,' part of the Quran?
It is a verse at the beginning of every surah
It is unanimously considered outside the Quran
It is a verse from an-Nas
It is an independent verse of al-Fatihah
Seeking refuge is unanimously considered outside the Quran. Its wording is declarative, while its meaning performs a request. Pronunciation: A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim.
tajweed-0293: If a reciter briefly interrupts recitation because of sneezing or clearing the throat, then continues, what should happen?
Repeat the surah from the beginning
If recitation is interrupted by an incidental reason such as sneezing, clearing the throat, or speech connected to the recitation's benefit, the isti'adhah (seeking refuge in Allah) is not repeated.
tajweed-0297: Why is ghunnah (nasal resonance) omitted when nun sakinah (unvowelled nun) is assimilated into lam or ra?
Nasal resonance is omitted in this category to maximize ease, because retaining it makes pronunciation heavier.
tajweed-0298: According to tajweed (Quranic recitation) scholars, what is the benefit of idgham (assimilation)?
Assimilation eases pronunciation because the assimilated letter and the following letter are pronounced as one doubled letter.
tajweed-0299: Izhar halqi (clear throat-letter pronunciation) has three degrees. Before which two letters is it strongest?
Its degrees are strongest before hamzah and ha, intermediate before 'ayn and ha (voiceless pharyngeal), and weakest before ghayn and kha.
tajweed-0300: Before which letters is ikhfa (concealment) strongest and closest to assimilation?
Concealment is strongest before ta (emphatic), dal, and ta (non-emphatic), because nun's articulation point is close to theirs.
tajweed-0301: Before which two letters is ikhfa (concealment) weakest and closest to clear pronunciation?
Concealment is weakest before qaf and kaf because nun's articulation point is far from theirs.
tajweed-0302: What is one difference between ikhfa (concealment) and idgham (assimilation)?
Concealment has no nasal resonance, unlike assimilation
Concealment occurs only across two words
Concealment involves no doubling, unlike assimilation
Assimilation occurs only within one word
Concealment never involves doubling, unlike assimilation. A letter is concealed before another letter, but assimilated into another letter.
tajweed-0304: In which case is ghunnah (nasal resonance) fullest?
A doubled or fully assimilated letter

The commonly stated degrees are: fullest in doubled and fully assimilated letters, then incompletely assimilated letters, then concealed letters, then clearly pronounced unvowelled letters, then vowelled letters.
tajweed-0305: What is the technical definition of ghunnah (nasal resonance)?
A pleasant sound inherent in nun and mim
A quality of letters with complete sound blockage and breath restraint
Ghunnah is a pleasant sound inherent in nun and mim, in whose production the tongue plays no role.
asmaa-husna-0001: Which two names of Allah conclude the command in al-A'raf and Fussilat to seek refuge from Satan's incitement?

Allah says: «وَإِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ نَزْغٌ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ» [And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in Allāh. Indeed, He is Hearing and Knowing.]. Satan's incitement consists of whispers in the heart, to which knowledge pertains. Quran 7:200 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0002: In Ghafir, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is commanded to seek refuge from those who dispute Allah's signs without authority. Which two names conclude the verse?

«فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ» [So seek refuge in Allāh. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.]. These people's actions can be seen with the eyes. Quran 40:56 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0003: In ash-Shu'ara, accounts of the prophets and their peoples repeatedly end with «وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ ...» [And indeed, your Lord - He is ...]. What completes the verse?

«وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ» [And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.]. He supported His messengers through His mercy and took vengeance on their enemies through His might. Quran 26:9 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0004: In the context of breaking dawn, the sun's course, and adorning the nearest heaven with lamps, verses end with «ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ...» [That is the determination of ...]. Which two names follow?

«ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ الْعَزِيزِ الْعَلِيمِ» [That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.] occurs in al-An'am, Ya-Sin, and Fussilat. Precise determination proceeds from Allah's might and knowledge. Quoted English: Quran 6:96 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0005: Allah ends the verse about multiplying expenditure like a grain producing seven spikes with «وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ...» [And Allāh multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allāh is ...]. Which two names follow?

«وَاللَّهُ يُضَاعِفُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ» [And Allāh multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing.]. His giving is vast, and He knows who deserves multiplication. Quran 2:261 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0006: Which two names conclude «فَتَلَقَّى آدَمُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ كَلِمَاتٍ فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ ...» [Then Adam received from his Lord [some] words,[22] and He accepted his repentance. ...]?

«فَتَابَ عَلَيْهِ إِنَّهُ هُوَ التَّوَّابُ الرَّحِيمُ» [and He accepted his repentance. Indeed, it is He who is the Accepting of Repentance,[23] the Merciful.]. Many verses conclude with these two names in contexts of repentance and mercy. Quran 2:37 (QuranEnc) [22] Allāh taught Adam words of repentance that would be acceptable to Him. [23] Literally, He who perpetually returns, i.e., reminding and enabling His servant to repent from sins and then forgiving him. Thus, He is also the constant motivator of the repentance He accepts.
asmaa-husna-0007: «يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ أَنْتُمُ الْفُقَرَاءُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ هُوَ ...» [O mankind, you are those in need of Allāh, while Allāh is ...]. Which two names conclude the verse?
The pairing al-Ghani, al-Hamid recurs in the Quran, including this verse in Fatir. He deserves praise for His freedom from need, His praiseworthiness, and their combination. Quran 35:15.' (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0008: Al-Badr explains that Allah's names are proper names and descriptions. In referring to one essence, Allah's essence, how are they related?
Identical in wording but not meaning
In the first respect, referring to the essence, they are synonymous. In the second respect, each name's particular meaning, they are distinct.
asmaa-husna-0009: Allah named Himself al-Qawi and described Himself as possessing strength: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ ...» [Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider,[1548] ...]. Which name concludes the verse?

The verse in adh-Dhariyat is «إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ» [Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider,[1548] the firm possessor of strength.]. Quran 51:58 (QuranEnc) [1548] Providing everything required by His creations during their decreed existence. His provision includes guidance.
asmaa-husna-0010: Allah declares Himself free of lughub (weariness): «وَمَا مَسَّنَا مِنْ لُغُوبٍ» [and there touched Us no weariness.]. Weariness contradicts the perfection indicated by which name?

Al-Badr explains that Allah named Himself al-Qawi and declared Himself free of weariness or being burdened by preserving the heavens and earth, because these contradict His perfect strength. Quran 50:38 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0011: «وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا» [And never is your Lord forgetful]. Allah denies forgetfulness of Himself because it contradicts the perfection indicated by which name?
Allah named Himself al-'Alim and declared Himself free of inattention and forgetfulness, because they contradict His perfect knowledge. Quran 19:64 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0012: According to al-Badr's classification by meaning, which name indicates an intransitive attribute whose effect does not extend to an object?
The second category indicates intransitive attributes, exemplified by al-Hayy, al-'Azim, al-'Ali, and al-Ahad. Al-Ghafur, ar-Razzaq, and al-Bari' indicate transitive attributes.
asmaa-husna-0013: Scholars call the name al-Hayy's indication of power, hearing, sight, and knowledge what kind of indication?
Al-Hayy indicates the essence together with life by full correspondence, either one by inclusion, and power, hearing, sight, and knowledge by necessary implication.
asmaa-husna-0014: Which name is exclusive to Allah, so no other may be named by it?
Al-Badr gives Allah, ar-Rahman, al-Khaliq, al-Bari', and al-Qayyum as exclusive names. The words malik, 'aziz, and karim may be applied to others, with a difference in meaning and perfection.
asmaa-husna-0016: Which hadith indicates that some of Allah's names are known only to Him in His knowledge of the unseen?
The supplication for entering the market
The supplication for seeking guidance in a decision
The supplication for anxiety and grief

Ibn Mas'ud's hadith includes «أسألك بكل اسم هو لك ... أو استأثرت به في علم الغيب عندك» [I ask You by every Name belonging to You ... or preserved in the knowledge of the Unseen with You.]. It is said by someone afflicted with anxiety or grief (HadeethEnc), explanatory quotation, checked 2026-11-01. Pronunciation: As'aluka bi-kulli ismin huwa laka ... aw ista'tharta bihi fi 'ilm il-ghaybi 'indaka.
asmaa-husna-0017: What scholarly consensus did an-Nawawi report concerning «إن لله تسعة وتسعين اسمًا من أحصاها دخل الجنة» [Verily, Allah has ninety-nine names, ... Whoever memorizes them all will enter Paradise.]?
Allah's names are restricted to this number
The accompanying enumeration of these names is authentically established
Enumerating them means merely counting the words
The hadith does not limit Allah's names to this number

An-Nawawi said: 'Scholars agree that this hadith does not limit His names.' Its purpose is to state that encompassing these names leads to Paradise (HadeethEnc), checked 2026-11-01. The ellipsis omits the publication's additional 'one-hundred minus one,' matching the shorter source quotation.
asmaa-husna-0018: What is the status of narrations that enumerate the ninety-nine names individually and attribute the list to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him?
Authentic, recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim
Sound, uniquely recorded by Imam Ahmad
Al-Badr explains that no hadith enumerating the names is established. The list was inserted from the words of some early scholars.
asmaa-husna-0019: Ibn al-Qayyim gives three levels of encompassing the beautiful names. The first is enumerating their wording and number. What is the second?
Calling upon Allah by them in worship and requests
Making them a morning and evening litany
Writing and hanging them in houses
The levels are enumerating their wording and number; understanding their meanings and implications; then calling upon Allah by them in worship and requests.
asmaa-husna-0020: In Anas's hadith, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, heard a man supplicating and said, «لقد سألت الله باسمه الأعظم» [You have asked Allah by His greatest name]. Which name appeared in that man's supplication?

The man said: «اللهم إني أسألك بأن لك الحمد، لا إله إلا أنت وحدك لا شريك لك، المنان...» [O Allah, I ask You because all praise belongs to You. There is no deity except You alone, without partner, al-Mannan (the Bestower)...]. Reported by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and an-Nasa'i. Pronunciation: Allahumma inni as'aluka bi-anna laka al-hamd, la ilaha illa Anta wahdaka la sharika laka, al-Mannan...
asmaa-husna-0021: Abu Umamah's hadith says: «اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا دُعي به أجاب في ثلاث سور: البقرة وآل عمران و...» [Allah's greatest name, by which He answers when called upon, is in three surahs: al-Baqarah, Al 'Imran, and ...]. What is the third surah?
Reported by Ibn Majah and al-Hakim and included in al-Albani's as-Silsilah as-Sahihah (746). Al-Hayy, al-Qayyum occurs in all three surahs.
asmaa-husna-0022: In Buraydah's hadith, a man prayed: «أنت الله لا إله إلا أنت الأحد ... الذي لم يلد ولم يولد» [You are Allah, there is no God but You, the One, ... Who did not beget, and was not begotten]. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, «لقد سأل الله باسمه الأعظم» [He has asked Allah by His greatest name]. Which name is missing?

Its wording is «الأحد الصمد الذي لم يلد ولم يولد ولم يكن له كفوًا أحد» [the One, the Eternal Refuge, Who did not beget, and was not begotten, and to Whom no one is equal.]. Its chain is authentic (HadeethEnc). Pronunciation: Anta Allahu la ilaha illa Anta al-Ahad ... alladhi lam yalid wa lam yulad.
asmaa-husna-0024: Which third name joins Allah and ar-Rabb in encompassing the meanings of all the beautiful names, with all three occurring in al-Fatihah?
Allah encompasses the attributes of divinity; ar-Rabb, those of lordship; and ar-Rahman, those of kindness, generosity, and benevolence.
asmaa-husna-0025: According to al-Badr, ar-Rabb encompasses the attributes of lordship, and ar-Rahman those of kindness and generosity. What does the name Allah encompass?
Attributes of strength and irresistible power
Attributes of knowledge and all-encompassing awareness
He said: 'The name Allah encompasses the attributes of divinity; ar-Rabb, those of lordship; and ar-Rahman, those of kindness, generosity, and benevolence.'
asmaa-husna-0028: According to al-Badr, how many Quranic verses begin with Allah's name Allah?
He said: 'Allah, majestic and exalted, began thirty-three verses with it.'
asmaa-husna-0029: According to al-Badr, what is the origin and meaning of the name Allah?
He said: 'This name's origin is al-ilah, meaning the one worshipped.' Al-Ilah is one of Allah's names found in the Quran.
asmaa-husna-0031: Evidence for the name al-Ilah includes «وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ...» [And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, ...]. Which two names conclude the verse?

Al-Baqarah, verse 163: «وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ» [And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.] (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0032: How did al-Badr explain «وَهُوَ الَّذِي فِي السَّمَاءِ إِلَهٌ وَفِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَهٌ» [And it is He [i.e., Allāh] who is [the only] deity in the heaven, and on the earth [the only] deity.]?
He knows everything in heaven and earth
He owns and manages everything in them
The inhabitants of heaven and earth worship Him
He alone created heaven and earth
He said: 'The inhabitants of heaven and earth worship Him willingly and unwillingly.' The aspect of the name Allah relating to the servant is servitude. Quran 43:84 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0033: According to al-Badr, how often does the name ar-Rabb occur in the Quran in different settings and contexts?
About one hundred and fifty times
He said: 'It recurs in the Noble Quran in numerous settings and varied contexts more than five hundred times.'
asmaa-husna-0034: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name ar-Rabb?
The One possessing lordship over His creation through creating, owning, acting, and managing
The One needing none, while every other created being needs Him
The One free of every defect, deficiency, and affliction
The One possessing divinity and the right to worship over all His creation
He said: 'Ar-Rabb means the One possessing lordship over all His creation through creating, owning, acting, and managing.'
asmaa-husna-0035: Al-Badr quotes Ibn al-Athir: the word rabb, without an attached complement, applies only to whom?
A leader obeyed by his people
The one who improves and maintains something
Ibn al-Athir said: 'Without an attached complement, it applies only to Allah Most High. When applied to another, a complement is added: the rabb of such-and-such.'
asmaa-husna-0036: Allah's lordship has two kinds: general, encompassing every creature, and special. What constitutes special lordship?
Creating and providing for all creatures, righteous and wicked, believers and disbelievers
Nurturing His allies and guiding them to faith and servitude
Giving life, causing death, and general management
Sending rain upon the righteous and wicked
General lordship nurtures all creation through creating, providing, and managing. Special lordship concerns His allies, guiding them to faith and fulfillment of servitude to Him.
asmaa-husna-0037: Who narrated in Muslim: «ذاق طعم الإيمان من رضي بالله ربًّا، وبالإسلام دينًا، وبمحمد رسولًا» [He finds the taste of Imān who is pleased with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, and with Muhammad as Messenger.]?
Al-Badr cited it when explaining ar-Rabb and attributed it to Sahih Muslim (34), from al-'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him (HadeethEnc).
asmaa-husna-0038: Al-Badr distinguished ar-Rahman from ar-Rahim. What does ar-Rahim mean in his explanation?
The One merciful to His servants, whose mercy reaches its recipients
The One who conceals and overlooks His servants' sins without exposing them
The One whose mercy is an inherent, enduring attribute
The One who does not hasten to punish sinners

'Ar-Rahman is the One whose attribute is mercy; ar-Rahim is the One merciful to His servants.' Thus the Quran says: «وَكَانَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ رَحِيمًا» [And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.]. Quran 33:43 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0039: The Quran does not say 'rahman toward the believers'; rather, it says «وَكَانَ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ ...» [And ever is He, to the believers, ...]. Which word concludes the verse?
Al-Badr used this verse to show that ar-Rahim indicates mercy reaching its recipients, unlike ar-Rahman. Quran 33:43.' (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0041: In the hadith agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, «إن لله مائة رحمة أنزل منها رحمة واحدة...» [Allah, the Almighty, has one hundred mercies, of which He sent down one mercy ...], how many mercies did Allah reserve for His servants on the Day of Judgment?

«وأخّر الله تسعًا وتسعين رحمة يرحم بها عباده يوم القيامة» [Allah, the Almighty, deferred ninety-nine mercies with which He will bestow mercy on His slaves on the Day of Judgment.]. Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim; the wording is Muslim's (HadeethEnc).
asmaa-husna-0042: Allah pairs general mercy with knowledge in the Throne-bearers' supplication: «رَبَّنَا وَسِعْتَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ رَحْمَةً وَ...» [Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and ...]. What completes it?
Al-Badr said that everything reached by His knowledge is reached by His mercy, because Allah pairs this mercy with knowledge. Quran 40:7 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0043: In how many Quranic locations do al-Hayy and al-Qayyum occur together?

In Ayat al-Kursi, the beginning of Al 'Imran, and Ta-Ha: «وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ» [And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.[858]]. Quran 20:111 (QuranEnc) [858] See footnotes describing these attributes in 2:255.
asmaa-husna-0044: In which surah does «وَعَنَتِ الْوُجُوهُ لِلْحَيِّ الْقَيُّومِ» [And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.[858]] occur?
It is Ta-Ha, verse 111, the third occurrence of these paired names after al-Baqarah and Al 'Imran (QuranEnc) [858] See footnotes describing these attributes in 2:255.
asmaa-husna-0045: «وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي ...» [And rely upon the Ever-Living who ...]. What completes the verse?
«وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ» [And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die]. Al-Furqan: 58. The One deserving worship is the Ever-Living who does not die (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0046: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Qayyum?
The One who does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him
The One free of every deficiency and defect
The One whom eyesight cannot encompass
The Self-Sustaining One who sustains His creation
He said: 'Al-Qayyum affirms self-subsistence as Allah's attribute: He sustains Himself and sustains His creation.'
asmaa-husna-0047: According to al-Badr, which name encompasses attributes of action such as creating, providing, giving life, and causing death?
'Al-Hayy encompasses attributes of the essence, and al-Qayyum encompasses attributes of action.'
asmaa-husna-0049: In the supplication agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, «أعوذ بعزتك لا إله إلا أنت أن تضلني، أنت الحي الذي لا يموت، و...» [I seek refuge in Your Might. There is no god but You, that You do not lead me astray. You are the Ever-Living Who never dies, ...], what completes it?
But the Jinn and humans die
«كل من عليها فان» [Everyone upon it [i.e., the earth] will perish]
«كل نفس ذائقة الموت» [Every soul will taste death]

Al-Badr cited it in explaining al-Hayy, from Ibn 'Abbas. Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim; the wording is Muslim's (HadeethEnc). Pronunciation: A'udhu bi-'izzatika la ilaha illa Anta an tudillani, Anta al-Hayyu alladhi la yamutu, wal-jinnu wal-insu yamutun. Quranic alternative choices: 55:26 and 3:185 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0050: In how many Quranic locations does al-Khallaq occur in its intensive form?

In al-Hijr: «إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ» [Indeed, your Lord - He is the Knowing Creator.], and Ya-Sin: «بَلَى وَهُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ» [Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.]. Quran 15:86 and 36:81 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0051: Which name is paired with al-Khallaq in both of its Quranic occurrences?

«إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ» [Indeed, your Lord - He is the Knowing Creator.] (al-Hijr: 86); «بَلَى وَهُوَ الْخَلَّاقُ الْعَلِيمُ» [Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.] (Ya-Sin: 81) (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0052: In «فَتَبَارَكَ اللَّهُ أَحْسَنُ الْخَالِقِينَ» [So blessed is Allāh, the best of creators.[950]], what does creation mean when attributed to human beings?

When describing humans, creation means determining a design. Originating without a prior model belongs exclusively to the Lord of the worlds. Quran 23:14 (QuranEnc) [950] i.e., the most skillful and only true Creator.
asmaa-husna-0053: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Bari'?
The One giving everything its image and form
The One determining things in accordance with His wisdom
The One bringing things into existence after nonexistence
The One preserving things from ceasing to exist
'Al-Khaliq determines things in accordance with His wisdom; al-Bari' brings them into existence after nonexistence; and al-Musawwir...'
asmaa-husna-0054: In «هُوَ اللَّهُ الْخَالِقُ الْبَارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ» [He is Allāh, the Creator,[1666] the Producer,[1667] the Fashioner;[1668]], how is al-Khaliq explained?
The One determining things in accordance with His wisdom
The One bringing things into existence after nonexistence
The One originating things all at once without stages
The One giving each creature the form He wills

Explaining creation as determination makes sense of the three names' sequence: determination, then bringing into existence, then fashioning. Quran 59:24 (QuranEnc) [1666] i.e., He who destined existence for His creation. [1667] i.e., He who brings His creation into existence. [1668] i.e., He who gives every creation its particular form.
asmaa-husna-0055: Why were the Children of Israel addressed in al-Baqarah with «فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ» [So repent to your Creator]?
Their taking the calf for worship
Their refusing to enter the Holy Land

«يَا قَوْمِ إِنَّكُمْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أَنْفُسَكُمْ بِاتِّخَاذِكُمُ الْعِجْلَ فَتُوبُوا إِلَى بَارِئِكُمْ» [O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship]. So repent to your Creator]. Mentioning 'your Creator' highlights the enormity of their offense. Quran 2:54 (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0056: «هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ» [It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills.] is evidence for the name al-Musawwir. In which surah does it occur?
It is Al 'Imran, verse six. Al-Badr cited it when explaining al-Musawwir (QuranEnc)
asmaa-husna-0057: Allah's name al-Maleek occurs once in the Quran: «فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ ...» [In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, ...]. Which word follows?

It is al-Qamar, verse 55, the only occurrence of al-Maleek, paired with al-Muqtadir. Published English: 'Perfect in Ability.[1591]' (QuranEnc) [1591] Who accomplishes whatever He wills whenever He wills.
asmaa-husna-0058: According to al-Badr, how many times does Allah's name al-Malik occur in the Quran?

Al-Badr said: 'The name al-Malik occurs in the Noble Quran in five locations,' including «الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ» [the Sovereign,[1658] the Pure,[1659]] in al-Hashr. Quran 59:23 (QuranEnc) [1658] And owner of everything in existence. [1659] i.e., transcendent above any aspect belonging to His creation. Also, the possessor and grantor of blessings.
asmaa-husna-0059: «فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ الْمَلِكُ ... لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ» [So exalted is Allāh, the Sovereign,[969] ... there is no deity except Him, Lord of the Noble Throne.]. Which word is missing?
It is al-Mu'minun, verse 116, which al-Badr cited for the name al-Malik (QuranEnc) [969] And owner of everything in existence.
asmaa-husna-0060: The meaning of sovereignty in the names al-Malik and al-Malik includes three matters: Allah possesses the attributes of kingship; all creatures belong to Him; and third:
He accepts His servants' repentance and pardons many of their misdeeds
He cannot be seen by the eyes in this world
He does not hasten to punish the disobedient
His governance takes effect, and He decrees whatever He wills within His dominion
Third: His governance takes effect, and He decrees whatever He wills within His dominion. His judgment in it encompasses divine decree, religious law, and recompense.
asmaa-husna-0061: Allah's sovereignty includes three kinds of judgment: judgments of divine decree, judgments of religious law, and ...
Judgments of recompense reward or punish deeds, good and bad, in this world and the Hereafter. All are aspects of His sovereignty.
asmaa-husna-0062: In how many places in the Quran does Allah's name ar-Razzaq occur in this exact form?

It occurs in ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الرَّزَّاقُ ذُو الْقُوَّةِ الْمَتِينُ﴾ [Indeed, it is Allāh who is the [continual] Provider,[1548] the firm possessor of strength. [1548] Providing everything required by His creations during their decreed existence. His provision includes guidance.] (adh-Dhariyat 51:58) (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0063: When prices rose during the Prophet's lifetime (peace and blessings be upon him) and the Companions asked him to fix prices, which two complementary names of Allah did he mention in his reply?

In Anas's hadith: «إن الله هو الخالق القابض الباسط...» [Indeed, Allah is the Creator, the Withholder, the Expander...]. Narrated by Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and Ahmad with an authentic chain. The related.
asmaa-husna-0064: Allah's provision for His servants is of two kinds: general provision nourishes bodies; special provision is:
What a person receives without effort or earnings
Revelation and miracles provided only to prophets
Abundant wealth, children, and status in worldly life for whichever servants He wills
Nourishment of hearts with knowledge and faith, and lawful provision that supports religion
Special provision nourishes hearts with knowledge and faith, together with lawful provision that helps make one's religious life sound. It is specific to believers.
asmaa-husna-0065: The Quran reminds people that Allah alone provides for His servants in two contexts: the context of favor and gracious giving, and the context of:
Calling to obedience, goodness, and kindness
Al-Badr states that this reminder comes in two contexts: favor and gracious giving, and calling to obedience, goodness, and kindness.
asmaa-husna-0066: How many times does Allah's name al-Ahad occur in the Noble Quran?

Al-Badr says it occurs in one place, in Surat al-Ikhlas: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,[2011] [2011] Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds.] (112:1) (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0067: Yusuf said to his two fellow prisoners, ﴿أَأَرْبَابٌ مُتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيْرٌ أَمِ اللَّهُ ...﴾ [O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Yusuf 12:39; al-Badr cites it as evidence for the name al-Wahid. The full verse is: [O [my] two companions of prison, are separate lords better or Allāh, the One,[597] the Prevailing?[598] [597] Single, individual and unique in His attributes and His deeds.
[598] He who subdues doubts and false arguments with clear evidences and who subdues and imposes His will upon all creation.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0068: The names al-Wahid and al-Ahad imply that takyif is invalid. What does takyif mean?
Diverting the wording of attributes from its apparent meaning to other meanings without evidence
Using the mind to delve into how the Lord's attributes are
Affirming Allah's attributes without likening them to creation
Takyif (trying to specify how divine attributes are) is a person's attempt, using their limited mind, to know how the Lord's attributes are. This is impossible.
asmaa-husna-0069: Al-Badr calls singling Allah out for worship, because He alone creates, provides, gives life, and causes death, an implication of al-Wahid and al-Ahad. What does he call it?
Tawhid of the names and attributes
Acknowledging and believing that He alone possesses perfection is tawhid (affirming Allah's oneness) of knowledge. Singling Him alone out for worship is tawhid of practice.
asmaa-husna-0070: «الله الواحد الصمد ثلث القرآن» [Allah, al-Wahid, as-Samad, is one third of the Quran]. Which Companion narrated this hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari?
Al-Badr cites it in his explanation of the name as-Samad, from Sahih al-Bukhari (4727), on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.
asmaa-husna-0071: How did Ibn Abbas explain Allah's name as-Samad in the report narrated by Ibn Jarir?
The First, before whom there is nothing
The One near to whoever calls on Him, who answers their request
The One who grants protection and against whom none can grant protection
The Master whose mastery is perfect
Ibn Abbas said that as-Samad is the Master whose mastery is perfect, and the Noble One whose nobility is perfect...
asmaa-husna-0072: Ibn al-Qayyim explained that the derivation of as-Samad indicates two meanings. What are they?
He said it derives from gathering and directing one's intent: all intent is directed toward Him, and all attributes of mastery are gathered in Him.
asmaa-husna-0073: Which statement is among the early Muslims' explanations of Allah's name as-Samad?
The One who conceals His servants' faults and does not expose them before creation
The One who judges between His servants in truth
The One who has no hollow interior and neither eats nor drinks
The One who accepts little and rewards abundantly
They said that as-Samad has no hollow interior and neither eats nor drinks. These explanations are all correct because the name indicates numerous attributes.
asmaa-husna-0074: In how many places does Allah's name al-Wahhab occur in the Noble Quran?
In Al Imran (8) and in Surat Sad (9) and (35).
asmaa-husna-0075: ﴿رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنْبَغِي لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ ...﴾ [My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are ...] (QuranEnc) How does Sulayman's supplication (peace be upon him) end?

Sad 38:35; one of three occurrences of al-Wahhab. Full verse: [He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom such as will not belong to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower."] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0076: The name al-Wahhab has the Arabic morphological pattern fa''al. What does this form indicate?
Seeking and striving to perform an action
Two or more sharing in an action or gift
Intensification, indicating abundant, successive, and extensive gifts
Al-Badr says that fa''al is an intensive form in Arabic. It indicates the abundance, succession, variety, and extent of the gifts.
asmaa-husna-0077: Into how many groups does Allah divide married couples in ﴿يَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ إِنَاثًا وَيَهَبُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ الذُّكُورَ﴾ [He gives to whom He wills female [children], and He gives to whom He wills males.] (QuranEnc) and the following verse?
Those He gives daughters, those He gives sons, those He gives both, and those He makes infertile.
asmaa-husna-0078: ﴿قُلْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَنَا رَبُّنَا ثُمَّ يَفْتَحُ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَهُوَ الْفَتَّاحُ ...﴾ [Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes the verse?

Saba' 34:26 pairs al-Fattah with al-Alim. The translation renders the paired names together: [Say, "Our Lord will bring us together; then He will judge between us in truth. And He is the Knowing Judge."[1232] [1232] Literally, "Opener," i.e., He who decides and lays open all matters in truth and justice and who opens the way to victory, success, relief, knowledge and understanding.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0079: What is the meaning of Allah's name al-Fattah, as explained by al-Badr?
The One who gives the disobedient respite and does not hasten their punishment, so they may repent
The One who accepts His servants' repentance again and again
The One who gives His servants without request or compensation
The One who judges between His servants however He wills and decrees concerning them whatever He wishes
The name means that He judges between His servants however He wills and decrees concerning them whatever He wishes; none can overturn His judgment.
asmaa-husna-0081: ﴿قُلْ يَوْمَ ... لَا يَنْفَعُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِيمَانُهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ [Say, [O Muḥammad], "On the Day of ... the belief of those who had disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."] (QuranEnc) [as-Sajdah: 29] Which word is missing?

Allah calls it the Day of Conquest because He judges between His servants with a judgment that distinguishes those upon truth from those upon falsehood. Full verse: [Say, [O Muḥammad], "On the Day of Conquest the belief of those who had disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved."] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0082: Which prophet supplicated to his Lord, ﴿رَبَّنَا افْتَحْ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ قَوْمِنَا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ [Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth,] (QuranEnc)?
Al-Badr cites this supplication of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) in Surat al-A'raf (89).
asmaa-husna-0083: Allah's name as-Sami' occurs in the Quran in approximately:
Al-Badr says that this name occurs in the Quran in approximately fifty places.
asmaa-husna-0084: A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: «الحمد لله الذي وسع سمعه الأصوات» [Praise be to Allah Whose hearing encompasses all voices.] (HadeethEnc). This concerned:
The three who were left behind
The slander incident and the revelation declaring her innocence
The blind man who came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him)
The woman who disputed with the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) about her husband

The woman came and spoke to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), while A'ishah could not hear what she was saying. Allah then revealed: ﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّتِي تُجَادِلُكَ فِي زَوْجِهَا﴾ [Certainly has Allāh heard the speech of the one who argues [i.e., pleads] with you, [O Muḥammad], concerning her husband] (QuranEnc) (al-Mujadilah 58:1).
asmaa-husna-0085: «ارْبَعوا على أنفسكم، فإنكم لا تدعون أصمّ ولا غائبًا، ولكن تدعون سميعًا ...» [Be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; rather, you are calling upon One who hears, ...]. How does the hadith continue?
Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said it when they raised their voices with takbir (saying Allahu akbar) while traveling.
asmaa-husna-0086: In the worshipper's words, «سمع الله لمن حمده» [Allah responds to whoever praises Him].

Hearing attributed to Allah can mean responding, as in ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ﴾ [Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.] (QuranEnc) (Ibrahim 14:39), and «سمع الله لمن حمده» [Allah responds to whoever praises Him].
asmaa-husna-0087: In Allah's words to Musa and Harun, ﴿إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَى﴾ [Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.] (QuranEnc) (Ta Ha 20:46), the mention of hearing conveys:
Al-Badr divides hearing in the sense of perceiving sound into three contexts: threat, support, and showing all-encompassing awareness. This verse conveys support.
asmaa-husna-0088: ﴿أَمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّا لَا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهُمْ وَنَجْوَاهُمْ﴾ [Or do they think that We hear not their secrets and their private conversations?] (QuranEnc) (az-Zukhruf 43:80). What does the mention of hearing convey here?
Al-Badr gives it as an example of hearing attributed to Allah that conveys a threat.
asmaa-husna-0089: In Surat Al Imran, Zakariyya (peace be upon him), asking for good offspring, invoked Allah through His attribute in ﴿إِنَّكَ ...﴾ [Indeed, You are ...] (QuranEnc)

Al Imran 3:38: ﴿هُنَالِكَ دَعَا زَكَرِيَّا رَبَّهُ قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ﴾ [At that, Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."] (QuranEnc).
