asmaa-husna-0090: ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُ رَبُّهُ فَصَرَفَ عَنْهُ كَيْدَهُنَّ إِنَّهُ هُوَ ...﴾ [So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse concerning Yusuf (peace be upon him)?

Yusuf 12:34. Al-Badr cites it when discussing prophets' supplication through the name as-Sami'. Full verse: [So his Lord responded to him and averted from him their plan. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0092: ﴿وَلَوْ بَسَطَ اللَّهُ الرِّزْقَ لِعِبَادِهِ لَبَغَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ ... إِنَّهُ بِعِبَادِهِ ...﴾ [And if Allāh had extended [excessively] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. ... Indeed He is, of His servants, ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Ash-Shura 42:27: He sees whose condition wealth would improve and whose condition it would corrupt. Full verse: [And if Allāh had extended [excessively] provision for His servants, they would have committed tyranny throughout the earth. But He sends [it] down in an amount which He wills. Indeed He is, of His servants, Aware and Seeing.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0094: A servant's awareness that Allah sees them and knows their condition brings them to the highest station of religion. Which station is that?
«أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه، فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك» [It is to worship Allah as if you see Him, for if you do not see Him, He sees you.] (HadeethEnc). This is the highest station of religion.
asmaa-husna-0095: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ إِلَى أَهْلِهَا ... إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ ...﴾ [Indeed, Allāh commands you to render trusts to whom they are due ... Indeed, Allāh is ever ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete this verse of an-Nisa'?

An-Nisa' 4:58. Ending with these two names praises Allah's commands, because their Lawgiver is as-Sami', al-Basir. Full verse: [Indeed, Allāh commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allāh instructs you. Indeed, Allāh is ever Hearing and Seeing.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0097: Which statement does al-Badr use to explain Allah's name al-Alim?
The One who hears secrets and private conversation and answers supplication
The One who judges in truth between His servants on the Day of Resurrection regarding their disagreements
The One who sees an ant moving over solid rock
The One whose knowledge encompasses the outward and inward, the past, present, and future
Al-Alim is the One whose knowledge encompasses outward and inward matters, and the past, present, and future. Nothing is hidden from Him.
asmaa-husna-0098: ﴿يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ ...﴾ [He knows that which deceives the eyes ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse continue?
Ghafir 40:19. Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Alim as a deterrent to sins. Full verse: [He knows that which deceives the eyes and what the breasts conceal.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0099: Ash-Shinqiti reported scholarly consensus that 'the greatest admonition and strongest deterrent to descend from heaven to earth' is:
Considering the fates of destroyed nations
Reflecting on the terrors of the Day of Resurrection
A servant's knowledge that Allah watches them and knows what they do

Al-Badr cites this as an effect of belief in al-Alim: scarcely can one turn a page of the Mushaf (written Quran) without finding this admonition, ﴿بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [Knowing of all things.] (QuranEnc) (wording also in al-Baqarah 2:29).
asmaa-husna-0100: ﴿لَا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصَارَ وَهُوَ ...﴾ [Vision perceives Him not,[332] but He perceives [all] vision; and He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Al-An'am 6:103 is a verse pairing these names. Full verse and notes: [Vision perceives Him not,[332] but He perceives [all] vision; and He is the Subtle,[333] the Aware.[334] [332] In the life of this world. The people of Paradise will be able to see Allāh in the Hereafter. See 75:22-23.
[333] Perceptive of the most precise and unapparent matters and the intricacies of all affairs. Also, He who benefits His servants in indiscernible ways.
[334] See footnote in 6:18.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0101: According to al-Badr, Allah's name al-Khabir means:
The One who accepts His servants' repentance
The One who gives His servants without their asking and begins bestowing blessings before they deserve them
The One whose knowledge reaches secrets and who knows the innermost contents of hearts
The One who protects His servants from destruction
Al-Khabir knows secrets, the innermost contents of hearts, hidden seeds, and the subtleties of affairs.
asmaa-husna-0102: Allah's name al-Latif has two meanings. One is the meaning of al-Khabir. What is the other?
The One whom eyes cannot perceive in this world
The One who conceals His servants' sins and does not hold them accountable for everything they earn
The One who brings His servants what benefits them through ways they do not perceive
The One who gives the wrongdoer respite without neglecting him
The second meaning is the One who brings His servants and allies what benefits them, through His subtle kindness and goodness, in ways they do not perceive.
asmaa-husna-0103: Al-Badr distinguishes Allah's lutf 'with a servant' from His lutf 'for a servant.' What does lutf 'for a servant' mean?
Making their affairs easy, facilitating paths of good, and helping them
Repelling the promptings of their soul that commands evil
Providing them beneficial knowledge that they act upon
Arranging causes outside their power that bring them benefit

Lutf (subtle kindness) 'with' a servant means easing their affairs and helping them. Lutf 'for' a servant means arranging external causes that benefit them, as in Yusuf's story: ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفٌ لِمَا يَشَاءُ﴾ [Indeed, my Lord is Subtle[619] in what He wills.] (QuranEnc) (Yusuf 12:100). [619] Perceptive of unapparent matters within which is benefit to His servants.
asmaa-husna-0104: ﴿اللَّهُ لَطِيفٌ بِعِبَادِهِ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ ...﴾ [Allāh is Subtle[1419] with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Ash-Shura 42:19. Part of His subtle kindness is determining His servants' provision according to His knowledge of their welfare, rather than their desires. Full verse: [Allāh is Subtle[1419] with His servants; He gives provision to whom He wills. And He is the Powerful, the Exalted in Might. [1419] See footnote in 12:100.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0105: When al-Afuww and al-Ghafur occur together, which is more emphatic according to al-Badr, and why?
al-Ghafur, because it conveys both erasing and pardoning and is thus more comprehensive
They are equal, with no difference when paired
al-Ghafur, because it occurs more often in the Quran
al-Afuww, because it conveys erasing, which is more emphatic than covering
Ghufran (forgiveness) conveys covering, while afw (pardon) conveys erasing. Erasing is more emphatic than covering. This distinction applies when they are paired.
asmaa-husna-0106: ﴿وَإِنِّي لَغَفَّارٌ لِمَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا ثُمَّ ...﴾ [But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then ...] (QuranEnc) Which word completes the verse?
Ta Ha 20:82. Al-Badr cites it for al-Ghaffar. Full verse: [But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0107: Al-Badr explains that at-Tawwab turns toward whichever servants He wills in two ways. What are they?
First enabling repentance, then accepting it
Delaying punishment, then erasing the sin
Concealing in this world, then pardoning in the Hereafter

He turns toward them by enabling repentance: ﴿ثُمَّ تَابَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [Then He turned to them] (QuranEnc) (at-Tawbah 9:118), and by accepting it: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَقْبَلُ التَّوْبَةَ عَنْ عِبَادِهِ﴾ [And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants] (QuranEnc) (ash-Shura 42:25).
asmaa-husna-0108: «ليس أحدٌ أصبرَ على أذى سمعه من الله؛ إنهم ليدعون له ولدًا، وإنه ...» [None, or nothing, is more patient about the offensive statements he hears than Allah. Verily, they ascribe a son to Him, ...] (HadeethEnc). How does the hadith continue?
Yet He grants them good health and sustenance
He forgives them if they repent
He is forbearing toward them and conceals their faults
He gives them respite without neglecting them
Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Musa. Al-Badr cites it regarding Allah's general pardon of evildoers by averting punishments from them.
asmaa-husna-0109: Allah's pardon is of two kinds: general pardon includes even disbelievers, by averting punishment and continually bestowing blessings. For whom is His special pardon?
Everyone who pronounces the two testimonies, even if they persist in sins and never repent
Those who repent, seek forgiveness, supplicate, and endure affliction seeking reward
The angels brought near and the bearers of the Throne
The second kind is His special pardon and forgiveness for those who repent, seek forgiveness, supplicate, worship, and endure calamities seeking reward.
asmaa-husna-0110: ﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لَا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ...﴾ [Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allāh. ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ [Indeed, Allāh forgives all sins.[1354] Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.] (QuranEnc) (az-Zumar 39:53). [1354] For those who repent and correct themselves.
asmaa-husna-0111: In the hadith qudsi (a hadith conveying Allah's words), «أذنب عبدي ذنبًا، فعلم أن له ربًّا يغفر الذنب و...» [My servant committed a sin and then realized that he has a Lord Who forgives sins ...] (HadeethEnc). How does it continue?

Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah. It ends: «اعمل ما شئت فقد غفرت لك» [Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.] (HadeethEnc), meaning as long as you continue repenting and returning to Allah.
asmaa-husna-0112: ﴿عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ الْكَبِيرُ ...﴾ [[He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes this verse from Surat ar-Ra'd?
Ar-Ra'd 13:9 is evidence for the name al-Muta'ali. Full verse: [[He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0114: The names al-Aliyy, al-A'la, and al-Muta'ali indicate Allah's absolute exaltedness: exaltedness of His essence, His status, and His:
He is exalted in subjugating power: He has subdued everything, and all beings submit to Him.
asmaa-husna-0115: According to al-Badr, in how many Quran verses does ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ [and then established Himself above the Throne.[378]] (QuranEnc) occur?

He says it occurs in six Quran verses: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوَى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ﴾ [and then established Himself above the Throne.[378]] (QuranEnc) (wording in al-A'raf 7:54), explaining that He rose and was high above it. [378] There are several linguistic meanings of the words "istawā ʿalā," among them: to settle upon, to assume ascendancy above, and to assert authority over. However, it is known that all the attributes of Allāh are eternal, i.e., they have always existed and were present before He created. Thus, it cannot be said that He "rose" above the Throne, as Allāh has always been ascendant. Because the Creator may not be compared to His creation, the Prophet's companions and early scholars refused speculation as to how His actions could be interpreted, considering any such attempt unlawful. Similarly, the true nature of the Throne is known only to Allāh, the Exalted.
asmaa-husna-0117: Allah's statement, ﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ﴾ [And He is the subjugator over His servants.] (QuranEnc) (al-An'am 6:18), is evidence of His exaltedness. Which type of evidence is it?
Explicitly stating that some creatures are raised to Him
Al-Badr places it in the first type of evidence for exaltedness: explicitly stating His being above.
asmaa-husna-0118: ﴿إِلَيْهِ يَصْعَدُ الْكَلِمُ الطَّيِّبُ وَالْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ ...﴾ [To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work ...] (QuranEnc) Which word completes the sentence?

Fatir 35:10. Al-Badr cites it as evidence of exaltedness through the explicit mention of ascending to Him. Verse: [To Him ascends good speech, and righteous work raises it.[1246]] [1246] For acceptance by Allāh, meaning that righteous deeds are confirmation and proof of what is uttered by the tongue (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0119: Abu Nasr as-Sijzi reported agreement among imams such as Sufyan, Malik, and Ahmad that Allah Himself is above the Throne, and that:
His Throne is the greatest created thing
He descends to the lowest heaven every night
His knowledge is in every place
His Kursi encompasses the heavens and the earth
As-Sijzi said they agreed that Allah Himself is above the Throne and that His knowledge is in every place.
asmaa-husna-0120: ﴿ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ هُوَ الْبَاطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ ...﴾ [That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete this verse of al-Hajj?

Al-Hajj 22:62. Belief in Allah's exaltedness produces reverence for Him and sincerity in worship. Full verse: [That is because Allāh is the True Reality, and that which they call upon other than Him is falsehood, and because Allāh is the Most High, the Grand.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0121: In the hadith qudsi (a hadith conveying Allah's words) cited by al-Badr when explaining al-Kabir and al-Azim: «الكبرياء ردائي، والعظمة ...» [Grandeur is My cloak, and greatness is ...]. How does it continue?

«فمن نازعني واحدًا منهما قذفته في النار» [Whoever contends with Me over either of them, I will cast into the Fire]. Narrated by Ahmad and Abu Dawud from Abu Hurayrah with a hasan (sound) chain. Related HadeethEnc entry 6107 has different wording, which is not substituted here.
asmaa-husna-0122: It is authentically reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said in bowing and prostration: «سبحان ذي الجبروت والملكوت و...» [Glory be to the Possessor of greatness, dominion, ...] (HadeethEnc). How does this dhikr (remembrance) continue?
Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and an-Nasa'i from Awf ibn Malik with an authentic chain. Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Kabir and al-Azim.
asmaa-husna-0123: Why was saying 'Allahu akbar' prescribed in prayer and the adhan (call to prayer), rather than 'Allahu a'zam', according to Ibn Taymiyyah as quoted by al-Badr?
Because greatness is an attribute of action and grandeur an attribute of essence
Because grandeur includes greatness and is more complete
Because the word a'zam does not occur in the Quran
Only because akbar is easier to pronounce

Ibn Taymiyyah said that kibriya' (grandeur) includes azamah (greatness), but grandeur is more complete. That is why grandeur is likened to the upper garment and greatness to the lower garment. 'Allahu akbar' means Allah is greater; 'Allahu a'zam' means Allah is more immense.
asmaa-husna-0124: As Ibn Abbas said, part of Allah's greatness is that the seven heavens and seven earths in His hand are like a ... in one of our hands. What is missing?
Al-Badr quotes Ibn Abbas when discussing the meanings of grandeur and greatness connected with Allah's attributes.
asmaa-husna-0125: Al-Badr explains Allah's name al-Matin as:
The One who gives respite without neglecting
The One whose command is firm and whose judgment does not change
The One whose knowledge encompasses everything
Al-Matin means the One of intense strength. It occurs only once, paired with ﴿ذُو الْقُوَّةِ﴾ [possessor of strength.] (QuranEnc) (adh-Dhariyat 51:58).
asmaa-husna-0126: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Qawiyy?
The One who gives abundantly and is pleased with a little righteous work from His servants
The One who takes charge of His servants' affairs and manages their concerns
The One who answers the distressed when they call upon Him and removes harm
The One whom nothing incapacitates, whom none can overcome, and whose decree none can repel
Al-Qawiyy is the One whom nothing incapacitates, whom none can overcome, and whose decree none can repel. His command takes effect and His decree is carried out among His creation.
asmaa-husna-0127: ﴿كَتَبَ اللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ أَنَا وَرُسُلِي إِنَّ اللَّهَ ...﴾ [Allāh has written [i.e., decreed], "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allāh is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete this verse of al-Mujadilah?

Al-Mujadilah 58:21. His granting victory to His prophets and supporting His allies are signs of His power. Full verse: [Allāh has written [i.e., decreed], "I will surely overcome, I and My messengers." Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0128: In how many places in the Quran does Allah's name ar-Raqib occur?
In an-Nisa' (1), al-Ahzab (52), and al-Ma'idah (117), where it is paired with ash-Shahid.
asmaa-husna-0129: The names ar-Raqib and ash-Shahid are paired in Isa's words (peace be upon him), ﴿فَلَمَّا تَوَفَّيْتَنِي كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [but when You took me up, You were the Observer over them,] (QuranEnc) In which surah do they occur?
Al-Ma'idah 5:117: ﴿كُنْتَ أَنْتَ الرَّقِيبَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْتَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾ [You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0130: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلَيْكُمْ رَقِيبًا﴾ [Indeed Allāh is ever,[159] over you, an Observer.[160]] (QuranEnc) This concludes the first verse of which surah?

The first verse of an-Nisa' ends with ar-Raqib, one of its three occurrences. [159] When used in conjunction with Allāh's attributes, the word "ever" (occurring repeatedly throughout this sūrah and elsewhere, such as in sūrah al-Aḥzāb) is quite inadequate in imparting the sense of continuation expressed by the word "kāna" in Arabic, which indicates "always was, is, and always will be." [160] Ever-present and taking account of everything.
asmaa-husna-0131: According to al-Badr, what does Allah's name ash-Shahid mean?
The One who takes care of His servants through victory and support
The One sought for every need and resorted to in distress and hardship
The One who observes everything and bears witness for and against His servants concerning their deeds
The One who sends down sustenance and apportions provision
Ash-Shahid observes everything; nothing is hidden from Him. He bears witness for and against His servants concerning what they have done.
asmaa-husna-0132: According to Ibn Sa'di as quoted by al-Badr, what is the relationship between ar-Raqib and ash-Shahid?
They are synonymous, indicating the all-encompassing nature of His hearing, sight, and knowledge
Ash-Shahid applies only to the Day of Resurrection
The first is an attribute of essence and the second an attribute of action
They are opposites that cannot occur in one context
Ibn Sa'di says that ar-Raqib and ash-Shahid are synonymous. Both indicate that Allah's hearing encompasses everything audible, His sight everything visible, and His knowledge everything knowable.
asmaa-husna-0133: As al-Badr explains, what is the reality of muraqabah, the fruit of a servant's knowledge that Allah watches them?
Withdrawing from people and devoting oneself exclusively to worship
Continually knowing and being certain that Allah observes one's outward and inward state
Taking oneself to account at the end of every day
Weeping often out of fear of Allah in solitude and spending long nights in prayer
Muraqabah (awareness of Allah's watchfulness) means continually knowing and being certain that Allah observes one's outward and inward state.
asmaa-husna-0135: Allah's name al-Muhaymin occurs in only one place in the Quran. In which surah?

In ﴿الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ﴾ [the Sovereign,[1658] the Pure,[1659] the Perfection,[1660] the Grantor of Security,[1661] the Overseer,[1662] the Exalted in Might,[1663] the Compeller,[1664] the Superior.[1665]] (QuranEnc) (al-Hashr 59:23). [1658] And owner of everything in existence.
[1659] i.e., transcendent above any aspect belonging to His creation. Also, the possessor and grantor of blessings.
[1660] Literally, "Free" from any imperfection. Also, "Peace" or "Soundness."
[1661] And safety, i.e., reassurance that His promise is always fulfilled. Also, He who bestows faith.
[1662] i.e., who observes, guards and protects. Also, "the Criterion."
[1663] Refer to footnote in 2:129.
[1664] Whose irresistible force is without limitation; the one above all things who compels the creation to be as He wills it. Also, "the Amender" or "the Rectifier" who repairs, restores, completes or sets something right once again, out of His mercy.
[1665] Supreme, complete and perfect in His essence, attributes and actions.
asmaa-husna-0136: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ ...﴾ [And to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allāh, of all things, ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes this verse of an-Nisa'?

An-Nisa' 4:126 is evidence for al-Muhit, indicating that His knowledge, power, and subjugation encompass everything. Full verse: [And to Allāh belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And ever is Allāh, of all things, encompassing.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0137: Allah's name al-Muqit occurs in one place in the Quran, ending a verse about:
Rulings on fasting and compensatory feeding
Interceding for good and for evil

﴿مَنْ يَشْفَعْ شَفَاعَةً حَسَنَةً يَكُنْ لَهُ نَصِيبٌ مِنْهَا ... وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا﴾ [Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share [i.e., reward] therefrom; ... And ever is Allāh, over all things, a Keeper.[205]] (QuranEnc) (an-Nisa' 4:85). [205] Providing, protecting, witnessing, keeping precise records and capable of recompense.
asmaa-husna-0138: Ibn Kathir quotes Ibn Abbas explaining ﴿وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقِيتًا﴾ [And ever is Allāh, over all things, a Keeper.[205]] (QuranEnc) (an-Nisa' 4:85). What does Muqit mean in that explanation?

Ibn Abbas, Ata', and Qatadah explain Muqit as preserving; Mujahid says witnessing; ad-Dahhak says the Provider. Note [205]: Providing, protecting, witnessing, keeping precise records and capable of recompense.
asmaa-husna-0139: The One who expands provision for believers alone
The One whose attributes, descriptions, greatness, bounty, and goodness are boundless
The One whose House accommodates all worshippers
The One who is not constrained by numerous requests and does not tire of persistent petitioners
His attributes, descriptions, and their objects are boundless, as are His greatness, authority, dominion, bounty, and goodness.
asmaa-husna-0140: ﴿وَإِنْ يَتَفَرَّقَا يُغْنِ اللَّهُ كُلًّا مِنْ سَعَتِهِ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ وَاسِعًا ...﴾ [But if they separate [by divorce], Allāh will enrich each [of them] from His abundance. And ever is Allāh Encompassing ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse end?

An-Nisa' 4:130. Al-Badr cites it to show the abundance of Allah's provision. Full verse: [But if they separate [by divorce], Allāh will enrich each [of them] from His abundance. And ever is Allāh Encompassing and Wise.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0141: ﴿فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ ...﴾ [So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face[37] of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete al-Baqarah 2:115?

Al-Badr cites it for al-Wasi', a name occurring in several Quranic passages. Full verse: [And to Allāh belongs the east and the west. So wherever you [might] turn, there is the Face[37] of Allāh. Indeed, Allāh is all-Encompassing and Knowing. [37] See footnote to 2:19.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0142: Ya'qub (peace be upon him) said, ﴿فَاللَّهُ خَيْرٌ ... وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾ [But Allāh is the best ... and He is the most merciful of the merciful.] (QuranEnc) What is missing?
Yusuf 12:64 is evidence for al-Hafiz. Verse: [But Allāh is the best guardian, and He is the most merciful of the merciful.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0143: Preservation in al-Hafeez and al-Hafiz encompasses two matters: His preserving all knowable things in His knowledge, and:
Preserving created things so they remain throughout their allotted existence and do not perish
Protecting wealth from theft and loss
Protecting tongues from lying and backbiting
Second: Allah preserves created things, including the heavens, earth, and everything in them, so they remain throughout their allotted existence and do not perish.
asmaa-husna-0144: Allah's preservation of His servants is of two kinds: general preservation includes the righteous and the wicked. His special preservation of His allies consists of:
Providing them food, drink, and air
Successive angels guarding them by Allah's command from in front and behind
Protecting their bodies from illness in every circumstance
Protecting their faith from doubts, trials, and destructive desires
Special preservation protects His allies' faith from misleading doubts, trials, and desires, and grants them victory over their enemies.
asmaa-husna-0145: Which Companion did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) advise with «احفظ الله يحفظك» [Be mindful of Allah, and Allah will protect you.] (HadeethEnc)?
Narrated by Ahmad and at-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan sahih (sound and authentic). Al-Badr cites it among the effects of the name al-Hafiz.
asmaa-husna-0146: Which prophet said to his people, ﴿إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ حَفِيظٌ﴾ [Indeed my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.] (QuranEnc)?
Hud 11:57, in his address to his people, Ad. Al-Badr cites it as evidence for al-Hafeez. Note [560]: Protecting and preserving the existence and attributes of His creations.
asmaa-husna-0147: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا قَنَطُوا وَيَنْشُرُ رَحْمَتَهُ وَهُوَ ...﴾ [And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?
Ash-Shura 42:28 is evidence for al-Waliyy. Full verse: [And it is He who sends down the rain after they had despaired and spreads His mercy. And He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0148: ﴿وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِاللَّهِ هُوَ مَوْلَاكُمْ فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى وَنِعْمَ ...﴾ [and hold fast to Allāh. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse end?
The end of al-Hajj (78). Al-Badr cites it as evidence for al-Mawla. Verse: [and hold fast to Allāh. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0149: Allah says of all creation, ﴿ثُمَّ رُدُّوا إِلَى اللَّهِ مَوْلَاهُمُ الْحَقِّ﴾ [Then they [i.e., His servants] are returned to Allāh, their true Lord.] (QuranEnc) (al-An'am 6:62). What does His being the mawla of disbelievers mean?
He owns them and disposes of their affairs however He wills
He helps them and supports them against their enemies
He loves them and enables them to obey
He takes care of them through forgiveness and mercy

This is general wilayah (authority and guardianship). What is denied in ﴿وَأَنَّ الْكَافِرِينَ لَا مَوْلَى لَهُمْ﴾ [and because the disbelievers have no protector.] (QuranEnc) (Muhammad 47:11) is the special guardianship of love, enabling obedience, and victory reserved for believers.
asmaa-husna-0150: When Abu Sufyan said at Uhud, «لنا العزى ولا عزى لكم» [We have al-Uzza and you have no Uzza].
Allah is higher and more majestic
Allah is our protector, and you have no protector
Allah is our Lord, and you have no lord
Allah is our guardian, and He is the best of helpers
Narrated by al-Bukhari (4043). Al-Badr cites it regarding special guardianship that entails support and victory.
asmaa-husna-0151: ﴿إِنَّ وَلِيِّيَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْكِتَابَ وَهُوَ يَتَوَلَّى ...﴾ [Indeed, my protector is Allāh, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to ...] (QuranEnc) Which word completes the verse?

Al-A'raf 7:196. Allah's allies are those whose deeds are made righteous through obedience to Him. Full verse: [Indeed, my protector is Allāh, who has sent down the Book; and He is an ally to the righteous.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0152: The four names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir, and al-Batin occur together in one Quranic passage. In which surah?

﴿هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [He is the First[1623] and the Last,[1624] the Ascendant[1625] and the Intimate,[1626] and He is, of all things, Knowing. [1623] Before whom nothing existed. Also, He who is supreme, foremost or uppermost.
[1624] Enduring eternally when nothing else remains.
[1625] Nothing being above Him. Another meaning is "the Apparent," i.e., evident through His creation and revelation.
[1626] Nothing being nearer than Him by way of His knowledge. Another meaning is "the Unapparent," i.e., concealed from man's physical senses.] (al-Hadid 57:3) (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0153: In the bedtime supplication narrated by Muslim, how did the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) explain al-Batin?
There is nothing nearer than You

«وأنت الظاهر فليس فوقك شيء، وأنت الباطن فليس دونك شيء» [You are the Highest and there is nothing above You, and You are the Nearest and there is nothing nearer than You.] (HadeethEnc). Narrated by Muslim (2713), from Abu Hurayrah.
asmaa-husna-0154: The four names al-Awwal, al-Akhir, az-Zahir, and al-Batin concern two kinds of encompassing: al-Awwal and al-Akhir encompass time; az-Zahir and al-Batin encompass:
Al-Badr describes two kinds of encompassing: temporal and spatial. Being First and Last encompasses before and after; being az-Zahir and al-Batin encompasses everything outward and inward.
asmaa-husna-0155: As al-Badr explains al-Zahir, what does Allah's zahiriyyah mean?
The clarity of His signs in the universe to observers
His being above and exalted over everything
His zahiriyyah means His being above and exalted over everything. In the hadith: «وأنت الظاهر فليس فوقك شيء» [You are the Highest and there is nothing above You,] (HadeethEnc).
asmaa-husna-0156: What did Ibn Abbas advise someone troubled by whisperings of doubt to say?

﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ﴾ [Allāh - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living,[98] the Self-Sustaining.[99]] [98] Whose life is perfect, complete and eternal, without beginning or end, and through whom all created life originated and continues. [99] Dependent on none for His existence while being the sustainer and administrator of all created existence. (2:255) (QuranEnc)

﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,[2011]] [2011] Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds. (112:1) (QuranEnc)

﴿لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ﴾ [There is nothing like unto Him,[1411] and He is the Hearing, the Seeing.[1412]] [1411] There is no similarity whatsoever between the Creator and His creation in essence, in attributes or in deed.
[1412] See footnotes to 17:1. (42:11) (QuranEnc)

﴿هُوَ الْأَوَّلُ وَالْآخِرُ وَالظَّاهِرُ وَالْبَاطِنُ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ [He is the First[1623] and the Last,[1624] the Ascendant[1625] and the Intimate,[1626] and He is, of all things, Knowing.] [1623] Before whom nothing existed. Also, He who is supreme, foremost or uppermost.
[1624] Enduring eternally when nothing else remains.
[1625] Nothing being above Him. Another meaning is "the Apparent," i.e., evident through His creation and revelation.
[1626] Nothing being nearer than Him by way of His knowledge. Another meaning is "the Unapparent," i.e., concealed from man's physical senses. (57:3) (QuranEnc)
Narrated by Abu Dawud (5110) with a good chain, from Abu Zumayl, from Ibn Abbas. He advised this dhikr (remembrance) to repel whisperings and end doubts.
asmaa-husna-0157: Approximately how many times does the name al-Hakim occur in the Quran?
Al-Badr says Allah's name al-Hakim occurs in the Noble Quran approximately one hundred times.
asmaa-husna-0158: Allah's name al-Hakim establishes which two things for Him?
Al-Badr says this great name indicates that Allah possesses perfect judgment and perfect wisdom.
asmaa-husna-0159: When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) heard Hani' ibn Yazid's people calling him Abu al-Hakam, he said, «إن الله هو الحكم وإليه الحكم» [Allah is al-Hakam, and judgment belongs to Him]. Which kunyah (name beginning with Abu) did he then give him?

He asked which of his sons was eldest. He answered Shurayh, so he said: «فأنت أبو شريح» [Then you are Abu Shurayh]. Narrated by Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i, and authenticated by al-Albani. It is evidence for al-Hakam.
asmaa-husna-0160: What does Allah's perfect wisdom in His creation and religious law mean?
He places things in their proper positions and assigns them their proper ranks
He immediately punishes everyone who disobeys Him
He gives every petitioner exactly what they ask for, at the time they desire
He does not question His servants about their deeds
His perfect wisdom is established in His creation, command, and religious law: He places things in their proper positions and assigns them their proper ranks.
asmaa-husna-0161: How many times does Allah's name al-Mu'min occur in the Noble Quran?

﴿الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ السَّلَامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ﴾ [the Sovereign,[1658] the Pure,[1659] the Perfection,[1660] the Grantor of Security,[1661] the Overseer,[1662]] (QuranEnc) (al-Hashr 59:23). [1658] And owner of everything in existence. [1659] i.e., transcendent above any aspect belonging to His creation. Also, the possessor and grantor of blessings. [1660] Literally, "Free" from any imperfection. Also, "Peace" or "Soundness." [1661] And safety, i.e., reassurance that His promise is always fulfilled. Also, He who bestows faith. [1662] i.e., who observes, guards and protects. Also, "the Criterion."
asmaa-husna-0162: Mujahid said, 'al-Mu'min: the One who declared His own oneness by saying...' Which verse did he cite?
﴿فَاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ [So know, [O Muḥammad], that there is no deity except Allāh] (47:19) (QuranEnc)
﴿وَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ [And your god is one God.] (2:163) (QuranEnc)

﴿قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ [Say, "He is Allāh, [who is] One,[2011]] [2011] Alone, without another, indivisible with absolute and permanent unity and distinct from all else. The one and only true deity, unique in His essence, attributes and deeds. (112:1) (QuranEnc)
﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ [Allāh witnesses that there is no deity except Him,] (3:18) (QuranEnc)
Al-Badr quotes this in explaining al-Mu'min: it is a mighty testimony, from the greatest witness, to the greatest truth attested.
asmaa-husna-0163: How did Ibn Abbas explain Allah's name al-Mu'min, as reported by Ibn Kathir?
He confirmed His messengers through miracles
He declared His own oneness by His testimony
He assured His creation that He would not wrong them
He affirmed His word as true
Ibn Abbas said al-Mu'min means He assured His creation that He would not wrong them. 'He affirmed His word as true' is Qatadah's explanation.
asmaa-husna-0164: The meaning of iman in Allah's name al-Mu'min concerns:
Al-Badr says iman (affirmation) here concerns confirmation and affirmation, and what these entail of guidance and confirming those who speak the truth.
asmaa-husna-0165: In the hadith graded hasan (sound) by at-Tirmidhi, when a servant says «لا إله إلا الله والله أكبر» [there is no god but Allah, and Allah is Greatest,] (HadeethEnc), what does Allah, Blessed and Exalted, say?
My servant has spoken the truth; there is no god but Me, and I am Greatest
My servant has praised and glorified Me
My servant remembered Me, so I remembered him in an assembly
My servant testified to the truth, so bear witness for him
Narrated by at-Tirmidhi (3430) and Ibn Majah; included in as-Silsilah as-Sahihah (1391). Al-Badr cites it among the evidences for al-Mu'min.
asmaa-husna-0166: How many places in the Quran contain Allah's name al-Ghani?
Al-Badr says this name occurs in eighteen places in the Quran.
asmaa-husna-0167: Sulayman (peace be upon him) said, ﴿وَمَنْ شَكَرَ فَإِنَّمَا يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ رَبِّي ...﴾ [And whoever is grateful - his gratitude is only for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse end?

An-Naml 27:40. His perfect self-sufficiency means that the obedient person's obedience does not benefit Him and the disobedient person's disobedience does not harm Him. Verse ending: [And whoever is ungrateful - then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0168: ﴿وَرَبُّكَ الْغَنِيُّ ذُو ...﴾ [And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of ...] (QuranEnc) Which word follows in this verse of al-An'am?
Al-An'am 6:133. Al-Badr begins his evidence for al-Ghani with this verse. Verse: [And your Lord is the Free of need, the possessor of mercy.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0169: ﴿قَالُوا اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَدًا سُبْحَانَهُ هُوَ ...﴾ [They[533] have said, "Allāh has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is ...] (QuranEnc) Through which name does Allah declare Himself above having a son here?

Yunus 10:68. Whoever attributes deficiency to Allah attributes to Him what contradicts His self-sufficiency. Verse: [They[533] have said, "Allāh has taken a son." Exalted is He; He is the [one] Free of need.] [533] The Christians and others (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0170: Al-Badr says that whoever knows their Lord's absolute self-sufficiency knows their own:
Whoever knows their Lord's absolute self-sufficiency knows their own absolute need. Whoever knows their Lord's complete power knows their own complete incapacity.
asmaa-husna-0171: The only occurrence of Allah's name al-Akram in the Quran is:
﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ الْكَرِيمِ﴾ [O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous,] (82:6) (QuranEnc)
﴿رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ﴾ [Lord of the Noble Throne.] (23:116) (QuranEnc)
﴿فَإِنَّ رَبِّي غَنِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ﴾ [then indeed, my Lord is Free of need and Generous.] (27:40) (QuranEnc)
﴿اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ﴾ [Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous -] (96:3) (QuranEnc)

Al-Badr says al-Akram occurs once: ﴿اقْرَأْ وَرَبُّكَ الْأَكْرَمُ﴾ [Recite, and your Lord is the most Generous -] (QuranEnc) (al-Alaq 96:3). In ﴿رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ﴾ [Lord of the Noble Throne.] (QuranEnc) (al-Mu'minun 23:116), al-karim is genitive in Hafs's recitation, describing the Throne.
asmaa-husna-0172: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الْإِنْسَانُ مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ...﴾ [O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes the verse?
Al-Infitar 82:6; one of three occurrences of al-Karim. Full verse: [O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous,] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0174: How does al-Badr begin explaining Allah's name al-Karim?
The One who conceals faults and does not expose them
The One who gives the disobedient respite and does not hasten their punishment
The One who judges justly between His servants
The One of abundant goodness and immense benefit
Al-Karim is the One of abundant goodness and immense benefit. Karim describes the best and finest of anything. Karam (generosity and nobility) encompasses good and praiseworthy qualities.
asmaa-husna-0175: What does al-Badr identify as the greatest means of attaining honor from al-Karim?
Being mindful of Him in private and public

Those most honored by Him are His servants most mindful of Him: ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ﴾ [Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1521] of you.] (QuranEnc) (al-Hujurat 49:13). [1521] Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.
asmaa-husna-0176: Al-Badr states that Allah's name as-Salam encompasses:
Attributes of action, excluding attributes of essence
Matters of the Hereafter, excluding this world
All His attributes: each is free from every fault and deficiency
He says it encompasses all Allah's attributes. Every attribute of His is free from every fault and deficiency.
asmaa-husna-0177: In Ibn al-Qayyim's account of as-Salam, quoted by al-Badr, Allah's self-sustaining nature and power are free from:

His life is free from death, drowsiness, and sleep. His self-sustaining nature and power are free from fatigue and weariness. His knowledge is free from anything escaping Him or any forgetfulness occurring.
asmaa-husna-0178: An implication of as-Salam is that Allah is the One who gives salam. What does this mean?
The One who calls disputants to reconciliation
The One who protects bodies from all diseases
The One who made salam the Muslims' greeting only in this world
The One who greets His messengers, allies, and servants in Paradise with peace

Salam (a greeting of peace): He greets His messengers and prophets, ﴿سَلَامٌ عَلَى نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ [Peace upon Noah among the worlds.] (QuranEnc) (as-Saffat 37:79), and His servants and allies in the gardens of bliss, ﴿سَلَامٌ قَوْلًا مِنْ رَبٍّ رَحِيمٍ﴾ [[And] "Peace," a word from a Merciful Lord.] (QuranEnc) (Ya Sin 36:58).
asmaa-husna-0179: ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَدْعُو إِلَى دَارِ السَّلَامِ﴾ [And Allāh invites to the Home of Peace [i.e., Paradise]] (QuranEnc) In which surah does this verse occur?
Yunus 10:25. Allah made His Paradise the Home of Peace because its people are free from death, illness, and sorrow.
asmaa-husna-0180: How many times does Allah's name al-Quddus occur in the Noble Quran?
In Surat al-Hashr (23) and at the beginning of Surat al-Jumu'ah.
asmaa-husna-0181: ﴿يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ الْمَلِكِ الْقُدُّوسِ ...﴾ [Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allāh,[1685] the Sovereign, the Pure, ...] (QuranEnc) How does the first verse of Surat al-Jumu'ah end?

The first verse of al-Jumu'ah is the second of the two occurrences of al-Quddus. Full verse: [Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is exalting Allāh,[1685] the Sovereign, the Pure, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.[1686] [1685] See footnote to 57:1.
[1686] Refer to footnote in 6:18.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0182: Evidence for as-Subbuh is A'ishah's hadith in Sahih Muslim: the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said in bowing and prostration, «سبّوح قدّوس ربّ الملائكة و...» [You are the Most Glorious, the Most Holy, and the lord of the angels ...] (HadeethEnc).

Narrated by Muslim (487). It combines tasbih (declaring Allah above imperfection) and taqdis (declaring His holiness), as in the angels' words: ﴿وَنَحْنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَ﴾ [while we exalt You with praise and declare Your perfection?] (QuranEnc) (al-Baqarah 2:30). Note [18]: An additional meaning is "...and we purify ourselves for You."
asmaa-husna-0183: Al-Badr explains that declaring Allah's glory and holiness means affirming that He is free from every evil and fault, together with:
Denying attributes for fear of likening Him to creation
Consigning the meanings of all the names to Allah
Affirming His praiseworthy qualities and perfect attributes
Restricting oneself to names without attributes
Ibn Taymiyyah says that the command to glorify Allah entails declaring Him free from every fault and evil and affirming the praiseworthy qualities for which He is praised.
asmaa-husna-0184: Commenting on ﴿فَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ﴾ [Then exalt [Him] with praise of your Lord] (QuranEnc) (an-Nasr 110:3), Ibn Rajab said, 'Not every declaration of transcendence is praiseworthy.' Which group's declaration did he give as an example?
He says the Mu'tazilah's declaration of transcendence entails negating many attributes. Glorification through denial of attributes is blameworthy.
asmaa-husna-0185: At his death, Nuh (peace be upon him) advised his son to say «سبحان الله وبحمده» [Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Him]. What did he say about its merit?
It fills what is between heaven and earth
It sheds sins as leaves fall
It is the speech most beloved to Allah
It is the prayer of everything, and through it creation is provided for
Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad with an authentic chain, and included in as-Silsilah as-Sahihah (134). Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Quddus and as-Subbuh.
asmaa-husna-0186: According to al-Badr, how many times does Allah's name al-Hamid occur in the Noble Quran?
He says this name occurs in the Noble Quran seventeen times.
asmaa-husna-0187: According to al-Badr, Allah's name al-Hamid means:
The One to whom all praise belongs, praised in His essence, names, and attributes
The One praised only for outward blessings
The One who appreciates a little work and gives abundant reward for it
The One who praises His obedient servants among His angels
All praise belongs to Him. He is praised in His essence, names, and attributes; His names are the finest and His attributes the most perfect.
asmaa-husna-0188: Ibn Taymiyyah divided praise of Allah into two kinds: praise for His goodness to His servants, which is a form of gratitude, and praise:
For what He intrinsically deserves because of His perfect attributes
Only for the afflictions He averts
That occurs in the Hereafter but not in this world
Exclusive to angels rather than humans
The other kind is praise for what He intrinsically deserves because of His perfect attributes. Such praise belongs only to One who possesses attributes of perfection.
asmaa-husna-0189: ﴿فَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي نَجَّانَا مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ [then say, 'Praise to Allāh who has saved us from the wrongdoing people.'] (QuranEnc) According to al-Badr, for which blessing is Allah praised here?
Receiving a child in old age
Victory over enemies and safety from their evil
Revelation of the Book without crookedness
Entering Paradise, the abode of bliss
Al-Badr identifies it as a verse giving specific reasons for praise. It is al-Mu'minun (28).
asmaa-husna-0190: The angels said to Ibrahim's household, ﴿رَحْمَتُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ إِنَّهُ ...﴾ [May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names end the verse?

Hud 11:73. Ibn al-Qayyim says it is most fitting that al-Majid is paired with al-Hamid. Verse: [May the mercy of Allāh and His blessings be upon you, people of the house. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Honorable.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0192: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Majid?
The One whose attributes are vast and great, and whose descriptions are many and noble
The One free from faults, deficiencies, and imperfections
The One who answers supplication and accepts a little work
The One to whom all praise belongs in this life and the Hereafter
His attributes are vast and great, and His descriptions are many and noble. Al-Majid concerns the greatness, abundance, and vastness of His attributes.
asmaa-husna-0193: According to al-Badr, how many of Allah's beautiful names occur in Ayat al-Kursi, the greatest verse of the Quran?
He says Ayat al-Kursi, the greatest verse of the Noble Quran, contains five of Allah's beautiful names and more than twenty of His attributes.
asmaa-husna-0194: In the hadith «قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين» [I have divided prayer between Myself and My servant into two halves,] (HadeethEnc), when the servant says ﴿مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ [Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.[5]] (QuranEnc), what does Allah say?
This is between Me and My servant

Narrated by Muslim (395). Praise corresponds to ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ [[All] praise is [due] to Allāh,] (QuranEnc), extolling to ﴿الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,] (QuranEnc), and glorifying to ﴿مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ [Sovereign of the Day of Recompense.[5]] (QuranEnc). [5] i.e., repayment and compensation for whatever was earned of good or evil during life on this earth. The response choices follow.
asmaa-husna-0195: Ibn al-Qayyim explained why the Ibrahimic invocation in the tashahhud (testimony recited while sitting in prayer) ends with «إنك حميد مجيد» [Verily, You are Praiseworthy, All-Glorious.] (HadeethEnc). It is a context of:
Asking for more and seeking abundant, continuing gifts
Seeking refuge from punishment in the grave and the Fire
Praising the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) as he deserves
Because one is asking for more and seeking abundant, plentiful, continuing gifts, a name appropriate to that request is used.
asmaa-husna-0196: Ash-Shakur occurs in four Quranic passages. How many times does ash-Shakir occur?
Ash-Shakir occurs in al-Baqarah (158) and an-Nisa' (147); ash-Shakur in Fatir (30, 34), ash-Shura (23), and at-Taghabun (17).
asmaa-husna-0197: ﴿إِنْ تُقْرِضُوا اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا يُضَاعِفْهُ لَكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ شَكُورٌ ...﴾ [If you loan Allāh a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allāh is [most] Appreciative[1694] ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse end?

At-Taghabun 64:17; one of four occurrences of ash-Shakur. Full verse: [If you loan Allāh a goodly loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. And Allāh is [most] Appreciative[1694] and Forbearing,[1695] [1694] Who gives much in return for little.
[1695] Refer to footnote in 2:225.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0198: From their Quranic contexts, what meaning does al-Badr derive for ash-Shakur and ash-Shakir?
The One who punishes in this world those who deny His blessings
The One who loves His servants to praise Him abundantly
The One thanked for His outward and inward blessings at every time
The One who accepts a little work and rewards it abundantly
With ash-Shakur and ash-Shakir, no worker's deed is lost. He accepts a little work and rewards it abundantly.
asmaa-husna-0199: In three of its four Quranic occurrences, ash-Shakur is paired with which name?

﴿إِنَّهُ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾ [Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.[1250]] (QuranEnc) (Fatir 35:30); ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّنَا لَغَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾ [Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative] (QuranEnc) (Fatir 35:34); and ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ﴾ [Indeed, Allāh is Forgiving and Appreciative.[1421]] (QuranEnc) (ash-Shura 42:23). The fourth is paired with al-Halim. [1250] i.e., He gives much in return for little and multiplies rewards. [1421] See footnote in 35:30.
asmaa-husna-0200: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Halim?
The One who conceals His servants' faults and does not expose them before creation on the Day of Resurrection
The One who does not hasten to punish His servants for their sins
The One who gives His servants more than they ask for
The One who accepts repentance from those who turn to Him
He does not hasten to punish His servants for their sins and disobedience; He gives them respite so they may repent. His forbearance comes with knowledge and power, not incapacity.
asmaa-husna-0201: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُمْسِكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ أَنْ تَزُولَا ... إِنَّهُ كَانَ ...﴾ [Indeed, Allāh holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. ... Indeed, He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete this verse of Fatir?

Fatir 35:41. His holding the heavens and earth lest they cease, despite humanity's many sins, is part of His forbearance. Full verse: [Indeed, Allāh holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they should cease, no one could hold them [in place] after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing[1256] and Forgiving. [1256] Refer to footnote in 2:225.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0202: About which people did al-Hasan al-Basri say, 'Look at this generosity and bounty: they killed His allies, yet He calls them to repentance and forgiveness'?

He said it about ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ فَتَنُوا الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَتُوبُوا﴾ [Indeed, those who have tortured[1898] the believing men and believing women and then have not repented] (QuranEnc) (al-Buruj 85:10). Al-Badr cites it as evidence of Allah's forbearance. [1898] Or, in this instance, the literal meaning of "burned" is also appropriate.
asmaa-husna-0203: ﴿قَوْلٌ مَعْرُوفٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ خَيْرٌ مِنْ صَدَقَةٍ يَتْبَعُهَا أَذًى وَاللَّهُ ...﴾ [Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allāh is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Al-Baqarah 2:263 pairs al-Halim with al-Ghani: His forbearance is accompanied by complete freedom from need of His servants. Full verse: [Kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allāh is Free of need and Forbearing.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0204: A sign of Allah's forbearance, despite Pharaoh's extreme tyranny, is His command to Musa and Harun:
To pray immediately for his destruction
To speak gently to him, so that he might be reminded or fear Allah
To avoid him and never speak to him
To leave with their people without calling him to faith

﴿اذْهَبَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّهُ طَغَى فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّنًا لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشَى﴾ [Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed. And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [Allāh]."] (Ta Ha 20:43-44) (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0205: According to al-Badr, how many Quranic passages contain Allah's name al-Haqq?
He says Allah's name al-Haqq occurs in the Noble Quran in ten places.
asmaa-husna-0206: ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ الْحَقَّ وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ ...﴾ [That Day, Allāh will pay them in full their true [i.e., deserved] recompense, and they will know that it is Allāh who is the ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes the verse?

An-Nur 24:25 is the only occurrence of al-Mubin, paired with al-Haqq. The translation renders the pair together: [That Day, Allāh will pay them in full their true [i.e., deserved] recompense, and they will know that it is Allāh who is the manifest Truth [i.e., perfect in justice].] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0207: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Haqq?
The One who revealed the Book in truth to His Messenger
The One who manifests truth and supports its people in this world
The One concerning whom there is no doubt, in His essence, names, attributes, or divinity
The One who judges justly between His servants on the Day of Resurrection concerning their disputes
There is no doubt or uncertainty concerning Him: neither His essence, His names and attributes, nor His divinity.
asmaa-husna-0208: Which meaning of Allah's name al-Mubin does al-Badr mention?
The One who exposes His servants' secrets to people
The One who spoke the Quran in clear Arabic
The One who makes clear to His servants the path of right guidance and what earns reward or punishment
The One who makes truth clear only through resurrection and reckoning in the Hereafter
He makes clear to His servants the path of right guidance. Another meaning is that His oneness is evident.
asmaa-husna-0209: Which of the names al-Qadeer, al-Qaadir, and al-Muqtadir occurs most often in the Noble Quran?
Al-Badr says all these names occur in the Quran, most often al-Qadeer, then al-Qaadir, then al-Muqtadir. Qadeer and Qaadir distinguish the two Arabic vowel patterns.
asmaa-husna-0210: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ أَوْ مِنْ تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾ [Say, "He is the [one] Able to send upon you affliction from above you or from beneath your feet] (QuranEnc) In which surah does this verse occur?
Al-An'am 6:65. Al-Badr cites it as evidence for al-Qaadir.
asmaa-husna-0211: ﴿... فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ ...﴾ [... and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allāh is ever, over all things, ...] (QuranEnc) Which name completes this verse of al-Kahf?
Al-Kahf 18:45 is evidence for al-Muqtadir. Verse: [and [then] it becomes dry remnants, scattered by the winds. And Allāh is ever, over all things, Perfect in Ability.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0212: Al-Badr quotes Imam Ahmad's concise statement on the relationship between belief in divine decree and Allah's attributes. Which is it?
Divine decree is Allah's prior knowledge
Divine decree is Allah's effective will
Divine decree is Allah's preserved Book
Imam Ahmad said, 'Qadar (divine decree) is Allah's power.' Denying divine decree denies Allah's power, indicated by al-Qadeer, al-Qaadir, and al-Muqtadir.
asmaa-husna-0213: Ibn Jarir narrates that Ibn Abbas explained those with knowledge in ﴿إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى اللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ الْعُلَمَاءُ﴾ [Only those fear Allāh, from among His servants, who have knowledge.] (QuranEnc) (Fatir 35:28) as:
Those who memorize the Quran and act upon it
Those who know that Allah has power over everything
Those who offer many voluntary prayers and fasts
Those who teach people what is lawful and unlawful
Ibn al-Qayyim comments that this shows Ibn Abbas's understanding, knowledge of interpretation, and awareness of the realities of Allah's names and attributes.
asmaa-husna-0215: Allah's name al-Wadud occurs in two Quranic passages: one in Hud, and the other in:
asmaa-husna-0216: ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّي ...﴾ [And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is ...] (QuranEnc) With which two names did Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) conclude his call to his people?
Hud 11:90 is the first occurrence of al-Wadud. Full verse: [And ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate."] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0217: Ibn Sa'di says al-Wadud means both the One who loves and the One who is loved. These meanings imply:
He loves all creation equally without distinction
He loves His allies and chosen servants, and they love Him
He is loved but cannot be described as loving
He loves angels alone, excluding all other creation
He is al-Wadud in the senses of loving and being loved: He loves His allies and chosen servants, and they love Him.
asmaa-husna-0218: According to Ibn Sa'di, what may be the reason al-Wadud is paired with al-Ghafur in ﴿وَهُوَ الْغَفُورُ الْوَدُودُ﴾ [And He is the Forgiving, the Affectionate,] (QuranEnc) (al-Buruj 85:14)?
The names mean the same thing and are paired for emphasis
He forgives the repentant person's crimes and then restores His affection and love for them
Al-Wadud is exclusive to prophets and al-Ghafur to others
Forgiveness is in this world and affection in the Hereafter
He forgives those crimes and restores His affection and love for the person. Ibn Sa'di says this may be the reason for pairing al-Wadud with al-Ghafur; Allah knows best.
asmaa-husna-0219: The transmitted supplication «أسألك حبك، وحب من يحبك، وحب عمل يقربني إلى حبك» [I ask You to grant me Your Love, the love of those who love You, and the love of deeds that bring me closer to Your Love.] (HadeethEnc) is narrated by:
Narrated by Ahmad and at-Tirmidhi in a long hadith from Mu'adh, authenticated by at-Tirmidhi. Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Wadud.
asmaa-husna-0220: Allah's name al-Barr occurs in one Quranic passage: ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا مِنْ قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْبَرُّ ...﴾ [Indeed, we used to supplicate[1556] Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, ...] (QuranEnc) How does it end?
At-Tur 52:28 is the only occurrence of al-Barr. Full verse: [Indeed, we used to supplicate[1556] Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful." [1556] i.e., worship.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0221: According to al-Badr, Allah's name al-Barr means:
The One whose goodness, favor, and giving encompass all beings
The One who rewards the good-doer and punishes the wrongdoer
The One who never breaks His promise and wrongs no one
The One who knows the righteousness, sin, good, and evil concealed in hearts
His goodness, favor, and giving encompass all beings. He is the bestower of blessings, abundant in giving and constant in goodness.
asmaa-husna-0222: In the hadith agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, Allah brings the believer near on the Day of Resurrection, conceals him, and makes him acknowledge his sins. Then He says:
My angels interceded for you, so I forgave you
I replaced your bad deeds with good deeds because of your patience
I pardoned you for your many prayers and fasts
I have concealed them for you in the worldly life, and I forgive them for you today
Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim from Ibn Umar. Al-Badr cites it as evidence for al-Barr: His pardoning His servants and concealing their sins. Fourth option: (HadeethEnc).
asmaa-husna-0223: How did Qatadah explain ﴿لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾ [Never will you attain the good [reward][138] until you spend [in the way of Allāh] from that which you love.] (QuranEnc) (Al Imran 3:92)?
You will not enter Paradise until you give away all you own
You will not attain your Lord's goodness until you spend from wealth you cherish
You will not attain piety until you abandon worldly life
Your prayer will not be accepted until you pay zakah

Al-Badr quotes him from Ibn Jarir's tafsir (Quran commentary): you will not attain your Lord's goodness until you spend from wealth you admire and desire. [138] Another meaning is "You will never attain righteousness."
asmaa-husna-0224: In how many Quran verses does Allah's name ar-Ra'uf occur?
Al-Badr says this name occurs in ten verses of the Noble Quran, then presents them with their implications.
asmaa-husna-0225: Al-Badr quotes Ibn Jarir's explanation of ra'fah as:
Mercy toward animals rather than people
Ibn Jarir says ra'fah (compassion) is the highest degree of mercy. It encompasses all creation in this world, and some of them in the Hereafter.
asmaa-husna-0226: When explaining ar-Ra'uf, al-Badr quotes a scholarly principle: ending a verse with one of Allah's names indicates:
The ruling mentioned in it relates to that name
Its ruling has been abrogated by another verse
The verse was revealed in Makkah before the Hijrah
The name is greater than all other names
Ending Quran verses with Allah's beautiful names indicates that the ruling mentioned in the verse relates to that noble name.
asmaa-husna-0227: ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْرِي نَفْسَهُ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاتِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ ...﴾ [And of the people is he who sells himself, seeking means to the approval of Allāh. And Allāh is ...] (QuranEnc) How does the verse end?
Free of need of the worlds

Al-Baqarah 2:207. These are people whom Allah enabled to give themselves in seeking His approval. Full verse: [And of the people is he who sells himself, seeking means to the approval of Allāh. And Allāh is Kind to [His] servants.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0228: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جَاءُوا مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا وَلِإِخْوَانِنَا ... رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ ...﴾ [And [there is a share for] those who come after them, saying, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers ... Our Lord, indeed You are ...] (QuranEnc) How does this supplication in Surat al-Hashr end?

Al-Hashr 59:10. Part of His compassion is that He makes later believers love and pray for earlier believers. Full verse: [And [there is a share for] those who come after them, saying, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0229: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Hasib?
The One who recompenses good deeds but not bad deeds
The One who counts days and years
The One who only takes creation to account on the Day of Resurrection
The One who suffices His servants in their concerns and preserves their deeds
He suffices His servants in all their religious and worldly concerns. Another meaning of al-Hasib is that He preserves everything His servants have done.
asmaa-husna-0230: Regarding ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾ [And whoever relies upon Allāh - then He is sufficient for him.] (QuranEnc) (at-Talaq 65:3), some early Muslims said Allah made the recompense for relying upon Him:
His own sufficing of His servant
He did not say, 'We will give him such-and-such reward,' as He said for deeds. Rather, He made Himself the One who suffices the servant relying on Him.
asmaa-husna-0231: Allah follows ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسْبُهُ﴾ [And whoever relies upon Allāh - then He is sufficient for him.] (QuranEnc) with ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا﴾ [Allāh has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.] (QuranEnc) (at-Talaq 65:3). According to Ibn al-Qayyim, what is the wisdom?
To show that reliance does not help against divine decree
To prevent assuming that sufficiency must come immediately when one relies on Him
To show that sufficiency is exclusive to prophets

One might assume that sufficiency must come immediately when one relies on Him, so He follows it with ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا﴾ [Allāh has already set for everything a [decreed] extent.] (QuranEnc), meaning an appointed time that it does not exceed.
asmaa-husna-0232: When going to bed, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «الحمد لله الذي أطعمنا وسقانا وكفانا وآوانا، فكم ممن ...» [Praise be to Allah Who gave us food and drink, provided for us sufficiently, and gave us shelter, for how many there are ...] (HadeethEnc).
Who have no one to provide for them or to give them shelter
Who have no family or wealth
Who have no refuge or dwelling
Who have no food or drink
Narrated by Muslim (2715). Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Hasib.
asmaa-husna-0233: Which verse does al-Badr cite for Allah's general disposal of all creation's affairs?

﴿حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ﴾ [Sufficient for us is Allāh, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.] [150] The one entrusted and relied upon; sufficient to manage all matters. (3:173) (QuranEnc)
﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ وَكِيلًا﴾ [And rely upon Allāh; and sufficient is Allāh as Disposer of affairs.[1179]] [1179] Refer to footnote in 3:173. (33:3) (QuranEnc)
﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ [And He is Disposer of all things.] (6:102) (QuranEnc)

﴿أَلَّا تَتَّخِذُوا مِنْ دُونِي وَكِيلًا﴾ [that you not take other than Me as Disposer of affairs,[726]] [726] i.e., trust in Allāh, knowing that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) is responsible for every occurrence. (17:2) (QuranEnc)

General wakalah (disposal of affairs) means providing for created things and managing them, as in ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ﴾ [And He is Disposer of all things.] (QuranEnc) (al-An'am 6:102). Special wakalah concerns believers who rely on Him.
asmaa-husna-0234: Tawakkul combines two foundations: the heart's reliance on Allah alone, and:
Taking the means one has been commanded to take

Tawakkul (reliance on Allah) combines reliance of the heart on Allah alone, without partner, and taking commanded means, as in ﴿فَاعْبُدْهُ وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ [so worship Him and rely upon Him.] (QuranEnc) (Hud 11:123).
asmaa-husna-0235: Al-Badr compares the position of reliance on Allah among the stations and deeds of religion to:
The soul in relation to the body
The body in relation to the head
The foundation in relation to a building
Reliance on Allah is the foundation of all religious stations. Its position is like that of the body in relation to the head: just as the head can only be supported by the body...
asmaa-husna-0236: ﴿رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ ...﴾ [[He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as ...] (QuranEnc) Which word completes the verse?

Al-Muzzammil 73:9. Al-Badr cites it regarding Allah's call to His servants to rely on Him alone, explaining al-Wakil. Full verse: [[He is] the Lord of the East and the West; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of [your] affairs.[1782] [1782] i.e., trust in Allāh and rely upon Him.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0237: According to al-Badr, how many Quranic passages contain Allah's name an-Nasir?

Examples include ﴿نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ﴾ [Excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.] (QuranEnc) (al-Anfal 8:40) and ﴿وَكَفَى بِاللَّهِ نَصِيرًا﴾ [and sufficient is Allāh as a helper.] (QuranEnc) (an-Nisa' 4:45).
asmaa-husna-0238: How does al-Badr explain Allah's name an-Nasir?
The One who answers the distressed on land and sea and removes their harm
The One who accepts the intercession of intercessors on the Day of Resurrection
The One who undertakes to help His servants, support His allies, and defend them
The One who grants victory to everyone who fights, even a wrongdoer
An-Nasir undertakes to help His servants, support His allies, and defend them. Victory comes only from Him.
asmaa-husna-0239: When setting out for battle, the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «اللهم أنت عضدي و...، بك أجول وبك أصول وبك أقاتل» [O Allah, You are my support and ..., through You I move about, through You I attack, and through You I fight]. What word is missing?
Narrated by Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi, who graded it hasan (sound), from Anas. Al-Badr cites it in explaining an-Nasir.
asmaa-husna-0240: According to Ibn al-Qayyim as quoted by al-Badr, a servant can strive against and overcome an outward enemy only if they:
Ally with someone stronger than the enemy
Strive against their inward enemies: the soul, desire, Satan, and worldly life
Withdraw from people and devote themselves exclusively to worship
Have more people and equipment than the enemy
Only one who strives inwardly against these enemies can strive against an outward enemy. Whoever is given victory over them is given victory over the outward enemy.
asmaa-husna-0241: Of the names in this verse of al-Hashr, ﴿الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ﴾ [the Exalted in Might,[1663] the Compeller,[1664] the Superior.[1665]] (QuranEnc), which occurs nearly one hundred times in the Quran?

Al-Badr says al-Jabbar occurs only in this verse, whereas al-Aziz occurs nearly one hundred times. Al-Hashr 59:23 notes: [1663] Refer to footnote in 2:129. [1664] Whose irresistible force is without limitation; the one above all things who compels the creation to be as He wills it. Also, "the Amender" or "the Rectifier" who repairs, restores, completes or sets something right once again, out of His mercy. [1665] Supreme, complete and perfect in His essence, attributes and actions.
asmaa-husna-0242: The might indicated by al-Aziz has three meanings. One is 'might of invulnerability.' What does that mean?
He refrains from answering those who do not deserve it
He is intrinsically free of need, depends on no one, and His servants cannot reach Him with harm or benefit
He withholds provision from His servants if they disobey
He cannot be seen by the eyes in this world
He is intrinsically free of need and depends on no one. His servants cannot reach Him with harm so as to harm Him, or with benefit so as to benefit Him.
asmaa-husna-0243: Which meaning of al-Jabbar concerns gentle mercy and compassion?
The One who immediately punishes the arrogant
The One who mends the broken, enriches the poor, and eases difficulty
The One who compels His servants to do their deeds
The One who takes vengeance on wrongdoers only in this world

Al-Jabbar has three meanings: the Subduer; the One who mends the broken and enriches the poor; and the One exalted above everything. It does not mean that a servant is compelled to perform their deeds.
asmaa-husna-0244: Between the two prostrations, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: «اللهم اغفر لي وارحمني و... واهدني وارزقني» [O Allah, forgive me, have mercy on me, ... guide me, and provide for me]. Which missing phrase relates to al-Jabbar?
Narrated by at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from Ibn Abbas, and authenticated by al-Albani. Jabr (mending) here means setting the servant's condition right and averting hardships.
asmaa-husna-0245: Salih (peace be upon him) said to his people, ﴿فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ ثُمَّ تُوبُوا إِلَيْهِ إِنَّ رَبِّي ...﴾ [so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is ...] (QuranEnc) With which two names did he end?
Hud 11:61; al-Mujib occurs nowhere else. Verse: [so ask forgiveness of Him and then repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive.] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0246: According to al-Badr, the nearness indicated by ﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِي عَنِّي فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ﴾ [And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near.] (QuranEnc) (al-Baqarah 2:186) is:
Spatial nearness specifically to people in mosques
Nearness that makes supplication and asking unnecessary
General nearness in essence to all created things
Special nearness to those who supplicate and worship, whose effects are known through kindness and response
The nearness indicated by these verses is special nearness to worshippers who love Him and supplicants who respond to Him. Its effects are known.
asmaa-husna-0247: ﴿قُلْ إِنْ ضَلَلْتُ فَإِنَّمَا أَضِلُّ عَلَى نَفْسِي وَإِنِ اهْتَدَيْتُ فَبِمَا يُوحِي إِلَيَّ رَبِّي إِنَّهُ ...﴾ [Say, "If I should err, I would only err against myself. But if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is ...] (QuranEnc) Which two names complete the verse?

Saba' 34:50; one of the three occurrences of al-Qarib. Full verse: [Say, "If I should err, I would only err against myself. But if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and near."] (QuranEnc).
asmaa-husna-0248: «إذا دعا أحدكم فلا يقل: اللهم اغفر لي إن شئت، ولكن ليعزم المسألة وليعظم الرغبة؛ فإن الله ...» [When one of you supplicates, he should not say: O Allah, forgive me if You will. Instead, let him supplicate with resolve and express his desire strongly, for indeed, ...].
Is near to whoever calls upon Him
Loves those who persist in supplication
nothing is too great for Allah to give
Does not tire until you tire
Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah; wording from Muslim. Al-Badr cites it in explaining al-Mujib. The correct choice reproduces the matching.
asmaa-husna-0249: According to al-Badr, the mutawatir (mass-transmitted) hadith of Allah's descent in the last third of the night was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, by:
He said: 'It is a mass-transmitted hadith narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, by a group of Companions numbering twenty-eight.'
asmaa-husna-0250: «ما من مسلم يدعو بدعوة ليس فيها إثم ولا قطيعة رحم إلا أعطاه الله بها إحدى ثلاث» [No Muslim invokes Allah with a supplication that does not involve sin or severing ties of kinship, except that Allah will grant him one of three (HadeethEnc)] His supplication is answered soon, it is saved for him in the Hereafter, or:
An equivalent amount of evil is averted from him
He is raised a rank in Paradise
Narrated by Ahmad, al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, and al-Hakim, who graded it authentic. Responding to a supplicant is broader than giving the exact thing requested.
asmaa-husna-0251: Both occurrences of Allah's name al-Qahir in the Quran are in Surah:

﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَهُوَ الْحَكِيمُ الْخَبِيرُ﴾ [And He is the subjugator over His servants. And He is the Wise,[296] the Aware.[297] Notes: [296] Whose wisdom includes precise, perfect and absolute knowledge of all realities and outcomes, according to which He decrees and causes circumstances and occurrences.
[297] Fully acquainted and familiar with every hidden thought, intent and condition of His servants. — Quran 6:18 (QuranEnc)]; ﴿وَهُوَ الْقَاهِرُ فَوْقَ عِبَادِهِ وَيُرْسِلُ عَلَيْكُمْ حَفَظَةً﴾ [And He is the subjugator over His servants, and He sends over you guardian-angels until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers [i.e., angels of death] take him, and they do not fail [in their duties]. — Quran 6:61 (QuranEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0252: The name al-Qahhar occurs six times in the Quran. In every occurrence it is joined to which two names?
Al-Badr said: 'Allah's name al-Qahhar occurs six times in the Noble Quran, in every case joined to the two names Allah and al-Wahid.'
asmaa-husna-0253:
﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ...﴾ [Say, [O Muḥammad], "I am only a warner, and there is not any deity except Allāh, the One, the Prevailing,[1332] Notes: [1332] Refer to footnotes in 12:39. — Quran 38:65 (QuranEnc)] The source quotation also includes the opening of 38:66, whose full translation is: [Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might,[1333] the Perpetual Forgiver."[1334] Notes: [1333] Honored for absolute power associated with wisdom and justice.
[1334] Who continually conceals sins and faults (QuranEnc)]. Which two names end these verses of Surah Sad?
Verses 65-66 of Surah Sad. This is the fourth occurrence of al-Qahhar, in a passage establishing Allah's sole right to worship. The quotation ends with a gap before the requested names.
asmaa-husna-0254: The name al-Warith occurs in the Quran in three passages. In all three it takes which form?

﴿وَنَحْنُ الْوَارِثُونَ﴾ [And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.[674] Notes: [674] Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) remains after all creation has passed away. — Quran 15:23 (QuranEnc)]; ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ [And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors." — Quran 21:89 (QuranEnc)]; ﴿وَكُنَّا نَحْنُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ [And how many a city have We destroyed that was insolent in its [way of] living, and those are their dwellings which have not been inhabited after them except briefly.[1114] And it is We who were the inheritors. Notes: [1114] By travelers seeking temporary shelter. The reference is to the ruins which were visible to the Quraysh during their journeys. — Quran 28:58 (QuranEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0255: How did al-Badr explain the meaning of Allah's name al-Warith?
The One who divides estates among heirs
The One who remains after creation perishes, to whom all return and finally go
The One who grants prophets knowledge and wisdom as an inheritance
The One who owns the earth and its inhabitants in this world but not the Hereafter and recompense
Al-Warith means the One who remains after creation perishes. Everything besides Him passes away... He causes owners and their possessions to perish and inherits all creation.
asmaa-husna-0256: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَنَحْنُ نُحْيِي وَنُمِيتُ وَنَحْنُ ...﴾ [And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritor.[674] Notes: [674] Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) remains after all creation has passed away. — Quran 15:23 (QuranEnc)] Which word completes the gapped Arabic verse from Surah al-Hijr?
Surah al-Hijr, verse 23: We inherit the earth and all upon it, and no living one remains except Us.
asmaa-husna-0257: Which prophet invoked Allah through the meaning of al-Warith, choosing a name appropriate to what he requested?
Ibrahim, peace be upon him, when building the House
Sulayman, peace be upon him, when asking for kingship
Zakariyya, peace be upon him, when asking for a child
Ayyub, peace be upon him, when afflicted by harm
