﴿رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ [And [mention] Zechariah, when he called to his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors." — Quran 21:89 (QuranEnc)] Allah answered him and granted him Yahya.
asmaa-husna-0258: According to al-Badr, the inheritance in Zakariyya's supplication ﴿يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ﴾ [Who will inherit me[809] and inherit from the family of Jacob. And make him, my Lord, pleasing [to You]." Notes: [809] Inherit from me religious knowledge and prophethood. — Quran 19:6 (QuranEnc)] is:
An inheritance of money, land and houses
An inheritance of lineage and social standing
An inheritance of knowledge, prophethood and calling to Allah, rather than money
An inheritance of kingship and authority
He said: 'The inheritance mentioned here is an inheritance of knowledge, prophethood and calling to Allah, the Almighty and Majestic, rather than an inheritance of money.'
asmaa-husna-0259: «يقول ابن آدم: مالي مالي، وهل لك يا ابن آدم من مالك إلا ما أكلت فأفنيت، أو لبست فأبليت، أو ...» [The.]
Left as an inheritance and gave away
Gave in charity and sent ahead
Gave as a gift and pleased others
Narrated by Muslim (2958) from Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir. Al-Badr cited it in explaining al-Warith.
asmaa-husna-0261: How did Qatada explain Allah's name al-Mutakabbir?
The One who punishes arrogance in this world
The One who humiliates the arrogant
The One who regards Himself as above His creation
The One exalted above every evil
Qatada said: 'He is exalted above every evil.' Abu Ishaq as-Sabii said: 'The One too exalted to wrong His servants.'
asmaa-husna-0262: When explaining al-Mutakabbir, whom mentioned in the Quran did al-Badr call 'the leader of the arrogant'?

'He, exalted is He, mentioned Iblis, the leader of the arrogant': ﴿إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ اسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ [Except Iblees;[1336] he was arrogant and became among the disbelievers. Notes: [1336] See footnote to 2:34. — Quran 38:74 (QuranEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0263: Al-Badr described al-Muqaddim and al-Muakhkhir as paired, contrasting names. What does that mean?
They mean the same thing, so either one suffices
They concern only Judgment Day and the Reckoning, not this world
They apply equally to Allah and His creation
Neither is applied to Allah without being paired with the other
'These two are paired, contrasting names: neither is applied alone to Allah without the other, because perfection lies in their combination.'
asmaa-husna-0264: In Ali's report in Muslim, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would say «اللهم اغفر لي ما قدمت وما أخرت ... أنت المقدم وأنت المؤخر لا إله إلا أنت» [O Allah, forgive my past and future sins, ... Indeed, You are the One Who puts forward, and You are the One Who puts back. There is no god but You (HadeethEnc)] When did he say this?
Between the tashahhud (testimony recitation) and taslim (closing salutation)

«ثم يكون من آخر ما يقول بين التشهد والتسليم...» [Then, one of the last things he would say between the Tashahhud and Taslīm is (HadeethEnc)] Narrated by Muslim (771), as evidence for the two names. The question's Arabic also includes a gap, then al-Muqaddim and al-Muakhkhir and the declaration that there is no deity but Allah.
asmaa-husna-0265: The advancing and delaying indicated by al-Muqaddim and al-Muakhkhir may concern Allah's cosmic decree and also:
Reasoning that people discern through reflection alone
Religious preference, such as favoring prophets over creation and some prophets over others
Choice, according to a servant's wish and will
'It may also concern religious preference, as He favored prophets over creation and some over others... All of this follows His wisdom, exalted is He.'
asmaa-husna-0266: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw his Companions hanging back and said: «تقدموا فائتموا بي، وليأتم بكم من بعدكم، لا يزال قوم يتأخرون حتى ...» [Come forward and be close to me and let those who come after you, follow your lead. If people continue to fall behind, ... (HadeethEnc)] Complete the warning that people continue to hang back until:
They are denied the first row
Narrated by Muslim (438) from Abu Said al-Khudri. Al-Badr cited it among the fruits of believing in al-Muqaddim and al-Muakhkhir.
asmaa-husna-0267: The root meaning of tayyib is purity and freedom from foulness. Accordingly, how does al-Badr explain Allah's name at-Tayyib?
The One who provides His servants with wholesome foods
The Holy One, exalted above every deficiency and flaw
The One who loves pleasant fragrances
The One who comforts His servants' hearts with admonition
It means that He, exalted is He, is holy and above all deficiencies and flaws, because the root meaning of tayyib is purity and freedom from foulness.
asmaa-husna-0268: As al-Badr and Ibn al-Qayyim explained, which expression in the tashahhud (testimony recitation) encompasses the meaning of at-Tayyib?
Ibn al-Qayyim said that at-tayyibat describes an omitted noun: all good words, deeds, attributes and names belong to Allah alone.
asmaa-husna-0270: In Allah's statement ﴿سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ طِبْتُمْ فَادْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ﴾ [But those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened and its keepers say, "Peace be upon you; you have become pure; so enter it to abide eternally therein," [they will enter].[1362] Notes: [1362] In such honor and joy that is beyond description - thus, the omission of this conclusion in the Arabic text. — Quran 39:73 (QuranEnc)] entry follows goodness with the connective fa. What does this indicate?
Their goodness is the reason for their admission to Paradise
The greeting of peace is a condition for entry
'He made entry follow goodness with the letter fa, indicating that it is the reason for entry: because of your goodness, you were told to enter.'
asmaa-husna-0271: Al-Bukhari narrated that a Companion performed ruqyah (healing recitation) for Thabit al-Bunani using the Messenger's words: «اللهم رب الناس مذهب الباس، اشف أنت الشافي...» [Oh Allah, Lord of mankind, Remover of harm. Cure, You are the Curer (HadeethEnc)] Who was he?

Abdul-Aziz ibn Suhayb said: Thabit and I visited Anas ibn Malik, who said: 'Shall I perform for you the healing recitation of Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him?' Narrated by al-Bukhari.
asmaa-husna-0272: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name ash-Shafi?
The One who created medicines but not illnesses
The One who heals only those sincere in their intentions
The One who intercedes for His servants on Judgment Day
The One from whom comes healing of hearts from doubts and bodies from illness
Ash-Shafi means the One from whom healing comes: healing hearts from misconceptions, doubts and envy... and healing bodies from diseases and afflictions.
asmaa-husna-0273: The Bedouins asked the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, about medical treatment. He said: «تداووا؛ فإن الله لم يضع داء إلا وضع له شفاء غير داء واحد» [Seek treatment, for Allah has not made a disease without making a cure for it, except for one disease.] What is it?
Narrated by Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Hibban with an authentic chain from Usama ibn Sharik. Seeking treatment does not contradict believing that Allah is ash-Shafi.
asmaa-husna-0274: Which is one of the three things that must be understood about means, as al-Badr explained under ash-Shafi?
To rely inwardly on a means as long as people have found it useful
To believe that a means acts independently by itself
To regard something as a means only if established by revelation or by observable causation
To abandon all means in reliance upon Allah

The three are: recognize only means established by revelation or observable causation; rely on the One who causes their effects rather than on the means themselves; and know that they are bound to Allah's decree and predestination.
asmaa-husna-0275: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said «إن الله جميل يحب الجمال» [Verily, Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty (HadeethEnc)] in answer to a man asking about:
A man's liking his clothes and shoes to look good
Narrated by Muslim (91) from Ibn Masud. The continuation is «الكبر بطر الحق وغمط الناس» [Arrogance is to reject the truth and look down on people (HadeethEnc)] This is evidence for the name al-Jamil.
asmaa-husna-0276: Ibn al-Qayyim listed four aspects of Allah's beauty: His essence, His attributes, His actions, and His:
His beauty has four aspects: beauty of essence, attributes, actions and names. All His names are beautiful.
asmaa-husna-0277: The hadith «إن الله جميل يحب الجمال» [Verily, Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty (HadeethEnc)] includes two great principles. The first is knowledge; the second is:
One first knows Allah through His beauty, in which nothing resembles Him, and worships Him through the beauty He loves in words, deeds and character.
asmaa-husna-0278: Al-Badr quoted Ibn al-Qayyim when explaining al-Jamil: 'Love has two motives: beauty and ...'
Love has two motives: beauty and majesty. The Lord, exalted is He, possesses absolute perfection in these, for He is beautiful and loves beauty.
asmaa-husna-0279: Muslim narrated the hadith «فيكشف الحجاب فما أُعطوا شيئًا أحب إليهم من النظر إلى ربهم» [He will then lift the veil, and out of all the things they are given, nothing will be dearer to them than looking at their Almighty Lord (HadeethEnc)] from which Companion?
Muslim (181), from Suhayb. Al-Badr cited it when explaining al-Jamil: the greatest blessing is that the people of Paradise see their beautiful Lord, exalted is He.
asmaa-husna-0280: How did al-Badr explain qabd and bast in Allah's names al-Qabid and al-Basit?
Qabd is restricting provision; bast is expanding it
Qabd is withholding punishment; bast is hastening it
Qabd is taking souls; bast is spreading creation on Resurrection Day
Qabd is closing the gates of repentance; bast is opening them
Qabd means restricting provision; bast means expanding it and making it abundant. All of this is in Allah's hand, according to the benefit He sees in it.
asmaa-husna-0281: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا ... وَاللَّهُ يَقْبِضُ وَيَبْسُطُ وَإِلَيْهِ ...﴾ [Who is it that would loan Allāh a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? And it is Allāh who withholds and grants abundance, and to Him you will be returned. — Quran 2:245 (QuranEnc)] What completes the gapped Arabic verse?
Surah al-Baqarah, verse 245. Ibn Jarir explained that restricting and expanding people's provision is in Allah's hand alone.
asmaa-husna-0282: When did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say «اللهم لك الحمد كله، اللهم لا قابض لما بسطت، ولا باسط لما قبضت...» [O Allah, all praise belongs to You.]
During the Farewell Pilgrimage sermon at Arafah
At Uhud when the polytheists withdrew
On entering Makkah at its conquest
He told his Companions, 'Stand in order so that I may praise my Lord,' and they formed rows behind him. Narrated by Ahmad and al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad; al-Albani graded it authentic.
asmaa-husna-0284: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Mannan?
The One whose favors are upon His servants, while none of them has any favor over Him
The One who withholds gifts from whichever servants He wills
The One who gives in proportion to a servant's deeds
The One who gives and then hurts the recipient by recounting His gifts
Al-Mannan gives abundantly, bestows great gifts and has vast beneficence... He begins giving before being asked. His favors are upon His servants, while none has any favor over Him.
asmaa-husna-0285: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا قُلْ لَا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ ...﴾ [They consider it a favor to you that they have accepted Islām. Say, "Do not consider your Islām a favor to me. Rather, Allāh has conferred favor upon you that He has guided you to the faith, if you should be truthful." — Quran 49:17 (QuranEnc)] What completes the gapped Arabic verse?

Surah al-Hujurat, verse 17. Al-Badr cited it for the favor of guidance to this religion when discussing al-Mannan. The full published verse is supplied in brackets; options transliterate the Arabic completions.
asmaa-husna-0286: According to al-Badr, in how many hadiths does Allah's name al-Hayiyy occur?
The report of Yala ibn Umayya in Abu Dawud and an-Nasai, and the report of Salman al-Farisi in Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah.
asmaa-husna-0287: In Salman's report, «إن ربكم تبارك وتعالى حييٌّ ...، يستحي من عبده إذا رفع يديه إليه أن يردهما صفرًا» [Verily, your Lord is Bashful ... He is too Bashful of His slave to let him go empty-handed when raising his hands to Him (HadeethEnc)] Which name occupies the Arabic gap?
Narrated by Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah; included in Sahih al-Jami. This is one of the two reports containing al-Hayiyy.
asmaa-husna-0288: In the report of three men who approached the Prophet's gathering, what did he say of the one who sat behind the circle? «...» [....]
He sought refuge with Allah, so Allah gave him refuge
He felt shy before Allah, so Allah was shy toward him
He turned away, so Allah turned away from him
He humbled himself before Allah, so Allah raised him
Agreed upon, from Abu Waqid al-Laythi. Al-Badr cited it as an instance of bashfulness being attributed to Allah as a verb.
asmaa-husna-0289: Ibn al-Qayyim described the Lord's bashfulness toward His servant as beyond human comprehension. It is bashfulness arising from:
Weakness and inability to hold someone accountable
The Lord's bashfulness toward His servant is of another kind, beyond comprehension and beyond minds' ability to describe its manner: bashfulness of generosity, kindness, munificence and majesty.
asmaa-husna-0290: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَنْ يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَا ...﴾ [Indeed, Allāh is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller[15] than it. And those who have believed know that it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allāh intend by this as an example?" He misleads many thereby and guides many thereby. And He misleads not except the defiantly disobedient, Notes: [15] Literally, "above it," i.e., greater in smallness. — Quran 2:26 (QuranEnc)] Which word fills the gap in the Arabic verse?
Surah al-Baqarah, verse 26. Al-Badr cited it as an instance of bashfulness attributed to Allah in verb form.
asmaa-husna-0291: The Banu Amir delegation said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, 'You are our master.' He replied:
«السيد الله تبارك وتعالى» [The Master is Allah (HadeethEnc)]

Narrated by Abu Dawud with a good chain from Abdullah ibn ash-Shikhkhir; evidence for as-Sayyid. Its continuation is «السيد» [Say what you have to say, or part of what you have to say, but do not let the devil deviate you (in praising me) (HadeethEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0292: Ibn Abbas explained Allah's statement ﴿قُلْ أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبًّا﴾ [Say, "Is it other than Allāh I should desire as a lord while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [blame] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ." — Quran 6:164 (QuranEnc)] as:
Al-Badr quoted this from at-Tabari's commentary. Ibn Jarir said: 'Should I seek a master other than Allah to rule over me, when He is the master of everything besides Him?'
asmaa-husna-0293: What did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, mean by «السيد الله» [The Master is Allah (HadeethEnc)] according to al-Badr?
The word sayyid applies only to prophets and messengers, not other people
True mastery belongs to Allah: He is the Owner, Patron and Lord, and creation are His servants
It is absolutely forbidden to call anyone sayyid
Sovereignty belongs to Allah only in the Hereafter, not in this world
He meant that true mastery belongs to Allah, the Almighty and Majestic: He is the Owner, Patron and Lord, and all creation are His servants.
asmaa-husna-0294: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said «يا عائشة إن الله رفيق يحب الرفق في الأمر كله» [O Aisha, Allah is gentle and loves gentleness in every matter.] after she:
Rebuked a Bedouin who urinated in the mosque
Answered Jews who said 'Death be upon you' with 'Rather, death and the curse be upon you'
Reproached a servant who was slow with an errand
Was harsh with a woman asking about her religion
Narrated by al-Bukhari (6927) from Aisha; evidence for ar-Rafiq.
asmaa-husna-0295: What is rifq, the meaning indicated by Allah's name ar-Rafiq?
Gentleness, ease and deliberation in affairs, the opposite of harshness
Rifq means gentleness, ease, deliberation and taking time with matters; its opposite is violence and severity.
asmaa-husna-0296: Which action did al-Badr mention as an instance of Allah's gentleness?
Creating things gradually despite being able to create them all at once
Delaying the sky's creation until after the earth only to teach people the order of creation
Revealing all religious laws at once
Making this world an abode of recompense rather than deeds
Part of His gentleness in His actions is that He created all things gradually, little by little, according to His wisdom and gentleness, although He could have created them all at once.
asmaa-husna-0297: «من يُحرم الرفق يُحرم الخير» [He who is deprived of gentleness is deprived of goodness (HadeethEnc)] Who narrated this hadith in Sahih Muslim?
Narrated by Muslim (2592) from Jarir. Al-Badr cited it when explaining ar-Rafiq.
asmaa-husna-0298: Allah's name al-Witr is established in Abu Hurayra's report agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim. What is that report about?
The number of washes in wudu (ablution)
The witr (odd-numbered prayer) at the end of the night
The virtue of enumerating the ninety-nine names

«لله تسعة وتسعون اسمًا، مائة إلا واحدًا، لا يحفظها أحد إلا دخل الجنة، وهو وتر يحب الوتر» [Allah has ninety-nine names – one hundred minus one – and no one memorizes them but that they will enter Paradise. He is One, and He loves odd numbers (HadeethEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0299: Al-Witr is one of Allah's names established in the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition). According to al-Badr it means:
The One who loves night prayer
The Unique One with no partner or equal
The One who makes all numbers odd
The One who judges creation once
Al-Witr is the Unique One with no partner or equal. The name indicates Allah's oneness and His exclusive possession of perfect attributes.
asmaa-husna-0300: Abu al-Abbas al-Qurtubi explained al-witr in the Prophet's statement «الوتر» [He is One, and He loves odd numbers (HadeethEnc)] as referring to:
He said al-witr means tawhid: Allah is one in His essence, perfection and actions, and He loves the affirmation of His oneness.
asmaa-husna-0301: Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: «إن الوتر ليس بحتم كالمكتوبة، ولكن رسول الله ﷺ أوتر ثم قال: أوتروا يا أهل ...، فإن الله وتر يحب الوتر» [Witr is not an obligation like the prescribed prayer. However, Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, performed witr and then said: Perform witr, people of ... , for Allah is Witr and loves what is witr.]
Narrated by Ahmad, the Sunan compilers and Ibn Khuzayma; at-Tirmidhi graded it good. Al-Badr cited it under al-Witr.
asmaa-husna-0302: Allah's name al-Muti is established in Sahih al-Bukhari in Muawiya's report: «المعطي» [When Allah intends good for someone, He gives him understanding of the religion.]
Narrated by al-Bukhari (3116) from Muawiya, may Allah be pleased with him.
asmaa-husna-0303: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Muti?
The One who gives believers only in the Hereafter, not this world
The One who gives everyone precisely what they ask for
The One who gives in proportion to people's deeds
The sole true Giver: none can withhold what He gives
Al-Muti is the sole true Giver: none can withhold what He gives, and none can give what He withholds... His giving encompasses all servants.
asmaa-husna-0304: How did al-Badr explain Allah's name al-Jawad?
The One whose generosity reaches only believers in the Hereafter, not other creatures in this world
The One who meets needs through means alone
The One who is not questioned about what He does
The One whose generosity encompasses all beings and fills them with His bounty and blessings
Al-Jawad means the One who gives abundantly, whose generosity encompasses all beings and fills them with His bounty, kindness and varied blessings.
asmaa-husna-0305: Ibn Uthaymin collected ninety-nine of Allah's names in al-Qawaid al-Muthla. How many did he derive from Allah's Book?
He said: 'This is what we selected through investigation: eighty-one names in Allah's Book and eighteen in the Sunnah of Allah's Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him.'
asmaa-husna-0306: Of the ninety-nine names Ibn Uthaymin collected, how many did he derive from the Prophet's Sunnah (Prophetic tradition)?

They include al-Jamil, al-Jawad, al-Hakam, al-Hayiyy, ar-Rabb, ar-Rafiq, as-Subbuh, as-Sayyid, ash-Shafi, at-Tayyib, al-Qabid, al-Basit, al-Muqaddim, al-Muakhkhir, al-Muhsin, al-Muti, al-Mannan and al-Witr.
asmaa-husna-0307: In al-Qawaid al-Muthla, Ibn Uthaymin expressed hesitation about including which two names in the ninety-nine?
He said he had reservations about including al-Hafiyy... and also al-Muhsin, because he had not examined its narrators in at-Tabarani.
asmaa-husna-0308: Why did Ibn Uthaymin hesitate to include al-Hafiyy among Allah's beautiful names?
It occurs only in a weak-chain report that hadith scholars cannot use as evidence
It occurs in an irregular, non-mass-transmitted reading
It describes a prophet rather than Allah

It occurs in a qualified context in Allah's statement about Ibrahim: ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾ [[Abraham] said, "Peace [i.e., safety] will be upon you.[815] I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me. Notes: [815] Meaning "You are secure" or "I will not harm you." — Quran 19:47 (QuranEnc)]

He said: 'Because it occurs only in a qualified context in Allah's statement about Ibrahim': ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾ [[Abraham] said, "Peace [i.e., safety] will be upon you.[815] I will ask forgiveness for you of my Lord. Indeed, He is ever gracious to me. Notes: [815] Meaning "You are secure" or "I will not harm you." — Quran 19:47 (QuranEnc)]
asmaa-husna-0309: To which source did Ibn Uthaymin attribute Allah's name al-Muhsin in a footnote to al-Qawaid al-Muthla?
Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab at-Tawhid, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him
At-Tabarani's al-Awsat; al-Haythami said its narrators are trustworthy
The footnote says: 'At-Tabarani in al-Awsat; al-Haythami said its narrators are trustworthy.' He stated that he had not examined its narrators and that Shaykh al-Islam included it among the names.
asmaa-husna-0310: Which name did Ibn Uthaymin count among those established in the Prophetic Sunnah rather than in the Quran?
Ibn Uthaymin placed as-Subbuh among the names from the Sunnah and attributed it to Muslim. Al-Quddus, as-Salam and al-Mumin occur in the Quran in the verse of Surah al-Hashr.
asmaa-husna-0311: Which name did Ibn Uthaymin include among those he derived from Allah's Book?

Al-Maleek is among the Quranic names according to Ibn Uthaymin: ﴿عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ﴾ [In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.[1591] Notes: [1591] Who accomplishes whatever He wills whenever He wills. — Quran 54:55 (QuranEnc)] As-Sayyid, at-Tayyib and ar-Rafiq are established in the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition).
easy-fiqh-0001: By scholarly consensus, which of these invalidates wudu (ablution)?

Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that passing feces, urine, semen or wind from the anus, and loss of reason, are states of ritual impurity, each of which invalidates purification and requires ablution.
easy-fiqh-0002: A man with wudu (ablution) laughs loudly outside prayer. What is the ruling on his ablution?
It is invalid and he must repeat it
It is invalid if he laughs aloud rather than smiles
It remains valid; he need not repeat it
He must wash his mouth and then perform ablution
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that laughter outside prayer does not invalidate purification or require ablution.
easy-fiqh-0007: By scholarly consensus, when is water najis (ritually impure), whether the quantity is small or large?
When fallen leaves change its color
When impurity changes its taste, color or smell
When the sun heats it in a metal container
When an animal lawful to eat drinks from it
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that if impurity falls into a small or large quantity of water and changes its taste, color or smell, it is impure as long as it remains so.
easy-fiqh-0008: A little impurity falls into a great river such as the Nile without changing its color, taste or smell. What is the ruling on the water?
Only the place where it fell is impure
It retains its status and may be used for purification
Using it for wudu (ablution) is disliked until it flows onward
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that if impurity falls into abundant water such as the Nile or sea without changing its color, taste or smell, it retains its status and may be used for purification.
easy-fiqh-0009: A sheep drinks from a vessel of water. What is the ruling on the water left behind?
Impure; it must be poured away
Pure for drinking but not for wudu (ablution)
Pure; it may be drunk and used for ablution
The vessel must be washed three times
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that water left after an animal lawful to eat has drunk is pure and may be drunk and used for ablution.
easy-fiqh-0010: Someone performing wudu (ablution) washes his left hand before his right. What is the ruling on his ablution?
He must rewash both hands and everything after them
Invalid if he did it deliberately
Valid; he need not repeat it
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who starts with his left side before his right in ablution need not repeat it.
easy-fiqh-0013: A man is wearing gloves. May he wipe over them instead of washing his hands in wudu (ablution)?
Yes, by analogy with leather socks
No; he must remove them and wash his hands
Yes, if he put them on while ritually pure
Yes, when traveling and in extreme cold
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that this wiping is not permissible over gloves or coverings of the forearms.
easy-fiqh-0015: A traveler has little water and fears thirst if he uses it for wudu (ablution). By scholarly consensus, what should he do?
Keep his water for drinking and perform tayammum (dry purification)
Wash his face and hands and perform dry purification for the rest
Delay prayer until he finds more water
Use it for ablution and rely on Allah
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a traveler who has water but fears thirst should keep it for drinking and perform dry purification.
easy-fiqh-0017: A man performs tayammum (dry purification) as commanded, then finds water before starting prayer. What is the ruling on his dry purification?
He prays with it, then repeats the prayer with wudu (ablution)
He may use it for an obligatory prayer but not a voluntary one
He prays with it and disregards the water
It becomes invalid; he must purify himself with water

Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that if someone performs dry purification as commanded, then finds water before entering prayer, his purification is invalidated and he must purify himself again and pray.
easy-fiqh-0018: May someone who performed wudu (ablution) with water lead people who performed tayammum (dry purification) in prayer?
No, because their forms of purification differ
Valid for voluntary prayer but not obligatory prayer
Valid if the imam is traveling
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who purified himself with water may lead those who performed dry purification.
easy-fiqh-0019: What invalidates tayammum (dry purification) without disagreement among scholars?
A full hour passing after it
Leaving the place where it was performed
Ibn al-Qattan said: Every event that invalidates ablution also invalidates dry purification; no scholar disagrees about this.
easy-fiqh-0021: A woman has a wet dream and sees fluid after waking. What is her ruling?
She washes only the affected place
She must perform ghusl (full ritual bathing), like a man
Wudu (ablution) suffices because she is a woman
Full ritual bathing is recommended but not obligatory
Ibn al-Qattan said: I know of no disagreement that a woman who has a wet dream and sees fluid must perform full ritual bathing, like a man.
easy-fiqh-0022: What is the purity status of the sweat of someone in janabah (major ritual impurity) or a menstruating woman?
Impure; it must be washed from clothes
Pure from the person in major ritual impurity, impure from the menstruating woman
Impure, but a small amount is excused
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the sweat of someone in major ritual impurity is pure, and likewise that of a menstruating woman.
easy-fiqh-0023: By scholarly consensus, what must a menstruating woman make up after becoming pure?
She need not make up anything
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that she need not make up prayers missed during menstruation, and agreed that she must make up fasts missed during it.
easy-fiqh-0024: What must a woman with nifas (postpartum bleeding) do when her bleeding stops and she becomes pure?
Wash only the place affected by blood
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a woman with postpartum bleeding must perform full ritual bathing when she becomes pure.
easy-fiqh-0025: A piece is cut from a sheep's thigh while it is alive. What is the ruling on that piece?
Lawful to eat if Allah's name is pronounced over it
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a limb cut from a sheep, camel or cow while the animal is alive is ritually impure.
easy-fiqh-0026: A man shears wool from his living sheep. What is the ruling on using that wool?
Permissible after washing it seven times
Permissible for furnishings but not clothing
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that using their hair, fur and wool is permissible when taken while the animals are alive.
easy-fiqh-0028: Which is preferable for removing traces of discharge from the two private passages: water or stones?
Stones, because they are the original method
Stones during travel and water at home
Water is preferable; stones are a concession

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars today agree that istinja (cleansing the private parts) with water is preferable, while istijmar (cleansing with stones) is a concession and allowance. They all regard water as more cleansing and wholesome.
easy-fiqh-0029: A man cleans himself with three stones, but impurity remains on the area. What must he do?
Remove it until the area is clean
Repeat using only three more stones
Nothing, because he used the required number
Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslims agreed that someone who uses three stones without removing the impurity must remove it.
easy-fiqh-0031: A man performs wudu (ablution) before the time for Zuhr (noon prayer), and remains pure when the time begins. What is the ruling on his purification?
It becomes invalid when the time begins
It suffices only for voluntary prayer
Complete; he may pray with it
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who purifies himself with water before the prayer time has complete purification.
easy-fiqh-0032: How many times must the face be washed for wudu (ablution) to suffice?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Washing the face three times is the complete practice; by consensus, one wash suffices if it covers the whole face.
easy-fiqh-0034: Someone performing wudu (ablution) wipes only his ears and no part of his head. What is the ruling?
It does not fulfill wiping the head
It suffices if he intends the ears as the head
It suffices if he wipes them three times
Ibn al-Qattan said: The Muslim community does not disagree that wiping only the ears is insufficient.
easy-fiqh-0036: A man is certain he invalidated his ritual purity, then doubts whether he performed wudu (ablution) afterward. What must he do?
Pray, then perform the prostration of forgetfulness
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone certain of ritual impurity but doubtful about ablution, or certain that he has not performed ablution, must perform it.
easy-fiqh-0037: A man urinates, sleeps, then passes wind before performing wudu (ablution). How many ablutions must he perform?
Three, one for each invalidating event
One ablution and one ghusl (full ritual bathing)
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that one ablution suffices after many invalidating events, whether of the same or different types.
easy-fiqh-0038: A man has intercourse with his wife several times before performing ghusl (full ritual bathing). How many baths suffice?
One bath and one wudu (ablution) for each time
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that one full ritual bath suffices for someone who has intercourse repeatedly with one woman or with several women.
easy-fiqh-0042: By consensus, which act of worship is a menstruating woman prohibited from performing?
Invoking blessings upon the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him
Ibn al-Qattan said: The prohibition of prayer, fasting, circumambulation and vaginal intercourse during menstruation is established by certain consensus, without disagreement among Muslims.
easy-fiqh-0043: What is the ruling on a man eating and drinking with his menstruating wife?
Permissible if they do not share a vessel
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a husband may eat and drink with her, meaning his menstruating wife.
easy-fiqh-0045: What is the ruling if a small amount of flea blood gets on the clothes of someone praying?
It must be washed before prayer
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that flea blood is overlooked and excused if it is not excessive.
easy-fiqh-0046: What is the ruling on a sheep's hide if the sheep was slaughtered according to Islamic law?
Pure; using and selling it are permissible
Pure, but selling it is impermissible
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that the hide of an animal lawful to eat is pure when it is properly slaughtered, and may be used and sold.
easy-fiqh-0047: What is the purity status of human urine?
Pure if the quantity is small
Pure if its color has not changed
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed on the impurity of urine.
easy-fiqh-0048: What is the ruling on prayer and fasting for a woman during nifas (postpartum bleeding)?
She prays and fasts like a woman who is pure
She abstains from both, like a menstruating woman
She fasts but does not pray
She prays but does not fast
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that when a woman gives birth... that blood is unquestionably postpartum blood; during it she abstains from prayer, fasting and intercourse.
easy-fiqh-0049: By scholarly consensus, when does the time for Zuhr (noon prayer) begin?
When the sun rises and ascends
When the sun passes its zenith
When an object's shadow becomes twice its length
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Zuhr begins when the sun passes its zenith.
easy-fiqh-0050: By scholarly consensus, what marks the beginning of Maghrib (sunset prayer)?
The appearance of all the stars
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Maghrib becomes due when the sun sets.
easy-fiqh-0051: By scholarly consensus, what marks the beginning of Subh (dawn prayer)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Subh begins at dawn.
easy-fiqh-0052: What is the Sunnah (Prophetic practice) regarding the direction a muezzin faces while giving the adhan (call to prayer)?
Face the qiblah (direction of the Kabah)
Turn his back to the prayer direction
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that facing the direction of the Kabah when giving the call to prayer is part of the Prophetic practice.
easy-fiqh-0055: By scholarly consensus, what is the ruling on intention in prayer?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that prayer is invalid without intention.
easy-fiqh-0056: At which point in prayer did scholars agree that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his hands?
When sitting between the two prostrations
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his hands when beginning prayer.
easy-fiqh-0059: A woman attends Jumuah (Friday prayer) and prays with the imam. What is the ruling on her prayer?
It suffices in place of Zuhr (noon prayer)
It does not suffice; she must pray Zuhr
It suffices if she is with her husband
She prays two more rakahs (prayer units) afterward to complete four
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Friday prayer is not obligatory for women, and agreed that if women attend and pray with the imam, it suffices for them.
easy-fiqh-0061: A resident misses Jumuah (Friday prayer). How many rakahs (prayer units) does he pray instead?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that residents who miss Friday prayer pray four units.
easy-fiqh-0063: A resident prays Zuhr (noon prayer) behind a traveling imam who shortens it and ends after two rakahs (prayer units). What must the resident do?
End with him; his prayer is valid
Pray one more unit, then end
Restart the prayer from the beginning
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that when a resident follows a traveler who ends the prayer after two units, the resident must complete the prayer.
easy-fiqh-0066: A free adult woman prays with her whole head uncovered. What is the ruling on her prayer?
Valid if she is at home
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a free adult woman covers her head when praying, and that if she prays with her entire head uncovered, she must repeat the prayer.
easy-fiqh-0067: Which period did scholars agree is a time for witr (odd-numbered prayer)?
Between Maghrib (sunset prayer) and Isha (night prayer)
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the period between Isha prayer and dawn is a time for witr.
easy-fiqh-0069: A man gives the adhan (call to prayer) and iqamah (call to begin prayer) in a mosque. Must everyone there give both calls individually?
Yes; each person gives the call for himself
Each gives the second call but not the first
It suffices for men but not women
No; it suffices for everyone in the mosque
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that when one person gives the two calls in a mosque, that suffices for everyone there.
easy-fiqh-0070: What is the ruling on speaking between the adhan (call to prayer) and iqamah (call to begin prayer)?
It requires repeating the second call
Ibn al-Qattan said: Speaking between the two calls is permissible by the consensus of the Muslim community.
easy-fiqh-0071: A traveler wants to give the adhan (call to prayer) while riding his animal. What is the ruling?
Valid if the animal is stationary
Valid for the iqamah (call to begin prayer), but not the first call
Ibn al-Qattan said: A traveler may give the call to prayer while mounted; I know of no disagreement about it.
easy-fiqh-0072: A man wants to perform the obligatory Zuhr (noon prayer) on behalf of his busy, living brother. What is the ruling?
Permissible if his brother authorizes him
Impermissible; nobody performs prayer on behalf of another
Ibn al-Qattan said: By consensus, nobody performs prayer on behalf of another.
easy-fiqh-0074: A man prays in a direction without investigating or asking about the qiblah (direction of the Kabah), then learns that he did not face it. What is the ruling on his prayer?
Valid with the prostration of forgetfulness
Valid if its time has ended

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who prays without investigating or seeking the prayer direction, then learns he did not face it, has an invalid prayer, like someone who prays without purification.
easy-fiqh-0076: A man sleeps through five consecutive prayers. What must he do after waking?
They are waived because he is excused
Make up only the last prayer
Pray the current prayer and seek forgiveness
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who sleeps through five prayers makes them up.
easy-fiqh-0079: In which rakahs (prayer units) of Maghrib (sunset prayer) is recitation audible?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that Maghrib consists of three units, with audible recitation in the first two and silent recitation in the third.
easy-fiqh-0080: How does the imam recite in Zuhr (noon prayer) and Asr (afternoon prayer) at Arafah on the pilgrimage day?
Audibly in the first prayer, silently in the second
Audibly in both, as in Friday prayer
Audibly in the first two rakahs (prayer units)
Ibn al-Qattan said: All scholars whose views are recorded agreed that the imam does not recite audibly in Zuhr and Asr at Arafah.
easy-fiqh-0081: How does omitting qunut (standing supplication) affect a prayer's validity?
It does not invalidate the prayer
The prostration of forgetfulness is required for validity
Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslims agreed that omitting the standing supplication does not invalidate prayer.
easy-fiqh-0082: What did scholars agree ruku (bowing) is a place for?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that bowing is a place for magnifying Allah through glorifying Him and declaring His holiness, and agreed that it is not a place for Quran recitation.
easy-fiqh-0083: Someone prostrates with his knees covered by clothing and his feet in socks. What is the ruling?
Valid if the socks are thin
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that a worshipper may prostrate with knees covered by clothing, and likewise with feet in leather socks, ordinary socks or sandals.
easy-fiqh-0084: By scholarly consensus, which movement has no transition takbir (saying Allahu akbar)?
Standing after the first tashahhud (testimony recitation)
Ibn al-Qattan said: By consensus, there is no takbir when lifting the head from bowing; rather, there is tasbih, meaning here tasmi (saying that Allah hears whoever praises Him).
easy-fiqh-0085: How many sittings for the tashahhud (testimony recitation) are there in Fajr (dawn prayer)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that each prayer has two sittings... except Fajr, in which one sits only once, at its conclusion.
easy-fiqh-0086: What is the Sunnah (Prophetic practice) concerning audible or silent recitation of the tashahhud (testimony recitation)?
A person praying alone recites it audibly
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone regards silent testimony recitation as the Prophetic practice; reciting it aloud is an innovation and ignorance.
easy-fiqh-0087: Someone praying alone finishes with nobody else present. What does he say in the taslim (closing salutation)?
He gives no salutation because nobody is there
Only as-salamu alayna (peace be upon us)
He merely turns his head without speaking
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone praying alone says 'Peace be upon you' even though nobody is present to receive the greeting.
easy-fiqh-0088: A man is greeted while praying and responds with a gesture. What is the ruling?
He performs the prostration of forgetfulness
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that someone greeted while praying who responds by gesture incurs nothing.
easy-fiqh-0089: A man prays while his food is ready, completing the prayer without omitting any obligatory part. What is the ruling?
Valid only as a voluntary prayer
He repeats it within its time
His prayer suffices according to the four schools, although praying while preoccupied with the food is disliked. Some Zahiri scholars disagreed.
easy-fiqh-0090: A worshipper's mind wanders to his business during prayer. What is the ruling on his prayer?
He must perform the prostration of forgetfulness
He repeats the rakah (prayer unit) in which he was distracted
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that thinking about worldly affairs does not invalidate prayer.
easy-fiqh-0092: What did scholars agree about intentionally speaking during prayer in early Islam?
It remains permissible for the imam
It was permissible only in voluntary prayer
Ibn al-Qattan said: All scholars agreed that intentional speech was once permissible, and agreed that this was abrogated.
easy-fiqh-0094: Must every follower in congregational prayer place an individual sutrah (prayer barrier) in front of himself?
Yes; every follower places his own barrier
Only those in the first row place one
No; the imam's barrier suffices for all
Ibn al-Qattan said: The certain, unquestioned consensus is that no follower is required to place another prayer barrier; the imam's barrier suffices for everyone.
easy-fiqh-0095: A man enters the mosque after the imam has risen from bowing and is standing upright, then joins him. Does that rakah (prayer unit) count for him?
He catches it if he prostrates with the imam
He has missed it; it does not count
He catches it because he catches the prostration
He catches it if it is the first unit
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who joins after the imam has raised his head from bowing and stood upright... has missed that unit and does not count those two prostrations.
easy-fiqh-0096: A man prays with an imam and nobody else. Where does the follower stand?

Discussing Ibn Abbas standing on the Prophet's left and being moved to his right, Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that this is the Sunnah (Prophetic practice) for someone praying alone with an imam.
easy-fiqh-0097: Where does a woman stand when praying in congregation with men?
In front of the first row

Ibn al-Qattan said: The Sunnah (Prophetic practice) is for a woman to stand behind the men, not alongside them. They agreed that she may pray alone behind a row or behind a single man, and that this is her prescribed practice.
easy-fiqh-0099: A man performs a voluntary prayer behind an imam performing an obligatory prayer. What is the ruling?
Disliked to the point of prohibition
Ibn al-Qattan said: By consensus, performing a voluntary prayer behind someone performing an obligatory prayer is permissible.
easy-fiqh-0102: A follower makes a mistake in prayer behind the imam. Does the imam prostrate for the follower's forgetfulness?
Yes, if it involved adding something
The imam does not prostrate for the follower's forgetfulness
Yes, if the follower alerts him
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars do not disagree that the imam does not prostrate because of a follower's forgetfulness.
easy-fiqh-0104: A worshipper forgets to bow and goes into prostration, then remembers while prostrating. What should he do?
Stand up so that he can bow
Finish prostrating and perform the prostration of forgetfulness
Complete his prayer, then repeat it
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone agreed that a worshipper who forgets bowing and prostrates, then remembers while prostrating, must stand up so that he can bow.
easy-fiqh-0105: A man prays with impurity on his clothes without knowing it. What is his ruling regarding sin?
Sinful if there is much impurity
Sinful if he is the imam
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone agreed that someone who prays with impurity on his clothes without knowing it is not disobedient.
easy-fiqh-0106: A man enters the mosque after the imam has given the prayer's closing salutation. Has he caught the congregational prayer?
Yes, if the imam has not stood up
Yes, if he says the opening takbir (Allahu akbar) before the rows stand up
No, he has not caught it
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone arriving after the imam has ended the prayer has not caught it.
easy-fiqh-0108: A man prays Jumuah (Friday prayer) with wudu (ablution) but without ghusl (full ritual bathing). What is the ruling on his prayer?
Invalid; he repeats it as Zuhr (noon prayer)
Invalid; he repeats it as Friday prayer
Valid if he is a traveler
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Friday prayer performed with ablution but without full ritual bathing suffices.
easy-fiqh-0111: When are the two Friday sermons delivered in relation to the prayer?
One before prayer and the other after
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that the two Friday sermons come before prayer.
easy-fiqh-0112: A man talks idly while the imam gives the Friday sermon. Must he repeat Jumuah (Friday prayer)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who talks and engages in idle speech does not repeat Friday prayer.
easy-fiqh-0113: What is the ruling on someone who misses Jumuah (Friday prayer) three times without excuse when it is obligatory for him?
He is a defiantly disobedient sinner for doing so
He is a disbeliever outside Islam

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who misses it three times without excuse is a defiantly disobedient sinner, and agreed that someone able and obliged to attend who misses it does not become a disbeliever by doing so.
easy-fiqh-0114: By scholarly consensus, which pair of prayers cannot be combined?
Zuhr (noon prayer) and Asr at Arafah
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Asr and Maghrib cannot be combined, nor Isha and Subh (dawn prayer).
easy-fiqh-0115: A man performs a voluntary prayer seated although he can stand. What is the ruling?
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that a person may perform voluntary prayer seated if he wishes.
easy-fiqh-0116: What is the ruling on the two rakahs (prayer units) after Maghrib (sunset prayer)?
Voluntary: one may perform or omit them

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that the two units before Fajr (dawn prayer), the two after Zuhr (noon prayer), before Asr (afternoon prayer), after Maghrib and after Isha (night prayer), and Ramadan night prayer are all voluntary: one may perform or omit them.
easy-fiqh-0117: Does night prayer have a fixed maximum number of rakahs (prayer units) that may not be exceeded?
No fixed limit; one prays as much as one wishes
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that night prayer has no fixed limit and is voluntary; whoever wishes may pray as he wishes, a little or a great deal.
easy-fiqh-0119: A traveler on his mount wants to perform voluntary prayer while it faces away from the qiblah (direction of the Kabah). What is the ruling?
Permissible, whatever direction it takes him
Valid only if he faces the prayer direction throughout
Ibn al-Qattan said: The Prophet's Companions used to pray on their animals while traveling, whatever direction they faced. This is agreed upon, with no scholarly disagreement.
easy-fiqh-0120: What is the time for the two Eid prayers?
From Subh (dawn prayer) until Zuhr (noon prayer)
From the sun's passing its zenith until Asr (afternoon prayer)
From the sun's rising high until it passes its zenith
Ibn al-Qattan said: The time for both Eid prayers is from the advance of the forenoon until the sun passes its zenith; scholars do not dispute this.
easy-fiqh-0121: Does the imam recite audibly or silently in Eid prayer?
Silently in the first rakah (prayer unit), audibly in the second
Audibly in the first, silently in the second
The Sunnah (Prophetic practice) is for the imam to recite audibly in both Eid prayers; jurists do not disagree about this.
easy-fiqh-0122: Which comes first at the two Eids: the prayer or the sermon?
The first sermon, then prayer, then the second sermon
Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslim scholars do not disagree that the prayer precedes the sermon at the two Eids.
easy-fiqh-0123: By scholarly consensus, what distinguishes Eid prayer from other prayers?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that Eid prayer contains additional takbirs beyond those of other prayers, but differed on their number.
easy-fiqh-0125: How is a deceased Muslim's body washed?
By wiping the body without pouring water
Like ghusl al-janabah (full bathing after major ritual impurity)
By tayammum (dry purification), even when water is available
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the deceased is washed in the manner of full bathing after major ritual impurity.
easy-fiqh-0126: What is the ruling on a woman washing her husband's body after his death?
Permissible if no men are available
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a woman may wash her husband when he dies.
easy-fiqh-0128: A newborn is known to have been alive, cries aloud, then dies. What is the ruling on the funeral prayer?
A funeral prayer is performed if the child reached one year
Only supplication, without a funeral prayer
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a funeral prayer is performed for a child known to have been alive and to have cried at birth.
easy-fiqh-0130: What is the ruling on burying a deceased Muslim?
A communal obligation: if some fulfill it, the others are relieved
An individual obligation on everyone who knows of the death

Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that burying the deceased is binding and obligatory upon people, who may not omit it when able. If some perform it, the obligation is lifted from the rest of the Muslims.
easy-fiqh-0131: A deceased person is washed with plain water without sidr (lote-tree leaves). What is the ruling?
It suffices only if lote-tree leaves are unavailable
Invalid; it must be repeated with lote-tree leaves
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that washing the deceased with plain water without lote-tree leaves is permissible.
easy-fiqh-0132: May a deceased person receive tayammum (dry purification) instead of washing when water is available and washing can be done without harm?
Yes, to ease the burden on the family
Yes, if the water is cold
No; only when water is unavailable or cannot be used
Ibn al-Qattan said: One may not substitute dry purification when water is available; it is performed when water is unavailable. Scholars do not dispute this.
easy-fiqh-0134: In which direction does someone face when performing the funeral prayer?
Toward the deceased wherever the body lies
Toward the qiblah (direction of the Kabah)
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that the funeral prayer must face the direction of the Kabah.
easy-fiqh-0137: What must not accompany a funeral procession, without scholarly disagreement?
Ibn al-Qattan said: A funeral must not be followed with raised sound or fire; I know of no scholarly disagreement about this.
easy-fiqh-0138: A worshipper recites a Quranic verse of prostration, prostrates for it, then resumes his prayer. What is the ruling on his prayer?
He must perform the prostration of forgetfulness
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that if someone recites a Quranic prostration verse during prayer, prostrates, then resumes the prayer, it is not invalidated.
easy-fiqh-0139: A traveler on his mount recites a verse of prostration. How does he perform the recitation prostration?
Dismount and prostrate on the ground
Omit it because he is traveling
Gesture for it while on his mount
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a traveler gestures for the recitation prostration while on his mount.
easy-fiqh-0142: By scholarly consensus, zakat (obligatory alms) is due on which animal?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that obligatory alms are due on camels, cattle and sheep/goats.
easy-fiqh-0143: What is the minimum number of camels on which zakat (obligatory alms) is due?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that obligatory alms are not due on fewer than five camels.
easy-fiqh-0144: What zakat (obligatory alms) is due on five camels after a full year?
A bint labun (female camel that has completed two years)
A bint makhad (female camel that has completed one year)
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that one sheep/goat is due on five camels.
easy-fiqh-0145: What is the minimum number of sheep/goats on which zakat (obligatory alms) is due?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that obligatory alms are not due on fewer than forty sheep/goats.
easy-fiqh-0146: A man owns 150 freely grazing sheep for a full year. How many must he give as zakat (obligatory alms)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that one sheep/goat is due on forty through 120; once the number exceeds 120, two are due up to 200.
easy-fiqh-0147: How are buffalo classified for zakat (obligatory alms)?
No alms are due on them
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that buffalo have the same ruling as cattle.
easy-fiqh-0148: A man owns twenty sheep and twenty goats. Are they combined to reach the nisab (minimum alms threshold)?
Yes, they are combined for obligatory alms
No, because they are two kinds
Combined if they share one pasture
Combined if their numbers are equal
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that sheep and goats are combined for zakat (obligatory alms).
easy-fiqh-0150: A man has dates and raisins, neither separately reaching the nisab (minimum alms threshold). Are they combined for zakat (obligatory alms)?
Add the smaller amount to the larger
Dates are not combined with raisins
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that date palms are not combined with raisins.
easy-fiqh-0151: How much is due on 200 silver dirhams after a full year?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that five dirhams are due on 200 dirhams.
easy-fiqh-0157: How many months make up the hawl (year required for alms)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Nobody in the Muslim community disagrees that the year consists of twelve months.
easy-fiqh-0158: A man pays zakat (obligatory alms) on his dates after harvesting them, then keeps them unsold for another year. Does he pay again?
No; they are assessed only once
Yes, at half the first amount
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that alms recur on wealth at the end of each year, except crops and fruits... Once these categories have been assessed, no further alms are ever due on them.
easy-fiqh-0161: By scholarly consensus, for whom does a man pay zakat al-fitr (alms at the end of Ramadan)?
Himself and his young children who have no wealth
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the alms at the end of Ramadan are obligatory on someone able to pay them for himself and his young children who have no wealth.
easy-fiqh-0162: An unmarried woman has wealth. Who pays zakat al-fitr (alms at the end of Ramadan) for her?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that before marriage, a woman pays the alms at the end of Ramadan for herself.
easy-fiqh-0164: What is the minimum amount of dates or barley that suffices for one person's zakat al-fitr (alms at the end of Ramadan)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that less than one sa of either barley or dates does not suffice.
easy-fiqh-0165: A poor man owns absolutely nothing. Is zakat al-fitr (alms at the end of Ramadan) obligatory for him?
He must borrow and pay it
It is not obligatory for him
It remains a debt he owes
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that it is not obligatory on someone who has nothing.
easy-fiqh-0168: May a man give his zakat (obligatory alms) to his poor father, whose maintenance he is obliged to provide, for the father's needs?
Yes; his father has the strongest claim
Permissible if his father is ill
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that alms may not be given to parents or children when the giver is obliged to maintain them.
easy-fiqh-0169: May a man give his wife some of his zakat (obligatory alms) for her needs?
No, because her maintenance is obligatory upon him
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a man does not give his wife obligatory alms, because he must maintain her and she is provided for through his wealth.
easy-fiqh-0172: May someone employed to administer zakat (obligatory alms) take his share despite being wealthy?
Yes; it is lawful for him even if wealthy
Only if he belongs to another eligible category

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that alms are lawful for their administrators, those who buy the donated goods with their own money, and those to whom the goods are given as gifts, even if they are wealthy.
easy-fiqh-0173: A man gives charity to a relative, then the relative dies and he inherits it. What is its ruling for him?
He gives it to the public treasury
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that charity someone gives and later inherits is lawful for him.
easy-fiqh-0175: What is the zakat (obligatory alms) ruling on freely grazing mules and donkeys not kept for trade?
Half the camel alms rate is due
Alms are due as on camels
Alms are due if they number ten
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that no obligatory alms are due on mules and donkeys, even if freely grazing.
easy-fiqh-0176: What zakat (obligatory alms) rate applies to crops watered by rain, springs or rivers?

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that one tenth is due on rain-fed crops and those watered by springs and rivers, and half a tenth on crops watered by animal-powered water lifting and water wheels.
easy-fiqh-0177: What zakat (obligatory alms) rate applies to crops irrigated at a cost using animal-powered water lifting or water wheels?

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that one tenth is due on rain-fed crops and those watered by springs and rivers, and half a tenth on crops watered by animal-powered water lifting and water wheels.
easy-fiqh-0178: A man's dates are estimated for zakat (obligatory alms), then a calamity destroys them before harvest. What must he pay?
The monetary value of the alms
Ibn al-Qattan said: All scholars whose views are recorded agreed that if dates are estimated and then destroyed by a calamity before harvest, nothing is due.
easy-fiqh-0180: A man has several date varieties, such as Ajwa and Barni. Are they combined to reach the nisab (minimum alms threshold)?
No; each variety has its own threshold
Only good-quality dates are combined with other good-quality dates
Ibn al-Qattan said: Date varieties are likewise combined: Ajwa, Barni, Sayhani and all other varieties. There is no disagreement about this.
easy-fiqh-0181: How many sas (volume measures) make one wasq (larger volume measure)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: The hadith states «والوسق ستون مختومًا» [A.], meaning sas. This is the view of every scholar whose opinion is recorded.
easy-fiqh-0182: How many dirhams equal one uqiyyah (silver weight measure)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: An uqiyyah is forty dirhams by scholarly agreement.
easy-fiqh-0183: What is the ruling on someone who withholds zakat (obligatory alms), denying its obligation while knowing it is an Islamic duty?
Disciplined but not declared a disbeliever
Ibn al-Qattan said: Withholding obligatory alms in denial of them is apostasy by consensus.
easy-fiqh-0184: What is due on thirty-six camels?
A hiqqah (female camel that has completed three years)
A bint labun (female camel that has completed two years)
A bint makhad (female camel that has completed one year)
A jadhah (female camel that has completed four years)
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that two sheep/goats are due on ten camels... a two-year-old female camel on thirty-six, a three-year-old female on forty-six, and a four-year-old female on sixty-one.
easy-fiqh-0185: What is due on forty-six camels?
Two bint labuns (female camels that have completed two years)
A jadhah (female camel that has completed four years)
A hiqqah (female camel that has completed three years)
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that... a three-year-old female camel is due on forty-six, a four-year-old female on sixty-one, and two two-year-old females on seventy-six.
easy-fiqh-0186: What is due on sixty-one camels?
Two bint labuns (female camels that have completed two years)
A hiqqah (female camel that has completed three years)
A jadhah (female camel that has completed four years)
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that... a four-year-old female camel is due on sixty-one, two two-year-old females on seventy-six, and two three-year-old females on ninety-one through 120.
easy-fiqh-0187: What is due on ninety-one through 120 camels?
Two jadhahs (female camels that have completed four years)
Two bint labuns (female camels that have completed two years)
Two hiqqahs (female camels that have completed three years)
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that... two three-year-old female camels are due on ninety-one through 120.
easy-fiqh-0188: What is due on ten camels?
A bint makhad (female camel that has completed one year)
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that two sheep/goats are due on ten camels, three on fifteen, and four on twenty.
easy-fiqh-0191: What is the zakat (obligatory alms) rate on gold that reaches the nisab (minimum threshold) and is held for a full year?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that one quarter of a tenth is assessed annually on twenty dinars.
easy-fiqh-0192: By scholarly consensus, how many days can a lunar month have?
Ibn al-Qattan said: A month may have thirty days or twenty-nine days, by consensus.
easy-fiqh-0193: The crescent is seen after the sun passes its zenith on the twenty-ninth of Shaban. When does fasting become obligatory?
From the night of the thirty-first
Ibn al-Qattan said: By consensus, if the crescent is seen after the sun passes its zenith, fasting is obligatory only from the next day.
easy-fiqh-0194: A large body of people reports seeing Ramadan's crescent. What is the ruling on fasting?
Obligatory only for those who saw it
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that when a large body of people reports sighting the crescent, fasting or ending the fast accordingly becomes obligatory.
easy-fiqh-0195: An elderly man and woman cannot fast. What is the ruling on their not fasting in Ramadan?
Permitted only with a doctor's authorization
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that an elderly man or woman unable to fast may refrain from fasting.
easy-fiqh-0198: A pregnant woman fears fasting will harm her fetus. May she refrain from fasting?
It is forbidden for her to stop fasting
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone agreed that a pregnant woman fearing for her fetus and a nursing woman fearing for her child may refrain from fasting.
easy-fiqh-0199: What is the ruling on suhur (the pre-dawn meal) for someone fasting?
Obligatory; fasting is invalid without it
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the pre-dawn meal is recommended.
easy-fiqh-0200: When may a fasting person break the fast?
When Maghrib (sunset prayer) becomes due at sunset
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that breaking the fast becomes lawful when Maghrib becomes due, and agreed that Maghrib belongs to the night.
easy-fiqh-0205: A fasting person swallows an unavoidable tiny amount of food from between his teeth with his saliva. What is the ruling on his fast?
He must make it up as a precaution
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that nothing is required of a fasting person who swallows what passes with saliva from between his teeth when he cannot prevent it.
easy-fiqh-0206: A fasting person sleeps during a Ramadan day and has a wet dream. What is the ruling on his fast?
Invalid; he must make it up
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a daytime wet dream does not invalidate fasting.
easy-fiqh-0211: A woman owes two consecutive months of fasting. She fasts part of them, then menstruates. What does she do after becoming pure?
Resume counting from what she has already fasted
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a woman owing two consecutive months who fasts part of them and then menstruates resumes counting from what she has fasted after becoming pure.
easy-fiqh-0212: A man misses Ramadan days due to illness, then makes them up before the next Ramadan. What else is required?
Feeding one poor person per day

Ibn al-Qattan said: If someone misses fasting in Ramadan because of illness, travel, menstruation or another excuse, then the excuse ends and he can make it up, nothing else is required by agreement if he makes it up before the next Ramadan.
easy-fiqh-0214: A living man cannot fast. May someone fast on his behalf?
Nobody fasts on behalf of a living person
Yes, his guardian may fast for him
Yes, if he directs it in a bequest
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that nobody fasts on behalf of a living person.
easy-fiqh-0215: By scholarly consensus, how many Laylat al-Qadr (Nights of Decree) are there in one year?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that the Night of Decree is real, and agreed that it is one night in each year.
easy-fiqh-0216: A man vows to fast three days if Allah heals his sick relative. The person recovers. What is the ruling on fasting those days?
Disliked because the vow was conditional
An obligation that must be fulfilled
He offers oath expiation without fasting
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that fasting vowed upon a condition that is not sinful is obligatory.
easy-fiqh-0217: What is the ruling on voluntarily fasting alternate days while avoiding days on which fasting is prohibited?
Obligatory for someone who vowed it
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that voluntarily fasting one day and not the next is good, provided one does not fast the prohibited days.
easy-fiqh-0219: A man makes up his missed Ramadan fasts on consecutive days. What is the ruling?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone agrees that someone who makes up Ramadan fasts consecutively is obedient.
easy-fiqh-0220: What is the basic ruling on itikaf (devotional retreat in the mosque)?
Obligatory once in every Muslim's lifetime
Obligatory in Ramadan's last ten days
Not obligatory unless a person binds himself by a vow
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that devotional retreat is not an obligatory duty unless someone makes it binding on himself, in which case it becomes obligatory for him.
easy-fiqh-0222: Someone in itikaf (devotional retreat in the mosque) needs to urinate or defecate. May he leave the mosque?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone in devotional retreat may leave his place of retreat to urinate or defecate.
easy-fiqh-0224: What invalidates itikaf (devotional retreat in the mosque) without disagreement among jurists?

Intentional intercourse invalidates devotional retreat without disagreement among jurists, because Allah says: ﴿وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ﴾ [It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are a clothing for you and you are a clothing[67] for them. Allāh knows that you used to deceive yourselves,[68] so He accepted your repentance and forgave you. So now, have relations with them and seek that which Allāh has decreed for you [i.e., offspring]. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the night [i.e., sunset]. And do not have relations with them as long as you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allāh, so do not approach them. Thus does Allāh make clear His verses [i.e., ordinances] to the people that they may become righteous. Notes: [67] Also a source of tranquility and rest.
[68] Prior to this revelation, marital relations were unlawful during nights preceding fasting. Some were unable to refrain and secretly disobeyed, but they did not deceive Allāh. — Quran 2:187 (QuranEnc)]
easy-fiqh-0226: By scholarly consensus, what is the recommended time for itikaf (devotional retreat in the mosque)?
The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that its recommended time is all or part of Ramadan, and agreed that it is permissible throughout the year.
easy-fiqh-0229: What is the miqat (designated entry point) for Madinah's people to enter ihram (pilgrimage consecration) for Hajj or Umrah?

Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that Dhu al-Hulayfa is for Madinah's people, al-Juhfa for people of the Maghrib, Qarn for Najd's people, Yalamlam for Yemen's people, and al-Masjid al-Haram for Makkah's people, as entry points for Hajj and Umrah, except Umrah for Makkah's people.
easy-fiqh-0230: At which miqat (designated entry point) does someone coming from Yemen enter ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?

Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that Dhu al-Hulayfa is for Madinah's people, al-Juhfa for people of the Maghrib, Qarn for Najd's people and Yalamlam for Yemen's people... as entry points for Hajj and Umrah.
easy-fiqh-0231: Qarn al-Manazil is the miqat (designated pilgrimage entry point) for which region's people?
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that Dhu al-Hulayfa is for Madinah's people, al-Juhfa for people of the Maghrib, Qarn for Najd's people and Yalamlam for Yemen's people.
easy-fiqh-0232: A pilgrim enters ihram (pilgrimage consecration) before reaching his miqat (designated entry point). What is the ruling?
Valid only if combining Hajj and Umrah in qiran
He owes a sacrifice and it is invalid
Invalid until renewed at the entry point
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone entering pilgrimage consecration before the designated entry point is consecrated.
easy-fiqh-0234: A man intends Hajj but accidentally pronounces the talbiyah (pilgrimage invocation) for Umrah. What is binding on him?
His ihram (pilgrimage consecration) is invalid; he must restart
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that if someone intends Hajj but announces Umrah, or intends Umrah but announces Hajj, what binds him is the intention in his heart, not what his tongue pronounces.
easy-fiqh-0235: By scholarly consensus, which act is prohibited for someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated pilgrim is prohibited from intercourse, killing game, perfume, certain clothing, removing hair and clipping nails.
easy-fiqh-0238: A consecrated pilgrim needs to shave his head because of an affliction. What choices does he have for the fidyah (compensation)?
Fasting, charity or a sacrificial animal
Charity equal to the hair's value
Fasting ten days or freeing a slave
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who shaves his head for an excuse or necessity may choose among what Allah specified: fasting, charity or sacrifice.
easy-fiqh-0241: By scholarly consensus, which may a woman in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) wear?
A garment dyed with wars (a fragrant yellow dye plant)
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated woman may wear shirts, long gowns, trousers, head coverings and leather socks.
easy-fiqh-0242: What is the ruling on a man covering his head while in ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated man is prohibited from covering his head.
easy-fiqh-0244: What is the ruling on sea game for someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?
Eating it is permitted, catching it is not
Catching and eating it are permitted
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated pilgrim may catch, eat, sell and buy sea game.
easy-fiqh-0246: A man enters janabah (major ritual impurity) while in ihram (pilgrimage consecration). May he bathe?
He delays bathing until leaving consecration
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated pilgrim may bathe after major ritual impurity.
easy-fiqh-0247: What is the ruling on someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) using the siwak (tooth-cleaning stick)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a consecrated pilgrim may use the tooth-cleaning stick.
easy-fiqh-0249: Must women perform ramal (a brisk gait) during tawaf (circumambulation) around the House?
Yes, only in the first circuit
No brisk gait is required of them
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that women are not required to move briskly around the House or during sai (walking between as-Safa and al-Marwa).
easy-fiqh-0250: What is the ruling on drinking water during tawaf (circumambulation)?
Disliked to the point of prohibition
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that drinking water during circumambulation is permissible.
easy-fiqh-0254: According to the Sunnah (Prophetic practice), where does one begin sai (walking between as-Safa and al-Marwa)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who begins at as-Safa and ends at al-Marwa follows the Prophetic practice.
easy-fiqh-0256: A person from outside the miqat region performs Umrah in the Hajj months, remains in Makkah and performs Hajj that year. What does he owe?
A hady (sacrificial offering) if available; otherwise fasting

Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone from outside the miqat region who enters Umrah in the Hajj months, comes to Makkah and completes it, then stays and performs Hajj that year, is performing tamattu (Umrah followed by Hajj). He owes a sacrificial offering if available; otherwise he fasts.
easy-fiqh-0258: What is the ruling on standing at Arafah during Hajj?
An essential obligation; missing it means missing Hajj
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that standing at Arafah is obligatory and that someone who misses it has no Hajj.
easy-fiqh-0259: A pilgrim stands at Arafah without ritual purity. What is the ruling?
It suffices if he purifies himself before sunset
It suffices, but he owes a sacrifice
He has caught Hajj and owes nothing
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who stands at Arafah without ritual purity has caught Hajj and owes nothing.
easy-fiqh-0260: Which two prayers does a pilgrim combine at Muzdalifah?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the Sunnah (Prophetic practice) is for a pilgrim to combine Maghrib and Isha, meaning at Muzdalifah.
easy-fiqh-0261: Which jamrah (stoning pillar) alone is stoned on the Day of Sacrifice?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that only Jamrat al-Aqaba is stoned on the Day of Sacrifice.
easy-fiqh-0262: A pilgrim stones the pillars during the Days of Tashriq after the sun passes its zenith. What is the ruling?
It suffices only on the first day
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that stoning the pillars during the Days of Tashriq after the sun passes its zenith suffices.
easy-fiqh-0267: A young child taken on Hajj cannot stone the pillars. What is the ruling?
Someone stones on the child's behalf
Stoning is delayed until the child grows up
The guardian sacrifices a sheep/goat for the child
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone stones on behalf of a child unable to do so.
easy-fiqh-0268: For a man leaving Hajj consecration, which is better: shaving the head or shortening the hair?
Shortening if his hair is long
Shaving is better for a man, because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, supplicated three times for those who shaved and once for those who shortened their hair. Agreed upon.
easy-fiqh-0269: A healthy, capable man owes the obligatory Hajj. Does another person's performing it on his behalf suffice?
Yes, if he pays the expenses
Yes, if the substitute is a relative
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone capable of performing the obligatory Hajj must perform it himself; another person's performing it on his behalf does not suffice.
easy-fiqh-0271: A child performs Hajj before puberty, then reaches puberty and becomes able. Does the earlier Hajj fulfill the obligatory Hajj?
Yes, if performed with his father
Yes, if he had reached discernment
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Hajj performed by a person with insanity who later recovers, or by a child who later reaches puberty, does not fulfill the obligatory Hajj.
easy-fiqh-0272: What is the ruling on hunting game in the Haram (sacred precinct) for someone outside pilgrimage consecration?
Forbidden for both consecrated and unconsecrated people
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that hunting game in the sacred precinct is forbidden for both consecrated and unconsecrated people.
easy-fiqh-0273: What is the ruling on cutting naturally growing trees in the Haram (sacred precinct)?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that cutting its trees, meaning those of the sacred precinct, is forbidden.
easy-fiqh-0274: What is the ruling on vegetables and crops people cultivate in the Haram (sacred precinct)?
Cutting them is forbidden like the precinct's trees
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that everything people grow in the sacred precinct, including vegetables, crops, fragrant plants and other things, is permissible.
easy-fiqh-0275: May a man prevent his wife from leaving for a voluntary Hajj?
Only if she lacks a mahram (unmarriageable male relative or husband)
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a man may prevent his wife from leaving for a voluntary Hajj.
easy-fiqh-0276: By scholarly consensus, which is the first Hajj month?

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Shawwal, Dhu al-Qada and nine days of Dhu al-Hijja are among the Hajj months and times for entering ihram (pilgrimage consecration), and agreed that months other than Shawwal, Dhu al-Qada and Dhu al-Hijja are not Hajj months.
easy-fiqh-0277: A man from Makkah wants to perform Umrah. Where does he enter ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?
In the hill (area outside the sacred precinct)
