Ibn al-Qattan said: A man from Makkah does not enter Umrah until he goes outside the sacred precinct and enters consecration there. Scholars agree without disagreement.
easy-fiqh-0278: A man begins a voluntary Hajj or Umrah. May he abandon it before completion?
Yes, if he offers a sacrifice
Ibn al-Qattan said: Once someone begins a voluntary Hajj or Umrah, he must complete it; scholars do not dispute this.
easy-fiqh-0279: How loudly does a woman in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) recite the talbiyah (pilgrimage invocation)?
She does not recite it at all
Only loudly enough to hear herself
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a woman raises her voice in the invocation only enough to hear herself.
easy-fiqh-0280: A man in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) has an izar (waist wrapper). May he wear trousers instead?
Scholars agreed that a consecrated man who has a waist wrapper may not wear trousers, but doing so does not invalidate his consecration.
easy-fiqh-0282: A consecrated pilgrim is offered live land game as a gift. May he accept it?
He may neither accept nor buy it
Yes, and release it after consecration
Yes, if the giver is unconsecrated
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a consecrated pilgrim may not accept game given to him, buy it or hunt it.
easy-fiqh-0283: May a woman in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) cover her head and hair?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a woman's consecration pertains to her face, and that she may cover her head and hair while consecrated.
easy-fiqh-0284: Unrelated men pass a woman in ihram (pilgrimage consecration). What did scholars agree she may do?
Let cloth hang down lightly over her face from above her head
Fasten a niqab (face veil) over her face
Cover her face with perfumed cloth
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that she may let cloth hang down lightly over her face from above her head to conceal herself from men's gaze.
easy-fiqh-0285: May someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) take shade in a tent or pavilion?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that a consecrated pilgrim may enter a tent or pavilion.
easy-fiqh-0286: May someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) slaughter chickens and livestock he owns?
Permissible only outside the sacred precinct
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that he may slaughter whichever livestock and domestic chickens he owns... while consecrated and within the sacred precinct.
easy-fiqh-0288: Someone performing sai (walking between as-Safa and al-Marwa) stands at the base of as-Safa without climbing it. What is the ruling?
He must repeat the entire walking ritual
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that standing at as-Safa's base without climbing it suffices.
easy-fiqh-0289: What is the ruling on tawaf (circumambulation) around the House during times when prayer is prohibited?
Permissible by day but not at night
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that circumambulation is permissible during times when prayer is prohibited.
easy-fiqh-0290: When are the two rakahs (prayer units) of tawaf (circumambulation) performed?
After sai (walking between as-Safa and al-Marwa)
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that the two units are performed only after the seven circuits.
easy-fiqh-0292: What are the 'numbered days' mentioned in Allah's statement ﴿واذكروا الله في أيام معدودات﴾ [And remember Allāh during [specific] numbered days. Then whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no sin upon him; and whoever delays [until the third] - there is no sin upon him - for him who fears Allāh. And fear Allāh and know that unto Him you will be gathered. — Quran 2:203 (QuranEnc)]?
The first ten days of Dhu al-Hijja
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that the Days of Tashriq are the days at Mina and are the numbered days.
easy-fiqh-0293: By consensus, when does the time for standing at Muzdalifah end?
When the sun passes its zenith on the Day of Sacrifice
At sunrise on the Day of Sacrifice
At midnight on the eve of the Day of Sacrifice
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that when the sun rises on the Day of Sacrifice, the time for standing at Jam (Muzdalifah) has passed.
easy-fiqh-0294: Where in Mina do pilgrims stay on the Day of Tarwiyah?
They must stay by Masjid al-Khayf
They must stay by Jamrat al-Aqaba
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that pilgrims stay wherever they wish in Mina.
easy-fiqh-0295: When is the Arafah-day sermon delivered in relation to the prayer?
Between Zuhr (noon prayer) and Asr (afternoon prayer)
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that its sermon, meaning Arafah's sermon, precedes prayer.
easy-fiqh-0296: A pilgrim does not stone the pillars during the Days of Tashriq before sunset on their last day. What is the ruling?
He stones them later and owes nothing
He does not stone them later; he compensates for the omission
He repeats Hajj the following year

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who fails to stone during the Days of Tashriq until sunset on their last day does not stone afterward, and compensates by sacrifice or food, according to their differing views.
easy-fiqh-0299: A pilgrim performing tamattu (Umrah followed by Hajj) can obtain and afford a sacrificial offering. May he fast instead?
Yes, if poor in his home country
Fasting is not an option for him
Yes, if he fasts ten days
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that fasting is not an option for the pilgrim performing tamattu when he can obtain the offering.
easy-fiqh-0300: What is the linguistic meaning of Umrah?

Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that Umrah linguistically means visiting. In religious law, it means heading from outside the sacred precinct to circumambulate the House and perform sai (walking between as-Safa and al-Marwa).
easy-fiqh-0302: Is Umrah obligatory for a Muslim more than once in a lifetime?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Umrah is not obligatory twice.
easy-fiqh-0304: Which hady (sacrificial offering) is best in Hajj?
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that camels are better offerings than cattle and sheep/goats; disagreement concerns udhiyah (Eid sacrifices).
easy-fiqh-0306: Does a jadha (young goat) suffice for a hady (pilgrimage offering) or udhiyah (Eid sacrifice)?
It suffices as a pilgrimage offering only
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a young goat of this age does not suffice as a pilgrimage offering or Eid sacrifice, but differed over a young sheep.
easy-fiqh-0307: In what order did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, perform the rites on the Day of Sacrifice during his Hajj?
Stoning Jamrat al-Aqaba, sacrifice, then shaving

Ibn al-Qattan said: It is established that during his Hajj he stoned the pillar on the Day of Sacrifice, then slaughtered his camels, then shaved his head. They agreed that this is the Sunnah (Prophetic practice).
easy-fiqh-0309: Which plant in the Haram (sacred precinct) did scholars agree may be cut for use?
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that no vegetation may be cut in the sacred precinct except idhkhir, which they permitted because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, allowed it.
easy-fiqh-0310: How does killing game in Mina and the rest of the Haram (sacred precinct) compare with killing it in Makkah?
Compensation is due only in Makkah
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that killing game in Makkah, Mina and the rest of the sacred precinct equally requires compensation.
easy-fiqh-0311: By Muslim consensus, when is the first departure from Mina?
The third day counting from the Day of Sacrifice
The second day counting from the Day of Sacrifice
Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslims agreed that the first departure is on the third day counting from the Day of Sacrifice.
easy-fiqh-0313: What is the ruling on touching the Black Stone during tawaf (circumambulation)?
An obligation compensated by sacrifice if omitted
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed on touching the Black Stone.
easy-fiqh-0315: What does nadh mean in rulings on purifying clothes?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Nadh means sprinkling, without disagreement; scholars regard it as purification for something whose impurity is doubtful.
easy-fiqh-0317: A woman's menstruation ends, but she finds no water for bathing. What should she do?
Delay prayer until she finds water
Perform wudu (ablution) with whatever little water is available
Perform tayammum (dry purification), like someone in janabah (major ritual impurity)
Ibn al-Qattan said: If a woman whose menstruation has ended finds no water, she performs dry purification like someone in major ritual impurity. This is consensus.
easy-fiqh-0318: How does someone in janabah (major ritual impurity) perform tayammum (dry purification) when water is unavailable?
He must roll in the dust
Wipe his whole body with dust
Make as many strikes as there are body parts to wash
In the same manner as dry purification for minor ritual impurity

Ibn al-Qattan said: Dry purification for major ritual impurity, menstruation and postpartum bleeding has the same form as that for removing minor ritual impurity. Those who recognize any of these practices and dry purification do not disagree about this.
easy-fiqh-0321: Must body parts be washed in a particular order during ghusl al-janabah (full bathing after major ritual impurity)?
It is a condition for validity
Yes, beginning with the right side
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that all body parts must be washed during full bathing after major ritual impurity; everyone agrees that no particular order is required.
easy-fiqh-0322: What is the ruling on prayer and fasting for a woman with istihadah (non-menstrual bleeding)?
She omits both like a menstruating woman
She prays but does not fast
She fasts but does not pray
Both are commanded because she is ritually pure

Ibn al-Qattan said: A woman with non-menstrual bleeding differs from a menstruating woman: she is pure and commanded to pray and fast, as shown by the Sunnah (Prophetic tradition) and the community's agreement.
easy-fiqh-0324: What is the ruling on voluntary prayer without ritual purification?
Valid if it is two brief rakahs (prayer units)

Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslims throughout the earth agreed that voluntary prayer is valid only with purification, necessarily by wudu (ablution), ghusl (full ritual bathing) or tayammum (dry purification).
easy-fiqh-0326: In which rakah (prayer unit) of witr (odd-numbered prayer) is qunut (standing supplication) performed?
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that the standing supplication is performed in witr's last unit after recitation.
easy-fiqh-0328: A man is holding back urine to a degree that prevents him from fulfilling the obligations of prayer. What did scholars agree he should do?
Not pray while holding urine in that condition
Invalidate his wudu (ablution) and perform tayammum (dry purification)
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that nobody should pray while holding back urine if that prevents him from completing the obligations of prayer.
easy-fiqh-0329: What is the ruling on playing with pebbles or similar things during prayer?
Ibn al-Qattan said: The prohibition of playing or fidgeting with pebbles during prayer is agreed upon; the same applies to fidgeting with other things.
easy-fiqh-0331: Someone passes in front of a worshipper, who cannot reach him from where he stands. Should the worshipper walk toward him to stop him?
Interrupt the prayer and stop him
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that if someone passes in front of a worshipper who cannot reach him from his prayer position, he does not walk toward him to stop him.
easy-fiqh-0332: An imam leads people while in janabah (major ritual impurity). What is the ruling on his own prayer?
Valid if the followers do not know
Ibn al-Qattan said: If someone in major ritual impurity leads a group, his prayer is invalid whether he knew his condition when starting or had forgotten it; there is no disagreement.
easy-fiqh-0333: Must a woman attend congregational prayer?
Only Friday prayer is obligatory for her
It is not obligatory for her
It is obligatory if she is elderly
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars did not disagree that attending congregation is not obligatory for a woman as it is for a man.
easy-fiqh-0334: Where do three men stand when praying behind one imam?
One on his right and two behind
Ibn al-Qattan said: They likewise agreed that when there are three besides the imam, they stand behind him.
easy-fiqh-0338: People perform Jumuah (Friday prayer) during Zuhr (noon prayer) time after the sun passes its zenith. Is it within its time?
Valid only before the sun passes its zenith
They performed it as a make-up prayer
They performed it within its time
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who performs Friday prayer during Zuhr time has performed it within its time.
easy-fiqh-0339: A man from Makkah goes to Mina outside the Hajj days. May he shorten prayers there?
He shortens Zuhr (noon prayer) but not Isha (night prayer)
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone who goes to Mina outside the Hajj days does not shorten prayer.
easy-fiqh-0340: A man is pursued by an enemy who wants to kill him. Prayer becomes due while he is mounted. What did scholars agree he may do?
Omit it without making it up
Make it up two days later
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone being pursued may pray on his mount.
easy-fiqh-0341: Abu Bakr performed witr (odd-numbered prayer) early in the night, while Umar performed it late. What is the ruling on performing it early?
Disliked to the point of prohibition
Ibn al-Qattan said: Abu Bakr's performing it when going to bed, and Umar's performing it late at night... indicate its permissibility at that time, which is agreed upon.
easy-fiqh-0342: A Muslim is wounded fighting disbelievers, carried away alive, and lives long enough to eat and drink before dying. Is his body washed and a funeral prayer performed?

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that a martyr wounded fighting disbelievers who is carried away alive, does not die on the battlefield and lives to eat and drink is washed and prayed over, as was done for Umar and Ali, may Allah have mercy on them.
easy-fiqh-0343: May a deceased person be shrouded in thin cloth that reveals the body rather than concealing it?
Such cloth is not used for the shroud
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that a deceased person is not shrouded in cloth so thin and light that it reveals the body and does not conceal it.
easy-fiqh-0345: A man dies in Muslim lands, with neither disbelief nor Islam known of him. Where is he buried?
Left unburied until his status is known
In cemeteries of the People of the Book
Ibn al-Qattan said: Everyone agreed that someone who dies with neither disbelief nor Islam known of him is interred in Muslim cemeteries.
easy-fiqh-0346: A man has saved gold ingots reaching the nisab (minimum alms threshold), without wearing or using them. What is their zakat (obligatory alms) ruling?
None is due because they are not coins
Ibn al-Qattan said: Someone holding gold or silver bullion or jewelry not used for wearing pays alms every year. There is no disagreement if it is not intended as women's adornment.
easy-fiqh-0348: A traveler misses Ramadan fasting days because of travel. How many days must he make up?
A full month regardless of the number
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that someone who misses fasting because of travel or illness must make up as many days as he missed, provided another Ramadan has not come upon him.
easy-fiqh-0349: A man vows to fast a specific day, which turns out to be Eid al-Fitr. Does he fast it?
Ibn al-Qattan said: By consensus, someone vowing to fast a particular day or year that includes either Eid must not fast that day. They differed about making it up.
easy-fiqh-0350: A pilgrim spends the night before Arafah outside Mina, then reaches Arafah within the required standing time. What does he owe?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone spending the night before Arafah away from Mina owes nothing if he reaches Arafah within the required time.
easy-fiqh-0351: A pilgrim combines Maghrib (sunset prayer) and Isha (night prayer) at Muzdalifah. Does he perform voluntary prayer between them?
He performs the regular Maghrib voluntary prayer between them
He does not perform voluntary prayer between them
He performs witr (odd-numbered prayer) between them
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone combining the two prayers does not perform voluntary prayer between them.
easy-fiqh-0352: When did the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stone Jamrat al-Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice?
After the sun passed its zenith
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stoned Jamrat al-Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice after sunrise.
easy-fiqh-0354: A consecrated pilgrim falls ill and needs medicine without perfume. What is the ruling on using it?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars do not disagree that a consecrated pilgrim may drink and use for treatment what is not perfume.
easy-fiqh-0355: According to the agreed Sunnah (Prophetic practice), how many rakahs (prayer units) are performed after each seven-circuit tawaf (circumambulation)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: The undisputed, certain Prophetic practice upon which Muslims agreed is two prayer units with every seven circuits.
easy-fiqh-0356: An imam leads Zuhr (noon prayer) and Asr (afternoon prayer) at Arafah without delivering a sermon. What is the ruling on their prayers?
They must repeat them as Friday prayer
Zuhr suffices but Asr does not
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that if the imam prays at Arafah without a sermon, it suffices; he recites silently and shortens the prayers if traveling.
easy-fiqh-0357: Without scholarly disagreement, to whom does the designation 'those present at al-Masjid al-Haram' apply?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that Makkah's people fall under the designation 'those present at al-Masjid al-Haram.'
easy-fiqh-0359: By Muslim consensus, which tawaf (circumambulation) is intended in Allah's statement ﴿وليطوّفوا بالبيت العتيق﴾ [Then let them end their untidiness and fulfill their vows and perform ṭawāf around the ancient House." — Quran 22:29 (QuranEnc)]?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Muslims agreed that this is Hajj's principal circumambulation.
easy-fiqh-0360: Does a woman's ihram (pilgrimage consecration) differ from a man's regarding the prohibition of perfume?
Yes; perfume is lawful for her, not him
Only mild perfume is lawful for her
No; the prohibition is the same for both
Forbidden for her in Hajj but not Umrah
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that all perfume is forbidden for Hajj and Umrah pilgrims after consecration; there is no scholarly disagreement that men and women have the same ruling.
easy-fiqh-0361: A traveler has no water and wants to perform tayammum (dry purification). By scholarly consensus, which material is valid?
Ibn al-Qattan said: All scholars whose views are recorded agreed that dry purification using soil that produces dust is permissible.
easy-fiqh-0362: Someone deliberately speaks in prayer without intending to correct any part of it. What is the ruling on the prayer?
Valid with the prostration of forgetfulness
Valid if the speech is brief
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that prayer is invalid when someone deliberately speaks in it without intending to correct something in the prayer.
easy-fiqh-0363: A man deliberately eats and drinks during an obligatory prayer. By scholarly consensus, what must he do?
Repeat the rakah (prayer unit) in which he ate
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone deliberately eating and drinking in an obligatory prayer must repeat it.
easy-fiqh-0364: How many rakahs (prayer units) are in Jumuah (Friday prayer), led by the imam after the sermon?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that Friday prayer consists of two units.
easy-fiqh-0365: Is Jumuah (Friday prayer) obligatory for a woman as it is for a man?
Obligatory if she lives near the mosque
Obligatory if she is a resident
Ibn al-Qattan said: All scholars whose views are recorded agreed that Friday prayer is not obligatory for women.
easy-fiqh-0366: Is recitation in the two rakahs (prayer units) of Jumuah (Friday prayer) audible or silent?
Audible in the first, silent in the second
Silent in the first, audible in the second
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Friday prayer, when held with its conditions fulfilled, consists of two units with audible recitation.
easy-fiqh-0367: A traveler is on a journey permitting shortened prayers. How many rakahs (prayer units) does he pray for Maghrib (sunset prayer)?
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed... that Maghrib is three units for someone afraid or secure, traveling or resident.
easy-fiqh-0368: A sick person cannot stand in an obligatory prayer. What is required?
Delay prayer until able to stand
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone unable to stand must pray seated.
easy-fiqh-0369: A worshipper who can bow and prostrate merely gestures for both in an obligatory prayer. What is the ruling on his prayer?
It suffices if he is the imam
It suffices if he prays at home
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the prayer of someone who is able does not suffice unless he bows or prostrates.
easy-fiqh-0370: What did scholars agree a man must cover in prayer?
The front and rear private parts
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that the front and rear private parts are among what a man must cover in prayer.
easy-fiqh-0371: How many times must a capable Muslim perform the obligatory Hajj (pilgrimage) if he has not vowed to perform Hajj?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a person owes one Hajj in his lifetime, the obligatory Hajj, unless he makes a vow, which he must fulfill.
easy-fiqh-0373: Which of these garments is a man in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) unanimously prohibited from wearing?
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that a person in ihram is prohibited from wearing a shirt, a turban, trousers, leather socks, and hooded cloaks.
easy-fiqh-0375: What is the ruling on someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) eating oil, clarified butter, and animal fat in his food?
Permissible, with a compensatory offering due
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that a person in ihram may eat oil, clarified butter, and animal fat.
easy-fiqh-0376: A pilgrim stones Jamrat al-Aqabah on the Day of Sacrifice after sunrise and before noon. What is the ruling regarding its timing?
He stoned it too early and must repeat it after noon
He stoned it after its time and owes a sacrifice
He stoned it within its time
He stoned it outside its time and owes charity
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed ... that whoever stones it from this time [after sunrise] until noon has stoned it within its time.
easy-fiqh-0377: A man slaughters his udhiyah (Eid sacrifice) on the night before Eid al-Adha, before dawn on the Day of Sacrifice. What is the ruling on slaughtering it then?
Permissible for villagers but not city dwellers
Permissible if he distributes its meat after dawn
Permissible because it is one of the Eid nights
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that sacrificial animals may not be slaughtered before dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.
easy-fiqh-0378: Someone traveling for Hajj (pilgrimage) on a journey lasting three days or more prays Zuhr and Asr as two units each. What is the ruling on his prayer?
He repeats both as four units each
Both suffice and he performs prostrations for forgetfulness
Zuhr suffices but Asr does not
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that whoever performs Hajj or Umrah, fights the polytheists, or travels for three days or more, and prays Zuhr and Asr as two units each has fulfilled his obligation.
easy-fiqh-0379: A fasting person intends the Ramadan fast each night and then fasts. What is the ruling on his fast?
Deficient because he repeated the intention
Ibn al-Mundhir said: They agreed that someone who intends the fast each night of Ramadan and then fasts has a complete fast.
easy-fiqh-0380: How many verses are in Surat al-Fatihah, which is recited in every rakah (prayer unit)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: The Muslim community agreed that Fatihat al-Kitab consists of seven verses.
easy-fiqh-0381: In which of these prayers is recitation not aloud in any of its units?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that Fajr consists of two units with aloud recitation, and Zuhr and Asr consist of four units each, with no aloud recitation in any of them.
easy-fiqh-0382: In which prayer unit is takbirat al-ihram (the opening declaration of Allah's greatness) performed?
In the first and third units
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that the opening takbir is only in the first unit.
easy-fiqh-0383: When is the taslim (closing salutation) in prayer, according to the text and scholarly consensus?
Before sitting for the final testimony
After rising from the first prostration
At the end of the final testimony
Ibn al-Qattan said: According to the text and scholarly consensus, the closing salutation occurs only at the end of the testimony.
easy-fiqh-0384: A worshipper deliberately gives the closing salutation before completing his prayer. What is the ruling on his prayer?
Valid, and he completes what remains
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that deliberately giving the salutation before completing the prayer invalidates it.
easy-fiqh-0385: A worshipper knowingly and deliberately adds a prostration in prayer that is neither for recitation nor forgetfulness. What is the ruling on his prayer?

Ibn al-Qattan reported agreement that deliberately and knowingly adding a prostration while in prayer, other than the commanded prostrations, the aforementioned prostration, or prostration for forgetfulness, invalidates the prayer.
easy-fiqh-0386: What is the ruling on the two units of tahiyyat al-masjid (greeting the mosque) for someone entering at a time when voluntary prayer is permitted?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars do not disagree that the mosque's two units are recommended for someone entering at a time when voluntary prayer is permitted.
easy-fiqh-0387: What is the ruling on standing in an obligatory prayer for someone able to stand?
Obligatory only in the first unit
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that standing in the prescribed prayer is obligatory.
easy-fiqh-0388: What does 'the remembrance of Allah' mean in the verse about Friday prayer: ﴿فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله﴾ [O you who have believed, when [the adhān] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumuʿah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allāh and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew. — Quran 62:9 (QuranEnc)]?

Ibn al-Qattan said regarding Allah's words ﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله﴾ [O you who have believed, when [the adhān] is called for the prayer on the day of Jumuʿah [Friday], then proceed to the remembrance of Allāh and leave trade. That is better for you, if you only knew. — Quran 62:9 (QuranEnc)]: They agreed that remembrance here means the prayer and sermon.
easy-fiqh-0389: How many units does the Eid prayer comprise when performed at the open-air prayer ground?
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that the prayer of the two Eids comprises two units in the open air.
easy-fiqh-0390: What was the Prophet's practice, peace and blessings be upon him, concerning voluntary prayer at the prayer ground before and after Eid prayer?
He prayed two units before it
He prayed neither before nor after it
He prayed two units both before and after it
He prayed four units after it
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not pray at the prayer ground before or after the Eid prayer.
easy-fiqh-0391: A woman dies while menstruating. How should her body be washed?
Wait until her menstrual days have elapsed
Perform dry purification for her without washing
Treat her as other deceased people are treated
Ibn al-Qattan said: If a person in major ritual impurity or a menstruating woman dies, they are treated as others are treated. This is the view of every scholar whose opinion I have preserved.
easy-fiqh-0392: What is the ruling on wailing over the dead?
Permissible during the first three days
Not permissible for men or women
Permissible for women but not men
Permissible if the deceased is a relative
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that neither men nor women may wail over the dead.
easy-fiqh-0393: A woman owns wealth reaching the nisab (minimum zakah threshold), and a lunar year has passed over it. What is the ruling on her zakah (obligatory alms)?
Required only if she is unmarried
Her husband must pay it for her
Obligatory for her as for a man
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that zakah is obligatory for women as it is for men.
easy-fiqh-0394: A sheep owner owes one sheep in zakah (obligatory alms), but the collector insists on taking two. What is the ruling?
Permissible if the flock is large
Permissible if both sheep are small

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars do not disagree that if one sheep is due to the collector and he accepts nothing less than two, this is forbidden for him; the owner is not religiously obligated to satisfy him.
easy-fiqh-0395: A man owns forty grazing sheep, all male, and a lunar year has passed over them. What is the ruling on their zakah (obligatory alms)?
Not required until females are present
Required as it is for females
Not required until they reach eighty
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that for livestock subject to zakah, whether camels, cattle, or sheep, mixed males and females and either sex alone are treated alike.
easy-fiqh-0396: A fasting person breaks his fast thinking night has begun, then discovers it has not. What is his status regarding sin?
Sinful if the day was cloudy
Ibn al-Qattan said: All agreed that someone who breaks his fast because he thinks night has begun ... is not disobedient to Allah Most High. Scholars then differed over whether he must make it up.
easy-fiqh-0398: Is it permissible to perform itikaf (mosque retreat) outside Ramadan on days of the year when fasting is not prohibited?
No, it is restricted to Ramadan
No, it is restricted to the last ten nights
No, it is restricted to the sacred months
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that itikaf is permissible throughout the year, except days when fasting is prohibited, which are disputed.
easy-fiqh-0399: What is the ruling on Hajj (pilgrimage) for a young child who has not reached puberty?
Obligatory if he has provisions and a mount
Obligatory if he can distinguish matters
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that Hajj is not obligatory for a child until puberty.
easy-fiqh-0400: A capable person has performed neither Hajj (major pilgrimage) nor Umrah (minor pilgrimage). Which rite should he begin with?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Hajj and Umrah are two rites; scholars do not differ that a capable person may begin with whichever he wishes.
easy-fiqh-0401: What is the ruling on someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) removing body hair without necessity?
Permissible during Umrah but not Hajj
Not permissible while he remains in ihram
Ibn al-Qattan said: They do not disagree that someone in ihram may not remove any body or head hair without necessity while remaining in ihram.
easy-fiqh-0402: What is the ruling on someone in ihram (pilgrimage consecration) lightly scratching his head and body?
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars do not disagree that someone in ihram may lightly scratch his head and body.
easy-fiqh-0403: What is the Sunnah (Prophetic practice) concerning the connection between sai (walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah) and tawaf (circumambulation)?
It should follow directly after tawaf
A long voluntary prayer should separate them
It should be delayed until the following day
It should follow the overnight stay at Mina
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that the Sunnah is for sai to follow directly after tawaf.
easy-fiqh-0404: A person performs the two units following tawaf (circumambulation) in al-Masjid al-Haram, away from Maqam Ibrahim and outside al-Hijr. What is the ruling?
They do not suffice until prayed behind the Maqam
They suffice, with a sacrifice due
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that someone performing tawaf may pray the two units wherever he wishes and can in the mosque; nothing is due if he does not pray by the Maqam.
easy-fiqh-0405: In how many circuits does an arriving Hajj or Umrah pilgrim perform ramal (brisk, short-stepped walking) during tawaf (circumambulation)?
Ibn al-Qattan said: I know of no disagreement that ramal is an increase in walking pace and occurs only in three circuits ... of the arrival tawaf for someone coming to Makkah for Hajj or Umrah.
easy-fiqh-0406: A pilgrim misses the daytime standing at Arafah but stands there on the night before the Day of Sacrifice, before dawn. What is the ruling?
It does not suffice and he has missed Hajj
It does not suffice until he stands on the Day of Sacrifice
It suffices in place of the daytime standing
It suffices for Umrah but not Hajj
Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that standing there at night suffices in place of standing by day.
easy-fiqh-0408: Which acts must a person performing Umrah (minor pilgrimage) complete after entering ihram (pilgrimage consecration)?
Circumambulation, walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah, and shaving
Walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah, staying overnight at Mina, and shaving
Circumambulation, stoning the pillars, and shaving
Standing at Arafah, circumambulation, and shaving

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that someone performing Umrah does not perform all the acts of Hajj, but must complete the acts of Umrah: tawaf (circumambulation), sai (walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah), and shaving.
easy-fiqh-0409: A man voluntarily dedicates a sacrificial camel, but it becomes lost before reaching its designated place. What must he do?
He must replace it and fast three days
He may replace it or leave it

Ibn al-Qattan said: They agreed that if a dedicated sacrificial camel becomes lost or dies, it must be replaced if vowed; if voluntary, he may replace it or leave it. Scholars do not disagree on this.
easy-fiqh-0410: A voluntary sacrificial animal reaches its designated place and is slaughtered. May its owner eat from it?
Yes, provided he donates an equal amount
No, eating from it is forbidden for him
Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that when a voluntary sacrificial animal reaches its designated place, its owner may eat from it if he wishes.
easy-fiqh-0411: Which is better for the owner of a sacrificial animal: slaughtering it himself or appointing someone else?
He must appoint a resident of the Sacred Precinct

Ibn al-Qattan said: There is no disagreement that slaughtering one's sacrificial animal oneself is better than assigning it to another, because the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, did so.
easy-fiqh-0412: A pilgrim completes his Hajj rites and the stoning, then performs tawaf al-ifadah (the main Hajj circumambulation). What becomes permissible for him?
Everything forbidden to him by ihram

Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that someone who performs tawaf al-ifadah on the Day of Sacrifice or afterward, having completed the Hajj rites and stoned, may hunt, have sexual relations, use perfume, wear fitted clothing, marry, arrange marriages, and do everything prohibited by ihram (pilgrimage consecration).
easy-fiqh-0413: What is the ruling on ihram (pilgrimage consecration) for Hajj?
A duty whose omission is compensated by a sacrifice
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that ihram for Hajj is obligatory.
easy-fiqh-0414: A woman prays with her whole body covered except her face. What is the ruling on her prayer?
Deficient; she repeats it within its time
Invalid because her face was uncovered
Complete only if she prays at home
Ibn al-Qattan said: A woman must cover her whole body except her face. If she does so, her prayer is complete by agreement.
easy-fiqh-0415: What is the ruling on facing the qiblah (prayer direction) for someone who can see the Kabah and is neither fighting nor afraid?
Obligatory in congregation but not alone
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that facing the qiblah for prayer is obligatory for someone who can see it or knows its indicators, unless fighting or afraid.
easy-fiqh-0416: Which of these requires ghusl (a full ritual bath) by scholarly agreement?
Ejaculation of semen through intercourse or a wet dream
Touching a woman with desire without ejaculation
Discharge of pre-ejaculatory fluid during fondling

Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that the discharge of gushing fluid, after which the penis becomes flaccid, whether through intercourse, a wet dream, or any other means, from a man or woman, requires ghusl.
easy-fiqh-0417: Someone who performed tayammum (dry purification) because water was unavailable prays behind an imam who performed wudu (ablution) with water. What is the ruling on his prayer?
Valid for voluntary but not obligatory prayer
Ibn al-Qattan said: Scholars agreed that someone who performed tayammum may follow someone who performed wudu.
easy-fiqh-0418: A man performing wudu (ablution) washes part of his face and leaves part unwashed. Does his face washing suffice?
It suffices if he is traveling
It suffices if he washed his forehead and cheeks
Ibn al-Qattan said: Washing only part of the face in wudu does not suffice, by consensus.
easy-fiqh-0419: To which place is the Hajj (pilgrimage) obligatory for Muslims directed, by scholarly consensus?
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that Hajj is to Makkah, not elsewhere.
easy-fiqh-0420: Scholars agreed that whoever says in his talbiyah (pilgrimage response): «لبيك اللهم لبيك، لبيك لا شريك لك لبيك، إن الحمد والنعمة لك...» [Here I am, O Allah, here I am. Here I am; You have no partner; here I am.] has recited it. How does this talbiyah end?
And all command; none is worshipped besides You
And might and dominion; there is no god other than You
And all bounty; we have no Lord besides You
And sovereignty; You have no partner

Ibn Hazm reported agreement that reciting the talbiyah in this form suffices: Labbayka Allahumma labbayk ... inna al-hamda wa an-nimata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika lak (Here I am, O Allah, here I am ... praise, favor, and sovereignty belong to You; You have no partner).
easy-fiqh-0421: How many days after the Day of Sacrifice did scholars agree are days for stoning the pillars?
Ibn Hazm said: They agreed that the three days after the Day of Sacrifice are days for stoning the pillars.
poetry-fusha-0411: What did Zuhayr mean by: 'Whoever refuses the spear butts will obey the spearheads mounted on every keen shaft'?
Whoever disobeys his people is expelled
Whoever cannot make spears perishes by them
Whoever opposes the elders is obeyed by the young
Whoever rejects peace is humbled and softened by war
The Arabs presented the butt ends of spears when seeking peace. If both sides refused, they reversed their spears and fought with the points. Whoever rejected peace thus submitted to war.
poetry-fusha-0415: In Tarafah's verse, 'My companions halt there on their mounts, saying: Do not perish from grief; be steadfast,' what does 'tajallad' mean?
Tajallud means making oneself show fortitude: exercising patience.
poetry-fusha-0416: Tarafah likens death to an extended tether in: 'By your life, death, while it misses a youth, is like a slack tether whose folded ends are held in the hand.' What is this tether?
A rope extended to let an animal graze, with its end held by its owner
When death misses a youth, it is like a slack rope tethering an animal, with both ends held by its owner: the animal cannot escape it.
poetry-fusha-0418: What did Tarafah mean by: 'I do not settle in the ravines out of fear; whenever my people ask for support, I support them'?
He does not graze his camels in ravines for fear of floods
He avoids valleys for fear of enemies and lives in mountains
He does not hide in ravines to evade guests; he camps openly and helps whoever seeks his help
He dislikes traveling on high ground
He does not hide in ravines so guests and travelers cannot see him; he camps in the open and helps whoever asks him for aid.
poetry-fusha-0419: In Tarafah's words, 'He made me despair of every good I sought, as though we had placed him in a recessed grave,' what does 'rams' mean?
Rams means a grave, originally burial: he made him despair of any good, just as no good is expected from a dead person.
poetry-fusha-0422: In Imru al-Qays's description of rain, 'Some of its spray passed over al-Qanan, bringing the usm down from every perch,' what are 'usm'?
Ibex with a white marking on one foreleg
Usm is the plural of asam, an ibex with white on one foreleg. The rain brought them down from the mountain through the force of its downpour.
poetry-fusha-0423: To what did Imru al-Qays compare rain falling on the desert of al-Ghabit in: 'It laid its burden on the desert of al-Ghabit, like a Yemeni laden with bags alighting'?
A shepherd scattering his sheep in pasture
A Yemeni merchant alighting and spreading out his varied fabrics
He compared the kinds of plants brought forth by rain to the varieties of fabrics spread out for sale by a Yemeni merchant with bags of goods.
poetry-fusha-0424: In Imru al-Qays's description of a flood, 'The beasts drowned in it at evening, at its far edges, looked like anabish unsul,' what are 'anabish unsul'?
Anabish are plant roots, and unsul is wild onion. He likened the drowned, mud-covered beasts to them.
poetry-fusha-0427: Labid likened a wild cow to a seafarer's 'jumanah' in: 'She shines against the darkness, like a seafarer's jumanah with its string removed.' What is a 'jumanah'?
Juman and jumanah mean a pearl-shaped bead fashioned from silver, then are used figuratively for a pearl.
poetry-fusha-0428: In Labid's words, 'She spent the night while dripping rain poured from a dimah, continuously watering the thickets,' what is a 'dimah'?
Persistent rain lasting at least half a day and a night
Dimah is persistent rain lasting at least half a day and a night.
poetry-fusha-0429: What does 'its clouds kafara the stars' mean in Labid's verse, 'Repeated rain rises over the ridge of her back, on a night whose clouds kafara its stars'?
The stars shone through the clouds
The clouds parted from the stars
The clouds concealed and covered the stars
Kafr means covering and concealing: on a night whose clouds covered its stars.
poetry-fusha-0432: What does Antarah mean by: 'I have been told that Amr is ungrateful for my favor; ingratitude sours the benefactor's soul'?
A benefactor dislikes those who thank him
Ingratitude discourages a benefactor from giving
Too many blessings corrupt their recipient
He says: I was told that Amr does not thank me for my favor; ingratitude discourages the benefactor from giving.
poetry-fusha-0433: In Antarah's words, 'When they used me as a shield against spearheads, lam akhim; rather, my advance grew constrained,' what does 'lam akhim' mean?
Khaym means cowardice: they made him a barrier between themselves and the spearheads, and he did not lose courage before them.
poetry-fusha-0434: In Antarah's description of rain, 'Pouring and streaming, water runs over it every evening, lam yatasarram,' what does 'lam yatasarram' mean?
It did not reach the ground
Tasarrum means cessation: rainwater flows over it every evening without stopping.
poetry-fusha-0435: In Antarah's words, 'In the hawmat al-harb, whose depths heroes complain of only with murmurs,' what is 'hawmat al-harb'?
Its main center, where it rages
Hawmat al-harb is its main center, where the battle revolves or rages.
poetry-fusha-0437: In al-Nabighah's description of the Euphrates, 'When its high waters surge, its awadhi cast foam on both banks,' what are 'awadhi'?
Jashat means surged; ghawarib are the high parts of the water; awadhi are waves; and abran are the two banks.
poetry-fusha-0438: What did al-Nabighah ask of al-Numan in: 'Judge like the maiden of the tribe when she looked at a flock of pigeons coming to the waterhole'?
To hunt pigeons at the water
To marry him to the tribe's maiden
To judge his case wisely and reject the informer against him
Be wise like the maiden of the tribe when her statement proved correct, and do not accept the words of one who informed against me.
poetry-fusha-0439: What lesson did al-Asha illustrate by: 'Like an ibex butting a rock one day to split it: it did not harm it, but weakened its own horn'?
Whoever attempts what he cannot manage brings harm upon himself
Whoever endures hardships achieves his goal
The strong always defeat the weak
You burden yourself with what you cannot manage or attain, and its harm returns to you.
poetry-fusha-0446: In Abu Ishaq al-Ilbiri's poem in ta, opening 'The days grind your heart to pieces,' he says, 'Abu Bakr, I have called you, if only you would respond, to what benefits you, if you understand.' What does he call Abu Bakr to in this poem?
The poem advises and encourages the pursuit of knowledge. The following line says: 'To knowledge through which you become a leader.'
poetry-fusha-0448: In Qatari ibn al-Fujaah's words, 'I say to her, when she has scattered in terror before the champions: Take heart; you shall not be frightened,' whom does 'I say to her' address?
He says to his soul, scattered by fear of the champions: Do not panic; be brave and patient.
poetry-fusha-0449: In Qatari ibn al-Fujaah's verse, 'The garment of survival is no garment of honor, to be folded away from the submissive yara,' what does 'yara' mean?
The submissive man is abased, and yara means a heartless coward. Survival for a coward is no garment of honor.
poetry-fusha-0450: Al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani said: 'You are a sun, and kings are stars; when you rise, no star is visible.' What is the purpose of the poem containing this verse?
Apologizing to al-Numan ibn al-Mundhir and praising him
Boasting of his people, Banu Dhubyan
Al-Alam al-Shantamari introduced it by saying: He spoke apologizing to al-Numan ibn al-Mundhir and praising him.
poetry-fusha-0455: In a verse in Diwan al-Hamasah, 'I stayed with the family of al-Muhallab in winter, far from my homeland, in a time of mahl,' what is 'a time of mahl'?
A time of war and turmoil
A time without rain, when pasture dries up
The Hajj season and sacred months
A harvest time with abundant fruit
Mahl originally means cessation of rain and drying of pasture. He stayed with the family of al-Muhallab in winter while afflicted by drought and scarcity.
poetry-fusha-0457: In a verse in Diwan al-Hamasah, 'Every generous man averts blame through qira; among the righteous there is a path for truth,' what is 'qira'?
Qira means food served to guests. The generous man spends his wealth to protect his honor, averting blame by feeding guests.
poetry-fusha-0458: What does this verse in Diwan al-Hamasah mean: 'If a man cannot attain noble conduct while young, seeking it in maturity is difficult for him'?
One who fails to attain noble conduct in youth is unlikely to attain it in maturity
Noble conduct is sought only after maturity
One who seeks noble conduct young grows tired of it when mature
An old man is more capable of noble conduct than a young man
If a person is too weak to attain noble conduct while young, attaining it in maturity is remote for him.
poetry-fusha-0459: In Diwan al-Hamasah, the poet says: 'Wealth and poverty do not arise from a youth's resourcefulness, but are allotted portions and fortunes.' He holds that wealth and poverty are:
The result of intelligence and good planning
Portions Allah has allotted among His servants
Determined by how much one travels
Wealth and poverty are not obtained through planning and effort; they are portions Allah has allotted among His servants.
poetry-fusha-0462: What does this verse in Diwan al-Hamasah affirm: 'There is no good in handsome, stately bodies unless minds adorn their beauty'?
Physical beauty and perfection are of no good without reason
Reason appears only in a beautiful body
Physical beauty and perfection are of no good without reason, through which adornment and perfection become complete.
poetry-fusha-0463: In a verse in Diwan al-Hamasah, 'When among tall men, I rise above them with an arifah until I am called tall,' what is an 'arifah'?
Arifah is a favor bestowed. Among tall men, he rises above them through his kindness until he is called tall.
poetry-fusha-0464: What does this verse in Diwan al-Hamasah mean: 'Thus was I disciplined until it became my character; I found good manners to be the foundation of noble disposition'?
Good manners are inborn and cannot be acquired
Character can be mastered only through good manners
Good manners are sought for wealth and status
He was raised with good manners until they became his character, and finds nothing through which character can be mastered except good manners.
poetry-nabati-0359: By what name did people know Muhammad al-Awni's poem opening, 'O Allah, Ruler over every ruler, the best One called upon to remove great affliction'?
Al-Abbudi stated that people knew it as Al-Tawbah (Tawbat al-Awni) and recited it in gatherings.
poetry-nabati-0361: Who composed this verse: 'O Knower of wrong and right, protect me for long from the evil of Your creation'?
The verse is from Muhammad al-Awni's poem Al-Tawbah.
poetry-nabati-0368: Who composed this verse about worldly life: 'The world destroyed them and its mill turned; in what we witnessed, its lessons became clear to us'?
Al-Abbudi included it among Muhammad al-Awni's poems outside war and politics, under 'He spoke about worldly circumstances.'
poetry-nabati-0374: Who composed: 'High deeds and glory are not attained by wishes, by a mere hope uttered by an immature heart'?
The verse is from a poem by Muhammad al-Awni opening 'The ascent to eminence stands upon cutting blades.'
poetry-nabati-0375: Who composed: 'Poetic lines in my chest seem woven together; I open the way to sound judgment when its door is shut'?
Al-Abbudi included it among Muhammad al-Awni's short poems.
poetry-nabati-0377: Muhsin al-Hazzani describes a fine camel: 'A great, high-fronted, noble camel; its rider could not restrain it but for its bara.' What are 'bara'?
A camel's equivalent of a horse's bit, attached to the halter
A rope securing loads on a camel's back
A whip used to urge a camel on
A hobble securing a camel at pasture
Al-Abbudi said: Bara is the plural of barah, a camel's equivalent of a horse's bit, attached to the halter, with which the rider checks its pace.
poetry-nabati-0378: Who composed this description of a fine camel: 'Well-trained, no different from swirling dust; no one can match it on the day of encounter'?
Al-Abbudi quoted it from Muhsin al-Hazzani's description of a fine camel, as evidence for the word bara.
poetry-nabati-0379: Who composed this description of a she-camel: 'Strong-cheeked, when the long deserts stretch, she crosses the wilderness like a sailor's boom vessel'?
The verse is from a poem Muhammad al-Abd Allah al-Qadi sent to Muhammad ibn Ali al-Arfaj, recorded by the orientalist Socin.
poetry-nabati-0380: Mandil al-Fuhayd said: 'Whoever calls it Nabati has no proof; this is our language, clear and sound in meaning.' What name does he consider correct for this poetry?
The preceding line says: 'Poetry is our literature, and its name Popular is correct.' He favors calling it popular poetry and rejects calling it Nabati.
poetry-nabati-0382: In Abd al-Rahman al-Rubayyi's verse, 'I think none mastered Nabati poetry like Ibn Arfaj, with whom the Qawadi contend,' who are the 'Qawadi'?
The judges of al-Qasim who adjudicate disputes
Poetry narrators who correct its meters
Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi and several poets from his family
The poets of Unayzah generally, without distinction
Al-Abbudi said: Qawadi is the plural of al-Qadi, referring to Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Qadi and several poets in his family.
poetry-nabati-0384: In al-Hurayyis's words, 'I praise Him who replaced naft with shash,' what do 'naft' and 'shash' mean?
Al-Abbudi explained: Naft means tar, and shash means perfume.
poetry-nabati-0385: In Sanad ibn Qaid al-Khamshi's words, 'Ghawsh, valiant men whose work serves the valiant; they work only for honorable people,' what does 'ghawsh' mean?
Al-Abbudi explained: Ghawsh here means brave men of gallantry, hence their description as valiant.
poetry-nabati-0386: In Ibn Fallaj's words, 'My pity for the man whom the shuqr have left a beggar,' what are the 'shuqr'?
Palm trees, plural of shaqra, the known palm variety
Al-Abbudi explained: Shuqr is the plural of shaqra, the known palm tree, and tawwaf means a beggar.
poetry-nabati-0387: In Ibn Fallaj's words, 'Whoever wants kayf should plant on the outskirts,' what does 'kayf' mean?
Al-Abbudi explained: Kayf means money that brings enjoyment and pleasure; the outskirts are those of Buraydah.
poetry-nabati-0388: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Samhan said in Bilbays, Egypt: 'My moan is like the moan of the fatir brought to Bilbays.' What is the 'fatir'?
Al-Abbudi explained: Fatir is an aged she-camel. The moan here figuratively means sorrow and anguish.
poetry-nabati-0389: In Muhammad ibn Dukhayyil ibn Yusuf's words, 'They run dry when the Arabs quench their thirst, while those of the kawakib draw tirelessly,' what are the 'kawakib'?
Al-Abbudi explained: Kawakib is the plural of kawkab, a well with abundant water; tanzah means its water runs out.
poetry-nabati-0397: Who composed this Nabati verse, cited as evidence of stone and tree worship among the Bedouin of Najd: 'If you ask about my people, O Mani, do not ask: worthless stones and trees they worship'?
The book Dawat al-Shaykh Muhammad Abd al-Wahhab wa Atharuha fi al-Alam al-Islami attributes it to the vernacular poet Rashid al-Khalawi.
